# Bugs

Known compiler defects: incorrect output, crashes, miscompiles, rejection of valid code, missing diagnostics for unsafe code.

For missing features and language design gaps see `TODO.md`.

Each entry's first line is a **[priority size]** tag plus a one-sentence summary; the full description follows on the next lines. Priority is one of:

- `IMM` -- users hit this in their first non-trivial program (or basic Python idioms);
- `HIGH` -- users hit this regularly in non-trivial programs / stdlib work;
- `MED` -- specific patterns or advanced features;
- `LOW` -- latent / quality / hardening, no current user impact.

Size is one of `small` (hours-1d), `medium` (1-3d), `large` (~week), `xlarge` (bigger).

Entries may carry an immutable **slug** in brackets right after the headline (e.g. ``[`union-nocopy-field-store`]``) -- a stable anchor for pointing at one entry out of hundreds. Add one when an entry is first referenced (from source, a test, or another entry); new entries get one up front. Every reference, in code comments and inside this file alike, is spelled ``BUGS.md#<slug>`` -- an anchor-style token that cannot collide with ordinary prose, so one grep finds every reference. A slug never changes once assigned, even if the headline is later reworded, and `tpyc/test_bugs_slugs.py` fails on a reference whose entry is gone -- so a fixed entry cannot be deleted while a stale pointer to it survives. **What that check does NOT cover:** it validates `BUGS.md#<slug>` citations only. Around 150 source and test files still mention `BUGS.md` as a bare file reference, which cannot dangle but also cannot be resolved to an entry, and nothing counts them down. The backlog this convention has to work through is therefore the REFERENCE side, not the entry side -- an un-slugged entry costs nothing, an un-slugged reference is the thing that sends a reader to an 829-entry file.

Entries tagged `deferred: MIR` must NOT be patched in the current AST/sema model; do not pick them up with `/tpy-fix-bug`. Lifetime and loan defects (dangling views and borrows, missing or spurious invalidation warnings, escapes through returns, frames, closures and fields) are routed to the analysis-only MIR, which replaces sema's borrow machinery rather than extending it (`docs/MIR_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`); a few older tagged entries that are not lifetime defects (tuple and union element forms in `## Compiler bugs`) wait on the borrow/storage form duality instead (`docs/IR_DESIGN.md` Open Questions 9/11/13). Bugs outside that machinery -- C++ build failures, codegen form, readonly, copy-vs-alias -- stay ordinary bugs even when they sit in the Safety section.

## Compiler bugs

- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A user record's `__getitem__`, `__call__` or `__contains__` with a type parameter of its own fails the C++ build.** [`generic-user-nonop-dunder-type-param-ill-formed`] `def __getitem__[C: AnyFixedInt](self, k: C) -> int64` renders the `operator[]` shim as `int64_t operator[](::tpy::readonly_form_t<C> k) const` with no template header (`'C' was not declared`); `__call__` does the same to its `operator()` shim, and `int32(3) in v` over a generic `__contains__` calls `v.__contains__(3)` with no template argument, which `readonly_form_t<C>` cannot deduce. Sibling of the operator dunders, which are refused at the definition since 2026-09-30 (TODO.md "A user operator method with a type parameter of its own"); these three are dispatched outside the operator resolver and were left out of that refusal. Probes `/tmp/agents/gdunder/gi.py`, `gc.py`. Pre-existing. Fix shape: the same as the TODO entry (the shim spells the member's template argument), or extend the definition-site refusal to them. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A user record's `__pow__` fails the C++ build.** [`user-record-pow-renders-std-pow`] `def __pow__(self, k: int32) -> Own[V]` used as `v ** int32(2)` renders `std::pow(v, 2)` (the `__pow__` row of `DUNDER_CPP_TEMPLATES`, `tpyc/sema/operators.py`, which user methods take as their `cpp_template`), and g++ reports *no matching function for call to 'pow(V&, int)'*; `__rpow__` has the same row. No friend shim exists for it either (C++ has no power operator). Probe `/tmp/agents/gdunder/p_pow2.py` (2026-09-30). Pre-existing. Fix shape: `__pow__` / `__rpow__` render as a direct method call on a user record, as `__floordiv__` does. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence, run-time panic) An `int` shift by a count no `int32` holds panics.** [`bigint-shift-count-beyond-int32-panics`] `x >> 3000000000` over `x: int` (and `p >> 3000000000` over a literal-seeded local, which the literal makes an `int`) renders `x >> ::tpy::BigInt(3000000000LL)`, and `BigInt::operator>>(const BigInt&)` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/bigint.hpp`) narrows the count with `to_fixed_check<int32_t>()`, so it panics *int32 overflow: value out of range* where CPython prints 0 (or -1 for a negative `x`); `<<` by such a count cannot allocate in CPython either, so only `>>` diverges. The fixed-width sibling (`int64(-1) >> int64(100)` panics) is the documented shift-count divergence; this one is the `int` side, undocumented. Probe `/tmp/agents/wide/b4.py` (2026-09-30). Pre-existing. Fix shape: `>>` by a count past the magnitude's bit length answers 0 / -1 in the runtime.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence, run-time panic) An integer power with a negative exponent panics where CPython returns a float.** [`int-pow-negative-exponent-panics`] `2 ** -1` prints 0.5 under CPython and panics in TPy with *Negative exponent not supported (would require float)*; `pow(a, b)` over ints does the same. `docs/EXCEPTION_DESIGN.md` names it as a TPy limitation, with no entry here until now. Pre-existing. A literal-seeded local now reaches it through a constant store too: `n = 1; n = 2 ** -1` makes `n` an int (the constant folds to no literal, and the operation types `int`) and panics at run time (probe `/tmp/agents/pint/c/negexp.py`, 2026-09-30). Fix shape: type `int ** <negative constant>` as a float in sema, and decide what a run-time negative exponent over an int-typed result does. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic wording) A folded constant stored into a fixed-width local is reported as a literal the source never wrote.** [`folded-constant-range-names-literal`] With `u` a `uint8` loop variable, `u = 3 - 4` is refused with *Integer literal -1 is outside uint8 range [0, 255] in reassignment to 'u'* (probe `/tmp/agents/review2-parity/u8_folded.py`, 2026-09-30); no `-1` appears in the source. The message should name the expression as written and offer the fix (annotate the local, or convert explicitly). A literal-seeded local takes such a constant as a literal store (`u = uint8(5); u = 3 - 4` makes `u` an `int32` and prints -301, as CPython), so the refusal is reached only for a local whose type is fixed another way. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output; ill-formed C++ under `-Werror=conversion`) A fixed-width index wider than `int32` into a `list` is passed unconverted to its `int32_t` index parameter.** [`wide-fixed-index-unconverted`] `k: int64 = int64(4294967296); print(xs[k])` with `xs: list[int32]` emits `::tpy::__getitem__(xs, k)`, and C++ converts the `int64_t` to the `int32_t` parameter implicitly: a plain `tpy` build prints `xs[0]` (probe `/tmp/agents/pint/c/wi.py`, 2026-09-30) where CPython raises `IndexError`, and the test harness's `-Werror=conversion` rejects the build. A `BigInt` index takes the checked `.to_fixed_check<int32_t>()` narrow (`_bigint_index_disposition`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`); a wider fixed-width one takes no conversion at all. Now also reached by a literal-seeded local an `int64` store widens (`k = 0; xs[k]; k = int64(1)`). Fix shape: the fixed-width sibling of the BigInt narrow (a checked narrow into the receiver's index width), keyed on the same disposition. Found building `tests/cases/int/pending_num_locals`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (SILENT wrong order / wrong value, no diagnostic; pre-existing) An inherited-field write in `__init__` runs AFTER later own-field member-inits.** [`inherited-field-write-runs-after-member-inits`] The base constructor owns an inherited member, so `self.<base field> = x` in a subclass `__init__` runs in the constructor body; it does not end the member-init list, so an own-field init after it that does not read it stays in the list and runs FIRST. `super().__init__(); self.tag = pick(1); self.a = pick(2)` (`tag` inherited) prints `pick 2` then `pick 1` where CPython prints `pick 1` then `pick 2` (probe `/tmp/agents/r3review/parity/p4.py`), and an inherited write that reads an `Own` param a later member-init moves reads it moved-from: `self.tag = str(p.v); self.b = p` renders `b(std::move(p))` in the list and the `tag` write after it, printing `0 4` where CPython prints `4 4` (probe `/tmp/agents/r3review/safety/inh1.py`). A later own-field init that reads the inherited field DIRECTLY is demoted to the body (`CTOR_DEMOTE_READS_INHERITED`), so that face is correct. Fix shape: an inherited-field write ends the member-init chain like any body statement (`chain_broken` in `lower_constructor`, `tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`), at the snapshot cost of moving every own-field init after an inherited write into the body. Found 2026-09-29 by the review of the admission-by-form unit.
- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no diagnostic) A record's fields take `__init__` ASSIGNMENT order, so the facts derived from field order follow it where CPython follows annotation order.** [`record-field-order-follows-init`] Own fields are reordered to the order `__init__` assigns them (`reorder_fields_by_init`: a base-less record at parse time, a record with bases at registration), which keeps the C++ member-init list in source order. With `@dataclass(order=True) class V: y: int32; x: int32` and `__init__` assigning `x` then `y`, `V(5, 1)` prints `V(x=5, y=1)`, `astuple` gives `(5, 1)`, `asdict` `{'x': 5, 'y': 1}` and `case V(p, q)` binds `5 1`; CPython prints `V(y=1, x=5)`, `(1, 5)`, `{'y': 1, 'x': 5}` and `1 5`. The same record with a base (`class U(A)`) gives `astuple` `(0, 5, 1)` and `asdict` `{'a': 0, 'x': 5, 'y': 1}` against CPython's `(0, 1, 5)` and `{'a': 0, 'y': 1, 'x': 5}`, while its positional class pattern still binds in annotation order (`__match_args__` is settled before the based reorder) (probe `/tmp/agents/r4review/parity/p4.py`). A plain class with no `__match_args__`, which CPython refuses to match positionally (`TypeError: D() accepts 0 positional sub-patterns`), binds its positional sub-patterns in assignment order, with or without a base (probe `/tmp/agents/r4review/cg/p6.py`). Fix shape: keep the declared order as the order every derived fact (repr, `astuple` / `asdict`, `__match_args__`, order comparison) reads, and give the C++ layout its own order. Found 2026-09-29 by the review of the admission-by-form unit. On a based `@dataclass` the divergence is also internal: `repr` prints annotation order (`U(a=0, y=1, x=5)`) while `astuple` / `asdict` give assignment order (`(0, 5, 1)`), where master gave CPython's `(0, 1, 5)` but ran the initializers out of source order.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A `dict` union, a `dict(d)` copy and a `set` union with a literal operand are type errors, even into a local.** [`dict-union-and-dict-copy-reject`] With `d: dict[str, int]`, `c = d | d` fails `Invalid operand types for '|': Ref[dict[str, int]] and Ref[dict[str, int]]`, and `c = dict(d)` fails `dict() cannot be constructed from dict[str, int]`; CPython builds a new dict either way (probe `/tmp/agents/docsync_pb/p6.py`). `set(s)` and `s | s` on a `set[int]` compile, but `a | {3}` at `a: set[int]` types the literal `set[int32]` and fails `Invalid operand types for '|': set[int] and set[int32]` (probe `/tmp/agents/abf/r5/docs/setor.py`; master too). The field-admission sweep's `dict[str,int]__binop` (`a | {"z": 1}`) and `__conv` cells (10) are these errors at a field sink. Found 2026-09-29 by the review of the admission-by-form unit.
- **[MED small] (SILENT copy where CPython aliases, no warning; pre-existing) A chained assignment into two reference-typed fields copies the source into each field with no diagnostic.** [`chained-field-assign-copies-silently`] `self.p = self.q = a` (`p, q: P`, `a: P` a param) stores two independent copies: `a.v = 102` afterwards prints `chained 1 1 102` where CPython prints `102 102 102`; `self.p = self.q = P(7)` then `self.p.v = 111` prints `111 7` where CPython prints `111 111`, and the constructor and local-holder spellings do the same. The single-target `self.p = a` warns `copies P into field`; the chained form is desugared into one write per target, and the copy warning never sees the shared source. Fix shape: warn (or reject) at the desugaring when a reference-typed source feeds more than one target. Probes `/tmp/agents/r2review/parity/p14.py`, `p15.py`. Found by the review of the admission-by-form unit 2026-09-29.
- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) The field sink still refuses a handful of source shapes at every position.** [`field-sink-remaining-rejects`] Measured by `scripts/thir_migration/review/field_admission_sweep.py` (positions ctor / method / generator method / async method / local holder, cell counts summed over them); the constructor and the method agree cell for cell. (1) A tuple ELEMENT source `t[0]`: 57 cells over every slot type (`subscript.tuple_shape`; `res.param_type:tuple` in a frame). (2) A walrus: 28 cells -- `expr.walrus` at every value-type and view slot and at the union / container slots from a borrowed value, `res.local_storage` for a frame's Optional / union local; a walrus naming a fresh record (`self.p = (q := mk(1))`) lowers and warns the copy. (3) A value-type select with two name arms (`self.s = a if c else b` at an `Optional[str]` / `Optional[bytes]` / value-union / `P | Q` field): 20 cells at `expr.ifexpr`. The literal-armed select `self.b = b"z" if c else None` lowers now. (4) A `StrView` field from another field, a field chain, an element, a `dict.get` or a select: 25 cells at `assign.field_write_shape` -- the view slot's fence, which has no provenance fact to admit a source that outlives the object. (5) A `list` slice into a list field (a slice is a `Span`, so the assignment is a type mismatch) and a `set` `|` with a literal operand: 10 cells, sema type errors of the sweep's program, not field-sink rejects -- the same source is refused into a local. The `set` and `dict` rows are `BUGS.md#dict-union-and-dict-copy-reject`. (6) A `P | Q` borrow-returning method result (5, `return.own_union_source`). (7) A generator / async frame's Optional-str / Optional-bytes / value-union LOCAL at a field write: 12 cells at `res.local_storage`. (8) A body write of an Optional or tuple VIEW field (`StrView | None`, `tuple[StrView, int32]`) from a name (`self.o = s`), a select with a `None` arm or a tuple literal: `assign.field_write_shape`, as on master; `None` lowers, and a member-init takes a name (not measured by the sweep). Each is its own lowering arm; none is a field-sink gate any more. Found 2026-09-29 by the review of the admission-by-form unit.
- **[LOW small] (latent; the lowering compensates) A materializing view->owned coerce feeding an `Optional[str]` slot is typed by sema as the Optional, not as the owned value it builds.** [`materialize-coerce-typed-as-optional`] The coerce that copies a `StrView` into an owned `str` at an `Optional[str]` slot carries the slot's `str | None` as its result type, although what it materializes is the owned inner, which the slot's converting assignment absorbs. The THIR lowering undoes it (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`, the `disp == "materialize"` branch of the coerce lowering: an Optional result type is unwrapped to its inner before the `THIRFormConvert` is built), so every consumer that reads the coerce's type before that point sees the wrong one. Fix shape: sema types the coerce's result as the materialized owned inner, and the lowering's unwrap goes.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) In an `async def`, a value-Optional local bound from an `await` reads bare after narrowing.** [`async-await-bound-narrowed-optional-read-bare`] `w = await pick_whole(5)` (`-> int32 | None`), then `if w is not None: y = w + 1` renders `y = (::tpy::add_check<int32_t>(w, 1));` inside the coroutine frame -- `w` is the frame's `std::optional<int32_t>` member, so g++ reports `cannot convert 'std::optional<int>' to 'int'`. The narrowed read's `(*w)` deref is missing. The same body with the local bound from a literal (`w: int32 | None = 5` after an `await`) renders `(*w)` and runs, so the trigger is the await-bound binding, not the frame. `print(w)` there compiles only because the print arm wraps the whole optional (`print_optional_val(w)`) and ignores the narrowing; a value-position read breaks. Repro `/tmp/agents/cppr2/c/m5.py` (control `m6.py`), 2026-09-28. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic wording) Four constructor / destructor diagnostics explain themselves in C++ terms.** [`init-del-diagnostics-name-cpp`] PITFALLS forbids C++ in diagnostics; these predate the parent-init rule and are pinned in `diag.txt` files: (1) the split-point warning `field 'x' is not initialized before the constructor body; it will be default-constructed in C++ (in CPython, the attribute would not exist)` (`_check_init_field_assignments`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) -- e.g. "starts default-initialized"; (2) `'Parent.__del__(self)' is not callable via the unbound-self form. C++ invokes each base destructor automatically.` and its `super().__del__()` twin (`tpyc/sema/methods.py`) -- e.g. "each base's `__del__` runs automatically after the child's"; (3) `Parent class has __del__() which will be called automatically by C++ ...` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`); (4) the multi-base order warning `... C++ runs base constructors -- and evaluates their argument expressions -- in declaration order ...` (`validate_multi_base_init_calls`, `tpyc/sema/registration.py`) -- e.g. "TPy initializes the bases in declaration order". The THIR reject format ("not yet supported by C++ code generation") is intended and stays. Reword in Python terms and regenerate the pinned `diag.txt` files. Pre-existing on master.

- **[LOW small] (diagnostic wording) The frozen-field error names `@dataclass` for a generic record flag any macro can set.** [`frozen-field-error-names-dataclass`] `RecordInfo.is_frozen` is a generic "fields are immutable after `__init__`" flag that a class macro sets through `macro_api` (`record.is_frozen = True`), but the assignment check in `tpyc/sema/statements.py` hardcodes its kind as `"frozen dataclass"` (`Cannot assign to field 'x' of frozen dataclass 'R'`), so a `@model` or user macro that freezes a record gets a message naming `@dataclass`. The compiler provides the mechanics and the macro owns the policy: word it generically ("frozen record") or build it from the macro that set the flag (the record's macro origin, the way synthesized-`__init__` messages use `macro_origin`). Pre-existing on master.

- **[HIGH small] (rejects valid code, loud; everyday shape) Printing a type-parameter-typed field inside a generic class's method is rejected.** [`generic-method-print-typeparam-field`]
  `class G[U]` with `a: U` and `def show(self) -> None: print(self.a)`, then
  `G[int32](1).show()`, rejects at
  `stmt.expr_stmt:print.arg.generic_field_access`; so does
  `print(pre, self.a)` with `pre: U`, and `G[str]` the same. CPython prints
  `1`. `print(str(self.a))` compiles and runs; binding the field first
  (`x = self.a`) rejects at `decl.slot_type` instead. Probes
  `/tmp/agents/cpyparity_r4/q8.py`, `q7.py`. Pre-existing on master
  `c854c7b482`. Found 2026-09-26 by the parent-initializer review. Needs
  `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) A container literal passed to an INHERITED generic `__init__` parameter is rejected.** [`inherited-generic-init-container-literal`]
  With `class G[U]` taking `def __init__(self, a: U)` and
  `class H[W](G[list[W]]): pass`, `H[int32]([1, 2])` rejects at
  `expr.container_literal`, and one level further
  (`class M[T](H[tuple[T, T]])`, `M[int32]([(1, 2)])`) the same. The same
  literal straight to the owner (`G[list[tuple[int32, int32]]]([(1, 2)])`)
  compiles, and a named argument (`xs = [(1, 2)]; M[int32](xs)`) compiles,
  so the literal's element type is not resolved against the parameter
  after the inherited `U` is substituted through the class chain. Sibling
  of BUGS.md#inherited-generic-ctor-view-arg (same inherited-ctor route,
  view-family argument). CPython runs all of them. Probes
  `/tmp/agents/cpyparity_r4/r1.py`, `r2.py`, `q1.py`, `q2.py`. Pre-existing
  on master `c854c7b482`. Found 2026-09-26 by the parent-initializer review.
  Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain error shown to the user) A generic function's local first assigned from a parameter in both branches of an `if` fails the C++ build at every instantiation.** [`generic-hoisted-param-alias-drops-const`]
  `def pick[T](a: T, b: T, f: bool) -> T: if f: r = a else: r = b; return r`
  hoists `T* r;` and assigns `r = &(a)`, but `a` is
  `::tpy::param_val_or_ref_t<T>`, a `const T&` for a record, so g++ rejects
  `const Coord*` -> `Coord*` (`int32` and `str` fail the same way:
  `const int*` -> `int*`, `string_view*` -> `string*`). The hoisted slot's
  type is spelled from `T` instead of from the parameter form it aliases; the
  non-generic twin is fine. Related to the hoisted match-capture const drop
  (`const_borrow_tuple_locals` entry above). Reproduces on master
  `d32f0f0108`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium] (rejects valid code, misleading message) An `__init__` with a `*args` parameter cannot be called.** [`star-args-init-rejected`]
  `class Acc: def __init__(self, *xs: int32)`: `Acc(1, 2)` reports
  *'Acc' has no __init__; use @dataclass or define __init__ to accept
  constructor arguments*, and `Acc()` rejects at THIR `expr.call`. The same
  for a `ValueType`. Free functions and methods take `*args`
  (LANGUAGE_FEATURES "`*list` unpacking at call sites"); the constructor
  call path never learned the variadic signature, and the first message
  names the wrong cause. Found 2026-09-26 by the placeholder design review.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, located) A ternary cannot join mutable and readonly aliases of the same record at a readonly return.** [`readonly-record-ternary-join-rejected`]
  In a function taking `a: Cell` and `b: readonly[Cell]` and returning
  `readonly[Cell]`, `return a if flag else b` rejects because the ternary
  branches have incompatible types. The equivalent separate branches,
  `if flag: return a` followed by `return b`, compile; both return an alias
  through the readonly result. The rejection happens during semantic analysis,
  before THIR or MIR. Audit common-type selection and expected-type propagation
  for readonly reference branches alongside Optional/union and other readonly
  joins; neither branch should acquire mutable access or require a copy.
  Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) Binding a borrowed result from an `@readonly` free function drops return constness.** [`readonly-free-return-binding-drops-const`]
  With a plain reference-type `Cell`, a free function decorated `@readonly`
  and defined as `def keep(cell: Cell) -> Cell: return cell` emits
  `const Cell& keep(const Cell& cell)`, but the caller's
  `saved = keep(cell)` emits `Cell& saved = keep(cell)`. The C++ compiler
  rejects the binding for discarding qualifiers, even when the caller only
  reads `saved.value`.
  Free-function signature emission projects constness from the declaration's
  `is_readonly`, while the inferred local binding misses that projected return
  access. An explicit `readonly[Cell]` return annotation works in the probe.
  Audit the shared result-access decision across declaration, reseat,
  forwarding and sibling callable forms before fixing individual consumers.
  MIR's selected signature fact preserves emitted access and refuses
  mismatched caller bindings.
  Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) Discarding a tuple-returning call with a record constructor argument is rejected.** [`discarded-tuple-call-rejects`] With a hook-free `Cell(value: int32)` and `def pair(cell: Cell) -> tuple[int32, int32]: return cell.value, 1`, the expression statement `pair(Cell(1))` inside an ordinary function fails with `expr.call:call.ret_type.tuple`. The result is unused, but the call must still run with its argument evaluated. This is an existing frontend/THIR-lowering rejection before MIR, found during named-argument storage review on 2026-09-23. Handle in the separate tuple-completeness work: audit discarded call results alongside binding, unpacking and return positions, preserving argument evaluation and temporary lifetime. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) A record constructor argument in a boolean-combined while condition rejects, while the equivalent ternary condition compiles.** [`while-bool-record-argument-rejects`] With a hook-free `Cell(value: int32)` and `positive(cell: Cell) -> bool` returning `cell.value > 0`, `while flag and positive(Cell(value)):` fails with `stmt.while:expr.call:call.arg_shape.record_f1`. The same loop using `while positive(Cell(value)) if flag else False:` compiles, as does the direct condition `while positive(Cell(value)):`. A return-position boolean combination also compiles. This is a frontend admission difference, before MIR; the named-storage work preserves the current source boundary. Reproduced during its scope probes on 2026-09-23. Audit condition-position argument lowering alongside ordinary lazy operands before extending the gate; preserve deferred construction and fresh per-iteration storage.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A generic STATIC on a generic `@native` record called through the class name drops the class template arguments.** [`native-generic-static-class-targs-dropped`] `NBox[int32].of(3)` renders `::ns::NBox::of(3)` (ill-formed for a class template), while the module-qualified `nm.NBox.of(4)` renders `::ns::NBox<int32_t>::of(4)`. The same-module generic-native static arm in `_marker_call_kind` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) spells `ri.native_name::method` itself instead of composing through `static_class_cpp` / `_compose_static_targs`. Probe `/tmp/agents/r3cg/nat/`, found in the enum-methods review 2026-09-23. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A module that reaches an enum only through another module's function spells the enum type bare.** [`transitive-enum-type-spelled-bare`] `std::optional<Hue> m = ::tpyapp::mid::maybe(true);` in a module that never imports `Hue` fails with "'Hue' was not declared"; the decl type renders the short name without the declaring module's qualification. No enum methods involved. Probe `/tmp/agents/r3cg/xf/`, 2026-09-23. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) An inline generic member body (a record method template, or a generic enum method) that uses a record declared LATER in the file gets "invalid use of incomplete type".** [`inline-generic-member-later-record-incomplete`] The template body is emitted in-struct, before the later record's definition. Related to the `@overload` inline-in-struct entry but not covered by it. Probes `/tmp/agents/r3cg/p8b.py`, `p9.py`, `p10b.py`, 2026-09-23. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A generic body returning `tuple[T, T]` built from `(w[0], x)` fails to compile at `T=str`.** [`generic-tuple-return-str-view-element`] `to_val_or_ptr` receives a `string_view` where the tuple element is `std::string`; the free function `twicef("b")` fails the same way. Probes `/tmp/agents/r3cg/p1.py`, `p2.py`, 2026-09-23. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A method inferred readonly that returns a module-global list is emitted `const std::vector<T>& get() const`, so mutating the result fails to compile.** [`readonly-method-global-list-return-const`] `b = x.get(); b.append(3)` -- records and enum methods alike; CPython aliases the global. The inferred-readonly return projection makes the borrowed return const although the list is not reached through `self`. Probes `/tmp/agents/r3par/recget.py`, `alias.py`, 2026-09-23. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud; pre-existing) A user class named `__enum_<Name>` next to an enum `<Name>` with methods collides with the enum's companion record.** [`enum-companion-name-collision`] Rejected with an unrelated "Record '__enum_Color' has no field 'v'"; CPython runs it. The companion's name is reserved; a located "reserved name" error would be the fix. Probe `/tmp/agents/r3par/clash.py`, 2026-09-23.
- **[LOW small] (cosmetic C++) An enum `@property` getter is declared non-const (`bool warm();`) while every other enum method and every record property getter is `const`.** [`enum-property-getter-non-const`] The getter is only ever called on the companion's temporary wrapper (`__enum_Color{c}.warm()`), so no call fails; the difference is only in the emitted declaration. Found by the enum-methods readiness check (probe `/tmp/agents/enumretro/`, 2026-09-23). **Stopped 2026-09-28:** the direct fix -- let enum property getters take part in const inference -- collides with BUGS.md#readonly-method-global-list-return-const. Property getters live in `rec.properties`, outside the const inference in `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`; once inferred, an enum getter returning a module-global list would render `const std::vector<...>& fns() const` and `c.items.append(5)` would stop compiling. Fix that entry first.
- **[LOW small] (misleading diagnostic location; pre-existing) A diagnostic on a node of a macro fragment cites the fragment's own line number against the module file.** [`macro-fragment-diag-local-line`] A class macro that adds `def broken(self) -> int32: x: int32 = 1; y: str = "a"; return x + y` through `cls.add_method_from_source` reports `main.py:4: error: Invalid operand types for '+': int32 and str` -- line 4 is the `return` line counted inside the dedented fragment, while `main.py` line 4 is unrelated (a blank line in the probe). The fragment parser stamps `SourceLocation.fragment_lines` on every fragment node (which the source echo now reads), but diagnostic formatting ignores it and prints `loc.line` against the module's file. `quote_fun` and `ast.quote` fragments share the parser, so they share the defect; builder-trace `emit_function` hides it only because `_strip_fragment_locs` (`tpyc/sema/builder_trace.py`) clears the locations. Fix shape: when a diagnostic's location carries `fragment_lines`, cite the macro application site (the decorated class / call) and name the generated member, with the fragment line as secondary detail. Probe `/tmp/agents/cppr3/fragdiag/`, 2026-09-28. One fix covers this entry and BUGS.md#macro-body-source-echo-wrong-file: give each macro fragment its own source identity (a virtual file registered with its lines on the compiler, named by `loc.file`), so the echo and diagnostic formatting both index the right source. A fix that carried the fragment's lines on every `SourceLocation` for the echo alone was built and reverted 2026-09-28: it left a location with two answers to which source it indexes.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, pre-existing) An `Optional` holding a plain-`Enum` member whose VALUE is 0 tests falsy.** [`optional-enum-zero-member-falsy`] `o: Optional[Color] = Color.Red` (`Red = 0`) then `"t" if o else "f"` prints `f` under TPy and `t` under CPython: a plain `Enum` member is always truthy (only an `IntEnum`'s truth is its integer), but `::tpy::is_truthy(std::optional<T>)` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/core.hpp:603`) tests `static_cast<bool>(*opt)`, which reads the underlying 0. The optional-truthiness warning fires with a "may exclude falsy non-None values" reason that is wrong for a plain Enum, which has no falsy members. A bare (non-Optional) member tests truthy correctly. Probes `/tmp/agents/r2par/truth.py`, `/tmp/agents/r2cg/tr.py`, verified 2026-09-23. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud) A borrow returned from an enum `@property`'s `self` is treated as borrowing the receiver, so binding it off a call receiver rejects.** [`enum-method-self-borrow-temporary`] `x = get().nm` through a `@property` rejects at `local_decl.lends_from_temporary` (the method spellings `get().nm()` / `get().me()` compile since, re-measured 2026-09-29), although an enum member has no storage to borrow from (`.name` is a view into static storage). The record-method return-borrow facts (receiver slot `-1`) are applied to the companion's by-value `self`. Safe (loud), found by the enum-methods review (probes `/tmp/agents/enumsm/i.py`, `j.py`, 2026-09-22).
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud) A record getter that returns a GLOBAL (or an argument), read off a temporary receiver, is treated as borrowing the temporary.** [`getter-global-off-temporary-rejects`] `x = mk(1).gprop` with `@property def gprop(self) -> Inner: return G` rejects at `local_decl.lends_from_temporary`; CPython binds `G` itself (`x.v = 5` then `print(G.v)` prints `5`). As a `key=` lambda body (`key=lambda r: mk(r).gprop`) it rejects at lowering (`expr.lambda`). The value-category helpers (`value_category.returns_borrow` / `is_rvalue_source`) take the result of a getter called on an rvalue receiver as an rvalue without consulting the getter's recorded borrow source, which here is the global, not `self`. Safe (loud); the enum twin is `enum-method-self-borrow-temporary`. Probe `/tmp/agents/ltbr/gprop.py`, 2026-09-27.
- **[LOW small] (over-conservative const) A method called on a container element or loop variable without `@readonly` marks the container mutated, so a `list[...]` param loses `const`.** [`non-readonly-method-on-element-unconsts-container`] `def f(xs: list[Color]): for x in xs: x.label()` emits `std::vector<Color>& xs`; the same holds for a record element (`P.label` on `list[P]`). Nothing is rejected; the caller just cannot pass a readonly list without `@readonly` on the method. For an enum the receiver is a copy, so the mark is never needed. The same happens through a field: `h.c.lab()` makes a `Holder` param non-const (probe `/tmp/agents/r2safe/`). Found by the enum-methods review (probes `/tmp/agents/enumsm/b.py`, `g.py`, `o.py`, 2026-09-22).
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A static method carrying `@error_return` cannot be CALLED: both the direct call under `try` and the propagating call from another `@error_return` body reject at `method.marker.static.plain`.** [`static-error-return-method-call`] `class R: @staticmethod @error_return(Bad) def f(k: int32) -> int32` then `R.f(2)` inside `try/except Bad` (`stmt.expr_stmt:method.marker.static.plain`) or `return R.f(k) + 1` from an `@error_return(Bad)` function (`expr.method_call:...`); the free-function twin lowers at both shapes (`tests/cases/error_return/auto_propagate_chain`). The static-call arm in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py` has no `std::expected` unwrap/propagate row, only the free-call arm does. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/enum_r/se.py`, verified 2026-09-22 on 0.6.0.dev0. Surfaced probing `@error_return` on enum methods (an instance method on an enum lowers; a `@staticmethod` hits this). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) Iterating an enum TYPE inside a comprehension is rejected as `'Color' is not a variable`, while the `for` statement over the same enum lowers.** [`enum-type-comprehension-source`] `[c.name for c in Color]` (and the genexpr / set / dict forms) errors in sema at the comprehension source; `for c in Color:` sets `enum_iterable` on the statement and works. The comprehension source analysis resolves the iterable as a value name and never consults the ENUM binding the statement path does. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/enum_r/q.py`, verified 2026-09-22 on 0.6.0.dev0. Everyday shape (`[c.label() for c in Color]` is the natural consumer of enum methods). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; was a C++ build failure) A walrus in the initializer of a field whose type has no default constructor is refused.** [`nocopy-field-walrus-init-rejects`] `self._r = Resource((n := seed))` in `__init__`, with `Resource` a `@nocopy` / `__del__` record whose only constructor takes arguments, is refused with ``field '_r' of non-default-constructible type 'Resource' must be initialized before any local variable is bound ... the assigned expression binds a local (`:=`)``; CPython runs it. The walrus binds a constructor-body local the member initializer list has no scope to declare, so the init demotes to the body (`CTOR_DEMOTE_BINDS_LOCAL`, `_member_init_demote_reason` in `tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`), and a body assignment needs a default-constructed field first. Before 2026-09-28 the member-init was emitted with an undeclared `n` and the C++ build failed; the located error is the stopgap. Pinned by `tests/cases/records/error_nocopy_del_field_walrus`; the workaround is the factory the message names, or computing `n` in a `@staticmethod`. A fix needs a scope for the local that runs before the member initializer list (e.g. a delegating constructor that receives the walrus value as a parameter).
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A `@dispatch` record method's parameters are never const-inferred, so an rvalue argument the signature-const verdict admits bare cannot bind the emitted `T&`.** [`dispatch-method-params-never-const-inferred`] `class K: @dispatch def take(self, r: R): self.n = r.n; @dispatch def take(self, s: str): ...` emits `void take(R& r)` although the body only reads `r` (also `y = 0.5; y = K().tot2(empty_list(3))` on a `@dispatch` method taking `list[float]`, probes `/tmp/agents/parity-ihc3/ov05_method.py`, `/tmp/agents/ihc-r5/w/meth_only.py`), because the codegen signature pass skips mutation facts for every function whose `overload_form` is set (`_get_method_mutated_params` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`, meant for the bodyless `@overload` stubs) -- while sema's `const_borrow_params` for the same variant says the slot IS const. The argument rows that bind a prvalue in place trust the sema verdict, so `k.take(mk())` (record) and `k.fill(mks())` (container, `k.fill(xs: list[str])`) render bare into the mutable reference and the C++ compiler refuses (the container face was a located reject, `call.ret_type.container`, until the rvalue-call result gate stopped being record-only). The same skip also picks `overloads[-1]`'s facts for every variant of a set. The fix is codegen's: read the variant's own mutation facts (a bodied `@dispatch` variant has them) and spell the non-mutated params `const T&` like any other method's; every `@dispatch` record method signature over a reference-typed param changes with it. Found by the route-merge review.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (spurious diagnostic on valid code) A borrow-returning callee's result bound to a local from a HOISTED temporary argument is warned as dangling.** [`lend-back-of-hoisted-temp-warned-as-dangling`] `r = head(mk())` with `def head(xs: list[Rec]) -> Rec: return xs[0]` prints `warning: Result borrows from temporary argument 'xs'; the temporary is destroyed at end-of-statement`, but the emit hoists the argument into a named local at the binding's own scope (`std::vector<Rec> __tmp_1 = mk(); Rec& r = head(__tmp_1);`), so nothing dangles and the program runs correctly. Sema's lend-back check models the argument as a statement-scoped temporary; the hoist rows made it a block-scoped local. Same text for a record and a container argument. The condensed `calls/borrowed_argument_storage` case also pins a position difference: its free-function and loop calls warn, while the method and constructor-tail twins do not. The fix is sema's: a lent-back argument hoisted into a scope enclosing every use is not destroyed at end-of-statement. Hoisting alone does not make a borrow safe when its holder escapes that block; direct temporary-bearing pointer declarations and reseats remain rejected, while alias-mediated escapes from already-admitted backing are not yet prevented (see `BUGS.md#select-slot-alias-escape-unchecked`). Found by the route-merge review.
- **[LOW small] (wrong signature consulted) The user-method argument gate reads the FIRST overload's signature facts, not the resolved overload's.** [`record-method-arg-gate-reads-first-overload`] `_lower_method_arg_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) passes `overloads[0]` to `_record_method_arg_ok`, so every row that reads `const_borrow_params` or `mutated_params` off `req.overload` (the const-slot rows, the rvalue-in-place rows) judges an overload SET by its first member; a set whose variants differ in which parameter they mutate gets the wrong verdict for the later variants. Masked today by `dispatch-method-params-never-const-inferred` (the signatures are all mutable anyway). The fix threads the resolved `FunctionInfo` the call carries. Found by the route-merge review.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A BORROW-returning `__add__` whose payload is a CONTAINER has no render at an `Own` return slot, in either spelling.** [`dunder-borrow-container-own-return`] `def __add__(self, o: Pool) -> list[int32]` then `def f(p: Pool, q: Pool) -> Own[list[int32]]: return p + q` rejects at `stmt.return:binop.shape.+.record`, and so does the explicit `return copy(p + q)` -- the binop's own lowering declines a RECORD operand at the borrow-bind read the copy-construct tail takes. The RECORD payload of the same shape lowers (`tests/cases/returns/warn_return_record_borrow_dunder`), so the two families disagree on one operator spelling; sema warns the copy at both. Pinned by `tests/cases/returns/error_return_container_borrow_dunder`. The binop result gate keeps the record slice for this reason: widened, the borrow-dunder result binds a const alias and a write through it is a C++ error instead (`binop-borrow-result-alias-bound-const`). Found while downgrading the Own-return borrowed-source error to the owning-slot warning 2026-09-06.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) `list([...])` over a str-element literal has no lowering arm.** [`list-ctor-over-str-literal-unlowered`] `a = list(["x", "y"])` rejects at `expr.call:call.special.call_type.builtin_generic` (`tests/cases/list/error_list_ctor_str_element_literal`); the bare literal `["x", "y"]` and `list(xs)` over a named list compile. The builtin-generic call form (`list(<literal>)`) is one of the special-builtin callee kinds the call lowering has no arm for when the element target the call derives is a str literal's. Found while pinning the reject tag during the route merges.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) `if xs:` on a pointer-repr `Optional[container]` name has no render: the truthiness mode sema attaches is the None test alone.** [`optional-container-truthiness-drops-emptiness`] `def probe(xs: list[int32] | None) -> bool: if xs: ...` rejects at `stmt.if:cond.name` (`tests/cases/none_safety/error_truthy_optional_container`). The pointer-repr Optional NAME row in the truthiness lowering renders the bare pointer test, which is the whole truth for a record pointee (a record without `__bool__` / `__len__` is truthy whenever it is not None) and half of it for a container's: CPython's `if xs:` is `xs is not None and len(xs) > 0`. Sema attaches no truthiness mode to the Optional name, so the row cannot tell the two apart and keeps the container rejecting rather than emit `(xs)` and print True for an empty list. The fix is sema's: a pointer-repr Optional over a type whose own truthiness is an emptiness or dunder test gets a mode that says so, and the row renders `xs != nullptr && <pointee test>` (the value-repr Optional already renders `::tpy::is_truthy` over the whole optional). Found by the route-merge sweep when the Optional-ptr binding stopped being record-only.
- **[LOW small] (hidden allocation; pre-existing) A `str` local re-bound after a block that declared it takes owning storage even for a literal.** [`str-rebind-after-block-local-owns`] `if k == 1: r = "a"; print(r)` then `r = "b"; print(r)` emits `std::string_view r = "a";` in the block and `std::string r = "b";` after it (probe `/tmp/agents/batchC/elif_impl/t8.py`, same on master 1ea64345ea); nothing in the function needs owning storage, so the second declaration heap-allocates for a static literal. The `if`/`elif` spelling shows it too (`tests/cases/control_flow/elif_arm_bound_local`, section `rebind_after`). Likely the view resolution keying the name's settled type on its last declaration (`var_decl_by_name`), which the second block-level binding is.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated; pre-existing) A `str` local bound from a concatenation in one `if` arm and from a `str` PARAM in the other assigns a view into the owned string.** [`branch-str-param-into-owned-local`] With `a: str` a param, `if c: s = a + "!" else: s = a` then `print(s)` emits `::tpy::String s;` in front of the `if` and `s = a;` in the `else` arm; g++ rejects the assignment (`no match for 'operator=' (operand types are 'tpy::String' and 'std::string_view')`). The per-arm `elif` form fails the same way at the declaration (`::tpy::String s = a;`, *conversion from 'std::string_view' to non-scalar type 'tpy::String' requested*). CPython prints both values. Probes `/tmp/agents/meta_gc/n1.py`, `/tmp/agents/meta_gc/w5c.py`, same on master 1ea64345ea. The joined type is right (one arm owns a fresh string); the arm binding the param view is missing the view-to-owned conversion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated; pre-existing) A module that imports a global and rebinds its name at top level declares it twice.** [`imported-global-rebound-at-top-level`] `from helper import VAL` (`VAL = 10` in `helper.py`), a top-level read, then `VAL = 5` at top level emits both `inline auto& VAL = ::tpyapp::helper::VAL;` and `extern int32_t VAL;` in the importing module's header; g++ reports `conflicting declaration 'int32_t tpyapp::predecl::VAL'`. CPython prints the import's value, then 5. Probe `/tmp/agents/batchC/r1_rest/predecl.py` (with its `helper.py`), found 2026-09-26. The body lowering already carries the order-aware spelling for this shape (`_LowerCtx.pre_decl_import_cpp`); the header's import alias and the module's own global are what collide. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) A loop-body local read after its `for` is rejected only when a module global shares its name.** [`loop-local-read-after-loop-with-same-named-global`] `w = 50` at module level and `def f(): for j in range(2): w = j` then `print(w)` stops with `variable 'w' may not be assigned at this point`; without the global the same function compiles and prints `1`, as CPython does (probes `/tmp/agents/batchC/r1_rest/p2h.py` / `p2i.py`, found 2026-09-26; pre-existing, identical on 1ea64345ea). The local is the function's own either way (it is assigned there, no `global`), so the global's presence should not move the definite-assignment verdict. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) `del xs[i]` on a list literal local that is otherwise unmutated spells the fixed-size array.** [`del-item-array-literal-local`] `xs = ["a", "b"]; del xs[0]; print(xs)` resolves `xs` to `std::array<std::string, 2>` and fails at `__delitem__(std::array<...>&, int)` (no matching function); CPython prints `['b']` (probe `/tmp/agents/rv2r2/p_delarr.py`, verified 2026-09-23). A `del` of an item is a structural mutation the list-literal optimization does not count, so the Array form survives. Sibling of `copy-array-literal-into-list-slot` (another use the Array decision misses).

- **[MED small] (compiler crash) A nested def that returns a borrow inside a function returning a VALUE is validated against the ENCLOSING function's return type.** [`nested-def-return-validated-against-enclosing`] `def outer() -> int32: def inner() -> R: return GR; ...` stops with `Internal error: outer: THIRReturn at ...: BORROW return value for value-typed return int32` -- the THIR validator checks the nested def's `THIRReturn` against `outer`'s return type. The record spelling crashes on master; the container spelling (`def inner() -> list[int32]: return GL`) crashed the same way from 2026-09-22, where it had been the located reject `return.record_source.ptrlocal.borrow`, so the crash is the only diagnostic the shape gets. Fix shape: the validator's return check reads the function whose body the `THIRReturn` sits in (the nested def), not the enclosing frame's. Probes `/tmp/agents/unify/review/safety/p18/main.py` (record), `p19/main.py` (container). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the gate unification.
- **[MED small] (compiler crash) A `match` arm spelled `case _ as v:` over a RECORD subject crashes the lowering.** [`match-bound-wildcard-record-arm-ice`] `match r: case _ as v: v.x += 1` raises `AttributeError: 'TpyWildcardPattern' object has no attribute 'patterns'` in `_match_record_arm_always` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`): its docstring says a wildcard arrives as `test is None`, but an `as`-BOUND wildcard arrives as a `TpyWildcardPattern`, and the tail assumes an or-pattern (`for a in test.patterns`). `case v:` over the same subject lowers. Fix shape: treat a `TpyWildcardPattern` test as the always-arm before the or-pattern walk. Surfaced building the reference-sink sweep 2026-09-22 (its `match_capture` sink is spelled `case v:` because of it).
- **[MED small] (compiler crash) A tuple literal over a CAPTURED unannotated list local inside a nested def crashes sema.** [`nested-def-tuple-of-captured-pending-list-ice`] `s0 = [1, 2]` in a function, then `def inner() -> None: t = (s0, 1)` raises `AssertionError: Internal error: composite expr type tuple[PendingList[...]#N, IntLiteral(1)] still has a Pending* leaf after finalization` (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`, via `_analyze_nested_def` -> `resolve_all`): the captured literal is finalized in the enclosing body after the nested def was analyzed, so the tuple built inside it still holds the pending leaf. An annotated `s0: list[int32]` compiles, and so does the same tuple in the enclosing body. Hits list, record-element list and Array sources in a function, a method and a constructor (9 cells of the reference-sink sweep, 2026-09-22).
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic quality) Passing a recursive-alias-typed parameter to a parameter of the same alias reports `Type mismatch in argument: expected Json, got Json`.** [`recursive-alias-param-identity-mismatch`] `type Json = None | bool | int32 | str | list[Json]`, `def take(p: Json)`, `def f(pv: Json): take(pv)`: the check compares alias INSTANCES rather than the alias, so the same spelled type on both sides is reported as a mismatch a reader cannot act on. Surfaced by the reference-sink sweep 2026-09-22 (`ru_wrap__nested__param__*` rows).
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud, internal-sounding message) The `protocol_slot` argument cell admits a FIELD read when the gate is told there is no flush position, and lowering then rejects it from inside with a prose message instead of a tag.** [`protocol-slot-field-arg-no-flush-tag`] At a flush-less argument position -- the nested constructor one is the reachable spelling -- `_protocol_slot_arg(..., temps_ok=False)` returns True for a field read at a structural-protocol slot, and the render then raises `protocol arg-temp outside a flush position`, which reaches the user as *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (protocol arg-temp outside a flush position)*. Every other reject at that position spells a `call.ctor_arg.<family>` tag, so this one reads like an internal assertion and cannot be histogrammed with the rest. The gate and the render disagree about which faces are temp-free: the predicate's `temps_ok=False` leg excludes the structural-RVALUE temp but not the field read's. Reproducer: a `@dynamic` protocol `DynP`, a record `K` whose `__init__` takes a structural-protocol parameter `p: P`, a fixture `class B` with a field of a conforming record type, then `Rc.new(Box(K(b.field)))` -- `tests/cases/calls/ctor_nested_tempfree_args` is the same chain with the shapes that do work. Tripwire: the cells `proto_p__ro__obj_field__nested` and `proto_p__ro__nested_field__nested` of `scripts/thir_migration/review/arg_family_sweep.expected.json` hold that message as their verdict. Workaround: bind the field to a local first (`p = b.field; Rc.new(Box(K(p)))`), which the bare-NAME face admits. Fix shape: the predicate's no-flush leg excludes every face whose render hoists, so the gate's answer and the render's agree -- the field read then falls through to the family tail and gets its tag. Found sharing the temp-free rows into the nested ctor family, 2026-09-21. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A frame re-renders an ITERATOR-OBJECT `for` source rooted at a frame LOCAL, or reached through a free function, at every advance, so an impure accessor handing one back runs once per element.** [`frame-iter-next-source-reevaluated`] Inside a generator or `async def` the `next` / `iter_next` strategies spell the advance off the source expression itself -- `__for_r_0.emplace(h.get().__next__());` -- so a source that names existing storage is EVALUATED once per step. With
  ```python
  class Holder:
      calls: int32
      def get(self) -> SimpleIter: self.calls += 1; return self.it
  def rows(h: Holder) -> Iterator[str]:
      for v in h.get():
          yield "x " + str(v)
  ```
  TPy reports `calls 4` over three elements where CPython reports `calls 1`; the values are right, the side effects are not. NARROWED 2026-09-22: a method-call source whose receiver chain is rooted at a param, a capture or `self` is now held by reference in the frame (`frame_slot<T&>` of the source's own `decltype`; `iter_object` in `tests/cases/generators/frame_for_source_once` counts one call), so the shape above is fixed. What still re-renders: a chain rooted at storage the frame holds BY VALUE -- a frame local (`h = Holder(); for v in h.get():`) or a by-value param (`h: Own[Holder]`, a value type, an owned `str` copy, a deduced `Fn` / static-protocol slot; `own_param_iter` in the same case pins the shape) -- because the reference would point into the frame's own storage (a frame no longer moves once entered, 2026-09-23, so that alone no longer forces the re-render); a chain with a hop that returns BY VALUE (`self.make().get()`), which would point into a temporary; and a FREE-function call returning a reference (`for v in pick(h):`), whose root the receiver walk does not see. Both keep `__for_r_0.emplace(<call>.__next__())` per advance. Repro `/tmp/agents/review_loopsrc/testcov/p4_iternext_lvalue.py` (rewrite `h` as a local). Surfaced by the test-coverage review of the loop-source ownership branch, 2026-09-21.

- **[MED small] A script filename containing a hyphen produces an invalid C++ namespace.** [`hyphenated-script-name-cpp-namespace`] Running a valid Python script named `m317-parity-independent.py` emits `namespace tpyapp::m317-parity-independent`, which the C++ compiler rejects. Renaming the same script to `m317_parity_independent.py` builds and runs successfully; CPython accepts either filename. `module_to_cpp_namespace` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py` replaces dots with namespace separators but does not escape the script basename. Found by an independent parity probe during the MIR tuple-storage review; unrelated to MIR admission or tuple storage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught, pre-existing) A comprehension whose ELEMENT is a borrow-returning method call spells an array of references.** [`comprehension-elem-borrow-call-array`] `ys = [b.rec_m() for _ in range(2)]`, with `def rec_m(self) -> R` returning a field by reference, emits `std::array<R&, 2>` and the C++ compiler rejects it ("forming pointer to reference type"). Verified on master and on the property-read-normalization branch alike, so it is not the normalization's. The comprehension's element slot takes the call's BORROW return form as the element type instead of deciding between an owning copy and a container that cannot hold a reference -- the same question the accessor spelling of the same comprehension is refused for (`container_elem.accessor_lends_storage`, `tests/cases/records/error_property_elem_lends_storage`), which is why only the method spelling reaches the emitter. The TUPLE-element sink of the same source renders an owning copy instead, so the fix is the comprehension sink's, not the whole element family's. Loud, never silent. Fix shape: give the comprehension element slot the same verdict the tuple element slot takes (copy, warned) or the reject the accessor spelling takes; the choice is the element-slot rule, so it belongs with `container_elem.accessor_lends_storage` rather than beside it. Tripwire: the cells `comp_elem__rec__meth__{named,temp}` of `scripts/thir_migration/review/property_position_sweep.expected.json` are `ok` at the comp phase and fail the script's `--exec` half. Found by building and running the sweep's new rows, 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent missing null check, WARNED as present) A `@property` read through an UNPROVEN `Optional[record]` receiver emits the bare member call with no null check, while the line warns that one was added.** [`property-read-unproven-optional-receiver`] `def via_prop(h: H | None) -> int32: return h.val` with `@property def val(self) -> int32` emits `return h->val();` and warns *Potential None access on optional value; generated code adds runtime null check* -- the check is NOT there, so a None receiver dereferences a null pointer where CPython raises. The METHOD twin on the next line gets it: `h.val_m()` emits `return ::tpy::deref_check(h).val_m();` under the identical warning. Probe `/tmp/agents/t1safety/p10_opt_recv.py`; identical on master, so the property-read normalization neither caused nor fixed it. The warning is the aggravating half: a reader who sees it has been told the program is safe. Cause, and the fix's home: sema stamps `needs_optional_runtime_check` on the ACCESS node when the receiver's type is an unproven Optional, and the property path never renders it -- on master because the synthesized getter call was built before the stamp and carried `deref_depth == 0`, and on this branch because `become_method_call` (`tpyc/parse/nodes.py`) deliberately does NOT transfer the receiver-shape markers (`needs_optional_runtime_check`, `deref_depth`, `deref_narrowed_to`, `ptr_non_null`): they were stamped for a FIELD lookup, and transferring them made three cases spell hops the getter render does not take (`method.marker.deref.ptr`). So the fix is not to transfer the marker but to ask the RECEIVER's category where the getter call is lowered, the way the method-call arm already does -- one question at the dispatch, not a marker copied across a node-kind change. Surfaced by the property-read normalization review (safety-model), 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, located) A `@property` read in both arms of a TERNARY off a read-only receiver has no render, because the binding's const-ness is not taken from the receiver.** [`getter-source-const-not-tracked`] `v = s.r if c else s.r` with `@property def r(self) -> Rec` in a body that only reads `s` is a located reject, `expr.ifexpr`, on master and on the property-read normalization alike -- the arm stays closed precisely because the render it would take is ill-formed: the body emits `void prop_ternary(const Src& s, bool c)`, the const receiver selects the `@auto_readonly` const twin whose return is `const Rec&`, and the binding form spelled off the getter's DECLARED return is `Rec& v = ((c) ? (s.r()) : (s.r()));` -- *binding reference of type 'Rec&' to 'const Rec' discards qualifiers*. The container flavour is the same (`v = s.xs if c else s.xs` -> `std::vector<int32_t>& v = ...`). The spelled-method twin COMPILES: `s.r_m()` is not `@readonly`, so the call marks the receiver mutated, the parameter stays `Src&` and the non-const overload runs -- `void meth_ternary(Src& s, bool c)`. So the cost today is a reject where the method spelling renders, not wrong code. Probe `/tmp/agents/task1/impl/const_getter_pair.py`. Cause: the local's binding FORM is computed from the getter's DECLARED return (`Rec`, a borrow -> `T&`) while its CONST-ness is not taken from the receiver at a composite init. The bare decl `v = s.r` escapes it only by accident -- `_is_borrowing_auto_readonly_accessor` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) credits that init as a mutation of `s`, so the parameter is `Src&` and the non-const twin runs; a ternary init is not a method call, so no credit fires and the two halves disagree. Both halves are one decision: the TODO entry *"A borrow DECLARATION is credited as a mutation of its source"* proposes rooting that credit on the WRITE instead, which removes the accidental escape and makes the const-ness question unavoidable -- so fix them together. This entry BLOCKS the storage-ref lift arms queued in TODO.md (a ternary arm lifting `optional_to_ptr(s.o())` spells `const T*` off a const receiver and hits the identical mismatch). Surfaced by the property-read normalization review (codegen-correctness), 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output / wild pointer) The literal-bound-local proof that a loop runs does not see a mutation that empties the container.** [`literal-bound-local-proof-ignores-mutation`]
  `NarrowingTracker._name_bound_to_nonempty_literal` (`tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`)
  proves a `for` head runs at least once when the name it iterates has exactly
  one write in the write history and that write is a non-empty container
  literal. Mutation is not a write, so the proof survives everything that can
  empty the container in between:

  ```python
  boxes = [Box(1), Box(2)]
  boxes.clear()
  for b in boxes:
      last = b
  last.n = 99          # accepted; `Box* last;` is read uninitialized
  ```

  TPy writes through a wild pointer (no diagnostic; the run above survives only
  by luck); CPython raises `UnboundLocalError`. Same with `boxes.pop()` twice,
  with `del boxes[0]`, and with the container passed to a callee that drains it
  -- the interprocedural spelling being the one no local check can see.
  Reproducer `/tmp/agents/review_zt/safety/pW_wildptr.py`. Loud alternatives
  (`items: list[Box] = []` then `append`, a parameter, a call result) do not
  prove and are unaffected.
  **Fix shape:** the container-non-empty flow-fact family TODO.md's emptiness-guard
  entry describes -- a fact keyed on the container place, seeded by a non-empty
  literal binding and by `len(c) > 0` / a truthiness test, KILLED by a rebinding
  and by any mutation that can empty it (`clear`, `pop`, `remove`, `del`, a pass
  to a mutating parameter), merged at joins like `ValueRange`. One family closes
  this defect and that feature gap together; neither should be built without the
  other, since the kill set is what makes the seed sound.
  **Interim bounds**, each independent of the family: null-initialize the
  hoisted pointer predecl and keep the promoted local out of the proven
  non-null set after the loop, so the unsound slice is a checked null
  dereference instead of a wild pointer; or drop the proof when the name has
  any method call, `del` or pass-as-argument between its binding and the loop.

- **[LOW small] (lost check elision + duplicated decoder, no diagnostic) A literal `range()` bound is recognized by the loop-runs proof but not by the range-facts recorder.** [`range-literal-bound-arm-unreached`] Two decoders read the same `range()` arguments and disagree. `NarrowingTracker._range_arg_range` peels `TpyCoerce` and so proves `for i in range(int32(3))` runs; `_track_for_range_facts` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) does not, so the same head leaves the loop variable the generic `ValueRange.for_range_index()` (lo=0, no upper bound) instead of `[0, N-1]`. Verified 2026-09-18 by wrapping the method and recording its argument node kinds: `range(4)` arrives as `('TpyCoerce', 'TpyIntLiteral')` while `range(len(a))` arrives as `('TpyCall', None)` and takes its own arm. Consequence: `a = [1, 2, 3, 4]` + `for i in range(4): total += a[i]` emits the checked `::tpy::__getitem__(a, i)` where the symbolic `range(len(a))` spelling emits the bare `a[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)]`. The asymmetry runs the other way for the `while` spelling: `i = 0; while i < int32(3):` does NOT prove the loop runs, because `condition_provably_true` reaches the operand through `_operand_range` rather than through the literal peel. **Fix shape:** one decoder for a `range()` bound and one for an integer operand, both peeling coercions, with `_track_for_range_facts` and the two proofs calling them -- not a second copy of the peel. Filed rather than applied because widening the loop variable's range changes bounds- and div-check elision across the corpus. The same literal-recognition narrowness sits on the `while` side: `liveness.while_head_always_true` matches the literal `True` node alone, so `while 1:` and `while not False:` take the opposite verdict from `while True:` for one program -- a name bound on every `break` path out of them is reported unassigned (verified 2026-09-18, `/tmp/agents/verify_zt/safety/c3_while1.py` and `c4_whilenotfalse.py`). The missing-return check shares that narrowness and REJECTS valid Python: `def f(n: int) -> int:` + `while 1:` + `if n > 3: return n` + `n += 1` errors *'f' can reach the end of the function without returning a value*, while the `while True:` spelling compiles (verified 2026-09-26). `sema.literal_utils.numeric_literal_truth` already decides a numeric literal's truth for the THIR truth-test fold; the while-head predicates should ask it too.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) A `for` over a set, dict or bytes LITERAL at the head is not lowered.** [`hoisted-local-over-set-dict-literal-head-unlowered`]
  `for x in {1, 2, 3}: y = x` then `print(y)` reports `this construct is not yet
  supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:foreach.branch_decls)`; with
  `y` given a value before the loop the same head reports
  `iter.set_literal_shape` (`iter.dict_literal_shape`,
  `iter.bytes_literal_shape` for the sibling spellings). So the literal head is
  unlowered on its own, and a body-first local read after the loop just takes
  the earlier of the two rejects. Binding the same literal to a name first
  (`s = {1, 2, 3}` then `for x in s:`) compiles and runs, which is the
  workaround and also what shows the gap is the head form alone. Sema proves
  these heads run (`for_head_provably_runs`) because whether a loop RUNS is a
  language truth and must not encode a lowering gap -- so the program reaches
  the honest lowering reject instead of a definite-assignment message that
  would be wrong. **Fix shape:** give the literal-head routes in
  `tpyc/thir/lower/` the `hoist_decls` the container / range / enum routes
  already take, and materialize the literal as the iteration source the way the
  name-bound spelling does.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong value / missing safety check) A `while True:` loop's `else` clause never runs, but its narrowing facts reach the code after the loop.** [`whiletrue-else-facts-escape`]
  The `else` clause of a `while True:` is dead code -- nothing falls out of the
  head -- yet what it proves is merged into the post-loop state:

  ```python
  def f(flag: bool) -> int:
      x: int | None = None
      while True:
          if flag:
              break
      else:
          x = 5                  # never runs
      return x + 1               # TPy prints 1; CPython raises TypeError
  ```

  TPy emits an unchecked dereference of the `int | None` (the `else` clause's
  `x = 5` narrowed it to `int`) and prints `1`; CPython raises
  `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'`.
  Pre-existing and identical at `a8c56ce958`. Repro
  `/tmp/agents/verify_zt/safety/h1_whiletrue_else_narrow.py`. **Fix shape:**
  the same predicate that already tells the body join there is no fall-through
  edge (`liveness.while_head_always_true`) should keep the `else` clause's
  facts out of the post-loop state entirely -- the clause is unreachable, so it
  contributes nothing, neither bindings nor narrowing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code) A `break` or `continue` inside a `try` whose `finally` binds a name does not count that binding.** [`break-join-ignores-finally-binding`]
  The post-loop assignment join snapshots the assigned set AT the `break`, so a
  name bound by a `finally` the break unwinds through is missing from it, and a
  read after the loop is rejected with `variable 'w' may not be assigned at
  this point`. Repro: `for i in range(3):` / `try:` / `if flag: break` /
  `finally: w = 9`, then `return w` -- CPython runs the `finally` on the break
  path and prints `9`. The `continue` edge is the same snapshot and the same
  gap: `for i in range(1):` / `try: continue` / `finally: v = 1`, then
  `return v` is rejected where CPython prints `1` (verified 2026-09-18,
  `/tmp/agents/verify_zt/safety/b1_try_finally_continue.py`). The conservatism
  is on the safe side (it rejects, never miscompiles) and no corpus case has
  either shape. **Fix shape:** take the snapshot after the `finally` bodies the
  edge unwinds through rather than at the `break` / `continue` statement
  itself -- one fix for both edges, since they file into one record.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) After a bare `raise` in an `except E as e` handler of a return-tier `try`, a `finally` nested INSIDE that handler reads `e` moved-from.** [`reraise-moves-bound-error-before-finally`]
  `except Bad as e: try: raise / finally: print("finally sees:", e.message)` inside an `@error_return(Bad)` function prints `finally sees: ` under TPy and `finally sees: boom` under CPython. `e` is `auto& e = *__err_opt_N`, and the bare `raise` parks `__tpy_ret = ::tpy::make_unexpected(std::move(*__err_opt_N))` BEFORE the finally body runs, so the body reads the moved-from object (`tpyc/thir/emit.py`, unchanged by the return-exception value work). Only the nested form reaches it: in a `finally` of the OUTER try CPython has already unbound `e`. A data-carrying return exception (a `str` or container field) is what makes it observable. Fix shape: materialize the parked value after the finally chain, or copy instead of move when a finally frame is active. Found by /tpy-review (safety-model) 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++, loud) The `ReturnException` marker as a type-parameter bound renders a struct where C++ expects a concept.** [`return-exception-marker-as-type-param-bound`]
  `def show[E: ReturnException](e: E) -> None` emits `template<::tpy::ReturnException E>`; `::tpy::ReturnException` is the empty value BASE of user return exceptions, so C++ reads a class-type non-type template parameter and g++ fails at the first call ("expected a constant of type 'tpy::ReturnException', got 'E1'"). The declaration alone compiles. Before the value base existed the same bound failed for lack of any such symbol, so this never worked. The marker has no methods to bound a generic over, so the cheap fix is a sema reject of the marker as a bound; the structural one is TODO.md "Return exceptions: follow-ups" item 3 (a base-spelling entry separate from `ProtocolInfo.cpp_concept`). Found by /tpy-ready's second opinion 2026-09-18.

- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence) `str(e)` of a return exception is its declared `message` field and nothing else, so it differs from CPython's `args` rendering, and `print(e)` disagrees with `str(e)`.** [`return-exception-str-reads-message-only`]
  Three faces, probed 2026-09-18. (2) A class that declares `message`, stores it, and calls a bare `super().__init__()` (legal; it clears `args` in CPython): TPy prints the message, CPython prints `""`; likewise a `super().__init__(msg)` followed by `self.message = other` prints `other` where CPython prints `msg`. (3) For a class that declares `message`, `str(e)` and an f-string print the message while `print(e)` prints `<Missing object at 0x...>`: the `__str__` codegen emits for the field is invisible to `_record_has_str_repr`, which picks the `operator<<` body (the thrown tier's same `print(e)` symptom is the `print(e)` / `str(e)` entries below). (4) A class-level default (`message: str = "x"` with an argless `__init__`): TPy's `str(e)` is `x`, CPython's is `""`. No diagnostic on any of them; the rule is documented in docs/ERROR_RETURN_DESIGN.md "Exception Type", which is not a warning. (2) and (3) are consequences of the return-exception value work. Root and fix are one design question -- no implicit `__str__`, the class writes its own, which CPython runs identically -- in TODO.md "Return exceptions: follow-ups", item 4. Found by /tpy-ready's second opinion. Face (1) -- a subclass `__init__` that skips `Exception.__init__`, so CPython's `str(e)` renders the constructor's arguments (`(1, 'x')` where TPy printed `""`) -- is no longer silent on either tier: skipping the call is warned ("TPy default-constructs the 'Exception' part instead"), though the warning does not say the message is affected; a call's one argument on a return exception initializes the declared `message` field (`/tmp/agents/rev_skipwarn/p8.py`). The THROWN tier has face (2) too: a subclass's `self.message` is the runtime exception's own `message` field (the one `str(e)` reads), so `super().__init__(); self.message = m` prints `m` for `str(e)` where CPython prints `""` (`/tmp/agents/final_par/p1.py`); `super().__init__(m)` is the spelling both agree on.
- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid, CPython raises) Two parent-initializer spellings CPython rejects compile and run.** [`exception-message-init-accepts-invalid`] (1) On a return exception that declares `message: str`, `super().__init__(m)` initializes the field, so `e.message` reads `m`; CPython keeps the argument only in `args` and raises `AttributeError: 'E2' object has no attribute 'message'` (`/tmp/agents/final_cg/p10.py`). (2) `super().__init__(message=why)` is accepted on both tiers -- a thrown exception prints `why` for `str(e)` (`/tmp/agents/final_par/p6.py`), a return exception takes the keyword as its message (`/tmp/agents/final_par/p5.py`) -- where CPython raises `TypeError: K() takes no keyword arguments`. Cause: the `Exception.__init__` stub names its parameter `message`, so a keyword call resolves against it, and the return tier's declared field doubles as the attribute CPython never sets. Fix shape: make the stub parameter positional-only; for (1), reading a declared `message` that only the parent call wrote is the CPython-divergent half of `BUGS.md#return-exception-str-reads-message-only` and is settled with it. Found by the parity review of the parent-init branch 2026-09-27.

- **[HIGH small] (SILENT miscompile) Inside an `@error_return(E)` function, `try: return <@error_return(E) call>` never runs its `except E` handler: the callee's result is returned as-is, unchecked.** [`try-return-error-call-skips-handler`]
  `@error_return(Bad) def outer(k): try: return inner(k) / except Bad as e: print("handler ran"); raise` with `inner` raising `Bad`: CPython prints `handler ran` and then the caller's `outer caught`; TPy prints only `outer caught`. With a mutation in the handler (`e.line = 99` before the bare `raise`) the caller sees the unmodified error. Not an ordering divergence -- the handler body never executes. The `return` operand is a call whose `std::expected<T, E>` already is the enclosing function's return type, so the statement renders `return ::inner(k);` with NO unwrap; the `has_value()` check that would `goto __except_N` (`_er_check_stmt` / `_er_check_inline`, `tpyc/thir/emit.py`, both of which do consult `try_except_label`) is never emitted, and the handler label is dead code. The pass-through is right outside a `try` and wrong under a return-tier `try` whose handler catches `E`. The ASSIGNMENT form (`v = inner(k)` then `return v`) checks and dispatches correctly, which is why no case reaches it. Distinct from the all-return-tier entry below (a non-`@error_return` outer whose `goto` tier lacks a trailing return under `-Werror`; its handler runs) and from the expression-level unwrap skipping `finally` bodies (there the call IS unwrapped). Unchanged by the return-exception value work (identical at its branch point); found by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH medium] (rejects-valid, loud) A caught exception cannot be passed where its base class is expected: `except ValueError as e: log(e)` with `def log(e: Exception)` is a type mismatch.** [`exception-value-upcast-rejects`]
  `Type mismatch in argument 'e': expected Exception, got ValueError`, for every builtin exception and for a user `class MyErr(Exception)` alike -- the everyday "hand the error to a logging helper" shape. The child-to-parent value upcast in `sema/compatibility.py` admits only `is_user_record` nominals on BOTH sides, and the builtin exception stubs are `@native` records, so the hierarchy the C++ side really has (`::tpy::ValueError : ::tpy::Exception`, bindable to `const ::tpy::Exception&`) is never consulted. `isinstance(e, KeyError)` on an `Exception`-typed binding is refused by the same blindness, with a message that is false as worded: "isinstance() check type(s) 'KeyError' are not subclasses of 'Exception'" (see also the two `isinstance()`-on-an-exception entries below). Out of scope for the fix: a `ReturnException` class, which is a plain value outside the Throwable hierarchy and has its own pointed diagnostic. Found 2026-09-18.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) Passing a caught exception to a `Throwable` parameter fails the C++ build.** [`exception-as-throwable-arg-ill-formed`]
  `def takes(t: Throwable) -> None` called as `takes(e)` under `except ValueError as e` passes sema and emits `::tpy::RefAdapter<::tpy::Throwable, ::tpy::ValueError> __tmp_1{e};` -- g++: "variable ... has initializer but incomplete type". `Throwable` is a `@dynamic` protocol the exception classes INHERIT (`BaseException : ::tpy::Throwable`), so the argument should bind the base reference directly; the call site instead takes the structural-conformer path and wraps it in an adapter that is never defined for a nominal implementer. Found 2026-09-18.

- **[LOW small] (parity) `repr()` of an exception value does not render CPython's `Name(args)` form.** [`exception-repr-form`]
  `repr(e)` prints `<__main__.NF object at 0x...>` for a user exception class (host-dependent text, so it cannot be snapshotted) and an empty string for a bound `StopIteration`; CPython prints `NF()` / `NF('msg')` and `StopIteration()`. Sibling of the two `print(e)` / `str(e)` entries below, which cover the message form. A thrown subclass can no longer skip `Exception.__init__` (the parent-init rule requires the call), so CPython's args are always the ones that call passes; the faces above are unaffected. Found 2026-09-18.
