A builtin exception shows the same class: `repr(ValueError("x"))` prints the bare message `x` and `repr(KeyboardInterrupt())` an empty string, where CPython prints `ValueError('x')` and `KeyboardInterrupt()`.

- **[LOW medium] Cyclic enum imports can leave a stale reference wrapper in a function signature.** [`cycle-enum-stale-reference-signature`]
  With `a` importing enum `Color` from `b` and `b` importing `a.lookup`,
  `a.lookup() -> Color` can retain `Ref[Color]` in its registered FunctionInfo
  after its finalized AST return becomes value-type `Color`. Declaration
  registration saw the cycle placeholder before enum classification; the
  later normalization preserves the existing Ref wrapper. The existing
  `imports/mutual_cycle_with_enum` case still builds and runs correctly, so
  no runtime defect is established. The inconsistency prevents a faithful
  semantic signature join; THIR callee metadata stays absent for this shape.
  Fix requires checking declaration finalization across cycle peers and
  sibling parameter/aggregate signatures, separately from metadata carriage.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong value) A `Callable`-typed local LAMBDA copies the enclosing local it reads, with no diagnostic, where the identical `def` spelling warns.** [`callable-local-lambda-copies-capture-silently`] `read: Callable[[], int32] = lambda: len(data)` renders `[data]` -- a full copy taken at creation -- so a later `data.append(...)` is invisible to it: TPy prints `2` where CPython prints `3`. Writing the same body as a nested `def` produces the `copies local ... preventing move` warning; the lambda spelling produces nothing, although the divergence is the same one that warning exists to announce. Probe `/tmp/agents/review3/p16_lambda_copy.py`; pinned as the `lambda`/`lambda_sibling` lines of `tests/cases/nested_def/escaping_local_copy`. The constructor face: `self.getter = lambda: p.n` in `__init__(self, p: P)` copies `p` into the closure at construction, so `q = P(1); h = H(q); q.n = 5; h.getter()` prints 1 where CPython prints 5 (probe `/tmp/agents/abf/r1/pl/ctor.py`; master the same). The same store in a method or a free function (`h.getter = lambda: p.n`) rejects at `expr.lambda` -- a lambda stored into a field outside the member-init keeps that reject for this reason -- and a lambda capturing `self` stored into a field is a sema error in both ("A lambda stored in field 'x' cannot capture 'self': a copy or move of the object would leave the closure pointing at the original"; the other spellings of that store are `BUGS.md#escaping-closure-captures-raw-this`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A `Callable` lambda that copy-captures a tuple of records and passes it to a `tuple[Point, Point]` parameter fails the C++ build.** [`lambda-copied-tuple-capture-to-tuple-param`] `t = (Point(), Point())`, `f: Callable[[], int32] = lambda: first_size(t)` with `def first_size(t: tuple[Point, Point]) -> int32` renders `[t]() -> int32_t { return first_size(::tpy::tuple_to_pointer<std::tuple<Point*, Point*>>(t)); }`: the by-value capture is `const` inside the non-`mutable` lambda, so the borrow-form conversion takes `const Point*` where the parameter (`const std::tuple<Point*, Point*>&`) spells non-const element pointers, and g++ stops with *invalid conversion from 'const Point*' to 'Point*'* (`format.hpp` `to_pointer_form`). CPython prints `lambda_tuple 3` (probe `/tmp/agents/r8fix/gaps/lambda_tuple.py`). The copy capture itself is `BUGS.md#callable-local-lambda-copies-capture-silently`; this is the constness of what it captures meeting a mutable-element borrow form. Fix shape: decide at the lambda where its captured copy is read through a borrow that may mutate -- the lambda is `mutable`, or the borrow form is the const one when the callee does not mutate the element. Found 2026-09-30 probing the captured tuple-name return.
- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) Two nested `def`s with the SAME name in one scope reach the C++ compiler as a redeclaration.** [`duplicate-nested-def-name-in-one-scope`] Two `def h()` at the same level of one body is legal Python (the second rebinds the name); tpyc emits two `auto h = [...]` in one block and g++ reports `conflicting declaration 'auto h'`, naming generated code rather than the source. The block-scoped spelling (one per `if` arm) is fine -- each arm is its own C++ block. **Fix shape:** either reject at the second `def` with a located diagnostic, or emit the rebind as an assignment to the first slot. Probe `/tmp/agents/r3/dupname.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A nested `def` does not capture a name only its own LAMBDA reads.** [`nested-def-lambda-only-capture-missing`] `def sib(): f = lambda: len(xs); return f()` inside a function that owns `xs` builds a lambda with no capture-default over a name the enclosing def never captured: g++ reports `'xs' is not captured`. A nested def's capture set comes from the name references its body's statements make, and a lambda withholds its body from that walk because it is its own scope -- so the name reaches neither capture list. Probe `/tmp/agents/task2/siblam.py`; reproduces at `21dcef707b` (the capture formula is unchanged there). Found 2026-09-17 checking whether `TpyNestedDef.captured_names` needs a lambda-aware fallback -- it does not, because this shape does not compile either way. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED medium] (valid source rejected) Importing one module under multiple names loses earlier bindings.** [`duplicate-module-import-alias`]
  With a module `store` defining `count`, `import store` followed by
  `import store as alias` rejects a function returning `store.count` with
  `Undefined variable: 'store'`. CPython keeps both names bound to the same
  module. The parser's module-keyed alias map retains only one local name,
  and its top-level import list deduplicates by module. These paths are
  unchanged by M2.10. Fixing import registration is separate from MIR's
  qualified global identities and needs `/tpy-fix-bug` analysis of aliases,
  repeated imports, dotted modules and import initialization.

- **[MED medium] (silent wrong result) Imported scalar bindings track later rebinding in the defining module.** [`imported-scalar-binding-tracks-foreign-rebind`]
  With `store.count = 1`, `from store import count as saved`, followed by
  `store.reset()` setting count to 9, CPython retains saved=1 while TPy reads
  9. Bool bindings have the same divergence. The emitted imported-name read
  and `store.count` both name the defining C++ global; Python's import binds
  the current value independently. Reexported attributes have the same risk.
  Reproduced with native execution and CPython during M2.10; the relevant
  emission paths are unchanged from master. Distinct from the view-lifetime
  defect `BUGS.md#imported-global-view-outlives-foreign-rebind`.
  M2.10 excludes from-import bindings and reexported module attributes.
  Fixing import storage and initialization needs a separate `/tpy-fix-bug`
  analysis across scalar, reference, tuple, view and reexport bindings.

- **[MED small] (valid source rejected) A record-union local cannot be initialized directly from self.** [`self-record-union-initializer`]
  In an ordinary `Cell` method, `saved: Cell | Other = self` fails THIR lowering
  at `decl.ptr_union_source`, even for eligible plain records. The equivalent
  typed union initialized from a record parameter is supported; an Optional
  local initialized from self also compiles. The union declaration source
  selector in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` does not admit the receiver form.
  Reseating a union to self similarly fails `decl.union_reseat_source`; an
  Optional initialized to None then assigned self fails `decl.opt_reseat_source`.
  Audit receiver identity, value-versus-pointer form and readonly propagation
  across declarations, assignments, methods and constructors before extending
  the shared selector. M2.8 pins this existing source gate and excludes the
  shape; fixing source admission is outside its analysis-only scope.
  Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) Copying a readonly record-union parameter into a local drops pointee constness.** [`readonly-record-union-local-copy`]
  With ordinary `Cell` and `Other` records holding `value: int32` and an
  `__init__` that assigns it, this function passes frontend analysis:

  ```python
  def observe(current: readonly[Cell | Other], other: Cell) -> int32:
      saved = current
      other.value = 12
      if isinstance(saved, Cell):
          return saved.value
      return 0
  ```

  Import `int32` and `readonly` from `tpy`. The parameter emits
  `::tpy::Union<const Cell*, const Other*>`, but `saved` emits
  `::tpy::Union<Cell*, Other*> saved = current;`, which cannot convert
  without dropping constness. The narrowed local also selects `Cell*`.
  Spelling the parameter `readonly[Cell] | readonly[Other]` has the same
  failure. CPython returns 12 for `observe(cell, cell)`; directly narrowing
  `current` without copying it also works in TPy and observes the shared
  mutation. Preserve the selected source capability through local union
  binding and extraction; audit inferred constness and sibling transfer
  sites rather than adding a cast. Distinct from the call-admission gap
  `BUGS.md#readonly-union-arg-at-inferred-const-slot`.
  Confirmed by generated C++ and `g++ -fsyntax-only` during M2.5 design
  probes on M2.4's merged tree (`f22952127f`). Deferred with user approval;
  this source shape remains outside proposed M2.5 coverage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) Reassigning a scalar-union parameter writes through its const-reference parameter slot.** [`scalar-union-parameter-reassign-const`]
  With `int32` imported from `tpy`:

  ```python
  def scalar(current: bool | int32) -> int32:
      saved = current
      current = True
      if isinstance(saved, int32):
          return saved
      return 0
  ```

  The signature emits `const ::tpy::Union<bool, int32_t>& current`, then
  the body emits `current = true;`. C++ rejects assignment through the
  const reference. CPython's `scalar(int32(7))` returns 7: `saved` retains
  its value while the local parameter binding changes. Copying `current`
  into a separate local and reassigning that local works in TPy.
  Reconcile the union parameter convention with parameter-rebinding
  storage; simply removing const would incorrectly mutate caller storage.
  Audit value-union parameter reassignment alongside other wrapper and
  callable positions. Confirmed by generated C++ and `g++ -fsyntax-only`
  during M2.5 design probes on M2.4's merged tree (`f22952127f`). Deferred
  with user approval; parameter reseats remain outside proposed M2.5
  coverage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) A tuple literal combining a mutable record local and a readonly record parameter is rejected.** [`readonly-record-tuple-literal-rejected`]
  With a `Cell` class whose constructor assigns its `int32` field `value`:

  ```python
  def example(source: readonly[Cell]) -> int32:
      local = Cell(1)
      pair = (local, source)
      local.value = 9
      return pair[0].value
  ```

  THIR lowering rejects the tuple declaration at
  `stmt.var_decl:decl.tuple_literal_shape`; the scalar bindings work.
  CPython, using the TPy annotation stubs, returns 9. A tuple containing
  only the mutable local, `(local,)`, lowers; mutation after capture must
  remain visible through that tuple. Preserve each element's access and
  alias semantics when extending tuple-literal admission, and audit the
  declaration, hoist, parameter and return siblings. This fails before MIR
  construction and is distinct from the auto-copy metadata defect
  `BUGS.md#readonly-auto-tuple-copy-fact`.
  Confirmed during M3.11 probes on 2026-09-21; deferred for a separate fix
  with user approval. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW medium] (latent THIR metadata) Auto copies of readonly borrowed tuples can claim mutable payloads.** [`readonly-auto-tuple-copy-fact`]
  For `def inspect(pair: tuple[Cell, int32], writer: Cell): saved = pair; writer.value = 7; return saved[0].value`, inferred deep constness can emit `const std::tuple<const Cell*, int32_t>& pair`; the `auto saved = pair` copy preserves those const pointers, but `THIRVarDecl.tuple_layout` claims a mutable Cell payload. Explicit whole-tuple readonly and alias chains have the same mismatch in free functions, methods and constructors. The `decl.btuple_alias` producer in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` consults `const_borrow_tuple_locals`, whose `ensure_borrow_tuple_const` deliberately records only reassigned/hoisted bindings. Mutable parameter copies and mixed-access annotated elements remain correct. M2.7 MIR rejects the mismatched copy (`payload copy type or access mismatch`), so this neither changes emitted C++ nor admits unsafe analysis. Do not fix only the first parameter hop or broaden the existing const set without auditing its rendering/admission consumers; preserve the selected per-element source capabilities through all auto-copy chains. Related to, but distinct from, the tuple-unpack fact below. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (latent THIR metadata) Optional record tuple-unpack reads lose the selected readonly capability.** [`optional-tuple-unpack-readonly-fact`]
  Unpacking an Optional record from a const tuple emits `const Cell*`, but
  subsequent `THIRName.optional_read` facts describe a mutable
  `THIRBorrowedRecord` (`readonly=False`). Minimal source:

  ```python
  from tpy import int32

  class Cell:
      value: int32

      def __init__(self, value: int32):
          self.value = value

  def read(pair: tuple[int32, Cell | None]) -> int32:
      n, item = pair
      if item is not None:
          return item.value
      return n
  ```

  The tuple parameter is inferred const; both the presence-test read and
  the narrowed field-receiver read of `item` carry the wrong capability.
  A chained source also reproduces it: `n, item = holders[0].pair` with
  `holders: readonly[list[Holder]]` and
  `Holder.pair: tuple[int32, Cell | None]`.
  Tuple-unpack lowering in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` records the target
  in `lc.pointers` and selects `const Cell*` in `target_cpps`, without
  recording that constness in `lc.const_locals`. Optional read-fact
  production in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` consequently loses it.
  Generated C++ remains correct, and MIR currently rejects tuple unpack
  for the whole body, so these facts do not admit an unsafe MIR body.
  Fix and test capability propagation before admitting this shape to MIR;
  audit sibling unpack paths and existing consumers of `lc.const_locals`
  before changing the shared context. Confirmed before and after the
  master merge (`3d041b21d8`, `b4f5d1e8a9`); recorded for a separate fix
  with user approval. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, toolchain-caught) Immediate field access through a walrus tuple uses value access on a pointer.** [`walrus-tuple-immediate-field-access`]
  With a record `Cell` holding `value: int32`,
  `print((saved := (current,))[0].value)` emits `.value` on the `Cell*`
  returned by `std::get<0>`, and the C++ compiler rejects it. CPython prints
  the field normally. Reading a scalar member of a mixed walrus tuple and
  accessing its record member later through `saved` avoids this immediate
  projection path. Fix the tuple-element receiver access classification;
  this is separate from tuple capture loan registration. Found during the
  M2.3 prerequisite audit; deferred with user approval.

- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) Forwarding an `Fn` parameter to a non-storing named helper is rejected by THIR's callable argument gate.** [`fn-parameter-named-forwarding-rejected`]
  `def relay(f: Fn[[], int32]) -> int32: return f()` and
  `def use(f: Fn[[], int32]) -> int32: return relay(f)` pass semantic analysis,
  but `use(lambda: 3)` rejects at the forwarding call with
  `expr.call:call.arg_shape.other_callabletype`. CPython prints `3`; neither
  helper stores or returns the callable, so this is not the designed restriction
  on escaping `Fn` values. Replacing both parameter annotations with `Callable`
  admits the corresponding forwarding shape. The rejection comes from the
  argument-admission fallback in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`; fixing it must check
  templated callable argument lowering and forwarding lifetime/ownership, not
  simply remove the gate. Reproducer: the two definitions above, imported
  `Fn`/`int32` from `tpy`, followed by `print(use(lambda: 3))`. Confirmed at
  `d9c5173358` during the callable-contract feasibility pass, independently of
  any proposed admission rule. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) A generic method calling a `Callable` with an open-type argument can force that argument const.** [`generic-method-callable-param-forced-const`] `def invoke(self, cb: Callable[[T], None], x: T): cb(x)` inside `Runner[T]`, instantiated at a mutable reference type such as `Cell`, emits `readonly_form_t<T>` for `x` although the callback needs `param_val_or_ref_t<T>` (`const Cell&` versus `Cell&`); C++ compilation fails while CPython runs. Direct callable fields and indexed callable fields have the same failure; the free-function twin works. Callable argument mutation tracking deliberately skips open `T` (`sema/calls.py`), then an inferred-readonly method forces parameter constness (`sema/functions.py`, `param_const.py`). These paths predate indexed callable-field support. Fixing this requires reconciling generic callable mutation and method const inference, including the existing generic combinator corpus, rather than changing field dispatch. Related to `BUGS.md#generic-ref-param-drops-const` and the `Wrap[T]`/`cmp_to_key` readonly-receiver entry, but this failure involves an independent method argument. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/p03_safety/{named_method,direct_generic,named_generic}.py`, measured 2026-09-16. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) A lambda body cannot materialize a temporary for a mutable-reference call argument.** [`lambda-body-reference-argument-temp`] `f: Callable[[], int32] = lambda: cb([1])`, where `cb: Callable[[list[int32]], int32]`, rejects at `expr.lambda:lambda.body:expr.call:call.arg_shape.container`; the same call in an ordinary function body works. Lambda expression lowering has no argument-temporary flush point. Named, direct-field and indexed callable spellings now share that existing gate, rather than some reaching C++ with an invalid rvalue-to-reference binding. General lambda-body temporary storage and its lifetime need a separate lowering change, not a per-callee exception. Pinned by `tpyc/thir/test_computed_callable_args.py`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; was ill-formed C++) An `and` / `or` in a lambda body whose left operand is not a plain name is rejected.** [`lambda-body-operand-temp-hoisted-outside`] `apply(lambda a: pick(a) or pick(1), 3)` at an `f: Callable[[int32], int32]` parameter rejects at `expr.lambda:lambda.body:temp.no_statement`; CPython prints `6`. The scalar select holds its left operand once, in a `auto&& __tmp_N = pick(a);` declared before the enclosing STATEMENT, and a lambda body has none: until the placement scope landed the declaration was hoisted outside the lambda (`auto&& __tmp_1 = pick(a);` above the `std::cout` line, where `a` is not in scope, so g++ stopped; with a name that does resolve outside it would have evaluated the operand once, eagerly, at the wrong time). The same body in a nested `def` works. The lambda needs a flush region of its own (the sibling `BUGS.md#lambda-body-reference-argument-temp` names the same missing home), not a per-operator exception. Pinned by `tests/cases/calls/error_lambda_operand_temp`. Probe `/tmp/agents/mil-b/lam_or.py`, 2026-10-01.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) An `and` / `or` in a dict comprehension's key or value whose left operand is not a plain name hoists its temporary outside the loop.** [`dict-comp-operand-temp-outside-loop`] `d = {x: (pick(x) or 1) for x in range(3)}` renders `auto&& __tmp_1 = pick(x);` before the loop that binds `x`, so g++ stops with *'x' was not declared in this scope*; CPython prints `{0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 4}`. The list and set comprehension element (and every comprehension's filter) flushes its temps inside the loop body, but the dict emitter flushes nothing around `insert_or_assign`, so the key and value sit under the ENCLOSING statement's flush and an operand temp lands there. Fix shape: give the dict insert the same in-loop flush the element has (one region for every comprehension body), then the validator's member-init invariant can treat key and value as flushable like the element. Probe `/tmp/agents/mil-b/impl/p_dict.py`, found 2026-10-01 while scoping the placement region.

- **[MED medium] (rejects valid, loud) Indexing a container field directly from a record-returning call hits the shared receiver gate.** [`call-rooted-container-field-index`] `def get(a: App) -> App: return a` followed by `get(a).values[0]`, where `values: list[int32]`, rejects at `subscript.recv.field_chain`; binding `b = get(a)` first permits `b.values[0]`. This also limits `get(a).callbacks[0](x)` after indexed callable-field disambiguation is fixed. Semantic analysis accepts the receiver and must analyze it only once; the remaining gap is the common THIR container-field receiver admission, shared by reads and writes, rather than callable invocation. Expanding that family requires checking borrowed versus owning call results and temporary lifetimes across its consumers. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/p03_call_rooted_container.py`, measured 2026-09-16. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A ternary whose arms are record-valued rvalues cannot be the body of a lambda or nested `def`.** [`closure-body-record-ternary-rejected`] `direct(lambda k: Node(0) if flag else Node(1), n)` at an `f: Fn[[Node], Own[Node]]` slot stops with *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.lambda)*, and the same body spelled as a nested `def` (`return Node(0) if flag else Node(1)`) stops with `stmt.return:return.record_source.TpyIfExpr.storage` -- so both closure spellings refuse it and there is no way to write the shape. CPython runs it and prints `0`. The neighbours compile: a scalar ternary lambda body (`lambda n: n if n > 0 else 0`) runs, and so does a record ternary of LVALUE arms (`lambda k: ns[0] if flag else k` at a borrow contract), so the gap is a record-typed ternary with a non-lvalue arm (a constructor call, or `copy(k)`) rather than ternaries in closures generally. A `copy()` call alone in a lambda body is fine (`lambda k: copy(k)` at an `Own` contract runs), so the two lower independently and only their composition rejects. Also blocks the natural remedy for a closure with mixed borrow/fresh return paths ("copy on the borrow path"), which is exactly this shape. Probes `/tmp/agents/fn_doc_probes/tern/{t1,t4,t5,t6,t7}.py`, measured 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (accepts invalid, silent) `sorted` / `min` / `max` take `key` POSITIONALLY, where CPython makes it keyword-only -- so a program that compiles and runs under TPy is not valid Python.** [`key-arg-accepted-positionally`] `sorted(xs, negate)` prints `[3, 2, 1]`, `min(3, 1, negate)` prints `3` and `max(3, 1, negate)` prints `1` under TPy; CPython over the same source raises `TypeError: sorted expected 1 argument, got 2` (and reads the extra argument of `min`/`max` as one more value to compare). The stubs declare `key` as an ordinary positional parameter (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_funcs.py:525` for `sorted`, `:125`/`:131`/`:174`/`:180` for `min`/`max`), and nothing marks it keyword-only. The over-accept is not even self-consistent: the positional form takes a named function but rejects a lambda (`sorted(xs, lambda n: -n)` -> *Lambda parameter types cannot be inferred without context*), while `key=` accepts both. Fix shape: a keyword-only marker on those stub params, so the positional spelling gets a located error naming `key=`. Probes `/tmp/agents/fn_doc_probes/p_key2.py` (accepted) and `p_key3.py` (the `key=` spelling, parity-clean), measured 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) An `Fn` contract whose result is a REFERENCE-typed Optional is unsatisfiable: the contract states the STORAGE form (`std::optional<Node>`) while the callee and the contract body's own call-result local both render the BORROW form (`Node*`).** [`fn-contract-reference-optional-result`] `def find(f: Fn[[Node], Node | None], a: Node) -> int32:` with a body `r = f(a)` / `if r is not None: return r.v` emits, and both ways of feeding it fail the C++ build. A `def` callee (`def pick(n: Node) -> Node | None`) fails the `requires` clause, with no TPy source location -- the diagnostic names only the generated `.hpp`/`.cpp`:

  ```
  error: no matching function for call to 'find(Node* (&)(Node&), Node&)'
  note: constraints not satisfied
  note: '__fn(__a0)' does not satisfy return-type-requirement
     17 |       { __fn(__a0) } -> std::convertible_to<std::optional<Node>>;
  ```

  A lambda (`find(lambda n: n, a)`) passes the clause, because the lambda's own return is rendered in the contract's storage form -- `[](Node& n) -> std::optional<Node> { return n; }`, itself a silent COPY of a node CPython would alias -- and then the contract's BODY rejects the same mismatch from the other side:

  ```
  error: cannot convert 'std::optional<Node>' to 'Node*' in initialization
     41 |     Node* r = f(a);
  ```

  So no callee spelling satisfies the contract. Cause: `_gen_fn_template_parts` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py:357`) spells the constraint from `fn_type.return_type.to_cpp()`, the bare storage form, while a `def` returning `Node | None` and the call-result local inside the `Fn` body both take the pointer borrow form -- the two halves of one contract disagree on the form. VALUE-typed Optionals are unaffected: the same shape at `Fn[[int32], int32 | None]` compiles and runs, since storage and borrow form coincide there, so the trigger is a reference-typed inner (class / `list` / `dict` / `set`). The wrapper spelled to PROPAGATE the result (`def find(f: Fn[[Node], Node | None], a: Node) -> Node | None: return f(a)`) never reaches C++ at all -- it stops at `error: in function 'find': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return)`. The designed resolution is already sliced: `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md` carries a located reject row for the reference-typed `Optional` / union callable result (no callee can satisfy `Fn[[Node], Node | None]`, and the spelling reaches C++ ill-formed today); this entry is the measured shape behind it. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/fn_file_bugs/{b1b_fn_optional_local,b1d_fn_optional_lambda,b1c_fn_optional_value,b1_fn_optional_result}.py`, measured 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0 with `uv run tpy` (g++-14). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) `Own[Callable[...]]` at a RETURN slot rejects at `return.slot_type` for every callee spelling, while the bare `Callable[...]` return it is supposed to resolve to works.** [`own-callable-return-rejected`] `def make() -> Own[Callable[[int32], int32]]` stops with `error: in function 'make': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return:return.slot_type)` whether the returned value is an annotated closure local (`f: Callable[[int32], int32] = lambda i: i + 1` / `return f`), a module-level function reference (`return inc`), or a nested `def`. Dropping the `Own` wrapper makes all four spellings -- including the direct `return lambda i: i + 1` -- compile and run, printing `2`. `Own[T]` at a return is defined to resolve to plain `T` (CLAUDE.md, "at a return it resolves to plain `T`"), so the two spellings name the same slot and only one of them lowers. Cause: `ret_callable` (`tpyc/thir/lower/context.py:791`) is `isinstance(rt, CallableType) and not rt.is_template`, and the `Own` peel sitting right beside it (`own_value_scalar`, `:797`) covers only scalars, `char` and protocol-`auto` slots -- so an `OwnType` over a `CallableType` matches no `ret_supported` row and the return arm is never entered. The contextual-inference half is fixed: a direct lambda now receives its parameter types through `Own[Callable[...]]`, including at argument and container bindings. The return still reaches the existing THIR return-slot rejection; the remaining defect is lowering, not inference. Returning a `Callable` is documented as the supported shape -- `docs/CLOSURES_CALLABLE_DESIGN.md:155` rejects `-> Fn[...]` with "cannot return Fn (use Callable)" -- and the bare form honours that; it is the owning respelling of the same return that has no lowering. Distinct from BUGS.md#move-only-closure-in-callable-slot, which is a bare `Callable` return whose closure MOVE-captures a non-copyable value (a C++-level `std::function` copyability failure, not a lowering gate). Reproducers `/tmp/agents/fn_file_bugs/{b2_return_callable_own,b2b_local_then_return,b2g_own_funcref,b2h_own_nested_def}.py` (rejecting) and `{b2c_bare_callable,b2f_bare_lambda_direct,b2d_funcref,b2e_nested_def,b2j_own_param_funcref}.py` (working), measured 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Inside a generator or `async def`, `except StopIteration` over an `@error_return` call is refused whenever the `try` needs frame states of its own.** [`frame-try-next-error-return-miscompiles`] `def my_zip2[A, B](ia: Iterator[A], ib: Iterator[B]) -> Iterator[tuple[A, B]]` driving two iterators with `try: x = next(ia)` / `except StopIteration: break` errors at the `try` line instead of miscompiling. **The silent miscompile is CLOSED** (2026-09-15, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/resumable_cfg.py` `_build_try`): it used to emit `x.emplace((*({ auto __er_1 = ::tpy::next(ia); if (!__er_1.has_value()) ::tpy::tpy_panic("unhandled error return"); &::tpy::unwrap_ref(*__er_1); })));` under a `catch (const ::tpy::StopIteration&)` that nothing throws -- exhaustion PANICKED instead of breaking, and the slot was filled from a pointer into a statement-expression local dead at the semicolon. **What remains is the feature.** Sema classifies a `ReturnException` handler as the return tier (`TpyTry.tier`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py:_classify_try_tier`); the sync emit honours it with `auto __try_tmp_2 = ::tpy::next(ia); if (!__try_tmp_2.has_value()) goto __except_1;` (the form `math.sumprod` relies on), but the resumable CFG carries `TryRegion.tier` without an edge for the failing unwrap, so it would wrap the region in a C++ `try`/`catch` that never fires -- `StopIteration` is never THROWN in TPy (`raise StopIteration` auto-promotes to an error return, and in a non-`@error_return` frame it is rejected outright), and every unwrap inside it would fall back to the unhandled (panic) disposition because `_EmitState.try_except_label` is only set by the sync `_emit_try_return`. **Exactly which shapes reject:** a DECOMPOSED try (one holding an `await`/`yield`, or a `break`/`continue` leaving it) whose body holds a call the handler catches -- sema decides that at the call-admission check (`sema/calls.py:_check_error_return_handled`) and records it on `TpyTry.handled_error_return`, which `_build_try` reads. Across generator and `async def`; `next(it)`, a user `@error_return` callee, and the discarded-call form; a frame-slot, frame-field or value target; with and without a `finally`; inside a `with` body; `yield` inside the `try` body. All of those were wrong before the reject. Unaffected (correct before and after, pinned by `tests/cases/generators/frame_try_return_exception`): a LEAF try in a frame (no suspension inside it, no transfer leaving it), a whole suspension-free loop in a frame, a DECOMPOSED try whose handler no call in the body can enter (`try: yield x / except StopIteration: pass|break|return` -- the dead catch is harmless), module level, and every sync position. **Fix shape** (the precedent is `AsyncForAdvance`, which already spells exactly this edge): give the CFG a terminator for a handled `@error_return` call -- `ok_bb` / `failed_bb`, the latter the handler entry -- splitting the try body at each such call; skip the C++ `try`/`catch` for a return-tier `TryRegion` in `_emit_case`; render the check as `if (!__try_tmp_N.has_value()) { __state = S_...; continue; }` with the bind shapes `_for_advance_parts` already enumerates. An `as`-binding handler additionally needs its `__err_opt_N` capture as a frame field. Pinned rejecting by `tests/cases/generators/error_frame_try_return_exception` (the tripwire: it fails the day the shape lowers); the `async def` twin goes through the same `_build_try` arm and is covered by the compiling `async def` sections of `tests/cases/generators/frame_try_return_exception`. Blocks writing `zip` in TPy source (TODO.md "Builtin combinators in TPy source"). Found 2026-09-13 by the combinator feasibility probe; miscompile closed 2026-09-15, reject narrowed to the handled shape the same day. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.

- **[MED small] (compiler crash on valid code) A `@dispatch` pair of GENERATOR bodies crashes sema with a bare `AssertionError`.** [`dispatch-generator-pair-sema-crash`] Two same-named `@dispatch` defs that both return `Iterator[T]` and both have a `yield` body abort the compile with `Internal error:` and no message -- `assert elem_type is not None` in `_analyze_yield` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py:3895`): the function whose body is being analyzed has no `generator_yield_type`. Reproduces both for a pair differing in a PARAM TYPE (`pred: Fn[[T], bool]` vs `pred: None`, `/tmp/agents/probe_tpy_combinators/px_dispatch.py`) and for one differing in ARITY (`.../px_dispatch2.py`), so it is generator bodies under `@dispatch` generally, not the `None` param. `typing.overload` is the other spelling of an overload set (`docs/OVERLOAD_DESIGN.md`) and was not probed for this shape; either way an unlocated crash is the wrong answer. Blocks the `filter(None, it)` variant of a TPy-source `filter` (TODO.md "Builtin combinators in TPy source"). Found 2026-09-13 by the combinator feasibility probe. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) A comprehension unpacking a POINTER-TUPLE yield skips the `tuple_elem_ref` deref the `for` statement applies.** [`comp-unpack-pointer-tuple-skips-deref`] `[n.v for i, n in my_enumerate(nodes)]`, where `my_enumerate` is a TPy generator yielding `tuple[int32, T]` (rendered `std::tuple<int32_t, ::tpy::val_or_ptr_t<T>>`, hence `std::tuple<int32_t, Node*>` at `T = Node`), emits `auto& n = std::get<1>(__tup_1);` and g++ rejects `n.v` with *request for member 'v' in 'n', which is of pointer type 'Node*'*. The `for`-STATEMENT over the same generator is correct in the same TU -- `auto&& n = ::tpy::unwrap_ref(::tpy::tuple_elem_ref(std::get<1>(__tup_1)));` -- so it is the comprehension's unpack head that misses the normalization, not the yield form. Sibling of BUGS.md#comp-dict-items-ref-value, which is the same unpack head over `d.items()`; a fix should cover both faces. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_tpy_combinators/nest_comp.py` (built with `tpyc -b`, error confirmed 2026-09-13). Blocks consuming a TPy-source `enumerate`/`zip` from a comprehension (TODO.md "Builtin combinators in TPy source"). Found by the combinator feasibility probe. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) `list(gen)` over a generator yielding a POINTER TUPLE pushes the borrow form into a storage-form vector.** [`collect-pointer-tuple-into-storage-vector`] `list(my_enumerate(nodes))` renders `::tpy::construct<std::vector<std::tuple<int32_t, Node>>>(my_enumerate<Node>(nodes))` over a generator whose yield type is `std::tuple<int32_t, ::tpy::val_or_ptr_t<T>>`, and `collect`'s `result.push_back(unwrap_ref_move(*__r))` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/ranges.hpp:188`) is handed a `std::tuple<int32_t, Node*>`: *no matching function for call to `std::vector<std::tuple<int, Node> >::push_back(std::tuple<int, Node*>)`*. `unwrap_ref_move` normalizes a whole ref-wrapped element, but nothing lifts a tuple ELEMENT from the borrow form to the storage form at this seam; the precedent that does is `tuple_to_storage` / `tuple_to_storage_move` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/format.hpp:886` / `:905`), already used where a borrow-form tuple reaches an owning slot. `construct`'s other arm, `from_range`, assigns straight from the range's iterators with no element conversion either, so the lift belongs at the `construct` seam rather than in one arm. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_tpy_combinators/nest_listctor.py` (built with `tpyc -b`, error confirmed 2026-09-13). Found by the combinator feasibility probe. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) `float32` arithmetic with an `int` (BigInt) VARIABLE operand emits `static_cast<float>(BigInt)`, which does not compile.** [`float32-bigint-operand-static-cast`] `a = float32(1.5); n: int = 2; a + n` renders `(a) + static_cast<float>(n)` and g++ rejects the cast from `tpy::BigInt`; every float32 operator overload taking `other: int` (`+ - * / // % **` and the reflected forms) spells the same `static_cast<float>({0})`, so all of them fail with an int VARIABLE, while an int LITERAL operand takes a different path and works. The `float32.__add__(self, other: int) -> float32` stub overload admits the operand, so the fix is the operand render: route a BigInt through its explicit conversion (`static_cast<float>(n.to_double())` or the BigInt-to-float helper the `float` operators use). Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the scalar-rename followups.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) The synthesized async-factory wrapper lambda `std::move`s every non-value param, so an `async def` with a plain reference-type param (no `Own`) passed as a callable value fails the C++ build.** [`async-factory-wrapper-moves-borrow-param`] `async def runit(xs: list[int32], n: int32) -> int32` (an ordinary borrow param plus a scalar) passed as the `f` argument of `async def drive(f: Callable[[list[int32], int32], Own[Cancellable[int32]]], xs: list[int32])`, whose body spawns it with `asyncio.create_task(f(xs, 4))`: the function ref is coerced to the `Callable` slot, `_async_factory_wrap_cpp_facts` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) synthesizes the coroutine-factory wrapper lambda, and g++-13 rejects it --

  ```
  error: cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type 'std::vector<int>&' to an rvalue
         of type 'std::remove_reference<std::vector<int>&>::type' {aka 'std::vector<int>'}
     63 | __sub_0.emplace([](std::vector<int32_t>& __a0, int32_t __a1) -> std::unique_ptr<::tpystd::coro::Cancellable<int32_t>> { return ::tpy::make_adapter<::tpystd::coro::Cancellable<int32_t>>(::tpyapp::factory_listparam::runit(std::move(__a0), __a1)); }, (*data));
  note: initializing argument 1 of '__coro_runit runit(std::vector<int>&, int32_t)'
  ```

  Cause: the forward loop spells `std::move(__aN)` whenever `isinstance(ptype, OwnType) or not ptype.is_value_type()`, and the second disjunct is wrong for a borrow. `CallableType._callable_param_cpp` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) renders a non-`Own` reference-type hint param as a MUTABLE lvalue ref `T&`, and the frame factory the lambda calls takes `T&` as well, so the move turns the lambda's own lvalue parameter into an rvalue that cannot bind. Every non-`Own` reference-type param is affected (`list`/`dict`/`set`/class); `Own[T]` params and value-typed params are correct. Fix shape: move only for `OwnType` params -- the owned form the callee consumes -- and forward a borrow by bare name so it stays an lvalue. Toolchain-caught, never silent. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/review_adl/factory_listparam.py`, built with `uv run tpy --cxx gcc-13` on 2026-09-14 (0.6.0.dev0). Pre-existing and independent of the ADL free-callee fix: that fix changed only the wrapper's callee SPELLING, while the forward loop and the `T&` lambda parameter it cannot bind are byte-identical before it, so the shape fails the same way on master. Adjacent with a DISTINCT trigger: BUGS.md#async-fn-borrow-param-own-hint is the mirror case -- there the callable HINT says `Own[T]` while the async fn's param is a borrow, and the fix is a sema rejection of the coercion; here hint and callee AGREE on the borrow and it is the wrapper's own render that is wrong, so neither fix covers the other. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the ADL free-callee fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) A literal-specialized overload set mangles its callee at the CALL site but not at the DEFINITION site, so a `@dispatch` set over `Literal` params never builds, and an `@overload` one never builds across modules.** [`literal-dispatch-overload-unmangled-definition`] Three faces of one gap between `literal_mangled_name` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py:171`) and the emitters that spell a definition.
- **[HIGH small] (SILENT wrong overload, no diagnostic; pre-existing) An int literal argument to a `@dispatch` pair taking `bool` and `int` picks the `bool` variant.** [`dispatch-int-literal-picks-bool`] A record with `@dispatch def mv(self, x: bool) -> int: return 2` and `@dispatch def mv(self, x: int) -> int: return 3`: `c.mv(7)` prints `2`, CPython `3` (`c.mv(True)` is right). Same on generic records. It is the int-literal sibling of the str-literal pin (a `const char*` converts to `bool`): the C++ overload set prefers the `int -> bool` standard conversion over the user-defined conversion to `BigInt`, so the literal needs the same per-slot pin the str literal gets (`_strlit_pin_slot`). Probe `/tmp/agents/ge/f3/nb.py`, found 2026-09-28 by the gate batch-E parity review.
  - **(a) `@dispatch`, any module.** Two bodied same-named variants with `Literal` params (`/tmp/agents/review_adl2/lit_main.py`: `pick(m: Literal["a"])` / `pick(m: Literal["b"])`) emit `int32_t pick(std::string_view m)` TWICE -- g++ reports `redefinition of 'int32_t tpyapp::lit_main::pick(std::string_view)'` -- while every call site spells `pick__lit_a` / `pick__lit_b` (`free_literal_mangled_name`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:3807`), which then do not exist. A `@dispatch` variant is self-contained (no stub/impl pair), so it never reaches `_gen_literal_specialized_function` (`functions.py:1172`), the one emitter that renames a definition; it takes the ordinary per-function path and keeps the plain name. The declarations in the header collide the same way.
  - **(b) `@overload`, cross-module only.** The stub/impl form DOES mangle both definition and declaration (`litmod2.hpp` declares only `mode__lit_r` / `mode__lit_w`), but the importing module's re-export line is spelled from the SOURCE name: `using ::tpyapp::litmod2::mode;` -> `'mode' has not been declared in 'tpyapp::litmod2'` (`/tmp/agents/review_adl2/lit_main2.py`). Same-module `@overload` is fine (`tests/cases/calls/overload_literal_bool`), and the call-site spelling is right in both cases -- only the `using` is wrong; it should name every mangled specialization (or the re-export should be dropped for a literal-only set, since callers spell the qualified mangled name anyway).
  - **(c) `@dispatch` with ONE Literal-param variant.** The mangle fires whenever the resolved variant has any `Literal` param and the set has more than one member, so a mixed set breaks too: `g(x: int)` beside `g(x: str, mode: Literal["r", "rb"])` spells `g("b", "r")` -- and, once `mode` has a default, `g("a")` -- as `g__lit_r__rb(...)`, a symbol nothing defines -- g++: `'g__lit_r__rb' is not a member of ...` (`/tmp/agents/literal/p/dispatch_mixed_nodef.py`, verified 2026-09-26). Same missing naming fact; the lowering-gate face of it is `BUGS.md#literal-param-proxy-gates-reject-plain-call`, and the two are planned as ONE branch.

  (a) and (b) verified 2026-09-14 on 0.6.0.dev0 with `uv run tpy`, (c) on 2026-09-26. Pre-existing and independent of the ADL free-callee fix: the definitions and the `using` line are rendered from the source name either way, and the pre-fix call sites spelled the same mangled names unqualified. Fix shape: make the definition/declaration name and the re-export read the SAME `literal_mangled_name` decision the call site reads -- one naming fact per overload variant, consulted by every emitter, rather than a rename applied only on the stub/impl path. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A method, constructor, static method or module-qualified free function with a `Literal`-typed parameter cannot be called: the lowering reads "has a `Literal` param" as "the callee name is mangled", and a single-overload callee is not mangled.** [`literal-param-proxy-gates-reject-plain-call`] With no default involved, `c.m("rb")` on `def m(self, mode: Literal["r", "rb"]) -> str` rejects at `method.fi_kind`, `C("r")` on `def __init__(self, mode: Literal["r", "rb"])` at `expr.call`, and `C.s("r")` on a `@staticmethod` at `method.marker.static.plain` (probes `/tmp/agents/literal/p/meth4.py`, `ctor3.py`, `meth3.py`, verified 2026-09-26); CPython runs all three, and the same callee written as a free function and called by its bare name compiles. Called through its MODULE it is refused too: with `def open(filename: str, mode: Literal["r", "rb", "r+b", "rb+"] = "rb")` in `gzip`, both `gzip.open(p, "rb")` and `gzip.open(p)` reject at `expr.method_call:method.marker.module.plain`, while `from gzip import open as gz_open; gz_open(p, "rb")` compiles and runs (probes `/tmp/agents/zlib/m1/p2.py`, `p3.py`, 2026-09-27). This blocks `gzip.open`'s `mode` parameter (and a `mode` on `GzipFile.__init__`, the constructor face): `gzip.open(filename)` stays read-only with no `mode` until the fix lands. Eleven gates in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py` and `predicates.py` spell `any(isinstance(p.type, LiteralType) for p in fi.params)` as the stand-in for the `__lit_` rename (`_plain_method_fi_ok`'s `literal_mangled_ok`, `_ctor_shape_ok`, the native-ctor and static arms), while the rename itself (`method_literal_mangled_cpp` / `free_literal_mangled_name`) applies only to a MULTI-overload set -- so a plain, unmangled call is refused. A dataclass with a `Literal` field goes through the generated `__init__` and is refused the same way. Disabling the ctor gate alone lowered the ctor and dataclass probes correctly (the argument rows already carry `_str_literal_literal_slot_arg`). Fix shape, decided 2026-09-26: ONE per-variant naming fact ("is this callee literal-mangled, and to what") that every lowering gate, call-site spelling and definition emitter reads, fixed on its own branch together with `BUGS.md#literal-dispatch-overload-unmangled-definition` (whose definitions and re-exports miss the same fact). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output, plus loud faces) Consumers keyed on the base type's predicates miss a `Literal`-typed value, so a `Literal` value prints, formats and captures unlike its base type.** [`literal-value-consumers-miss-base`] Four faces, all verified 2026-09-26 with no default involved (probes under `/tmp/agents/literal/p/`): (a) SILENT -- `print(flag)` with `flag: Literal[True, False]` (param or annotated local) renders `std::cout << flag` and prints `1` / `0` where CPython prints `True` / `False`; a plain `bool` renders `::tpy::print_bool(flag)` (`bool_print.py`). (b) An f-string over an `int` or `bool` Literal rejects with `Type Literal[1, 9] cannot be used in f-string (no __str__ or __repr__ method)` (`litvals.py`, `boollit2.py`); a str Literal and `str(x)` work. (c) `str(level)` with `level: Literal[-1, 0, 9]` emits `::tpy::fixed_to_str<int8_t>(level)` over the `int32_t` param -- correct at run time, but `-Werror=conversion` (the test harness's flags) fails the build (`int_str.py`). (d) A `Literal[str]` parameter of a generator or `async def` is captured as an owned `std::string` (`__gen_g2 g2(std::string mode)`), where a plain `str` parameter borrows as `std::string_view` -- a hidden copy (`genlit.py` vs `genstr.py`). Fix shape: peel `LiteralType` to its base where these consumers classify (print dispatch, f-string renderability, the int-to-str width pick, the frame param form), or give `LiteralType` the base's answers once. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) A union with a `Literal` member (`Literal["r", "rb"] | int`) is unlowered at its call argument and in an `isinstance` test.** [`literal-in-union-param-unlowered`] `def f(mode: Literal["r", "rb"] | int) -> int` called as `f(3)` / `f("r")` rejects at `stmt.expr_stmt:call.arg_shape.union`, and `if isinstance(mode, int):` in its body at `stmt.if:cond.call` (probes `/tmp/agents/literal/p/union_lit_nodef2.py`, `union_lit_nodef.py`, verified 2026-09-26); CPython runs both. Sema accepts the shape, a default on it included; the union argument and narrowing rows have no arm for a `LiteralType` alternative. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) `X: Final[Literal["r", "rb"]] = "rb"` is refused: "Final[Literal[...]] is not supported; only primitive types (int, float, bool, str, StrView, char, IntN) and tuple are allowed".** [`final-literal-annotation-rejected`] PEP 586 allows a `Literal` inside `Final`; CPython runs it, and it is the one spelling that would let a named constant serve as a `Literal`-typed default or argument (`def g(mode: Literal["r", "rb"] = LIT_MODE)`), since a `Final[str]` constant is a `str` and rightly rejects there (`/tmp/agents/literal/p/final3.py`, verified 2026-09-26). The Final-type allow-list has no `LiteralType` arm; it renders as its base, so the global would spell like a `Final[str]` one. Bare `X: Final = "rb"` is the separate `BUGS.md#bare-final-annotation-rejects`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (test-harness parity gap) The CPython `@dispatch` stub ignores `Literal` annotations, so a Literal-keyed set runs the first variant whose other params fit.** [`cpy-dispatch-stub-ignores-literal`] `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py`'s `_type_matches` skips annotations it cannot `isinstance` (a `Literal[...]` among them), so with `g(mode: Literal["r"])` declared before `g(mode: Literal["rb"] = "rb")`, CPython prints `binary text text` for `g(), g("r"), g("rb")` where TPy's static resolution means `binary text binary` (`/tmp/agents/literal/p/dispatch_lit.py`, verified 2026-09-26). No committed case reaches it today (a Literal `@dispatch` set cannot build, `BUGS.md#literal-dispatch-overload-unmangled-definition`), but the cpy phase would pass a wrong answer the day it does. Fix: match a `typing.Literal` annotation by value (`typing.get_args`) in `_type_matches`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output; a C++ build error where CPython raises) An `@overload` stub's parameter default decides which specialization an omitted argument selects, but the IMPLEMENTATION's default is the value passed, so a stub default that differs from (or is missing on) the implementation runs the wrong specialization or the wrong value.** [`overload-stub-default-ignored`] Plain form, wrong on master: stubs `k(n: int)` / `k(n: str = "x")` over the implementation `k(n: int | str = "y")` -- `k()` prints `s:x` in TPy, `s:y` in CPython (`/tmp/agents/meta-literal/q1.py`); with an implementation that has no default at all, TPy still runs it where CPython raises `TypeError` (`q3.py`). `Literal` form, reachable since `Literal`-typed defaults are accepted: stubs `stub(mode: Literal["r"])` / `stub(mode: Literal["rb"] = "rb")` over `stub(mode: str = "r")` call `stub__lit_rb()`, whose C++ default is the implementation's `"r"` -- a value outside the specialization's `Literal["rb"]`, so its folded `mode == "r"` test runs the wrong arm (TPy `binary:r`, CPython `text:r`, `/tmp/agents/literal-parity/p7.py`); an implementation without the default fails in g++ with `too few arguments to function 'stub__lit_rb'` where CPython raises `TypeError` (`p8.py`). All re-verified 2026-09-27. Mechanism: every emitted specialization declares the implementation's defaults (`stub__lit_r(std::string_view mode = "rb")` in `tests/cases/defaults/literal_defaults`), while overload resolution reads the stub's; `_validate_overload_signatures` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) checks a stub that OMITS a parameter against the implementation's default but never looks at a stub's own default. Planned fix (design note, not started): an omitted argument takes the implementation's default, as in CPython; overload resolution sees the call with that default filled in -- taken from the implementation signature's resolved type / literal value, not re-resolved at the call site (cf. `BUGS.md#param-default-resolves-in-caller-scope`); a stub's default only marks the parameter omittable; the only remaining error is a stub making a parameter omittable where the implementation has no default. (A stub-vs-implementation default-equality diagnostic was tried and dropped: comparing name defaults by value needed a second copy of sema's name resolution, which kept drifting.) Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong value) An `@overload` stub that declares a parameter NARROWER than the implementation converts the shared default to the stub's type: `v: float = 5` over `v: int32 | float = 5` passes `5.0` where CPython passes the int `5`.** [`overload-stub-narrow-type-converts-default`] Stubs `f(x: int32, v: float = 5)` / `f(x: str, v: int32 = 5)` over `def f(x: int32 | str, v: int32 | float = 5)` emit `std::string f(int32_t x, double v = 5)`, so `f(1)` sees a float: TPy prints `float int`, CPython `int int` (`/tmp/agents/parity2/floatstub.py`, verified 2026-09-27). The defaults agree, so this is not `BUGS.md#overload-stub-default-ignored`'s mismatch; the divergence is the specialization's parameter TYPE, which a type checker accepts (int is assignable to float) but which changes the value's runtime type. Fix: when the implementation's default is filled in (the planned fix above), keep it at the implementation's type rather than converting it to the stub's. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) Printing an `int8 | None` writes the raw byte, not the number.** [`print-optional-int8-raw-byte`] `x: int8 | None = int8(5); print(x)` -- and the same through a field or a parameter -- renders `std::cout << ::tpy::print_optional_val(x)` and writes byte `0x05`, where CPython prints `5`; a plain `int8` renders `static_cast<int>(y)` and prints correctly (`/tmp/agents/literal/p/opt_int8.py`, verified 2026-09-26). `print_optional_val` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/format.hpp`) streams the contained `int8_t` as a `char`; `uint8 | None` does the same (`opt_uint8.py`). Fix: route the contained value through the same integer print path a bare fixed-width int takes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (cpy-phase parity gap) The CPython `float32` stub rounds a `float`-typed VARIABLE operand to single precision, where TPy widens to double.** [`cpy-float32-double-precision`] `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py`'s `float32` class rounds every operand and result through `struct.pack('f', ...)`, which matches TPy for float32, int and float-LITERAL operands (a literal takes float32 in TPy). A `float`-typed variable operand (`f32 + d` with `d: float`) is a double in TPy (`__add__(self, other: float) -> float`) but a float32 under the stub, since Python cannot tell a literal from a variable at runtime. A case that prints such a mixed result cannot run under the cpy phase. Narrowed 2026-09-12 from the previous alias-of-float gap.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Slice assignment on a user record with a slice-keyed `__setitem__` is rejected outright.** [`record-slice-assign-rejected`]
  `g[0:2] = 9` on a record whose `__setitem__` takes `slice` fails at sema with `Slice assignment not supported for type 'Own[Grid]'`, while the plain `g[0] = 5` resolves and CPython runs both. The rule predates the dunder lookup; a slice key should resolve through `__setitem__` like any other. Found while closing the `@dispatch` `__getitem__` operator gap (2026-09-10).
- **[MED small] (unlocated diagnostic; ill-formed C++ inside a tuple) A `bytes` value at a `bytearray` PARAMETER never reaches the located cross-buffer rule.** [`bytes-at-bytearray-param-unlocated`] `def f(b: bytearray)` called as `f(p)` with `p: bytes` rejects at `call.arg_shape.record_nonf1`, and the tuple form `def f(t: tuple[bytearray, int])` called as `f((p, 1))` is accepted by sema outright and fails in the C++ toolchain -- codegen emits `std::tuple<ByteArray*, ...>{&(p), ...}`, taking the address of a `bytes` value for a `ByteArray*` slot. A `bytearray` is a reference type, so its parameter takes the reference/pointer form and the argument never routes through the value-bind check the rule lives on; the OWNING sinks of the same direction (a local, a field, a return) do reach it and give the `write 'bytearray(...)' around it` message. Pre-existing and unchanged by the tuple-element fix (verified against a detached worktree at 578932992e: identical on both). The fix is to route the reference-typed parameter bind through the same check, not to add a second one. Met 2026-09-10 while sweeping the recursive arms of `_check_compat`. The opposite direction -- a `bytearray` at a `bytes` parameter -- has the same gap and is silent rather than loud: [`bytearray-at-bytes-param-owned-silently`].

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) Binding the result of `dict.setdefault` on an `R | None` element type fails the C++ build.** [`dict-setdefault-optional-elem-result-ill-formed`] `d: dict[str, Pic | None] = {}; got = d.setdefault("a", Pic(3))` (or `None`, or a pointer-repr Optional local) renders `Pic* got = ::tpy::dict_setdefault(d, "a", ...)`, binding the returned `std::optional<Pic>&` to a `Pic*` -- the result gate admits the call but the Optional-element read-back has no lift (the sibling of the entry below); the call as a STATEMENT lowers. Found 2026-09-11 while admitting the pointer-repr Optional local at the argument slot; the argument was never what failed. Pre-existing on master `331fbc2948`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) `dict.setdefault` with a LIST-LITERAL default fails the C++ build.** [`dict-setdefault-list-literal-default`] `d: dict[int32, list[int32]] = {}; p = d.setdefault(1, [5, 6]); print(len(p))` passes sema and emits `::tpy::dict_setdefault(d, 1, {5, 6})`; g++ reports *no matching function for call to dict_setdefault(..., <brace-enclosed initializer list>)* -- `couldn't deduce template parameter 'DefArg'` (the runtime signature is `template<class K, class V, class KeyArg, class DefArg> V& dict_setdefault(ordered_map<K, V>&, const KeyArg&, DefArg&&)`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dict_ops.hpp`). A named default (`dflt = [5, 6]; d.setdefault(1, dflt)`) compiles. Fix shape: render the literal at the stub's `V` type (as other element-typed literal arguments are), or give the runtime a `V&&` overload. Found by the 2026-09-29 BUGS.md lifetime sweep.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Reading an `Optional` element back out of a container does not lower.** [`optional-container-element-read-unlowered`] With `d: dict[str, bytes | None] = {"k": b"ab"}`, `v = d["k"]` rejects at `stmt.var_decl:subscript.elem.optional` and `for v in d.values()` at `stmt.for_each:iter.method_call_shape`, while the STORE and `len(d)` both lower; CPython reads it back with no ceremony. The `list[bytes | None]` sibling rejects at the same tag; a for-each over a reference-typed `list[R | None]` (`for p in patches:`) rejects at `stmt.for_each:foreach.consuming_iter` while the index read `p = patches[i]` lowers. It is otherwise the VALUE-typed payload that fails, not Optional elements in general: the reference-typed `dict[str, R | None]` reads back and runs. Pre-existing and unrelated to the cross-buffer rule (no bytearray is involved in any witness); met 2026-09-10 while pinning that rule's wrapped face, which is why `tests/cases/bytes/bytearray_copy_into_bytes_sink` observes its copy on an Optional LOCAL and only counts the dict one.

- **[LOW small] (message quality; the rejection itself is correct) The container-LITERAL element seam rewrites every targeted diagnostic raised under it, so the remediation is lost.** [`literal-elem-seam-swallows-remediation`] `_analyze_list_literal`'s contextual arm wraps its per-element `check_type_compatible` in `except SemanticError` and re-raises a fixed *List literal element N has type X, incompatible with annotated element type Y*. Any rule that fires INSIDE that call and carries a fix -- the mismatch's conversion hint *write 'bytes(...)' around it*, `_check_polymorphic_slicing`'s *use `Box[Throwable]`* -- is replaced by the generic text, so the user is told what is wrong but not what to write. The dict/set literal arms wrap the same way. Pre-existing (the slicing hint has been swallowed there since it was added); surfaced 2026-09-10 when the bytearray-at-an-owning-bytes-sink rule reached the literal face. The fix needs a way for a targeted diagnostic to survive the wrapper (a marker on `SemanticError`, or the seam asking `_check_compat` first and framing only its `CompatError`) -- a shared-diagnostic change, so it is filed rather than improvised. `tests/cases/bytes/error_bytearray_in_bytes_literal` pins the seam's text as it stands. The same wrap-and-swallow shape recurs at the LAMBDA-RETURN check (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py` ~4180-4188), so a general fix should cover both rather than unwrapping the literal arm alone. A third face is the CONTAINER-INVARIANT path (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py` ~1199/1354/1375), which does not wrap a raised diagnostic but builds its own `CompatError` from the element pair and so never reaches the hint: `d2: dict[int, bytes] = d1` over a `dict[int, bytearray]` reports *expected bytes, got bytearray* and the `list` twin *expected list[bytes], got list[bytearray]*, both correct rejections with no *write 'bytes(...)' around it*. Verified identical at 305c187198, before the hint became data, so it is pre-existing there too; the fix shape is the same -- let the element check's own error through instead of re-forming one. A fourth face: an owning UNION-typed sink (`bytes | Indexed` field written from a bytearray) rejects through `_check_compat`'s union member loop, which asks the row veto per member but computes the *write 'bytes(...)' around it* hint only for the direct pair, so the message arrives without it. Same fix shape.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `Own[bytes]` parameter takes only a bytes LITERAL: every other source rejects.** [`own-bytes-param-takes-only-a-literal`] With `def take(b: Own[bytes]) -> int`, `take(b"ab")` lowers while `take(bytes(x))` (a call rvalue), `take(name)` (an owned `bytes` local) and the `BytesView`-typed local all reject at `call.arg_shape.own_bytes`; the constructor twin `H(bytes(x))` / `H(name)` rejects at `call.ctor_arg.own_bytes` while `H(b"ab")` lowers. The `Own[bytes]` CONTAINER-ELEMENT slot (`xs.append(bytes(x))`) takes all of them, so the gap is the non-element `Own[bytes]` slot rather than the payload: `_bytes_owned_slot_arg` / `_bytes_owned_name_arg` / `_bytes_owned_call_rvalue_arg` in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py` are reached from the element seam only. Pre-existing (no bytearray is involved in any witness). Found while pinning the bytearray-at-an-owning-bytes-sink rule; `tests/cases/bytes/bytearray_copy_into_bytes_sink` covers the element face and says why the other two are absent.


- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A generic record that INHERITS its `__init__` cannot be constructed at a view-family instantiation.** [`inherited-generic-ctor-view-arg`] `class Derived[T](Base[T]): pass` over `class Base[T]` with `def __init__(self, value: T)` rejects `Derived[str]("hi")` at `expr.call:call.ctor_arg.generic`, while `Base[str]("hi")` lowers through the same argument and `Derived[int32](5)` lowers through the same route -- so it is the pair (inherited `__init__`, view-family instantiation), not either alone. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/stringtype_impl/probe_move/derived.py`. Found by the merge hunt 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) Indexing a string LITERAL directly is ambiguous in C++.** [`str-literal-index-ambiguous`] `print("xyz"[1])` renders `::tpy::__getitem__("xyz", 1)` with a `const char[4]` argument, and `dunder.hpp` offers `__getitem__(const std::string&, int32_t)` and `__getitem__(std::string_view, int32_t)` -- two user-defined conversions of equal rank, so g++ reports *call of overloaded '__getitem__(const char [4], int)' is ambiguous*. Binding the literal to a local first (`s = "xyz"; s[1]`) compiles and runs, and the SLICE form (`"abc"[0:2]`) compiles because `str_slice` takes the view alone, so it is the index form on a bare literal only. `__len__` already carries a `const char*` overload for exactly this reason; the fix is the same one line for `__getitem__`. Pre-existing and identical on master (probed at 561766ec7e in a detached worktree). No case in the corpus indexes a bare literal. Found probing subscripts after the dispatch-split merge 2026-09-10.


- **[MED small] (hard C++ error) An escaping nested `def` emits a by-value capture with no copyability check.** [`nesteddef-copy-capture-uncheckable`] Sema's "used after the closure -- must copy, warn" branch (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`, the `should_move` / `names_used_after` split) leaves the name out of `move_captures`, and the nested-`def` capture-list builder (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`, the `stmt.escapes` arm) then spells it bare. Nothing asks whether C++ can copy it, so a record with `__del__` (or a `@nocopy` field) is emitted as `[g]` and g++ rejects the generated file: `g = Guard(5)` + an escaping `def inner(): return g.x` + a later `print(g.x)` warns "Escaping closure 'inner' copies local 'g' ..." and then fails with `use of deleted function 'Guard::Guard(const Guard&)'` (reproducer `/tmp/agents/gatefix/d/nested2.py`). The LAMBDA sibling of the same shape rejects in the front end (`expr.lambda`, via `_uncopyable_capture`), so the two closure forms disagree on the same capture. Fix shape: ask `_cpp_noncopyable_type` at the nested-`def` by-value entry the way the lambda entry builder does, and decide whether the answer is a front-end reject or an upgrade of the copy WARNING to an error -- the warning is already at the right site, it just does not know the copy is impossible. (A dormant tuple sibling -- `_cpp_noncopyable_type` not recursing into a value tuple whose element was a `ValueType` with `__del__` -- is moot: a `ValueType` cannot define `__del__`.) A second site: an escaping closure over a local that ALIASES other storage copies it (`_capture_aliases_other_storage`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) behind the "copies local" warning, and the same unchecked copy fails in g++ for a `@nocopy` record or one with `__del__`.

- **[LOW small] (warned, not silent) The tuple-copy warning at a yield names the copy but not its aliasing consequence.** [`tuple-yield-copy-warning-omits-aliasing`] A generator whose owning tuple local is still live after the yield copies the tuple out (`return (*t);`), so the consumer gets its own `C` and a mutation through the yielded element never reaches the generator: TPy `gen sees 0` / `gen sees 10` where CPython prints `gen sees 777` twice (probe `/tmp/agents/probe15/pB.py`). The divergence IS declared -- sema emits "copies tuple[int32, C] into owned storage; use copy() to make this explicit" -- but the text describes the cost (a copy) rather than the semantic change (the consumer no longer aliases the generator's object), which is the part a reader has to act on. Same text at every owned-storage sink, so the wording is a shared decision, not a yield-local one. Fix shape: extend the message with the aliasing clause where the source is a reference element the caller can observe through. Found analysing the tuple-yield ladders for the peephole deletion.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A generator cannot yield a tuple with a `@nocopy` element, on the premise that `__next__()` hands out a copy -- which the resumable frame does not.** [`nocopy-tuple-yield-gate-stale`] `Iterator[tuple[int32, Own[Handle]]]` at an `@nocopy` `Handle` is rejected at registration: "Generator cannot yield non-copyable type 'tuple[int32, Own[Handle]]': each yielded value is stored by value and handed out as a copy by __next__(), which requires a copy constructor." (probe `/tmp/agents/probe15/pG.py`). The resumable frame's `__next__` returns `std::expected<T, ::tpy::StopIteration>` BY VALUE and the owning frame slot is movable -- a dead-after-yield slot already renders `return std::move((*t));` for the copyable sibling -- so the copy the message asserts is not the one the frame makes. The gate closes the whole `Iterator[tuple[..., Own[@nocopy]]]` family before lowering ever sees it. Fix shape: make the gate ask whether the yield hands out a MOVE at this slot (the same liveness fact the move arm reads) rather than assuming a copy, and keep the reject for the shapes that genuinely copy. Found analysing the tuple-yield ladders for the peephole deletion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A tuple literal cannot contain the char produced by string indexing.** [`char-tuple-literal-admission`]
  Inside a narrowed `case str()` arm, `one = (x[0],)` rejects at `decl.tuple_literal_shape`, while the scalar `x[0]` and the byte-valued tuple sibling compile. `_value_tuple_element_ok` in `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py` excludes char; the nested value-tuple and tuple-declaration gates inherit that exclusion before lowering the element expression. This predicate and its explicit char exclusion predate the master merge at `987d04c5`. CPython's string-index result is a normal one-character string and can be stored in a tuple. Fix shape: assess char element construction, storage and reads across tuple positions together, preserving the scalar element's value semantics. **Measured 2026-09-15** while fixing the char-at-a-`str`-slot family: this is NOT that family's root -- `(x[0],)` has no `str` slot, its type is `tuple[char]`, so no coercion is involved and the char-to-string conversion those sinks now read does nothing here. Adding `_eligible_char` to `_value_tuple_element_ok` admits the LITERAL and moves the reject one gate on, to the element READ (`one[0]` -> `subscript.tuple_shape`), which is what makes this its own unit: every tuple position (literal, subscript read, param, return, unpack, container element, field) has to be walked, and `_eligible_char`'s own docstring names the reason char was held out of `_eligible_scalar` -- a str literal in a char slot renders a target-typed C++ char literal, which the scalar positions do not thread. Found while adding scalar/tuple controls for narrowed indexing; the passing regression uses the byte-valued sibling. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A comparison whose operand is a SUBCLASS of the record dunder's declared parameter is rejected.** [`record-eq-subtype-operand-rejects`]
  With `class Puddle(Dog)` and `Dog.__eq__(self, other: "Dog")`, `d == p` rejects at `stmt.expr_stmt:binop.shape.==.record`; CPython runs it (`True` when `Puddle` inherits the dunder, `False` when it overrides it -- Python gives a SUBCLASS operand's method priority in BOTH operand orders). The reject fires whether or not `Puddle` overrides `__eq__`, so it also refuses the shape where the upcast is plainly right. Same row as `BUGS.md#derived-ne-unchecked-operand`: `_record_dunder_operand_pair` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) gates the operand on sema's arg-compatibility predicate, which pins the operand to the declared parameter type rather than admitting a derived one. The explicit `d.__eq__(p)` spelling is accepted (and misbehaves -- see the entry below). **The fix's constraint:** admitting the upcast is only correct when the subclass does NOT override the dunder, or under `@dynamic` dispatch. Records are not polymorphic here, so an admitted upcast static-dispatches to `Dog::__eq__` and silently ignores `Puddle.__eq__` -- which is exactly the divergence the entry below measures at the spellings that already compile. So this reject is the only thing keeping the direct spelling off that divergence: fixing it alone WIDENS the silent one, and the two must land together. Probes `/tmp/agents/puddle/main.py` and `/tmp/agents/refunion_impl/puddle2/main.py`. Found while reviewing the reference-union storage form 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning, two spellings) A record `__eq__` overridden in a subclass is bypassed at every comparison that compiles, and an explicit dunder CALL picks the subclass's where Python does not.** [`record-eq-subclass-static-dispatch`]
  With `Dog.__eq__(self, other: "Dog")` returning `self.n == other.n` and `class Puddle(Dog)` overriding it to `False`, over `d = Dog(1)` and `p = Puddle(1)` (both fields `1`): `d.__eq__(p)` answers **False** where CPython answers True, and `takes(d, p)` / `takes(p, d)` with `def takes(a: Dog, b: Dog): return a == b` answer **True** where CPython answers False. Two different causes, one root -- C++ overload resolution standing in for Python's method lookup: (1) the explicit dunder call renders as the operator (`(d) == (p)`), and C++20's REVERSED candidate makes `Puddle`'s hidden friend `operator==(const Puddle&, const Dog&)` an exact match on both parameters where `Dog`'s needs a derived-to-base conversion, so the subclass's method wins a call that Python defines as unreflected; (2) through base-typed parameters both operands are `const Dog&`, the friends are non-virtual, so `Dog::__eq__` is called and the override is ignored -- Python would give the `Puddle` operand priority. No warning on either. CPython prints `True False` where TPy prints `False True`. Probe `/tmp/agents/refunion_impl/puddle4/main.py` (prints the fields, both explicit-dunder orders and both base-param orders). Sibling of `BUGS.md#record-eq-subtype-operand-rejects`, which is the reject that keeps the DIRECT `d == p` spelling from reaching cause (2); fix shape must decide how a record dunder dispatches when a subclass overrides it (virtual dispatch for an overridden dunder, or a rejection at the spellings that cannot honour Python's rule) rather than widening the operand gate first. Found while reviewing the reference-union storage form 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A type alias whose body names an IMPORTED type alias is rejected as an unknown type.** [`imported-alias-member-in-alias-body`]
  `from tpy import float64` then `type Mixed = Dog | int32 | float64` fails with `Type alias 'Mixed' references unknown type 'float64'`, and so does the bare `type Alias = float64`. The same type spelled inline in a signature (`def f(x: float64 | str)`) compiles, and a SAME-module alias-of-alias (`type Money = float` then `type A = Money | str`) compiles -- only the imported alias fails. `_validate_type_alias_members` in `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py` accepts a member `NominalType` only when it carries a `_module_qname` or resolves in the record registry; an imported alias binding has neither at that point, so the validator refuses a name it merely has not resolved yet. Reachable from the stdlib today because `float64` is itself an alias (`type float64 = float` in `lib/tpy/tpy/__init__.py`) and from any user module that exports one (`from m import Money`). CPython accepts every spelling. Workaround: spell the underlying type (`float`) or write the union inline -- `tests/cases/union/reference_union_storage_eq` cites this entry and takes the `float` spelling for that reason. Repro `/tmp/agents/refunion_impl/alias5/`. Fix shape: resolve imported alias bindings before the alias-member validation, or let the validator consult the alias table sema already holds -- the same check-runs-before-the-name-is-bound family as the cycle re-export entries. Found spelling the record-beside-numerics pack for the reference-union storage compare 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) The copy warning at a record-UNION field recommends `copy()`, and `copy()` rejects there.** [`union-field-copy-no-render`] `self.pq = u.f` at `pq: P | R` warns `copies P | R into field; use copy() to make this explicit`, but `self.pq = copy(u.f)` (and `copy(us[0])`) rejects at `expr.call:call.copy_source.union`: the explicit copy has no render for a union source, so the acknowledgment the warning asks for cannot be spelled. The Optional-record twin renders (`s.op = copy(xs[0])` compiles). Fix: a copy render for a union source (the variant copy of the active member) at both spellings. Found 2026-10-01 by review of `records/field_admission_warned`; pre-existing on master `31d73ca09c`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An aliased import of a generic tplib record (`from tplib import Box as TBox`) gives the annotation and the value two type identities.** [`aliased-generic-import-type-identity`] `f: TBox[P]` beside `self.f = TBox(P(1))` fails with `Type mismatch in assignment: expected Box[P], got TBox[P]`: the field annotation resolves to the record's own name while the constructor call's stamped type keeps the alias, so the two never compare equal. The unaliased `from tplib import Box` twin compiles. Found 2026-10-01 while pinning a Box field write; pre-existing on master `31d73ca09c`. Repro: a module that defines its own `Box` and imports tplib's under an alias.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Value-union boundaries reject a bytes member even though its signature and match body can lower.** [`bytes-value-union-boundary-rejects`] When these boundaries widen, the `bytearray_to_bytes` coercion's `identity` disposition (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`, the `_coerce_disposition` row) has to grow an arm: it assumes the only reachable `bytes` slot is the span view a `bytearray` satisfies bare, but at a union slot the alternative is `const ::tpy::Bytes*`, so an identity pass would render `::tpy::Union<..., const ::tpy::Bytes*>{&ba}` -- ill-formed C++, loud but unlocated. A materialize or a located reject belongs there before the admission widens.
  For `x: bytes | int32`, `if isinstance(x, bytes)` rejects at `stmt.if:cond.call`, before the body reaches subscript lowering. A local `data: bytes | int32 = b"abc"` likewise rejects at `decl.slot_type`. `_eligible_value_union` in `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py` admits str/StrView but omits bytes, and `_builtin_value_member` explicitly excludes the BYTES category. The union is value-form, so pointer-union admission cannot rescue it. The isinstance rejection reproduces before the master merge at `987d04c5` and after the match-subscript repair; the local gate uses the same unchanged eligibility predicate. The `bytes | Indexed` pointer-union sibling accepts a bytes-literal call and runs the same indexing body. Fix shape: settle bytes storage/view conversions across value-union construction, arguments, returns and extraction together, rather than widen one consumer. The exact value-union match body remains compile coverage in `tests/cases/match/narrowed_subscript`; its pointer-union sibling supplies native/CPython execution coverage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
