- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A union with a `BytesView` member does not lower its `isinstance` arm.** [`bytesview-union-member-rejects`] `def f(u: bytes | BytesView)` / `Span[readonly[uint8]] | BytesView` with `if isinstance(u, BytesView):` rejects at `stmt.if:cond.call`, where the same shape over `str | StrView` lowers. The widened union member class (`_ptr_union_member_wide`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) admits `str`, `bytes`, containers, value tuples and `Span` and has no row for the bytes view, so the isinstance narrowing over such a union never reaches the variant machinery. The signature itself renders (`tests/cases/bytes/distinct_spelling_union`, the view pair). Since 2026-09-10 the pair spells distinct alternatives (`::tpy::BytesView` is its own type), so admitting the view is a member-class row, not a spelling question; `tests/cases/bytes/error_bytesview_union_isinstance` pins the reject. Found 2026-09-10 converting the duplicate-spelling error case.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Two union operands of ONE type reject unless they were borrowed the same way.** [`ref-union-loop-var-vs-borrow-compare`]
  A union at a borrow position compares (`union/reference_union_borrow_eq`), but one union type has three C++ renders and none converts to another, so a pair drawn from two of them rejects at `binop.shape.==` although both operands are spelled `Pet` in the source. The three: the STORAGE element a `for e in xs` / comprehension variable binds (`::tpy::Union<Cat, Dog>`), the mutable borrow (`::tpy::Union<Cat*, Dog*>`), and the const-pointee read borrow (`::tpy::Union<const Cat*, const Dog*>`, taken by a `readonly[...]` annotation, by a param the callable only discriminates, and by a local lifted out of a const container). So `[e == u for e in xs]` rejects (at `expr.list_comp`). The two const-side pairs this entry also listed -- `def f(a: readonly[Pet], b: Pet): return a == b` and `def f(xs: list[Pet], u: Pet): a = xs[0]; return a == u` -- now compile: a non-mutating union parameter borrows const pointees, so the annotated and the inferred slot are one render and the const local is that render too. What is left is the STORAGE side. `_ptr_union_compare_pair` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) requires the two renders to agree rather than emit a compare that does not build; before the borrow form was its own type every one of these rejected at the same tag, so nothing regressed -- but CPython runs all three. Fix shape: lift the storage side at the compare, the way an argument at a borrow slot lifts it (`to_const_ptr_variant`) -- a form decision, not a gate widening. `tests/cases/union/reference_union_borrow_eq` cites this entry and takes two parameters in its comprehension section for that reason; its `readonly mixed` and `const local` sections pin the two pairs that now compile. Found landing the borrow-form union type 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A union whose members are all `Ptr[T]` reaches codegen at one position only.** [`ptr-member-union-unreachable`]
  `type PtrPet = Ptr[Dog] | Ptr[Cat]` renders its alias and a parameter signature (`const ::tpy::Union<Cat*, Dog*>&`) and nothing else: the call that would build the argument rejects at `call.arg_shape.union`, an annotated local at `decl.slot_type`, a return at `return.slot_type`, a field at `stmt.assign:assign.field_write_shape` (constructor and method alike), a container literal at `expr.container_literal`, a compare at `binop.shape.==` (`_eligible_value_union` excludes `Ptr` members, and `_eligible_ptr_union_wide` wants non-value members), and `isinstance(u, Ptr[Dog])` at "Generic type 'Ptr' cannot be used as a value". Identical on `cba2f6df73` and after the borrow-form type landed, so nothing regressed -- but every one of these runs in CPython. **What this entry protects**: such a union is the SAME C++ type as any other union's borrow form -- `::tpy::Union` over a pointer alternative pack -- at every position, owning ones included, because its members are already borrowed references; the consequence is that when it does compare it compares POINTEES, not addresses. It needs no carve-out in the renderer to get there: the alternatives carry the fact. That was decided with the borrow-form type (analysis fork 2.4 answer (i)) and must not be silently re-decided when these gaps close. `tests/cases/union/ptr_member_union_spelling` pins the two spellings that do render. Probes `/tmp/agents/ptrunion/ptrmix/`. Found probing the all-`Ptr` route for the borrow-form union type 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `bytearray` member keeps a union element from being read out of a container at all.** [`bytearray-union-element-read-rejects`]
  `a = xs[0]` with `xs: list[bytearray | int32]` rejects at `stmt.var_decl:subscript.elem.union`, with no narrowing or comparison involved; the same read over `list[list[int32] | int32]` or `list[Dog | int32 | float]` lowers and runs. So the union element path is reachable for record, container and scalar members and blocked by the `bytearray` member specifically. CPython runs it. Same `bytearray`-in-a-union family as `BUGS.md#bytes-value-union-boundary-rejects`, and the fix should settle the two together rather than widen one consumer. The third member of the family -- the whole-union deep-const argument bridge, which skipped its wrap because the same narrow member class excluded a zero-type-arg `bytearray` -- is fixed: that consumer now keys on the wide class. Repro `/tmp/agents/ptrunion/cell2.py`. Found spelling the borrowed-value-members section for the borrow-form union compare 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) Any protocol bound satisfies a `Copyable` requirement, so the bound check accepts a non-copyable type.** [`marker-bound-satisfies-copyable`] `def inner[T: Copyable](v: T)` called from `def outer[T: Stringable](v: T): return inner(v)` is accepted, and so is the end-to-end program that instantiates `outer` at a non-copyable class (a `__del__`, which deletes the generated copy ctor) with `__str__`. `protocols.py` correctly refuses an UNBOUND type param (pinned by `tests/cases/generics/error_copyable_marker_unbound_t`), but when the param HAS a protocol-typed bound the check delegates to that bound, and the `Copyable` marker arm (`tpyc/sema/protocols.py:437`) asks `not is_type_non_copyable(<the protocol type>)` -- False for any protocol, so the negation reports conformance. The bound therefore checks that SOME bound exists, not that it is `Copyable`. Today the owning-slot copy contract (`tpyc/sema/own_copy.py`) still catches the program with a located error, so the consequence is a bound that does not mean what it says rather than a build failure; it becomes a libstdc++-spew class for any future rule that leans on the bound check alone. Fix shape: the marker arm must ask whether the BOUND is (or extends) `Copyable`, not whether the bound type is copyable. Probes `/tmp/agents/bound/p14_any_bound_body.py` and `p15_hole_e2e.py`. Found measuring the explicit-bound fork for the generic copy contract 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) A generic base in a class header escapes the type-parameter bound check.** [`generic-base-decl-skips-bound-check`] `class Kid(Holder[Pinned])` with `class Holder[T: Copyable]` produces no TPy diagnostic at all; the C++ build then fails with `constraints not satisfied ... concept Copyable = std::is_copy_constructible_v<T>` plus two cascade errors. Every other route to the same instantiation IS checked: explicit type args and constructor inference both report `does not satisfy bound`. Sibling of the unslugged bare-annotation entry further down (`x: Box[Rc[int32]]` is unchecked for the same reason) but a different site: the base list is resolved in `tpyc/sema/registration.py`, which classifies parents without consulting `record_info.type_param_bounds`. Fix shape: validate a parent's substituted type args against the base's bounds where the parents are classified, mirroring the construction-site check. Probe `/tmp/agents/bound/p7_record_base_decl.py`. Found measuring the explicit-bound fork for the generic copy contract 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) `copy()` of a non-copyable type is not diagnosed, in a generic body or a monomorphic one.** [`copy-call-of-noncopyable-undiagnosed`] `xs.append(copy(v))` with `v: Pinned` (non-copyable: it defines `__del__`) passes sema and fails the C++ build with `use of deleted function 'Pinned::Pinned(const Pinned&)'` at `xs.push_back(::tpyapp::Pinned(v))`; the generic twin `xs.append(copy(v))` at an open `T` instantiated at `Pinned` fails identically at `xs.push_back(T(v))`. Generic and twin agree, and both are wrong. `copy()` is the acknowledged-copy escape hatch and is exempted at record time (`is_copy_call`) before any copy verdict is taken, so nothing downstream asks whether the acknowledged copy is possible. Same class as the `heapq` entry below, whose prescribed fix (add `T: Copyable` bounds) does not cover the monomorphic half. Fix shape: check copy-constructibility at the `copy()` call itself, so the hatch reports what it cannot do. Probes `/tmp/agents/bound/p17_copy_nomove.py` and `p18_copy_nomove_twin.py`. Found measuring the explicit-bound fork for the generic copy contract 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; everyday shape) A local list LITERAL passed to a `readonly[list[T]]` parameter fails the C++ build.** [`array-literal-into-readonly-list-param`] `def f(xs: readonly[list[int32]]) -> int32: ...` called as `bs = [1, 2]; f(bs)`: the literal resolves to `std::array<int32_t, 2>` and the call passes it where the param is `const std::vector<int32_t>&` -> `invalid initialization of reference of type 'const std::vector<int>&' from expression of type 'std::array<int, 2>'`. The same call against a plain `list[int32]` param compiles: passing the local there is what settles the literal as a list. The `readonly[...]` wrapper on the param evidently hides it from that Array-vs-list verdict (not confirmed in code). Records (`[Box(1), Box(2)]`) fail the same way; an annotated local (`bs: list[int32] = [1, 2]`) works. Found 2026-09-20 probing the genexpr entries; no genexpr is involved. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; everyday shape) A NESTED list literal whose rows reach a `list[T]` parameter stays a nested `std::array`.** [`nested-array-literal-row-into-list-param`] `rows = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]` then `for row in rows: total(row)` with `def total(xs: list[int32])` renders `std::array<std::array<int32_t, 2>, 2> rows` and fails the C++ build (`invalid initialization of reference of type 'const std::vector<int>&' from expression of type 'std::array<int, 2>'`); `total(rows[0])` rejects at `stmt.expr_stmt:call.arg_shape.container` instead. A flat literal passed straight to the parameter settles as a list; a use of one of the literal's ELEMENTS never reaches the outer literal's Array-vs-list verdict. Annotating the local (`rows: list[list[int32]] = ...`) works. Same class as the entry above. Verified 2026-09-23 on master 4713ba0943; probes `/tmp/agents/narrow/lit/lit.py`, `lit2.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A tuple with a `StrView` element cannot be built into a list: the literal and `append` forms both reject.** [`strview-tuple-into-list-rejects`] `vs: list[tuple[StrView, int32]] = [(StrView("p"), 1)]` -> `(expr.container_literal)`; `vs.append((StrView("p"), 1))` -> `(expr.tuple_literal)`. READING such a list works, including a genexpr that unpacks it (`sum(len(k) + v for k, v in vs)` compiles since genexprs lower to frames), so the container can be consumed but not produced in TPy. Surfaced 2026-09-20 when the genexpr reject that used to mask it (`genexpr.unpack`) went away; the masking case was `tests/cases/str/error_genexpr_unpack_view_target`.
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong value; toolchain-caught in the local faces) A resumable frame's internal names collide with user names.** [`frame-internal-names-collide`] A generator or coroutine frame is a C++ struct whose members include the state enumerators (`S_INITIAL`, `S_RESUME_<n>`, `S_JOIN_<n>`, `S_DONE`) and the `__state` field, and its body is a member function. A module global read inside the body by its bare name is hidden by a member of the same name: `S_DONE = 100` at module level, then `yield S_DONE` in a generator, yields `3` (the enumerator) where CPython yields `100` -- no diagnostic, verified 2026-09-23 on master fd40895525. A generator LOCAL of one of those names becomes a frame field of the same name and fails the C++ build (`S_DONE` / `S_INITIAL` -> `use of 'this' in a constant expression` at the case labels; `__state` -> a duplicate member). Fix shape: read module globals inside frame bodies by their qualified name (`::tpyapp::<mod>::S_DONE`), which removes the silent face for every member name at once, and rename a user local that collides with a frame-internal name the way C++-keyword locals are already escaped. Repros `/tmp/agents/pin1/names.py`, `/tmp/agents/pin1/names2.py`.


- **[LOW small] (silent divergence in `__del__` / `finally` timing) `del` of the last name holding an object, and a rebind of a name to another name's object, do not drop the object there.** [`del-last-alias-keeps-object`] `p = P(1); q = p; p = P(2); del q` prints `del 1` at scope end in TPy, before `after del q` in CPython (verified 2026-09-23; `P& q = (*p);` and the `del` emits nothing, the first object living in `__slot_1`). The generator face is the `finally`: `h = g; del g; g = counter(10); ...; del h` closes the first generator at scope end (probe `/tmp/agents/r3_cp/p11.py`), and so does `g = h` over a generator nothing else holds. Values are never affected; this is the timing half of the declared storage-of-its-own divergence (docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md, "Storage of its own"), which claimed until 2026-09-23 that `del` on the alias drops the object. Fix shape: a `del` (or an alias rebind) of the last holder of a slot the pass owns resets that slot -- the pass already knows the holders.
- **[LOW small] (spurious warning naming an internal temporary) A tuple unpack re-run by a loop warns that a parser temp will not keep the object.** [`unpack-in-loop-warns-internal-temp`] `g = Rec(1); for i in range(3): g, k = Rec(i * 10), 5` warns `'g' will not keep the object it was given -- '__unpack_0_0' is rebound on each iteration`, yet `g` does hold the last object, as in CPython (probe `/tmp/agents/arch3/unpack_rec.py`; the generator spelling is now rejected outright). The loop-reuse check treats the unpack's element temp as a user alias. Pre-existing.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (rejects-valid, loud; a documented restriction) A name holding a generator is bound once: rebinding it to a new generator is a compile error.** [`generator-rebind-rejects`] `g = counter(0); ...; g = counter(5)` reports `cannot rebind 'g' to a new generator` (the alias-rebind storage pass, for any rebind site some path reaches with a generator already bound; `tests/cases/generators/error_frame_rebind`), where CPython rebinds the name and closes the old generator once nothing else holds it. Three shapes report earlier with their own message: a rebind through `nonlocal` (`error_frame_nonlocal_rebind`), inside a `for` over the name (`error_frame_rebind_while_iterating`), and in a tuple unpack (`error_frame_rebind_unpack`); a rebind to a different generator function or another iterator is a separate restriction (type erasure allocates, `error_frame_rebind_other_generator`). Not rebinds, and unaffected: a first binding in both arms of a branch, a binding in a loop body, and swapping or re-seating aliases (`g, h = h, g`). The workaround is a new name, which keeps the old generator open to the end of the scope exactly as CPython does under a new name. History (2026-09-23/24): the branch first rebuilt the frame in place (`::tpy::frame_rebuild`) when a storage-pass proof said nothing still reached the old generator; five review rounds each found another way it still could -- an alias, a frame, a coroutine made directly or through a sync function, a task started by a callee, a live `str` or `Span` view of a yielded value -- so the rebind was removed rather than patched again. Fix shape, if rebinds are ever wanted: a per-object holder set that is complete by construction (a callee escape fact in the Phase-2 fixpoint, views traced to the object they read), then the in-place rebuild again under an ASan matrix with value-changing passes.


- **[MED small] (silent copy / ill-formed C++) A local bound from a structural-protocol PARAMETER copies the argument.** [`protocol-param-local-alias-copies`] `def bump(r: Settable): h = r; h.put(9)` with a record argument renders `auto h = r;` and mutates a copy: TPy prints `1`, CPython `9` (verified 2026-09-23). With a generator argument (`def f(g: Iterator[int32]): h = g`) the same copy is now a C++ build error, the frame's copy constructor being deleted. The decl spells `auto` for every structural-protocol-typed local; binding `auto&` would alias as CPython does, but whether that is right for a VALUE-type conformer inside the one template body (TPy copies a value type on assignment) is the open question. Found 2026-09-23 (probe `/tmp/agents/pin1/y_proto_param_alias.py`, `/tmp/agents/rv_par/p16.py`).

- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent divergence: a loop-bound generator closes a pass early) In a plain function, a generator or coroutine first bound in a loop body is destroyed at the end of each pass, where CPython closes it when the name is bound again on the next pass.** [`plain-loop-generator-closes-at-pass-end`] The local lives in the loop body's C++ block, so a pending `finally` runs before the loop head re-tests its condition. A `finally` that writes state the loop reads changes the program: with `def gen(st): try: yield 1; yield 2 finally: st.done = True` and `while not st.done: g = gen(st); n += first(g)`, CPython runs two passes (the first `g` closes when the second is bound) and TPy one (probe `/tmp/agents/fbo-n/p/whiledone.py`, verified 2026-09-25 on d4827a6abb). A read of the generator after the loop already declares it in front of the loop (`_promote_pending_loop_var`), which gives CPython's order when what it borrows outlives the loop. Fix shape: declare it in front of the loop and close it where the next pass rebinds it, which needs every write a pass makes to what the generator borrows accounted for -- the MIR entry "Loop-bound generators that borrow storage the loop writes" in `docs/IR_DESIGN.md`. Pre-existing.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent divergence: a block-bound generator closes early) In a plain function, a generator first bound in an `if` arm, a `with` / `try` body or a `match` arm and not read after the block is destroyed at the block's end, where CPython closes it when the function ends.** [`plain-block-generator-closes-at-block-end`] The local lives in the block's C++ scope, so a pending `finally` runs before the code after the block. A `finally` that writes state read later changes the value: with `def inner(xs): try: yield xs[0]; yield xs[0] + 1 finally: xs[0] = 9` and `if len(xs) > 0: g = inner(xs); for v in g: break` followed by `print(xs[0])`, CPython prints 0 and TPy 9 (probe `/tmp/agents/fbo-c/bf.py`). Pre-existing: master 1ea64345ea prints 9 as well. A read of the generator after the block declares it in front of the block, which gives CPython's order when it borrows only parameters, the receiver or module globals (`BUGS.md#generator-block-bind-borrows-local-rejects`). Fix shape: CPython's lifetime needs every write to what the generator borrows between the block and the function's end checked against the open frame -- the MIR entry "Loop-bound generators that borrow storage the loop writes" in `docs/IR_DESIGN.md`, which names this block case.
- **[MED small] (compiler crash) A local bound inside a `finally` whose `try` contains a `continue`, in a generator or coroutine, crashes the compiler with `Internal error: 'fv'`.** [`frame-finally-local-after-continue-ice`] Probe `/tmp/agents/fbo-int/m3/ice_fv_repro.py` (`try: if i % 2 == 1: continue ... finally: fv = first(g); print("fin", fv)` inside a `for` in a generator), verified 2026-09-25 on `frame-borrow-order`. No source location; the same local outside the `finally` compiles. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent divergence in `finally` / `__del__` timing) A local released by an escaping exception is released before the caller's handler runs.** [`locals-released-before-caller-handler`] CPython keeps a raising function's frame, and so its locals, alive through the traceback until the handler that catches the exception finishes; C++ stack unwinding destroys them on the way out. With `def f(): g = gen(); first(g); raise ValueError` and `try: f() except ValueError: print("caught")`, CPython prints `caught` and then `gen`'s `finally`, TPy the reverse (probe `/tmp/agents/fbo-n/p/tbkeep.py`, verified 2026-09-25). A resumable frame's loop-source release on an escaping exception (`rcfg.LoopSourceRegion`) follows the same order. Probably a documented divergence rather than a fix: keeping locals alive through a handler needs the exception to own them.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, toolchain-caught) A generator-METHOD call passed directly as an `Iterator[T]` argument fails the C++ build.** [`generator-method-call-arg-binds-rvalue`]
  With `def first_of(tag: str, g: Iterator[int32])` and a generator method `Holder.items`, `first_of("m", h.items())` emits `first_of("m", h.items())` against `void first_of(std::string_view, T_g&)`, and g++ refuses to bind the rvalue frame to `T_g&`; the free-function twin `first_of("m", gen())` hoists `auto __tmp_1 = gen();` and compiles. Binding the call to a local first compiles. Probe `/tmp/agents/fbo-frames/probes/meth_rv.py`, verified on d4827a6abb. The arg-temp hoist that serves a free generator factory does not see the method call as one. Pre-existing; found 2026-09-24 writing `tests/cases/generators/frame_field_order`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. The same happens at a protocol parameter of a free function (`drive(r.walk())` with `def drive(g: Iterator[int32])`: g++ `cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type '__gen_Rows_walk&' to an rvalue`); workaround: bind the generator to a name first.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (silent divergence in destructor timing) A generator passed as a temporary argument lives to the end of the enclosing block, not the statement.** [`generator-arg-temp-outlives-statement`]
  `first_of("x", gen())` in a plain function renders `auto __tmp_1 = gen(); first_of("x", __tmp_1);`, so the abandoned generator's `finally` runs when the function ends; CPython runs it right after the call, when the argument's last reference drops. Several such calls in one function print their `finally` lines at its end, in reverse order. Probe `/tmp/agents/fbo-frames/probes/ffo.py` before its abandon helpers, verified 2026-09-24. Fix shape: scope the hoisted temp to its statement (a block around the call), as a `for` over a temporary generator already is. Pre-existing.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Rebinding a local to `list()` of a DIFFERENT generator rejects.** [`list-of-generator-rebind-rejects`]
  `vals = list(g())` then `vals = list(h())` (both `Iterator[int32]`) rejects the first line at `expr.call:call.special.call_type.builtin_generic`; two names, or one generator function, compile. Probe `/tmp/agents/fbo-frames/probes/listgen.py`, verified on d4827a6abb. Pre-existing; found 2026-09-24.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; everyday shape) A list comprehension over an `Iterator[T]` PARAMETER of a plain function rejects.** [`list-comp-over-iterator-param-rejects`] `def show(g: Iterator[int32]) -> None: got = [v for v in g]; print(got)` fails with "this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.list_comp)"; a `for v in g: got.append(v)` loop over the same parameter compiles (probe `/tmp/agents/fbo-unwind/p/lc.py`, verified 2026-09-27 on `fbo-unwind`). The parameter is a protocol (deduced template) parameter, so the comprehension source has no lowering arm. Found while writing `generators/frame_cleanup_order`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; misleading message) A generator whose callee takes a protocol or `Fn` parameter cannot be held across a `yield` or `await`.** [`deduced-frame-local-across-suspension`] `r = relay(g)` with `def relay(src: Iterable[int32]) -> Iterator[int32]`, then `yield first(r)` twice in a generator (likewise in a generator method and a coroutine) fails with `local 'r' of protocol type aliasing a protocol-typed parameter is only supported across a suspension when bound exactly once directly from the parameter` (`_frame_fields` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`, the `FrameLocalKind.PROTOCOL` binding). The frame of such a call is a template over the deduced arguments with no spelled type, so the enclosing frame has no field type for it; the message describes a different shape (a local bound from a protocol parameter) and names no remedy that applies. The same local in a plain function compiles (`auto r = ...`). Master rejected every generator object held across a suspension with this message; since 2026-09-23 a spelled frame type fixes all but this face. Fix shape: spell a deduced frame's type (the struct template instantiated at the argument types sema resolved), which also lifts the rebind face in BUGS.md#generator-rebind-rejects; until then, a message that names the callee's protocol parameter. Found by the frame-field matrix (`/tmp/agents/narrow/m/cells/gen__relay__none.py`).
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A bound generator cannot be passed to an `Own[...]` parameter, appended to a container or boxed.** [`generator-into-own-sink-rejects`] Since 2026-09-24 a generator local never takes the last-use move (its frame may have started, and a started frame cannot move), so `keep(g)` with `def keep(it: Own[Iterator[int32]])` reports `non-copyable type 'Iterator[int32]' cannot be copied into 'it: Own[Iterator[int32]]'` even at `g`'s last use, where CPython hands the generator over. The move would be sound for a generator that has not been pulled yet; a move-only-while-unstarted rule (the coroutine one, `check_coro_move_unstarted`, generalised to frames) would admit it. The message says "copied" for what is really a move. Found by /tpy-review round 4 of `resumable-frames-alias`.
- **[MED small] (silent divergence; pre-existing) A generator expression that captures a narrowed name is not refused when the SAME tuple unpack rebinds that name.** [`genexpr-kept-scan-same-statement-rebind`] With `k` narrowed from `int32 | None`, `g, k = relay(x * k for x in xs), z` (with `z = None`) compiles and hands the frame `(*k)`, then sets `k = z`; the pull reads the now-empty optional where CPython raises `TypeError`. The two-statement form (`g = relay(...)` then `k = None`) is refused with `'k' is narrowed here, but this generator expression is kept past the statement`: the kept-genexpr rebind scan starts AFTER the binding statement, and the unpack's own target binding is inside it. Master emits the same C++ (probe `/tmp/agents/docsync5/p2.py`). Filed 2026-09-24; a face that used to sit in the removed entry `generator-bound-by-tuple-unpack`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; a silent copy before 2026-09-23) `it = iter(g)` over a bound generator fails the C++ build.** [`iter-of-bound-generator-fails-build`] `g = counter(); it = iter(g)` renders `auto it = ::tpy::__iter__(g);`: `__iter__` hands back the frame by reference and the `auto` decl copies it, which the frame's deleted copy constructor now refuses. Before frames became non-copyable the copy compiled and `it` advanced independently of `g` (CPython: `iter(g) is g`). The record face is the entry below, "Binding `it = iter(c)` ... COPIES the object", and both need the same fact: the result of `iter(x)` is `x` itself when `x`'s `__iter__` returns `self`. Typing it so means either special-casing `iter` by name, which the no-hardcoding rule forbids, or a stub-level way to say "returns its argument" -- a design question, `/tpy-add-feature`. `for v in g` and passing `g` to an `Iterator[T]` parameter are unaffected.

Workaround: use the generator inside the block, or pass it to a helper that consumes it. Fix shape: the invalidation check of docs/IR_DESIGN.md "Loop-bound generators that borrow storage the loop writes" (MIR), which would let the declaration take the borrowed locals with it.

- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (silent divergence in destructor timing) A generator's or coroutine's locals outlive its body: they die with the frame object, not when the body finishes.** [`finished-frame-keeps-locals`] A generator or async body that binds a local with cleanup -- an inner generator with a `finally`, a class with `__del__`, a socket or stream held by a Task's coroutine -- releases it when the frame OBJECT is destroyed. CPython releases it as the body finishes: `print("outer", list(outer()))`, where `outer` holds `g = inner()` and breaks out of it, prints `inner`'s `finally` before the `print` line in CPython and after it in TPy (the frame is the `list()` argument's temporary, alive to the end of the full expression); a finished asyncio Task keeps its coroutine's locals until the Task is dropped. The same holds for a parameter a frame holds by value (`relay(inner())`: `inner`'s frame is a by-value parameter member of `relay`'s). Found 2026-09-23 while pinning frame field order in `tests/cases/generators/frame_alias`.
  Fix shape, as built on `frame-borrow-order` and removed 2026-09-28 to keep that branch reviewable: a generated `__release_locals()` member that resets, in reverse declaration order, the frame fields whose type answers `drop_runs_user_code()` (`FrameField` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/frame_fields.py` carries the fact; only `frame_slot`-backed kinds can be reset -- a by-value parameter needs a releasable slot); a runtime `::tpy::frame_release_guard<Frame>` declared FIRST in `__next__` / `__poll__`, so it is destroyed last -- after a `return`'s value is built -- and calls `__release_locals()` when `__state == S_DONE`; and the `catch (...) { __state = S_DONE; throw; }` wrap around the state machine for every releasing frame, so an escaping exception releases too. With it, a loop that is the body's last statement and a loop an exception escapes outside every level need no release of their own (BUGS.md#frame-loop-source-late-release).
  Pitfalls found building it: (1) never release a local a by-reference yield lent to the caller -- a generator yielding elements of its own local list, consumed as `for n in g: drain(g); print(n.tag)`, is a use-after-free if the list is freed at finish; exclude every field the yields read, closed over `FrameField.borrows` / `spelled_from` (all fields when one has untraced borrows; reuse `frame_fields.lifetime_closure` rather than a second closure). `generators/frame_cleanup_order` `lent_after_finish` is the guard. CPython frees that list at finish and drops the elements the consumer does not hold, so exact parity needs per-element holder facts (MIR). (2) The escaping-exception path must release, and marking the frame done there also fixes BUGS.md#generator-resumes-after-escaping-exception for every releasing frame -- land them together or coordinate. (3) Record each loop's ITERATOR type in sema first: without it every frame with a loop over a user iterable releases a plain iterator for nothing (about 55 of 157 releasing frames in the first attempt were such noise) -- TODO.md "A frame's loop fields release only what may run user code". Release order follows the frame's reverse declaration order, which BUGS.md#locals-destroyed-reverse-creation-order already diverges on.
  Tests to add with it: the `done_outer` shape (a held generator broken out of, then the body finishes) and the yield-lent shape, each CPython-identical, both abandoned and run to the end.

Found 2026-09-22.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A suspending `for` over a CONDITIONAL of two list params whose body mutates through the loop var does not compile: the params stay captured `const`.** [`frame-ternary-params-mutation-not-propagated`] `def g(xs: list[Cell], ys: list[Cell], flag: bool) -> Iterator[int32]: for c in (xs if flag else ys): c.v += 10; yield c.v` captures both params as `const std::vector<Cell>&`, so the loop var deduces `const Cell*` (its field is spelled off the source, `::tpy::begin_elem_t<decltype((flag ? xs : ys))>`) and the write is ill-formed. The read-only body compiles and is pinned (`ternary_params_src` in `tests/cases/generators/frame_for_source_once`); the same loop over ONE of the params demotes it to `std::vector<Cell>&` and compiles. Cause: the for-head's loan registration (`register_iteration_loans` in `tpyc/sema/iter_loans.py`) files `loop_var_iterable` for a name, a subscript, a field or a call, and nothing for a conditional, so the write through the loop var climbs to no source; the shared provenance walker `lend_roots` (`tpyc/sema/scope_tracker.py`) does see both arms, and routing the for-head's non-lvalue sources through it is the fix shape (the call-edge side already does, since 2026-09-22). The plain-function twin is a located reject of the conditional source itself (`iter.if_expr_shape`), so this face exists only in a frame. Narrowed 2026-09-22 from the const-spelling entry this replaced, which the source-typed fields closed.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud -- C++ build failure, no TPy diagnostic) A loop variable bound by a const-source loop and by a MUTATING loop in one frame.** [`frame-shared-loop-var-const-join-mutation`] `def g(a: list[Cell], b: readonly[list[Cell]]) -> Iterator[int32]: for c in b: yield c.v` then `for c in a: c.v += 1; yield c.v` -- the two loops share one frame field, whose pointee is the C++ join of both loops' elements (`::tpy::const_join_t<const Cell, Cell>* c`, i.e. `const Cell*`), so the write in the second loop is `assignment of member in read-only object`. Valid Python; the read-only twin compiles (`shared_var_src` in `tests/cases/generators/frame_for_source_once`). Before the join the same program failed in the other loop (a mutable pointer seeded from a const_iterator), so the shape never compiled; what is missing is a located diagnostic -- sema's `mark_frame_const` already knows the binding is const from the first loop and could refuse the write there, or the two loops could take two fields. Surfaced by the tail review of the frame for-source unit, 2026-09-22.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A loop variable bound by TWO `iter_next` loops takes one loop's source-form spelling for both.** [`frame-shared-loop-var-source-form-last-wins`] `for c in it_a: yield c.v` then `for c in it_b: yield c.v` over two user iterables in one frame declares `::tpy::frame_slot<::tpy::for_elem_next_t<__for_src_1_t>> c;` (the second loop's) and the first loop's advance writes through it; where the two sources lend differently (one hands back a reference, one a fresh value) the first loop's bind is ill-formed. `source_form_fields` in `_frame_layout` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`) is last-wins, where the pointer-form payloads of the same layout are joined (`const_join_t`). Fix shape: join the two spellings the same way (a `frame_slot` over the common form), or give each loop its own field. Pre-existing on master (the same last-wins), surfaced by the tail review of the frame for-source unit, 2026-09-22.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, located) A tuple-typed unpack TARGET over an iterator source in a frame is refused.** [`frame-unpack-tuple-target-local-storage`] `for i, p in enumerate(zip(xs, ys)): yield i + p[0] + p[1]` in a generator stops with `res.local_storage`: `p` is a `tuple[int32, int32]` bound from the step result's member, and the frame has no field form for a tuple member handed out of a step result (the value-tuple local arms admit a bind from a name or a call, not from an unpack). The flat twin `for i, (a, b) in ...` is not Python-legal at a `for` head in TPy's parser either way; `for a, b in zip(xs, ys)` and `for i, v in enumerate(reversed(xs))` compile. - **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A tuple-unpack `for` over `zip` of a list with `T | None` record elements fails the C++ build in an ORDINARY function.** [`zip-unpack-optional-record-element`] `for p, k in zip(a, b): out.append(p.v if p is not None else -1)` at `a: list[N | None]` -> `cannot convert 'std::optional<N>' to 'N*' in initialization`: the unpack target is spelled as the pointer-repr Optional (`N*`) but bound straight from the combinator's tuple member, which is the STORAGE optional. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A NESTED generator expression as a comprehension or genexpr SOURCE rejects on both forms.** [`genexpr-nested-source`] `any(x > 1 for x in (y * 2 for y in xs))` -> `(expr.genexpr)`; `[x for x in (y * 2 for y in xs)]` -> `(expr.list_comp)`. Fix shape: an owned-rvalue arm like the generator-call one -- the inner genexpr's frame is a one-pass `next_iter_mixin` object, so the outer comp's `auto __obj_N = <inner>` capture drives it like a combinator, and the outer genexpr's frame builds it in place as its source. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `for v in d.values(): t += v` at `d: readonly[dict[int32, int32]]` is a sema error: "Augmented assignment value must be a numeric type, got readonly[int32]".** [`readonly-value-element-leak`] The dict view stubs spell their value as `auto_readonly[V]`, so a readonly receiver types the element `readonly[int32]` -- but a VALUE element is copied into the loop var, and the readonly marker means nothing on a copy; sema's numeric checks do not peel it. The THIR lowering peels it for the loop-var binding and the comprehension / genexpr result slots (`_peel_value_readonly`, `tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py`), so `sum(v for v in d.values())` and `[v for v in d.values()]` compile at a readonly receiver; only sema's own operator checks still see the marker. Either sema-side fix DELETES the three lowering peels (the `_peel_value_readonly` call sites in `_source_route`, the genexpr unpack head and the comprehension unpack head), which exist only because sema hands the marker down. - **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A comprehension unpack head over a dict `items()` view (or any proxy-tuple combinator) with an all-scalar tuple binds `auto& __tup_N = *__beg_N;` to a PRVALUE.** [`comp-unpack-prvalue-tuple`] `[k + v for k, v in d.items()]` at `dict[int32, int32]` fails the C++ build with `cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type 'std::tuple<const int&, const int&>&' to an rvalue` -- the items iterator's `reference` is a proxy tuple returned by value (`ordered_map::tuple_items_iterator_impl`), and sema's `const_loop_var` (`worth_const_ref`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) is False for a value tuple that is not expensive to copy, so the emit picks `auto&` instead of the `const auto&` that binds a prvalue (`dict_comp_unpack` passes only because its str value makes the tuple worth a const ref). (A genexpr's frame has no such bind: its unpack holder points at the step result in the frame's own slot.) - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, masked) A generator expression whose SOURCE CALL needs a hoisted argument temp rejects, where the comprehension over the same call compiles.** [`genexpr-source-needs-arg-temp`] `sum(v for v in make(Box(8)))` with `def make(b: Box[int32]) -> Own[list[int32]]` -> `(expr.genexpr)` (the landmark face; the inner reason is the no-temps arg gate), while `[v for v in make(Box(8))]` compiles and hoists `Box<int32_t> __tmp_1 = Box<int32_t>(8);` ahead of its statement -- the `@nocopy` ctor temp a by-reference param needs. `_lower_genexpr_frame` lowers its source with no temp right (`tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py`), while the comprehension route threads `allow_temps=True` (its source renders at statement level; `docs/COMPREHENSION_DESIGN.md` documents the asymmetry). An owned source renders inside the in-place factory lambda, which captures by reference, so a temp flushed ahead of the enclosing statement is reachable from it wherever the position has a flush point. A generic factory's scalar literal arg (`make(8, 3)` at `n: T`) hoists no temp and works on both forms. Fix shape: thread the enclosing position's temp right into the source lowering, so both forms admit the same arg shapes. Workaround: bind the argument to a local first. Probe `/tmp/agents/review_genexpr_fix/arg_temp_box.py`. Found reviewing the genexpr rvalue-source unification 2026-09-13.

- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A lazy combinator that OWNS a user-iterable temporary with a separate iterator cannot be moved into another owning consumer.** [`separate-iter-temp-no-flush-slot`] `zip(Noisy(2), xs)` with `def __iter__(self) -> Own[Cur]`: where the position has a statement-level slot and the temporary is a constructor or free-function call, tpyc binds it to a local and the combinator BORROWS it (`argtemp.separate_iter_source`), staying movable. Everywhere else -- a nested call argument, a member init, a genexpr's source, module level, an `and`/`or` operand, a method / static-factory / field-of-temporary source -- the combinator owns the record in place and is PINNED (`detail::owned_iter_source`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/itertools.hpp`: its `__iter__` is user code that runs at the call and the iterator may point into the record), exactly the pre-2026-09-18 behaviour. A pinned combinator handed to another OWNING consumer in such a position (`print(list(enumerate(zip(h.make(), xs))))`) fails the C++ build with a deleted move ctor, as every owning combinator nested in another did before they became movable; the GENEXPR face (`enumerate(a * b for a, b in zip(Noisy(2), xs))` -- a genexpr's source never has a slot, so its combinator is always pinned) is a located reject instead, `genexpr.pinned_into_owning`, pinned by `tests/cases/iterators/error_genexpr_pinned_into_owning`. Rare on three axes; zero occurrences in the test corpus and the stdlib. Workaround: bind the object first (`n = h.make()`). Closes when "Producers are movable only while unstarted" (TODO.md) gives the pinned kind a movable form.

Fix shape: emit a non-template frame struct after the inline definitions of the records whose deduced dunders its slots spell, or spell the slot from a declared return. Found 2026-09-26.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) An `Iterable[T]` parameter consumed only by a builtin (`list(xs)`, `sorted(xs)`, `sum(xs)`) stays `const T&`, so handing it a generator or an iterator fails the C++ build.** [`iterable-param-builtin-consumer-stays-const`] `def show(xs: Iterable[str]): print(list(xs))` with `show(words())` or `show(iter(ws))` renders `void show(const T_xs& xs)`, and the construct template then advances a `const` generator: g++ `passing 'const __gen_words' as 'this' argument discards qualifiers`. A record with a `const` `__iter__` (a `Bag` over a list) works. Fixing it changes the signature of every such param (`const T_xs&` -> `T_xs&`), so it wants its own branch. The `self` face: a method `def joined(self): return ",".join(self)` on a class whose `__iter__` returns a stored iterator (`return self.it`, a non-`const` `__iter__`) is inferred `const`, because the native consumer's slot records no receiver mutation, and `::tpy::__iter__(const Pairs&)` finds no overload (probe `/tmp/agents/dd/r46d/parity/o2.py`); a comprehension over `self` in the same class demotes the method and works. - **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (silent CPython divergence, pre-existing) A generator's or `async def`'s `for` over an object whose `__iter__` returns a STORED iterator copies that iterator into the frame.** [`frame-stored-iter-copied`] `class Src: def __iter__(self) -> Cnt: return self.it` (a member iterator, not `self`) then `def gen(s: Src): for x in s: yield x`: the frame's iterator slot is a value (`iter_type_t`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dunder.hpp`), so `list(gen(s))` yields every value, leaves `s.it` unadvanced, and a second `list(gen(s))` yields them all again, where CPython advances the stored iterator and the second pass is empty (`genfor [2, 1, 0] 0 []` in CPython; probe `/tmp/agents/dd/r46/parity/p16f.py`; the const-reference face is `readonly-iter-result-iterated-as-copy`). An `async def`'s `for` is the same frame loop and copies the same way. A second face, same slot: an `__iter__` returning ANOTHER object of its own class (`return self.others[0]`) passes for a self-iterator by type (`is_self_iterator_v` compares types), so the frame drives the source's own `__next__` and steps the wrong object (`genfor [4, 3, 2, 1, 0] 0 2` where CPython prints `[1, 0] 5 0`, probe `/tmp/agents/dd/r46c/codegen/s1.py` in its generator form; master behaves the same). Statement-scoped consumers (a comprehension, `sorted`, `sum`, `list()`, a plain `for`) are right on both faces. Aliasing the stored iterator from a frame (a pointer slot) is blocked on `BUGS.md#frame-iter-loan-blind-to-caller`: a frame keeps the alias across suspensions, and until a caller holding a live frame over `s` is barred from invalidating `s`'s stored iterator (growing the list it lives in, rebinding the field), the alias could dangle. Found 2026-09-26.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (rejects-valid, located) A generator expression over a user iterable or an `Iterable[T]` / `Iterator[T]` parameter is rejected, where the comprehension over the same source compiles.** [`genexpr-over-user-iterable`] `any(s == "a" for s in b)` over `class Bag: def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[str]` -> `genexpr.iterable_shape` (pinned by `tests/cases/iterators/error_genexpr_user_iterable`), and the same over `xs: Iterable[str]`. A genexpr is a frame: its source is captured by the frame and iterated through `resumable_iter_init` / `resumable_iter_next` across pulls, so admitting one needs everything a frame's loop over such a source needs: (1) a frame that ALIASES a stored iterator instead of copying it (`frame-stored-iter-copied`, which needs `frame-iter-loan-blind-to-caller`); (2) self-iterator detection that sees through protocol and generic slots and inheritance -- `is_self_iterator_v` is a C++ type test, so an inherited `__iter__ -> Base` slices and a generic `-> T` returns a reference that is not recognized, and a source behind a protocol param or a generic `T` is not visible to the compiler at all (round-3 probes `/tmp/agents/dd/r46c/parity/q1.py`, `safety/q4.py`, `q5.py`, `g1.py` copied); (3) the self-iterator `__iter__` call (`frame-for-skips-self-iterator-iter`). Admitting a borrow needs a durability verdict that follows the borrow any number of calls down: `pick(Holder().get())` lends `Holder()`'s storage through two calls, and a one-level check on `pick`'s operands passes it, a use-after-free (probe `/tmp/agents/dd/r46c/codegen/c1.py`). - **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence, pre-existing) An `__iter__` that mutation inference marks `@readonly` hands its iterator back as a CONST reference, so a combinator or a frame iterates a copy, and a statement loop fails the build.** [`readonly-iter-result-iterated-as-copy`] `class Wrap: def __iter__(self) -> Cur: return SHARED` (a module-level `Cur`): the method never mutates `self`, is inferred readonly, and renders `const Cur& __iter__() const`. Nothing can pull through a const reference, so three things happen by consumer: the lazy combinators copy it (`detail::iter_cursor` in `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/itertools.hpp` / `detail::iter_member_t` in `dunder.hpp`), and `zip(Wrap(), xs)` leaves `SHARED.i` at 0 where CPython reads the advanced count; a generator's or `async def`'s `for` copies it into the frame's iterator slot (`iter_type_t`, the same copy as `frame-stored-iter-copied`), so `gen(w)` yields every value and leaves `SHARED.i` at 0 where CPython reads 3 (probe `/tmp/agents/dd/r46b/parity/a1.py`); and every statement-scoped loop fails the C++ build loudly (`passing 'const Cur' as 'this' argument discards qualifiers`) rather than step a copy -- a comprehension, `sorted`, `sum`, `list()` hold the reference through `::tpy::iter_range` / `iter_of`, and a plain `for` binds `auto&& __itr = ::tpy::__iter__(src)` in its own `__iter__`/`__next__` loop.   class Pet: pass
  class Cat(Pet): pass
  class Dog(Pet): pass
  def give_union(d: readonly[Dog]) -> Pet | Cat: return d

- **[HIGH medium] (silent divergence) A generator without cleanup can resume after an exception escapes its body.** [`generator-resumes-after-escaping-exception`]
  In `def stream() -> Iterator[int]: yield 1; yield fail(); print("continued"); yield 3`, where `fail()` raises `ValueError`, retain the iterator and catch that error around the second `next()`. CPython leaves it exhausted: the next pull raises `StopIteration`. TPy instead executes `print("continued")` and yields `3`. The generated frame stores the post-yield resume state before evaluating the throwing expression; `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py` only emits the enclosing catch that marks `S_DONE` when `_dtor_cleanup_cases(cfg)` is nonempty. This emitter behavior is unchanged from session base `2bd8dec8b6`; the standalone witness imports no math and uses no nested records. Confirmed with native g++-14 execution and CPython in `/tmp/agents/session-triage/generator_exception_reuse.py` (logs `generator-reuse-native.log` and `generator-reuse-cpy.log`). Found during math propagation review; cleanup-bearing generators and coroutine siblings require their own audit. Since 2026-09-23 the entry case stores `S_DONE` before any body code, so an exception escaping before the FIRST yield finishes the generator; one raised while evaluating the first yield's own operand (`yield risky(0)` -- the resume state is stored before the operand runs) or after any resume still resumes. Storing `S_DONE` at the top of every resume case, or evaluating a yield's operand before storing its resume state, is the fix shape. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
