The shape behind it -- a `str` member's borrow-form alternative being a pointer to owned storage instead of the view -- is a design item in TODO.md (Type System, "borrow form of a union whose member is a view-param value type"); closing that absorbs this entry.


- **[LOW small] (warned, not rejected) A constructor member-init source that CALLS a method on `self` may read a field not yet initialized.** [`ctor-mil-self-method-source-unready-field`] `self.a = self.size()` in `__init__` before `self.n = n` hoists into the member-init list and `size()` reads `n` before it is set; sema warns `instance method called in __init__ before all fields are initialized`, and the 2026-09-04 member-init ordering gate (`mil_done_fields` in `tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`, which rejects a direct read of a not-yet-hoisted own field) deliberately does not treat a `self.method()` source as a read of every field, because that would turn every warned ctor into a hard reject. Whether the warning is enough is a language call; the gate is the place to escalate it.

- **[LOW small] (loud divergence) A slice bound that is a `BigInt` outside the int32 range panics `int32 overflow` where CPython clamps.** [`slice-bound-bigint-outside-int32-panics`] `xs[2:1000000000000]` reads and, since 2026-09-04, slice-assigns narrow the bound with `to_fixed_check<int32_t>()`, so an out-of-range bound is a runtime panic rather than a clamp to `len(xs)`; the read path always did this, the write path previously rejected at compile time. Fix shape: clamp a BigInt bound to the container length before narrowing, as the runtime's `BasicSlice` does for in-range values. A second face: a BigInt STOP variable with a list RHS on a slice ASSIGN emits ill-formed C++ (`template argument 2 is invalid`) rather than a panic.

- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) A subclass of a builtin container that declares no `__init__` emits `using <base C++ type>::<PYTHON name>;`.** [`inherited-ctor-using-spells-the-python-name`] `class MyBA(bytearray): pass` emits `using std::vector<uint8_t>::bytearray;`, which g++ rejects ("'bytearray' has not been declared in 'class std::vector<unsigned char>'"). `_cpp_base_name()` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) does not consult the TypeDef's `cpp_formatter`, so for a formatter-carrying builtin base the injected-class-name half of the `using` is the PYTHON name; the record emitter's comment (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/records.py`) says it derives that half "from the C++ side", which holds only for `@native`-renamed records. Only `bytearray` reaches it today: its zero-argument constructor makes `MyBA()` legal to sema, while the `list`/`dict`/`set` flavours stop earlier (sema demands the base constructor's argument and the call then rejects at `call.ctor_arg.protocol.static`). A subclass that declares its own `__init__` emits no `using` and builds -- that shape is `tests/cases/calls/stub_receiver_shapes`. Pre-existing (identical before the bytearray receiver fold, which only changed which reject the method CALL got); found 2026-09-05.
- **[MED small] (loud runtime panic on valid code) `sum()` over a `bytearray` accumulates in `uint8_t` and panics on the first overflow where CPython returns the exact sum.** [`sum-over-bytearray-overflows-uint8`] `sum(bytearray(b"\xff\xff"))` panics `uint8 overflow in addition` where CPython prints `510`: `builtin_sum<T>` deduces its accumulator from the ELEMENT type and `add_check<uint8_t>` traps, so any bytearray whose bytes total more than 255 is unusable. The accumulator should widen the way CPython's does (an `int32`/`BigInt` result for a narrow integer element), which is a stub/runtime signature question, not a lowering one. `bytes` has the same shape. Pre-existing for the bare NAME spelling; the FIELD spelling (`sum(self.buf)`) became reachable 2026-09-05 with the native-Iterable arg rows. Loud, not silent. Found by /tpy-review of the container-family fold. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) `bytearray(n)` with a runtime `BigInt` size emits `::tpy::bytes_from_size(n)` against a fixed-int parameter.** [`bytearray-size-bigint-unnarrowed`] Same family as the slice-bound narrowing closed in batch 3: a BigInt at a fixed-int native slot needs `to_fixed_check<int32_t>()`. Found 2026-09-04 in the doom example.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) `.copy()` on an `Array[T, N]` receiver emits `::tpy::list_copy`, which has no `std::array` overload.** [`array-copy-dispatches-to-list-copy`] `xs = [3, 1]; ys = xs.copy()` -- the unmutated literal resolves to `Array[int32, 2]` and the method resolves to the `list` stub, so g++ reports `no matching function for call to 'list_copy(std::array<int, 2>&)'` with no TPy location. Both spellings are affected: the assigned one is identical on master, the DISCARDED one (`xs.copy()` as a bare statement) reached a located `method.ret_type` reject on master and reaches the same broken call since 2026-09-05. The fix is the receiver's method resolution -- an Array receiver needs the array copy render, or the resolution must refuse the list stub -- not a family re-check at the result-shape row. `tests/cases/list/discarded_container_result` keeps its receiver a `list` on purpose (it appends) so it does not sit on this. - **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) `list(b)` on a bytearray rejects at `call.inst_arg_shape`.** [`bytearray-ctor-field-and-list-conv`] Adjacent bytearray rows met while pinning the bytearray return; neither has an oracle problem, they are plain missing arms. The third row is CLOSED since 2026-09-05: the TYPE-constructor spellings (`bytearray()`, `bytearray(seed)`, `bytearray(n)`) route, because `_container_storage_field` no longer demands type arguments and so admits the one non-generic reference container (`tests/cases/records/container_ctor_field_init`). - **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) An UNMUTATED list literal local returned inside a tuple at an `Own[list[T]]` element slot spells its Array.** [`array-literal-in-own-tuple-return`] `def f() -> tuple[Own[list[float]], int32]: a = [1.0, 2.0]; return a, 1` -- `a` resolves to `Array[float, 2]` and the return emits `std::tuple<std::vector<double>, int32_t>{std::move(a), 1}` from a `std::array`, which g++ rejects; sema accepts the Array-to-list-slot pairing. - **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) A comprehension over `d.items()` fails the build -- for a reference VALUE type and for a scalar one alike.** [`comp-dict-items-ref-value`] `[v.bump() for k, v in d.items()]` over `dict[int32, Node]` (and `{k: v + 1 for k, v in d.items()}` over `dict[int32, int32]`, repro `/tmp/agents/bug_comp_selfassign/p2/p_dict_plain.py`) emits `auto& __tup_1 = *__beg_0;`, binding a non-const lvalue reference to the view's rvalue `std::tuple<const int&, Node&>`; g++ rejects it. `d.items()` is a dict-view source, not a combinator, so the combinator route's element-form rule does not reach it; the unpack head needs `auto&&` (or the `tuple_elem_ref` normalization the for-statement uses). Found by the batch-2 closing review while probing the fence. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A comprehension over a SUBSCRIPT element source rejects where the `for` statement lowers.** [`comp-subscript-element-source-rejects`] `out = [v for v in rows[0]]` with `rows: list[list[int32]]` rejects at `expr.list_comp`; `for v in rows[0]:` lowers through the for-each's container-ELEMENT arm (`auto& __obj_N = ::tpy::__getitem__(rows, 0);`). Sema already files the element loan for both (`register_iteration_loans`, `tpyc/sema/iter_loans.py`), so the missing piece is the comprehension lowering's iterable admission. Found 2026-09-22 while fixing the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A comprehension over a two-hop FIELD chain source rejects.** [`comp-field-chain-source-rejects`] `ys = [x for x in self.a.xs]` in an ordinary method rejects at `expr.list_comp`, where CPython prints `w1 1` (probe `/tmp/agents/rv1-fix/compf4.py`, re-run 2026-09-24). When the entry was filed the `for` statement over the same source lowered, and so did a comprehension over a one-hop source; those two were not re-checked. Not consuming-method specific. Sibling of `BUGS.md#comp-subscript-element-source-rejects`, and the fix is in the same place: the comprehension lowering's iterable admission. Pre-existing; found 2026-09-23.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud; pre-existing) An unannotated NESTED list literal passed straight to `enumerate` finds no overload.** [`enumerate-nested-pending-literal`] `for i, cs in enumerate([[Cell(1)], [Cell(2), Cell(3)]]):` fails with *No matching overload for enumerate(PendingList[PendingList[Cell, 1]#0, 2]#2)* (`/tmp/agents/compsrc/b9/a.py`; identical at 64feef9932): the pending element type of the outer literal is not settled before overload resolution matches the `Iterable[T]` slot. Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; pre-existing) An `Own`-returning call whose result is a NESTED container cannot be stored as a container element.** [`own-nested-container-call-as-element`] With `def mk() -> Own[list[list[Cell]]]`, `t = [mk(), mk()]` rejects at `expr.container_literal` and `t.append(mk())` (into `list[list[list[Cell]]]`) at `expr.method_call:method.arg_shape` (`/tmp/agents/compsrc/b9/b.py`, `c.py`; identical at 64feef9932). The one-level form (`Own[list[Point]]` elements) lowers and moves, per `BUGS.md#generic-container-elem-from-call-rejected`, so the element-slot admission of a storage call rvalue appears not to see an owning return whose element is itself a container of containers; unverified whether the literal and the `append` share one gate. Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; everyday shape) A COMPREHENSION that mutates through its loop variable over a PARAMETER keeps the parameter const, and the build fails.** [`comprehension-loop-var-mutation-not-propagated`] `def f(ns: list[Cell]) -> list[int32]: return [n.bump(1) for n in ns]` renders `const std::vector<Cell>& ns` and dies with *passing 'const Cell' as 'this' argument discards qualifiers*; the same with a combinator source (`[n.bump(1) for n in filter(pos, ns)]`, `[n.bump(x) for n, x in zip(ns, xs)]`). The `for` statement's twin demotes `ns` (a loop var carries `loop_var_iterable` / the ITER loan, and a write through it climbs to the source), but the comprehension route (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`, `_enter_comp_scope`) installs no source provenance for its loop variable at all, so nothing there climbs -- over a local or a field the write compiles because those are never const. Fix shape as first filed: the comprehension's loop variable registers the same iterable provenance the for-statement registers (`register_iteration_loans`, `tpyc/sema/iter_loans.py`, and the `loop_var_iterable` record `_register_foreach_iter_loans` makes from it), so the mutation climb is one rule for both routes -- which the design notes below show is not enough on its own: that record is keyed by name and a comprehension target can shadow its own source's root. Pre-existing and untracked before 2026-09-22 (found by the review of the combinator element-form unit; the comprehension sections of `tests/cases/builtins/combinator_elem_off_source` iterate locals and fields for this reason). The implicit-dunder spelling is the same gap: `[c[k] for c in cs]` with `cs: list[Counts]` and a mutating (`@readonly(False)`) `__getitem__` credits the call to the loop variable `c`, which has no provenance to climb to `cs`, so `cs` stays const and the build fails exactly as with `c.bump()`.
  Design notes (2026-09-23): the comprehension-loan branch folded this in and then cut it after nine review rounds; every round from the second found a crash, a silent divergence or a use-after-free in it, all in the propagation layer. The fold-in recorded the comprehension variable's sources in `loop_var_iterable` (the for-each registration's own fact), so a write through the target climbed to the source, and a lend rule marked enclosing loop variables mutable. What the next attempt has to answer: (1) `loop_var_iterable` is keyed by NAME, and a comprehension target can shadow the ENCLOSING binding its own source is rooted at (`[n.bump(1) for n in n.kids]`, `sum([sum([sum([n.pop() for n in m]) for m in n]) for n in ns])`, `[n[1].bump(1) for n in zip(n.kids, others)]`): the entry becomes self-referential, the climb through `mark_param_mutated` / `mark_param_structurally_mutated` recurses without end (a compiler crash), a cycle guard turns it into a MISSING mark, and dropping a self-named entry drops its other keys too (`/tmp/agents/rv_arch9/p2.py`-`p4.py`). A cross-target shape (`for a in xss: sum([b.bump(1) + a.v for a, b in zip(ds, a)])`, `/tmp/agents/rv9_safety/c1.py`) is a loud build failure at master as well. The fact wants a binding identity (a `Place`), not a name. (2) Marking an enclosing `for` variable mutable from a comprehension write turns that loop CONSUMING over a last-use local while a borrow of an element outlives its block (`BUGS.md#consuming-loop-outlived-by-loop-var-borrow`; `/tmp/agents/rv9_safety/a1.py`, `a2.py`: `own_iter(std::move(hs))` and a dangling tuple capture), and a comprehension variable that shadows an enclosing loop variable leaks its write and consume marks to it (the untagged "Foreach scope binding" entry); a snapshot/restore of the shadowed name's facts closes that leak but also breaks the self-named shapes master builds only THROUGH it (`/tmp/agents/rv8_parity/sf`, `f`, `/tmp/agents/rv8_codegen/q4.py`), so the two have to land together. (3) A `for` unpack target's rebind writes into the element (`BUGS.md#borrow-unpack-target-rebind-writes-through`), which any lend to its source turns silent. Instrument: the write-route x loop-shape x source matrix in `/tmp/agents/compsrc/m4/` (`gen.py` generates the cells; `fe.py`, `build.py`, `maperr.py`, `cmp.py` classify them against CPython). A `.clone()` face of the same gap: `def clone_all(src: list[Rc[Node]]) -> Own[list[Rc[Node]]]: return [x.clone() for x in src]` keeps `src` const and fails the build.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A generator expression over an enclosing loop variable that writes through its own loop variable, or through its capture of it, leaves the outermost PARAMETER const, and the build fails at the frame creation.** [`genexpr-over-loop-var-param-stays-const`] `def f(css: list[list[Cell]]) -> int32: return sum([sum(c.bump(1) for c in cs) for cs in css])` renders `const std::vector<std::vector<Cell>>& css` while `cs` binds `auto&&`, so passing `cs` to the frame's `std::vector<Cell>&` source parameter discards qualifiers (`/tmp/agents/rv2_parity/p4.py`, `nest_gx_in_comp`; identical at 64feef9932). The creation (`_check_loop_var_arg_mutation` in `tpyc/sema/calls.py`) marks its loop-variable argument only as a MUTATED LOOP VAR, which fixes `cs`'s binding; the parameter it was iterated out of is reached through `mark_param_mutated`'s `loop_var_iterable` climb, and the frame's source mutation arrives as a call edge keyed on caller PARAMETERS, which a loop variable is not. The `for` twin fails the same way (`for cs in css: n += sum(c.bump(1) for c in cs)`, `/tmp/agents/rv_docs3/s.py`; identical at 64feef9932), so both spellings do (a comprehension-in-comprehension spelling is `BUGS.md#comprehension-loop-var-mutation-not-propagated`). A mutating CALLEE over the inner loop variable is the same class: `for cs in css: for c in cs: push(c)` (with `def push(c: Cell) -> int32` writing `c.v`) and its enumerate and zip spellings leave a PARAMETER `css` const and fail the build, while a local source builds (measured 2026-09-23 across every nested-loop head, `/tmp/agents/compsrc/m4/`). The CAPTURE form is the same class: `for xs in xss: t += sum(1 for _ in range(1) if grow(xs))` and `for r in rs: n += sum(1 for _ in range(1) if rename(r))` leave the parameter `xss` / `rs` const (`/tmp/agents/rv10_parity/pd_d10.py`, `pg.py` G5/G6). Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A write through a NESTED loop variable or `for` unpack target made inside a nested def does not reach the loop-variable write set, so the enclosing loop variable keeps `const auto&` and the build fails.** [`loop-var-write-routes-miss-write-set`] `for cs in css: for c in cs: def f() -> None: c.v += 1` then `f()` (and `def g() -> int32: return c.bump(1)`; the enumerate / zip head spellings alike) fails with *passing 'const Cell' as 'this' argument discards qualifiers*, at 64feef9932 as on the branch, for a parameter and a local source. The nested-def replay re-enters the enclosing function only through `mark_param_mutated` (`_analyze_nested_def`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`), and the loop variables' write set (`mutated_loop_vars`, filled by `mark_loop_var_mutated`) -- what the `for` statement's rule (`_iter_source_root`, which marks the loop variable its source is rooted at) reads -- is not fed from there. A walrus alias is the same gap (`if (d := c).v > 0: d.bump(1)`; a mutating call on the walrus itself is `BUGS.md#walrus-receiver-write-not-rooted`), and the callee / genexpr routes with a parameter source are `BUGS.md#genexpr-over-loop-var-param-stays-const`. Instrument: the write-route x loop-shape x source matrix in `/tmp/agents/compsrc/m4/` (`gen.py` generates the cells; `fe.py`, `build.py`, `maperr.py`, `cmp.py` classify them against CPython). History: a walrus bind-time mark (the `d = c` rule applied to a walrus target) was also tried and removed -- the walrus target is a function-scoped pointer, so a mark that turns an enclosing last-use loop consuming leaves it dangling. Feeding the write set from the write-through climb (`mark_param_mutated` calling `mark_loop_var_mutated`) was tried on the comprehension-loan branch and reverted: it also fired on the ADDRESS-TAKEN mark of a tuple capture (`t = (c, 1)`, which turned a last-use loop consuming and left `t` dangling -- `BUGS.md#consuming-loop-outlived-by-loop-var-borrow`) and on the generic-slot mark (`BUGS.md#generic-slot-marks-arg-mutated`, a per-element copy or a lost `const`). The fact has to be recorded where a write THROUGH the name is certain, not where any mutable use of it is. Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[MED medium] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A write through a NESTED `for` loop variable reached via a combinator or an unpack head (`for cs in css: for i, c in enumerate(cs): c.bump(i)`, the `zip` and `filter` spellings) does not make the outer loop variable mutable, and the build fails.** [`for-nested-write-via-combinator-head`] The `for` statement's rule that a mutated loop var marks the loop var its source is rooted at (`_iter_source_root` in `tpyc/sema/context.py`) finds no root through a combinator call, and a tuple-unpack head's synthetic loop var is marked mutated unconditionally, so it cannot tell a written target from a read one either. A comprehension in a `for` body writing through its own target (`for row in grid: t += sum([c.bump(1) for c in row])`) fails the same way, as the comprehension half of `BUGS.md#comprehension-loop-var-mutation-not-propagated`. Making the `for` route lend through combinators and unpack heads was tried in rounds 2-6 of the comprehension-loan branch and reverted, because two pre-existing defects turn every such lend unsound: (1) a rebind of a `for` unpack target writes into the element (`BUGS.md#borrow-unpack-target-rebind-writes-through`; fix = the loop-head unpack-target rebind reject, a USER decision, or a re-seatable target binding), and (2) a mutable outer loop var over a last-use local turns the loop consuming while a borrow of an element outlives its block (`BUGS.md#consuming-loop-outlived-by-loop-var-borrow`; `for h in hs: for i, x in enumerate(h.items): x.bump(1); last = (x, i)` read `last` from freed storage). Both must be fixed first. Instrument: `/tmp/agents/compsrc/m4/` (the write-route x head x source matrix, plus the write+rebind and consuming cells); every `for` cell must match 64feef9932 until then. Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence; pre-existing) A `match ... case X() as c:` capture rebinds a reference-typed LOOP VARIABLE `c` without the loop-variable reassignment reject.** [`match-capture-rebinds-loop-var`] `for c in cs: c.v += 1; match other: case Cell() as c: c.v += 1` compiles and writes into the list element (the capture assigns through the loop var's reference), where `c = other` in the same place is refused with *Cannot reassign loop variable 'c' of type 'Cell'*; silent at 64feef9932 (`/tmp/agents/rv6_parity/d1.py`). The reassignment check (keyed on `loop_vars`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`) is asked at the var-decl rebind only, not at a match capture binding an existing name. Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid wording, loud) A walrus rebinding a reference-typed LOOP VARIABLE is refused with the generic walrus message, whose remedy the loop-variable rule then refuses.** [`walrus-rebind-loop-var-message`] `for c in cs: if (c := other).v > 0:` fails with *walrus reassignment of non-value local 'c' is not supported yet; use a separate assignment statement*, and the separate `c = other` it suggests is itself *Cannot reassign loop variable 'c'* -- the walrus path never asks the loop-variable check (loud at 64feef9932 as on the branch; `/tmp/agents/compsrc/r6b/wl.py`). Fix shape: ask the loop-variable reassignment check before the generic walrus one. Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A read-only alias of a `for` UNPACK target over a const source binds a mutable reference.** [`unpack-target-alias-drops-const`] `for i, c in enumerate(cs): d = c; t += d.v + i` over `cs: list[Cell]` (unmutated, so `const std::vector<Cell>&`) renders `Cell& d = c;` and fails with *binding reference of type 'Cell&' to 'const Cell' discards qualifiers*, nested or flat; the plain-loop twin `for c in cs: d = c` renders `const Cell& d` (`/tmp/agents/rv6_codegen/p6.py`; identical at 64feef9932). The alias's const-ness follows the loop var's own binding for a plain loop var, but an unpack target's binding form comes from the unpack, not from the source's const-ness. Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) An `async def` with no `await` nesting `for i, c in enumerate(row)` inside `for row in grid` declares the inner loop's source frame slot from `decltype` of `row` before `row` exists.** [`async-nested-for-src-slot-order`] The frame declares `frame_loop_slot<__for_src_0_t>` with `__for_src_0_t` spelled off `decltype(... row)`, ahead of the outer loop's own slot, so `__for_src_0` is undeclared and the build fails (`/tmp/agents/rv6_codegen/p1b.py`, `async_nested`; identical at 64feef9932 per the round-6 codegen review). Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A tuple capturing a `const`-bound loop variable is spelled with a MUTABLE pointer element, so the capture fails the build.** [`tuple-capture-of-const-loop-var`] `for c in cs: last = (c, 1)` then `last[0].v += 5` (and `t = (h, n)` inside a `for h in hs:` whose `h` stays const) renders `std::tuple<Cell*, int>` and fails with *invalid conversion from 'const Cell*' to 'Cell*'* / *no matching function for call to 'std::tuple<Cell*, int>::tuple(...)'*, at 64feef9932 as on the branch (`/tmp/agents/rv8_parity/`, `/tmp/agents/rv7_safety/p1.py`). The write through the captured element is not credited to the loop variable (whose binding stays `const auto&`), while the tuple's element type is the mutable pointer form. When the loop variable IS mutable over a last-use local, the same capture is `BUGS.md#consuming-loop-outlived-by-loop-var-borrow`. Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan. The WALRUS twin: `if (t := (p, 1)): return t` with `p` a const-inferred parameter spells `std::tuple<P*, int32_t>` for the walrus local and fails in g++ the same way (`/tmp/agents/par/w1.py`, 2026-09-23; it used to stop at the Own-element return error). A container sink reaches it with no write at all: `for p in ps: t = (p, 1); r = [t]` over a `ps: list[P]` parameter fails g++ at the capture (*invalid conversion from 'const P*' to 'P*'*) after the element-copy warning (probe `/tmp/agents/b2fix/lv.py`, 2026-09-24). The CALL-ARGUMENT twin needs no loop and no write: `def f(r: A) -> int: return g((r, r))` with `r` a const-inferred parameter and a NON-mutating `g(p: tuple[A, A])` renders `g(std::tuple<A*, A*>{&(r), &(r)})` against the `const A&` binding and fails the build (*invalid conversion from 'const A*' to 'A*'*), for a SYNC callee, in a generator body (`for x in h((r, r))`) and through a keyword (`pair(p=(a, b))`) alike (probes `/tmp/agents/u1frame/r_t_e_sync.py`, `r_t_e.py`, `/tmp/agents/sm_r2/kw.py`, re-measured 2026-09-26). Its root is not the tuple element's provenance (a MUTATING callee, `bump((a, 1))`, has built since 2026-09-26, when the element started to lend like its scalar twin) but the literal's spelling: the callee renders the parameter `const std::tuple<const A*, const A*>&` from its `const_borrow_params` verdict, while the call-argument tuple-literal arm (`_lower_borrow_tuple_literal` from the tuple-slot branch of the argument lowering, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) picks the REF capture unless the slot is spelled `readonly`, so a const source cannot fill it. Fix shape: pass `target_readonly` there when the argument's index is in the callee's `const_borrow_params` too. The loop-variable spelling `for c in cs: bump((c, 1))` over a `cs` parameter now binds `c` mutable and fails at the const parameter exactly as the scalar `bump1(c)` does (the entry "Param mutation inference does not reach a LOOP ELEMENT" further down).
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; pre-existing) A mutating method called on a WALRUS expression does not reach the aliased storage.** [`walrus-receiver-write-not-rooted`] `def f(x: Cell) -> int32: return (d := x).bump(1)` renders `int32_t f(const Cell& x)` and fails the build, at 64feef9932 as on the branch (`/tmp/agents/compsrc/r9/wr.py`). The receiver-root walker `_root_name_of_expr` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) stops at a `TpyNamedExpr`, so the method-call mutation mark has no root, and the walrus binding marks nothing either (`BUGS.md#loop-var-write-routes-miss-write-set`). Fix shape: let the walker see through a walrus to its value's root. Measured: that also moves `tests/cases/control_flow/walrus_alias_sources` (`readonly_recv(x: Rec)` with `(p := x).get()` goes from `const Rec&` to `Rec&`, which is what the direct twin `x.get()` already renders for a `get` not declared `@readonly`), so it needs that pin re-examined. Found 2026-09-23 by the review of the comprehension iteration loan.

- **[MED small] (accepts-invalid, silent) A NESTED def drops the keyword-only marker, so a positional call CPython rejects compiles and runs.** [`nested-def-kwonly-marker-dropped`] `def outer(): def kwonly(x: int, *, k: int) -> int: ...; kwonly(3, 2)` -- CPython raises `TypeError: takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given`; TPy accepts it. Same root as `nested-def-default-ignored`: the nested-def `ParamInfo` carries no signature metadata (defaults, kw-only, arity) beyond the positional list. Found 2026-09-04 while adding the ignored-default warning. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, both paths) A hook-mode `match` capture of a REFERENCE type into a resumable frame slot is an emplaced COPY, so a mutation through the capture across a suspension never reaches the caller.** [`resumable-match-capture-frame-emplace-copies`] Anchor for the "Resumable-path variant" paragraph of the match-binding entry further down, which carries the shape, the `13 3` vs `13 13` witness, what THIR fences today and the fix shape (a pointer frame slot, borrow form). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (silent wrong data / double free, accepted on master; REGRESSION since v0.5.0, which copied) A comprehension whose element is a movable or record NAME at its last use moves it INSIDE the loop, so iterations 2..N use a moved-from object.** [`comp-element-move-inside-loop`] `ls = [b for i in range(2)]` with `b` a `Box` compiles, then aborts with `free(): double free`; with a plain record `r` it prints `9 1` where CPython prints `9 9`; `return std::move(b)` is emitted per iteration. The list-repeat path already guards this one-source-N-slots hazard with `suppress_move`; the comprehension element path does not. Pre-existing (identical on the pre-deletion emitter), found by the batch-2 review. **Tuple face** (2026-09-24): a tuple LOCAL that owns every element, `t = (P(1), P(2)); ys = [t for _ in range(2)]`, renders `__result.push_back(t);` -- a copy per item rather than a move, so nothing is moved from, but each item holds its OWN two objects where CPython stores the same two in every item: `a0, b0 = ys[0]; a0.xs.append(5); a1, b1 = ys[1]; len(a1.xs)` prints 1 under TPy and 2 under CPython, with no warning (probe `/tmp/agents/b2fix/comp_tuple.py`). A local holding BORROWED elements warns the per-element copy of those elements only; its OWNED elements copy per item silently too: `t = (P(5), p); ys = [t for _ in range(2)]` warns `tuple element 1` and prints 1 where CPython prints 2 through element 0 (probe `/tmp/agents/b2me/n2.py`). The container-element warning's per-element rule (`only=` the borrowed indices) is right at a true last use; inside a comprehension the read is not one, which is this entry's root. **Argument face** (2026-09-29): an `Own` parameter passed to an `Own` slot inside the element, `def many(b: Own[Box]): ys = [take(b) for _ in range(3)]` with `take(b: Own[Box])` storing `b`, renders `take(std::move(b))` inside the loop, so the second and third calls get a moved-from `Box`: TPy prints `[3, 0, 0]` where CPython prints `[3, 3, 3]` (probe `/tmp/agents/abf/p_c5.py`). A value payload (`Own[str]`) copies into a temp first and is not affected. Where the faces stand: the vector and iterable routes of a comprehension body (element, key, value, filter) move no name bound outside it (`lc.moves_only`, `tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py`), at a local, a field write and a constructor member-init, so their moved-from items are gone -- but each item is a COPY with no copy warning, because sema still reads the element's read as a last use: `self.xs = [p for _ in range(3)]` with `p: Own[P]` in a member-init or a method, then a mutation through the first item, prints `9 1` / `8 2` where CPython prints `9 9` / `8 8` (probes `/tmp/agents/abf/r5/cp/cp.py`, `/tmp/agents/r4review/parity/p7.py`), and a dict-comp value from a local record `{i: q for i in range(2)}` prints `2 1` where CPython prints `2 2` (`/tmp/agents/r4review/parity/p8.py`); a name the element does not read last (read again in the filter, or a borrowed param) copies WITH the warning. The `range(<literal>)` ARRAY route (`_lower_array_comprehension`, `array_from_index`) still MOVES an outer name per index: `ls = [q for i in range(2)]` leaves the second item moved-from (`fixed []`, CPython `[6]`, probe `/tmp/agents/r4review/cg/p20.py`; `2 0` where CPython prints `2 2`, `/tmp/agents/docsync_r3/c3.py`), where `range(n)` over the same name copies. The Own-slot ARGUMENT row decides from the `Own` parameter itself and still moves it once per iteration. Fix shape for every face: a read inside a comprehension element (or any loop body) of a name bound outside it is never a last use -- sema's fact, so every sink gets it. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`; fix before `BUGS.md#tuple-local-last-use-copies-owned-elements`, whose move-at-last-use fix would otherwise turn this silent copy into a use-after-move. A `@nocopy` outer name on the vector / iterable routes (`self.xs = [b for _ in xs]`, a dict-comp value, a filtered comprehension, `W(b)` as the element) is ACCEPTED by tpyc and then fails the C++ build with a deleted-copy-constructor error and no TPy diagnostic: the lowering emits `push_back(b)` where master emitted a per-iteration `std::move(b)` (a use-after-move that compiled). Fix for every face at once: in `tpyc/liveness.py`, a read of an outer name inside a comprehension body is never a last use (the rule lambdas and nested defs already have), so sema gives the `@nocopy` error and the copy warning and the three routes agree; the lowering's `moves_only` wraps then go.
- **[MED small] (silent drop, now warned) A parameter DEFAULT on a NESTED def is ignored: the lambda takes every argument, and a call relying on the default is rejected with an arity error that never mentions the default.** [`nested-def-default-ignored`] `def outer(): def scale(v, k=2): ...; scale(5)` -- identical on the pre-deletion emitter. Since batch 2 sema warns that the default is ignored (`tests/cases/nested_def/param_default_unused`); the fix is either to honour the default at closure call sites or to reject the def. Re-found 2026-09-26 analysing parameter-default provenance: `def outer(): def inner(b: int32 = 3) -> int32: ...; return inner()` fails with `'inner' expects 1 argument(s), got 0` where CPython prints `3` -- the nested def's signature is registered without its defaults (repro `/tmp/agents/dflt_file/nested.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (accepts a shape it then cannot render; sema asymmetry) Keyword arguments to a NESTED class constructor are not normalized into positional order.** [`nested-ctor-kwargs-unnormalized`] `Inner(v=1)` is normalized by sema; `Outer.Inner(v=1)` is not, so the THIR ctor arm has nothing to render and rejects (`tests/cases/calls/error_nested_ctor_kwargs`). The normalization should not depend on the callee's spelling.
- **[LOW small] (spurious warning, both paths) "Own[T] param 'a' is never consumed" fires when the param is moved into a returned container literal.** [`spurious-alias-warnings-select-and-own-literal`] `tests/cases/generics/generic_list_literal_elem` carries the warning annotated.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; the oracle SEGFAULTED) A module-scope union global initialized to `None` first -- `g: A | B | None = None` -- rejects at `top_level.global_slot_shape`.** [`global-union-none-first`] The pre-deletion emitter wrote the monostate through the still-null slot pointer (`(*g) = std::monostate{};`), built, and died with exit 139, so there is no render to mirror. The sibling shapes (a record or container rvalue, a field source, a subclass upcast) route since 2026-09-04 (`tests/cases/globals/global_slot_source_shapes`); this one needs the slot allocated before the None store. Related: a union global written from a SCALAR global name (`u: int32 | Point = n`) also rejects, where the oracle emitted `int32_t*` into a `std::variant<int32_t, Point>*` and failed the build. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; oracle ill-formed) A nested def capturing a NARROWED union name does not lower.** [`nested-def-narrowed-union-capture`] `nesteddef.narrowed_capture` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`): the pre-deletion emitter referenced the narrowing alias inside the lambda without capturing it (`'__u' is not captured`). The lambda needs the alias in its capture list, or the narrowing re-derived inside. The TPy `lambda` sibling took the second half of that fix on 2026-09-15 -- `_capture_entry_cpp` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) now spells the entry from `lc.narrow.narrowed`, and rejects a `spelled` (poly `(*__p_ptr)`) subject -- but only in the NON-ESCAPING (`Fn`) lane, whose entry is `&<alias>`. The escaping (`Callable`) lane over a reference-typed member rejects instead (`escaping-capture-of-narrowed-subject` below), so the capture-list shape is settled for the by-reference mode only; what remains here is the nested def's own list, whose ref/move modes have no alias form yet. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; the oracle read the walrus target UNINITIALIZED) A condition mixing a walrus and a hoisted temporary -- `if (m := g(n)) > take(m):` -- rejects at `if.mixed_walrus_temps` / `while.mixed_walrus_temps`.** [`cond-walrus-before-hoisted-temp`] The pre-deletion emitter hoisted `__tmp_1 = take(m)` ABOVE the walrus assignment, so the call saw `m` before it was written; the reject replaces silent garbage. The condition-temp flush must order the walrus store before any temp that reads its target (the walrus rows in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` are the place). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) A `match` `as` capture of a `str` from an `Optional[str]` subject returned at a `-> str` slot has no view-to-owned conversion.** [`match-str-capture-owned-return`] `match s: case str() as got: return got` emits `return got;` with `got` a `std::string_view` into a `std::string` return slot. Same family as `select-narrowed-optional-view-params-owned-sink`; `tests/cases/match/optional_inner_chain_guard` returns `"got:" + got` to sidestep it.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, sema misses a readonly violation) A COMPREHENSION loop variable over a `readonly[list[T]]` passed to a mutating consumer is not checked.** [`comprehension-loop-var-readonly-unchecked`] `def f(items: readonly[list[P]]): [bump(v) for v in items]` with a mutating `bump` passes sema (the for-statement form is rejected) and emits `bump(const P*)`, which g++ rejects. Same for `readonly[list[P | None]]` with an Optional-narrowed loop var. Pre-existing on master through the non-Optional form; the THIR fence that hid the Optional form went with the 2026-09-04 comprehension rows. The `for` statement projects `readonly` onto the loop variable of a readonly iterable (the `TpyForEach` arm of `StatementAnalyzer._analyze_stmt_dispatch` in `tpyc/sema/statements.py`, "Elements from a readonly iterable inherit readonly status"); the comprehension resolves its element type through `unwrap_readonly` (`_resolve_comp_iterable`) and never does. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, pre-existing on both paths) A value select over two NARROWED `Optional[bytes]` / `Optional[str]` params at an owned sink skips the materializing copy.** [`select-narrowed-optional-view-params-owned-sink`] `def f(a: bytes | None, b: bytes | None) -> bytes: if a is not None and b is not None: return a or b` tags the select STORAGE while both operands render views, so the return emits a `span` into a `std::vector` slot (`string_view` into `std::string` for the str twin); g++ rejects both. `_view_at_runtime` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) has no Optional-deref arm, while the sibling if-expression row (`_bytes_view_arm` / `_str_view_arm`) does and emits `bytes_copy` correctly -- the fold of the three runtime-view predicates the closing review of 2026-09-03 asked for closes this. Same in kind on the pre-deletion AST emitter.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; pre-existing in sema) A NESTED def's container param never gets the const-borrow verdict, and its non-const `T&` propagates to the ENCLOSING function's param and to the enclosing method's inferred `@readonly`.** [`nested-def-container-param-drops-const`] `def outer(xs: list[int32]) -> int32: def inner(v: list[int32]) -> int32: return len(v); return inner(xs)` emits `int32_t outer(std::vector<int32_t>& xs)` where the same body without the nested def infers `const std::vector<int32_t>&`; the lambda param renders `std::vector<int32_t>& v` unconditionally (`_lower_nested_def`, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`; the top-level path goes through the const-borrow verdict). Consequences: a `readonly[list[T]]` name or a `self.field` from a `@readonly` method cannot be passed to a non-mutating nested def, and a method whose only container use is through a nested def loses its inferred `@readonly`, so `def use(b: readonly[Bag]) -> int32: return b.total()` is rejected with `Cannot call non-readonly method 'total' on readonly reference`. Identical on the pre-deletion AST emitter, so sema-side (mutation inference never seeds a lambda param), but user-reachable only since 2026-09-03 when the nested-def container-param arm landed (master hard-rejected the shape). Fix shape: run nested-def params through the same const-borrow verdict as top-level params and let the verdict feed the enclosing function's inference. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) `xs.append(a or b)` into a `list[bytes]` rejects at `expr.method_call:method.arg_shape`.** [`bytes-select-into-method-arg`] The value select over two `bytes` params materializes correctly at every other owned sink (return, field, local) since 2026-09-03, but the method-arg table (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) has no row for a view-spelled select result at an owned-bytes element slot; the pre-deletion AST rendered `xs.push_back(::tpy::bytes_copy(...))`, so the render exists to mirror. Same table gap as `copy-str-view-result-into-owned-arg`. A repetition result has the same gap: `ys.append(b"Z" * 40)` into a `list[bytes]` rejects at the same tag (probe `/tmp/agents/r1a/bapp.py`), where a bytes literal argument lowers.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) The explicit dunder call `b.__eq__(b"xy")` with a bytes LITERAL argument rejects at `expr.method_call:method.ptr_template.arg_shape`, while the operator spelling `b == b"xy"` routes and the str twin `t.__eq__(s)` routes.** [`dunder-call-bytes-literal-arg`] The `record_template` argument ladder has no bytes-literal arm at a span slot; the operator row retags the literal through `_bytes_literal_view_slot` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`). One method, two spellings, two verdicts -- the class the TODO "dunders as named members" item removes wholesale.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `case x as y` -- a whole-subject `as` over a plain capture -- rejects on the record, union and optional-record `match` tiers.** [`match-as-capture-composite-tiers`] `match r: case x as y:` on a record subject, `match u:` on a `Cat | Dog` subject and `match o:` on an `Optional[Box]` subject all die at `stmt.match`; the scalar, chain, str-switch and poly tiers bind both names since 2026-09-03 (`THIRMatchArmEntry.pre_bindings`, case `tests/cases/match/scalar_arm_shapes`), and the inner-scalar face of the optional tier (`Optional[int32]`) routes through the scalar switch. Each composite tier composes its binding against an extraction alias (`__case_i`, `__match_inner_N`, a field base), so the second binding needs a per-tier rhs decision rather than the shared whole-subject one; the resumable hook mode and `case (x as y) as z` reject on every tier. The record tier is pinned by `tests/cases/match/error_as_capture_record_tier`; the union and Optional-record tiers have no pin. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; was ill-formed C++ on both paths) An `or` / `and` select over `bytes` operands whose runtime spellings differ rejects.** [`bytes-select-mixed-runtime-spelling`] With `a: bytes` a PARAM (a `::tpy::BytesView` at runtime): `v = a or f()`, `f() or a`, `a and f()`, `a or b"zz"`, `b"" or a` all reject at `binop.shape.||` / `binop.shape.&&` (detail `valuesel.bytes_mixed`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`), the same shape the if-expression row already rejects as `ifexpr.bytes_mixed`. The pre-deletion AST rendered every one ill-formed (`std::vector<uint8_t>` initialized from a span, or a span bound over an owned temporary -- dangling as well as ill-formed), so there is no render to mirror; the bytes family has no one-argument conversion in either direction, unlike the str arm's `std::string(sv)`. Measured against the oracle's own output with g++: param vs owned local is a hard compile error in either order (`vector` from `span`); `a or b"zz"` compiles but the literal arm DANGLES (a span over `bytes_literal_owned`'s temporary); `b"zz" or a` is valid (the literal is hoisted). An owned LVALUE against a view has a valid render the oracle never emitted (`(cond ? ::tpy::BytesView(c) : a)` -- spanning a live local), so closing that pair is a new mixed-pair cast rule, a decision. Same-spelling operands route, including two params at an OWNED sink (return, `Own[bytes]` return, record field -- materialized with `view_to_owned_conv`, i.e. `::tpy::bytes_copy(...)`, since the closing review of 2026-09-03; before that the select took its form from the result type and dropped the copy) and a still-view param against a REBOUND param (`b = bytes([113]); v = a or b` composes a span over the live owned local, safe). A rebound param against an owned local or a literal (`b = bytes([113]); c = bytes([1, 2]); v = b or c`, `v = b or b"xy"`) REJECTS: `_view_at_runtime` keeps answering "view" for a reassigned param on purpose -- an arm that answered "owned" from the reassignment facts was tried on 2026-09-03 and made `b or b"xy"` a same-spelling pair whose view result dangled over the vector temporary (ASan use-after-free, no diagnostic), so the reject stays until the mixed cast takes its direction from the sink (TODO "view-family mixed-operand cast direction"). One more face of the name-keyed answer: inside an `async def` a `bytes` param lives in the coroutine frame as an OWNED field (`is_owned_in_coro_frame`, no reassign prologue), so `a or c` against an owned local rejects as a mixed pair there although both operands are vectors at runtime. Found 2026-09-03 by the batch-1 review's bytes spelling matrix.

- **[MED small] (accepts-invalid at sema; was a SILENT divergence at the operator spelling) A comparison whose operand does not match the record dunder's declared parameter passes sema for the derived `!=`, the reflected `==` and the plain `==`.** [`derived-ne-unchecked-operand`] `t != n` with only `__eq__(self, other: str)`; `t == 2.5` with `__eq__(self, other: int32)` (printed True where CPython prints False); `t == 300` with `other: uint8` (C++ wrapped the literal, again True vs False). `t.__eq__(2.5)` IS a sema error (`Type mismatch in argument 'other'`), so only the operator spellings skip the check: `_validate_comparison` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) confirms the dunder EXISTS and records no resolution, so THIR's operand row (`_record_dunder_operand_pair`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) cannot tell "deliberately unresolved" from "overload resolution failed". Since the 2026-09-03 batch-1 review that row gates the operand on sema's own arg-compatibility predicate (`is_type_compatible`) and REJECTS a non-compatible one with a located diagnostic (`binop.shape.<op>.record` at the enclosing statement, e.g. `stmt.expr_stmt:binop.shape.==.record`), so the divergence is closed and the shape is loud but misattributed to codegen; the sema fix must cover the same-family slot mismatch (`int32` slot vs `float` operand, `uint8` slot vs `300`), not only the missing-overload case. The gate mirrors sema exactly, so `c == True` against an `int32` slot now also rejects (the explicit `c.__eq__(True)` is a sema type error) although the old bare render happened to agree with CPython; a value-preserving bool-to-int admission is sema's call, not the row's. The permanent fix is sema recording the resolved dunder (and its arg check) on the node for every operator spelling; the TODO cutover follow-ups carry that item.

- **[LOW small] (misattributed diagnostic) A user `__setitem__` call whose value parameter is a plain record warns "copies X into container" at the CALL SITE, although the parameter binds `const X&` and nothing is copied there.** [`setitem-copy-warning-at-call-site`] `s[0] = z` with `def __setitem__(self, index: int32, value: Data)` emits `::tpy::__setitem__(s, 0, z)` -- a by-reference pass -- yet sema reports `copies Data into container; use copy() to make this explicit` on that line. The copy, if any, is the callee's own field write (`self.a = value`), which sema already warns about on ITS line (`copies Data into field`), so the call-site warning double-reports and points at the wrong line; a user following it adds a `copy()` at a site that copies nothing. The warning is right for a BUILTIN container store (`xs[0] = z` on a `list[Data]`), which is where the wording comes from; the user-`__setitem__` path should not reuse it. Witness: `tests/cases/records/setitem_record_value_slot` pins the warning as emitted. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) A NUL `char` is falsy in a boolean context, where CPython -- and this project's own documented rule -- make every `char` truthy.** [`char-nul-truthiness-diverges`] `nul = char("\0")` followed by `if nul:` takes the ELSE branch under TPy and the THEN branch under CPython. `char` lowers to C++ `char`, and the condition renders as the bare `if (nul)`, which is C++'s `!= 0` test -- so the one code point whose integer value is zero flips. `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` puts `char` in the str-like family (`len(c)` returns 1) and states the truthiness rule for that family as `__len__() != 0`, which is constant-true for a `char`; CPython agrees, since a length-1 `str` is always truthy. So the C++ side is the wrong one, not the stub. Silent: no diagnostic fires, and the divergence is invisible to a test that never uses NUL. Reachable wherever a `char` comes from parsed or binary input -- a NUL terminator, a padding byte, a `chr(0)` sentinel -- which is exactly where a scanner would test it for emptiness. Both paths render identically, so this is not a lowering artifact. Fix shape: render a `char` condition as the constant-true form the str-like family already uses (evaluating the operand for its side effects), rather than falling through to the scalar `!= 0` test. Repro `/tmp/agents/grind2/probes2/char_truthy.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) `functools.reduce` COPIES its accumulator, so a function that mutates the accumulator in place loses the mutation.** [`reduce-accumulator-copied`] `reduce(add, [1, 2, 3], seed)` where `add(a: Acc, b: int32)` does `a.total += b; return a` prints `6 0` under TPy and `6 6` under CPython -- the reduction's own result is right, but the caller's `seed` was never touched. `lib/tpy/functools.py:20` opens with `acc: U = copy(initial)` (and the no-initial overload with `copy(a[0])`), where CPython's `reduce` aliases the seed and hands the same object to every call. Silent: no warning fires, because the copy is written explicitly in the stdlib body. **PRE-EXISTING.** Fix shape is a decision, not a patch -- the `copy()` is what gives the loop an owned local to rebind, so aliasing the seed means the accumulator has to be a borrow of the caller's value and the `Own[U]` return has to go, which changes `reduce`'s signature. In-place accumulation is a normal use of `reduce`, so the divergence is reachable without doing anything unusual. Re-confirmed 2026-09-15 on 0.6.0.dev0 (`/tmp/agents/fn_doc_probes/p_reduce.py`: `6 0` vs CPython's `6 6`). Designed resolution: `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md`, later slice **D2** -- the seed's fate is a parameter-position question, not a result-form one, so slice 1 leaves `functools.reduce` untouched and this entry open. D2 makes the consuming fold explicit (`Fn[[Own[U], T], Own[U]]` with `initial: Own[U]`, the accumulator round-tripping by move, which is also the only shape that works for a `@nocopy` accumulator) and designs a Python-compatible `reduce` SEPARATELY: CPython's borrows the seed initially, may own later results, and returns the seed itself for empty input, so respelling the seed `Own[U]` alone would consume it in the functional form too (`reduce(lambda a, x: a + [x], xs, seed); print(seed)`), trading this divergence for a use-after-move on a correct program. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `import math` does not compile at `--default-int BigInt`.** [`math-hypot-bigint-slice`] A program whose only import is `math` fails with `lib/tpy/math.py:144: error: in function 'hypot': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:subscript.slice_shape)`. The blocking line is `for c in coords[1:]:` over a varargs `*coords: float` param -- the slice-source shape has no lowering arm at that iteration position when the default int is BigInt. `int32` and `int64` both compile the same module, so the reject is keyed on how the slice bound renders, not on `hypot` itself. A whole stdlib module being unreachable at one `--default-int` setting is worse than the single missing arm suggests: nothing in `math` is usable, whether or not the program calls `hypot`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) `[r] * n` over a reference-type element COPIES each element and, unlike the sibling spellings, warns about nothing.** [`list-repeat-reference-elem-copy`] `rows = [r] * 3` then `rows[0].n = 99` leaves `rows[1].n` and `r.n` unchanged under TPy; CPython puts the SAME object in every slot, so all three see the write. The neighbouring spellings diverge identically -- `[r, r]` and `append(r)` also copy -- but both emit `copies Row into owned storage; use copy() to make this explicit`, so a reader is told. The repeat form emits no diagnostic at all, which makes it the one spelling where the value-vs-reference decision is invisible. **PRE-EXISTING.** The CONSTRUCTOR position is the same row one sink over: `self.rows = [r] * 3` in `__init__` lands the identical `from_range(repeat_range(..))` render in the member-init list and is likewise unwarned, so the family now has a silent face inside the ctor as well as at a local and a field write -- name all three when the warning is added. Minimum fix is that missing warning at the repeat row, so every spelling says the same thing; whether the repeat should instead ALIAS is the same question the sibling spellings raise and should be settled once for the family, not per row. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. Fourth sink (2026-09-04): the list-repeat admitted as a COMPREHENSION element (`[([c] * 2) for _ in range(2)]` prints `99 1 1 1` where CPython prints `99 99 99 99`, unwarned; `tests/cases/list/comp_element_list_repeat` covers value elements only). Still to be settled once for the family, not per row.

- **[LOW small] (silent wrong output) A fixed-int constructor over an INT-kind type parameter skips the range check.** [`int-tparam-ctor-unchecked`] `uint8(N)` inside `class Buf[N: int]` instantiated as `Buf[300]` emits the bare `return N;` -- `N` is a `std::size_t` non-type template parameter, so the implicit conversion truncates to 44 with no diagnostic, where the same constructor over a runtime `int32` would emit `::tpy::int_cast_check<uint8_t>`. Sema resolves the same-width `__init__(self, x: uint8)` overload (template `{0}`) because an INT type param matches any fixed int, and that overload is the one with no check. **PRE-EXISTING** and identical on both emit paths -- THIR mirrors the AST render, so no gate sees it. The value is a compile-time constant, so the fix can be a compile-time range diagnostic rather than a runtime check. Surfaced by the safety review of the INT-type-param ctor-arg lowering. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud) A record / container ternary is refused at several positions.** [`reference-ternary-position-gaps`] Two NAME arms, or one existing-object arm beside a fresh one, lower at a local binding, a method receiver and the transient consumers (an operand, a print argument, a non-retaining call argument), and -- as the plain prvalue `?:` with the copy warned -- at an `Own[T]` argument, a container insert, an `Own` return, a field write and a ctor member-init. Refused WHATEVER the arms: a mutable-reference argument (`mut(a if c else b)`, `call.arg_shape.record_f1` / `.container`); a native protocol argument whose arms are not both NAMEs (`len(a if c else mk())`, `call.native_arg.container` -- `_container_ternary_arg` is NAME-only); a field read off the ternary (`(a if c else b).n`, `field.receiver_shape`); a reassignment or a binding inside a `try` body (`decl.reseat_source`); a `for` head (`iter.if_expr_shape`); a subscript receiver whose arms are not both NAMEs (`_lvalue_container_ternary`); a FIELD arm (`w.a if c else b`, `field.result_type`). Refused only for the MIXED pair, because its fresh operand lives in a slot hoisted before the statement and admitted only where that slot provably outlives the consumer (`_select_slot_ok`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`; `expr.ifexpr` detail `ifexpr.ref_mixed_position`, `valuesel.ref_slot_position` for `a or make()`): a position whose statement writes its own lines before declaring pending slots -- a `for` head, an `assert` condition, a `with` item, a `match` guard, a `return` in a generator or async body (the frame skeleton splices it into its block and declares pending slots after that block; an owned async return of a mixed ternary takes the prvalue form and still lowers, `return a or C(5)` does not) -- and one with no statement at all -- a lambda body (the placement half of `_select_slot_ok`: the sink's flush right or a statement kind listed in `_SLOT_HOIST_STMTS`); an argument the callee keeps (an awaited coroutine's, a generator factory's); a coercion of the select (a `Span` / view taken of it); a method receiver whose result may borrow it (`.me()`, a view, an iterator, a generator or async method -- `method.recv.select_slot_lend`); a name reassigned from it, or a local that would own a copy of it (the existing arm would be copied where CPython binds it); an all-fresh select of generator frames at a local (`g = gen(1) if c else gen(10)`, `decl.slot_type`, as on master -- a frame has no prvalue slot spelling); a list-comprehension element; a tuple or container literal element (a mixed record member of a returned tuple is warned as a copy into owned storage before the lowering refuses it); an `Own[@dynamic P]` return mixing a name and a call (`make() if flag else q`, only records take the prvalue form; sema refuses it first, as a non-copyable payload at the `Own` slot); a module-level binding (`top_level.global_slot_shape`, a warned copy before). A local binding of a mixed pair in a generator or async body (an all-fresh select lowers there) is refused earlier, at the frame's alias bind (`res.alias_bind`), for the both-name ternary and `x = a or b` too (a warned copy before, for a mixed container pair). Frames need the alias and the slot as frame fields; module level needs a namespace-scope slot; a comprehension element and an owned-copy local could take the prvalue form (`SinkForm.SELECT_PRVALUE`) with the copy warned. Probes `/tmp/agents/ternmix/q/`. Found fixing the mixed-category ternary.

- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (destructor timing) A select used only for its value keeps its fresh operand alive to the end of the enclosing block.** [`select-slot-extends-fresh-lifetime`] `print("v", (a if c else mk(7)).get()); print("after")` prints `v 7 / after / del 7` where CPython prints `del 7 / v 7 / after`: the fresh operand lives in a slot declared before the statement, which the block owns. - **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output) An escaping closure MOVES a captured local that is not the sole name for its object, emptying storage something else still reads.** [`escaping-closure-moves-shared-local`] Two shapes the declaration-init alias test (`_capture_aliases_other_storage`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) does not see: a `with h as x` target (the binding is not a `TpyVarDecl`, so it keeps the owner verdict and `[x = std::move(x)]` moves the caller's object out -- CPython `k5 2 2`, TPy `k5 1 1`), and an OWNER `x` captured while an alias of it (`y = x`) is used afterwards (`y.append(3)` then writes a moved-from vector -- CPython `k9 3`, TPy `k9 2`). - **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output; pre-existing) An ESCAPING nested def over an `Own[T]` PARAM captures it by move although the enclosing body reads the param afterwards.** [`escaping-closure-moves-own-param`] `def escaped(x: Own[Point])` with `def size() -> int32: return len(x.items)` handed to a `Callable` field (`h = Holder(size)`) renders `auto size = [x = std::move(x)]() ...`, and the later `print("read", len(x.items))` reads the moved-from param: TPy `read 0`, CPython `read 3`; a later consume of `x` forwards the empty object. `_finalize_nested_def_escapes` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) moves every `Own[T]` param capture of an escaping closure unconditionally, while the local twin asks `names_used_after` and copies with a warning (`[x]`, correct). - **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning; pre-existing) A nested def returning a CAPTURED name into an `Own[T]` return copies it silently.** [`nested-def-captured-own-return-copies`] `def outer(x: Own[Box]) -> int32: def g() -> Own[Box]: return x`, then `y = g(); y.n += 1; return x.n + y.n` renders `[&x]() -> Box { return x; }`, a copy of the captured object, so TPy prints 3 where CPython prints 4 (`y` is `x`), and no copy warning fires. - **[MED small] (silent wrong output) A reference-type local that owns its storage, rebound from an existing object, copies the object where CPython rebinds the name.** [`owned-local-rebound-from-lvalue-copies-silently`] `x = [1] or [2]` (or any fresh init that makes `x` own a `std::vector`), then `x = a` or `x = a or mk()`, then `a.append(5)`: TPy's `x` is a copy and misses the append (`len(x)` 1 where CPython prints 2), with no diagnostic. The TUPLE-UNPACK head stops at lowering with a located reject -- `for name, num in pairs: pass` then `yield name` gives *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (res.local_storage)*, pinned as `tests/cases/generators/error_gen_head_unpack_after_loop`. A REFERENCE-typed head target takes the same failure, and the `for`/`else` idiom that makes one definitely-assigned does not change it: `for x in make_cells(): break` / `else: raise ValueError("empty")`, then `yield "sep"` and a write `x.v = 77`, emits the write in the resume block against a head target declared only in the loop's own block -- *'x' was not declared in this scope*, with `make_cells()` a temporary or a named list alike (verified 2026-09-21, `/tmp/agents/verify_loopsrc/code/a2_loopvar_break.py` and `a3_loopvar_lvalue.py`; the frame reserves a field for the target, so only the declaration in the later blocks is missing). Without the intervening `yield` the read is in the loop's own state block and the program compiles and prints `2/4`, so the suspension is the trigger. The SYNC twin of both spellings compiles and prints `b/9` / `2/4`, matching CPython (verified 2026-09-20; probes `/tmp/agents/review_hoist/meta/q4_innerloopvar.py` and the two-function sync twin `def sync_unpack_head(): pairs = [("a", 7), ("b", 9)]; for name, num in pairs: pass; return f"{name}/{num}"`). Same class as [`resumable-comp-walrus-scope`] -- a binder whose target never enters the frame layout plan -- with the `for` head as the binder. **Fix shape:** a `for`-head target read after the loop is a binding of the enclosing body, so the frame layout must claim it like any other local read across a suspension; the single-target and tuple-unpack heads take one rule. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid code) A `@dataclass` with a `bytes` field cannot be compiled: the generated `__repr__` has no way to render it.** `uv run tpyc` on `@dataclass class P: x: bytes; n: int` fails with `No matching overload for repr(bytes)` reported at the DECORATOR line, while CPython runs the same program fine. The `@dataclass` class macro synthesizes a `__repr__` over every field, and `repr` has no `bytes` overload -- so declaring the field is enough to break the module, whether or not anything ever reprs it. Note the error's location is the decorator rather than the field, which sends a reader to the wrong line. Two plausible fixes: give `repr` a `bytes` overload (CPython renders `b'z'`, so there is a spelling to match), or have the macro skip/degrade unrepresentable fields -- the first is the better one, since the second would make `repr` silently lossy. Surfaced while writing a `match` field-pattern case that happened to use a `bytes` field on a dataclass; the case was rewritten with a plain record class to sidestep it. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (confusing diagnostic) Two `match` diagnostics on the SAME recursive-alias subject print it two different ways.** `'case None:' requires None to be a member of the union subject; got '<expanded>'` (`tpyc/sema/match.py:1077`) renders the internal stand-in -- e.g. `int32 | list[Tree[int32]]` -- while the member-check four lines below names the subject as the user wrote it (`Tree[int32]`), because it reads `stmt.subject_type` where this one reads the local `subject_type`. A reader hitting both sees two type names for one value and no indication they are the same thing; the expanded spelling also leaks a representation the source never mentions. **Confirmed pre-existing** (both spellings behave identically at the branch point), but the sibling was just changed to the user-facing form, so the inconsistency is newly visible and newly owned. No case covers it. Fix shape: read `stmt.subject_type` here too, and check the file for other arms still printing the local. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready second opinion of the body-diagnostic re-homing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A recursive type alias whose union names `None` directly is rejected at PARSE time, while the generic spelling of the same type is accepted.** `type Nest = None | list[Nest]` fails with `Recursive type alias 'Nest' must use a union form ...`: the parser canonicalizes `None | list[Nest]` into an optional and then no longer sees a union to recurse through. `type Tree[T] = T | list[Tree[T]]` instantiated as `Tree[None]` denotes the same type and compiles and runs (`tests/cases/match/union_recursive_none_leaf`), so the two spellings disagree on a type they agree on the meaning of. Same canonicalization class as the sema entry below -- a `None`-bearing union collapsing to an optional and taking a path meant for a different shape -- one layer earlier, so whichever fix lands should check the parser and sema together rather than treating them as separate. CPython accepts both spellings. Surfaced probing recursive-alias coverage while adding the newly-accepted match subject. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) No member of a recursive alias's LEAF UNION can be named in a `match` class pattern.** [`recursive-alias-leaf-union-member-unnameable`] `type Tree[T] = T | list[Tree[T]]` with `def describe(t: Tree[int32 | str])` rejects `case int32():` -- and equally `case str():` -- with `'<T>' is not a member of union '<alias>'`. The wrapper struct's `std::variant` carries ONE slot for the whole leaf union (`RecursiveAliasInstanceType.alternatives()`, `tpyc/typesys.py:3420`, deliberately does NOT canonicalize: it substitutes positionally so the variant ordering stays fixed), so a leaf member has no independent slot to dispatch on. The plain `UnionType` path has no such gap, so this is specific to a union at a recursive alias's parameter position. **Not a CPython parity divergence -- a capability gap.** CPython compiles and runs the program; it also does not take that arm, because `int32` is an `int` subclass while the literal is a plain `int`, so `case int32()` is False and the wildcard wins. TPy refuses to build a program CPython executes, which is the defect; matching CPython's *output* would additionally require deciding what a leaf-member pattern should mean. Fix shape: dispatch through the nested variant. **Wording, when this is fixed or while it stands:** the message is self-contradictory to a Python reader, since the union spelling it prints visibly contains the name it says is not a member; it should say the member sits inside the leaf union and has no variant slot of its own. Previously this shape was ACCEPTED by sema and rejected later by codegen's `_variant_index` (sema stood the subject in as a flattened `make_union(...)` that codegen never used); sema now builds the stand-in from `alternatives()` verbatim and rejects first, so the two sides agree and only the capability gap remains. Witness `tests/cases/match/error_recursive_union_union_arg`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) `open()` on a DIRECTORY succeeds instead of raising.** `open("/")` returns a file object under TPy and the surrounding `try` sees no exception; CPython raises `IsADirectoryError` (an `OSError` subclass), so a program with `except (PermissionError, OSError):` takes that arm there and falls through to the success path here -- the probe that found it prints `opened` where CPython prints `os-error`. Silent: no diagnostic, and the divergence only shows up in whatever the program does with the bogus handle. Passing a directory where a file was meant is an ordinary user error, and the whole point of the exception is to catch it at the boundary. Fix shape: have `open()` stat the path and raise `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, matching CPython's errno mapping. Repro: `try: f = open("/"); f.close(); return "opened" / except (PermissionError, OSError): return "os-error"`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (fact-check), re-running the sweep's fallback probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, at least two independent triggers) A `match` binds its dispatch subject to a borrow-form POINTER without dereferencing it.** Two shapes reach it, and they are not the same shape -- an earlier draft of this entry called it generator-only, which the second witness falsifies. **(1) A union-typed local inside a generator**: iterating `list[Dog | Cat]` and matching the loop variable emits `auto& __match_subject_1 = p;` where `p` is `std::variant<Cat, Dog>*`, then `__match_subject_1.index()` and `std::get<1>(__match_subject_1)` -- g++ rejects both ("request for member 'index' ... which is of pointer type", "no matching function for call to 'get<1>(variant<...>*&)'"). No generator, no union, no suspension. So the defect is in how the match subject binding decides to deref a pointer-repr subject, not in either lowering path specifically, and a fix scoped to the frame would leave the second witness standing. Both are front-end-clean and surface only at the C++ build, as STL overload noise naming neither the subject nor the match. Repro (2), the smaller: `def describe(x: Optional[Box]) -> str:` with `if x is not None:` then `match x: case Box(val=0): ... case Box(val=v): ...`. Repro (1): a generator over `list[Dog | Cat]` matching its loop variable with a `yield` in an arm. Surfaced by the pre-deletion adversarial dual-path sweep. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
