- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent wrong output) A local returned under a `finally` that MUTATES it and may also REBIND it loses the mutation.** [`finally-mutate-then-rebind-return`] `b = Box(1); try: return (b, 5) finally: b.n += 1; b = Box(9)` returns `n == 1` where CPython returns the original object mutated to `n == 2`; the scalar `return b` does the same. A finally that rebinds the returned name anywhere makes the return keep its eager capture (a deferred pointer would see the rebind), so the capture copies before the chain and the mutation is lost. The rebind need not execute (`finally: b.n += 1; if c: b = Box(9)` with `c` False: TPy 1, CPython 2 -- the SCALAR form of this untaken-rebind shape was correct before 2026-09-23, when a rebind anywhere in the finally started forcing the eager capture), the order does not matter, and the rebind may sit in an OUTER finally while an inner one mutates (probes `/tmp/agents/rv3r2/e/e23_cond_rebind_untaken.py`, `/tmp/agents/rv3r2/p3_rebind_forms.py` `outer_fin`; verified 2026-09-23). An `__add__`-style augmented assign in the finally (a record with no `__iadd__`) counts as such a rebind; an in-place one (`__iadd__`, list `+=`, set `|=`) does not -- except inside a NESTED def: a closure's `nonlocal a; a += 5` is counted as a rebind whatever its operator (the nested-def walk runs before sema resolves it), so an `__iadd__` record there loses the mutation too (TPy 1, CPython 6; probe `/tmp/agents/rv3r3/p/a3b.py` `selfi_nonlocal`). Fix shape: the pending deferred capture is a live alias of the local, so the alias-gated rebind pass (`tpyc/sema/alias_rebind.py`) gives the finally's rebind storage of its own and the deferral can stay; for the tuple member that needs tuples admitted by `is_reference_local`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. DESIGNED FIX (user 2026-09-23: file, do on its own branch after `u1-tuple-meds`): make the pending finally-deferred return a live holder of the captured local in `tpyc/sema/alias_rebind.py` -- a loan on the local that stays live through the enclosing `finally` -- so the pass stamps the `finally`'s rebind OWN (the local becomes a pointer local and the rebind takes fresh storage) instead of IN_PLACE; drop the eager-capture fallback for rebound names (`liveness.collect_finally_rebound_returns` and the `_decline_deferred_return` path) and have the deferred capture take the object the local currently points at (`auto* p = t;`, not `&t`), returning `std::move(*p)` after the chain. `alias_rebind` already admits record locals, so this covers a scalar `return t` and the record members of a returned tuple literal (`return (b, 5)`); a whole-tuple local and a frame slot wait on the tuple extension of `alias_rebind` (plan, U5 paragraph). Closes this entry, the `@nocopy` refusal (a `@nocopy` local returned under a finally that rebinds it -- `t += 5` via `__add__` or a plain rebind -- is rejected today because the eager capture would copy it; pinned by `exceptions/error_return_nocopy_rebound_under_finally` and `tuple/error_tuple_return_nocopy_rebound_under_finally`, which carry a TO-BE-FIXED note), and most of `BUGS.md#finally-rebind-eager-move-alias-read` (no eager capture left to move). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A borrow-tuple unpack inside a `with` body, or a `try` body with a `finally`, rejects at `stmt.tuple_unpack` (`tuple_unpack.target_form`).** [`try-finally-borrow-unpack-target-predeclared`] `try: x, k = g(b); x.n = 88` + `finally: print(b.n)` (for `def g(b: Cell) -> tuple[Cell, int]`) rejects, and so does `with Ctx() as v: x, k = g(b)`, where the same unpack at function scope, in an `if` / `match` arm / `@error_return` body and under `try`/`except` compiles and aliases. The targets reach `_standalone_unpack_target_binds` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) already in `declared` while sema still marks them `is_new` (verified 2026-09-22), and the borrow leg admits only a target that is fresh AND undeclared. Fix shape: a predeclared borrow target takes the pointer assign the for-head hoist spells (`x = &(::tpy::unwrap_ref(::tpy::tuple_elem_ref(std::get<i>(__tup))));`, the `frame_ptr_elem` render) over a pointer predecl, with its reads through `lc.pointers`. A third face with no `try` and no temporary (2026-09-28): the same borrow unpack bound in BOTH arms of an `if` / `else` and read after it (`if n > 0: b, k = pick(keep)` / `else: b, k = pick(keep)`, then `b.v = 7`) rejects with the same bare `stmt.tuple_unpack` -- the second arm meets targets the first arm predeclared. The `try` / `finally` face still reproduces with a plain local argument. Probes `/tmp/agents/ge/file/g_if_alias.py`, `g_try_only.py`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A tuple unpack that rebinds the same names in a second `try` body rejects at `stmt.tuple_unpack`, even over a scalar tuple.** [`second-try-tuple-unpack-rebind-rejects`] `try: x, k = pick(3)` / `except ValueError: ...` followed by `try: x, k = pick(4)` / `except ValueError: ...` (for `def pick(n: int32) -> tuple[int32, int32]`) stops at the second unpack with the bare *not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.tuple_unpack)*; CPython runs it. The same holds for `tuple[str, int32]`, for a reference element (`tuple[Cell, int32]`), and for the everyday socket face `conn, peer = srv.accept()` in two `try` blocks. Binding the names before a `try` and rebinding them inside it compiles, as does a scalar unpack in both arms of an `if` / `else` (verified 2026-09-29). Likely the same mechanism as `BUGS.md#try-finally-borrow-unpack-target-predeclared` (the second site meets targets the first one declared), but here it is not limited to the borrow leg. Probes `/tmp/agents/r3fix/int_twice.py`, `str_twice.py`, `unpack_twice.py`, `accept_twice.py` (controls `int_faces.py`).
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An rvalue argument at a METHOD's mutated reference parameter rejects at `expr.method_call:method.arg_shape`; the free-function twin compiles.** [`method-rvalue-arg-at-mutable-ref-param`] `h.mut(Cell(1))` for `def mut(self, b: Cell) -> None: b.n = 5` rejects, while `fmut(Cell(1))` for the same free function binds the argument temporary (`%argtmp`) and runs, and `h.ro(Cell(1))` at a readonly parameter compiles (verified 2026-09-22). An everyday call shape; the workaround is binding the argument to a local first. The reject is raised by the method-call arg gate (`_require_method_call_arg`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`); which free-call row admits the temporary there is not yet traced.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) An augmented assign through an `__add__`-only type on a reference LOOP target copy-assigns into the iterated element instead of rebinding the name.** [`borrow-unpack-target-rebind-writes-through`] `for v, k in zip(vs, ks): v += k` over `vs: list[Vec]` where `Vec` defines only `__add__` prints `[11, 22]` where CPython prints `[1, 2]`, and the plain loop variable does the same (`for v in vs: v += 1` -> `[2, 3]` vs `[1, 2]`; it slips past the plain loop variable's reassignment reject) (verified 2026-09-23 on `u1-tuple-meds`, probe `/tmp/agents/mm2/faces.py`). The other rebind faces this entry listed are fixed on `u1-tuple-meds`: a rebound unpack target is a pointer local (`x = q`, a chain `c = d = other`, a swap `a, b = b, a`, `a = b` between targets, standalone and at a single-level for head over a local or a param). Still open as loud C++ build failures (identical on master fd40895525): the NESTED for-head forms (`for cs in css: for c, k in zip(cs, ks): ...` with a rebind and a write, a match capture, `+=` on a list element; probes `/tmp/agents/rv6_safety/p1.py`, `p3.py`, `p10.py`, `/tmp/agents/rv6_parity/p1.py`, `e3.py`), which lend nothing mutable through an unpack head by design (`BUGS.md#for-nested-write-via-combinator-head`); the match-capture face is `BUGS.md#match-capture-reuses-alias-writes-through`. Fix shape for the `+=` face: an aug-assign that resolves to a rebinding `__add__` is a reassignment of the target (the pointer-local form), and the plain loop variable's reassignment check sees it.
- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) `self: auto_own[Self]` combined with `@overload` emits every specialization TWICE with identical signatures.** `class W: @overload def m(self: auto_own[Self], x: int32) -> auto_own[int32]: ...` plus a `str` stub and an impl emits four member functions -- `int32_t m(int32_t)` and `int32_t m(std::string_view)` each declared twice -- and g++ rejects ("cannot be overloaded with"). Method expansion clones both the stubs and the impl into borrowing + consuming halves, so each stub appears twice; `_gen_overload_specialized_method` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`) then takes `is_readonly=stub.is_readonly` but `is_consuming=impl.is_consuming` -- so the consuming axis comes from whichever clone `_collect_method_overload_groups` registered first and never varies per stub, leaving the two clones of each stub spelling one signature. Note the ownership consequence even if the duplication were suppressed: one polarity of the pair would be unreachable for the whole overload set, selected by clone-registration order rather than per-stub intent. The non-composed `auto_own` pair (no `@overload`) is unaffected -- it emits a borrowing and a consuming body correctly. Pre-existing and unrelated to THIR: the emission is the AST path, and `codegen_cpp/functions.py` is untouched by the branch that found it. Loud, no corpus witness. Fix shape: derive the consuming polarity per STUB the way const-ness already is, and suppress the duplicate where both clones of a stub would spell one signature. Repro `/tmp/agents/ovl/aown.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the THIR overload-clone skip; the reviewer reported it as a silent polarity collapse, and building the repro showed it is actually a hard compile error. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A record inheriting a builtin container with NO explicit `__init__` emits `using std::vector<int32_t>::list;` -- the inherited-constructor `using` spells the TPy type name instead of the C++ base's constructor.** `class Plain(list[int32]): pass` then `Plain([1, 2, 3])` fails with `'list' has not been declared in 'class std::vector<int>'`; a second error rides along (the ctor arg renders `std::array<int32_t, 3>` where the base wants `std::vector<int>`). The inherited-ctor `using` is emitted from the record's TPy base NAME, but the base's C++ spelling comes from the container formatter, so the two never agree for a formatter-carrying builtin -- the injected-class-name is `vector`, not `list`. Declaring any `__init__` avoids it (the record then has its own constructor). Loud, no corpus witness. Pre-existing -- reproduces unchanged at `5af9b227b`. Fix shape: emit the inherited-ctor `using` against the base's rendered C++ type (its injected-class-name), or suppress it for formatter-carrying builtin bases and synthesize a forwarding ctor. Repro `/tmp/agents/inh3/noinit.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the THIR inherited-container row and confirmed independently. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid) `x in t` is rejected when `t` is a record inheriting `set` -- "Cannot use 'in' with non-iterable type Tags".** `class Tags(set[StrView]): ...` then `"x" in t` errors, though the record inherits `__contains__` from the set stub and CPython accepts it. The membership dispatch resolves `__contains__` / iterability against the receiver's own record, not its inherited builtin base, so every container-inherited operator-protocol dunder is suspect here (`in`, and by the same shape iteration and comparison dunders) -- ordinary inherited METHOD calls (`t.add(...)`, `t.discard(...)`) resolve correctly, so the gap is specific to the operator paths. Loud (sema-rejected), not silent. Workaround: call the method form. Pre-existing and unrelated to THIR (the reject is in sema). Witness: the shape was cut from `tests/cases/inheritance/inheritance_builtin_dict_set` for exactly this reason. Fix shape: let the membership / iterability resolution walk the record's parents to a builtin container base, as the method-call path already does. Surfaced writing that case. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A parent-initializer call into a builtin container base is rejected, whatever its arguments.** [`builtin-container-base-init-unlowered`] `class MyList(list[int32]): def __init__(self, name: str): super().__init__([1, 2, 3])` errors "in the constructor of 'MyList': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (ctor.non_f1_base)"; `super().__init__([])` rejects the same way, and `super().__init__()` is an arity error because the `list` / `dict` / `set` stubs declare only the one-argument `__init__` (CPython's `list.__init__(self)` takes the iterable as optional). CPython runs all three. `lower_constructor` (`tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`) admits a builtin-container base only when the body makes no base-init call, since the member-init list would have to spell the container's own initializer. LANGUAGE_FEATURES "Inheriting from builtin types" claimed the seeding call works. Skipping the call is no divergence -- CPython's `__new__` has already built the empty container, as the C++ base default constructor does -- so the parent-init rule owes such a base nothing (`TypeRegistry.base_init_duty`, `tpyc/typesys.py`); what is missing is only the call itself. Fix shape: a zero-argument `__init__` variant in the three stubs plus a base-initializer lowering arm that renders the stub's constructor at the member-init position. Repro `/tmp/agents/native_uniform/p4.py`. Found 2026-09-27 making the parent-init rule uniform.

- **[LOW small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) `super().<method>()` on a builtin-container base spells the TPy method name against the C++ base type, ignoring the stub's `@native` rename.** In `class Overrider(list[int32])`, an overriding `append` calling `super().append(value)` emits `this->std::vector<int32_t>::append(value)` -- `std::vector` has no `append`, g++ rejects. The qualified-super render composes `NominalType(parent).to_cpp()` with `escape_cpp_name(method)`, so it never consults `fi.native_name` (`push_back`) the way the ordinary inherited call does (`ml.append(10)` -> `ml->push_back(10)`, correct); a `@native(function=True)` stub like `pop` would need the free-function form instead, which that render cannot spell at all. Loud, no corpus witness -- overriding an inherited builtin method is already warned about ("Method 'Overrider.append' hides 'list.append'"), and no case does it. THIR keeps this on the AST path (the super-marked call is outside the plain-member slice), so no mirror to unwind. Fix shape: route the super/unbound-self dispatch through the same fi-driven native-name / free-function selection the plain member call uses, keeping only the base qualification. Repro `/tmp/agents/inh/ovr.py`. Surfaced probing the THIR inherited-container receiver row's override boundary. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `return <void call>` at a `-> None` slot rejects at `call.ret_type.void`, in a sync def and an `async def` alike.** [`async-void-return-drops-call`] `def outer() -> None: return noisy()` and `async def outer() -> None: await asyncio.sleep(0); return noisy()` (`noisy() -> None`, prints) both fail with `(expr.call:call.ret_type.void)`: the return lowering sees a non-None operand and lowers it as a value, and the call lowering refuses a void result, where CPython evaluates the call and returns its None. Before the `return None` canonicalization (2026-09-13) the async form was WORSE -- the resumable ReturnT arm keyed the whole render on the slot being void and never evaluated the operand, so the call was silently dropped; the one `_return_carries_value` verdict now routes any non-None operand at a void slot down the value arms, so both positions reject loudly and the silent drop is gone. Fix shape: a non-None operand at a void return slot is evaluated as a discarded statement before the bare `return;`, in the sync arm and the resumable ReturnT arm alike (one rule, both positions). Probes `/tmp/agents/review_retnone2/p_sync_void_call.py`, `/tmp/agents/review_retnone2/p_async_void_call.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, async-sink cells 4-7 round); re-verified after the canonicalization 2026-09-13. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A pointer-repr container NAME in a REF vararg pack takes `&name` over the un-deref'd pointer.** A module-global `list[T]` (a `T*` pointer slot) passed by name into a `*args: T`-style REF pack renders `&xs` -- `T**` where the `std::array<const T*, N>` element needs the deref'd `&(*xs)` -- a hard g++ error on BOTH codegen paths (reviewer-probed with the AST alone). No corpus witness (the committed vararg cases pass locals/elements). A second face: record LOCALS that are rebound elsewhere in the function become pointer-locals, and a pack over them renders `std::array<const Point*, 2> __tmp_1{&a, &b};` over the pointers (probe `/tmp/agents/r4_sm/p14.py`, 2026-09-24). THIR mirrors the render; the BORROW_BIND threading in `_lower_vararg_pack` documents that its "renders identically" claim holds only for the currently-reachable record slice. Fix shape: the pack element render should read pointer names through the same deref the value positions apply. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, cells 15 round). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A `match` capture passed as a VARARG takes the address of an already-pointer local.** [`vararg-of-pointer-capture-takes-address`] `def bump_all(*counters: Counter)` called as `case Bag(c=q): bump_all(q)` emits `std::array<Counter*, 1> __tmp{&q}` where `q` is already a `Counter*`, so g++ reports `cannot convert 'Counter**' to 'Counter*' in initialization`. The capture binds to the pointer form (it aliases the subject's field), and the pack element render does not deref a pointer-repr NAME before taking its address. Same mechanism as the module-global `list[T]` REF pack entry above -- the pack element render is pointer-blind for every pointer-repr source, not just globals -- so fix them together. Pre-existing: identical on master, where the const-inference miss adds a second error ahead of it. This is why `tests/cases/match/match_capture_mutation_credited` has no vararg section, although the vararg arm of the call-edge attribution it covers does handle captures. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_vararg_simple.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the capture-attribution branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++) A raw-lowered `@error_return` call with a nested `@error_return` call in its argument subtree renders ill-formed C++.** `self.p = make(inner(n))` (both callees `@error_return`, inside a try or auto-propagate body) emits the outer `__try_tmp_N` block with the inner call's expression-level unwrap misplaced -- g++/clang reject (`cannot convert std::expected<int,E> to int32_t`; `deduced type 'void' for '__try_tmp' is incomplete`). Any raw statement-level er sink reaches it (name bind, field target, discard); no corpus witness exists because sema/codegen never gated it -- the THIR side rejects the shape via `_reject_nested_error_return_arg` at all four statement sinks, keeping both paths in fallback lockstep without blessing the broken render. Fix shape: the AST's raw-call statement handlers must pre-hoist nested er unwraps (or reject with a diagnostic). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, long-tail cells 11 round) with a direct g++ compile of the AST-only output. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small, latent UB] A top-level global-slot write inside a FOR-loop body leaves the global pointing at a BLOCK-scoped slot; the WHILE-body twin freezes the first iteration.** At module init, a first rvalue write to a non-value global inside a for-each body emits the backing slot WITHOUT `static` (`Point __global_slot_1 = Point(i);`) and then `p = &__global_slot_1;`, so any read after the loop exits derefs a dead stack slot -- latent UAF that happens to pass exec (the frame memory is typically intact within `__tpy_init`; the repro below builds, runs and prints `2`). The `static` is dropped by `branch_scope=in_branch` on the `GLOBAL_RVALUE` `THIRPtrLocalDecl` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:4503`, gated to for-bodies at statements.py:7609) and consumed at `tpyc/thir/emit.py:3843` (`_gs_static = "" if stmt.branch_scope else state.slot_static`). The sibling scopes do NOT share the defect and must not be conflated with it: the same write inside an `if`/`while`/`with`/`try` body is a hard reject (`stmt.var_decl:top_level.global_slot_branch`, statements.py:7606), so until 2026-09-04 the for-body arm was the only one that emitted; the `if` / `with` / `try` bodies now emit too, correctly with `static` (`tests/cases/globals/global_slot_branch_and_hoist` for `if`, `tests/cases/control_flow/with_target_reuse_read_after_global` for `with`; `try` probe-verified); the `while` body still rejects (`tests/cases/globals/error_global_slot_while_write`), so the for-body arm is the one outlier still emitting the unsafe form. The `while`-body twin (2026-09-04, oracle-verified) is worse than latent: a module-level `while` whose body writes a non-value global prints `0 0 0` where CPython prints `0 1 2`, because the slot's first-iteration value is re-read on every pass; it still rejects on THIR. Witness: `inference/reassign_none_loop_narrowing` (post-loop `if x is not None: print(x.x)`). Repro: `class Point` with an `int32` field, `p: Point | None = None`, `for i in range(3): p = Point(i)`, then `if p is not None: print(p.x)`. Fix shape: NOT a bare static-ize -- `static T slot = init;` initializes once, which would freeze the first iteration's value. Route the for-body write through the existing hoisted flavor instead (`GLOBAL_HOIST_RVALUE`: a `static std::optional<T>` slot declared outside the loop, re-emplaced per iteration), which gives both a stable address and per-iteration assignment. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] Sema stamps concrete narrow facts on statically-dead branches of exhaustively-folded isinstance or-chains, emitting dead extractions.** `if isinstance(v, A) or isinstance(v, B):` on `v: A | B` folds the second leaf to `true` (the chain is tautological), yet the implicit-else path carries a concrete `{v: A}` fact -- the AST emits an unreachable `auto& __v = *std::get<A*>(v);` past the early-return if (and, for the negated flavor, inside the dead branch). Semantically harmless (unreachable code) but wrong facts on dead paths; both paths emit it identically (THIR mirrors the oracle per the byte-diff discipline -- see the or-chain wave ledger entry, 2026-08-12; witness `tests/cases/union/union_isinstance_or_chain`'s `two_member`/`negated_or`). Fix belongs in sema's fold-aware fact stamping, not in either emit path.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A NARROWED-Optional field as a borrow-tuple element has no lowering arm.** In a method returning `tuple[Inner, int32]` (a `std::tuple<const Inner*, ...>` borrow tuple), `return (self.maybe, 1)` under `if self.maybe is not None:` dies with `error: in function 'get': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.tuple_literal)`, while the plain-field flavour `return (self.inner, 0)` compiles (both verified with `uv run tpyc` on 2026-09-03). The earlier symptom was the un-deref'd `&(this->maybe)` -- an `std::optional<Inner>*` into the `const Inner*` slot, rejected by g++ -- and it is gone with the AST emitter. The field-element leg (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:11596`, rejecting at `:11612` with detail `btuple.elem_source`) excludes an Optional-DECLARED field deliberately, but its comment's rationale -- that the AST emitted the broken render there so the shape must defer until the AST is fixed -- is stale: that emitter is gone and this leg is the only author, so it simply owes the narrowed deref. Fix shape: render `&((*this->maybe))` for a proven-narrowed Optional field element instead of rejecting. No corpus witness (the committed borrow-tuple cases use plain fields/names). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; was uncompilable C++) A bytes ternary mixing a view arm and a bytes literal is refused.** [`bytes-ternary-view-literal-rejects`] Re-checked 2026-09-28: the shape stops at `ifexpr.bytes_mixed` at every position -- the return below, a local (`v = b if len(b) > 3 else b"x"`, `b` a local bound to a literal), and a `bytes` FIELD written from a param in the constructor or a method (`self.b = src if c else b"z"`); probes `/tmp/agents/ge/file/c_ret.py`, `c_bytes_tern.py`, `c_bytes_tern_m.py`. The `or` / `and` twin is `BUGS.md#bytes-select-mixed-runtime-spelling`. The history as filed: `def f(c: bool, b: bytes) -> bytes: return b if c else b"x"` rendered `return ((c) ? (b) : (::tpy::bytes_literal_owned("x", 1)));` -- the span param and the owned-vector literal have no common type, so the emit fails at the C++ step (clang: no conversion from `std::span<const unsigned char>`). Hidden because no exec witness exercises the shape (the narrowed `Optional[bytes]`-param flavor takes the whole-ternary `bytes_copy` wrap and compiles). Surfaced 2026-08-07 by the THIR wave-39 widening: THIR's arm is narrowed to the value-opt-param flavor and the plain-param flavor keeps deferring (the fence pin that documented it went with the THIR unit suite) until this emit is fixed -- the likely fix is applying the same owned materialization the str-mixed arms get.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, `__del__`-observable) A value moved into an `Optional[Own[R]]` PARAMETER is destroyed at the callee's return, while CPython keeps it alive to the caller's frame end.** [`opt-own-by-value-param-early-del`] `def take(p: Own[Pic] | None) -> int32` called as `take(other)` with `other: Pic | None` at its last use (or a plain local moved into the same slot, `auto_move/auto_move_own_optional_narrowed`): the parameter is a by-value `std::optional<Pic>`, so the moved-in payload dies when the callee returns, where the caller's `other` still names the object in CPython. The plain `Own[Pic | None]` spelling binds `&&` and matches; `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` states the `T&&` contract for `Own` parameters and now names this exception. Fix shape: give the `Optional[Own[T]]` parameter the same `&&` form. Pre-existing at the constructor slot; reachable from free functions and methods since 2026-09-11. Found 2026-09-11 in review.

Same flat-CFG-scoping family as the `await`-in-`except ... as e:` entry below, different root: the U4 persistent assert-narrow alias is emitted block-scoped while its narrowing fact stays live for the rest of the function. Found probing the shadow_scope field classification (gate-c scoping branch), 2026-09-27. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

Loud (duplicate definition + undefined reference), no corpus case (the shape cannot pass exec). Fix shape: mangle bodied literal-stub DEFINITIONS with the same `literal_mangled_name` (definition + forward decl + cross-module attr spelling), or reject the bodied-Literal combination in sema. Repro: the two bodied `Literal` stubs above plus the `k(1, "fast")` call, through `--dump-code` (the unit that carried the source went with the THIR unit suite). Surfaced re-pinning the callee-reject units for the THIR literal-overload round. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, pre-existing) An augmented assignment through a CALL receiver (`o.get().v += 1`) double-evaluates the receiver call in generated C++ where CPython evaluates it once.** [`augassign-call-receiver-double-eval`] The aug-assign arm of `_lower_stmt` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` lowers `stmt.target` TWICE -- once as the assign lvalue, once as the binop's left operand (the `else` leg beside the class-constant `_lower_class_const_write_target` split) -- so `target OP= value` becomes `target = (target OP value)` with the receiver call spelled on both sides. Verified 2026-09-03: `uv run tpyc --dump-code` emits `o.get().v = (o.get().v) + (::tpy::BigInt(1));`, and `uv run tpy` reports 2 receiver calls where CPython reports 1. The only exercised receivers are pure accessors (Box.get), so the cpy phase stays green. **The `@property` spelling is HELD at a reject**: a read is a method call from sema on, so `b.rec.x += 1` would otherwise emit `b.rec().x = ::tpy::add_check<int32_t>(b.rec().x, 1);` and run an IMPURE getter twice -- the shape that makes this observable rather than merely wasteful. Because evaluation order is a postponed language decision, fixing that one site would settle the class by accident and leave the spelled-method twin disagreeing, so a getter anywhere on the target's receiver chain rejects with `augassign.recv.accessor_double_eval` (`_augassign_recv_is_accessor`, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`), pinned by `tests/cases/records/error_property_augassign_receiver`. The reject goes when this entry is fixed, not before. The `<call>.field += ...` spelling (`borrow_out(b).x += 1`) is untouched and still double-evaluates; it is pinned as a render by `tests/cases/records/property_read_positions`' `return_pos` section, whose comment names it. Same family as the temp-hoisted argument ordering entry below: one expression, spelled more than once in the render, where CPython spells it once. Fix: evaluate the receiver once into a local and aug through the alias; the class-constant leg already splits its receiver eval off exactly once via `recv_eval`/`recv_wrap`, so extend that split to a general call receiver. **User `__getitem__` face, same root:** `r[0][0] += 1` through a user `__getitem__` below the outermost subscript spells `::tpy::__getitem__(r, 0)` on both sides (a mutating getter runs twice); it is held at the same reject (`_augassign_recv_is_accessor`), pinned by `tests/cases/records/error_record_getitem_augassign`. The hold covers a pure getter too (`g[0][1] += 10` on a matrix class); `row = g[0]; row[1] += 10` is the working spelling. It keys on the receiver type (`_record_getitem_key`) because sema stamps `getitem_function_info` only on non-reference `__getitem__` returns, so a `@native` record's reference-returning `__getitem__` is not covered yet. **Subscript-index face, same root:** `xs[f()] += 1` spells `f()` in both the `__setitem__` and the `__getitem__` (`['a', 'a']` vs CPython `['a']`, probe `/tmp/agents/r2par/aug2.py`, 2026-09-23) -- the aug-assign arm lowers `stmt.target` twice, so the index needs the same once-into-a-local split. Newly reachable for `bytes` since `list[bytes]` / `dict[bytes, bytes]` element `+=` compiles (2026-10-01): `xs[idx()] += b"!"` and `db[k()] += b"w"` each call the index / key function twice (a counter reads 4 after two such statements, CPython 2; probes `/tmp/agents/vr-review/cg/p19.py`, `/tmp/agents/vr-review/parity/ag1.py`); the `str` and `int32` twins did so before. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) Copying a non-copyable recursive-union member out of an accessor (`w = box.get()`) passes sema and fails only at g++.** A recursive-union wrapper (`type Value = int | str | Neg` where `Neg` owns a `@nocopy` `Box[Value]`) holds `Neg` by value in its `std::variant`, so `Neg`'s deleted copy ctor deletes `Value::Value(const Value&)` -- and a plain decl `w = n.inner.get()` (a borrow-returning accessor result copied into an owned local) emits `Value w = n.inner.get();`, which g++ rejects with `use of deleted function`. CPython runs the same line fine (it aliases). No front-end diagnostic points at the copy; contrast `error_union_box_field_copy`, which catches the structurally identical copy at a FIELD-assignment site -- the local-decl sink is missing the same check. Both codegen paths emit the identical (uncompilable) C++, so this is an AST-side sema gap, not a THIR divergence. Repro: the wrapper-accessor decl above run through the toolchain (probe left at `/tmp/agents/probe_wrapper_copy3.py`); the unit fixture that carried it went with the THIR unit suite. Fix shape: extend the union-member copy check that guards field assigns to owned-local decl (and likely return/arg storage) sinks. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the THIR receiver-row wave. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) `is_type_non_copyable` has no `UnionType` arm, so a store into a field/container typed as a union of `@nocopy` members is never rejected.** [`union-nocopy-field-store`] With `A` and `B` both `@nocopy` and a field `u: A | B`, `self.u = tmp` emits `::tpy::to_value_variant<std::variant<A, B>>(tmp)` and dies in raw libstdc++ spew (`no matching function for call to 'std::variant<A, B>::variant(...)'` -- the variant's copy ctor is deleted because an alternative's is) with no TPy diagnostic. The structurally identical store into a `@nocopy` RECORD field IS rejected (`cannot copy non-copyable type 'Box[Expr]' into field`, pinned by `tests/cases/union/error_union_box_field_copy`), so this is one missing arm, not a policy. Both `tpyc/sema/context.py:1337` (`is_type_non_copyable`, which upgrades the copy WARNING to an error) and its narrower sibling `is_type_nocopy` (`:1296`) walk `Readonly` / `Own` / `Optional` / `Tuple` / `RecursiveAliasInstanceType` / dyn-protocol / record and then fall through to `get_record_for_type(<union>)` -> `None` -> `False`. The recursive-alias arm exists for exactly this reason (its comment: a non-copyable alternative propagates through the wrapper's `std::variant`), and a plain union lowers to a `std::variant` just the same. Sema-layer, so both codegen paths inherit it. Independent of the last-use copy-warning suppression: verified at the local's last use (no warning at all) and at a non-last use (warns `copies B into field` but never upgrades), both spewing. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. Fix shape: give both helpers a `UnionType` arm returning True when any member is non-copyable. Repros `/tmp/agents/nocopyunion/main.py` (last use) and `/tmp/agents/nocopyunion2/main.py` (non-last use). Surfaced probing the field-store copy-warning suppression. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud) `await` inside an `except ... as e:` handler body reads `e` out of scope in the generated coroutine.** The handler binding is a C++ `catch (const MyErr& e)` parameter, but the resumable frame splits the handler body at the suspension, so the post-resume code reads `e` from a later, disjoint `case` block after the catch scope has already exited -- g++ reports `'e' was not declared in this scope`. Idiomatic async retry/logging code (`try: await op() / except TimeoutError as e: await report(e)`) is valid Python and gets raw compiler spew. Root cause is that an except capture is never given frame storage: it lives only in the catch parameter, so it has nowhere to survive a suspension. The `with` member of this family is fixed -- a target is frame-resident unconditionally and the emit binds through that field -- and the remaining siblings are this one, which has no gate at all, and the match capture, whose `needs_frame_field` gate is still narrower than the construct (see the match entry below). Fix shape: give a handler binding read after a suspension a frame slot and copy the caught value into it at catch time, so the resume block reads the slot rather than the dead parameter. Note the capture must take an OWNING frame copy, not the aliasing form the `with` target uses: `_classify_pointer_alias_locals` deliberately excludes handler bindings because the caught object dies at handler end, so a pointer would dangle. Verified on master, independent of the capture-registration work. Three separate review passes converged on this same missing-frame-storage gap, of which this is the sharpest form. The generator shape fails the same way: `except ValueError as e: yield 1; print(str(e))` in a generator body (probe `/tmp/agents/fbo-n/p/exc_cap.py`, verified 2026-09-25 on d4827a6abb and on `frame-borrow-order`; also the `except` cells of the frame matrix `/tmp/agents/fbo-int/m3`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (cpy stub divergence, blocks test coverage) The `lib/cpy` `Span` stub mis-bounds a span minted by `take_ptr(x).span(n)`, so the last element raises where TPy reads it fine.** `a = Array[int32, 3]([10, 11, 12]); s = take_ptr(a[0]).span(3)` then `s[2]` prints `12` under TPy and raises `RuntimeError: span index out of bounds` under `PYTHONPATH=lib/cpy python3`, while `len(s)` reports `3` on both -- so the stub's length and its index bound disagree. Stub-only (`lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py` ~406, seen only by CPython), so it is a test-infrastructure defect rather than a compiler one, but it blocks cpy-comparing any case whose shape needs a pointer-minted Span: `control_flow/with_target_pointer_bearing_value` had to drop its `Span` half for exactly this reason (the shape is still covered by the compiler fix and a scratch probe, just not by an exec+cpy case). Repro `/tmp/agents/scopens/spanchk/main.py`. Surfaced authoring the pointer-bearing-value with-target case.
- **[LOW small] (inconsistent fact, no observable effect today) A `with ... as t` target records `Own[T]` as its frame-local type where an ordinary binding of the same value records `T`.** `def __enter__(self) -> Own[Item]` makes the target's `generator_locals` entry `Own[Item]`, while `t = make()` over the same `-> Own[Item]` function records `Item`. The storage consequence is closed -- the frame-layout plan now looks THROUGH `Own` at the object it names, so both spellings land on the same `frame_slot<Item>` field (before that, the target's `Own` read as a value type and took a bare field, which default-constructed at frame creation and so failed to build outright whenever `Item` held a non-default-constructible member such as a `Box`; pinned now by `control_flow/with_target_own_enter_no_default_ctor`). What remains is the recorded type itself: two different answers for the same value depending on how it was bound, which any future consumer keying on it would read differently. Fix shape: record `T` at the with target, matching the ordinary-binding spelling, and drop the plan's `Own` unwrap if nothing else needs it. Surfaced by the inverse test of the with-target storage fix.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A return-tier `try`/`except` in which EVERY path returns emits an unreachable fallthrough with no return, so `-Werror=return-type` rejects it.** `def outer(k: str) -> int32: try: return inner(k) / except NotFound as e: return e.code` (with `inner` `@error_return`) emits the `goto`-based return tier ending `__after_try_1:; }` -- both real paths return, but the label is still a syntactic fallthrough point, so g++ reports "control reaches end of non-void function". A plain `uv run tpy` builds it (the harness compiles with warnings-as-errors, which is what surfaces it), so it bites the test suite and any `-Werror` build. Pre-existing and independent of name shadowing -- reproduced with a non-colliding binding, `/tmp/agents/scopens/p_rt_plain.py`. Existing return-tier corpus cases miss it because they re-raise or continue after the try rather than returning on every path. Workaround: assign in the handler and return after the try (what `tests/cases/name_shadowing/except_return_tier_shadow` does). Fix shape: emit an unreachable-return (or `__builtin_unreachable`) after the join label when every tier path terminates. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A `match` capture that persists past the match and is read by a LATER suspension gets no frame slot.** `needs_frame_field` (`sema/match.py:171-175`) only scans for suspensions inside the match statement's own arms, but a capture is an ordinary function local in Python and stays live afterwards -- so `case 5 as hit: ...` followed later in the body by `yield hit` leaves `hit` as a C++ local scoped to one switch-`case`, read out of scope from a later one. Undiagnosed C++ build failure. The predicate needs to ask whether the capture is read after any suspension anywhere in the body, not just within the match. Reproduced: `case 5 as hit: pass / case _ as hit: pass` then `yield 1` / `yield hit` gives `error: 'hit' was not declared in this scope` where CPython prints `1` then `5` -- repro `/tmp/agents/scopens/v_match_after.py`. Pre-existing (byte-identical on master). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `with ... as NAME` capture that reuses an already-bound name, and any `with` whose `__enter__` returns a tuple, are hard compile errors.** `x = 1` then `with Counter(5) as x:` (a `-> Counter` `__enter__`) prints `error: in function 'f': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.with)` -- valid Python, since CPython simply rebinds the name. A borrow-form TUPLE target is the second face and needs no reuse at all: `__enter__ -> tuple[Item, int32]` bound by a single `with CM(base) as p:` rejects with the same bare `stmt.with`. `_lower_with` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:15100`) admits a fixed ladder of target rows -- plain non-value hoist, pointer predecl, the frame-resident flavors -- and raises `stmt_reject_reason(stmt)` with no detail for everything else, so the message names no shape. Two things are owed: a located TYPE diagnostic for the incompatible-type reuse (`_analyze_with` in `tpyc/sema/statements.py` still calls `current_scope.define` unconditionally, bypassing the reassignment-type-mismatch check that guards a plain `x = ...`), and a tuple-target row. The SAME-type value reuse this entry also covered is FIXED: `case 1 as v:` then `with CM(7) as v:` (a `-> int32` `__enter__`) now emits `auto v = __ctx_1.__enter__();` in its own scope, builds and runs. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the with-target storage branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (misleading diagnostic) A read of a name shadowed by a later-arm `match` capture reports callability, not the shadowing.** `case Cat(lives=helper): ... / case Dog(): return helper()` where `helper` is also a module function reports `'helper' is not callable` -- correct to reject (CPython raises `UnboundLocalError`, since the capture makes the name a function-local), but the message names neither the `match` capture nor the scoping rule, so a user whose code compiled before this became reachable has no path from the message to the cause. Pinned by `tests/cases/name_shadowing/error_match_capture_shadows_function`. Fix shape: when the shadowing binding is a pattern capture, say so and point at the capture. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid) A `match` capture does not make its name a function-local for the arms BEFORE it, so an earlier arm can still reach an outer binding of that name.** Python makes a capture pattern's name a function-local everywhere in the enclosing function, so any arm referencing it raises `UnboundLocalError` unless that arm bound it -- verified: `case Cat(lives=helper): ... / case Dog(): return helper()` raises in CPython. Arms AFTER the capture behave correctly (the binding is visible and the read is rejected); arms BEFORE it still resolve the name to the module-level function and silently succeed. Same family as the post-handler `except` read entry below: TPy models captures as block-scoped where Python scopes them to the function. Closing both means function-scoped capture locals (bind-then-mark-dead), a variable-model change tracked in TODO.md -- not a local patch, and NOT fixable by resetting the namespace per arm, which would re-break the after-arms case that now works. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud -- no front-end diagnostic) A pointer-repr tuple LOCAL whose literal RHS value-captures an owned element emits ill-formed C++ at both the decl and the reassign.** [`pointer-repr-tuple-local-value-capture-literal`] `t: tuple[int32, Cell] = (1, Cell(2))` followed by `t = (3, Cell(4))` emits `std::tuple<int32_t, Cell*> t = std::tuple<int32_t, Cell>{1, Cell(2)};` and a matching bare assign, which g++ rejects (`conversion ... to non-scalar type` at the decl, `no match for 'operator='` at the reassign). The reassign is what promotes the local to borrow form, so the DECL breaks too -- the same decl alone, without the later reassign, builds fine. The trigger is the element's CAPTURE, not its freshness: a VALUE-captured element (`Cell(4)` inline, or a `std::move`d local) breaks, while a REF-captured one (a `Cell` param) renders `std::tuple<int32_t, Cell*>{3, &(b)}` and runs. Also reached without an annotation when the reassign sits under a branch: `t = (H(1), 5); if c: t = (H(10), 6)` renders `std::tuple<H*, int32_t> t = std::tuple<H, int32_t>{H(1), 5};` (verified 2026-09-22, probe `/tmp/agents/u1b4w/sync_rebind_plain.py`; with an element alias in between, `/tmp/agents/rv4r2/p20s_field_list_hop_sync.py`). `tpyc` emits no diagnostic at all; only the C++ build fails. Root cause: `_lower_borrow_tuple_literal` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:11324`) spells the element's VALUE part and takes no `&()` lift for a VALUE-capture element, so the node's `spelled_cpp` is the STORAGE tuple at a borrow slot (witness `btuple.literal`, `:11674`); reached from the decl arm (`decl.btuple_literal`, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:9499`) and the reassign arm (`btuple.reseat_literal`, `:8253`). Fix is a DESIGN FORK, not a patch: render the literal against the borrow target, or route the prvalue through an owning slot + `tuple_to_pointer` -- pick one before coding. Possible second defect at the same site, untraced: `t = (3, b)` renders `std::move(b)` where CPython would alias. Surfaced by the ast-fix-0823 identity-lift pin lane. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. **Reach grew 2026-09-23:** a tuple local bound on one branch from a borrowed member and on the other from `copy(...)` (`if c: pair = (b, 0) else: pair = (copy(b), 1)`), or seeded with `copy(b)` and rebound to `(b, i)` in a loop, and then returned by name into an `Own` element slot, used to stop at a located sema error (the Own-element return tier). That slot now warns and copies, so the program reaches this decl and fails in g++ instead (probes `/tmp/agents/meta/del/`, `/tmp/agents/cgr/R.py` `f_loop`); the decl fails the same way without the return. A container-element sink reaches it too: `t = (P(1), P(2)); t = (p, p); return [t]` (or the rebind under an `if`/`else`) emits `std::tuple<P*, P*> t = std::tuple<P, P>{P(1), P(2)};` and fails g++ (probe `/tmp/agents/b2fix/r1.py`, 2026-09-24).
- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence; globals rank last) A module-GLOBAL tuple returned by name into an `Own` element slot copies with no warning.** [`global-tuple-name-own-return-unwarned`] `G = (P(1), 0)` then `def f() -> tuple[Own[P], int32]: return G` renders `return G;` -- a copy of the global's element, TPy `gl 1 2` where CPython prints `gl 2 2` -- while the scalar twin (`G = P(1)`, `return G` at `-> Own[P]`) warns `copies P into owned storage`. The per-element name rule reads a local's construction facts, a parameter's or a loop variable's declared elements, and nothing for a global. Waits on the TODO design entry "Module scope is the body of __tpy_init" (a global takes its local twin's form), not a per-shape patch. Probes `/tmp/agents/par/gl.py`, `/tmp/agents/par/gs.py`. Found by the tuple-element `Own` tier review 2026-09-23.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, unlocated) `yield t` of a borrow-form tuple NAME into `Iterator[tuple[Own[P], int32]]` gets no warning and fails the C++ build.** [`yield-tuple-name-own-element`] `t = (p, 1); yield t` emits `return t;` into `std::expected<std::tuple<P, int32_t>, ...>`, which g++ rejects (the borrow tuple does not convert); the literal `yield (p, 0)` warns and copies. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A HOISTED mixed owned+borrow tuple local fails to build when its OWNED element is not C++-default-constructible.** `try: p = make_mixed(c)` / `except: p = make_mixed(c)` for `-> tuple[Own[Guard], Cell]` emits the hoisted decl `std::tuple<Guard, Cell*> p;` and then assigns -- but a class with `__del__` (a user `__del__`, or `Box[T]` / `Rc[T]` / `Arc[T]`) suppresses the C++ default ctor, so g++ reports `no matching function for call to tuple<Guard, Cell*>::tuple()`. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `Optional` of a tuple containing a record (`tuple[Rec, int32] | None`) is unusable as a param: the slot takes value-form storage while the body and call site use borrow form.** The param renders `std::optional<std::tuple<Rec, int32_t>>`, but the body reads an element as a pointer (`std::get<0>((*t))->v` -- "base operand of `->` has non-pointer type") and the call site builds the borrow form (`std::tuple<Rec*, int32_t>` -- "could not convert ... to `std::optional<std::tuple<Rec, int32_t>>`"). Distinct from the nearby tuple entries: no `Own` marker, no rvalue source, and the mismatch is the Optional-WRAPPED tuple param rather than a bare tuple. **Second, separable defect on the same shape:** adding a default (`= None`) emits `= std::nullopt` at the free-function declaration, instantiating `std::optional<std::tuple<Rec, ...>>` over the still-incomplete `Rec` -- the hazard `default_needs_call_site_fill` (`typesys.py`) exists to dodge, which it misses here because it tests the Optional's inner for `NominalType.is_user_record` and that inner is a `TupleType`. Toolchain-caught throughout, no silent wrongness. Repros `/tmp/agents/tuple_default_probe.py` (all three errors) and `/tmp/agents/tuple_nodefault_probe.py` (the two form errors alone, proving provenance). Surfaced by the semantic-conflict pass of `/tpy-merge-master` on `fix-positional-defaults`, probing whether master's new tuple-form facts interact with the default-suppression rule. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence) A MIXED owned+borrow tuple GLOBAL (`G: tuple[Box, Box] = make_mixed(V)`) takes owning storage and COPIES its borrowed element where the local twin aliases it.** [`global-tuple-ref-storage-form`] The all-borrow half of this entry is closed (2026-09-22): a tuple of references at a module global is the tuple of the pointer slots every reference-typed global is (`std::tuple<Box*, Box*> G{}`, bound once at module init, rebind from a function body refused with the scalar's error), so `G: tuple[Box, Box] = (V, V)` then `G[0].n = 43` reaches `V` (TPy 43, CPython 43); a fresh literal element makes the global OWN it (sema marks it `Own` on the binding, storage form, nothing to alias), and an importing module reads the form off the binding type. What remains is the MIXED global: `mixed: tuple[Box, Box] = make_mixed(V)` for `-> tuple[Own[Box], Box]` records `tuple[Own[Box], Box]` on the binding, keeps storage (`std::tuple<Box, Box> mixed`), and `tuple_to_storage` copies the borrowed element, so `mixed[1].n = 44` prints TPy **2** vs CPython **44**, silently -- pinned by the `mixed_write` section of `tests/cases/tuple/element_vs_singleton_global` (which keeps `no_cpython.txt` for exactly this line). The local twin (`p = make_mixed(V)`) takes the mixed render `std::tuple<Box, Box*>` and aliases; the global would take the same render -- the owned element by value in static storage, nothing dangles -- with the declare-then-assign default-constructibility caveat the `Own`-element entry below records. Until then the cheap half is the stopgap warning at this sink (TODO: "Warn at the mixed-tuple module GLOBAL as a stopgap"): the per-element copy warning the field and container sinks already give, so the divergence is acknowledged rather than silent. The same form closes a second cell: a tuple global that OWNS a reference element (`tg = mk(1)` off `-> tuple[Own[Box], int32]`, or `(1, Box(5))`) is its own storage, so a module-level rebind (`tg = mk(7)`) would overwrite the object a pointer-slot target unpacked out of it (`gx, gk = tg` -- `gx` points into `tg`); the scalar global re-points at a fresh static slot and keeps the old object. That rebind is REFUSED at sema once such an unpack has happened (`Cannot reassign global variable ... a module-level unpack borrowed an element of it`, pinned by `globals/error_owning_tuple_global_rebind`; with no alias the rebind stays a plain storage assign, and the function-body form is held by the `global.unseeded` lowering reject rather than by the rule), which is the diagnostic that holds the cell until the owning tuple global is a pointer at per-assignment static backing -- the one mechanism both this and the mixed global need. The same backing is what a LATER module-level literal with a FRESH element needs: `P: tuple[Box, int32] = (V, 1)` then `P = (copy(W), 2)` at module level rejects (`expr.tuple_literal`) where the scalar `S = copy(W)` allocates a fresh static slot and re-points -- the elementwise render is `static Box __global_slot_N = copy(W); P = {&__global_slot_N, 2}` (loud today, a tuple-equals-scalar position gap; the first literal's fresh element is handled by the `Own` marking on the binding, a later one has no slot). The mixed global's LAST use passed to a mixed `tuple[Own[Box], Box]` parameter copies its owned element in unwarned (`tuple_to_pointer`): sema calls a tuple global's last use a move, which static storage cannot make -- the fully owned twin's `f(auto(G))` decay copy is the same silent copy (`tests/cases/tuple/mixed_own_param_writes`, `global` section). Fix shape: either the alias decl follows the catch parameter's const-ness, or the handler catches by mutable reference where the binding is later aliased -- the decl and the catch signature must agree. Accepts-invalid on pathological input, and the value read inside the handler is correct (that was the shadowing bug, fixed) -- only the post-handler region diverges. Closing it means modelling Python's function-scoped locals for captures (bind-then-mark-dead rather than unbind), which is a variable-model change, not a local patch: TPy's whole local model is block-scoped. Surfaced by the capture-registration fix.

- **[LOW small, latent, unverified] `get_resolved_type`'s `var_types` short-circuit now resolves pending CONTAINER types too, and no test exercises that half.** The short-circuit was fixed to route through `resolve_type()` so a tuple-unpack target's `PendingStrType` no longer leaks out unresolved; `resolve_type()` also resolves `PendingListType`/`PendingDictType`/`PendingSetType`. That is the architecturally right chokepoint (the non-`var_types` path has always resolved both), but the container half is a behavior widening nobody has a witness for. The specific worry is one level down, in `_resolve_pending_container`'s BEST-EFFORT fallback (`make_list(elem)` / `make_dict` / `make_set`, taken when sema's resolution never ran). Before this change that path could not be reached from the short-circuit, so an unresolved pending list surfaced as a LOUD `PendingListType should be resolved before codegen` crash; now it can silently become `list[T]` where the truth is `Array[T, N]` -- a reference-vs-value guess, and a copy-vs-alias decision keyed on it would be a SILENT divergence, the project's most serious class. (The resolved answer itself is the truthful one -- returning it is strictly better than returning the raw pending node, which is why the fix is not to narrow the resolution back to views.) A whole-corpus comp run over both variants (view-only vs container-inclusive) produced byte-IDENTICAL output, and a review pass could not construct a reachable case across ~89 `get_resolved_type` call sites, so there is no evidence of a live defect -- this is filed because "unverified across 89 call sites" is exactly what resurfaces later as an aliasing bug, not because a symptom exists. Fix shape if a witness appears: audit the call sites that ask `is_value_type()` / a value-vs-reference question about a `var_types` entry, rather than narrowing the resolution back to views. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity, self-tagged low confidence) on `fix-pending-view-unpack`.
- **[MED small] (wrong answer from a type predicate, latent) `Own[T]` reports `is_trivially_destructible() == True` for every `T`, so `Own[bytes]` / `Own[list[int]]` claim to be cheap heap-free value types.** `OwnType.is_value_type()` returns `True` unconditionally (deliberate -- documented as "Own[T] uses T&& at param boundaries; treat as value type for other purposes", `tpyc/typesys.py:1673`), and `is_expensive_copy()` is NOT overridden, so it falls through to the base implementation whose `_nominal_td()` is None for a wrapper type and returns `False`. `is_trivially_destructible()` is `is_value_type() and not is_expensive_copy()` (`tpyc/typesys.py:523`), so it is `True and not False` regardless of the wrapped type -- confirmed directly: `OwnType(NominalType('builtins.bytes')).is_trivially_destructible()` is True where the bare `bytes` answers False. Any consumer asking an `Own[T]` whether a move is cheap gets the wrong answer; the live consumer is `_del_var_trivial` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:584`, the `del x` emit-nothing skip), not confirmed reachable with an OwnType, hence latent rather than a live miscompile. Found the hard way: a candidate fix for the `_maybe_move` frame-local regression used `is_trivially_destructible()` directly and silently kept dropping the move on `Own[bytes]`; the shipped fix unwraps `Own` explicitly to sidestep this, which is a workaround at the consumer, not a fix. Fix shape: forward `is_expensive_copy()` (and probably `is_trivially_destructible()`) to `self.wrapped` on `OwnType` -- but check each existing consumer first, since `is_value_type()`'s unconditional `True` is load-bearing at param boundaries and the three predicates are entangled. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An unbound-self read of a `@native`-RENAMED base field is a hard compile error.** `BaseA.x` inside a descendant method, where `BaseA` is `@native` with `x: int32 = native_field("m_x")`, dies with `error: in function 'read': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return:field.receiver_shape)` (verified 2026-09-03 with `uv run tpyc --dump-code`). `_unbound_self_field_ok` in `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py` refuses the shape outright when `e.native_field_name is not None`, deferring to a renderer that no longer exists; the plain non-native sibling compiles fine to `this->BaseA::x`. Fix: spell the rename in the unbound-self render (`this->{parent}::{native_field_name}`) and drop the predicate's `native_field_name` exclusion. Exotic shape -- an `@native` base carrying a per-field rename, read unbound from a subclass method; no corpus witness. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Printing a NARROWED value-repr `Optional[scalar]` module GLOBAL emits the bare optional.** `g: int32 | None = 5` then `if g is not None: print(g)` emits `std::cout << g` where `g` is `std::optional<int32_t>`, which has no `operator<<` -- the C++ build fails. The same construct on a LOCAL or a param renders `print_optional_val(g)` correctly, so it is the module-global binding that misses the narrowed-read wrap. Loud, pre-existing (reproduces on master), no corpus witness. Note the THIR overlay already emits the CORRECT `print_optional_val(g)` here, so this is one of the few places the two paths disagree with THIR being right; the field-write/containers wave widened admission enough that more bodies containing this construct now route, which is how it was found (no in-corpus case newly routes -- the whole-corpus byte-diff stayed green). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) A walrus binding a record inside a loop body rejects at `expr.walrus`.** `saved = (p := Point(i))` inside a `for` body, with `saved` declared before the loop and `p.x = 99` after the walrus, is refused with *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.walrus)*; CPython prints `99` for `saved.x` after the loop. It used to compile and copy where CPython aliases (`ScopeTracker.lend_roots` has no `TpyNamedExpr` arm, so the scope-escape check never saw the walrus source); the reject replaced that silent copy. Fix shape: an aliasing walrus lowering for a record, with `lend_roots` resolving a `TpyNamedExpr` to its bound name so the escape check covers it. Workaround: bind first (`p = Point(i); saved = p`). - **[MED small] (warned wrong output) A loop-body local captured CONDITIONALLY mid-loop observes the LAST iteration's value, not the captured one.** `saved = Point(0); for i in range(3): p = Point(i); if i == 0: saved = p` then `return saved.x` gives TPy `2`, CPython `0`. The loop-body local's storage is hoisted to ONE function-scope slot, so every iteration emplaces over the same object and an alias taken earlier follows it. WARNED since the escape diagnostic was reworded to state the consequence ("'saved' will not keep the object it was given") and name `copy()`, so this is an acknowledged divergence rather than a silent one -- but the emitted program is still wrong for anyone who does not act on the warning. Needs no post-loop code, which makes it the most reachable shape of the family. Reproduces identically in a generator/frame context. Fixing it needs per-iteration storage: a slot per BINDING still leaves iterations of one binding sharing a slot. Two mechanisms were prototyped and discarded (see TODO.md) -- a two-slot rotation and a move-at-escape. Repro:
  ```python
  saved = Point(0)
  for i in range(3):
      p = Point(i)
      if i == 0:
          saved = p
  return saved.x   # TPy 2, CPython 0
  ```
  Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the block-local scope-revoke branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

The for-head hoist admits the name (the pointer flavor every ladder shares since 2026-09-14) and each bind site takes a function-scope `__slot_N`, which the module init has no home for: `_rejects_global_slot` (`tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`) turns every slot-allocating node into the reject. Inside a function the same shape lowers (`cases/control_flow/hoist_nonvalue_read_after_loop`). **Fix shape:** the hoisted pointer-slot global already owns a `static std::optional<T> __global_slot_N` per write site (the GLOBAL_HOIST_RVALUE arm); a loop-hoisted global should route its per-site slots there instead of the function-scope family. - **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, `__del__`-observable only) A non-value local hoisted at an `if` inside a loop and aliased in the same iteration drops the superseded object at the REBIND, one statement before CPython.** [`loop-if-hoist-alias-early-del`] `for i in xs: if c: f = Flat(i) else: f = Flat(-i); g = f` -- both arms reseat one function-top `std::optional<Flat> __slot_N`, so the next iteration's `f = Flat(..)` destroys the object `g` still names in CPython (which waits for `g`'s own rebind): with a `__del__` that prints, TPy prints `del 0` before the next iteration's first line, CPython after it. No read can observe the clobber (the alias is block-scoped in C++), so it is the destructor-order half of the tension the entry above documents (a slot per site would fix the order and break the eager drop `records/destructor_reassign` pins); the fix is the same liveness-aware slot design. Pre-existing tension on master `ecc8da665a`, new witness.

- **[LOW small] (CPython-parity gap in the stubs, not the compiler) A `Deref` type's transparent dereference is TPy-only -- the `lib/cpy` stub forwards no attribute access, so the same source raises `AttributeError` under CPython.** `r = Rc.new(Point(1)); r.x` reads the payload's field in TPy (`__deref__`), but `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py`'s `Deref` protocol only declares `__deref__` and nothing forwards `__getattr__`/`__setattr__`, so CPython looks the attribute up on the handle and fails. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) ANY local first declared in a try's `else` body fails the C++ build: the handlers' `goto` crosses its initialization.** [`try-else-body-decl-crossed-by-goto`] Everyday shape, plain function, nothing after the try needed: `try: print(100 // d)` / `except ValueError: pass` / `else: t = 0; print(t)` -- g++ `jump to label '__after_else_1' ... crosses initialization of 'int32_t t'` (verified 2026-09-28, `/tmp/agents/bundle3/row3/impl/v/else1.py`). Raised MED -> HIGH 2026-09-28: it was filed as needing an assignment after the try, but a fresh local alone hits it. A `return` in that `else` body under a `finally` hits the same cause: its pending-return capture (`auto* __tpy_retp_0 = ...` / `__tpy_ret_0`) is declared in the unbraced `else` and crossed by `goto __after_else_N` -- `jump to label '__after_else_1'`, scalar and tuple returns alike (probes `/tmp/agents/rv3r3/p/e1_else.py`..`e3_else.py`, fails on `a6a22715c3` too, 2026-09-23). `try: ... except E: pass else: n = 7` then `n = 9` after the try. Every other block-emitting statement revokes its declarations at the block close so the post-block assignment declares the function-scope local (`cases/control_flow/block_local_reassign_after`), but the `else` body emits UNBRACED in the enclosing C++ scope with the handlers' `goto __after_else_N` jumping past it, so a fresh declaration there is crossed by the jump -- g++: `jump to label '__after_else_1' crosses initialization of 'int32_t n'`. A warned copy's temp hits it too (and since the exception-edge liveness fix, a consume in the `else` followed by any statement, whose `finally` reads the name): `else: keep(p); print(len(p.xs)); break` under a `finally` declares `P __tmp_1 = p;` in the unbraced `else` (`/tmp/agents/lja/try_else_copy_break.py`, fails on a0bf4f4671 too; since the loop-jump liveness fix a plain `else: keep(p); break` whose `finally` reads `p` reaches it as well). Site: `_emit_try_except` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:2796`) writes the else body at the ENCLOSING `level` and appends `{label}:;` after it (`:2830`). Fix shape: brace the else body (`{ ... }` with the label outside) and scope-revoke it like the other blocks. NB that brace changes emitted C++ for every try/else case (4 snapshots: `control_flow/try_except_shapes`, `control_flow/with_exit_isinstance_class_dispatch`, `exceptions/throw_else`, `exceptions/throw_else_var`). Repro:
  ```python
  try:
      print(100 // d)
  except ZeroDivisionError:
      pass
  else:
      n = 7
  n = 9        # g++: jump to label '__after_else_1' crosses initialization
  ```
 Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A tuple-unpack of an `Own[Optional[T]]`-element call result onto a pointer-form Optional frame local fails the C++ build: the unpack temp is pointer-lifted, then the frame arm can't convert.** In a generator/async body, `saved, extra = make_pair(9)` (returning `tuple[Own[Optional[Point]], int32]`, `saved: Optional[Point]` pre-declared) emits `auto __tup_1 = ::tpy::tuple_to_pointer<std::tuple<Point*, int32_t>>(make_pair(9));` -- the owning call result is converted to BORROW form at the unpack temp -- and the frame unpack arm then emits `saved = ::tpy::optional_to_ptr(std::get<0>(__tup_1));`, which does not compile (`optional_to_ptr` has no `T*` overload). Even if it converted, the pointer would aim into the conversion's dying temporary. The SYNC path for the same source works (it materializes the storage tuple and moves the element into a persistent rebind slot). Fix shape: form selection, not a slot patch -- the unpack temp must stay STORAGE form when any target is a pointer-form frame field (then the element copies into a per-site frame slot like the scalar rvalue writes), which intersects the mixed-Own-tuple per-element form work. Probe `/tmp/agents/probe1/main.py` (sync twin in `main2.py`). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the frame ptr-slot placement fix, which initially misread it as a silent UAF -- the toolchain catches it. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; internal names in the diagnostic, pre-existing) In a generator, a local aliasing a list parameter cannot be rebound to a new list.** [`generator-param-alias-rebind`] `def gen(xs: list[float]) -> Iterator[int32]: ys = xs; ys = [x * 2.0 for x in xs]; yield len(ys)` fails with `in function 'gen': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (res.alias_bind)`; CPython runs it. The same body in a plain function compiles: the alias is a pointer that the rebind reseats to a `__slot_N` holder of the new value. The resumable frame has no such holder for the rebind (`_lower_alias_bind`, tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py); the reject-queue row for that site (`scripts/thir_migration/review/bins_stmt2.json`, `res.alias_bind`) records only its async twin (`a = items[0]` reseated from a constructor call). Distinct from `BUGS.md#resumable-alias-identity`, an alias of a tuple element held by value. Probe `/tmp/agents/ihc-impl/gen_alias.py` (and `/tmp/agents/ihc/split/gen.py`, whose int comprehension is now refused first). Found while fixing the inferred-hint int-to-float conversion.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (rejects-valid, located; was a silent wrong value) An alias of an element held BY VALUE in a tuple frame slot that the body can rebind AFTER the alias is rejected.** [`resumable-alias-identity`] In a generator or `async def`, `t = (A(1), A(2)); saved = t[1]; yield saved.v; if c: t = (A(9), A(8))` rejects (`alias.rebound_tuple_slot_elem`, `_rebound_tuple_alias_reject` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) with a located diagnostic in the program's names: `binding 'saved' to an element inside 't' is not yet supported in a generator when 't' can be reassigned while 'saved' is live; bind 'saved' after the last reassignment of 't'` (reason tag `res.alias_bind` still on the error object). The diagnostic names only that rebind-first remedy, which compiles for every path. Binding a copy (`saved = copy(t[1])`) is the documented other workaround, not suggested: it compiles for one subscript off an all-owned slot (`t[1]`) and for a record field then a list subscript (`t[0].xs[1]`), but not off a MIXED slot, a nested tuple or a tuple reached through a container or a field (BUGS.md#tuple-elem-copy-mixed-or-list-rejects), nor for a non-copyable element. Both workarounds are pinned by `generators/frame_tuple_elem_alias`; before 2026-09-22 it compiled and printed `2 8 8` where CPython prints `2 2 8`, because the rebind emplaces the new tuple into the same `frame_slot<std::tuple<A, A>>` the alias points into. The reject applies when the path from the frame slot to the aliased element crosses a tuple held by value (the slot itself counts) and some write of the slot can run after the alias -- later in program order, in the body of a loop enclosing both (a loop's `else` does not count), or from a nested def through `nonlocal`. Shapes that reject: the literal rebind above, the owning-CALL rebind (`t = make_pair(1); saved = t[1]; ...; t = make_pair(2)`, was `1 2` vs `1 1`), the `async def` twin (was `2` vs `1`), the OWNED element of a MIXED slot (`t = (A(1), b); saved = t[0]; ...; t = (A(9), b)`, was `1 9` vs `1 1`), the CHAINED paths of subscript and field hops: a nested tuple `t = ((A(1), A(2)), A(3)); saved = t[0][1]` (generator and async), a list inside a tuple `t = ([A(1), A(2)], 2); saved = t[0][1]`, a record field inside a tuple (`t = (H(1), 5); saved = t[0].xs[1]` and `t[0].p[1]`, generator and async), a tuple inside a list slot `xs = [(A(1), A(2))]; saved = xs[0][1]; ...; xs = [(A(9), A(8))]`, and a container root crossing a record's TUPLE field (`xs[0].p[1]` on a list, mutated or literal, and `d[1].p[1]` on a dict -- before, a wrong value or a dangle); a rebind in a `finally` after an alias in an `except` handler (was `2 8 8` vs `2 2 8`); and a rebind from a nested def through `nonlocal t`, which before failed the C++ build (`frame_slot` has no `operator=`, see the record twin in BUGS.md#nested-def-nonlocal-frame-slot-assign) rather than going wrong silently. The error cases pin four of them: `generators/error_frame_tuple_elem_alias_rebind` (literal), `error_frame_tuple_elem_alias_rebind_mixed` (async, mixed owned element), `error_frame_list_of_tuples_elem_alias_rebind` (tuple inside a list slot) and `error_frame_tuple_chained_alias_rebind` (field hop `t[0].xs[1]`). Still admitted and correct (`generators/frame_tuple_elem_alias`): an alias with no later rebind -- every rebind before the alias, or no rebind at all -- and an alias of a BORROWED element (already a pointer; its object lives outside the slot, so a rebind leaves it alone). A rebind in a branch exclusive with the alias but later in program order still rejects (the timing test is positional, not path-sensitive). The real fix is plan unit U5: the record shape closed with the alias-gated slot model (a record local with an OWN rebind goes pointer-form over per-site frame fields), but a tuple is a value type, so the alias-rebind storage pass never stamps its rebinds -- opening that gate needs the per-element ownership verdict per rebind site, minted today only in codegen (`init_verdict` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`), decided once in sema, plus the tuple twin of that frame form (a pointer over per-site `frame_slot<std::tuple<..>>` fields). A BORROW-form tuple local (`t = (a, 2); saved = t[0]; t = (b, 3)`) reseats pointers at objects that live elsewhere and must stay quiet. **Scope note on the sinks:** of the consuming sinks an owning tuple frame local can reach, only the yield renders today -- a free-call arg, a container insert and a constructor arg fail closed at lowering (`expr.call:call.arg_shape.own_tuple`, `expr.method_call:method.arg_shape`, `expr.call:call.ctor_arg.own_tuple`, measured 2026-09-10); widening them must bring the alias question with them.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; internal names in the diagnostic, pre-existing) Binding a local to a reference element of a MIXED tuple local or of a tuple inside a list -- by alias or by `copy()` -- is refused, in a plain function too.** [`tuple-elem-copy-mixed-or-list-rejects`] `t = (A(1), b); saved = copy(t[0])` (`b: A` a parameter) rejects at `stmt.var_decl:subscript.tuple_shape` in a plain function and at `subscript.tuple_shape` in a generator or `async def`; `xs = [(A(1), A(2))]; saved = copy(xs[0][1])` rejects the same way, also over a mutated list or a `list[tuple[A, A]]` parameter, and the plain alias `saved = xs[0][1]` rejects at `stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type`. CPython runs all of them. The all-owned tuple's `copy(t[1])`, the chained `copy(t[0].xs[1])` and the element read `xs[0][1].x` compile. The refusal is the tuple-subscript admission in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` (the `subscript.tuple_shape` raise): none of its rows admits a reference element of a mixed storage tuple, or of a container element tuple, as a `copy()` argument or a declaration source. In a generator the same refusal reaches every `copy()` of a tuple element whose tuple is not the frame slot itself: a nested tuple `t = ((A(1), A(2)), A(3)); copy(t[0][1])` (the outer tuple all-owned or mixed), a record's tuple field `t = (H(1), 5); copy(t[0].p[1])`, over a list `xs = [H(1)]; copy(xs[0].p[1])` or a dict `copy(d[1].p[1])`, a list of tuples inside a tuple `copy(t[0][0][1])`, a list held directly in a tuple `t = ([A(1), A(2)], 2); copy(t[0][1])` (at `subscript.recv_type`, in a plain function too, where the plain alias `saved = t[0][1]` rejects at `decl.tuple_literal_shape`; probes `/tmp/agents/cgr2/p/p7.py`, `/tmp/agents/r2f/p7_plain2.py`, `p7_plain3.py`; the generator case is pinned by `generators/error_frame_tuple_list_elem_alias_rebind`), and a record local's tuple field `h = H(1); copy(h.p[1])`, whose plain alias compiles (probes `/tmp/agents/r1r/v2.py`, `v3.py`, `v5.py`-`v9.py`); a final hop into a list (`copy(t[0].xs[1])`, also off a mixed slot) compiles. The BUGS.md#resumable-alias-identity diagnostic names only its rebind-first remedy: `copy()` compiles for the shapes listed above (one subscript off an all-owned tuple slot, `t[1]`; a record field then a list subscript, `t[0].xs[1]`) but never for a non-copyable element (`@nocopy`, or a record holding one; `generators/error_frame_nocopy_elem_alias_rebind`), and is documented in docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md, not suggested. Probes `/tmp/agents/u4a/m_plain.py`, `m_gen.py`, `p_copy_mut.py`, `p_copy_param.py`, `p_alias_mut.py` (2026-09-29).

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A record local declared inside a TOP-LEVEL loop body is emitted as a C++ function-local `static`, so it is constructed ONCE and every later iteration reuses the stale object.** [`top-level-loop-local-static-slot`] At module scope the slot carries `static` so it outlives `__tpy_init` (`slots.global_scope`), but inside a top-level `while`/`for` body that makes the initializer run only on the first pass: `i = 0` / `while i < 3: q = Point(i * 10); print(q.x); i += 1` emits `static Point __global_slot_1 = Point(i * 10);` and prints `0, 1, 2` (the value carried over and mutated) where CPython prints `0, 10, 20`. Silent: no diagnostic, wrong output. The same code inside a `def` is correct -- only module-level loops are affected, so it is easy to miss. A loop-local at module scope needs a non-static slot scoped to the loop body (or a static slot plus a per-iteration assignment), not a static initializer. **Settle it together with [`block-level-module-binding-has-no-slot`]**, the sibling defect over the same storage: that one is about a block-level top-level binding codegen emits NO slot for at all, and its fix shape (a namespace-scope slot ASSIGNED where the block assigns it, not initialized there) is the one that satisfies both -- a per-iteration assignment is exactly what this entry needs. Found probing `declare_rebind_slot`'s global-scope branch for test coverage.

The three lower to structurally different C++ (loop induction variable / `__enter__` result decl / arm capture decl), so each needs its own sema route + AST arm + THIR arm -- no shared emit chokepoint. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A binary operand is re-read AFTER a sibling operand's walrus writes it, so the left operand sees the new value.** `n = 1; return n + (n := n + 100)` yields 202 where CPython yields 102 -- C++ leaves the two operands of `+` unsequenced, and codegen renders the left operand as a bare name read rather than materializing it before the walrus assigns.
