- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A membership needle or chained-comparison operand is re-read after a sibling operand assigns to it.** `c.n in (bump(c), 1)` and `0 < a.x < bump(a)` (where `bump` writes the operand) answer TPy `False` / CPython `True`: CPython reads each operand once, before the siblings run, while TPy renders it where the write is already visible. Probes `/tmp/agents/chain-dup/{widen,nameneedle,chainwrite,subscript2,walrus4}.py`. Affects every operand shape that names storage -- a bare name, a field, a subscript, a walrus target and a ternary of lvalues were each confirmed on this branch; an operand that renders its own value (a call, a property) is unaffected, since nothing can write it. Same root as the two-operand ordering entry below and unfixed for the same reason -- a fix must capture the operand's VALUE before the sibling runs (a reference re-reads), which costs a copy on every chained compare with a call in it, to fix code that assigns to an operand mid-comparison. Implemented and REVERTED on `fix-operand-snapshot` after review: correct, but it bought a rare guarantee for four new operand predicates plus THIR node fields, and left the two-operand form still wrong, so the guarantee was incoherent. Do it with the two-operand entry, or not at all. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) Tuple-literal membership short-circuits the ELEMENTS, but CPython builds the tuple first and so evaluates every element.** Reachable for a `bytes` needle too since 2026-09-10, when the chain admitted the bytes family. `"A" in (a(), b())` runs only `a()` in TPy (the `==` OR-chain stops at the first match) where CPython runs both before `CONTAINS_OP` -- so an element's side effects are silently skipped. Probe `/tmp/agents/chain-dup/b2_probe.py` (TPy `evaluated: a`, CPython `evaluated: ab`). Distinct from the needle-vs-haystack ORDER entry above: that one is about which side runs first, this is about an element not running at all. The sibling half of the needle entry above: that one is about the needle being re-read, this one about an element never running. Both are open, and a fix for either should consider the other. A fix has to give up the OR-chain's short circuit (materialize every element, then compare) and so trades code size on the common all-literal form, which is why it is not a follow-on tweak. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A PLAIN re-assignment that widens an inferred-`int32` MODULE GLOBAL to `BigInt` emits invalid C++ instead of a diagnostic or a coercion.** `acc = 0` then `acc = acc * 10 + n` at module level with `n: int` (BigInt) keeps the global's `int32` width while the right side analyzes as `BigInt`, so g++ rejects the build (`mul_check` over mixed types; re-probed 2026-09-30, `/tmp/agents/pint/c/gw.py`). CPython has one arbitrary-precision int and accepts it. Workaround: annotate `acc: int = 0`. Fix shape: extend the pending integer locals to module variables, or refuse the store with the annotation to write. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid) The nested-capture retype reject is READ-INSENSITIVE: it fires even when the outer name is never read after the nested bind, where the program was correct before.** `_reject_nested_capture_retype` (`tpyc/sema/match.py`) keys on `rebound_captures`, which carries no post-bind-read condition, so `case Cat(lives=v): print(v); match b: case Dog(lives=v): pass` (int32 outer, int64 nested, `v` unread afterwards) is rejected although master compiled it and printed the CPython answer. Narrow: it needs BOTH an implicitly C++-convertible type pair AND no later read -- a non-convertible pair (`int`/`str`) already failed the build on master via the branch-decl hoist, and a later read is the truncation the gate exists to catch. The rejected programs are latent rather than correct (the truncating write into the shared slot does happen; only its result is unobserved), so the reject is a rename away and a future read would have made it a silent wrong answer -- that is why the gate ships read-insensitive rather than guessing. Fix shape: gate the error on the name being read after the nested bind, or restrict it to names the definite-assignment predecl would hoist anyway (a proxy for readable-after) and skip the hoist entirely when types disagree otherwise; a wrong read-analysis reinstates the silent truncation, so it needs its own verification pass. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid) A HOISTED `match` capture of a reference type drops the subject's const, so a never-mutated param subject yields `T* q;` against a `const T&` -- ill-formed C++.** `def show(h: Holder): match h: case Holder(inner=q): print(q.n)` with a post-match read of `q` emits `Inner* q;` then `q = &(__match_subject_1.inner);` where `h` renders `const Holder&`, so g++ reports `invalid conversion from 'const Inner*' to 'Inner*'`. Root cause is phase ordering: `record_stmt_borrow_binding` (`tpyc/sema/context.py:503`) derives the stmt-borrow const flag from the DECLARED type in Phase 1, but a borrowed param's const-ness is decided by mutation inference in Phase 2, so a capture of a never-mutated param reaches the hoist with const=False. Only the hoisted path is affected (a block-scoped `auto&` capture takes the subject's const-ness for free); the hoist fires via the branch-decl predecl (post-match read) or the rebound-capture predecl. A CONTAINER-typed field capture hits the same decl (`std::vector<int32_t>* q;` under a `const Holder&` subject, measured 2026-09-05), so the fix has to cover every reference type, not only records. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. `_route_hoists` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py:822`) picks the `"ptr_const"` flavor over `"ptr"` only when `_match_capture_borrows_const` (`:793`) sees a NESTED match re-seating the capture; the single-match shape stays on the Phase-1 verdict. The LOOP-BODY hoist reads the same stale verdict, so `match` is not the only face: `def mono_rec(items: list[Pic])` with `for it in items: held = it`, a sibling loop, then `print(held.n)` emits `void mono_rec(const std::vector<Pic>& items)` (Phase 2 inferred the param const) but `Pic* held;` and `held = &(it);`, which g++ rejects -- `invalid conversion from 'const Pic*' to 'Pic*'`. The DECLARED `readonly[list[Pic]]` twin emits `const Pic* held;` correctly, which is the Phase-1-vs-Phase-2 split in one pair, and the generic twin (`def gen_fn[T](items: list[T])`) is accepted into the same failing build (`invalid conversion from 'const int*' to 'int*'`). Probes `/tmp/agents/r2_codegen/{p19_monorec.py,p20_roalias.py,p18_generic.py}`, verified 2026-09-16. Fix shape: settle the borrow const verdict in Phase 2 (or route the decl through `tpyc/codegen_cpp/param_const.py`'s chokepoint), then widen the re-ask to the single-match shape. Surfaced by /tpy-fix-bug of the nested-match capture reuse. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) Mutating through a `match` class-pattern KEYWORD capture does not mark the subject param as mutating, so the emitted C++ writes through a `const` alias and fails to compile.** `def f(h: Holder): match h: case Holder(items=xs): xs.append(9)` emits `int32_t f(const Holder& h)` and then `push_back` on the resulting `const std::vector<int32_t>&` -- ill-formed. Mutation propagation enumerates writes through names and field paths but not through a match capture's alias into the subject, so the param keeps its const-borrow verdict. CPython accepts all three (the capture aliases the matched object). Blocks a corpus case that would give the reference-typed keyword-capture family an exec+cpy mutation witness -- today that family is covered only by THIR unit pins and read-only cases, which are parity-blind. Sibling of the HOISTED-capture const entry below and probably one fix: that one loses const on the pointer where the subject IS const, this one never makes the subject non-const in the first place -- both hang on where the borrow const verdict is settled. Distinct from the sibling-arm stale-alias and nested-rebind entries: this one is the subject param's const verdict, not the capture's own binding form. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion of the capture-rebind hoist. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

When this lowers, the rebind must also reach the int/float rebind refusal (`refuse_int_float_rebind`, `tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`): sema does not ask it for a `with` target today, so `x = 1; with cm() as x:` over a float `__enter__` would compile silently.

The reject is broader than the numeric case that motivated it: under POLYMORPHIC dispatch a nested reuse naming a different subclass (`case Square() as p:` / nested `case Circle() as p:` off a `@dynamic` protocol subject) is the idiomatic shape and is rejected, where it once silently returned the OUTER arm's object (probe: `4` vs CPython `27`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. The FLAT shape -- one capture name at different types in sibling arms of one `match`, each arm reading its own (`case Cat(lives=v): v = v + 1` / `case Dog(name=v): v = "d:" + v`) -- compiles since captures keep per-arm storage (the `capture_types` section of `tests/cases/control_flow/sibling_arm_join`); reading such a capture AFTER the match is `BUGS.md#match-capture-disagreeing-types-read-after`. - **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (diagnostic noise) Non-scalar field writes can warn when a call result borrows only the containing record.** [`record-field-borrow-false-invalidation`]
  Numeric/character stored-field writes no longer warn: assigning an integer or
  augmenting it preserves both the record and its field storage. The remaining
  distinction is a borrow of the whole record versus a borrow into a field's
  payload. A call returning the record itself can still leave an ELEMENT loan
  on its root, so replacing a string/container field warns even when the result
  only aliases the record and remains valid. The same replacement can invalidate
  a view into that field, and a property setter can replace arbitrary storage,
  so neither warning may be suppressed by the field's type alone. Resolve the
  projected borrow contract before narrowing these residual warnings.

Fix shape: a `bytearray_stepped_slice` returning `Own[bytearray]` (mirror of `bytes_stepped_slice`; bytearray is a reference type, so unlike the value-typed `bytes` returns the `Own` spelling is load-bearing there). - **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) `print(...)` writes each argument as it is evaluated, so an argument whose evaluation itself writes to stdout interleaves ahead of the earlier arguments' output.** [`print-arg-output-interleaves`] `print("prefix:", noisy())` where `noisy()` prints `side effect` and returns 7 emits `prefix: side effect` then `7`; CPython evaluates the whole argument list first and emits `side effect` then `prefix: 7`. The call lowers to a chained `std::cout << "prefix: " << noisy()`, and C++17 sequences an overloaded `<<`'s left operand before its right, so the literal reaches the stream before the callee runs. Silent, output-only, and needs a print argument that itself writes to stdout -- a debug/logging helper nested in a print is the realistic shape. Distinct from the reflected-binop and hoisted-arg ordering entries: those reorder the *evaluations*, this one interleaves the *output* while evaluation order is correct. Fix shape: evaluate every argument into temps before the first stream write (the temp-hoist machinery already exists for other arg shapes). The `WritableOstream` adapter (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/as_ostream.hpp`) forwards each `<<` of the chain, so a container or tuple argument arrives as its brackets, elements and separators (`print([1, 2], file=w)` makes `[`, `1`, `, `, `2`, `]`, `\n` -- six calls where CPython makes two), while an empty `sep=`/`end=`/`""` argument is dropped from the chain and `write("")` is never called. Output is byte-identical; only a sink that counts or inspects its pieces sees it. Fix shape: format each argument to a string before writing when the sink is a user record (the three concrete sinks stream directly and are unaffected), and keep the empty tokens. `tests/cases/exceptions/keyboard_interrupt_print` (`sink_tail`) cites this entry rather than pinning CPython's count. Surfaced by the `print()` check point review, 2026-10-01; the adapter was buffered before and split the same way.

Silent -- output-only, observable only when both operands carry side effects (no corpus case; `truediv_floordiv_distinct` uses names/literals). Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) probing the record-dunder rvalue admission (2026-07-22 wave). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) Membership with a CALL haystack evaluates the haystack before the needle -- CPython evaluates the needle first.** `needle_expr in f()` emits the haystack call's render first (the receiver of `.contains`/`.find`/`__contains__`), then the needle; CPython's bytecode evaluates the needle expression before the container expression, so when BOTH sides have side effects the observable order differs. Silent -- output-only divergence, only observable when both operand expressions carry side effects (rare; no corpus case). Pre-existing (unrelated to the `getitem_function_info` tagging); surfaced writing the accessor-generic-returns temporary-receiver test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (project const onto the const-twin ternary return arm, mirroring the statement-return path).

Repros `/tmp/agents/thir-tail-0821/impl-rd/smoke/e_prop_mut.py`. Same accessor-return family as the `@property` pointer-repr Optional entry below. - **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `@property` getter returning a pointer-repr `Optional[T]` (`-> Rec | None`) emits an `std::optional<T>&`-returning accessor whose body returns rvalues/nullptr -- uncompilable C++ for any non-field-backed getter.** [`property-getter-pointer-optional-return`] Reachable from the `@export` boundary too since Optional crosses it (2026-09-22): an exposed-class `@property -> Optional[Cls]` is admitted by the boundary validator and fails in the module half with the same error, one line away from where a non-ext program fails -- the fix is this entry, not a boundary-side reject. Same accessor-optional family as the record-`__getitem__` fix on `fix-accessor-generic-returns` -- there the CONSUMER was wrong, here the EMISSION convention is. - **[MED small] (miscompile) A plain record pointer-local reseated from a `readonly[T]` param emits `Point* p = &(q);` off a `const Point&` -- invalid const conversion, uncompilable.** `def f(q: readonly[Point], c: bool): p = Point(1); ...; p = q` renders the address-of without const-propagating the pointer decl (`const_indirect_locals` never sees the reseat-source constness). Identical on BOTH the AST and THIR paths (byte-identical, both broken); no corpus case exercises it. Either propagate const from the reseat source into the decl (making every read `const Point*`) or reject at sema (a mutable-pointer local aliasing a readonly param is arguably a readonly-model violation -- consider the sema-error tier first). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the escape-hoist cell.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Pending-container resolution never runs for a NESTED-function body, so ANY container literal declared inside a closure is unresolved at codegen.** [`nested-def-pending-container-unresolved`] The straight-line everyday shape is enough: `def outer(): def inner(): xs = [1, 2, 3]; xs.append(4); print(len(xs))` fails with `error: in function 'outer': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:container_lit.slot_family)` (the diagnostic names the ENCLOSING function, not the closure the literal is in). The free-function, method and top-level sites each call `LocalTypeDeduction.resolve_all()` immediately after `_prescan_and_analyze_body` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`); `_analyze_nested_def` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) is the one body site that does not, and `nested_def_scope` (`tpyc/sema/scope_tracker.py`) then discards the nested `FunctionTrackingState` via `restore_function_state`, so the nested body's pending stores -- `pending_branch_decl_maps`, `pending_composite_exprs`, `pending_loop_vars` -- are lost unfinalized and the enclosing function's later `resolve_all` never sees them. Second witness, a hard crash rather than a reject: a literal first declared inside an if/try/with/match BRANCH of a nested def reaches codegen as `PendingListType should be resolved before codegen` (`def outer(c): def inner(): if c: xs = [1, 2] else: xs = [3]; return xs[0]; return inner()`). Third witness, from the frame-captured-view hoist: `gen([1, 2, 3])` at a `Span[int32]` generator param inside a closure rejects with `generator/coroutine view argument's backing type is unresolved` -- the hoist spells its backing temp off the RESOLVED container type, and inside a nested def there is none. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/nested/a.py` (reject) and `/tmp/agents/nested/b.py` (view hoist). Fix shape: run the deduction pass for a nested body exactly as the outer one does -- `self.deduction.resolve_all()` inside the `nested_def_scope` block, right after `_prescan_and_analyze_body` -- which covers all three stores at once; that one line compiles both reproducers (corpus impact unmeasured). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + safety-model) of `fix-pendinglist-branch-decls`; broadened from the branch-only flavor while closing the frame-captured-view hoist. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (crash) A container instantiation over a literal with NESTED literal elements crashes codegen: `PendingListType should be resolved before codegen`.** `a = list([[1, 2], [3]])` (also the single-element `list([[1, 2]])`) at plain function scope -- no nested def, no branch topology, so this is NOT the nested-def lifecycle entry above. The OUTER literal resolves (it is the call's arg), but the inner literals stay `PendingListType` and reach `to_cpp()` through the ctor's `@cpp_template` substitution (`_resolve_cpp_template_type_params`, `tpyc/sema/calls.py:361` -> `typesys.py:4181`) -- the instantiation path never runs the nested-literal resolution that the equivalent annotated decl (`a: list[list[int32]] = [[1, 2], [3]]`) does. Flat element literals are fine (`list([1, 2])`); the named-local form (`src: list[list[int32]] = [[1, 2]]; a = list(src)`) compiles. Same expected-type-into-nested-literal family as the annotated dict-literal-of-list-literals entry below. Fix shape: resolve the arg literal's nested element types before the ctor template substitution reads them. Surfaced by adversarial dualgen probes around the THIR container-literal instantiation arm; pre-existing on master. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. A genexpr yielding the literal's elements into the instantiation reaches the same crash (`list(r for r in grid)`), and handing one to an `Iterable[list[int32]]` parameter is a loud reject instead (`Type <genexpr>[PendingList...] does not conform to protocol Iterable[list[int32]]`): the yield type is still the unsettled literal type when the call is checked. Seen reviewing the genexpr frames 2026-09-21.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A NESTED list literal first declared in sibling branches (`try: xs = [[1, 2]] except ...: xs = [[3]]`) fails the C++ build at the branch slot-assign render.** The branch-decl force now resolves both nesting levels to plain `vector` (the type side is sound -- `_force_branch_decl_lists` recurses into the pending element type), but the slot-assign arm renders the nested literal as a flat brace-init against `std::optional<std::vector<std::vector<int>>>`, which trips the explicit `vector(size_type, alloc)` constructor (g++ "would use explicit constructor"). Flat literals work; a nested literal in a PLAIN decl also works (different emit arm) -- only the branch predecl slot-assign spelling is wrong. Probe `/tmp/agents/plfix/p_nested1.py`. Fix shape: render the literal through the same nested-container emit the plain decl uses (typed construction, not bare brace-init) at the slot-assign arm. Surfaced by the readiness retrospective's nested-literal probe on `fix-pendinglist-branch-decls`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Calling an `auto_own[Self]` method directly on a freshly-constructed temporary fails the C++ build.** `Pair[Node](a, b).first()` passes sema, selects the consuming (`&&`) overload, and moves the field -- but codegen still types the bound local as `Node&`, so g++ rejects it ("cannot bind non-const lvalue reference to an rvalue"). The named-local form (`p = Pair[Node](a, b); p.first()`) compiles: a general method call hard-codes `is_consuming_receiver=False` (`tpyc/sema/methods.py`), so only the rvalue-receiver syntax reaches the consuming overload. Fix shape: bind the consuming call's result by value (or reject the rvalue-receiver form at sema) -- decide which, the render is currently inconsistent with the overload it selected. Pre-existing on master (verified in a worktree); surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) while checking the auto_own clone-pair carve-out. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid) Reassigning an alias to a NESTED list element fails when the outer list is unannotated.** `m = [[Point(1)], [Point(2)]]; row = m[0]; row = m[1]` errors with `Type mismatch in reassignment to 'row': expected list[Point], got Ref[PendingList[Point, 1]#0]` -- the element's pending type never resolves before the reassignment compatibility check, so the SECOND bind compares a resolved `list[Point]` against a raw pending node. The annotated form (`m: list[list[Point]] = ...`) compiles and runs. Two defects in one: the code is valid and rejected, and the message leaks the internal repr (the same leak as the pending aug-op entry above, different trigger). Repro `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/bugcheck/main.py`. Fix shape: resolve the subscript result's pending element type before `coerce_reassignment` compares it. Surfaced by adversarial dualgen probes around the THIR element-borrow decl arm; pre-existing on master, unrelated to that cell. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A container literal first declared in a try's ELSE body (with the except-handler declaring the same name) emits assignments to an undeclared predecl slot -- g++ `'xs' was not declared in this scope` / `'__slot_N' was not declared`.** `try: ... except ValueError: xs = [3] else: xs = [1, 2]` then a post-try read: the branch-decl predecl machinery covers the handler's decl but the ELSE body's assignment renders the slot/pointer form (`xs = &*(__slot_2 = {1, 2})`) without the corresponding declarations reaching its scope. The try/except both-branch merge (decl in try body + handler) works; only the else-body topology is broken. Pending-type resolution is NOT the issue (the resolved brace-init shows in the bad emit) -- this is a predecl scoping hole in the try emit. Probe `/tmp/agents/plfix/p_try_else.py`. Surfaced pinning a cpython-parity probe during the `fix-pendinglist-branch-decls` review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A tuple ternary whose arms carry DIFFERENT C++ tuple forms is a hard compile error.** `t = p if c else h.pair` (a borrow-form `std::tuple<int32, Box*>` param against a storage-form `std::tuple<int32, Box>` field) prints `error: in function 'f': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type)` -- the decl's slot ladder (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:9978`) has no row for a ternary whose arms disagree on tuple form, so nothing lifts one side to the other's. The const-qualification twin is caught earlier and better, by sema: two params differing only in `readonly[...]` on an element give `Incompatible types in ternary expression: 'tuple[int32, Box]' and 'tuple[int32, readonly[Box]]'`. Loud either way. Fix shape: give the tuple ternary a row that lifts a storage arm via `tuple_to_pointer`, or reject the mixed pair in sema with the message the readonly twin already gets. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the wave-next13 tuple-ternary admission. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (misleading diagnostic) The per-element `Own`-coercion warning and error name the WHOLE tuple where a single element is at stake.** Rebinding a mixed tuple local to an all-borrow storage source (`p = h.pair` for `p: tuple[Own[Box], Box]`) warns `copies tuple[Box, Box] into owned storage; use copy() to make this explicit` -- but only element 0 is copied; element 1 still aliases, which the pinned case's own output shows (`elem0: 7`, `elem1: 66`). The `@nocopy` variant is worse: `cannot copy tuple[Guard, Box] into owned storage of type 'Guard'; target is non-copyable` conflates the whole-tuple SOURCE type with one element's TARGET type in a single sentence. Root cause: the tuple-to-tuple element-wise compat recursion (`_check_compat`, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py` ~1141) passes the whole-tuple `source_expr` unchanged into each per-element check, so the generic Own-coercion message reads `get_expr_type(source_expr)` -- the aggregate -- instead of the element's own type. The sibling `warn_pointer_repr_tuple_copy` path (container append) already gets this right and appends `(tuple element i)`, so it is the fix shape: pass the element's source (or at least the index) into the per-element check. Not silent and not a miscompile, but it weakens the "warned, therefore acknowledged" premise the `tuple/mixed_own_tuple_local_realias` `no_cpython` pin rests on -- a user can reasonably read it as "the whole tuple is deep-copied". Pre-existing in `compatibility.py`; newly REACHABLE because the mixed-tuple rebind now compiles. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the mixed-tuple decl-path fix. The same text now declares the argument copy at a MIXED tuple PARAM (`borrow_write(t)` for a live mixed local reads `copies tuple[Own[Box], Box] into owned storage`, and a live fully owned param `copies tuple[Own[Box], Own[Box]] ...`), where only the owned element is copied (`tests/cases/tuple/mixed_own_param_writes`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Param mutation inference does not reach through a TERNARY call argument, so a param mutated only via a ternary is inferred const and the C++ build fails.** `def via(b: Box, c: Box, pick: bool) -> int32: return bump(b if pick else c)` (where `bump(b: Box)` writes `b.val`) emits `int32_t via(const Box& b, const Box& c, bool pick)` and then `bump(((pick) ? (b) : (c)))` -- g++ `binding reference of type 'Box&' to 'const Box' discards qualifiers`. Passing the same param DIRECTLY (`bump(b)`) infers `Box&` correctly, so the gap is the ternary arg specifically: `mutation_propagation` walks call args but does not descend into a `TpyIfExpr` to attribute the callee's mutation to each arm's name. Loud (toolchain-caught), no TPy diagnostic, pre-existing (reproduces at merge base). Any arg shape that wraps names in an expression is worth checking with it (an `and`/`or` arm is the obvious sibling). Workaround: bind the selected object to a local first, or use an if/else statement. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/mixdecl/y2_ternary_const.py`. Surfaced probing decl paths during the mixed-tuple borrow-position work. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Param mutation inference does not reach a LOOP ELEMENT passed to a mutating callee, so the source param is inferred const and the C++ build fails.** `def f(*ps: Point): for p in ps: touch(p)` (where `touch(p: Point)` writes `p.x`) emits `void f(::tpy::varargs<const Point> ps)` and then `touch(p)` -- g++ `binding reference of type 'Point&' to 'const Point' discards qualifiers`. Mutating the element DIRECTLY in the loop body (`p.x += 1`) infers the mutable slot correctly, so the gap is specifically a mutation that only happens inside a callee: `mutation_propagation` attributes the callee's param mutation to the loop VARIABLE, and neither the vararg flip (`_maybe_flip_vararg_readonly`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) nor its sibling `_sync_inferred_const` climbs from a loop var to the container/pack it iterates. Not vararg-specific and not generator-specific -- measured on all four cells: `*args` pack and plain `list[Point]` param, each on a plain function and on a generator (the generator twin emits `touch((*p))` against the same const element). Loud (toolchain-caught), no TPy diagnostic; pre-existing (the vararg flip and the const inference both predate the frame's varargs admission). A generator expression's source is a PARAM of the function sema builds for it, so since genexprs became frames this also reaches a genexpr over a LOCAL list (`sum(len(r) for r in ll if append_one(r))`, which the closure render compiled). Workaround: mutate the element inline in the loop body, or take an explicitly mutable slot. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/fixround/p17_flip.py` (pack, plain fn), `p18_flip_gen.py` (pack, generator), `p19_list_sibling.py` (plain `list` param). The tuple-element spelling is the same gap: `for c in cs: bump((c, 1))` with `bump(p: tuple[A, int])` writing `p[0]` binds `c` mutable and leaves `cs` const (`/tmp/agents/u1r3/lv.py`, beside the scalar `lv1.py`, 2026-09-26). Fix shape: mutation propagation must map "loop var over X is mutated" back to X (the same climb `_borrow_storage_root`/`loop_var_iterable` already record for borrow tracking), so both const-inference flips see it. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the resumable-frame varargs admission. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A container literal first declared inside a TRY body of a generator/async function types the frame slot from one arm's fixed-size Array while the writes emplace a vector -- g++ "no matching function for call to `emplace`".** `async def f(n): try: xs = [n, n] except ValueError: xs = [0]` + a post-try read emits `::tpy::frame_slot<std::array<int32_t, 1>> xs;` (the size from the HANDLER's literal) against `xs.emplace(std::vector<int32_t>{n, n});` -- the write site reads the sema branch-decl snapshot (forced off the Array optimization by `_force_branch_decl_lists`, so `list[int32]`), but the frame-slot field is spelled from `func.generator_locals`, which keeps the unforced per-decl type. The if/else and match-arm topologies are correct (their frame local carries the merged list), so the gap is the generator-locals collection not consulting the branch-decl snapshot. Loud (toolchain-caught). Repro `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/smoke13/trybody4/main.py` (`tpyc --dump-code` shows the mismatch directly). Fix shape: apply the branch-decl snapshot type when collecting generator locals (the same override `_emit_branch_decls` performs on `var_types`), so the slot and its writes agree. NB THIR mirrors the WRITE side by applying that same override (`lc.frame_local_types` in `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py`); when the slot spelling is fixed, both paths stay in lockstep. Surfaced by the THIR branch-nested frame-decl cell (wave-next13). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, latent] A MIXED async tuple return (pointer-repr record element + value element) emits uncompilable C++ at BOTH ends -- the surviving sibling of the fixed value-tuple untargeted render.** `async def mixed(r: Rec, n) -> tuple[Rec, int32 | None]: return (r, None)` is sema-accepted and breaks twice: (1) the callee's return render stays untargeted -- `std::tuple<Rec, std::optional<int32_t>> __tpy_async_ret = std::tuple<Rec*, std::monostate>{&(r), nullptr};` -- because the tuple-literal-targeted arm in `_async_return_value_cpp` deliberately gates on `not has_pointer_repr_element()` (the async return slot is the STORAGE tuple even for mixed shapes, so the borrow-form spelling never converts); (2) the CALLER's await-bind declares the frame field in borrow form (`std::tuple<Rec*, std::optional<int32_t>> a;`) and assigns the callee's storage tuple into it (`a = std::move(__r0).value();` -- no operator=). Fixing (1) is not just widening the gate: a param-rooted record element at a storage slot needs the sync arm's deref-COPY discipline (`tuple_to_storage` family), and (2) is a borrow/storage-form decision at the frame boundary -- the recurring duality class (docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md "Borrow Form vs Storage Form"). Both shapes unreached in the corpus; probes `/tmp/agents/fix-async-ret/probe_retro.py` (return site) + `probe_mixed_call.py` (both sites). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion on the value-tuple render fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (consider sema-rejecting the shape first if the form design is deferred).
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) An `async with` whose `__aexit__` is typed `exc_val: None -> bool` (a suppressing manager) compiles without a diagnostic but does NOT suppress a body exception -- TPy panics with an uncaught exception where CPython suppresses and continues.** The `None`-typed `exc_val` slots past the block that gates the `Optional[BaseException]` suppression form (`BUGS.md` async-with entry / the diagnostic at that path), so this shape silently emits non-suppressing cleanup. Distinct from the documented `exc_val: Optional[BaseException]` async-with-suppression gap (blocked by a diagnostic): this variant compiles clean and miscompiles. Pre-existing -- reproduces on `ffb79ebbef`, unrelated to the cleanup-double-run fix; surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) probing adjacent shapes. Fix shape: either reject the `exc_val: None` + `bool`-return async-`__aexit__` shape with the same diagnostic the `Optional` form gets, or implement suppression for it. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (coordinate with the async-with suppression design).
- **[MED small] (missing diagnostic) The `'raise' in '__del__' cannot propagate` warning skips `try` subtrees, so a `__del__` that raises from inside a `try`/`except`/`finally` compiles silently.** A bare `raise` in `__del__` warns at the raise line; the same raise inside any `try` subtree (handler body, `finally` body, or the `try` body itself) produces NO warning -- the walker that finds raise sites does not descend into `TpyTry`. The user's only signal is the runtime `TurboPython panic: uncaught exception in __del__` abort (`tests/cases/exceptions/panic_del_try_finally_raise` pins it). Reproducer `/tmp/agents/finally-fix/probe_del.py` (silent) vs `probe_del_bare.py` (warns). Fix shape: descend into `try_body`/handler bodies/`finally_body` when collecting `__del__` raise sites. Was previously noted only as an aside inside the finally-fall-through-elision entry (whose other half is now fixed); re-filed standalone so it isn't lost. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (silent CPython divergence) A `return <reference-type local>` under a finally that CONTAINS a suspension (`await`/`yield` -- the CFG pending-return lowering) still captures the value eagerly, so the suspending finally's mutation of the local is invisible in the returned object.** The CFG arm parks the value in the frame's `__finally_ret_<n>` slot before transitioning to the finally states; a deferred borrow there would be a frame-self-pointer surviving suspensions (the async-borrow-escape family, BUGS 309/311), and multiple return sites share one slot, so deferral needs a parked discriminant (which return fired) materialized at AsyncFinallyExit -- or frame pinning. Excluded from the finally-deferred-capture fix in `liveness.collect_finally_return_candidates` (suspension check suppresses the WHOLE subtree of a suspending-finally try, so this also covers a return under an inner NON-suspending finally with a suspending-finally ancestor -- probe `/tmp/agents/finally-return-mut/probe_cfg_inner.py`, same eager-copy divergence, and the list shape keeps its loud copy() error there). Probe `/tmp/agents/finally-return-mut/probe_cfg.py`: TPy 10, CPython 11. For a `@nocopy` payload the eager pending-slot store (`this->__finally_ret_<n> = ...`) is a deleted-copy-assignment C++ BUILD FAILURE, not just a silent divergence. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. The eager copy also carries no `copies ... into owned storage` warning (`this->__finally_ret_0 = (*p);`, noticed 2026-09-25 by the liveness exit-edges review).
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] A `nonlocal` REBIND inside a nested def overwrites the outer local's storage IN PLACE (no slot model), observable through any alias of that local.** [`nonlocal-rebind-overwrites-in-place`] When the outer local is itself an ALIAS (`x = b`, or a borrowed tuple-unpack target `x, k = one(b)`), the closure's `nonlocal x; x = q` writes `q` into `b` (TPy `80 8`, CPython `1 80`; verified 2026-09-22). `scan_reassigned_vars` deliberately does not recurse into nested defs, so a local rebound ONLY via `nonlocal b; b = ...` in a closure never gets the `__slot_N` pointer indirection a direct rebind gets -- the closure's assignment clobbers the same C++ storage, where CPython rebinding leaves the old object alive for existing references. The finally-deferred return capture EXCLUDES such names from deferral (`liveness._collect_nested_def_nonlocal_rebinds`) so the pure-rebind-from-finally shape keeps the CPython-correct eager copy; the residual: a closure that both MUTATES and rebinds the name, called from a finally around `return <name>`, loses the mutation in the returned object (eager copy, TPy pre-mutation vs CPython post-mutation). Fix shape: teach `scan_reassigned_vars` to count nested-def nonlocal writes as reassignments (slot model), then drop the deferral exclusion -- corpus-wide codegen change for closures that rebind. NOW ALSO REACHABLE IN RESUMABLE BODIES: since nested defs in async defs/generators compile (frame member functions), the same in-place rebind clobbers the frame FIELD -- an alias taken before the rebind sees the new object (TPy `1,999,999` vs CPython `1,1,999`); previously that shape was a loud C++ build error. Probes `/tmp/agents/finally-review/probe_closure_rebind2.py`, `/tmp/agents/nested_probe/p2_alias_rebind.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + cpython-parity) of the structural-deferral widening; resumable reachability by the nested-def frame-member review. The alias-gated slot model (2026-09-14) leaves a `nonlocal` rebind FOREIGN by construction: the storage is the enclosing function's, and a slot of the closure's own would die with the lambda, so the lowering keeps rejecting an rvalue rebind of an enclosing POINTER-local (`nested_def.rebind_slot_hoist`) and a plain-storage outer local still takes the in-place write above. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid) The closure-del guard for finally-deferred returns fires without reachability analysis: a nested def deling the returned name is rejected even when the closure is only invoked from a handler or the normal path, never from a finally.** `_check_closure_del_of_deferred_returns` pairs any deferred `return x` with any nested-def `nonlocal x; del x` in the function; under structural candidacy this rejects programs that previously compiled (probe: return in try, closure-del called only from an except handler, finally empty). Sound but over-broad by design (documented in the helper). Fix shape: narrow to closures reachable from a finally body's call expressions, or accept and document. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A pre-try alias bind of a local read later in a finally consumes it eagerly: `a = b; try: return a; finally: b.n += 1` moves `b` into `a` at the bind, so the finally's mutation of `b` is lost.** The backward last-use walker's `TpyReturn` handling clears the live set, discarding the finally's `b`-is-read fact for code positioned BEFORE the try -- `a = b` compiles as `std::move(b)` although `b` is read afterwards on the return path (TPy prints the pre-mutation value, CPython the post-mutation one). Independent of the finally-deferred return capture (reproduces at its merge-base; `return a` is not a deferral candidate since `a` is a reference bind, not an owned var). Fix shape: the return-statement arm of the backward walk must seed liveness from the enclosing finally frames before clearing. Probes `/tmp/agents/finally-parity/probe_alias_reverse.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity + safety-model). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A union-typed local returned as `Own[A | B]` from inside ANY try/finally emits invalid C++ (ptr-variant to value-variant conversion).** `v: A | B = A(); try: return v; finally: ...` -- `_make_return`'s finally capture binds `std::variant<A, B> __tpy_ret = v;` where `v` is the borrow-form `std::variant<A*, B*>` local, with none of the ptr-to-value-variant conversion the no-finally return path applies; the C++ build fails loudly. Independent of whether the finally reads `v` (probe `/tmp/agents/finally-return-mut/probe_union_noread.py`); pre-existing, surfaced while gating union locals out of the finally-deferred return capture (whose recipe also does not cover variants -- fixing this shape should add a deferred recipe too, so a finally mutating the returned union local matches CPython aliasing like the scalar fix). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Initializing a pointer-repr Optional local with a ternary whose arm is a fresh constructor call emits address-of-rvalue C++.** `b: Box | None = Box() if flag else None` -> `Box* b = flag ? &(Box()) : nullptr;` -- the slot-model materialization (`__slot_N`) is not applied to ternary-arm rvalues, so the C++ build fails loudly (`taking address of rvalue`). The plain form `b: Box | None = Box()` materializes correctly. Surfaced while writing `finally_mutates_returned_local`; workaround: assign in an `if`/`else`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A `finally` body that terminates on every path but doesn't END in a literal `raise`/`return` emits an unreachable `throw;` after its catch-path copy.** `_lower_try` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:14853`) computes `finally_terminates` as a SHALLOW `isinstance(last, (TpyRaise, TpyReturn))` on the finally's last statement (`:14990`), while the normal-path elision asks the DEEP `stmts_terminate` / `try_terminates_ignoring_finally` question (`tpyc/liveness.py:227`/`:277`). So `finally: if c: raise A else: raise B` gets `finally_terminates=False`, and the catch-path copy -- which already always throws -- is followed by a dead `throw;` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:2789`). The flag also rides `THIRTry.finally_terminates` into the finally-chain emit, driving the `[[maybe_unused]]` tagging and the trailing `return`/`throw` suppression at EVERY return/break/continue site inside the try body -- so the dead code appears at each exit site, not just once. Harmless: the shallow check can only err in the SAFE direction (a literal `raise`/`return` last statement always terminates, so the flag is a possible false negative only, never a false positive), and a false negative merely emits unreachable code the C++ compiler drops. Behavior is correct (verified against CPython). Fix shape: compute `finally_terminates` with `stmts_terminate(stmt.finally_body)` so both questions use one predicate. Surfaced by /tpy-ready of the finally-fall-through-elision fix.
- **[MED small] An except clause naming a class AND a subclass of it emits an unreachable C++ catch arm -- fails a strict-warning build (`-Werror=exceptions`).** `except Base:` followed by `except Sub:` (Sub derives from Base), or the single-clause tuple spelling `except (Base, Sub):`, emits `catch (const Base&)` before `catch (const Sub&)`; g++-14 rejects the second under the test harness's `strict_warn_flags`: "exception of type 'Sub' will be caught by earlier handler [-Werror=exceptions]". Valid Python that CPython accepts (the later arm is simply dead), and TPy issues no diagnostic of its own, so a user hits it as a raw C++ build error. **Pre-existing** -- the hand-written sibling form reproduces identically and predates the tuple form -- but the tuple form raises exposure sharply, because the natural Python spelling of an errno/OS group puts a base and its subclass in one clause (`except (OSError, PermissionError):`; PermissionError derives from OSError). NB `uv run tpy` does NOT reproduce it: the CLI leaves `warn_flags` empty, so only the test harness (and any user passing strict flags) sees it. The spelling-based dedup in `_except_clause_types` (`tpyc/parse/parser.py`) collapses only a literally repeated name, never a subclass relationship, which the parser cannot know. Fix shape is a **design decision**, not a patch: drop an arm whose type derives from an earlier arm's (semantics-preserving -- the earlier arm already catches it) in sema where the hierarchy is known, and/or warn on an unreachable except clause (a genuine Python-level lint CPython does not give). Both faces (tuple + hand-written siblings) should be decided together. Reproducer: a `tests/cases/` case with `except (Base, Sub) as e:` -- fails the exec phase; the same case with two sibling clauses fails identically. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity flagged the shape; the coverage test the review asked for immediately failed the build). Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (the diagnostic/collapse design), not `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A QUALIFIED `asyncio.run(...)` call resolves to a USER function of the same bare name, emitting an undeclared-namespace C++ error.** A module-level `async def run(x: int) -> int` alongside `asyncio.run(main())` emits `::tpyapp::__main__::run<std::monostate>(::tpy::make_adapter<...>(main()))` -- the qualified `asyncio.run` bound to the user's `run` -- and g++ rejects it ("'tpyapp::__main__' has not been declared"). CPython runs the same source fine (the qualified name can only mean the module's). Loud (toolchain-caught), rejects-valid; the wrong-namespace spelling suggests the call is resolved by BARE name with the qualifier dropped, so a user function shadowing any qualified stdlib call is the general shape -- same family as the qualified-`except mod.X` builtin-shadow entry below, and worth root-causing together. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/mx/shadow.py` (10 lines). Workaround: rename the user function. Surfaced while probing `await` inside an `except (A, B)` body (the async probe used a helper named `run`); unrelated to that feature. Independently re-surfaced authoring the Phase-D3 `await_in_for_else` test (a local `async def run` shadowed `asyncio.run`; a duplicate LOW entry from that surfacing was folded into this one) and again writing `tests/cases/async/async_view_local_owned_frame` (its coroutine renamed to dodge it). A third duplicate was folded in from a `MED` filing that added: `run` is a likely collision in exactly the async programs that need `asyncio.run`; the g++ face varies with the user function's shape (a zero-arg `async def run()` under `asyncio.run(run())` reports `expected primary-expression before '>' token` on the stray template argument list rather than the undeclared namespace); and this is distinct from the module-qualified entries below, which are about resolution FAILING rather than resolving to the WRONG target. Second reproducer `/tmp/agents/awfix/shadow.py` (12 lines). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `isinstance()` on an EXCEPTION binding takes the union/variant path and emits `std::holds_alternative` against a class reference -- ill-formed C++.** `class Sub(Base)` (Base an Exception subclass), then `try: raise Sub()` / `except Base as e: if isinstance(e, Sub): ...` emits `std::holds_alternative<Sub>(e)` and `auto& __e = std::get<Sub>(e)` where `e` is `const Base&` -> g++ "'const Base' is not derived from 'const std::variant<_Types...>'". The same isinstance-against-a-descendant on a NON-exception class correctly warns ("folds to False (static dispatch; use @dynamic for runtime type checks)") and folds -- so the exception binding is the only receiver that reaches the variant path with no union in sight. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent, but it rejects the natural disambiguation idiom for any base-typed catch. Note the correct behavior here is NOT obvious: a caught exception IS genuinely polymorphic (C++ catch does real RTTI matching), so folding to False like a plain class would be wrong; a `dynamic_cast` narrow is the honest lowering. That makes this a design question as much as a fix. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/mx/iso.py`. Workaround: none for exceptions -- restructure into one `except` clause per concrete type. Surfaced by the cpython-parity review of the `except (A, B)` tuple-form design (it blocks the join-typed-binding ergonomics). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A non-fixed-int ctor wrapper (`int(...)`) around a >int32 literal DEFAULT on a BigInt field still renders bare, and the parser mis-renders `int(x)` as a truncating C++ cast.** `big: int = int(90000000000)` as a record-field default: `records.py`'s field member-init uses `fixed_int_literal_value_from_expr`, which peels only FIXED-int ctor wrappers (`int64(...)`) -- `int` is not in `_FIXED_INT_NAMES`, so it falls through to the parser's pre-rendered string. Separately, `_get_default_value` (`tpyc/parse/parser.py`) renders a non-fixed-int 1-arg ctor call as `f"{func}({args})"` -> `int(90000000000)`, which in C++ is a truncating `int` cast, not a BigInt. So the field emits `::tpy::BigInt big = int(90000000000);` -- both the macOS `long -> BigInt` ambiguity (via the inner bare token) AND a value truncation. `default_to_cpp` (function/ctor params) avoids this because it recurses through ANY 1-arg `TpyCall`. Pathological spelling (`int(...)` wrapping a literal whose field is already `int`); no realistic user impact. Fix shape: either broaden the field member-init to recurse like `default_to_cpp`, or fix `_get_default_value`'s non-fixed-int-ctor arm to not emit a C++ truncating cast. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/ctorwrap.py` (swap `int64` for `int`). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the int-literal-default fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] An empty (`pass`-body) subclass used as a struct FIELD emits an incomplete-type C++ error.** `class Sub(Base): pass` then `class Holder: _s: Sub` (or ctor `def __init__(self, s: Own[Sub])`) fails to compile: `error: field '_s' has incomplete type 'Sub'` -- codegen forward-declares `Sub` but emits `Holder` (which needs `Sub` complete for the inline field) before `Sub`'s full definition. Reproduces with NO iteration / readonly / generics -- just an empty subclass as a field (`/tmp/agents/gap2/emptysub.py`). A non-empty subclass (adds its own field) is unaffected. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. Emit-ordering bug: an empty subclass isn't ordered before a record that holds it by value. Fix shape: include empty subclasses in the same complete-before-use topological emit ordering non-empty records get. Surfaced writing an inherited-`__iter__` test for the for-loop const-receiver fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The for-loop const-receiver `__iter__` fix doesn't cover a self-METHOD-CALL iterable (`for v in self.get_container():`).** `_record_iter_receiver_mutation` (`tpyc/sema/iter_loans.py`) bails when `_root_name_of_expr(iterable_expr)` is None (a call has no name root), so a for-loop iterating the result of a self-method call whose `__iter__` mutates the returned receiver won't demote the enclosing method -> the same const-receiver compile error the fix eliminates for name/field iterables. `methods.py`'s explicit-call path has a None-root chain-to-self fallback (methods.py ~923) this helper omits. Exotic (a self-returning-mutating-iterable call) and loud (compile error), so filed rather than handled in the fix. Fix shape: add the chain-traces-to-self fallback (mark self mutated) for a None-root iterable, mirroring methods.py. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the const-receiver `__iter__` fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A bound cross-module coroutine handle whose callee name collides with a local coro is read as a self-edge, so valid code is rejected as `recursive coroutine embedding`.** `_bound_frame_targets` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py` ~888) keys the emit-ordering edge on the bare `(coro_func_name, owner_record)` pair and never consults `ConcreteFrameType.frame_module_qual` (`tpyc/typesys.py:4100`), so a handle whose struct is `helper::__coro_step` -- already complete via that module's header -- matches a same-named LOCAL unit instead. Trigger is narrow: `from helper import step as hstep` then `h = hstep()` inside a local `async def step()` DOES reproduce, while the attribute form `helper.step()` does NOT (it resolves the qualifier elsewhere), so the shape needs a bare-or-aliased import plus a name collision. Loud, no miscompile. The four owner-bearing edge sources route through `same_module_dep_unit` (`resumable_cfg.py`) for exactly this reason; this fifth source predates that helper and was left out. Fix shape: skip when `frame_module_qual` names another module, or route the owner-bearing form through the helper. Probes `/tmp/agents/iterfix/bound/main2.py` (fails) and `control.py` (compiles). Confirmed pre-existing by A/B (neutering that collector alone makes the probe compile). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent] A generator METHOD's frame const verdict is looked up in the FREE-function table, so a name collision hands it another function's answer.** `_frame_deep_const_verdict` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py:363`) branches on its `record_name` argument, but every generator path reaches it with `None` -- the eligibility gate (`generator.py` ~885, and the fwd-decl pass) builds and MEMOIZES the CFG before `gen_coro_struct` can pass the real record name, and the docstring sanctions that ("Generators never await, so the gate path may pass None"). So a method takes the `registry.get_function(func.name)` leg: normally that misses and yields None (benign), but a method whose name matches a module-level function picks up the FREE function's `deep_const_borrow_params`. That verdict drives the const spelling of pointer-repr tuple/union frame captures and the CFG-window const seeding, so a wrong answer is a wrong field const-ness, not just a missing one. No constructed repro (needs a generator method sharing a name with a free function that has deep-const params). Pre-existing. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An unannotated list mixing a small int literal with a >int32 one infers an `int32` element type, truncating the wide literal (C++ `-Wnarrowing` build error).** `a = [0, 1234567890123456789]` emits `std::array<int32_t, 2> a = {0, 1234567890123456789}`, which g++ rejects (narrowing `long` -> `int` inside brace-init). Also `sum([100000, 3000000000])` and `x = [100000, 3000000000]; sum(x)`, where CPython prints `3000100000` (probe `/tmp/agents/parity-ihc5/sumlit.py`). A list with ONLY the wide literal (`[1234567890123456789]`) infers `BigInt` correctly (`std::array<::tpy::BigInt, 1>`); the bug is the element-type JOIN over mixed int literals -- the small literal pins the common type to `int32` without checking that a sibling literal overflows it. Loud (toolchain-caught), rejects-valid; an explicit `list[int]` annotation avoids it (gets `BigInt`, and the >int32 element now renders ambiguity-safe -- the target-less int-literal render in `int_literals.py`). Fix shape: the int-literal list-element join must widen to a type holding EVERY member (BigInt when any element exceeds the fixed width), not collapse to the narrowest present. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/inf.py`. Surfaced fixing the macOS BigInt list-literal ambiguity. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `@error_return` is not rejected on `__del__` -- a `try`/`except <ReturnException>` (or any @error_return propagation) in a destructor lowers to a `return ::tpy::make_unexpected(...)` / `return {};` inside the C++ destructor body, which is invalid C++ ("returning a value from a destructor").** A destructor has no return slot, but the @error_return lowering emits its goto-based `return <expected>` unconditionally. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid-looking code; exotic (no reason to use @error_return machinery in a `__del__`). Reproduces on master (pre-existing, unrelated to the fail-fast wrap). Fix shape: reject `@error_return` / return-exception propagation in a `__del__` body at registration (alongside the other `__del__` shape checks in `tpyc/sema/registration.py`). Surfaced by the codegen-correctness review of the `__del__` fail-fast change. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `async def __del__` is accepted and silently mishandled -- it emits a synchronous destructor running the body (dropping the `async`) PLUS a dead coroutine struct.** A class with `async def __del__(self)` compiles: codegen emits a real `~T()` whose body runs the method statements synchronously (ignoring that the method is a coroutine -- there is no way to `await` during C++ destruction) AND a separate, never-instantiated `__coro_T___del__` resumable-frame struct. So the async-ness is silently discarded and dead code is generated. A destructor cannot be async (destruction is synchronous), so this should be a clean sema rejection (like `self: Own[Self]` on `__del__`, already rejected). Exotic -- no user writes an async destructor -- so no current impact; loud only in that the dead struct is emitted. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/deldrop/asyncdel.py`. Fix shape: reject `async` on `__del__` at registration (alongside the existing `__del__` shape checks). Surfaced by the codegen-correctness re-review of the conditional `__del__`-wrap change. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An @error_return call nested in the ARG subtree of another @error_return call is a hard compile error.** `x = f(g(3))` and `return f(g(3))` (both @error_return) fail codegen with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:error_return.nested_call)` / `(stmt.return:error_return.nested_call)`, raised by `_reject_nested_error_return_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:3233`, called from the var-decl arm at :3271 and the return arm at :10243). The shape was never admitted because the render it would have to reproduce is ill-formed C++: the statement handler unwraps the OUTER call, but arguments render first, so the inner fallible call consumed the handled-call flag and the inner `g` emitted as a raw `std::expected` where its success value was needed. Everyday shape -- composing two fallible calls is the ordinary way to write them in an @error_return body -- so worth queueing. Fix shape: give the inner call its own unwrap temp before the outer call composes, keying the handled-call state to the specific node instead of a single boolean, then widen the admission. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_400_nested_er_arg.py` and `02_400b_return_form.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) The expression-level @error_return propagate unwrap skips active finally bodies; the statement-level one runs them -- an inconsistent early return that silently drops cleanup.** Inside an @error_return function a fallible call in EXPRESSION position (`return f(a) + f(b)`, an argument, a condition) unwraps through `_er_check_inline` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:2513`), whose propagate arm emits a bare `if (!__er_1.has_value()) return ::tpy::make_unexpected(__er_1.error());` with no walk of `state.finally_frames` -- while its statement-level sibling `_er_check_stmt` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:2532`) routes the same propagate through `_emit_finally_return`, so the finally body runs. Confirmed: `@error_return(E) def expr_pos(a, b): try: return f(a) + f(b) finally: print("cleanup")` with a failing `f` prints nothing under TPy and `cleanup` under CPython. Silent -- the output diverges only when the error path fires under an active finally. Fix shape: route the expression unwrap's propagate arm through the same finally-frame walk `_er_check_stmt` uses (the statement expression can hold multi-statement checks), or hoist expression-level fallible calls to statement temps under an active finally. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_401_er_expr_finally.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The system-lib version guard only fires when pkg-config can report a version; a too-old system lib installed without a `.pc` file still fails deep in the C compiler.** `system_version_too_old` (`tpyc/build/third_party.py`) probes `pkg-config --modversion` and is deliberately permissive when the version is undeterminable (no pkg-config, no `.pc`) so a valid from-source install is not blocked -- but that means a too-old from-source install (e.g. mbedTLS 2.27 headers in a non-standard prefix, no `.pc`) bypasses the guard and hits the cryptic API-mismatch compile error the guard exists to prevent. Acceptable today (from-source installs of a managed dep are rare and usually ship a `.pc`), but the guard is best-effort, not complete. Fix shape: fall back to a `MBEDTLS_VERSION_NUMBER`/equivalent compile-probe against the resolved headers when pkg-config yields nothing. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective of the version-guard work. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] The CMake-emit path (`tpyc -o`) never compiles TPy-owned third-party glue, so a `sources.cmake`-based build of any `ssl`/`datetime`/`zlib`/`gzip` program is missing the FFI shim in EVERY mode.** `resolve_build_plan` puts the glue (`mbedtls_shim.c`/`cacert_data.c`, `date_shim.cpp`) in `ThirdPartyBuildPlan.c_sources`, which only the direct-compile path (`tpyc -b` -> `BuildLayout.build_cpp_commands`) consumes. `Compiler.generate_cmake` (`tpyc/compiler.py`) and `emit_cmake_snippet` (`tpyc/build/third_party.py`) receive `third_party_plan.libs` but NOT `c_sources`, so the generated CMake project never builds the shim -- `tpystd::ssl` would link with undefined `tpy_tls_*` (and datetime with the missing date facade). `zlib` joined the set with `zlib_shim.c`: `tpyc -o` of a program importing `zlib` emits a `sources.cmake` with no shim and undefined `tpy_zs_*` (probe `/tmp/agents/zlib/t1/cm/`, 2026-09-26). Pre-existing (the shim was in `bundled_source_files`, also c_sources-only, before the system-mode work), and untested (the harness + nightly use the direct-compile path). Fix shape: thread `plan.c_sources` (source + per-file flags) through `generate_cmake`/`emit_cmake_snippet` into the emitted `sources.cmake`, mirroring how the direct path adds them. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the system-mode glue fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `@overload`-dispatched methods still emit inline-in-struct -- the residual member-body kind that needs complete sibling types at struct scope.** The ctor/special-member fix moved `__init__` ctors, `__del__` dtor/move ops, and `__copy__` copy ops to namespace scope (`records.py` `_gen_ctor_def` / mode-aware `_gen_move_and_destructor` / `_gen_copy_ops`), and plain methods already default out-of-line -- but `@overload`-specialized methods stay inline regardless of size (the emitters take a `mode` param that is always "inline" there). A body that references a mutually-recursive sibling record (or any record defined later in the module) odr-uses an incomplete type at struct scope -- clang rejects, gcc happens to accept (same mechanism as the fixed ctor case, `tests/cases/records/recursive_record_mutual`). Exotic combos, loud (toolchain-caught). Fix shape: partition-aware overload dispatch (thread the decl/def mode through the specialized-method emitters); for simple generators either fall off the peephole for cycle members or emit the factory after the structs. Surfaced by the recursive-record ctor fix survey. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (acknowledged divergence, no longer a nightly blocker) TPy `asyncio.Future()` is constructible without a running loop; CPython >= 3.14 raises `RuntimeError` there.** CPython 3.14 turned the "no current event loop" deprecation into an error: `asyncio.Future()` outside a running loop now raises `RuntimeError: There is no current event loop` (from `events.get_event_loop`). TPy's `lib/tpy/asyncio` still allows loop-less construction (matching pre-3.14 permissiveness) -- a silent parity divergence, but with no diagnostic/escape-hatch today. `tests/cases/async/future_basic` was restructured to construct the Future inside `asyncio.run`'s loop (so it no longer trips the divergence and the 2604 row passes), but the divergence itself is unfixed. To close it: bind Future construction to a running loop like modern CPython (raise when none), or accept it explicitly with a documented note. Surfaced by the nightly CI 26.04 rows (Python 3.14.4).
- **[LOW small] (silent misbinding, not unsound) A genuinely-new method type param whose NAME collides with an intermediate generic subclass's class param is misclassified as class-bound -- explicit type args silently discarded, mismatched args wrongly rejected.** `class Base[T]: def pick[U](self, other: U) -> U`; `class Mid[U](Base[U])`; `class Leaf(Mid[int32])`: through `Leaf`, the composed class subst carries `U -> int32` (Mid's param), so `_analyze_generic_method_call`'s classification (receiver params UNION subst keys, `tpyc/sema/methods.py`) treats the genuinely-fresh `U` on `pick` as constrained: `l.pick[StrView](5)` compiles silently dropping the type arg (interim: the hoisted arity check now rejects it loudly, though the "expects 0 type argument(s)" message is misleading -- there IS a genuine new param), and `l.pick("hello")` is wrongly rejected "expected int32". Type-consistent end-to-end (not unsound); exotic shape. Pre-existing family: before the subclass-receiver fix this shape errored "Cannot infer" (the by-name pre-substitution in `substitute_method_type_params` erased `U` regardless -- that name-capture is the true enabler). Fix shape: return the DECLARING RecordInfo from `lookup_record_method_overloads` (3-tuple), classify against the declaring class's params, and filter the subst to those params before pre-substitution (alpha-scoping the by-name capture). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model + architecture-fit) of the subclass-receiver bound fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The super() and unbound-self `Base.m(self, ...)` dispatch paths never compose the class subst down to the DECLARING base -- a shadowed-bound method inherited from a generic base above the named/direct parent still fails "Cannot infer type arguments".** [`parent-call-generic-subst-one-level`] Both paths (`tpyc/sema/methods.py` ~1208 `resolve_ancestor_instantiation` and ~2247 `get_parent_type_subst`) build the subst from the direct/named parent only, unlike `_analyze_instance_method`, which gets the level-by-level composition from `lookup_record_method_overloads` -- so the exact bug fixed for instance calls on this branch persists there whenever the declaring generic base sits one level above. Loud failure (wrong rejection), same family. Fix shape: route both paths through (or share the composition of) `lookup_record_method_overloads` instead of the two parallel one-level lookups. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the subclass-receiver bound fix. The `__init__` face (`_parent_init_target`, `tpyc/sema/methods.py`, which substitutes the parent's arguments into the MRO entry of the `__init__` owner -- an entry spelled in the params of the class that names the owner as its direct base): under `class G[U]` with an `__init__`, `class H[W](G[list[W]]): pass` and `class M[T](H[tuple[T, T]]): pass`, a `class L(M[int32])` calling `super().__init__([(1, 2)])` or `M.__init__(self, [(3, 4)])` fails with "Unknown type parameter 'W'" and no line number (`/tmp/agents/cpyparity_r3/p12a.py`, `p12b.py`); and naming a generic grandparent's `__init__` directly -- `Holder.__init__(self, 3, [4])` from `class L2(Mid[int32])` over `class Mid[T](Holder[T, list[T]]): pass` -- fails "Type mismatch in argument 'a': expected T, got IntLiteral(3)" (`/tmp/agents/cpyparity_r3/p11.py`). CPython runs all three. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic quality, not unsound) The class-shadowed method-bound check on OPERATOR dispatch sites silently short-circuits for a subclass receiver -- a violation surfaces as a cryptic C++ `requires` error instead of the clean sema diagnostic.** The method-CALL path resolves shadowed bounds through subclass receivers (fixed on `fix-method-bound-subclass-receiver`: classification uses the composed class subst), but the operator sites still derive the class-param set and subst from the RECEIVER's record: `operators.py` (`_check_operator_method_bound`) does `if record is None or not record.type_params: return` -- empty for a subclass, so the check is skipped; `expressions.py` `__contains__`/binop-dunder sites pass `record.type_params` + `build_type_substitution(receiver)`, both empty for a subclass (and the binop site's `record.get_method` doesn't walk bases at all, so an inherited dunder may miss this path entirely); `protocols.py:790` (protocol-conformance / `hash()` path) likewise passes receiver-own `record_info.type_params`, so `find_method_class_param_bound_violation` bails at its `not class_type_params` gate for a subclass. Not unsound -- codegen's `requires` clause still rejects at C++ build -- but the user sees a template error instead of `Method '...' requires type parameter 'T' to satisfy '...'`. Repro shape: `class NEBag(Bag[NotEq, 4])` + `x in b` where `__contains__[T: Equatable]`. Fix shape: derive (declaring-class params + composed subst) for operator sites the way `_analyze_instance_method` does -- likely by threading `lookup_record_method_overloads`'s composed subst into the operator bound check instead of the receiver-record fields. Surfaced by the subclass-receiver bound-inference fix's sibling survey. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A borrow/reference local reused across sibling/outer scopes is declared in the inner C++ scope, not hoisted -- the later use is an undeclared identifier (C++ build error).** A local bound from a reference-returning accessor (`s = arc.get()`) or a `with ... as g` guard, first assigned inside a nested block (a loop body or a `with` body) and then read/reassigned in an enclosing or sibling scope, is emitted with its C++ declaration INSIDE the inner block; the later use emits `s = &(...)` / `g = &(...)` against a variable no longer in scope -> `'s' was not declared in this scope`. Two `with m.lock() as g:` blocks in one function reusing `g`, and `s = shared.get()` inside a `while` loop then reused after the loop, both reproduce. A third face: two SIBLING `except` handler bodies reusing one name (`except X as e: v = e.code.get(...)` / `except Y as e: v = e.code.get(...)`) -- the decl lands in the first handler's scope and the second emits `'v' was not declared in this scope`; reachable from hand-written sibling clauses, so it predates (and is independent of) the `except (A, B)` tuple form, whose arms are ordinary sibling handlers. Value-typed locals hoist to function scope correctly; only borrow/reference locals mis-scope. Loud (toolchain-caught), workaround = distinct names / restructure so a borrow local lives in one scope. Fix shape: hoist borrow/reference locals to their common enclosing scope like value locals (or declare-at-first-dominating-assignment). Surfaced building the Condvar ping-pong test (tpy.sync). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects reasonable code; CPython-parity trap) A generic METHOD cannot infer its type parameter from an argument whose type is a generic-class instantiation matching a `Generic[T]`-shaped parameter.** `def wait[T](self, mutex: Mutex[T])` called as `cv.wait(m)` with `m: Mutex[PingState]` errors `Cannot infer type arguments for method 'wait'. Specify explicitly: .wait[T](...)` -- the unification `Mutex[T]` <- `Mutex[PingState]` (and its `readonly[...]`-wrapped form) is not solved for a method-level type param. The suggested explicit spelling `cv.wait[PingState](m)` compiles in TPy but is INVALID Python (`method[X]` raises `TypeError: 'method' object is not subscriptable`), so any stdlib API that needs it breaks CPython parity. Workaround: give the method a non-generic param instead of the generic handle -- e.g. a non-`@dynamic` structural protocol the handle conforms to (monomorphized, so still a static call), which is what `Condvar.wait(lock: _CondvarLock)` does to take a `MutexGuard[T]` without a method type-param. Fix shape: extend method type-param inference to unify into a generic-class-typed (and readonly-wrapped) parameter, so `wait[T](guard: MutexGuard[T])` could be written directly. Surfaced designing `Condvar.wait` (tpy.sync). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Readonly-inference gap for `async for` (iteration-family sibling, latent behind a bigger gap).** Every other implicit dunder call on a receiver -- the for-loop `__iter__`, `x in h` (`__contains__`, or `__iter__` when there is none), a subscript's `__getitem__`, `with`, `await` -- records the receiver mutation through `tpyc/sema/receiver_calls.py`. `async for` over a field does not: `_analyze_async_for` marks only `TpyName` iterables, not a field access. It is currently unreachable, because a user `async def __aiter__` + `yield` hits "async generators are not yet supported". Fix shape: route `__aiter__` through `credit_implicit_receiver_call` like the sync loop's `__iter__`. Surfaced fixing the for-loop const-receiver `__iter__` bug. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A NARROWED value-repr `char | None` operand compared to a str literal (`if o is not None: ... o == "a"`) is a hard compile error.** Codegen fails with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (binop.narrowed_char_eq_literal)`, raised at `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:4231`. The char-literal coercion keys on the RESOLVED operand type, which for a narrowed operand is `Optional[char]`, so the target-typed char render (`_lower_char_targeted`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:15149`) misses and the only render left was `((*o) == "a")` -- `char` against `const char*`, invalid C++. Reproduces for narrowed NAME and narrowed FIELD subjects. Exotic (`char | None` locals are rare) but valid Python. Fix shape: unwrap the narrowed Optional before the char-literal coercion decides, then lift the reject. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_413_narrowed_char_eq.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A `char` frame local of a generator/async function initialized with a char literal (`c: char = 'a'`) emits `c = "a";` (`const char*` -> `char`, invalid C++).** A local live across a `yield`/`await` is captured as a frame field and written by `_lower_frame_field_assign` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:6682`, reached from the resumable leaf decl arm at `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py:1929`), whose init render is deliberately POSITION-BLIND -- it lowers the init against no target, so the char-literal SOURCE (`'a'`, a str literal in the AST) renders as the string `"a"`. The SYNC path is fine: a plain `c: char = 'a'` local goes through `_lower_char_targeted` and renders `char c = 'a';`. Position-blindness is correct for the other value scalars (an int/BigInt literal stays `0`, bool/float neutral); only `char` needs the target type to turn the str-literal source into a char literal. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid; confirmed for both generators and `async def` (g++: `invalid conversion from 'const char*' to 'char'`). Fix shape: the frame-field init render for a `char` slot must apply the same target-typed char render the sync decl arm uses. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_414_char_frame_local.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Truthiness of a value-repr `Optional[bytes]` (`if b:` / `not b` / `while b:` on a `bytes | None`) emits `::tpy::is_truthy(std::optional<::tpy::BytesView>)`, which the generic `is_truthy(optional<T>)` compiles to an invalid `static_cast<bool>(span)`.** The runtime has `is_truthy(optional<std::string>)` and `is_truthy(optional<std::string_view>)` overloads (str-optional truthiness works) but NO `is_truthy(optional<::tpy::BytesView>)` overload, so a bytes-optional falls to the generic template (`opt.has_value() && static_cast<bool>(*opt)`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/core.hpp:561`) and g++ rejects `static_cast<bool>` of a span. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. `b is None` (`has_value()`) and passing the optional whole are fine; only truthiness of the bare optional trips it. THIR mirrors the render byte-identically (the shape can never appear in a green corpus/exec case, so it stays routed per the AST-miscompile mirror criterion). Fix shape: add an `is_truthy(const std::optional<::tpy::BytesView>&)` overload (empty span / nullopt -> false) alongside the string ones -- or, more generally, a span/BytesView `is_truthy` so bare `bytes`/`BytesView` truthiness is covered too. Same root cause for a value-repr `Optional[user record]` with `__bool__`/`__len__` (e.g. `Own[Flag] | None`): the generic template's `static_cast<bool>(record)` fails to compile instead of dispatching to the dunder -- a record-dunder-aware overload (or per-inner dispatch) should land with the same fix. Surfaced routing value-repr Optional[bytes] params through THIR. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) `Own[list[T]]` at an `@export` parameter passes the boundary validator and fails the C++ build.** [`export-own-container-param-uncompilable`] `def take(xs: Own[list[int32]]) -> int32` in an `ext_module` is admitted (the container admission strips Own like every wrapper), but the glue binds the marshalled copy to an lvalue local and passes it to the callee's `std::vector<int32_t>&&` parameter -- a hard C++ error with no TPy location; `Own[Optional[list[int32]]]` fails the same way. Pre-existing (the plain form fails identically without any Optional), surfaced by the 2026-09-22 Optional-boundary review. Fix shape: either reject `Own[container]` at a boundary param with the located Own[Cls]-style message (the host keeps its reference, but a container IS a fresh copy, so the honest alternative is) to `std::move` the owned local into the `&&` param, the way the property setter path already moves its marshalled local. Probe: an `@export` fn with `xs: Own[list[int32]]`, `uv run tpyc -b`.
- **[LOW small] Returning a view-form `str`/`StrView` value whole into an `Optional[str]` (`-> str | None`) return slot emits an un-convertible bare `return <string_view>;` (invalid C++).** [`optional-str-return-view-source`] A function `def f() -> str | None: x = "y"; return x` (or any `return <StrView local/param>` where the WHOLE view value, not a param passed through the `Optional[str]`->`Optional[str]` shim, feeds an `std::optional<std::string>` return) emits `return x;` -- but `std::string_view` does not convert to `std::optional<std::string>` (the `optional<string>` converting ctor is explicit), so g++ rejects it ("could not convert 'x' ... to 'std::optional<std::string>'"). The AST omits the `std::string(...)` wrap it emits at a plain `-> str` owned return. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. A str LITERAL (`return "y"`) compiles (bare `const char*` -> `optional<string>` is implicit), and an `Optional[str]` param returned whole takes the correct `s ? std::make_optional(std::string(*s)) : std::nullopt` shim; only a view-form value SOURCE is wrong. Workaround: wrap explicitly (`return str(x)` is not spellable; bind through the optional). Fix shape: at an `Optional[str]` return, a view-form source must take the same `std::string(view)` wrap the owned `-> str` return applies (then materialize into the optional).
