This is why THIR gate-rejects the shape (`return.opt_view_source`) rather than mirroring it, and a boundary pin now holds it there deliberately. **Confirmed end to end through `uv run tpy`, not inferred**: `def f(k: str) -> str | None: return k` fails the build with `error: could not convert 'k' from 'std::string_view' ... to 'std::optional<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char> >'`, which also confirms the toolchain-caught characterization above. Surfaced routing value-repr Optional[str] returns through THIR. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A NARROWED `int | None` NAME under a scalar-cast coerce at an `Own[int32]` call slot emits `(v).to_fixed_check<int32_t>()` -- the narrowing deref is dropped (invalid C++, `std::optional<BigInt>` has no `to_fixed_check`).** `def f(v: int | None): if v is not None: take(v)` (take taking `Own[int32]`) emits the coerce wrap over the BARE name where the narrowed read needs `(*v)`. Same narrowing-unwrap-dropped family as the `str | None` field-at-view-return entry below; here the coerce render path loses the deref. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. THIR gate-rejects the shape (`_own_coerce_cast_arg` requires the DECLARED type be the scalar itself) rather than mirroring the broken render -- lift that guard when fixing. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/adv_ptrlocal_coerce.py`; g++-confirmed. Surfaced by review round 12's meta-review probe of the own-coerce-cast leg. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A NARROWED `str | None` FIELD returned at a view (`StrView`) return slot emits a bare `return this->field;` -- invalid C++ (`std::optional<std::string>` does not convert to `std::string_view`).** `class Box: opt: str | None` with `def f(self) -> StrView: if self.opt is not None: return self.opt` emits `return this->opt;`; the narrowed read needs the unwrap (`return (*this->opt);`). Sibling shapes at the same slot are correct -- a plain owned `str` field emits the bare member read, which IS right there -- so it is the narrowing unwrap that is dropped, not the member render. Mirror image of the view-into-`Optional[str]` return entry above. THIR deliberately keeps this shape unrouted (it would emit the correct `(*this->opt)` and diverge from the broken oracle): the view-target coerce arm types its str-field admission on the DECLARED field type. Surfaced routing str-family field reads at the view-return sink through THIR (adversarial dual-path smoke; g++-confirmed). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A non-copyable `Own` local assigned inside a `try:` block cannot be MOVED afterwards -- it is stored optional-form and any later use silently copies (a hard error for a non-copyable type).** A `resp` bound by `resp = getresponse()` inside a `try` (getresponse returns `Own[HTTPResponse]`) is emitted as `std::optional<HTTPResponse>` (the possibly-unassigned-on-exception representation), so a later `Response(..., resp)` that should MOVE it instead attempts a copy -- rejected for the non-copyable `HTTPResponse` ("cannot be copied ... Only the original owner can be moved at its last use"), and for a COPYABLE type it silently copies (warned) + then miscompiles the move-into-`Own|None`-field via `ptr_to_optional_move(std::optional<T>&)` (expects `T*`). Reproduced whether the move is in the same try-scope, in a sibling branch, or after the try. The fix in `tplib.requests` was to bind the value from a HELPER-function return (`_send_recv`) instead of a try-scoped local -- a normal local from a call return moves cleanly. Toolchain-caught for non-copyable types (loud); SILENT extra copy for copyable ones. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/streamprobe/optmove{3,5}.py` (miscompile), `optmove4.py` (silent copy+warn), `optmove{6,7}.py` (helper-return workaround compiles). Surfaced building `tplib.requests` streaming (moving the `Own[HTTPResponse]` into `Response._raw`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A QUALIFIED `except mod.X:` clause whose bare name `X` shadows a builtin exception wrongly matches the BUILTIN of that name (and its subclasses), not the user's `mod.X`.** `import tplib.requests as requests` then `except requests.ConnectionError:` also catches a raw builtin `ConnectionResetError` (a subclass of builtin `ConnectionError`), even though `requests.ConnectionError` and builtin `ConnectionError` are unrelated sibling classes (both merely descend from `OSError`) -- real Python `isinstance` would never match. Root-caused to the qualified/dotted spelling specifically: the UNQUALIFIED `from tplib.requests import ConnectionError; except ConnectionError:` resolves correctly to the user class. Confirmed with a synthetic `class MyErr(OSError)` reached via `except mymod.ConnectionError` wrongly matching builtin `ConnectionResetError`, so it is a general builtin-name-shadow in qualified-except type resolution, not requests-specific. SILENT wrong control flow (reroutes to the wrong handler on a plausible real failure). Workaround: use the unqualified `from mod import X` spelling in the except clause. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/probe_exc_module_shadow.py`, `probe_exc_unqualified.py`. Surfaced by the cpython-parity review of `requests` streaming (newly reachable: `iter_content` is the first public API that lets a raw unwrapped OS exception escape). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. The same spelling also MISSES the class it names (2026-09-28): `from tplib import requests` then `try: requests.get("http://127.0.0.1:1/")` / `except requests.ConnectionError:` renders `catch (const ::tpy::ConnectionError&)` and the program dies with `TurboPython panic: uncaught tpystd::tplib::requests::ConnectionError`, and `except requests.HTTPError:` (no builtin twin) is refused with `Unknown exception type 'requests.HTTPError'`; probes `/tmp/agents/rel06/audit/req_exc_qual.py`, `req_exc_http.py` (control `req_exc_bare.py`), surfaced by the website docs audit.
- **[LOW small] Forwarding a borrow-form `bytes | None` (Optional[bytes]) parameter into another call materializes a fresh owned copy instead of a zero-cost pass-through.** A function `f(body: bytes | None)` that calls `g(body)` where `g` also takes `bytes | None` emits `body ? std::make_optional(::tpy::bytes_copy(*body)) : std::nullopt` -- copying the whole payload -- even though source and destination are the same `std::optional<::tpy::BytesView>` borrow form. Not a miscompile, a perf gap; bites `tplib.requests`'s hot send path (extracting `_send_recv(body: bytes | None)` now copies the entire request body once per POST/PUT/PATCH, including large multipart uploads, where the pre-extraction code passed the owned body straight to `conn.request` with no copy). Same body-copy family as the requests `_encode_body`/`bytesview_to_bytes` perf residuals already tracked in TODO.md. Fix shape: forward a borrow-form Optional param by pass-through (no `bytes_copy`) when the destination param is the same borrow form. Workaround (lib side): keep `conn.request(body)` in the caller rather than behind a `bytes|None`-param helper. Surfaced by the codegen-correctness review of `requests` streaming. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A `with EXPR as v:` whose EXPR is a call materializing a UNION-typed default argument emits the default's temp in a scope invisible to the with-header -- undeclared-variable C++ error.** `with obj.m("x", flag=True) as c:` where `m(self, a=None, verify: bool | str = True, flag: bool = False)` leaves `verify` to its default: codegen materializes the `bool | str` default as a `__tmp_N` variant temp but declares it in a block/statement-expression scope the with-header's `auto __ctx = obj.m(..., __tmp_N, ...)` cannot see -> g++ "'__tmp_N' was not declared in this scope". A SCALAR default (`int32 = 1`) needs no temp so does not trip it; a single union default in a FREE-function call in the with-header also compiled in isolation -- the trigger is the union-default temp landing in the with-context lowering (reproduced with a method call carrying a union default plus a later explicitly-passed arg). Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. Workaround: bind the call result to a local first (`r = obj.m(...)`) then `with r:` -- the pre-bound form compiles. Fix shape: hoist union-typed default-arg temps for a with-header call into the enclosing scope (the same scope the `__ctx` temp is declared in), not the with-body block. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/streamprobe/withmethod.py`. Surfaced adding `requests` streaming (`with s.get(url, stream=True) as r:`, where `verify: bool | str = True` defaults). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A non-`None` constant default on a POINTER-repr union parameter is rendered bare against the variant, so the declaration does not compile.** [`pointer-union-nonnull-default-renders-bare`] `def free(r: Rec | int32 = 1)` emits `int32_t free(const std::variant<int32_t*, Rec*> r = 1);` and g++ reports `could not convert '1' from 'int' to 'const std::variant<int*, Rec*>'`; `r: Rec | str = "x"` fails the same way. Only `None` has a valid spelling at such a slot (`none_default_cpp_spelling` gives `nullptr`), which is why the sibling `r: Rec | None = None` compiles and this stayed hidden. Pre-existing on plain FREE functions, but it now reaches more C++ entities: on a resumable generator/async METHOD the same bad text is emitted three times -- the in-class factory declaration, the frame constructor, and every call that omits the argument -- because those declarations gained defaults with the resumable-factory default fix. Sites: `default_emittable` / `default_to_cpp` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`) over the rule in `default_emittable_at` (`tpyc/typesys.py`). The call-site-fill regime that already handles record-typed `Optional`/union defaults is `default_needs_call_site_fill` (`tpyc/typesys.py`), and this shape misses it by the pointer-form escape (`inner.uses_pointer_repr() and not own` returns False): that escape was written for the INCOMPLETE-TYPE reason -- a `Rec*` alternative is complete where a free function is declared, unlike a value-form `std::variant<..., Rec, ...>` -- and it implicitly assumed the only default reaching a pointer-repr union slot is `None`. A non-`None` constant needs the address of an object, which no C++ default argument can name. Fix shape: route non-Optional union defaults with a non-`None` value through the call-site-fill regime like their record-typed value-form siblings (the fill already materializes a variant temp -- see the with-header entry above, which is that temp landing in the wrong scope), or render the default as a variant construction over a temp where one can be named. Repro `/tmp/agents/uniondef/main.py` (free + resumable method) and `/tmp/agents/uniondef/shapes.py` (shape matrix: `Rec | int32 = 1` and `Rec | str = "x"` fail, `Rec | None = None` compiles). Surfaced by the review round on the resumable-factory default fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A generator method that narrows an Optional reference-type `self` field is mis-inferred as `const`, const-poisoning the narrowed local.** A `def gen(self, n: int32 = 1) -> Iterator[T]` whose body does `x = self._field` (field `X | None`, `X` a reference type) then uses `x` gets emitted `const` (`__gen_C_gen C::gen(int32_t) const`), so if the method called on the narrowed local is `@readonly` (non-mutating) the local is `const X*` and a later non-const use is rejected ("invalid conversion from const X*"). Isolated triggers: yield-type is irrelevant (`int32` and `bytes` both hit it); the trigger is *narrowing an Optional reference-type self field inside the generator*. A generator that reads a non-Optional scalar field (`self._n`), or one where the narrowed field's method *mutates* self (so the generator is correctly inferred non-const), avoids it. Same "resumable generator method over a self field" family the async/generator TODO warns about. Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid. Workaround: ensure the narrowed field's method mutates self, or copy the field's needed data into a scalar local before the generator. Fix shape: a generator method's self-const inference must account for the resumable-frame's mutation of captured `self` state. The default-drop half this entry also carried is FIXED (2026-09-09): the in-class declaration and the frame ctor now both carry the default whatever the const verdict, verified on this entry's own shape. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/streamprobe/gen_c.py`. Surfaced building `tplib.requests` streaming (`Response.iter_content` over `_raw: HTTPResponse | None`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW] (CPython interop) A boundary-crossed user exception's `self.message = ...` attribute is unreadable on the `.so` (`e.message` -> AttributeError) though CPython-native carries it.** In TPy `self.message = msg` assigns the inherited `BaseException::message` field (the `what()`/`str()` source), NOT a data field -- so `info.fields` excludes it and the data-field setter does not set a `message` attribute; the reconstructed instance (`pytype(e.what())`) has no `.message` either. Under plain CPython (and `uv run tpy`), `self.message = msg` creates a readable instance attribute, so driver-side code reading `e.message` works there but raises `AttributeError` against the compiled `.so`. **Pre-existing** (already true for message-only excs before the data-field rung; just untested -- no driver read `e.message`), surfaced by the `interop-exc-data-fields` cpython-parity pass. **Genuinely unresolvable without modeling `super().__init__`:** TPy conflates `self.message = msg` (would expose `e.message` in CPython) with `super().__init__(msg)` (would NOT), so unconditionally setting a `message` attribute would diverge for the super-init idiom instead. Outside tpyc's diagnostic reach (the reader is plain-Python driver code). Low practical impact (data fields cross via their own attrs; `str(e)`/`e.what()` carry the message). Revisit only if it bites; a fix needs sema to record whether the user explicitly assigned `self.message`.
- **[MED small] `k in <dict>` on a const/readonly dict whose VALUE type is not `Equatable` is wrongly rejected -- the membership falls to a generic element-scan instead of `dict.contains`.** `k in d` where `d` is a const/readonly `dict[str, V]` (an inferred-const `self._store` in a readonly method, or a `readonly[dict[str, V]]` param) and `V` has no `__eq__` is a hard sema error: "'in' requires element type 'V' to conform to 'Equatable' (no '__eq__' method)". Two wrongs: (1) `in` on a dict tests KEYS, so it should never require the VALUE type Equatable; (2) even the fallback scans keys (when `V` IS Equatable, e.g. `dict[str, str]`, it compiles and returns correct key-membership), so `dict.contains` should have been used -- it's O(n), not O(1). A MUTABLE dict[str, V] with non-Equatable V uses `dict.contains` and compiles fine; only the const/readonly receiver drops to the buggy path. So the trigger is receiver const-ness, not the `__contains__` method name (an earlier read misattributed it). Same const-receiver-drops-the-right-lowering family as the borrow-local const-drop fixes already landed (and the storage-tuple/borrow-tuple residual entry below). Loud (sema-rejected), not silent. Workaround: give `V` an `__eq__` (makes `in` compile and scan keys), test membership on a mutable binding, or use `.get(k) is not None`. Fix shape: `k in d` must resolve `dict.__contains__(readonly[K])` on a const/readonly dict receiver too (the const path is dropping the builtin container-membership lowering and demanding the value Equatable). Reproducer `/tmp/agents/cookieprobe` (`name in self._store` in a readonly method over `dict[str, Cookie]`). Surfaced building `tplib.requests` CookieJar. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code) A class that explicitly defines `__hash__` + `__eq__` is still rejected as a `set` element / dict key -- "missing __hash__".** `class Counter: def __eq__(self, other): ...; def __hash__(self) -> int64: return self.value` then `s: set[Counter]` errors `Type 'Counter' cannot be used as a set element (missing __hash__; use @dataclass(frozen=True) or define it explicitly)` -- even though `__hash__` IS defined explicitly. Reproduces on a PLAIN (non-`@export`) class, so it is a general Hashable-conformance gap, not interop-specific. Likely either the hand-written `__hash__` isn't detected by the Hashable-conformance check, or the `-> int64` return type isn't accepted where a plain `int`/`Py_hash_t` is expected (unverified which). Rejects-valid: a user cannot put a hand-hashable class in a `set`/`dict` key at all; the only path is `@dataclass(frozen=True)`. Consequence for interop: an exposed class can never be a `set` element / dict key even in principle, which is *why* the container-element rung (`interop-container-element-exposed-types`) defers those positions rather than admitting them. Fix shape: make the set/dict-key Hashable check recognize an explicit `__hash__`+`__eq__` pair (and confirm the accepted `__hash__` return type). **When fixing, ALSO add + test a principled interop reject (`_unsupported_exposed_element` in `tpyc/interop/module_validators.py::_exposed_form_error`): an `@export` class cannot be a `set`-element / dict KEY at the CPython boundary regardless of its `__hash__` -- a class copies per element at the boundary (copy-on-cross), so it has no stable hash identity for a hash table. Today the over-broad Hashable check incidentally rejects it, so that interop reject would be un-observable dead code now; fixing THIS bug removes the shadow and would silently open the copy-vs-hash-identity footgun without the interop guard (see TODO container-boundary item 1-iv).** Reproducer `/tmp/agents/plain_hash.py`. Surfaced probing set-element admission during the container-element rung. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A view-form str source inside a NESTED list literal emits ill-formed C++ -- `m: list[list[str]] = [[sv]]` (StrView `sv`) renders `{{sv}}` with no `std::string` wrap.** The inner literal gets no element target at un-threaded nested positions (list elements do not thread, unlike Array elements and dict values), so the view->owned copy chokepoint never fires and the brace-init tries to seat a `std::string_view` in a `std::string` slot -- g++ rejects it. Loud (toolchain-caught), rejects-valid. Workaround: bind the inner list first (`row = [sv]; m = [row]`) or wrap explicitly (`[[str(sv)]]`). Fix shape: thread the element target through nested list-literal positions (the same threading Array/dict already get) so `_view_source_to_owned` fires. THIR gate-rejects the shape (`container_lit.nested_view`). Surfaced by the THIR container-literal cell's probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `q: Ptr[DynProto] = None` emits `auto q = nullptr;` -- a `std::nullptr_t` local, so a later `q = p;` is a hard C++ error.** Only dynamic-protocol pointees hit it (record pointees spell `Cell* q = nullptr;` correctly): `_cpp_decl_type` sends any protocol-containing decl type to `auto` without excluding the null-literal init. Loud (toolchain-caught), rejects-valid. Workaround: initialize from a real pointer or declare at first real assignment. Fix shape: spell the pointer type (not `auto`) when the init is a None literal, or special-case the null init in the protocol-containing branch. THIR gate-rejects the first-decl shape. - **[LOW small] (misleading diagnostic; one rejects-valid face) Global-shadowing edge cases are REJECTED by a lowering drilldown that names codegen and the global, never the shadowing local.** [`global-shadow-shapes-rejected-not-diverging`] Re-measured 2026-09-15; the three shapes this entry used to call silent divergences all stop the compile: `G += 1` with no `global` statement gives *not yet supported ... - **[LOW small] A member named like a recursive-union-alias wrapper still shadows it -- the last uncovered kind of the member/type-name collision class.** The shadow-qualification fix qualifies a local type reference inside a record whose member shares its name, but its `shadow_names` set (`sema/analyzer.py:_compute_record_shadow_facts`) and the flag-aware render paths cover only records, enums, and local `@dynamic` protocols. A recursive-union alias (`type Tree = int | list["Tree"]`) compiles to a wrapper struct named `Tree` with a *distinct* render path (`recursive_alias_cpp_names` / `RecursiveAliasInstanceType.to_cpp`, not `_cpp_base_name`), so a record with a member named `Tree` that references the `Tree` alias re-emits the original `'Tree' does not name a type` build error (compile-verified). Non-recursive aliases don't collide (they resolve to their target's C++ name). Toolchain-caught (loud), not silent; exotic shape. Fixing it conditionally means making a THIRD render path flag-aware -- more of the per-render-path parallel machinery the always-qualify consolidation (TODO.md `[consolidation debt]`) deletes outright; prefer closing it via that consolidation, not a 4th flag-aware branch. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion of the member/type-name collision fix.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) An `@overload`-ed `async def` emits one resumable frame PER OVERLOAD ENTRY, all sharing one struct name -- a C++ redefinition.** [`overload-async-frame-per-stub`] Two `@overload` stubs plus the impl for `async def go(...)` emit THREE `struct __coro_go` definitions and three `__coro_go::__poll__` bodies (the two stub frames carry the "fell through without returning a value" panic body), plus three factories all returning the same-named type -- g++ reports a redefinition. The generator twin does not have this: a `...` stub body is not a generator, so only the impl reaches the frame emitter and the set emits one frame. An `async def` stub is still async, so each entry reaches `gen_async.gen_coro_poll_def` / `gen_factory` in `codegen_cpp/generator.py`'s router. Toolchain-caught, not silent. Fix shape: skip frame + factory emission for an async OVERLOAD STUB (it has no body to drive a frame), leaving the impl's single frame, and give the factory the per-stub signatures the sync overload path already emits -- i.e. make the async router agree with the generator router about which entries own a frame. Consequence while it stands: THIR must keep rejecting the shape (the generator's one-body carve-out in `thir/lower/functions.py` deliberately does not extend to async; the unit that pinned that rejection went with the THIR unit suite). Repro: two `@overload` stubs over an `async def go(...)` impl -- each overload entry reaches the frame emitter, so three identically-named `__coro_go` frames are emitted. Beyond the redefinition, two further symptoms come with it: the stubs' `...` bodies become empty poll bodies, so the real implementation's body is DROPPED, and the emitted signatures reference `tpystd::coro` without the include (`'tpystd::coro' has not been declared`). The front end accepts the module, so all of it surfaces only at the C++ build. This entry absorbed a duplicate filed independently nine days later by a different lane -- one defect, two filings; the volume of concurrent agent work is what made that possible, so prefer grepping a symptom string before filing. Surfaced evaluating that carve-out for async during the THIR stdlib grind. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A generic dynamic-attribute dunder (`def __getattr__[T]`/`__setattr__`/`__delattr__`) passes comp and emits an uninstantiable template method -- C++ build error.** `_validate_dyn_dunder_kind` (`tpyc/sema/registration.py:219`) rejects @native/@staticmethod/@property/@overload/generator/@error_return on a dyn-attr dunder but NOT `type_params` (nor `is_async`), so `def __getattr__[T](self, name: str) -> str` translates cleanly to `template<typename T> std::string __getattr__(std::string_view) const` -- and the attribute-access lowering calls `__getattr__(name)` with no template args and `T` in no deducible position, so g++ can't deduce `T`. Toolchain-caught, not silent; exotic form, no current user impact. Fix shape: extend `_validate_dyn_dunder_kind` to reject `type_params` and `is_async` (the D16 dyn-attr feature is deliberately NOT coupled to the interop `export_shape` core -- narrower reject set, own messages). Surfaced by `/tpy-review` of the export-class-validation consolidation. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A generic function that forwards a protocol-typed param into another generic function's protocol bound emits an undeclared template param -- C++ build error.** Inside `def forward[A, B](p: Pair[A, B]): return take(p)` where `take[K, V, T: Pair[K, V]]`, the inner call renders `take<A, B, T>(p)` with `T` never declared in the enclosing scope -> g++ "'T' was not declared in this scope". Inference itself is correct (K/V solve from the protocol param, and this is the only end-to-end exercise of the `_infer_protocol_type_arg_from_protocol` protocol-to-protocol path); the failure is downstream codegen not monomorphizing the inner bound's `T` when the conformer is itself a protocol-typed local. Pre-existing and NOT multi-param-specific: the single-param analog (`forward[A](p: Src[A])` calling `take[R, T: Cont[R]]`) fails identically. Toolchain-caught, not silent. Related to the async-frame template-loss entries but a distinct sync generic-call site. Fix shape: monomorphize the inner call's bound type-param against the inferred conformer (the protocol-typed param's concrete instantiation) instead of emitting the bare bound name. Consequence: the `_from_protocol` multi-param inference path has no end-to-end test coverage (blocked here) -- filed as a TODO follow-up. Surfaced building multi-param associated-type inference. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW medium] A generic call that fails inference because an argument doesn't satisfy a generic-protocol bound reports the vague "Cannot infer type arguments" instead of the precise "does not satisfy bound".** `unwrap(NoGet(1))` where `def unwrap[R, T: Container[R]](x: T) -> R` and `NoGet` lacks `get()` errors `Cannot infer type arguments for 'unwrap'. Specify explicitly: unwrap[R, T](...)` -- the real problem is that `NoGet` doesn't conform to `Container[R]` (so the associated-type pass can't solve `R`, and it's rejected at the reject-unresolved loop `tpyc/sema/type_ops.py:1468` before ever reaching the bound-conformance check at :1477). The EXPLICIT-args spelling already gives the good message (`Type argument 'NoGet' does not satisfy bound 'Container[int]' for type parameter 'T'`, via `validate_type_param_bounds`); only the inferred path is vague. Root: `infer_type_params_for_function` returns a bare `None` for BOTH "genuinely uninferrable" and "bound violated", collapsing them so the caller can't tell which message to emit -- the `None` is deliberately silent so overload resolution can fall through to the next candidate (`type_ops.py:1481`). Rejects-invalid-code (correct rejection, misleading message), not a miscompile. Discriminator for the right message: when a sibling param stays unresolved, check whether the carrier conforms to the bound with the sibling left free -- non-conforming -> "does not satisfy bound"; conforming-but-sibling-unrecoverable -> "cannot infer" is correct. Fix shape (do NOT band-aid with a one-off out-param): the proper fix is a structured inference-failure result (reason + offending param/bound) returned by `infer_type_params_for_function`, routed so overload resolution stays silent (it discards the reason and tries the next candidate). SCOPE -- consolidate ONLY the tier that funnels through that primitive's `None` return: the free-function generic calls (`calls.py:3837/4353/5101/5128`), generic methods (`methods.py:2061`), and its record sibling `infer_type_params_for_record` (`calls.py:5484/5682`); the shared silent caller is `overloads.py:655`. Do NOT fold in two adjacent-but-separate mechanisms: the empty-container factory messages (`_raise_empty_container_from_arg` calls.py:761, and :1207/:1264) are `list()`/`dict()`/`set()` element inference keyed on `get_element_type`/`PendingListType`, a distinct path that may adopt the same failure vocabulary later but should not be force-merged here; and `_unsafe_cast_diagnostics` (:4727) is a bespoke per-function diagnostic with its own TODO to become a `@compiler_check` decorator. Touches overload resolution -- needs the `/tpy-fix-bug` design pass, not a spot patch. Regression guard `tests/cases/generics/error_assoc_type_unsolvable` pins the current (weak) message. Surfaced by user review of the associated-type-inference branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A None-typed generic result captured in a local cannot be used -- `std::monostate` vs `nullptr_t` hard C++ error.** `r: None = f()` where `f`'s type param inferred to `None` (e.g. `identity[R](x: R) -> R` called with `None`) emits a `std::monostate` local, and a later `r is None` renders `operator==` against `nullptr` -- no such overload, hard C++ error, no TPy diagnostic. Pre-existing (reproduces on merge-base with plain generic functions, independent of associated-type inference), but the `-> None`-satisfies-`R` protocol path makes it newly reachable via `spawn(none_task).join()` results bound to locals; consuming `join()` as a bare statement is unaffected. Toolchain-caught, rejects-valid. Fix shape: render a None-typed name read in an `is None` / boolean context as a constant `true`/`false` (its value is statically known), or map the comparison to monostate equality. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the associated-type-inference branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (parity) A temp-hoisted call argument evaluates BEFORE a side-effecting receiver, reversing CPython's receiver-first order.** `make("R").eat(Box(mk("A")))` where `make()` (the receiver) and `mk()` (nested in a value-union-param arg) both print: the arg is hoisted to a `std::variant __tmp = ...;` statement emitted BEFORE the `make("R").eat(__tmp)` call expression, so the arg's side effect ("arg A") runs before the receiver's ("recv R") -- TPy prints `arg A / recv R`, CPython `recv R / arg A`. Only observable when BOTH the receiver expression and a temp-hoisted arg have side effects (a plain inline arg keeps correct order; a plain-name receiver has no side effect). Silent (no diagnostic, wrong order). Independent of the value-union double-eval fix (that fixed the COUNT; this is ORDER) -- the lazy-args change moved arg emission after receiver GENERATION but the arg's hoisted temp STATEMENT still precedes the inline-receiver call expression. Fix shape: when the receiver expression is side-effecting/non-trivial and any arg hoists a temp, lift the receiver into its own temp first (emit it before the arg temps), or emit arg temps after the receiver temp. Self-contained repro: a `Box.__init__(self, tz: Fixed | Zone | None = None)` (two value-record union arms force the arg hoist) plus `make(tag: str) -> Own[Box]` and `mk(tag: str) -> Fixed` that each `print(tag)`, then `make("R").eat(Box(mk("A")))` -- prints `A` then `R` (CPython `R` then `A`). Surfaced adding a side-effecting-receiver arm to the double-eval regression test; pre-existing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (parity) Rebinding `self` inside a method silently reads the ORIGINAL receiver afterwards -- CPython reads the rebound object.** `def peek(self, other: "Chain") -> int: self = other; return self.n` -- codegen emits a fresh shadowing decl for the rebind (`const Chain& self = other;`) but every subsequent `self` read still renders against the receiver (`this->n` / `return (*this);`), so TPy returns the original object's state where CPython returns `other`'s. Silent (compiles clean, wrong value). Workaround: rename the local (don't rebind `self`). Root: codegen never seeds the receiver as a scope NAME, so the rebind creates a shadow local, but the `self`-read special-casing (the `this` render) doesn't know about the shadow. Fix shape: either reject `self` rebinds with a clear diagnostic (Rust-flavored; simplest and arguably better than the confusing CPython pattern) or route post-rebind reads through the shadow local. NB the THIR path GATE-REJECTS bodies with `self` rebinds (they fall back to this AST render), so fixing this fixes both paths. Self-contained repro: /tmp/agents/self_reassign_probe shape. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the THIR return-slot-tail branch; pre-existing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Reading an Optional-REFERENCE element out of a tuple param drops const -- ill-formed C++.** `def read(pair: tuple[Box | None, int]): first = pair[0]` where `Box` is a reference type: the tuple param lowers to `const std::tuple<const Box*, ...>&` (element 0 is `const Box*`), but the extracted local is typed `Box* first = std::get<0>(pair)` -> "invalid conversion from `const Box*` to `Box*`" (g++, -fpermissive). The const of the borrowed tuple isn't propagated to the pointer-repr Optional element local. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. A plain (non-Optional) reference tuple element and a value-type Optional element are unaffected; the bug is specific to the pointer-repr-Optional element read. Fix shape: the tuple-element-extraction local for a pointer-repr Optional slot must inherit the source tuple's const-ness (`const Box*`), mirroring how plain reference elements already const-propagate. Self-contained repro: `class Box: def __init__(self, v: int) -> None: self.v = v` + `def read(pair: tuple[Box | None, int]) -> int: first = pair[0]; return first.v if first is not None else -1`, called `read((Box(5), 9))`. Surfaced adding an Optional-borrow-slot arm to the tuple double-eval regression test (union/tuple_arg_union_eval_once); pre-existing, unrelated to that fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A value of a SUB-union type does not coerce to a param/slot of a wider union (`timezone | None` arg to a `timezone | ZoneInfo | None` param is a type error) -- rejects-valid.** Sema reports "Type mismatch in argument 'tzinfo': expected None | ZoneInfo | timezone, got timezone | None"; CPython/typing accept member-subset unions. Workaround: annotate the local as the full target union upfront (datetime.py strptime/fromisoformat do this, with a comment pointing here). Fix shape: union-to-union coercion when every source member coerces to some target member (the C++ side needs a variant-widening conversion helper, mirroring to_value_variant). Surfaced by datetime v4's tz-slot widening. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An Optional or union parameter on a nested def is a hard compile error.** [`nested-def-optional-param`] `def get(r: Rec | None)` or `def pick(x: int32 | None)` nested inside a function fails codegen with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.nested_def:nesteddef.param_type)`, from the nested-def param classifier at `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:4861`. The shape never worked: a nested def lowers to a C++ lambda whose params never receive the pointer/optional classification top-level params get, so the body read (`r.v`, field access on a never-classified name) and the call-site conversion (`get(a)` / `get(std::nullopt)`) disagreed and g++ rejected the combination -- the reject replaces that ill-formed render. Everyday shape (an Optional param on a helper closure is ordinary Python), so worth queueing. Container params (`list`/`dict`/`set`/`bytearray`, `readonly[...]` included) were admitted on 2026-09-03 (`tests/cases/nested_def/container_params`); Optional and union parameter forms remain rejected by the lambda parameter gate. Fix shape: seed the lambda's params with the same classification top-level params get, plus the optional-ptr call-arg conversion at closure call sites, then widen the admission. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_452_nesteddef_opt_param.py` and `02_452b_scalar.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
  An ordinary union parameter `y: str | int32` also rejects at `stmt.nested_def:nesteddef.param_type` before the nested body lowers. The gate admits scalar, char, enum, str/bytes and supported reference types but excludes UnionType, independently of match indexing or narrowed-union capture. It is unchanged from pre-merge `987d04c5`. The repair must align lambda signature/body parameter classification and closure-call conversions; nested helpers emitted as resumable frame members use a separate path without this gate.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A nested def shadowing a BUILTIN name is a hard compile error at the call site.** [`nested-def-shadowing-builtin-call-rejected`] `def abs(x)` inside a function, then `abs(-3)`, fails codegen with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.call:call.closure_import_shadow)`, from the callee classifier at `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:3747`. Previously this was SILENT wrong behavior -- the call reached `::std::abs`, not the closure, where CPython calls the closure -- so the loud reject is a strict improvement, but the valid program still does not compile. A closure shadowing a builtin is exotic, so low priority to queue. Fix shape: resolve the callee against the enclosing function's nested-def locals BEFORE the imported/builtin arm (sema's resolution already points at the closure), then widen the admission. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_453_nesteddef_shadow_builtin.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. The IMPORTED-name twin rejects the same way: `from tpy import dispatch` / `def outer(): def dispatch() -> int32: ...; return dispatch()` stops at `call.closure_import_shadow` (surfaced 2026-09-12 by `int/scalar_type_names`, whose nested-def section therefore defines the shadowing def without calling it).
- **[MED small] A package __init__ that calls submodule functions from record-method bodies emits circular C++ includes -- the build fails whenever a submodule TU is compiled first.** Package-import semantics emit `child.hpp #include parent.hpp` (importing `pkg._sub` imports `pkg` first), and the parent includes the child it uses -- a cycle. Harmless when the parent's uses are in free functions (defined out-of-line in .cpp; `os/` works this way), but record METHODS emit inline in the parent header, so a TU that includes `child.hpp` first sees the parent's inline bodies before the child's declarations (`#pragma once` skips the in-flight re-include) -> `'pkg::_sub' has not been declared`. Hit by the attempted `lib/tpy/datetime/` package split (class-heavy __init__ calling `_fmt`/`_parse` helpers from datetime methods); worked around by flat `_datetime_*` sibling modules (no parent edge, acyclic). Fix shape: emit forward declarations for the parent's cross-submodule uses, or drop the child->parent include when the child does not reference parent symbols, or emit record method bodies out-of-line in the .cpp when they reference submodules. Validation case once fixed: restructure datetime as a package with a pure re-export `__init__.py` + `_types.py` submodule holding the classes (the preferred target layout; a re-export-only parent does NOT dodge the bug today -- the parent must include the types module, so a sibling TU still enters it with its own header in-flight). Surfaced by the datetime v3 module split. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Tuple-unpack targets assigned in SIBLING branches are not hoisted -- the second branch emits an assignment to an undeclared name (invalid C++).** `if flag: a, b = pair(1) ... else: a, b = pair(2)` -- the first branch emits a block-scoped declaration (`::tpy::BigInt a = std::get<0>(...)`), the second emits plain `a = std::get<0>(...)` where `a` no longer exists -> g++ "'a' was not declared in this scope". Plain (non-tuple) assignments in sibling branches hoist correctly; the pre-scan hoisting misses tuple-unpack targets. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent; any multi-branch parser/dispatcher shape hits it. Workaround: unique per-branch names (datetime v3's `_apply_directive` ships with this workaround baked in -- revert to shared names when fixed). Fix shape: teach the pre-scan hoisting pass to treat tuple-assign targets like plain assign targets. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/dt_v3/repro_unpack_hoist.py`. Surfaced by datetime v3's strptime engine. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A format spec on a user-record, `bytes`, `bytearray` or `range` f-string placeholder is misapplied to the `__str__` result instead of dispatching (or being rejected) -- silent divergence for `std::format`-legal specs.** `f"{rec:>30}"` compiles to `std::format("{:>30}", ::tpy::__str__(rec))` and prints a 30-column right-padded `rec`; CPython calls `rec.__format__(">30")`, which for a plain record (`object.__format__`) raises `TypeError: unsupported format string passed to Rec.__format__`, and for spec-aware types (datetime delegates to strftime) produces entirely different output. The stub types that render through the same `__str__` row diverge the same way: `f"[{b:>10}]"` for `b = b"ab"` prints `[     b'ab']` and `f"{range(2):>12}"` / `f"{bytearray(b'ab'):>16}"` pad likewise, where CPython raises `TypeError: unsupported format string passed to bytes.__format__` (`range.__format__`, `bytearray.__format__`) -- probe `/tmp/agents/rbr/p5.py`, 2026-09-26. Specs that are NOT string-legal (`f"{dt:%Y}"`) fail as a raw g++ `std::format` error (leaky diagnostic, no TPy sema error). Sema rejects specs only on BigInt/IntLiteral (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py:4082`); the f-string emitter (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:1451-1455`) splices the spec around whatever the placeholder rendered, the `__str__` call included. Fix shape: sema rejects non-empty format specs on types without `__format__` -- user records and the bytes/bytearray/range stubs alike (loud, CPython-faithful) until a `__format__` protocol lands (TODO.md); datetime's strftime delegation rides on that feature. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_456_record_fstring_spec.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A ternary mixing a str slice with a str param is rejected: "Incompatible types in ternary expression: 'StrView' and 'str'".** `timestr = tstr[:i] if i > 0 else tstr` (with `tstr: str` a param) fails sema although both arms are the same runtime type (str IS StrView); spelled as an if/else assignment it compiles fine. Rejects-valid annoyance in parser-style code. Fix shape: unify str/StrView in the ternary join like assignment contexts already do. Surfaced by datetime v3's fromisoformat port. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A frozen dataclass with an `Optional[record]` field cannot synthesize `__hash__`: "No matching overload for hash(R | None)".** `@dataclass(frozen=True)` with `inner: R | None` fails at the synthesized `__hash__` because the `hash()` builtin overload set has no Optional arm (eq synthesis handles the field fine). Workaround: hand-write `__hash__` (datetime's aware `datetime` needed one anyway). Fix shape: an `Optional[T]`-accepting `hash` overload (hash the inner or a None sentinel, matching CPython's `hash(None)` stability) or field-wise None handling in the dataclass hash builder. Surfaced by the datetime v3 tzinfo-field probe. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) BigInt-default module: a LITERAL str/bytes slice bound is a hard compile error.** Under `--default-int BigInt` (or `default_int: BigInt`), `s[1:3]` fails codegen with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.expr_stmt:subscript.slice_shape)`, raised at `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:5952`. The shape was never admitted because the render it would have to reproduce is ill-formed C++: the slice-bound narrow appended the runtime-BigInt conversion to ANY bound with no literal exemption, so `::tpy::BasicSlice{1.to_fixed_check<int32_t>(), 3.to_fixed_check<int32_t>()}` lexed `1.to_fixed_check` as one preprocessing-number token. Negated literal bounds (`s[-2:i]`) are the same row. Everyday shape in a BigInt-default module, so worth queueing. Scope verified: the same slice compiles under the default int, and a name-bound slice (`lo = 1; s[lo:hi]`) compiles under BigInt -- the bind-a-local workaround stands. Fix shape: exempt literal bounds in int32 range from the narrow (the BasicSlice int32 field absorbs them) or parenthesize the render before appending, then widen the admission. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_459_bigint_slice_lit.py` and `02_459b_name_bounds.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The record-subscript BigInt-narrow width derives from `__getitem__`'s key param for ALL subscript operations -- a record whose `__delitem__`/`__setitem__` declares a different key width (or that has no single-int-key `__getitem__` at all) gets the wrong narrow on del/store.** [`record-subscript-bigint-narrow-width`] `bigint_index_narrow_type` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) consults `record_getitem_key_ret` only; sema's `del c[k]` requires just `__delitem__` and never validates the index against its key param (`tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~5166), so a record with `__delitem__(key: int)` and no `__getitem__` falls to the int32 default and `del c[2**40]` panics where CPython works -- the original BigInt-dict-key panic, alive on this rare path. A `__setitem__` key width differing from `__getitem__`'s narrows stores to the getitem width (AST and THIR share the helper, so both are consistently wrong the same way). Workaround: declare a single-int-key `__getitem__` with the intended key width. Fix shape: thread the operation's dunder into the helper (per-op key-param lookup via the same substitution-aware sema accessor, `__setitem__`/`__delitem__` falling back to `__getitem__`); the THIR mirror follows automatically (shared helper). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion on the BigInt-dict-key fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A structural protocol declaring `__getitem__` with a BigInt key param fails C++ concept satisfaction for conforming user records -- the shape never builds.** A `Protocol` with `def __getitem__(self, key: int) -> str` emits a concept requiring `::tpy::__getitem__(t, std::declval<::tpy::BigInt>())`, which a conforming record (methods/operator[], no free-dunder arm for the record type) does not satisfy -- g++ rejects at monomorphization. Loud, not silent. When this shape is made to work, note the subscript index render also needs the receiver's declared key width: `bigint_index_narrow_type` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) consults dict key types and concrete user-record `__getitem__` key params but falls to the int32 default for protocol-typed receivers, so a BigInt index would round-trip BigInt -> int32 and panic beyond int32. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bigint-dict-key/probe_proto.py`. Surfaced by the BigInt-dict-key subscript fix survey. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Enum members outside int32 range are accepted at sema but emit `enum class E : int32_t { A = 5000000000 }` -- ill-formed C++ (build failure).** `class BigE(Enum): A = 5000000000` compiles cleanly through sema, but the emitted enum's underlying type is unconditionally `int32_t` while the enumerator value exceeds it -- g++ rejects the narrowing. `EnumUtil<E>::from_value` similarly spells `.to_fixed_check<int32_t>()` for a BigInt arg (`einfo.underlying_type` is always int32 today), so even if the decl compiled, out-of-range lookups would panic. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. Workaround: keep enum member values within int32 range. Fix shape: infer the underlying type from the member value range (int32 -> int64 widening; reject beyond int64), threading it through `EnumInfo.underlying_type` so the decl, `from_value`, and the fstring/print `static_cast<int>` arms all agree -- or reject out-of-int32 members at sema with a clear diagnostic. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probes-bigint/probe2.py` (`BigE`). Surfaced by the THIR BigInt-narrow probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid) `not rec` is rejected for a user record without `__bool__`/`__len__`, although `if rec:` accepts the same operand.** `not make()` errors "Invalid operand type for 'not': Rec (expected bool, numeric, or type with __bool__/__len__)" while the bare truthiness context compiles and applies Python's always-true default. CPython accepts both (`not` is defined for every object). The asymmetry is sema-only -- codegen renders the negated always-true form fine, as the plain-enum sibling shows. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/truthy-arm/repro.py` (the removed `not make_rec()` line). Fix shape: let the `not` operand check accept any type the truthiness context accepts (the always-true default), rather than requiring a truthiness dunder. Do this together with the always-true truthiness WARNING queued in TODO.md -- both halves read the same no-truthiness-hook verdict sema already computes here, and fixing this one alone leaves `if rec:` silent about being unconditional. Surfaced fixing the folded-truthiness operand drop. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (missing diagnostic) The optional-truthiness warning does not fire for a `match` case GUARD, only for an `if`/`while` condition.** `case 1 if v:` with `v: int32 | None` compiles silently, where the equivalent `if v:` warns "Truthiness check on optional value may also exclude falsy non-None values; use 'is not None' for None-only checks". The guard is a boolean context with the same footgun (a `Some(0)` payload is falsy), so the user loses the nudge exactly where the pattern-match reads most like a None test. Codegen is correct -- only the sema diagnostic is missing; the warning is raised where `if`/`while` conditions are analysed and match guards do not route through it. Witness: `tests/cases/match/guard_truthiness` (its `# tpyc: ok` annotation pins the current no-warning behavior). Fix shape: raise the same warning from the match-guard analysis path. Surfaced fixing the resumable/guard truthiness render. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Un-narrowed truthiness of a pointer-repr `Optional[container]` (`list`/`dict`/`set`/`bytearray`) ignores inner emptiness -- `if xs:` on a `list[int] | None` emits the bare non-null pointer test, so a non-None but EMPTY container reads truthy (silent CPython divergence).** The un-narrowed form renders `if (xs)` instead of `xs != nullptr && !xs->empty()`; CPython's `bool(container)` is length-based, so an empty non-None container takes the branch in TPy but not in CPython. The *narrowed*-by-name form (`if xs is not None: if xs:`) IS correct -- it dispatches `::tpy::__len__((*xs)) != 0` via the narrowed-occurrence swap in `gen_truthy_expr`. The sibling `Optional[user-record]` case dispatches `::tpy::ptr_truthy` in both forms; containers are excluded from the un-narrowed `ptr_truthy` path by the `is_user_record` gate (`ptr_truthy` dispatches `__bool__`/`__len__` *member* calls that the container runtime types do not expose). Workaround: test `len(xs) > 0`, or narrow and bind. Fix shape: extend the un-narrowed pointer-repr Optional truthiness dispatch to route builtin-container inners through their `.empty()`/`__len__` truthiness. Sibling of the storage-form `Optional[record]` truthiness entry below (same "the source shape is excluded from the dunder dispatch" family). Surfaced during the `Optional[record]` truthiness fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Truthiness of a STORAGE-FORM `Optional[record]` source (a record FIELD or a container ELEMENT) skips the record's `__bool__`/`__len__` -- `if self.f:` / `if xs[0]:` on a `Record | None` field/element emits the bare `std::optional` non-null test, so a non-None but falsy record reads truthy (silent CPython divergence).** [`optional-record-elem-truthiness-has-value`] The pointer-repr `Optional[record]` truthiness fix dispatches the dunder only for sources that render as a raw `T*` (pointer name / call return); a field or container element is `std::optional<Record>` storage (`is_storage_form_optional_source`), which is deliberately excluded (a `ptr_truthy`/deref there would fail to compile) and falls back to the pre-existing `has_value()` render. The narrowed field form (`if self.f is None: ...; if self.f:`) is worse -- it emits `::tpy::__bool__(this->f)` against the `std::optional`, a toolchain-caught build error (pre-existing, unrelated to the un-narrowed silent case). Workaround: bind to a local first (`x = self.f; if x: ...`) so the source is a pointer name. Fix shape: unwrap the storage-form `std::optional` (`optional_to_ptr` / `(*opt)`) before dispatching the inner record's truthiness, mirroring what the pointer-name path does; the narrowed field build-error needs the same unwrap. THIR keeps these on the AST path (`truthy.optional_field_narrow`). Surfaced by the /tpy-review of the `Optional[record]` truthiness fix. **The `@property` spelling reaches the same arm since 2026-09-18** -- `if b.rec:` over an `Optional[Rec]` getter renders the bare engagement test exactly as the field read does, so the divergence is one spelling wider, not one deeper, and the fix at the shared arm (`_storage_opt_record_truthy`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) closes both; probe `/tmp/agents/r2/nt_rec.py` and its field twin. **An un-narrowed Optional CONTAINER receiver reaches it too since the runtime-checked receiver landed** -- `if xs[0]:` on `list[Rec | None] | None` (a `Rec` with `__bool__` returning False) prints the element truthy, like its narrowed and plain-list twins; probe `/tmp/agents/bundle3/review/parity/truthy.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `Any` holding a user record whose only truthiness hook is `__len__` is always truthy.** `any_to_bool_capable` in `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/any.hpp` recognizes bool construction, `.empty()`, and `.__bool__()`, but not `.__len__()`. It therefore installs Any's default always-true slot even though direct implicit truthiness correctly evaluates `::tpy::__len__(record) != 0`; an empty record wrapped in `Any` diverges from CPython. Workaround: define `__bool__` as well as `__len__`, or avoid erasing the value to `Any` before the test. Fix shape: add the `__len__` capability and dispatch to the same length-based truthiness used for direct records. THIR's `::tpy::to_bool(any)` mode faithfully preserves the existing runtime behavior. Surfaced by the THIR structured-truthiness probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A walrus-bound `with` manager (`with (m := CM()):`) is a hard compile error.** Codegen fails with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.walrus)`, raised at `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:6890` for a walrus target the prescan hoisted. The shape was never admitted because the render it would have to reproduce is ill-formed: the hoisted `std::optional<CM> m;` pre-decl landed at the first statement INSIDE the `try {}`, after the `auto __ctx_N = (m = CM(...), *m);` line that reads it, so g++ rejected `'m' was not declared in this scope`, and post-with reads dangled. Scope verified: an ordinary walrus in a condition (`if (m := n + 1) > 2:`) lowers fine, so only the hoisted-target / with-manager face rejects. Exotic; workaround is to bind first (`m = CM(); with m:`). Fix shape: place the hoisted pre-decl in the enclosing scope, before the `__ctx_N` header line rather than after it, then widen the admission. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_469_walrus_with.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A global-variable write BEFORE its `global` statement compiles and runs; CPython rejects it as SyntaxError.** `def f(): g = 1; global g; g = 2` compiles in TPy (both writes hit the module global; `f()` leaves `g == 2`) where CPython raises `SyntaxError: name 'g' is assigned to before global declaration`. Root: `ast.parse` accepts the shape (CPython's check lives in the symtable stage, which TPy's parser never runs) and sema's `_analyze_global_stmt` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) has no ordering check -- `function_global_decls` is a whole-function set, so every write is treated as a global write regardless of position. Accepts-invalid parity gap, not a miscompile: TPy's behavior is self-consistent (and the AST and THIR paths emit byte-identical code for the shape). Workaround: none needed -- valid programs are unaffected. Fix shape: reject an assignment to a name that a LATER `global` statement in the same function declares (a source-order pre-pass over the function body in `_analyze_global_stmt` or the function pre-scan). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion probing the THIR global-seeding invariant (reproducer `/tmp/agents/stmt-shapes/probe_global2.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent] `is_const_union_source` does not see const TUPLE-local roots -- a chain rooted at a const storage/borrow-tuple local still loses const at every const-spelling sink.** The recursive "rooted in a const source" predicate (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py:is_const_union_source`, shared by the union/optional lifts, REF_ALIAS, and `is_const_storage_source`) checks the base name only against `const_ref_params` / `const_indirect_locals`. A name bound const as a TUPLE local (`const_storage_form_tuple_locals` / `const_borrow_form_tuple_locals` / `const_optional_borrow_tuple_locals` -- e.g. a const `auto&&` storage-tuple alias) rooting a deeper chain (`q = pair[1]` where element 1 is itself a pointer-repr tuple, or a union field off such a local) is missed, so the sink declares mutable against a const lvalue (same ill-formed-C++ class as the fixed deep-source entry, one level deeper). Latent: needs nested pointer-repr tuples (or a union field off a const tuple local), not exercised in-corpus. Fix shape: widen the base-name check to all five const name sets -- but that changes `is_const_union_source` for its union/optional consumers too (value-variant lift, storage-optional lift, REF_ALIAS, `.get()` accessor, ptr-variant init), so each needs its own verification + sibling tests. Surfaced closing the deep-source `is_const_storage_source` entry. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) A value printed through an Any-ISINSTANCE-narrowed binding uses C++ default formatting, not Python's.** `def show(v: Any): if isinstance(v, float): print("x", v)` with `show(2.0)` prints `x 2` (CPython `x 2.0`); the bool face prints `1`/`0` instead of `True`/`False` (probes `/tmp/agents/while-arm/probe_floatfmt.py`, `probe_boolfmt.py`). Root: the print-arg classification keys on the DECLARED type (`get_resolved_type` reads the pre-narrow `Any` binding), so the narrowed alias streams raw (`std::cout << __v`) instead of taking the `::tpy::print_float` / `print_bool` formatter -- while a direct `print(2.0)` formats correctly. Un-narrowed Any prints route `::tpy::to_string`-family dispatch and are fine; only the narrowed-alias reads mis-classify. NB THIR mirrors this byte-identically (the D15 Any-narrow arm's print RAW / truthy TO_BOOL declared-type mirrors, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` print loop + `_lower_truthy`) -- when the AST classification is fixed to use the narrowed occurrence type, update both mirrors in lockstep (the unit pins that would have flagged them went with the THIR unit suite). Fix shape: classify print args (and the truthiness arm's declared-Any `to_bool`) by the sema-retyped occurrence type when the arg is a narrowed name. Surfaced by the THIR Any-isinstance arm's byte-diff. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) A `while` condition combining a WALRUS binding with a list-literal argument rejects at `call.arg_shape.container`.** `while (n := head(xs)) > 0 and show([n]) >= 0:` is refused; the record-temporary twin `show(Rec(n))` evaluates per iteration and prints like CPython. The per-iteration loop-head restructure (`while (true) { <temps>; if (!(cond)) break; }`) is gated to walrus-free conditions (`contains_named_expr`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) because an in-head temp could run before the walrus assignment it reads, and a borrow-form walrus aliasing a per-iteration temp would dangle after the loop. Fix shape: hoist an optional slot before the loop and emplace it per iteration (`std::optional<T> __tmp_slot;` + `auto& __tmp_N = __tmp_slot.emplace(<init>);` in the head), interleaving the temp after the walrus it reads. Workaround: `while True:` + `if not ...: break`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) A record rvalue or an owning CALL at a MUTATED method parameter has no hoisting row, where a container literal at the same slot hoists a named temporary.** [`record-rvalue-at-mutated-method-slot-unhoisted`] `a.absorb(A(4))` / `got = k.pick(R(3))` with `def pick(self, r: R) -> R: return r`, and `k.fill(mk())` with `def mk() -> Own[list[int32]]` or `k.fill(copy(d))` (`calls/error_own_call_at_mutable_method_slot`; the `copy()` spelling at a dict / set slot used to render bare and fail the C++ build), reject at `expr.method_call:method.arg_shape`, while `k.fill([1, 2])`, `k.pick([3, 4])` and `ListTaker(copy(w.items))` hoist `__tmp_N` and bind the mutable reference (`calls/method_literal_arg_mutable_slot`, `calls/ctor_mutated_slot_field_arg`). The method family's argument table has the hoist cell for the container literal only; the free-call and constructor families hoist a record rvalue through `_record_rvalue_temp_slot`. The fix is the argument-table family collapse (TODO.md, THE NEXT ORDER item 2), which gives every family the one hoist row. Workaround: bind the rvalue to a local first.
- **[LOW small] (DOES NOT REPRODUCE 2026-09-02 -- confirm and withdraw) isinstance narrowing inside an INFERRED-readonly method drops the const spelling on a plain ptr-union param.** As filed (2026-07-03): a method whose plain (unannotated) `A | B` param is const only by inference (`deep_const_borrow_params`) and which isinstance-narrows that param in its own body lowers to non-const `std::holds_alternative<A*>` / `std::get<A*>` where the AST emits the const forms (`const A*`); the named root was that `_narrow_member_cpp` keyed the const-pointee verdict only on `lc.const_locals` (the U2 field-lift chain) and was never seeded from the method fi's `deep_const_borrow_params`. **That root is gone**: `_narrow_subject_const` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) now falls through to `_param_is_deep_const`, and the described shape emits `std::variant<const A*, const B*>` in the signature with matching `const A*` template args in the narrowing. Re-checked on the cutover branch by emitting the same source both ways (`thir_codegen` False then True) -- byte-identical, with the method in the ROUTED set, so the agreement is not a fallback artifact. The original reproducer path is gone; the re-check used the plain shape the entry describes. Withdraw once someone identifies the commit that fixed it, or supplies a shape that still diverges.
- **[MED small] `match` over a union of two same-canonical-named records is miscompiled: one covering `case` is treated as exhaustive, so the other member hits `std::unreachable()` (UB / silent wrong output).** `from m import Point as Foreign`, local `class Point`, then `def f(p: Foreign | Point): match p: case Point(y=v): return v` -- the union is correctly `std::variant<main::Point*, shapes::Point*>`, but the match is wrongly marked exhaustive, so codegen emits `switch(index())` with only `case 0` (the local `Point` arm) followed by `::std::unreachable()` and a dead `return -1`. A `Foreign` (index 1) subject falls through to `std::unreachable()` -> UB; observed silent wrong output (`f(Foreign(7))` returned `9`, the previous local value's register, instead of falling through). Root cause: union coverage is keyed by `str(member)` (bare name) -- `_match_missing_cases`'s `UnionType` arm (`str(m) not in seen_types`) and `_build_pattern_type_key` (`str(resolved) + constraint`) -- so the two same-canonical-named members both render `"Point"` and collapse to one coverage key, making a single `case Point` look like it covers both. The third and most severe site of the bare-`.name`-as-match-identity family (the concrete + union-membership identity sites were fixed on `fix-match-class-pattern-identity`). Pre-existing on `master`. Fix shape: key union coverage/missing-case tracking by qname (mirror the enum `_match_missing_cases` fix on `fix-match-aliased-enum`), so distinct same-named members stay distinct and the match is correctly non-exhaustive (fall through to the after-match code instead of `unreachable`). Sibling survey needed: same-named enum members or literal patterns collapsing in the same `str()`-keyed coverage. Surfaced by a user probe (`Point | ForeignPoint` matching) after `/tpy-review` of `fix-match-class-pattern-identity`; reproducer `/tmp/agents/fp_union/`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An alias-imported record used as a `match` class-pattern against a UNION subject is wrongly rejected as "not a member".** `from m import Widget as W`, then `match u: case W(...)` where `u: W | Other` errors `'W' is not a member of union 'Widget | Other'`. `_resolve_pattern_type` (`tpyc/sema/match.py`) mints the pattern's NominalType with the source spelling (`name="W"`) while the union member carries the canonical name (`name="Widget"`), so the exact-member match (`m == resolved`, `NominalType.__eq__` includes `name`) and the same-bare-name membership check both fail on the alias. Concrete (non-union) subjects work -- they compare the resolved record's qname, not the union-membership path. Pre-existing on `master` (independent of the class-pattern-identity fix; that fix preserved this branch's condition verbatim). Rejects-valid. Workaround: import the record under its own name, or match on a concrete (non-union) subject. Fix shape: resolve the pattern name to its canonical record and mint the NominalType with the canonical name (or match union members by qname), so the alias spelling doesn't defeat membership. Surfaced during `/tpy-review` of `fix-match-class-pattern-identity` while adding a union happy-path test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `match` class-pattern against a union can still bind a wrong same-named *generic* record via the base-name fuzzy fallback.** `_resolve_pattern_type` (`tpyc/sema/match.py`) now rejects a wrong same-named record when all same-bare-named union members are non-parameterized, but when a same-bare-named member IS parameterized (e.g. `Box[str]`) the gate falls through to the pre-existing base-name fuzzy path, which -- for a single cross-module same-named generic member (`len(matches) == 1`) -- binds the pattern's fields against that member without a qname identity check. So `match u: case Box(...)` where `u: mod_b.Box[int32]` and the source-scope `Box` resolves to a distinct `mod_a.Box` can bind the wrong record. Narrow (needs two same-canonical-named generic records across modules, one aliased/in the union); NOT introduced by the class-pattern-identity fix -- that fix strictly added rejections and left this parameterized path unchanged from master. Fix shape: in the fuzzy fallback, require qname identity for a concrete (non-type-arg-ambiguous) pattern before binding, mirroring the non-parameterized gate. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` (safety-model, architecture-fit, cpython-parity) of `fix-match-class-pattern-identity`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `min()`/`max()` reject record operands that define the full comparison surface.** `max(date(2021, 1, 1), date(2020, 5, 5))` -> "No matching overload for max(date, date)" even though `date` (dataclass `order=True` and hand-written dunders alike) supports `<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=`/`==`. The min/max builtin overload set has no comparable-record arm, so every user value type is rejected. Owned `str` operands are refused the same way (`min(s1, s2)` with `s1 = ss[0]` -> "No matching overload for min(str, str)"), while the `key=` form over the same operands resolves. Rejects-valid, loud. Workaround: spell the comparison (`a if a >= b else b`). Affects all datetime types (date/time/datetime/timedelta). Fix shape: a protocol-bound generic overload (`min/max[T: Comparable]`) or routing through the comparable check `sorted()` uses. Surfaced by datetime v2 tests. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An explicit `bool(x)` call on a user value type without `__bool__` is rejected even though the implicit truthiness context works.** `t = time(14, 30); bool(t)` errors ("bool() cannot convert time") while `if t:` / `print(not not t)`-style truthiness correctly treats it as always-truthy (matching CPython's default object truthiness, e.g. time/date/datetime are always truthy since 3.5). The truthiness lowering has a default arm the `bool()` builtin overload set lacks. Rejects-valid, loud, generic (not datetime-specific). Workaround: use the value in a boolean context instead of calling `bool()`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of datetime v2. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (parity, silent wrong output) `abs()` of a BigInt EXPRESSION goes through `double`, so the result loses precision past 2^53 and prints as a float.** [`abs-bigint-expression-via-double`] `print(abs(-(2**40) - 1))` emits `::tpy::print_float(::std::fabs(static_cast<double>(...)))` and prints `1099511627777.0` where CPython prints `1099511627777` -- the value happens to survive at this magnitude, but the type does not, and past 2^53 the value does not either. A NAME-bound BigInt takes the correct arm: `n = -(2**40) - 1; print(abs(n))` emits `::tpy::BigInt::abs(n)` and prints the exact integer, so the two spellings of one expression disagree. Identical on both codegen authors, so this is not a migration artifact and the byte-diff cannot see it. The `abs` overload evidently resolves against a float arm when the argument is an unresolved arithmetic expression rather than a typed name -- the same unchecked float<->fixed-int family as the `round(huge_float)` entry below, but here the wrong arm is chosen at OVERLOAD RESOLUTION rather than inside the cast. Repro: `print(abs(-(2**40) - 1))` under plain `uv run tpy`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. A bare LITERAL past the int32 range takes the float overload too: `print(abs(-3000000000))` prints `3000000000.0` (CPython `3000000000`). Probe `/tmp/agents/ge/f3/abs.py`, found 2026-09-28.
- **[LOW small] (parity) `round(huge_float)` in a bare (default-int) context silently wraps instead of overflowing.** `r = round(1751551805.5 * 1000000)` with no typed target resolves `round[T]` to the default int32, and `round_to<int32_t>` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/builtins.hpp`) does an unchecked `static_cast<T>(std::nearbyint(x))` -> `-2147483648`, where CPython returns the exact int. With an `int`-typed target (`us: int = round(...)`) the BigInt arm is exact and correct. Silent wrong value in the bare case (same unchecked float->fixed-int cast family as `float(huge_int)` -> inf above, opposite direction). Fix shape: `round_to<T>` range-checks before the cast and raises `OverflowError`, or bare-context `round` defaults to BigInt. Surfaced probing datetime v2's `fromtimestamp`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED, deferred: MIR] A class-typed local alias in a resumable (suspending) `async def` follows its SOURCE variable's reassignment instead of preserving object identity -- a CPython divergence, now warned.** `p = w; w = Counter(999)` inside an async def that suspends: TPy reads the NEW instance through `p` (prints 999) where CPython preserves identity. The alias is frame-promoted to a slot that re-reads the source's storage rather than pinning the aliased object. General to resumable frames -- NOT coroutine-handle-specific (reproduces with plain class locals; predates the bound-coroutines feature) and NOT async-specific: an ordinary two-yield generator takes the same frame path, and there the frame is worse than sync -- `p = Point(11); while i < n: alias = p; p = Point(i); yield alias.x` yields `11 1 2` where CPython yields `11 0 1` (re-measured 2026-09-29; the frame alias is now warned, *'alias' will not keep the object ...*, but still emitted). Sync bodies are NOT correct here either, contrary to what this entry previously claimed: their separate rebind slot covers exactly ONE generation, so a loop rebind clobbers from the second iteration on -- the same single-slot-reuse root cause as the sync entry above. Probes `/tmp/agents/narrow/gen_trace.py`, `plain_trace.py`. Also underlies the bound-method-coroutine receiver capture: `w = Counter(40); c = w.bump(5); w = Counter(999); await c` silently reads the reassigned receiver. Wrong-value divergence under a warning. Repro: /tmp/agents/coro/general_alias_reassign_async.py (from /tpy-review of the bound-coroutines zero-alloc round, cpython-parity specialist). Fix shape: frame-promoted alias slots must pin the aliased OBJECT at bind time, not re-derive through the source slot -- align with the sync pointer-local model. DISPOSITION (bound-coroutines /tpy-ready): the feature's receiver-borrow guarantee knowingly ships with this hole (rebinding the receiver between bind and consume reads the new object through the handle); an owning MOVE of the receiver is caught (demoted to copy+warn, test async_bind_receiver_moved), reassignment is not -- a conservative rebind-while-borrowed guard symmetric with the move demotion is a design option deferred to this fix. No committed test pins the rebind divergence (it would pin wrong output); repro above. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `.cancel()` is callable on a bare coroutine value (not just Tasks) -- CPython raises AttributeError.** Every async-def call result conforms to `Cancellable[T]`, so `f().cancel()` (or `c.cancel()` on a bound handle) type-checks and compiles; CPython's coroutine objects have no `.cancel` (only Tasks do) and raise AttributeError at the same line. Pre-existing conflation (the TPy async model deliberately unifies coro/task cancellation via `Cancellable`), but bound-coroutine handles make it reachable through a named value -- and a `c.cancel()` read also clears the "never consumed" warning (see the bound-coroutines TODO exclusions entry), so the coroutine silently never runs with zero diagnostics where CPython fails loudly. Crash-direction divergence (TPy accepts a superset). Fix shape: either hide `cancel` from the user-facing surface of a *bare* coroutine value (accept it only where an owned handle is spawned/driven), or document the widened surface as a declared divergence and exclude `.cancel` reads from clearing the unconsumed warning. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the bound-coroutines feature. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An `Own[@dynamic P]` value passed to a *structural*-protocol param mis-templates -- the `unique_ptr<P>` is passed as the template arg instead of the pointee.** `poll_once(aw)` / any `Awaitable[T]`-typed structural consumer receiving an `Own[Cancellable[T]]` value emits `poll_once<T>(handle)` where the deduced param is `std::unique_ptr<Cancellable<T>>`, failing the C++20 concept check (no `__poll__` on unique_ptr). Pre-existing (repros on master via an explicit `Own[Cancellable[T]]` param forwarded to `poll_once`). For coroutine handles specifically this is now unreachable -- the bound-coroutines borrow rejection ("cannot borrow a coroutine handle into argument ...") fires first with a clean sema error -- but other `Own[@dynamic P]` sources (non-Cancellable protocols) still reach the broken emission. Fix shape: the structural-protocol arg path should deref an owned-erased source (`*handle`) like the @dynamic borrow path does, or reject with the same clean diagnostic. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the bound-coroutines feature. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The str-family respell in `gen_c_params` is dead code that reactivates silently if the C-ABI gate ever widens.** `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py` `gen_c_params` still maps `is_any_str_type(ptype)` to `const char*`, which is the exact machinery behind the (now-closed) HIGH silent wrong-code bug: the signature respelled to `const char*` while the body rendered against `std::string_view`, so `s == "hello"` compared pointers. It is unreachable today only because sema rejects str-family types at a C-linkage signature -- and the THIR fence (`sig.linkage_c_abi`) that used to be the second line of defence was deleted as part of that same change. So the arm is untested, unreferenced, and one gate widening away from being live again with no backstop. Fix shape: delete the arm (the gate makes it unreachable, and if str ever crosses a C boundary again it will be through the marshaling-wrapper design, which owns its own conversion), or keep it and add a unit asserting the sema gate makes it unreachable. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT) A `Ptr[T]`-returning `unsafe_` primitive borrows from a TEMPORARY argument with no diagnostic, so the pointer dangles before its first use.** `Ptr[T]` carries no lifetime facts and the borrow checker has no visibility into an `unsafe_` call's return, so whenever the argument is a temporary rather than a caller-owned lvalue the returned pointer is dead on arrival. Three confirmed faces, all silent, all producing garbage at runtime: `p = unsafe_ptr(s + "x")` (the concat's `std::string` dies at the end of the statement -- PRE-EXISTING on master, independent of any `unsafe_cstr` work); `p = unsafe_cstr("literal")` and `p = unsafe_cstr(v)` for a `str`/`StrView`-typed `v` (the `str -> String` conversion materializes a temporary bound to the helper's `const std::string&`). Consuming the pointer inside the SAME full-expression is safe and is the intended spelling (`c_fn(unsafe_cstr(name))`), so the hazard is specifically binding the result to a name, returning it, or storing it in a field. A held pointer is also invalidated if the owning `String` is later mutated or reallocated -- the ordinary `std::string::c_str()` caveat. Not specific to any one primitive: it is the untracked-`Ptr`-borrow property of the family, and `unsafe_` is the documented escape-hatch namespace, so the question is diagnosis rather than prohibition. **Fix shape:** region/lifetime tracking that reaches `Ptr[T]` returns is the real answer and is IR-gated (same territory as the async borrow-escape work); the available-now narrower option is a diagnostic when a borrow-returning `unsafe_` call's argument is a temporary AND the result is bound to a name rather than consumed in place. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/cabi-str/dang1.py`, `dang4.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + cpython-parity + safety-model) of the C-ABI type gate. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A module whose name is a C++ keyword emits an unusable namespace.** `inline.py` emits `namespace tpyapp::inline { ... }` and every reference to it (`::tpyapp::inline::__tpy_init()`), which g++ rejects -- the module name is pasted into the namespace without checking it against the C++ keyword set. Any Python-legal module name that is also a C++ keyword hits this (`inline`, `template`, `typename`, `new`, `delete`, `union`, `register`, ...). Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error at the first build), not silent, and the diagnostic points at generated code rather than at the filename, so the cause is not obvious from the message. Fix shape: `module_to_cpp_namespace` should mangle a reserved identifier the way `escape_cpp_name` already does for user identifiers -- the escaping helper exists, it is simply not applied to the module-name path. Surfaced while probing `unsafe_cstr` lifetimes during the C-ABI type gate review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
