- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] A `@cpp_template` that splices `{N}` as a receiver emits ill-formed C++ for a literal argument, and borrows from a dying temporary for a converted one.** `@cpp_template` substitutes the argument's *rendered text*, so `{0}.data()` / `{0}.c_str()` only work when the argument happens to render as an lvalue of the expected C++ type. `unsafe_ptr("literal")` emits `"literal".data()` -- `const char[8]` has no `.data()`, g++ rejects it; the same shape on any of the four `unsafe_ptr` overloads (`str`/`Array`/`list`/`bytes`) behaves the same way. The converted-argument face is worse than a build error: when sema inserts a coercion the template lands on the temporary (`std::string(s).data()`), so the returned pointer borrows a buffer that dies with the full-expression, silently. Toolchain-caught for literals, SILENT for coercions. Fix shape: a template whose placeholder is spliced in receiver position must either materialize the argument into a named temp (the `create-lend-drop` arm in `sema/calls.py` already does this for `Own[...]` rvalues lent to borrow params) or reject a non-lvalue argument; the alternative, used for `tpy.unsafe.unsafe_cstr`, is to declare the stub `@native` against a real C++ helper so the parameter applies the standard conversion instead of a text splice. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + safety-model) of the C-ABI type gate, where `unsafe_cstr` was converted away from `@cpp_template` for exactly this reason. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Slicing a readonly(-deduced) `list` param types the result `Span[T]` (mutable) -> ill-formed C++ (`span<const T>` does not convert to `span<T>`), no TPy diagnostic.** `def mid(items: list[int32], sl: basic_slice) -> int32: s = items[sl]; return s[0]` -- a read-only body const-deduces `items` (`const std::vector<int32_t>&`), so `::tpy::list_slice(items, sl)` returns `std::span<const int32_t>`, but sema types `items[sl]` as `Span[int32]` (an explicit `s: Span[int32]` annotation is accepted too), so the local declares `std::span<int32_t>` and g++ rejects the conversion. Same root family as the readonly-deduced `Own[Span[T] | list[T]]` return entry below (deduced receiver const-ness not propagated into the sliced Span's element); this is the plain-local face. Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error), not silent. Workaround: force the param mutable (e.g. the append/pop pair in tests/cases/operators/slice_var_index), or index elements directly. Surfaced drafting the THIR slice-ctor-call-arg corpus case. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A `String`-annotated binding from a view-form `str` source emits ill-formed C++ (`std::string m = s;` copy-init from a `std::string_view`).** `def f(s: str) -> None: m: String = s` -- sema inserts the `str_to_string` coercion (INIT context), whose codegen lambda is identity everywhere outside ARG, so codegen emits `std::string m = s;`; `std::string`'s `string_view` constructor is explicit, so the copy-initialization is ill-formed and g++ rejects it. The same identity arm covers ASSIGN and RETURN, so any non-ARG `str_to_string` over a VIEW source (a `str` param, a `StrView`-resolved local) miscompiles; an OWNED source (`String` value, owned str local) is fine (plain copy ctor). Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error), not silent. Workaround: keep the binding as `str`, or go through an explicitly-materializing source (a slice -- `strview_to_string` always wraps). Fix shape: the non-ARG identity must materialize for view-form sources; the coercion lambda cannot see the source's C++ form, so the fix belongs at the `_view_source_to_owned` chokepoint (the same one a plain `t: str = <view>` decl-init uses), not in the lambda. NB the THIR incr-42 coercion cell mirrors this emit byte-identically (`test_string_init_identity_mirrors_ast_miscompile` pins it); when the AST arm is fixed, the byte-diff + pin flag the THIR lockstep update. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_string_init.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the THIR incr 42-45 branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) Reusing a `with` as-target name whose binding is a VALUE (or value-repr Optional) slot is a hard compile error -- `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.with)`.** Two faces, both refused: (1) two `with` blocks reusing a value-typed target (`with V() as x: ...` twice, `__enter__ -> int32`); (2) a value-repr Optional slot (`x: int32 | None = None`, then `with V() as x:` in a branch). A SINGLE `with V() as x:` over the same value `__enter__` compiles, so the REUSE is the trigger. `_with_target_arm` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` classifies an already-declared target and returns None for every reuse that is not a same-record pointer-local (`ASSIGN_PTR`) or a hoist-predeclared optional-record slot (`ASSIGN_OPT`); the `if arm_et is None` guard at its caller raises. The RECORD reuse family still routes (`T* g = &(enter())` then `g = &(enter())`). This supersedes the older symptom -- the ill-formed `x = &(__ctx_N.__enter__());` (value slot assigned a pointer, address-of an rvalue) -- which no longer has an emitter: the mis-render is gone and the shape is refused instead. Exotic (one as-name reused across two `with` blocks); workaround: use distinct as-names per `with`. Fix shape: add a VALUE already-declared arm (`x = enter();` for a plain value slot, the same assign for a value-repr Optional slot), or reject the value-target reuse in sema with a clear message. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Mutating a `String` param (e.g. `name += "!"` in an `__init__` body) emits the mutation against the untouched `const std::string&` param -- ill-formed C++.** Sema accepts the aug-assign and records the param in `mutated_params`, but the emitted signature stays `const std::string&` and the body writes through it (`name += "!";` / `name = ...;` on the const ref), so g++ rejects every such body. Same missing owned-copy/mutable-binding family as the str/bytes aug-assign prologue entry below, on the `String` (owned, const-ref-param) face. Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error), not silent. Workaround: copy to a local first (`s = name + "!"`). Fix shape: a mutated `String` param must either lower `std::string&` (and callers adapt per `ctor_mutated`) or take the reassigned-param copy prologue; pick whichever matches the existing `param_needs_copy_for_reassign` model. NB the THIR ctor-arg check rejects mutated-String ctor slots (`_record_ctor_arg_supported`), so no THIR mirror exists to update. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/thir_with_tail/ctor_str5.py`. Surfaced probing the THIR str-arg ctor-slot cell. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A ctor param needing the reassigned-copy prologue emits `T name = __param_name;` against a ctor signature that never applies the `__param_` rename -- ill-formed C++ (undeclared identifier + param shadowing).** `def __init__(self, s: str, v: int32): self.tag = s; if v > 0: s = "pos"` (any owned str/bytes/String/BigInt param reassigned in a ctor body): gen_body emits the owned-copy prologue local `std::string s = std::string(__param_s);`, but the CTOR signature path (records.py `gen_params`) passes no `reassigned_params` -- unlike gen_function -- so the param keeps its source name and `__param_s` is undeclared; g++ rejects. Toolchain-caught, not silent. Workaround: bind to a differently-named local instead of reassigning the param. Fix shape: thread `reassigned_params` into the ctor signature emit exactly like gen_function's (same missing owned-copy/mutable-binding family as the mutated-String entry above). NB the THIR ctor gate rejects the shape (`ctor.param_reassign_copy`), so no THIR mirror exists to update. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/ctor_wave/params/probe_reassign.py`, `/tmp/agents/ctor_wave/body/probe_fw6.py`. Found independently by three THIR ctor-frontier cells. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A ctor param mutated only through a FREE-function call renders the call-site rvalue arg inline against the `A&` slot -- ill-formed C++ (prvalue bound to a non-const lvalue ref).** `class Sink: def __init__(self, a: A): mut(a); self.c = a.x` with `def mut(a: A): a.x += 1`, called `Sink(A(1))`: Phase-2 mutation propagation updates the REAL `__init__` FunctionInfo (the emitted signature is `Sink(A& a)`), but the call site's `ctor_mut` reads the SYNTHETIC constructor fi -- built by `_set_record_constructor_info` in `tpyc/sema/calls.py`, which COPIES `resolved_ctor.mutated_params` at resolution time and is never refreshed by the fixpoint -- so the mutated-slot rvalue-temp row never fires and `Sink s = Sink(A(1));` is emitted inline instead of hoisting `A __tmp = A(1);`. Direct method mutation in the ctor body (`a.bump()`) lands on the synthetic fi and works. Toolchain-caught (g++: "cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type 'A&' to an rvalue"), not silent. Workaround: bind the arg to a local first (`a = A(1); Sink(a)`), or mutate via a method call in `__init__`. Site: `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` -- the record-ctor arm of `_lower_expr` and `_lower_ctor_call_args` (which now serves the `raise X(args)` path too) both read `ctor_mut = fi.mutated_params` off that synthetic fi. Fix shape: refresh the synthetic ctor fi's `mutated_params` in the Phase-2 fixpoint, or have both reads go through `canonical_fi.mutated_params` (the synthetic fi already carries `canonical_fi=ctor.root`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Reassigning a pointer-repr tuple PARAM emits the assignment against the `const std::tuple<..., const T*>&` parameter -- ill-formed C++.** `def use(t: tuple[Rec, int32]) -> ...: t = (a, 5)` -- the signature renders the const borrow-tuple reference while the body emits the bare reseat (`t = ::tpy::tuple_to_storage<...>(...);`) against it; no viable `operator=`, g++ rejects. Toolchain-caught, not silent. Workaround: bind to a fresh local instead of reassigning the param. Fix shape: a reassigned borrow-tuple param needs the mutable-binding / copy-prologue family treatment (same missing-owned-copy class as the mutated-String and aug-assign param entries). NB THIR's borrow-tuple reseat dispatch EXCLUDES params (whole-body fallback, `_borrow_tuple_local_type` gate in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`), so no THIR mirror exists to update -- when the AST arm is fixed, widen that gate in lockstep. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/meta_w1/main.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + meta) of the wave-5 borrow-tuple cell. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A `::tpy::String` FIELD written from a str LOCAL emits invalid C++ (`::tpy::String` hides `std::string::operator=(string_view)`).** `s.name = v` with `name: String` and `v` a str local (a `std::string_view`) emits `s.name = v;`, and `::tpy::String` declares only its copy/move `operator=`, so the conversion that keeps plain `str` immune is hidden. Toolchain-caught (hard C++ error), not silent. Workaround: `s.name = String(v)`. Fix shape: route the field write through the family's view->owned bridge -- `_wrap_view_owned_sink` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`), the single chokepoint for the view->owned copy, which the owned-`bytes` local reassign goes through at its name-reassign arm in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`. The `bytes` face of this entry is closed by that arm; only the `String` field write is left. Probe `/tmp/agents/bug_any/p/c_precedent.py`, found 2026-09-13.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; the `int` face toolchain-caught) Aug-assign on a parameter whose only mutation is the aug-assign is refused for `str` / `bytes` and fails the C++ build for `int`.** `def f(a: str) -> str: a += "x"; return a` and `def f(a: bytes, b: bytes) -> bytes: a += b; return a` reject at `stmt.aug_assign`; `def f(n: int) -> int: while n > 0: n -= 1` emits `n = (n) - ...;` against the `const ::tpy::BigInt&` parameter and g++ rejects it. A parameter that is also plainly reassigned (`a = a + "x"`) gets the owned-copy prologue and compiles. Root: the reassigned-param prologue (`param_needs_copy_for_reassign` -> `std::string __param_a` rename + mutable local) keys on `scan.reassigned`, but the prescan records aug-assign targets in `scan.aug_assigned` only. Fix shape: include `aug_assigned` names in the `param_needs_copy_for_reassign` prologue / signature checks (functions.py, statements.py, param_const.py), then admit the aug-assign. Workaround: `a = a + "x"`, or copy to a local first. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `float(huge_int)` and BigInt-to-double conversions silently produce `inf` where CPython raises `OverflowError`.** `BigInt::to_double()` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/bigint.hpp`) returns `HUGE_VAL` via `strtod` for values beyond double range (e.g. `float(10**400)`), and every implicit int-to-float widening site (mixed `int`-with-`float` arithmetic, float ctor) inherits that, whereas CPython raises `OverflowError: int too large to convert to float`. Silent value divergence, but only for astronomically large ints. (int/int true division no longer goes through this path -- its dedicated `truediv` overloads raise `OverflowError` correctly.) Fix shape: `to_double()` raises `OverflowError` when the magnitude exceeds double range; audit callers that intentionally want saturation, if any. Surfaced while fixing the int/int correctly-rounded-division bug. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An oversized `-> int` (BigInt) `__len__` panics UNCATCHABLY where CPython raises a catchable `OverflowError`.** `class Huge: def __len__(self) -> int: return 10 ** 30` then `len(Huge())` (or truthiness `if Huge():`) -- the BigInt `__len__` template in `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dunder.hpp` narrows via `x.__len__().to_fixed_check<int32_t>()`, and `to_fixed_check` routes out-of-int32 magnitudes through `raise_fixedint_overflow` -> `tpy_panic` (`core.hpp:356`), an UNCATCHABLE panic ("int32 overflow: value out of range"), whereas CPython raises a catchable `OverflowError: cannot fit 'int' into an index-sized integer`. So `try: len(Huge()) except OverflowError:` never catches in TPy. Only for astronomically large `__len__` results (>= 2^31). The negative-`__len__` -> `ValueError` guard directly above the narrow is fine (fits int32, catchable); only the oversized branch diverges. Sibling of the `float(huge_int)` -> `inf` OverflowError entry above (same "should be catchable OverflowError, isn't" family). Fix shape: the `len()`/`__len__` oversized branch should raise a catchable `::tpy::raise<OverflowError>(...)` (CPython's index-size message) instead of `to_fixed_check`'s panic -- either a dedicated checked narrow in the `__len__` template or a `to_index_checked`-style extractor. Surfaced by `/tpy-next` while fixing the negative-`__len__` `ValueError` gap. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An operator inside a generic function does not dispatch through the type param's protocol bound.** `def combine[T: Addable](a: T, b: T) -> T: return a + b` errors `Invalid operand types for '+': Ref[T] and Ref[T]` even though the `Addable` bound requires `__add__`. The protocol-operand arm in `sema/expressions.py` (`is_protocol_type` -> `lookup_protocol_method_return`) handles protocol-TYPED operands but not `Ref[TypeParamRef]` operands whose bound is a protocol. Rejects-valid. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/proto_dunder/repro.py`. Surfaced while fixing the self-referential-protocol recursion crash. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Operator dunders on a `@dynamic` protocol value do not dispatch.** `c // 2` where `c: Counter` (`@dynamic` protocol requiring `__floordiv__(self, other: int) -> int`) errors `Invalid operand types for '//': Counter and IntLiteral(2)`; same for other operators. The @dynamic Adapter forwards named methods but the binop resolution path never consults the protocol's dunders for a @dynamic-typed operand (the structural monomorphized path does). Rejects-valid; the `@dynamic`-protocol-with-operator-dunder surface is effectively unimplemented -- routing it likely needs `/tpy-add-feature` rather than a spot fix. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/proto_dunder/repro5.py`. Needs triage.
- **[LOW small] A protocol method returning `Own[Self]` does not match a conformer returning plain `Self`-equivalent.** Protocol `__add__(self, other: Self) -> Own[Self]` vs `Meters.__add__(other: Meters) -> Meters` (a `ValueType`) -> "does not conform": `_protocol_type_matches` unwraps `Own` on the ACTUAL side only, so expected `Own[Meters]` never matches actual `Meters`, though for a value type the two describe the same by-value return. Rejects-valid. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/proto_dunder/repro4.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A union-typed operand on a binary operator is accepted by sema but cannot be built in C++.** `a + u` where `u: A | B` and `A` defines a monomorphic `__add__(self, other: A) -> ...` compiles in sema (the union operand is not checked against the operator's param type) but fails the C++ build: `operator+(A, variant<A, B>)` matches no overload. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/dt_probe/mono_union.py` (also reachable via an `@overload` operator's union impl-signature, though that path's spurious operator was removed in the datetime v0 fix). Consequence: a genuine union operand on any operator is a sema-accepts / codegen-fails hole. Pre-existing, independent of `@overload`. The COMPARISON form reproduces the same class on value unions: `a == k` where `a: int32 | float64` and `k: int32` emits the bare `(a == k)` -> `variant<int32_t, double> == int32_t` matches no `operator==` (same-type union compares work -- `std::variant` compares to itself). Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_union_value3.py` (the `c()` shape). Fix shape: either sema rejects a union operand on an operator (require the user to narrow first -- consistent with TPy's narrow-before-use rule), or codegen `std::visit`-dispatches the operand to the matching concrete operator. The narrow-first rejection is the cleaner static-language fit. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. Surfaced during datetime v0 (`docs/DATETIME_DESIGN.md`); the comparison form by the THIR F4 U1 probes. datetime v4 raised this class's exposure: `dt.tzinfo == tz` is now a natural user spelling (`.tzinfo` returns `timezone | ZoneInfo | None`) and hits the `==` form; TPy code narrows via isinstance first (see timezone.fromutc).
- **[MED small] A storage-form union value (a `variant<A, B>` field) at a borrow position is not bridged with `to_ptr_variant` -- one live miscompile, three hard rejects, one now caught by sema.** One root cause: the union storage->borrow conversion fires at the local-decl site but is missing at the other borrow sinks. **LIVE (4) const-blind member lift**: the pointer-variant arg lift ignores the SOURCE's const verdict -- a `const A&` param, a const loop var, or a readonly method's `self` passed as a member arg into a mutable `A | B` slot emits `std::variant<A*, B*>{&(a)}` where `&(a)` is `const A*` (g++: `no matching function for call to 'std::variant<A*, B*>::variant'`). The variant spelling is fixed at lowering from the SLOT's deep-const verdict alone (`_arg_ptr_union_slot` and the `THIRUnionArgLift` construction, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:14764-14840`) and rendered source-blind by `_emit_union_arg_lift` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:838`); the narrowed-subject face (a bare `const`-extracted alias into a mutable variant slot) hits the same wall. **REJECT (1) return**: `def r(h: H) -> A | B: return h.u` fails codegen with `(stmt.return)`. **REJECT (2) call arg**: `take(h.u)` fails with `(stmt.expr_stmt:call.arg_shape.union)`. **REJECT (5) `@error_return` unwrap into a ptr-variant local**: `x: A | B = A(1)` then `x = f(...)` where `f` is `@error_return` returning `Own[A | B]` fails with `(stmt.var_decl:error_return.bind_target)` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:3352`); this is also the only shape that reaches that sink's pointer-local guard, so it blocks a regression test for the guard until fixed. **RESOLVED (3) const mismatch**: a const-lifted local off a readonly receiver passed to a mutable-pointee slot is now a sema error (`Cannot pass readonly[A | B] as mutable A | B in argument 'u'`) -- the loud rejection this entry asked for, no codegen change needed. All faces are loud, none silent. Fix shape: route the return, call-arg and `@error_return`-bind borrow sinks through the same union conversion the local decl uses, and make the arg lift consult the SOURCE's const verdict (or have sema infer the param const) for face (4). Reproducers `/tmp/agents/bugs2/probes/02_508a_union_return.py` through `02_508e_union_er_bind.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `self.u = v` in a ctor with `v: Own[A | B]` warns "copies A | B into field; use copy()" although the emitted member-init-list MOVES (`u(std::move(v))`) -- a false-positive copy warning.** [`own-union-field-store-copy-warning`] The Own-param move is the intended zero-copy path, but the field-assign copy warning does not recognize the ctor MIL move for union-typed fields (the plain-record Own-param MIL assign does not warn). Several committed union cases carry the spurious line in their `diag.txt`. No behavioral impact; diagnostics quality only. Fix shape: suppress the copy warning when the source is an `Own[...]` param at its last use feeding the MIL move (mirror the record-field arm's verdict). The Optional-param twin is `BUGS.md#own-optional-param-field-store-copies`. Surfaced by the THIR incr-57 corpus case (`callarg_own_ctor`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] char-slot literal arguments are sema-accepted for free functions but sema-rejected for methods and constructors.** `take('a')` into `def take(c: char)` compiles (the target-typed char-literal render), but the same literal into a method (`p.set('q')`) or constructor (`P('a')`) char param is a sema type error -- the literal-into-char coercion only fires on the free-function call path. Inconsistent sema surface; reject-valid (loud), no miscompile. Workaround: bind the literal to a `char` local first. Surfaced by the THIR incr-47 char-field probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] An assign-narrowed union local read at a member-typed sink renders the bare variant name (no `std::get`) -> hard C++ error, in BOTH variant forms.** [`assign-narrowed-union-read`] `def m(k: int32): x: int32 | float64 = k; v = x` -- the member-source decl narrows `x` to `int32`, so `v` infers `int32`, but codegen renders the read as the bare name: `int32_t v = x;` where `x` is `std::variant<int32_t, double>` -- no conversion exists. The extraction the narrowed read needs (`std::get<int32_t>(x)`) is never emitted at the decl-init sink (the isinstance-narrowing extraction sites in `expressions.py`/`match.py` don't cover assignment-narrowed bare-name reads). Sibling of the narrowed-union match-capture entry (BUGS.md#match-capture-union-subject) -- same root, different sink; toolchain-caught, not silent. **The POINTER-variant flavor reaches this same decl sink**, so the split between the two entries is which SINK, not which variant form: `tmp: A | B = B(3)` then `other = tmp` narrows `tmp` to `B` off its initializer and emits `B other = std::move(tmp);` against a `std::variant<A*, B*>` -- g++ `conversion from 'std::variant<A*, B*>' to non-scalar type 'B' requested`. Reading the narrowed local DIRECTLY is fine (`(*std::get<B*>(tmp)).y`) and the isinstance route is fine (it has an extraction alias `__v`), so the local-to-local bind is the whole gap. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/probe_union_narrowlocal.py` (value variant) and `/tmp/agents/unionalias/main.py` (pointer variant). Workaround: re-annotate the local (`v: int32 | float64 = x`) or avoid the member-typed re-read. Fix shape: an assign-narrowed union name read at a member-typed sink must extract (`std::get<M>`) like the isinstance-narrowed sites do -- or sema should not narrow across a variant storage boundary it cannot render. NB the THIR F4 U1 gate rejects any narrowing-divergent union read (`_union_binding_divergent`), so THIR neither routes nor mirrors the shape -- verified for both faces (the pointer-variant repro falls back with `stmt.var_decl:name.union_binding_divergent`). Surfaced by the THIR F4 U1 probes. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `Send[Own[T]] | None` is not recognized as an owned (movable) param.** The `Send`/`Sync` marker distributes *inside* the Optional at construction (`Optional[Send[Own[T]]]`, not `Send[Optional[Own[T]]]`), so the owned-param peel `unwrap_optional_own(unwrap_readonly(unwrap_send_sync(ptype)))` sees `Send[Own[T]]` where it expects a bare `OwnType` and returns None -> the param is bound as a borrow instead of moved (a silent copy for a copyable T; a hard C++ error for `@nocopy`). Pre-existing (identical before the marker-peel fix; that fix covers bare `Send[Own[T]]` but not the Optional-wrapped shape). `tpy.thread.spawn`'s param is never Optional, so V1 is unaffected. Fix shape: either peel the marker per-Optional-member, or float the marker outside the Optional so the existing peel reaches it. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `Send[Own[ConcreteClass]]` param annotation fails at parse time with "not Send".** `def f(x: Send[Own[Box]])` where `Box` is a user class (even a Send-able one) raises `Parse error: 'Send[Own[Box]]': 'Own[Box]' is not Send`. Only the type-param form `Send[Own[T]]` (deferred to Phase-2) and the `@dynamic`-protocol form `Send[Own[Pet]]` are accepted; a concrete class is Send-checked too early (at parse, before the class's Send-ness is known). Workaround: use a bare `Own[Box]` param, or a generic `Send[Own[T]]`. Rejection-of-valid-code. Surfaced building the `tpy.thread.spawn` regression tests. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A tuple-typed parameter reassignment is not rejected by sema (unlike a record-typed param), so it emits an assignment against a `const std::tuple<...>&` param -> hard C++ error.** `def f(t: tuple[int32, int32], t2: tuple[int32, int32]): t = t2` emits `t = t2;` where `t` is a `const std::tuple<...>&` parameter, which g++ rejects (assignment to a read-only reference). A record-typed param reassignment is correctly rejected at sema ("Cannot reassign parameter 'x' of type 'Inner'"), but the tuple-typed param (and, presumably, other by-const-ref value aggregates) misses that diagnostic. Toolchain-caught (won't compile), not silent. Pre-existing on `master` -- reproduces without `--thir-codegen`; a pure AST/sema gap, not a THIR issue (the THIR value-scalar tuple subscript-read cell emits byte-identical broken text to the AST path). Workaround: assign to a fresh local instead of the param. Fix shape: extend the "cannot reassign parameter" sema check to tuple-typed (and other by-const-ref) value params, not just record params. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the THIR tuple subscript-read cell. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A bare `str` (view) argument doesn't auto-coerce into a `bool | str` (or other view-member union) parameter -- needs an explicit `String(...)`.** Calling `f(s)` where `f(verify: bool | str)` and `s` is a `str`/`StrView` fails the C++ build: `invalid initialization of reference of type 'const std::variant<bool, std::string>&' from expression of type 'const std::string_view'`. The view isn't wrapped to the union's owned `std::string` member at the call site. Workaround: `f(String(s))` (owned) compiles. Works once the value is already a `bool | str`-typed local (e.g. a reassignable `verify` local in curl.py), so the gap is specifically a fresh view -> union-param coercion. Same view->owned family as other union-member coercion gaps. Reproducer: `_ssl_context_for(CA_PATH)` in `tplib/requests_verify_context` (worked around with `String(CA_PATH)`). Toolchain-caught, not silent. Surfaced building the Increment 5 verify-context test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The clang-repl JIT backend (`--cxx clang-repl`, opt-in) cannot use modules needing runtime impls or managed third-party libs.** The default CompileBackend now compiles and links the session's build deps (runtime impl sources like os_impl.cpp, bundled third-party sources like PCRE2/Hinnant date, raw link flags) per eval, but the JIT backend has no link step to feed them into -- `import os` / `import re` / `from datetime import datetime` fail with unresolved symbols at JIT time. It accepts and ignores the `ReplBuildDeps` param (documented at the `execute` override). Fix shape: compile the support set to a shared object and load it into the interpreter (clang-repl `%lib`), or emit a clean "unsupported in the JIT backend, use the default backend" diagnostic when deps are non-empty. Split from the fixed CompileBackend link gap by `/tpy-fix-bug` (fix-repl-managed-libs). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED] `--mbedtls=bundled` via the CMake-emit path (`tpyc -o`) fails to link `mbedtls_shim.c` and `cacert_data.c`.** The vendored `runtime/cpp/third_party/mbedtls/CMakeLists.txt` shim (generated by `scripts/vendor_mbedtls.py`) globs only `library/*.c`, so the TPy-owned glue `runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/mbedtls_shim.c` and the CA-bundle blob `runtime/cpp/third_party/cacert/cacert_data.c` are never compiled in CMake mode -> undefined references to `tpy_tls_*` / `tpy_cacert_pem` at link. The direct-compile path (default; what `tpy file.py`, `tpyc -b`, and the test suite use) compiles both via `tpyc/build/mbedtls.py::_source_files` and works. Pre-existing for `mbedtls_shim.c` (since ssl Increment 2); the CA-bundle change adds a second file into the same untested CMake blind spot. Untested (no case exercises `tpyc -o` CMake emit with a managed lib). `--date=bundled` (datetime v2) has the same gap for `runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/date_shim.cpp` -> undefined reference to `tpy::stdlib::datetime::local_utc_offset_seconds` (the vendored `tz.cpp` itself DOES build in CMake mode via the upstream `CMakeLists.txt` + `BUILD_TZ_LIB=ON` -- only the TPy-owned shim is missed). Fix shape: the CMake-emit wiring must compile the shim + bundled extra sources too -- ideally reuse the same source list `_source_files` returns so the two build paths can't drift. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the bundled CA store; date face added by the datetime v2 review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] The else/elif arm of an `isinstance(x, str)` check on a `bool | str` union is not narrowed to `bool` -- `elif not x:` passes sema but emits `!(variant)` (hard C++ error).** `def f(verify: bool | str): if isinstance(verify, str): ... elif not verify: ...` -- sema accepts the elif arm's truthiness read, but codegen emits `(!(verify))` against `const std::variant<bool, std::string>&` -> g++ "no match for operator!". The RETURN-shaped sibling narrows correctly: `if isinstance(verify, str): return ...` followed by `if not verify:` compiles (the after-return continuation is narrowed; `_ssl_context_for` in tplib/requests relies on it), so the gap is specifically the elif/else-branch narrowing of an isinstance on a 2-member union. Two acceptable fix shapes: narrow the else/elif arm to the non-matched member (bool), or emit union truthiness (CPython accepts `not <union>`) -- either unblocks the shape. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. Workaround: restructure to isinstance + early return (what `_pool_key` in tplib/requests does). Surfaced building the Session connection-pool key. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (parity) Duplicate `Content-Length` response headers make `http.client` fall back to connection-close framing instead of using the length.** Two `Content-Length: 5` headers -> `HTTPResponse.getheader("content-length")` joins them `"5, 5"` (the documented duplicate-join), which `_digits_to_int` can't parse (-1) -> body framing degrades to read-until-EOF. CPython's `email.message` keeps a usable value and frames by Content-Length, so on a keep-alive connection TPy would read past the body / block where CPython stops at N bytes. Malformed-server-only (a conformant server sends one Content-Length). Fix shape: in `_init_framing`, take the first value of a comma-joined Content-Length (or reject per RFC 7230 6.3.2), rather than feeding the joined string to `_digits_to_int`. Surfaced by /tpy-review of http.client. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A view arg passed to an owned exception-constructor param isn't view->owned-wrapped, unlike an owned arg.** `raise UnknownProtocol(ver)` where `ver` is a `str` VIEW (a `list[str]` element / `split()` result) fails the C++ build ("no known conversion from `string_view` to `const std::string&`"); the same raise with an OWNED `str` (a `decode()` result) compiles, because owned binds the `const std::string&` ctor param directly. Workaround: `raise Ctor(String(ver))` (used in `http.client._read_status`). Same root family as the `String.encode()` gap (below) and the tuple-unpacked-view-local-seeding-owned-accumulator gap -- each a different codegen sink (concat-result method, owned-local init, exception-ctor arg) where the view->owned init wrap codegen applies to owned-param slots but not that position. Fix shape: apply the view->owned wrap at exception-constructor arg positions -- ideally fix the family at one chokepoint, not as separate narrow patches (per CLAUDE.md bug-fix discipline). Surfaced building `http.client`'s `UnknownProtocol` raise. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `.encode()` is missing on `String` (the owned string-concatenation result), though present on `str`/`StrView`.** `("a" + b).encode()` fails with "Cannot call method 'encode' on type String", but `s: str = "a" + b; s.encode()` (binding the concat to a `str`-typed local first) works, as does encoding a `list[str]` element -- so str->bytes from a freshly concatenated value needs an extra binding hop. Loud reject-valid, no miscompile; trivial workaround. Affects building byte payloads by concatenation (worked around in `http.client._build_request`, which accumulates `ln.encode()` over `list[str]` elements). Fix shape: expose `encode()` on `String`'s method surface, mirroring `str`/`StrView`. Surfaced building `http.client`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `print(v)` / `str(v)` of a recursive-union (JSON-like) value holding a top-level string prints the repr form (quoted) instead of the str form.** `type V = int | str | list[V]; s: V = "hi"; print(s)` outputs `'hi'`, CPython outputs `hi`. The recursive-union wrapper struct's `__str__`/`operator<<` delegates each member through the repr path, so a top-level `str` member is quoted as if nested in a container. Uniform across all rendering paths (`operator<<`, f-string, and `print`/`str` via `::tpy::__str__`) -- pre-existing, not introduced by the union-print fix. Plain (non-recursive) unions are unaffected: `x: int | str = "hi"; print(x)` correctly outputs `hi`. Silent wrong output (only for the top-level-string member; nested strings are correctly repr'd in both). Fix shape: the recursive-union wrapper's `__str__` should dispatch members through the str path (member `__str__`), not repr -- only the top-level rendering differs (container-nested members stay repr per Python). Surfaced fixing the bare-union print/str gap. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (parity) ASCII-only case/`is*` string methods give wrong results for Latin-1 (U+0080..U+00FF).** `upper`/`lower`/`capitalize`/`title`/`swapcase` and `isalpha`/`isupper`/`islower`/... only fold/classify ASCII: e.g. U+00E9 (small e-acute) is left unchanged by `.upper()` where CPython yields U+00C9, and `.isalpha()` on it is False vs CPython True -- silent wrong output for non-ASCII. Documented as ASCII-only in `docs/STRING_HANDLING.md`. Folded into the string-width/Unicode work: the fix is part of making `str` code-point-correct (`docs/STRING_WIDTH_DESIGN.md`), not worth a standalone patch ahead of that pass. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (string-width design).
- **[LOW small] A jagged list literal WRAPPED in a tuple/dict in a ternary / `and` / `or` branch is rejected ("Incompatible types in ternary expression"), unlike the same wrapped literal as a list element or dict value.** `(1, [2, 3]) if c else (4, [5, 6, 7])` rejects what CPython accepts. The BARE different-size case (`[1, 2] if c else [3, 4, 5]`, `xs or [4, 5]`) already works -- a top-level pending-list branch is forced to `vector` by the `needs_list_type` path (`collect_pending_source_types`), so both branches share one C++ type. The gap is only the WRAPPED case: `collect_pending_source_types` collects top-level pending lists, not ones nested in a tuple/dict, and the shared ternary/logical join (`_select_join`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) unifies a TOP-LEVEL pending pair through `_join_pending_containers` but compares a pending container nested in a tuple/dict with `==` (keeping size). Loud reject-valid, no miscompile. Fix shape: route the nested pending containers of the join through `unify_literal_types(left, right, on_pending_pair=self.compat._demote_pending_pair)` so the same demotion that converges list/dict siblings also converges ternary/logical branches; mind the existing `needs_list_type` forcing so they don't conflict. Surfaced finishing the jagged-nested-list generalization. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] A list of tuples of differing arity (`[(1, 2), (3, 4, 5)]`) is rejected as mixed types, though CPython accepts it.** The sibling tuple types `tuple[int32, int32]` and `tuple[int32, int32, int32]` don't unify (different arity), so the list literal has no common element type. Distinct from the jagged-list class (this is about tuple arity, not pending-list size) -- a heterogeneous tuple list would need a variant/union element type to represent. Loud reject-valid, no miscompile. Fix shape: a feature -- infer `list[tuple[...] | tuple[...]]` (a union element) for mixed-arity tuple peers, as the error message already hints. Surfaced surveying adjacent shapes for the jagged-nested-list generalization. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[MED small] An `isinstance`-narrowed union local read across a `yield` INSIDE a loop emits the `std::get` extraction twice in the same resume-case scope (`conflicting declaration 'auto& __t'`).** `def gen(t: A | B): if isinstance(t, A): for n in t.items: yield n` -- the narrowed `t` (a frame-resident `variant<A,B>`) is carried into the for-loop's resume state, where the narrowing alias `auto& __t = std::get<A>((*t))` is emitted both at the resume-case top (restoring the alias for resumed code) and inline before the yield, in the same `case S_JOIN_N: {...}` block -> g++ redeclaration. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/bottomup/dup_extract.py`. Exposed by (not caused by) the frame_slot-unwrap fix: before it, this shape failed earlier at `std::get`-against-`frame_slot`, so the double-emit was unreachable. Distinct from the simple narrow+yield+continue shape (no loop carrying the narrowed var across the suspension), which compiles -- so `os.walk` bottomup's union stack is unaffected. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. Fix shape: the resume-restoration of an isinstance-narrowed alias must not re-declare a name already extracted inline in the same scope (dedup the per-scope alias, or skip the inline extraction when the resume case already restored it). Surfaced building the `isinstance_union_frame` regression test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, located) A tuple unpack straight off `list.pop()` / `dict.pop()` whose tuple has reference-type elements rejects, and so does binding it first.** [`rvalue-ref-tuple-unpack-address-of-rvalue`] `stack = [(["x"], 1)]` then `a, b = stack.pop()` rejects at `stmt.tuple_unpack` (detail `tuple_unpack.target_form`); with an annotated stack (`stack: list[tuple[str, list[str], list[str], bool]] = []`, then `a, b, c, d = stack.pop()`) it rejects at `expr.method_call:method.ret_type`, and the old workaround `t = stack.pop()` rejects at `method.ret_type` too. The C++ build failure this entry used to describe (`to_pointer_form: cannot take the address of an rvalue`) is gone. Root cause: `list.pop` / `dict.pop` return `Own[tuple[...]]`; sema's unpack strips the outer `Own` (`_analyze_tuple_unpack`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~6252) and decides per-element ownership only from a per-element `Own` spelled in the tuple type (~6306), so the reference elements come out as borrows of a temporary; and the method-return gate has no row for a storage tuple with reference elements. Belongs to the slot-contract + element-form unit (docs/TUPLE_COMPLETION_PLAN.md U5). Sibling: `BUGS.md#pop-result-tuple-subscript-rejects` (`xs.pop()[1]`). Probes `/tmp/agents/u4d6/b/entry.py`, `/tmp/agents/u4d6/b/list_pop_free.py`, re-measured 2026-09-29. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (parity) `print(e)` / `str(e)` on a statically-typed USER exception subclass renders `<ClassName object at 0x...>` instead of the message.** [`print-exception-subclass-object-repr`] Both `except ssl.SSLError as e: print(e)` (a stdlib `OSError` subclass) and `class NotFound(KeyError): ...; except NotFound as e: print(e)` (a user subclass) print the object-default form: codegen emits a `print_object_default` `operator<<` for every user record, including exception subclasses, and the static type selects it over the inherited `tpy::BaseException` message-printing `operator<<` / `__str__`. Catching the SAME raise via a BUILTIN base (`except OSError as e` / `except KeyError as e`) prints the message correctly (the base's friend `operator<<` applies). CPython prints the message in both cases (and `KeyError.__str__` additionally repr-quotes the arg -- `'msg'` -- part of the same `__str__`-fidelity family). Silent wrong output, cosmetic; tests should match exception TYPE, not `str(e)` text. Fix shape: skip the `print_object_default` `operator<<` for records inheriting a Throwable/exception base and route `__str__`/f-string/print dispatch to the inherited rendering (virtual, or a forwarding `__str__` when the user class defines none). Pre-existing (visible in committed ssl.hpp snapshots); surfaced re-probing exception text during the CPython-exact OSError feature and probing `ZoneInfoNotFoundError(KeyError)` for datetime v4. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A SYNC tuple local reassigned from two literals that disagree on one element fails the C++ build with no TPy diagnostic.** `t = (a, 2)` then `t = (A(9), 3)` under an `if` -- the local takes ONE borrow-form C++ shape (`std::tuple<A*, int32_t>`), and the second literal builds the storage tuple, so g++ reports `no match for 'operator='`. Loud, rejects-valid. The element genuinely has no single form (one init needs the frame/scope to own a fresh object, the other to point at an existing one), so the fix is a diagnostic, not a form: the resumable-frame twin of this shape says so in Python terms (`'t' is bound both to a tuple holding a fresh object and to one borrowing an existing object ...`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`), and the sync local classifier (`storage_form_tuple_locals` / `borrow_form_tuple_locals`) needs the same verdict. Repro `/tmp/agents/tf2/lit/p_sync_lit.py`. The single-yield generator face went with the peephole: on the frame the same body takes the resumable twin's diagnostic (re-verified 2026-09-14). Filed 2026-09-10 while fixing the resumable-frame half.
- **[MED small] A tuple element with a reference member is read in BORROW form off an `__iter__`/`__next__` source that hands it back BY VALUE.** `def walk(xs: Iterable[tuple[int32, A]]) -> None: for t in xs: t[1].v += 1` -- the loop var binds `const std::tuple<int32_t, A>&` (a tuple is a value type, so `val_or_ref_t` gives the protocol's `__next__` a by-value result), but the element read spells `std::get<1>(t)->v` because the ELEMENT type is a reference. g++ reports `base operand of '->' has non-pointer type`. Loud, rejects-valid, and present in the SYNC emitter, not only in a resumable frame (where the same source fails at the advance instead: `no match for 'operator='` assigning the by-value tuple into a borrow-form field). The form is decided from the element TYPE while the binding is decided by the SOURCE -- the same split the frame's tuple-local family had; that half is fixed (the loop var points at the source element tuple; the literal owns per element), and this is the residue on the strategy whose source lends nothing to point at. Fix shape: decide the whole-tuple loop var's element form from the BINDING on the sync path too, so a by-value bind reads its elements by value. Repro `/tmp/agents/tf2/p_sync_iternext.py` (sync) and `p_loop_iternext.py` (frame). Narrowed 2026-09-10 from the non-unpack tuple-loop-var entry, whose `begin_end` and tuple-literal halves are fixed.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (latent, believed unreachable today) A resumable frame whose loop var aliases a TEMPORARY iterable holds a pointer into its own sibling field, which the frame's move does not retarget.** When the `iter_next` source is a temporary (`for p in make_bag(): ...`), codegen stores it by value in `__for_src_N` and the loop var's borrow points *into that same struct*: `frame_slot<for_elem_next_t<Bag>> p` (a `Point*`) aliasing `frame_slot<Bag> __for_src_0`. `frame_slot<T&>`'s move copies the raw pointer verbatim, so relocating the frame after the loop var has been bound leaves the new instance pointing at the old one's storage. Introduced by the loop-var storage-form fix: before it, `iter_next` never aliased, so this self-reference could not arise. Same family as the already-filed hoisted-rvalue-temp and generator-captures-self entries. Reachability NOT demonstrated: rebinding the generator to another local is a pointer copy (no relocation), passing it to a generic consumer binds by reference, and the one path that does emit `std::move(g)` -- an `Own[T]`-taking generic record ctor -- currently fails to compile for an unrelated reason (`T` infers to the bare protocol type, producing a field of concept type, which the equivalent explicit annotation is correctly rejected for). So this is filed to be found later rather than fixed now: fixing that generic-field gap could turn this live without anyone connecting the two. Fix shape: either retarget the alias on frame move (needs the frame to know which field it points into -- awkward), or keep a temporary source out of the aliasing path by treating a self-referential `__for_src_N` element as owned. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the loop-var storage-form branch.
- **[MED small] (harness, data loss) A TRANSIENT case failure during `--update-snapshots` DELETES that case's committed `expected/output.txt` and `expected/.fingerprints`.** Observed on a full `update_snapshots.py` run (which force-execs the whole corpus in parallel): 14 cases failed to build under the resulting load, and for two unrelated async cases -- `async/async_bind_cross_module`, `async/async_with_as_borrow` -- the run removed their `output.txt` and `.fingerprints`. Both cases were fine: re-run individually they build and print byte-identical output, so nothing about them had changed. The update path treats "produced no output this run" as "this case has no expected output" rather than as a failure to leave alone, so a build race silently discards the runtime-output oracle. Dangerous because the follow-up signal is weak: on a later plain run the case compares against a missing file, which reads as an ordinary snapshot mismatch, and for a `no_cpython` case nothing else would ever catch the loss. Only the `git diff` review before committing surfaced it here. Fix shape: never delete an existing `output.txt`/`.fingerprints` for a case whose build or run FAILED during the update -- only rewrite on a clean produce, and report the skipped cases. Surfaced regenerating snapshots for the loop-var storage-form unification. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (harness) Snapshot update mode reports a non-error case as passing when compilation fails outside its annotated lines.** [`snapshot-update-accepts-happy-compile-error`] `tests/test_case.py` only enforces `Non-error test failed to compile` outside `UPDATE_EXPECTED`. A new happy case with an unsupported unannotated expression therefore gets only `diag.txt`, no generated code or runtime output, and a green update result. A subsequent ordinary run catches it, but the update result alone falsely suggests execution succeeded. Observed while authoring the callable-container regression; the fixture was fixed and its executable output verified. The update-mode success contract is separate from callable inference and should be made consistent with ordinary mode.

- **[LOW small] (harness) A compile error in a STDLIB module surfaces as a pytest INTERNALERROR (SemanticError escaping the xdist plugin) instead of a clean per-case failure.** Seen when lib/tpy/zoneinfo.py briefly had a return-by-reference error during datetime v4.1: `update_snapshots` recorded diag.txt cleanly (per-case comp path), but the plain `pytest -k` run crashed with `INTERNALERROR> tpyc.diagnostics.SemanticError: Cannot return local or temporary...` -- the shared stdlib .o cache builder (conftest) compiles the stdlib outside the per-case diagnostics collection and lets the exception escape. Only reachable while the stdlib itself is broken (a dev-loop annoyance, not a user bug). Fix shape: wrap the conftest stdlib-cache build in a try that converts compiler diagnostics into a pytest-level error message naming the stdlib module. Surfaced by datetime v4.1 (zoneinfo available_timezones). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A container PARAM or an UNANNOTATED container local in an f-string is rejected ("cannot be used in f-string"), though an annotated container local renders fine.** `def f(xs: list[int32]) -> str: return f"{xs}"` errors `Type Ref[list[int32]] cannot be used in f-string (no __str__ or __repr__ method)`; same for `xs = [1, 2]; f"{xs}"` (errors on `PendingList[...]`). The ANNOTATED-local form `xs: list[int32] = [1, 2]; f"{xs}"` compiles and renders via `::tpy::list_to_str(xs)` -- so the renderability machinery exists and only the type-shape unwrap is missing: `_analyze_fstring` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) checks `container_to_str_template(resolved)` after peeling readonly/Own but not the `Ref[...]` param wrapper nor pending container types (`PendingList`/`PendingDict`/`PendingSet`). Loud reject-valid, no miscompile. Workaround: bind to an annotated local first (copies a param's container). Fix shape: extend the unwrap chain at that one check (Ref + resolve-pending), mirroring how print's arg path resolves the same shapes. Surfaced writing the THIR F6 S2 (f-string) eligibility tests. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium] (rejects valid code, loud) Exceptions have no `.args`, and an `Exception` subclass cannot pass more than one argument to `super().__init__`.** [`exception-args-missing`]
  `except ValueError as e: print(e.args)` errors *Record 'ValueError' has no field 'args'*; CPython prints `('x',)`. And `class error(Exception): def __init__(self, err: int32, msg: str): super().__init__(err, msg)` errors *'__init__' expects 0 to 1 arguments, got 2*, although that is how CPython's C modules build their errors (`termios.error`, `socket.herror`, ... carry `(errno, strerror)` in `args`). TPy's `BaseException` stores one `message` string, so `args` has no storage and `str(e)` of a multi-argument exception cannot be CPython's tuple rendering. Workaround in the stdlib: format the message as CPython's `str(e)` and pass that one string (`lib/tpy/termios.py`). Fix shape: give `BaseException` an `args` tuple of the constructor arguments, with `str(e)` derived from it the way CPython derives it (empty, the one argument, or the tuple's repr) -- the same question `BUGS.md#return-exception-str-reads-message-only` and TODO.md "Return exceptions: follow-ups" item 4 raise, so settle them together. Repros `/tmp/agents/termios_design/args.py`, `exc.py`. Found designing `termios` 2026-09-25. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (it adds a field every exception carries).
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code / ill-formed C++) A module constant from another module as a parameter default: the qualified spelling is rejected, and an imported `native_global` constant renders a name that does not exist.** [`imported-final-param-default`]
  With `import m` and `K: Final[int32] = 3` in `m`, `def f(x: int32 = m.K)` errors *default value 'm.K' is not a resolvable enum member* (`_validate_param_defaults` in `tpyc/sema/registration.py` treats every attribute-shaped default as an enum member), while `from m import K` + `x: int32 = K` compiles and runs. For a `native_global` constant even the bare imported spelling fails: `from termios import TCSANOW` + `def f(x: int32 = TCSANOW)` renders the default as `::tpystd::termios::TCSANOW` instead of the bound symbol `::tpy_const_termios_tcsanow`, and g++ rejects the header. CPython runs all three. `tty.setraw`/`setcbreak` spell CPython's `when=TCSAFLUSH` default as a `@dispatch` pair because of this. Fix shape: resolve a module-qualified default the way the bare name is resolved (a `Final` or an enum member), and render any `Final` default through the same path a read of the name takes, so a `native_global` binding is honored. The same default-resolution path is where `BUGS.md#param-default-resolves-in-caller-scope` binds a module constant in the CALLER's scope; fix the two together, since resolving the qualified spelling must also resolve it in the defining module. Repros `/tmp/agents/termios_impl/dflt/{a,b,c}.py`. Found implementing `tty` 2026-09-25. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent wrong fd) An fd outside C `int` range is narrowed by `static_cast<int>` instead of raising `OverflowError`.** [`fd-int-narrowing`] Every `os` fd function (`close`/`read`/`write`/`lseek`/`dup`/`dup2`/`fstat`/`isatty`/`ftruncate`/`fsync`/`get_terminal_size`/`get_blocking`/`set_blocking`, `runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/os_impl.cpp`) and `termios.tcgetattr`/`tcsetattr` (`runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/termios_impl.cpp`) take the fd as `int64` and cast it to `int`. CPython raises `OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C int` for any fd above `2**31 - 1`. In TPy an fd in `[2**31, 2**32)` wraps negative and surfaces as `OSError` / `termios.error` EBADF (wrong type), and an fd `>= 2**32` wraps to its low 32 bits, so `os.close(2**32 + 1)` silently closes fd 1 and `termios.tcgetattr(2**32)` reads stdin's attributes. Only reachable with a computed out-of-range fd (no syscall returns one). Fix shape: one shared fd-conversion helper in the runtime that range-checks against `INT_MAX` and raises `OverflowError` with CPython's message, used at every cast site. Found reviewing `termios` 2026-09-25.
- **[LOW small] (parity) `print(e)` on a caught exception binding prints the object repr, not `str(e)`.** `try: raise E("hi") except E as e: print(e)` prints `<E object at 0x...>` in TPy but `hi` in CPython (also `/tmp/agents/r4review/parity/p2.py`: `caught <E object ...>` against `caught boom`) (`print` calls `str`, which routes through the exception's `__str__`/`message`). `str(e)` directly DOES give `hi` -- so the message is stored and `__str__` works; it's `print()` of an exception-typed value that fails to dispatch through `__str__` (it falls to the default object repr). Pre-existing, orthogonal to interop (surfaced writing the user-exc `@export` boundary tests, which dodge it by routing parity through real CPython and not printing caught bindings on the TPy side). Affects any `print(caught_exc)`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (print/`__str__` dispatch for reference/exception-typed args).
- **[LOW small] A list literal mixing a str-family LOCAL (pending-str or `String`) with a str literal is rejected as "mixed types", with a degenerate message.** `v = "vv"; ys = [v, "c"]` errors `List literal has mixed types: element 2 is str, but earlier elements are str. Use a type annotation like list[str | str]` -- the two "different" types PRINT identically because a pending-str local and a str literal are the same family but fail element unification. Same for a `String` concat element: `[p + q, "z"]` -> `list[String | str]`. A str PARAM element (`[p, "c"]` with `p: str`) unifies fine, and the ANNOTATED form (`ys: list[str] = [v, "c"]`) compiles and correctly wraps the view element (`{std::string(v), "c"}`) -- so the machinery exists; only literal-element unification misses the str-family peers (PendingStr/StrView/String vs LiteralType[str]). **No str literal is needed to trigger it:** two PENDING-str peers fail the same way, because each carries its own `var_id` and so compares unequal to its sibling -- `x, y = src` then `xs = [x, y]` (both unpack targets, `tuple[str, str]` source) gives the same degenerate `str` vs `str` message. That sub-shape is the more common one, since CLAUDE.md style prefers the unannotated local; reproducer `/tmp/agents/pendview/r8_listinf.py`. Any fix must unify pending-str peers with EACH OTHER, not only against literals. Loud reject-valid, no miscompile; trivial workaround (annotate the local). Reproducers `/tmp/agents/probe_s5_bug2.py`, `/tmp/agents/probe_s5_bug3.py`. Fix shape: unify str-family peers to owned `str` in list/set/dict-literal element unification (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`, the "mixed types" check), mirroring how the annotated path resolves the element slot; the error message should also render distinguishable type names when it does fire. Surfaced probing the THIR F6 S5 (container-of-str) cell. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) A module-level `def print(...)` shadowing the builtin turns every `print(...)` call site into a hard compile error.** `def print(x: int32) -> None: return` then `print(5)` errors `in function 'main': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.call:call.builtin_special)`; drop the shadow and the same file compiles. `_is_builtin_print` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:13712`) correctly declines a shadowed `print` -- a same-module function/record of that name, or a local -- and the builtin print-stream arm (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:14482`) is the only thing that lowers a `print` call, so the shadowed call falls through to the special-builtin gate (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:3707`, `fi.qualified_name in _SPECIAL_BUILTIN_QNAMES or e.func_name == "print"`) and is refused. CPython calls the user's `print`. The old symptom was silent wrong output (the emitter intercepted `print` unconditionally, ignoring the shadow); the failure is now loud, so what remains is an unusable shape rather than a parity divergence. Exotic -- shadowing `print` is rare, and the internal-alpha audience makes it lower value than everyday rejections. Fix shape: route a shadowed `print` through ordinary function resolution instead of the builtin gate. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] The polymorphic-slicing guard over-rejects a polymorphic borrow passed to a `Callable[[Base], ...]` parameter, because `CallableType` param types skip the `RefType`-wrap ordinary params get.** `def f(cb: Callable[[OSError], None]): ...; cb(e)` where `e` is a caught (possibly-subclass) `OSError` is rejected by `_check_polymorphic_slicing` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py:250`) with "cannot store 'OSError' borrow as owned 'OSError' in argument ... (slicing)". But the guard is WRONG here: it returns early for `RefType`/`ReadonlyType` targets and only fires on a *bare* polymorphic `NominalType`; ordinary reference-type params are `make_ref`-wrapped before the guard sees them (and emit `const Base&`), but `CallableType.param_types` are stored raw, so the guard sees a bare `OSError` and treats the call as an owned store. Codegen would actually emit the callable param as `OSError&` (`_callable_param_cpp`: non-value -> `T&`), which binds a polymorphic borrow with NO slicing -- proven by the regular-param analogue `def handle(e: OSError)` which compiles, accepts a caught exception, and emits `const OSError&`. CONSEQUENCE: a plain `Callable[[OSError], None]` callback (the CPython-natural spelling) is rejected; users must annotate the callback param `readonly[OSError]` (which makes the target a `ReadonlyType` -> guard returns early -> emits `const OSError&`). This is what forces `os.walk`'s `onerror` param to be `Callable[[readonly[OSError]], None]` -- a workaround for THIS bug, not a real divergence (CPython needs no annotation). When the symptom is a named-function arg (not a lambda) the fall-through error is the unhelpful "'<name>' is not a variable" rather than anything about slicing/readonly. **Fix shape:** `RefType`-wrap (or otherwise treat as by-ref) `CallableType` param types before the slicing guard checks an argument against them -- a callable param slot is by-reference, never an owned store. Once fixed, drop the `readonly` from `os.walk`'s `onerror` (and any other `Callable[[exc], ...]` slot) so plain/lambda callbacks need no annotation. Surfaced + root-caused verifying the os.walk onerror `readonly` requirement. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, perf] A tuple-LITERAL needle of int literals against a tuple-keyed `dict`/`set` scans linearly instead of hashing.** [`tuple-literal-needle-linear-scan`] `(1, 2) in d` with `d: dict[tuple[int32, int32], str]` (or `tuple[int, int]` keys) emits `::tpy::seq_contains(d, std::tuple<int32_t, int32_t>{1, 2})`, O(n) over the keys, while `(a, a) in d` with `a: int32` on the same dict emits `d.contains(...)`. Sema's membership check resolves the container's `__contains__` overload against the needle's type, `tuple[IntLiteral, IntLiteral]` fails that match (the int-literal resolution there handles a scalar literal, not a tuple of them), and control falls through to the generic iterable path, leaving `resolved_contains` unset. Answers are correct; perf only. Fix shape: resolve int-literal members of a tuple needle against the parameter's element types before the overload match, as the scalar case does. Found 2026-09-25 probing readonly-haystack membership.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) `@overload __init__` on a user-defined class makes EVERY construction of that class a hard compile error -- `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.call)`.** `class Point: @overload def __init__(self, v: int32): ... @overload def __init__(self, v: str): ...` plus an implementation: both `Point(1)` and `Point("hi")` are refused at the call site, while dropping the two `@overload` stubs and keeping the same `v: int32 | str` implementation compiles -- so the overload GROUP is the trigger, not the union param. `_ctor_shape_ok` in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py` bails on `if len(overloads) != 1: return False`, and the ctor arm of `_lower_expr` in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` raises `ThirUnsupported(call_reject_reason("expr.call"))`. This supersedes the older accepted-then-silently-dropped symptom (only the first overload's ctor was emitted and a call matching the second failed against the first's signature): the parity hazard is gone and the gap is now plain missing support. Registration still accumulates the stubs; user-record ctor resolution and emission consult a single `__init__`. Methods and free functions DO support overloads; ctors are the gap. Builtin-stub ctor overloads (the exception family) work via per-overload `@native(function=True)`/`@cpp_template`, a different path. Fix shape: either wire user-record ctor resolution + codegen through the same overload-group machinery methods use (emit one C++ ctor per overload body), or reject `@overload __init__` on user records in sema with a diagnostic that names overloads. NB a full symmetric-ctor-overloads implementation was built and then reverted; it had no stdlib user once `timedelta` float ctor args were dropped. Consequence today: user OSError subclasses (`SocketError`, `gaierror`, the requests tree) keep a single `(errno, strerror)` `__init__`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (or `/tpy-add-feature`).
- **[LOW small] A container whose storage is not decided yet -- an unannotated container LOCAL, a list literal passed straight to the call, an empty list literal or `list()` that one overload fills, or an empty `{}` that two matching overloads leave unfilled -- matches no `@overload` / `@dispatch` candidate: "No matching overload for f(PendingList[...]#N)", with the internal type name in the message.** [`pending-container-overload-no-match`] The same for a list LITERAL passed straight to `@dispatch` overloads over `list[int32]` / `list[float]`: `f([1, 2])` fails with `No matching overload for f(PendingList[IntLiteral(1), 2]#0)` (probe `/tmp/agents/ihc-r3/pre/dispatch_list.py`, also `/tmp/agents/safety-ihc2/{ov1,ov3}.py`). - **[MED, deferred: MIR] A reference-type local hoisted across an if/else, match, or try/except branch that aliases a BRANCH-LOCAL source dangles -- scalar form is a SILENT use-after-free, tuple-unpack form is a loud C++ build error.** When a reference-type (record/list/...) local is first-assigned inside both arms of a branch and read after it, codegen hoists it to the outer scope as a `T*` and assigns `name = &(source_element)` per arm. If the source is itself branch-local (declared inside the arm), the pointee dies at arm exit and the hoisted pointer dangles. (try/except is also a site, since its branch-assigned vars hoist the same way: `try: o = make(); a = o except E: o2 = make(); a = o2; a.v = ...` hoists+dangles like the if/else face -- repro `/tmp/agents/tupuaf/ref_try_branch_local.py`.) Two faces:
  - **Scalar (silent UAF):** `if c: o1 = Box(1); a = o1 else: o2 = Box(2); a = o2` then `a.v = 99; print(a.v)` -> `Box* a; ... a = &(o1); ... a = &(o2);` with `o1`/`o2` branch-local. After the branch the pointee is freed; the post-branch read is a use-after-free with no diagnostic (reads freed stack -- "works" by luck). Repro: `/tmp/agents/tupuaf/ref_scalar_branch_local.py`.
  - **Tuple-unpack (loud error):** `if c: a, b = t else: a, b = t` (`t: tuple[Box, Box]`) then `a.v = ...` -- the two arms emit inconsistent forms: the is_new arm aliases (`a = &(unwrap_ref(tuple_elem_ref(std::get<0>(__tup))))`), the is_new=False arm takes the rvalue rebind-slot path (`a = &*(__slot = ...)`, `__slot` a `std::optional<Box>`) -> g++ "no known conversion from Box* to optional<Box>". The codegen asymmetry makes tuple fail to compile rather than silently dangle. Repros: `/tmp/agents/tupuaf/ref_branch_hoist.py` (durable source -- this one is actually safe to alias, see below), `/tmp/agents/tupuaf/ref_branch_local.py` (branch-local).
  
  **DURABLE-source version is correct and must stay:** when the source outlives the branch (a function-scope tuple/var, a param, the leaked for-loop var aliasing the live container), aliasing is right and matches CPython's shared mutation -- the scalar durable case already works (`/tmp/agents/tupuaf/ref_scalar_branch.py`), and the for-loop tuple case works (`/tmp/agents/tupuaf/ref_loopvar_after.py`). So the bug is specifically the BRANCH-LOCAL source; a blanket reject or blanket-own would break the durable case (owning a record also breaks the shared-mutation aliasing CPython has). **CPython note:** CPython survives the branch-local case because the binding keeps the object alive (refcounting); TPy's inline/stack records have no such keep-alive, so the branch-local target would need to *own* (move the element out of the dying source), while the durable target must *alias*. **Root cause:** reference-local hoist-across-branch aliases its source with no check that the source outlives the hoist scope. **Fix shape:** source-lifetime / escape analysis -- alias when the source outlives the target's hoist scope, own (move out) when it does not; this is the reference-type sibling of the str/bytes Option-B over-own item in TODO.md (same analysis, different remedy: str/bytes can conservatively own since a copy is observationally identical, reference types cannot). A conservative sema rejection of branch-local-sourced reference hoists is a possible interim but was deferred (it over-rejects the durable case and is inconsistent with the silently-compiling scalar form). Surfaced by /tpy-fix-bug of the (former) tuple-only S1; the scalar silent-UAF face was found during that analysis. Needs the escape-analysis work (IR) for the precise fix.
  - **Alias re-seated inside an `if` block (silent UAF, 2026-09-20):** `b = rows[0]` at function scope, then inside `if len(rows) > 1:` a block-local `loc = [B(100), B(101)]` with `for q in loc: b = q`, and `holder = b.rec_m()` after the block -- `B* b` at function scope is assigned `&(q)` into a `std::array` declared inside the `if`; TPy prints garbage, CPython `101`. `if`/`with` blocks carry no scope depth, so the scope-escape check cannot see the block-local storage at all. Probes `/tmp/agents/rev_tail/t4.py`, `t3.py`. Two more faces of the same blind spot (verified 2026-09-23, master 4713ba0943): the plain alias `p = P(0)`, then `if c: q = P(100); p = q` and `print(p.v)` after the block (`p = &(q);` into the block's `q`); and a tuple-unpack rebind in a block, `if c: p, k = P(100), 1`, which the parser splits into block-local `__unpack_0_0` temps and an alias bind (`p = &(__unpack_0_0);`) -- a generator target (`g, k = counter(100), 1`) dangles the same way. Probes `/tmp/agents/narrow/ub_rec.py`, `ub_rec2.py`, `/tmp/agents/narrow/shapes/unpack_block.py`.

If the narrowed fact and the declared member differ in a way `==` doesn't bridge (two cross-module records sharing a short name), the extraction is skipped and the "variant has no member" g++ build error appears -- a loud failure, not a silent miscompile. **Re-check and withdraw:** the generic-alias half was probed 2026-09-03 -- `def f(v: list[int] | str)` with `if isinstance(v, str): return 0` then `len(v)`, run through `tpyc --dump-code` -- and the extraction fires correctly (`auto& __v = *std::get<std::vector<::tpy::BigInt>*>(v);`), so a generic alias IS bridged by `==`. - **[LOW small] `os.strerror` uses non-thread-safe `std::strerror`.** `tpy::stdlib::os::strerror` (`runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/os_impl.cpp`) wraps `std::strerror`, which on some POSIX platforms returns a pointer into a shared static buffer -- a data race if `os.strerror` is called concurrently from multiple threads. glibc 2.32+ (the primary Linux target) is thread-safe, and CPython's `os.strerror` carries the same property, so this is latent hardening rather than an active bug. Fix shape: use `strerror_r` with a caller-supplied buffer. Surfaced by /tpy-review (runtime-cpp-correctness) of the os process/system batch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) A module-global value-Optional (`str | None` / `bytes | None`) cannot be narrowed with `is not None` at all.** `text: str | None = "hi"` then `if text is not None:` errors `stmt.if:if.cond_binop.is not.optional_other_nonetype:binop.shape.is not` in a plain function and `res.cond:binop.shape.is not` inside a generator/coroutine, so the for-loop the shape was filed for is never reached. `_lower_binop`'s `_IS_OPS` arm (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:3608-3623`) rejects unless one of `_is_none_compare_operand` / `_any_none_subject` / `_opt_record_none_subject` / the mixed-tuple ptr-element row recognizes the operand, and a global-slot read of a value-Optional is recognized by none of them. Tightly scoped (both probed): a module-global `int32 | None` narrows fine, and a function-local or param `str | None` narrows fine -- it is the GLOBAL + value-Optional pair specifically. Worth queueing: a module-level optional string is ordinary Python. This supersedes the older silent form of the entry -- the resumable for-source used to build its iterator from the raw global access with the optional deref missing, a wrong runtime result with no diagnostic; that emitter is gone, so the failure is loud instead. Fix shape: teach `_is_none_compare_operand` the global-slot value-Optional read, then confirm the resumable for-source over the narrowed global applies the global-slot + optional deref. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW] `os.path.realpath` can return a *relative* path when `std::filesystem::absolute()` fails.** `path_realpath` (`runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/os_impl.cpp`) does `abs = absolute(input, ec); if (ec) abs = input;` then `weakly_canonical(abs, ec)` with an `abs.lexically_normal()` fallback. If `absolute()` errors (a pathological cwd -- e.g. the cwd was removed), `abs` stays the un-absolutized relative input and the result can be relative, violating realpath's always-absolute guarantee (CPython joins cwd unconditionally). Rare; no TPy diagnostic. Fix shape: on `absolute()` failure, join `current_path()` manually rather than falling back to the raw input. Surfaced by /tpy-review (runtime-cpp-correctness) of os.path.realpath. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW] `os.path.expanduser` `~user` silently drops the home dir if the passwd entry exceeds the getpw buffer (ERANGE not retried).** `current_home`/`user_home` (`runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/os_impl.cpp`) size the `getpwuid_r`/`getpwnam_r` buffer from `sysconf(_SC_GETPW_R_SIZE_MAX)` (fallback 16384) and treat *any* non-zero return -- including `ERANGE` -- as "not found", returning `""` (-> expanduser leaves `~user` verbatim). A passwd entry larger than the buffer is misreported as a missing user rather than retried with a grown buffer. Practically unreachable (16384 covers real entries); robustness only. Fix shape: loop doubling the buffer on `ERANGE`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (runtime-cpp-correctness) of the pwd binding. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW] `os.environ` snapshot build reads `extern char** environ` without synchronization.** `environ_keys()` (`runtime/cpp/src/stdlib/os_impl.cpp`) walks `::environ`; a concurrent `setenv`/`unsetenv` (which may reallocate the array) is a data race per POSIX. NOT currently reachable -- the snapshot is built once at program startup, before any user thread runs -- so this is a latent hazard only if snapshot construction is ever moved off the startup path. No fix needed today; noted so a future change doesn't reintroduce a live race. Surfaced by /tpy-review (runtime-cpp-correctness).
- **[MED] An `@overload` method on a type imported from another module does not resolve at the call site (`No matching overload`).** A free function with `@overload` stubs resolves correctly across module boundaries, but the same overload set on a *method* does not: calling `inst.get(k)` where `inst`'s type (with an overloaded `get`) is defined in a different module fails with `No matching overload for 'get' with argument types (...)`, even for an arity/type that matches a stub exactly. Same class, same method, same call -- defined and called in *one* module resolves fine; split across modules fails. Confirmed with a 2-module repro (`/tmp/agents/osenv/pkg/{leaf,main}.py`: an `M` with `get(key)->str|None` / `get(key,default)->str` overloads, `inst=M()` in `leaf`, `inst.get("a")` in `main`). Likely the overload group (keyed by `id(first_impl)` in `analyzer.overload_groups`) is registered per-analyzing-module and not carried across the module registry for imported types, so the downstream module sees only one stub (or none) when resolving the call. Workaround: collapse the method to a single non-overloaded signature (e.g. `os.environ.get` is `get(key, default=None) -> str|None`, the `dict.get` shape, instead of the typeshed str / str|None overload pair). Surfaced building `os.environ` (the `_Environ.get` accessor, always called from a downstream user module). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW] `timedelta` day-overflow `OverflowError` message predates CPython 3.12.** `timedelta(days=10**9)` correctly raises `OverflowError` at the range check (`if d < -_MAXORDINAL_DAYS or d > _MAXORDINAL_DAYS` in `lib/tpy/datetime.py timedelta.__init__`), but the message is the old CPython `"timedelta # of days is too large"` vs 3.12's `"days=N; must have magnitude <= 999999999"`. Message-only divergence (the guard itself is correct -- an earlier "accepts-invalid" symptom was an artifact of a since-reverted two-overload ctor, not the current single ctor). Pre-existing. Align the message to 3.12 if a datetime parity pass revisits it.
- **[LOW small] Not every type-mismatch formatter routes through `disambiguated_pair`, so a same-short-name cross-module collision still renders unqualified at the un-converted sites.** `qualify-mismatch-diagnostics` + `fix-mismatch-diag-nested` route the main `expected X, got Y` sites (top-level + element/key/value) and the list-literal/comprehension element formatters through `disambiguated_pair`, qualifying nested leaves (`list[red.Tag]`) via the `_qualify_nominals_in_str` flag. Remaining gaps: (a) ~5 `expected {expected}, got {actual}` sites in `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py` (~1080/1091/1247/1258/1310) still interpolate bare `str()`; (b) the dict-key and set literal-element formatters in `tpyc/sema/expressions.py` only fire under a union/optional-guarded branch, so a plain `s: set[red.Tag] = {blue_tag}` collision routes elsewhere unqualified; (c) the union-vs-member shape (`Tag | int` param vs a narrowed `Tag` arg -> `expected Tag | int, got Tag`) is not a same-string collision so `disambiguated_pair` never fires. The rejection is correct in every case; only the label is ambiguous (rare cross-module same-name pairing). **Fix shape:** route the remaining `compatibility.py`/`expressions.py` formatters through `disambiguated_pair`; while consolidating, give `qualified_type_str`/`disambiguated_pair` a shared diagnostic-render home (a `sema/diagnostics.py` / `type_render` module rather than `typesys.py`) and let `NominalType.__str__` short-circuit on `_module_qname` before the `is_user_record` registry lookup. Surfaced by /tpy-review of `fix-mismatch-diag-nested`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] The two type-to-C++ rendering paths use different cross-module identity rules, a latent re-collision seam.** `NominalType.to_cpp` keys `native_cpp_names` by short name (`self.name`) with a qname-keyed lookup only as a *preference*; codegen's `TypeResolver.type_to_cpp` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/types.py`) is qname-aware via `imported_record_qualification_for_type`. `fix-cross-module-type-identity` made the qname path authoritative almost everywhere (and added qname keys to `native_cpp_names` so `to_cpp` disambiguates same-short-name records), but the two paths still look interchangeable while resolving identity differently. Any future emit site that reaches C++ via `to_cpp` for a type whose qname key was *not* registered (e.g. a record reachable only through a path that doesn't populate the qname key) would fall back to the short-name `native_cpp_names` entry and silently reintroduce the B114 same-name collision class. The specific sync point is record registration in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py` (the per-emit-module `native_cpp_names` population): a new record-registration path that sets the short-name key but forgets the canonical-qname key degrades silently, with no tripwire unless a same-short-name cross-module pair happens to exist in the program -- the most likely regression vector. No active miscompile today (the union/record/constructor paths are already qname-direct); this is a structural hazard. **Fix shape:** make `to_cpp` resolve the cross-module C++ name from the record's qname (mirroring `type_to_cpp` / `error_return_to_cpp`) rather than a short-name map with a qname fallback -- ideally collapsing the two paths. THIR is the natural home (see `docs/IR_DESIGN.md` Open Questions item 13). Surfaced by the `fix-cross-module-type-identity` retrospective. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] `is_return_exception` / `register_return_exception` still identify `ReturnException` types by bare short name: any user class sharing a registered exception's short name is treated as a `ReturnException`.** `register_return_exception` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) stores `record.name` and `is_return_exception` strips its (already-qualified) input back to a bare name before a compilation-global set lookup, so e.g. a user class named `StopIteration`, or a second `JsonError` colliding with `tplib.json`'s, is wrongly classified return-only.
