- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A nested `def` bound inside a block is not readable after the block, though Python makes its name a local of the whole enclosing scope.** [`nested-def-block-scoped-lambda-read-after-block`] `def main(): flag = True; if flag: def helper(x): return x + 100` / `else: def helper(x): return x + 200` then `print(helper(1))` after the `if` is valid Python (CPython prints 101) and TPy rejects it at the read: a nested def renders as a lambda declared in the C++ block its `def` sits in, so nothing after that block can name it, and each arm's lambda has a closure type of its own, so there is no bounded render for the read. The SILENT half is gone (2026-09-16): every path-shape of the read is now the located error `'helper' is not readable after the 'if' block on line N` (`SemanticContext.check_nested_def_shadowed_read` reading `func.nested_def_block_dead`, retired per block by `StatementAnalyzer.analyze_stmt`), where TPy used to call the MODULE `helper` and print 2, or -- with no module sibling -- pass the front end and fail the C++ build. What remains is the limitation: the callable needs a slot at FUNCTION scope, declared once and assigned per arm, which is the nested-def cell of the TODO design entry "a branch-first local is a DECLARATION WITHOUT AN INITIALIZER" (the slot holds an erased callable, not a lambda, so it also answers what a `Callable` local costs). Pinned by `tests/cases/nested_def/error_branch_local_read_after`; the `with` / `for` / `while` / `try` / `match` positions reject the same way. Found 2026-09-16 closing `nested-def-branch-local-read-resolves-outward`.

- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; everyday shape) A branch-first local that ALIASES a reference-typed parameter predecls a MUTABLE pointer against a const source.** [`branch-first-alias-drops-const`] `def probe(c: bool, r: Rec) -> int32:` with `try: v = r` / `finally: print("done")` / `return len(v.name)` emits `int32_t probe(bool c, const Rec& r) { Rec* v; ... v = &(r);` and g++ rejects *invalid conversion from 'const Rec*' to 'Rec*'*. Reproduces at `while`, `for`, `with` and `try`/`finally`; the `if` and `try`/`except` positions are well-formed only by accident (two arms binding makes the name `reassigned`, which marks the source parameter mutated and spells it `Rec&`), so the ABI of the function depends on how many arms bind. The POINTER hoist flavor spells `T*` unconditionally (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` ~2888 and ~3573) and takes its const bit from `function_stmt_borrow_decls`, a PHASE-1 fact derived from the init EXPRESSION's type (`tpyc/sema/context.py` ~660, `False` for a plain name source), while the parameter's const-ness is the PHASE-2 fixpoint verdict: two answers to one question, in two passes. Fix shape: the const-ness of a borrow binding is part of the local's slot verdict, closed over the borrow edges (`BorrowTracker.loans`) from the Phase-2 parameter verdict -- the same closure `ResumableFuncState.const_frame_bindings` already runs for frames; steps 1-2 of the TODO design entry "a branch-first local is a DECLARATION WITHOUT AN INITIALIZER". Do not patch the five ladders separately. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch6/branch-first-alias-drops-const/record_alias__{while,for,with}.py`, `try_finally_one_bind.py`. Found 2026-09-16 measuring the slot-verdict design.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught; everyday shape) A pointer-repr `Optional[Rec]` parameter of a generator or `async def` renders its frame field, factory signature and ctor as `Rec*` while the sync twin of the same TPy signature renders `const Rec*`, so forwarding the const pointer into the generator fails the C++ build.** [`frame-optional-capture-drops-const-verdict`] `def inner(p: P | None) -> Iterator[int32]: if p is not None: yield p.n` / `yield 0` and `def outer(p: P | None) -> int32:` summing `for v in inner(p)`: `outer` is inferred const (`const P* p`) and the call emits *invalid conversion from 'const P*' to 'P*'* (`initializing argument 1 of '__gen_inner inner(P*)'`). `FunctionInfo.const_borrow_params` holds the index in both twins; the frame drops it because the capture-kind cascade in `_frame_capture_const_names` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py` ~397) has no arm for a pointer-repr Optional (it covers REF, the ptr-repr tuple and the ptr-variant union), and `_classify_params`' POINTER/Optional arm (~507) spells `ptype_inner.to_cpp_param_type()` without consulting the verdict -- an EXPLICIT `readonly[P] | None` survives inside `ptype_inner` and renders `const P*`, an INFERRED one does not. Fix shape (measured, then reverted): add the Optional arm to the cascade and wrap the spelling in `ReadonlyType` when the name is in the deep-const set, exactly as the sibling tuple arm (~512-518) does; five committed cases change, every line `T*` -> `const T*` (`async/coro_pointer_optional_param`, `iterators/gen_pointer_optional_param`, `generics/optional_param_trait_form` (`opt_param_t` -> `opt_cparam_t`), `iterators/gen_default_args`, `async/async_borrowed_rvalue_arg`), each the frame adopting the ABI its sync twin already emits. Distinct from the two latent entries on `_param_is_const` and `_frame_deep_const_verdict`. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch6/frame-optional-capture-drops-const-verdict/p1.py`, `p2.py`, `p3.py`. Found 2026-09-16 measuring the emit-window const spelling.
- **[LOW small] (internal name in a diagnostic) An `Array[T, N]` slot fed a list literal of the wrong LENGTH reports the literal as `PendingList[T, M]#id`.** [`array-size-mismatch-names-pendinglist`] `a: Array[int32, 2] = [1, 2, 3]` errors *Type mismatch in variable 'a': expected Array[int32, 2], got PendingList[int32, 3]#0* -- the deferred-resolution type is a compiler-internal spelling with no meaning to the user, and the message says nothing about the real fault, the length. The dict-value face reports the same (`d: dict[str, Array[int32, 2]] = {"a": [1, 2, 3]}`). Every neighbouring mismatch already reports a user type (a wrong element type reports *List literal element 1 has type str*, a wrong container kind *got set[int32]*), so this is the one leak left on the literal paths. Reached wherever a pending list survives to an assignability check because the Array arm refused it: `pending_list_matches_array` (`tpyc/sema/type_ops.py`) is the size test, so the fix is a located message at that refusal (`a list of 3 elements does not fit Array[int32, 2]`), not a rendering rule for `PendingListType.__str__`. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch6/array-size-mismatch-names-pendinglist/f2_array_size_mismatch_local.py` (plain local) and `f1_array_size_mismatch.py` (dict value). Pre-existing at the plain local, and unchanged by the nested-literal fix. Found 2026-09-16 closing `dict-literal-list-value-stays-pending`, whose entry had noted the same leak for the dict-value shape it fixed.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A module that defines its own `run()` makes `asyncio.run(...)` emit a call into a namespace that does not exist.** [`asyncio-run-shadowed-by-module-run`] `import asyncio` + `async def amain(): ...` + `def run(): asyncio.run(amain())` emits `::tpyapp::__main__::run<std::monostate>(...)` and the C++ build fails with *'tpyapp::__main__' has not been declared* -- the qualifier is the literal `__main__` rather than the entry module's namespace, and the callee is the user's `run`, not `::tpystd::asyncio::run`. Renaming the user function makes the same program build and run. So the stdlib call's qualification is resolved against the user module's function table instead of the imported module's. Pre-existing; found 2026-09-16 while probing the async position of the for-each chain source (the probe's driver happened to be called `run`).
- **[MED small] (misleading diagnostic) Subscripting an UN-narrowed `Optional[dict]` reports the KEY as a bad index type instead of naming the Optional.** [`unnarrowed-optional-dict-subscript-message`] `def run(d: dict[str, list[int32]] | None) -> None: d["o"].append(3)` errors *Subscript index must be an integer type, got str* -- the receiver's Optional-ness is never mentioned, and the message accuses the (correct) `str` key. The `list` sibling is honest by accident: `d: list[int32] | None` / `d[0]` reaches THIR and rejects as *(stmt.expr_stmt:subscript.optional_check)*, because an int index passes the same test. Same message for the two other un-narrowed faces -- after an `if` whose narrowing has expired, and inside a nested `def`, where narrowing does not cross the closure boundary at all (`/tmp/agents/batch6/unnarrowed-optional-dict-subscript-message/c32_closure.py`; the non-Optional closure sibling compiles). Cause: the subscript's key-type check falls back to the list-index rule when the receiver type is not a resolved container, and an `Optional[dict]` is not; the fix is an arm at that check that names the Optional and points at the `is not None` narrowing, ahead of the index-type test. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch6/unnarrowed-optional-dict-subscript-message/u01_unproven_param_method.py`, `u02_unproven_param_bind.py`, `u03_unproven_after_else.py`. Found 2026-09-16 measuring the safety boundary of `narrowed-optional-elem-not-lowered`.
- **[MED small] (accepts invalid, C++ error) A module-level `def` written inside an `if` fails the C++ build, naming a symbol the user never wrote.** [`module-level-block-scoped-def-not-declared`] `FLAG = True`, then `if FLAG:` / `    def pick(x: int32) -> int32: return x + 1`, then `pick(1)` from any function: tpyc accepts the program and the C++ compiler reports `'pick' was not declared in this scope`. The function is emitted inside the module-init block its `def` sits in, so nothing else in the module can name it -- the same defect as `nested-def-block-scoped-lambda-read-after-block` one scope out, but the nested-def guard does not see it, because a module-level `def` is a module function and not a `TpyNestedDef`. `BUGS.md#conditional-def-lambda-block-scoped` is this same defect filed from the C++ side; close them together. Fix shape: decide whether a conditional module-level `def` is supported at all; if it is, it needs a module-scope declaration the block assigns into (the callable slot of the TODO "declaration without an initializer" design), and if not, a located error at the `def` rather than a C++ diagnostic. Pre-existing (identical on 01eb0bed07); found 2026-09-16 while making the nested-def block rule.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, located) A branch-FIRST `Optional[T]` local whose source is an optional FIELD read off an rvalue receiver rejects, where the straight-line decl and every rebind of it compile.** [`branch-first-opt-field-rvalue-source-rejected`] `if x > 1: p: Point | None = make_holder(x).value` / `else: p = None` with a read after the `if` errors *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (`stmt.var_decl:reseat.branch_rvalue_source`)*. The BRANCH_RVALUE reseat arm (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` ~9195) routes a branch-hoisted pointer local's rvalue through `_rebind_rvalue_source_ok` (~2931), whose admitted shapes are container literals and comprehensions, F1-record rvalues, `copy()`, a record method rvalue and the storage-call families -- a field read off an rvalue receiver is in none of them, so the vetted slice refuses it. Sibling table (measured 2026-09-16): the branch-first decl rejects under this tag in an `if` arm, a `with` body and a `try` body with `finally`; it COMPILES in a `while` or `for` body when the read stays inside the loop (no hoist); in a `try` body with `except` it rejects under the same tag, and in a `match` arm it rejects the whole statement (`stmt.match`, `BUGS.md#match-nonvalue-hoist-unadmitted`); and the straight-line decl REBOUND from the same source compiles in all seven statement kinds. The split is branch-first vs straight-line, not the statement kind. Fix shape: the branch-first decl needs the same materialization slot the straight-line decl takes (`reseat.opt_frame_storage_field` / OPT_STORAGE_CALL), so the hoist should read the decl's slot verdict instead of the reseat's rvalue-shape list -- the `LocalSlot` verdict of TODO.md's "A branch-first local is a DECLARATION WITHOUT AN INITIALIZER" entry is that verdict. Pinned by `tests/cases/optional/error_branch_first_opt_field_slot`. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch6/reseat_try/bf_*.py`, `bff_*.py` (branch-first) and `s_*.py` (the rebind controls). Found 2026-09-16 pinning the reject named in `optional/opt_slot_field_rebind`'s header.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, located) A `match` pattern capture bound at DIFFERENT types in different arms and read after the `match` does not lower.** [`match-capture-disagreeing-types-read-after`] `case Cat(lives=v): ...` / `case Dog(nick=v): ...` (an `int32` and a `str`) followed by `print(v)` after the statement fails with *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (`stmt.expr_stmt:name.global_read`)*: the capture keeps per-arm block-scoped storage (`tpyc/sema/match.py`, the `agreeing` gate over `capture_bind_types`), so nothing declares `v` where the read stands, while sema still binds the name after the `match` at the LAST arm's type. CPython prints whichever value the taken arm bound. Before the gate excluded such captures from the post-match hoist they shared one declaration of the last arm's type, silently (`std::string v; v = __case_0.lives;` printed `9` as a tab). The fix is a decision on what one slot of two capture types is (a refusal naming both types, as a statement binding gets, or a union local); the read-inside-each-arm shape is pinned by the `capture_types` section of `tests/cases/control_flow/sibling_arm_join`. Probe `/tmp/agents/arms/cap_after.py`. Found 2026-09-26 while joining sibling-arm bindings.
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output) A `for` loop target bound in one `if` arm is not joined with a binding of the same name in the sibling arm, so the wider binding truncates.** [`sibling-arm-loop-target-not-joined`] `if c: for y in range(3): pass` / `else: y = big` with `big: int64` = 10000000000, then `print(y)`, prints `1410065408` (CPython `10000000000`): the loop target keeps the `int32` the iterable gave it and the else-arm's `int64` binding is stored into that slot. Statement bindings in sibling arms join through the reassignment join (`_enter_sibling_arm`, tpyc/sema/statements.py); a loop target is typed by its iterable and never enters it. Probe `/tmp/agents/rv1-parity/F2.py`. Found by the review of the int/float hint/arm-join branch.
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output) A walrus rebind never widens an inferred fixed-width int local.** [`walrus-rebind-never-widens`] `y = 3; print((y := big))` with `big: int64` = 10000000000 prints `1410065408` twice (CPython `10000000000`), and so do a walrus in a sibling `if` arm (`if c: y = 3` / `else: print((y := big))`) and walrus bindings in the two arms of a ternary (`(y := 3) if c else (y := big)`). The walrus path checks its value against the local's type but does not ask the reassignment join that a plain `y = big` goes through, so the `int32` slot takes the `int64` value. - **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) An inferred tuple local whose int ELEMENT is rebound to a wider int is refused.** [`tuple-element-int-widening-refused`] `p = (3, 1); p = (big, 1)` with `big: int64` fails with `Type mismatch in reassignment to 'p' (tuple element 0): expected int32, got int64`, and the ternary `(3, 1) if c else (big, 1)` with `Incompatible types in ternary expression: 'tuple[int32, int32]' and 'tuple[int64, int32]'`; CPython binds either tuple. Since sibling arms join, `match` arms and a `try` body / handler binding such tuples are refused when the narrower binding comes first; the wider-first order compiles and prints the wide value, where master compiled only the wider-LAST order correctly and truncated the wider-first one silently (`(1410065408, 1)`). A structural join that widened tuple elements (and retyped a narrower tuple-literal ternary arm) was built and backed out: a slot widened after uses typed it at the narrower element needs the whole-function slot facts (TODO.md "Whole-function slot and element facts"). Probes `/tmp/agents/cgc/{p3,p8}.py`, `/tmp/agents/narrow/p/tup/t{1,2,3,4,5,6}.py`, `/tmp/agents/rv3-testcov/r4.py`. Found by the review of the int/float hint/arm-join branch.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, located; everyday shape) A module-level name bound to another global's container ELEMENT rejects, at any depth.** [`global-alias-of-global-element-rejected`] `G: list[list[int32]] = [[1]]` then `R = G[0]` at module level errors *at module level: this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (`stmt.var_decl:top_level.global_slot_shape`)*; the same binding inside a function compiles and aliases. Both names have static storage duration, so the borrow is sound -- the global slot model simply has no shape for a name whose value is a borrow (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`, the top-level decl arm). The nested receiver (`R = CUBE[0][0]`) rejects under the same tag, so it is the global-slot shape and not the element depth. - **[LOW small] (front-end perf) Resolving a subscript's chained RECEIVER re-walks the chain once per hop, so the cost is quadratic in the chain's length.** [`chained-subscript-recv-quadratic`] `_chained_subscript_recv_type` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) proves the receiver is a rooted lvalue with `_lvalue_chain_root`, which asks `is_rvalue_source` per hop; that predicate's field arm recurses to the root, so an n-hop receiver costs O(n^2) node visits, and every `a.b.c[i].d[j].e[k]` read in a body pays it once per subscript. It was EXPONENTIAL before the fold (the resolver fell through to two predicates that each re-entered it one hop shorter, T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2)); the fold to one walker removed that, and what is left is the ordinary re-walk. Nothing memoizes a receiver and nothing caps the depth. Invisible on the corpus (chains are two or three hops), which is the shape CLAUDE.md's "algorithmic cliffs" note warns about: size-proportional in a place no existing benchmark grows. Fix shape unchanged: memoize the resolution on the receiver NODE for one body lowering (`tpyc/identity_map.py` is the sanctioned table keyed on an object) -- the answer is a pure function of the node plus `locals_` / `pointers`, which do not change inside one resolution. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, S4) of batch 6; re-measured after the rooted-lvalue fold.

Measured siblings, all admitted: the same chain with a reference-returning accessor (`-> T`, not `-> Own[T]`) at the same hop, every stored-field and reference-element hop (`hs[0].pair`, `o.h.pair`, `self.o.h.pair`, `d[1].pair`, a module-global root, a `readonly` root), and a slice as the WHOLE iterable (`for b in xs[0:2]`), where the span is the loop's own. Each rejected form is legal Python that an ordinary program writes; the workaround is one line (`inner = self.get(); for x in inner.xs`), and it is what the pinned cases document. Site: the hop walk in `_lvalue_chain_root` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`), which asks `is_rvalue_source` per hop. Fix shape: materialize the temporary into a named holder that outlives the loop / the unpacked targets, and drive its lifetime from the statement rather than the expression -- a design row (where the holder is declared, and what happens when the same chain appears in a condition or a comprehension), not a predicate widening. Recorded 2026-09-16 while closing the accessor half of the chain rule.

- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid / silent wrong output) A class-qualified read or write of an INSTANCE field inside a subclass method resolves to `self`'s field, where CPython sees a class attribute that does not exist.** [`unbound-self-field-read-binds-self`] With `class Base: n: int32` (annotation only, set in `__init__`) and `class Derived(Base)`, `return Base.n` inside a `Derived` method renders `return this->Base::n;` and `Base.n = 9` renders `this->Base::n = 9;` -- the unbound-self spelling names THIS object's storage. CPython has no `Base.n` at all: the read raises *AttributeError: type object 'Base' has no attribute 'n'*, and the write creates a CLASS attribute that leaves the instance one untouched, so `Derived().bump(); print(d.n)` prints 7 under CPython and 9 under TPy. The reach is narrow: the resolution is gated on the qualifier being an ANCESTOR of the enclosing record, so `Base.n` inside `Base`'s own method is *'Base' is not an ancestor of 'Base'* and outside any method it is *'Base' is not a variable* -- only the subclass position diverges, and both its faces (read and write) do. Fix shape: an ancestor-qualified access whose target is an instance FIELD (rather than a class constant, a static method or a nested type) should be a located error naming the `self.` spelling, since no Python program means it; the existing ancestor gate is the place the field-vs-class-member split belongs. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch6/unbound-self-field-read/p2_scalar.py` (read), `p6_derived_write.py` (write) and `p3_own.py` / `p4_outside.py` / `p5_write.py` (the rejecting siblings). Noted in `tests/cases/inheritance/error_inheritance_base_field_iter_mutation`'s header, which reaches it through a `list` field. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity S3) of batch 6.
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output) A user `__aiter__` that returns `self` -- the canonical CPython async-iterator idiom -- copies the iterable into the coroutine frame, so everything the iteration advances is lost to the caller.** [`aiter-self-copied-into-frame`] `class Countdown` with `def __aiter__(self) -> "Countdown": return self` and an `__anext__` that decrements `self.n`: `c = Countdown(3)`, `async for v in c: print("v", v)`, `print(c.n)` prints `3` under TPy and `0` under CPython (probe `/tmp/agents/batch6/aiter-self-copied-into-frame/aiter_self2.py`; the yielded values match, only the shared object's state diverges). The frame's iterator slot is `::tpy::aiter_type_t<S>` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`, the async-for slot) and `aiter_type_t` is `std::decay_t<decltype(std::declval<S&>().__aiter__())>` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dunder.hpp:809`), so a BORROW-form return decays to an owned copy: the loop advances the copy's cursor and the caller's object is never touched. `tests/cases/async/async_for_method_awaiter_order` has exactly this shape but iterates a TEMPORARY (`async for v in Countdown(3)`), so its cpy phase is blind to the divergence. Fix shape: the frame slot takes the same borrow-vs-storage verdict every other frame slot takes -- a pointer/reference when `__aiter__` returns a borrow form (`self`, a field), the owned copy only when it mints a fresh iterator object -- as the sync path already does (`is_self_iterator_v` + `resumable_iter_init` / `resumable_iter_next`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/generator.hpp`); a `@nocopy` or `Own` source fails the build instead. A REFERENCE-typed element (`async def __anext__(self) -> Point`, then `async for p in w: p.x += 100`) additionally fails the C++ build: the `async_for` strategy never sets `pointer_form_loop_var`, so the `Point*` that `__anext__` returns is emplaced into a `frame_slot<Point>` (`invalid conversion from Point*`); fixing that alone would make the loop compile and silently mutate the copy, so the slot fix lands first (probe `/tmp/agents/prereq/asyncfor.py`). Context found with it (not a separate entry): the missing async-for invalidation warnings this entry was filed alongside are CLOSED -- since 2026-09-17 an `async for` files the same iteration borrow the sync for-each does, through the same registration, so `async for x in rows[0]` warns for an element method and for `rows.append` exactly as its sync twin does (`tests/cases/async/async_for_warn_iter_mutation`). Those warnings are what will keep the body honest once the slot below holds a borrow instead of a copy; the copy is still what makes the ITERABLE's own state diverge. Found 2026-09-16 in batch 6's round-4 parity review; pre-existing on master.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud C++ build error) A MUTATING (`@readonly(False)`) `__len__`, `__bool__` or operator dunder is called through const C++ glue.** [`mutating-dunder-const-wrapper`] The dunder itself is emitted non-const, but what calls it is not: the generated `size() const` wrapper for `__len__`, the `friend operator+(const T& lhs, ...)` / `friend operator==(const T& lhs, ...)` wrappers for a binary or comparison dunder, and the runtime's `::tpy::__bool__(const T&)` truthiness helper. So `d + 1`, `d == e` and `if d:` fail the g++ build (*passing 'const T' as 'this' argument discards qualifiers*, *no matching function for call to '__bool__'*) even on a mutable receiver, and a class that merely declares a mutating `__len__` breaks at its `size() const` wrapper whether or not anything calls it. Separately `len(d)` over a mutating `__len__` rejects in sema (*No matching overload for len(DD)*), where CPython calls it. The subscript and `in` dunders do not have the problem: they are called directly on the receiver, and sema credits them as receiver calls (`tpyc/sema/receiver_calls.py`); these sites need the same credit once their wrappers follow the dunder's const-ness. Repro `/tmp/agents/dd/mgi/p9_siblings.py` (`__bool__`, `__add__`, `__eq__`) and `/tmp/agents/dd/mgi/p5_ro_faces.py` (`__len__`). Found 2026-09-26.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud; precision) A record with several `__getitem__` overloads answers a subscript from the FIRST one.** [`record-getitem-overload-first-wins`] With `@dispatch def __getitem__(self, i: int32) -> int32` followed by `@dispatch @readonly(False) def __getitem__(self, k: str) -> int32`, `t["q"]` errors *Subscript index must be an integer type, got str*: the result type and the key check come from `lookup_record_method` / `record_getitem_key_ret` (`tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`), which take the first overload, so a later overload's key is never tried (the protocol sibling is `protocol-getitem-nonint-key-rejects`). The receiver-mutation credit already resolves the overload with `resolve_overload` over the substituted non-slice overloads and the index type, as the `__contains__` arm does (`_resolve_getitem_overload`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`), so `t[0]` on a `readonly[Two]` stays const; when resolution fails or is ambiguous it falls back to "any mutating overload counts". Two more first-wins spots: `_credit_user_setitem` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) credits the FIRST non-slice `__setitem__` overload, and an ambiguous `__getitem__` resolution falls back to "any mutating overload counts", which on a readonly receiver can raise a spurious *Cannot call non-readonly method '__getitem__' on readonly reference* for a key that would have picked a readonly overload. Found by the cpython-parity probes of the generator-frame perf review, 2026-09-17.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) The shared non-value hoist classifier has no UNION arm, so a union-typed local first bound in a loop or branch body of a PLAIN function and read after it is rejected at lowering.** [`union-local-hoist-unclassified`] `for i in range(2): u: Pic | Flat = Pic(i)` with `u = Flat(i)` under an `if` in the same body, then reading `u` after the loop behind an `isinstance`, dies with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:foreach.hoist_type)`; the binding loop in an `if` arm gives the same reject under `if.hoist_type`. The ternary spelling (`u: Pic | Flat = Pic(i) if flag else Flat(i)`) never reaches the hoist -- sema stops it first with *Incompatible types in ternary expression* -- so the two-statement spelling above is the repro (`/tmp/agents/r3_parity/b/union4.py`, verified 2026-09-17). `_nonvalue_hoist_flavor` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) classifies plain non-value, pointer-repr Optional, readonly and resumable shapes and falls through on a union, and every ladder ends in that one classifier, so all six positions reject together. Pre-existing and position-independent: the plain non-sibling, non-nested spelling rejects identically (verified 2026-09-16), so it is not an anchor-placement artifact. The union of two VALUE types is unaffected (it takes the plain-value hoist). **Scope: a plain (sync) body only.** In a generator or `async def` the name is a frame member, whose declaration is the frame layout's, so the hoist never reaches the classifier and the shape compiles -- verified 2026-09-20 with `/tmp/agents/review_hoist/docs/u_gen_union.py` and `meta/q3d_union_gen_plain.py` against the sync twin `u_sync_union.py` (rejects `foreach.hoist_type`). **Fix shape:** add the union arm to `_nonvalue_hoist_flavor` -- the borrow form at a local is `::tpy::Union<A*, B*>`, which is the POINTER flavor the classifier already renders, so the arm is a classification row rather than a new render. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) Reassigned non-value locals and some pattern captures hoisted out of `match` still reject in a plain function.** [`match-nonvalue-hoist-unadmitted`] Ordinary single-binding moves and copies now use the shared non-value storage flavors, independent of the subject strategy. Remaining scalar-match witnesses include a record constructed in BOTH arms (directly or inside a nested `for`), a mutable record parameter aliased in both arms, and tuple-unpacked record bindings read after the match. They still reject `stmt.match`: repeated owning writes need the match rebind-slot adapter, while capture/borrow hoists retain separate strategy and constness gates. In a record-subject match, a field capture sharing its name with an ordinary last-use assignment also rejects at `match.field_bind_ptr_hoist`; `match/error_capture_and_move_hoist` pins that separate capture-write boundary. The old blanket `nonvalue_ok` restriction no longer explains ordinary assignment failures. The value-typed two-arm loop twin remains pinned by `blk_match` in `control_flow/hoist_nonvalue_read_after_loop`. Generator/async frame-member hoists have their separate decl-less route. Verified 2026-09-22 by `/tmp/agents/local_binding_match_docs_probe.py`, including the original tuple-unpack witness `m_sync_record_match.py`. Extend the shared slot verdict and preserve capture write modes rather than dropping every match gate. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) A name a loop body binds in one `try` or `match` arm and a plain assignment binds in another is rejected after the block, where the same shape in an `if` compiles.** [`try-match-mixed-loop-arm-bind-rejected`] `try:` / `for a in range(3): v = a` / `except ValueError:` / `v = 9` then `print(v)` rejects with `variable 'v' may not be assigned at this point`; the `if`/`else` spelling compiles with one declaration in front of the `if`. Both readings assume the loop head provably runs (`range(3)` here) -- an unprovable head leaves the arm's binding maybe-unassigned on its own and the `if` spelling rejects too, which is the loop-clause rule, not this defect. The definite-assignment half is shared (the `if`, `try` and `match` merges all intersect assigned-or-loop-bound across arms, `FlowFacts.merge`), but the arm's direct binding is taken back out of the scope only at the `if` merge (`_unbind_branch_pending`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`), so at `try` and `match` the pending entry never becomes the sole authority and the read is the conservative reject. Workaround: assign the name once before the block. **Fix shape:** the unbind belongs where the arms already MEET -- the shared branch merge that the flow-facts lattice runs for every multi-arm construct -- not repeated per construct: replicating `_unbind_branch_pending` at the three `try` tiers and the `match` merge would be a third copy of a rule the merge is the single home for, and the next construct would need a fourth. Feed the merge the per-arm "new in scope" / "new pending" sets each construct already keeps for `record_branch_decls` and let it decide. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent uninitialized read) A walrus in an EXPRESSION position grants its target unconditionally, so a read after a short circuit that skipped it is never diagnosed.** [`expr-position-walrus-grants-unconditionally`] The per-path rule -- a walrus target in a condition counts as assigned on a branch only when EVERY way of reaching that branch evaluated it (`condition_walrus_assigned`, `tpyc/sema/flow_facts.py`) -- is consumed at the `if` and `while` heads only (`_analyze_condition_walrus`, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`). Outside a head the same shapes leave the target plainly assigned by the walk that analyzed them. `k = -1` / `v = 0 < k < (m := g(k))` then `return m` emits `int32_t m;` with no initializer and `return m;` reads it: TPy prints `False` then `0`, CPython raises `UnboundLocalError` (the chain stops at `0 < k`, so the walrus never runs). `v = 1 if flag else (b := g(2))` then `return b` is the same shape through the ternary arm: TPy `1` then `0`, CPython `UnboundLocalError`. Probes `/tmp/agents/verify5_zt/p1_chain.py` and `p2_ternary.py`, verified 2026-09-18; pre-existing, not specific to any loop shape. The `and`/`or` spelling is the one expression position that is already correct -- `x = a and (b := f())` then `return b` is rejected with *variable 'b' may not be assigned at this point* (`p3_and.py`), because `_analyze_binop` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py` ~911) saves `definitely_assigned` before the short-circuit operand and restores it after -- so one rule answers by OPERATOR today, and its correct answer comes from a blanket rollback rather than from the rule. **Fix shape:** grant `T & F` of the analyzed expression from the one function, so `_analyze_binop`'s arm and the ternary / chained-compare expression analysis all read `condition_walrus_assigned` instead of rolling back or granting outright; every position then inherits the rule and the head helper's subtraction step (`condition_walrus_targets` minus `if_true & if_false`) disappears with it. The same change folds `_walrus_paths` and `condition_walrus_targets` into one walk, and takes the `loop_bound_assigned` half of the rollback with it (the second spelling of the assignment lattice is not saved beside `definitely_assigned` there -- see the loop-anchor hygiene item in TODO.md). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud, two faces) A head whose truth the walrus path rule cannot relate to the branch taken loses the grant, although every path into the body ran the walrus.** [`cond-walrus-true-set-ignores-truth-facts`] `_walrus_paths` (`tpyc/sema/flow_facts.py`) computes the head's true-set structurally, with no access to the truth facts `NarrowingTracker` already holds, so two everyday heads under-approximate it. (a) An OPAQUE CALL over a short circuit: `while bool(flag and (z := g()) > 0): t += z` rejects the body read with *variable 'z' may not be assigned at this point*, and the `if` twin rejects identically; CPython runs both and prints `0 0` for `flag=False` (probes `/tmp/agents/verify2_zt/arch/d5_nested.py` and `d5_if_only.py`, verified 2026-09-18). Reaching the body implies the call returned true, but nothing relates an arbitrary call's result to which operand ran, so the walk falls to `_walrus_certain` of the call's arguments and gets the empty set; `bool(e)` specifically is the identity on truth and could be seen through. Remedy for users: drop the `bool(...)`. (b) A TERNARY head with an arm that is never true: `if (b := f()) > 0 if a else a:` and `if h((b := f()) > 0) if a else False:` both reject `print(b)` in the then-body; CPython prints `7` for each (probes `/tmp/agents/verify4_zt/safety/gen9/z4_tern_plain.py` and `z4_tern_cond_runtime.py`, verified 2026-09-18). The ternary rule intersects both arms' true-sets (`cond | (t_then & t_else)`) and has no way to drop an arm that cannot be true: the literal `False` arm is what `condition_provably_true` / the `_range_truth` fold (`tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`) already decides, and the bare `a` arm is false on the path that reaches it because the ternary's own condition is `a`. **Fix shape:** let the path walk consult the truth fold -- an arm the fold answers False for drops out of the intersection, and a truth-preserving wrapper (`bool`) is transparent to it. `_range_truth` has no `TpyIfExpr` arm today, so the ternary face needs one there as well. Both faces are loud and over-reject only; nothing miscompiles. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent CPython divergence, no diagnostic) A REFERENCE-typed for-loop VARIABLE read after the loop is hoisted into a value slot, so the name holds a COPY of the last element where CPython holds the element itself.** [`ref-loop-var-read-after-loop-copies`] `pics = [Pic(1), Pic(2)]` / `for p in pics: pass` / `p.n += 10` then `print(p.n, pics[1].n)` prints `lv 12 2` where CPython prints `lv 12 12`: the hoist emits `std::optional<Pic> p;` before the loop and `p = *__beg_0;` inside it, copying each element into the slot, so the post-loop mutation lands in the copy and the source list never sees it. Probe `/tmp/agents/review_parity_loop/p_loopvar_plain.py`, verified 2026-09-16. Four positions witness the same emit and the same divergence: the plain shape above; across an unrelated sibling loop (`p_loopvar_sib_list.py`, `lv4 13 3` against CPython's `13 13`, and the mutable-list twin `/tmp/agents/p31_mut.py`, `mut_iter 7 6` against `7 7`); out of an enclosing `with` (`p_loopvar_with.py`, `lvw 7 3` against `7 7`; re-verified 2026-09-17 with `/tmp/agents/r3_parity/lv3.py`, `lv_with 12 2` against CPython's `lv_with 12 12`); and at module level (`p_module_loopvar.py`, `mod 13 3` against `13 13`). A write through the loop variable INSIDE the body aliases correctly; only the read after the loop sees the copy (`xs = [R(1), R(2)]; for v in xs: pass; v.a = 99; print(xs[1].a)` prints `2` against CPython's `99`, `/tmp/agents/design_pos/side/forafter.py`). The body-LOCAL twin is CORRECT and shows the shape the fix wants: `for p in pics: last = p` then `last.n += 10` emits `Pic* last;` with `last = &(p);` in the body and prints `bt 13 13`, matching CPython (`/tmp/agents/round1_apply/t_bodylocal_twin.py`). What separates them is the borrow-decl fact: a statement-level binding records one (`stmt_borrow_decls`, `tpyc/sema/context.py`) and the hoist ladder then picks the pointer flavour, while the loop VARIABLE is bound by the loop machinery, records none, and the `hoist_loop_var` predecl (`_promote_pending_loop_var` in `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`, rendered from `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) falls through to the owning optional-storage slot. A VALUE-typed loop var copying is correct and unaffected. The same slot is the loud face after a `break`: `for x in xs: if len(x.xs) == 1: break` then `x.xs.append(5)` fails the C++ build (`'class std::optional<P>' has no member named 'xs'`; probe `/tmp/agents/lja/loopvar_brk.py`, found 2026-09-24, identical on master a0bf4f4671). **Fix shape:** give the promoted loop variable the pointer form its body-local alias already gets -- the loop var borrows the element by the language model, so the predecl is `T*` and the per-iteration reseat takes the element's address, which is exactly what the alias arm renders. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (does not compile, raw toolchain error) A for-loop VARIABLE promoted out of a READONLY container source gets a const-pointer predecl and a VALUE reseat.** [`readonly-loop-var-reseat-const-ptr`] `def ro_plain(xs: readonly[list[Pic]]): for p in xs: pass` followed by `print(p.n)` emits `const Pic* p;` before the loop and `p = *__beg_0;` inside it; g++ stops with *cannot convert 'const Pic' to 'const Pic\*' in assignment*. Probe `/tmp/agents/p12_roplain.py`, verified 2026-09-16. The two halves of one hoist disagree: the predecl takes the borrow form the readonly source implies, the reseat renders the storage form. Sibling of [`ref-loop-var-read-after-loop-copies`], the same disagreement settled the other way (both halves storage, hence a silent copy) over a mutable source -- one fix making the promoted loop var a borrow at BOTH halves closes both. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (does not compile, raw toolchain error) A TUPLE-of-reference-type local first bound in a loop body and read after the loop predeclares the borrow form and assigns the storage form.** [`tuple-of-reference-hoist-storage-mismatch`] `for i in range(2): x = (Pic(i),)` then `print(x[0].n)` emits `std::tuple<Pic*> x;` before the loop and `x = std::tuple<Pic>(Pic(i));` inside it; the build dies in libstdc++'s `<tuple>` on `__const_assignable<Pic*>`. Probe `/tmp/agents/p16_t1.py`, verified 2026-09-16. The predecl asks for the tuple's borrow form (the local/param spelling) while the literal renders its storage form, and nothing converts between them at the reseat, although `tuple_to_pointer` / `tuple_to_storage` are that conversion at every other boundary. A tuple of VALUE elements at the same position compiles. **Fix shape:** either predeclare the storage form (the slot owns the fresh tuple, and the read after the loop is an ordinary storage read) or insert the storage-to-borrow conversion at the reseat -- the same borrow-vs-storage decision the branch-first-hoist design entry in TODO.md settles once for every hoist. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) A MODULE-level `str`/`bytes` local whose later binding owns keeps the view slot, so the global points into a freed temporary.** [`module-level-view-slot-ignores-owned-binding`] `p = "abcdef"` / `s = p[1:]` / `s = p + "d"` at module level emits a global `std::string_view s` and assigns `str_concat(p, "d")` into it -- a view over a temporary destroyed at end-of-statement; the program happens to print `abcdefd`. The sibling-loop spelling (`for i in ...: ms = long[i:]` then `for k in ...: ms = ms + "tail"`) prints garbage, which is the same slot with the same missing decision. In a FUNCTION the two bindings join and the local owns (the one-type-one-storage rule); at module level `_infer_new_local_type` returns before the view family is consulted (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`, `if self.ctx.is_top_level`), so no storage decision is ever made and the first binding's view spelling stands. Fix shape: a module slot needs the same join -- either the deduction runs for module-init locals too (the slot is a global, so its storage must be chosen once for every binding), or a module-level view slot rebound from an owning source is rejected. Probes `/tmp/agents/one_rule/fam/a_mod.py` (flat) and `/tmp/agents/one_rule_impl/probes2/sections.py` (loop form, the `module_str` section, which is why that shape is NOT in `control_flow/hoist_nonvalue_read_after_loop`). Pre-existing; re-verified 2026-09-17 while landing the in-function join. A SINGLE binding hits the same missing decision when its view source is a temporary (2026-09-26): `G1 = first1(S + "x")` (`def first1(s: str) -> StrView: return s`) and the tuple twin `G = first((S, 1))` (`def first(t: tuple[str, int]) -> StrView: return t[0]`) at module level emit `std::string_view G1` / `G` globals over the argument temporary and print garbage, where the function-local twins own (`view_source_is_temporary`); probe `/tmp/agents/sm_r5/glob3.py`. Module globals rank last (TODO.md "Module scope is the body of __tpy_init"), which this falls under. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) An unannotated local bound to a SLICE of a temporary is not lowered.** [`unannotated-slice-of-temporary-unlowered`] `def f(p: str) -> None: t = (p + "x")[1:]` reports *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:subscript.slice_shape)*, while the same slice over a NAME (`t = p[1:]`) lowers. The local is correct sema-side -- its source is a temporary, so the storage deduction gives it an owned copy -- and it is the slice-of-a-non-name RECEIVER that the decl arm does not spell. CPython runs the program. Probe `/tmp/agents/one_rule/tmp2.py`. Pre-existing (the annotated spelling `t: StrView = (p + "x")[1:]` is a deliberate reject, not this). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (an extra copy per call in stdlib hot paths, never unsafe) The str/bytes storage join judges a binding after the first more strictly, so the two ORDERS of one pair of bindings can differ in whether the local copies.** [`view-storage-join-stricter-after-first-binding`] A local's FIRST binding is judged by source durability (`view_source_is_temporary`: a name, field or slice of either is a live borrow), a later binding by `is_view_compatible_source`, which fails closed on every shape its arms do not recognise -- a str SLICE among them. So `s = p[1:]` then `s = sv` (a view local) keeps the view, while `s = sv` then `s = p[1:]` makes `s` own a copy: same bindings, same type, different storage. The join itself is sound -- it takes the strictest demand, and the strict side is the copy -- but the rule the language states is that the POSITION of a binding never changes the answer, and here it changes this one. Unifying on durability alone was tried on 2026-09-17 and reverted: `is_view_compatible_source` asks the stronger question (it follows what a NAME's own binding borrows, which the durability walk does not), and answering the weaker one at the rebind site put `urllib.parse` / `tplib.requests` locals into views over dead storage -- 6 cases failed the exec phase with garbage output, a panic, and a `UnicodeDecodeError` on the captured output. Fix shape: one predicate that keeps the name-provenance arms of `is_view_compatible_source` and adds the durability answer for the shapes it fails closed on (a slice whose root is a live local), used by both the declaration seed and the rebind check. Four stdlib locals pay a per-call heap allocation for it, all of them a slice rebound into a name whose live root outlives them: `dirname`'s `head` and `expandvars`'s `name` (`os/path.cpp`), `urlsplit`'s `body` (`urllib/parse.cpp`), and `CookieJar._ingest`'s `domain_attr` / `d` (`tplib/requests.cpp`) -- each renders `std::string x = std::string(::tpy::str_slice(..))` where the same slice taken as the local's FIRST binding renders a `std::string_view`; `tests/cases/control_flow/hoist_nonvalue_read_after_loop` pins the same render in its `two_loop_str_views` section. Found 2026-09-17 landing the one-type-one-storage join, raised to MED 2026-09-17 on those witnesses. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (a heap allocation per iteration, never unsafe) A list-LITERAL local hoisted out of a loop loses the `std::array` slot its flat twin gets.** [`loop-hoisted-list-literal-loses-array-slot`] `for i in range(2): xs = [i, i]` with a later `xs = [9, 9]` renders `std::optional<std::vector<int32_t>> __slot_1;` per bind site and `xs = &*(__slot_1 = {i, i});` in the body -- a heap allocation on every iteration -- while the same two bindings with no loop render `std::array<int32_t, 2> __slot_1 = {1, 1};` (probes `/tmp/agents/r3_codegen/list_join.py` and `list_flat.py`, verified 2026-09-17). Neither literal is mutated or passed to a `list` param, so the Array resolution the flat shape reaches is available to the hoisted one too; the hoist's optional-storage slot is what forces the vector. Pinned (as the vector render) by `tests/cases/control_flow/block_local_reassign_after`'s `list_local` section and `tests/cases/control_flow/hoist_nonvalue_read_after_loop`'s `two_loop_list_sibling`. **Fix shape:** give the hoisted bind site the same Array slot when the resolution says Array -- the slot is value storage either way, so this is a slot-type question, not a new flavor. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud) A `String` local is not recognised as the owning root of a yielded view, while the `str` and `bytes` twins are.** [`string-local-not-view-root-for-yield`] `def g(s: str) -> Iterator[StrView]: v = String(s); yield v` is rejected with *Cannot return StrView referencing a local or temporary; use str or String to return an owned copy* -- the spelling the diagnostic recommends is the one that fails. The `str` twin (`v = s.strip()`) and the `bytes` twin (`v = b + b"xy"`) both compile and print the CPython answer, and a `String` local is the same owning frame field they are: the frame owns the buffer for the frame's whole lifetime, so a view of it is as valid a yield root. `_local_has_borrowable_storage` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) admits a VALUE-typed local as a view root only when `view_family_for_type` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) names its family, and that lookup ends in `_VIEW_OWNED_QNAME_TO_FAMILY`, keyed on the family's owned qname alone (`builtins.str`, `builtins.bytes`) -- so `String`, a value type in neither key, falls out. Probe `/tmp/agents/r6_verify/m6_string.py`, verified 2026-09-17. Fix shape: ask the family's own membership predicate (`ViewTypeFamily.is_any_member` / `promote_param_match`, which already recognise `String` and `ByteArray`) at this site instead of the owned-qname table. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (hidden copy, no diagnostic; contradicts the language model) A generator / `async def` frame stores a bare `str`/`bytes` PARAMETER as OWNED storage, so the argument is copied into the frame although the caller already keeps it alive for the frame's whole lifetime.** [`generator-frame-copies-str-param`] `def gen_str(s: str) -> Iterator[int32]` takes the view the language model prescribes at the factory (`__gen_gen_str gen_str(std::string_view s)`) and then copies it into an owned frame field, while the record parameter of its sibling `def gen_cell(c: Cell) -> Iterator[int32]` is held by reference:
  ```cpp
  struct __gen_gen_str : public ::tpy::next_iter_mixin<__gen_gen_str, int32_t> {
      int32_t __state;
      std::string s;                        // OWNED: a copy of the caller's view
      int32_t i;
      __gen_gen_str(std::string_view s_)
          : __state(S_INITIAL), s(std::string(s_)) {}
      ...
  };

  struct __gen_gen_cell : public ::tpy::next_iter_mixin<__gen_gen_cell, int32_t> {
      int32_t __state;
      const Cell& c;                        // BORROWED: no copy
      int32_t i;
      __gen_gen_cell(const Cell& c)
          : __state(S_INITIAL), c(c) {}
      ...
  };
  ```
  The caller already materializes a TEMPORARY argument into its own block for the loop's duration in BOTH cases, so the owned capture buys nothing and the `str` argument is copied twice:
  ```cpp
  {
      Cell __tmp_1 = Cell(5);
      auto __src_0 = ::tpyapp::q::gen_cell(__tmp_1);
      ...
  }
  {
      ::tpy::String __tmp_2 = (::tpy::str_concat("ab", "cdef"));
      auto __src_2 = ::tpyapp::q::gen_str(__tmp_2);
      ...
  }
  ```
  The language model says a `str` parameter IS a view -- `String` and `Own[str]` are the spellings that ask for owned storage -- so a frame must hold the parameter the way the sync signature receives it; the copy is a deviation from the declared type, not an implementation detail. The same shape covers the whole family: `bytes` renders `::tpy::Bytes b;` ctor-copied from `::tpy::BytesView b_`, `async def` renders `std::string s;` from `std::string_view s_`, and a `str | None` / `bytes | None` param copies into `std::optional<std::string>` from `std::optional<std::string_view>`.
  A frame cannot outlive the scope that materialized its arguments today: a generator cannot be RETURNED (`Protocol type 'Iterator' cannot be used as a return type. Only @dynamic protocols can be used as return types`) and cannot be stored in a FIELD (`Protocol type 'Iterator[int32]' cannot be used as a field type in 'Holder'. Protocols are only valid as function and method parameters`) -- both probed 2026-09-17. If a frame COULD escape, that is the borrow checker's job to warn or reject AT THE ESCAPE, exactly as it must for the `const Cell&` field above, which carries the identical exposure and is not copied -- never a reason to copy.
  Fix shape: hold `std::string_view` / `::tpy::BytesView` (and `std::optional<` those `>`) in the frame for a bare `str`/`bytes` param, which retires the owned-param-capture rule recorded in `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` (the "String Type Semantics" paragraph and the bytes view-deduction bullet). Then revisit the resumable-body rule stated in that same paragraph, which shrinks the "safe view" set for LOCALS sourced from those params: a view local sourced from a param is as safe in a frame as in a sync body once the param is itself a view. Release-blocking by its HIGH tag. Related: `BUGS.md#frame-view-arg-nonmaterializing-source`, the caller-side gap in that materialization (a slice or ternary source is not hoisted). Found 2026-09-17; witness `/tmp/agents/frame_param/q.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (does not compile, no diagnostic) A `def` inside an `if` is emitted as a lambda INSIDE that C++ block, so a call after the block is out of scope.** [`conditional-def-lambda-block-scoped`] A module-level `if True:` holding `def helper(t: str) -> StrView: ...`, then `helper("  padded  ")` after the block, emits into `__tpy_init`:
  ```cpp
  if (true) {
      auto helper = [](std::string_view t) -> std::string_view { ... };
  }
  ...
  std::cout << "p5:" << " " << helper("  padded value here  ") << ...
  ```
  and the C++ build fails with `'helper' was not declared in this scope`; the front end emits nothing. MODULE LEVEL is the only face left: the function-BODY spelling (`def main(): flag = True; if flag: def helper(x): ...` then `helper(1)` after the `if`) is now a located error naming the block, whether or not an outer binding of the name exists, so it can neither reach the C++ build nor silently call the outer function. That leaves this entry and `BUGS.md#module-level-block-scoped-def-not-declared` describing ONE defect from two sides -- a module-level `def` is a module function rather than a `TpyNestedDef`, so the block rule never sees it -- and they should be closed together. Same root cause (a branch-local `def` binds its name only from that statement on) and the same decided fix: reject the read at compile time as an error naming the block, rather than emitting a call to a block-scoped lambda. The C++ mis-scoping is also the `def` face of the borrow/reference-local hoisting gap filed above ("A borrow/reference local reused across sibling/outer scopes is declared in the inner C++ scope"): value locals hoist, these do not. Probed 2026-09-17 (`/tmp/agents/lready/p5_toplevel_nested.py`); the function-body face re-probed after the merge (`/tmp/agents/merge6/fnbody.py`, `modlevel.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud) A nested `def` returning a view of a CAPTURED enclosing name is rejected, while the enclosing body's own return of the same view is accepted.** [`nested-def-captured-view-return-rejected`] `def outer(p: str): o = p[1:]` then `def inner() -> StrView: return o` fails with `Cannot return StrView referencing a local or temporary; use str or String to return an owned copy`, although `o` views `p`, which outlives both calls -- and the same `return o` written in `outer` itself (declared `-> StrView`) compiles and is sound. A captured PARAMETER is rejected the same way (`def inner_param() -> StrView: return p`); the nested def's OWN parameter is accepted, so the rule is "captured name", not "any name". Mechanism: `_name_is_param_or_global` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) asks `ctx.func.current_function`, which during a nested-def body is the NESTED def -- a captured enclosing name is neither its parameter nor a module global, so `is_dangling_return`'s `TpyName` arm falls through to its fail-closed `return True`. The position of the binding changes the answer here because the check's notion of a durable root is scoped to one function, unrelated to the one-type-one-storage rule for locals. Fix shape: let the durability question walk the enclosing-function chain for a captured name (an enclosing param, and an enclosing view local whose own root is durable, are both durable for a NON-escaping closure), keeping the reject for an escaping one. Probed 2026-09-17 (`/tmp/agents/lready/p1_alias.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (does not compile, no diagnostic) An operator dunder that returns a BORROW is emitted const-only, so nothing can be written through its result.** [`borrow-returning-operator-dunder-render`] `def __add__(self, o: Acc) -> Acc: return self if self.n >= o.n else o` then `c = a + b` / `c.n = 9` is accepted by the front end and fails the C++ build with *assignment of member 'Acc::n' in read-only object*; CPython makes `c` the operand itself, so the write reaches `a`. The same body under a plain method name emits `Acc& rec_m(...)` and works. The hoisted-holder spelling (`holder = Rec(0)` / `holder = b + 1` against `friend const Rec& operator+(const B& lhs, int32_t k)`) fails with *invalid conversion from 'const Rec*' to 'Rec*'* for the same reason. Cause: `IMPLICIT_READONLY_METHODS` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) stamps `is_readonly` by NAME at registration (`tpyc/sema/registration.py`), before any body fact exists, so the const projection `infer_method_const` avoids for a borrow-returning method is applied anyway. Three dunders were fixed for exactly this -- `__getitem__`, `__deref__`, `__span__` get a mutable + const overload pair -- but through a SECOND name-keyed set, `IMPLICIT_AUTO_READONLY_METHODS`, rather than by the return shape (`_apply_implicit_auto_readonly`, `tpyc/sema/method_expansion.py`, already keys on `rtype.is_value_type()`); the arithmetic, reflected and unary dunders and `__copy__` (~20 names) never joined it. Broken the same way, measured 2026-09-20: `-> Optional[Rec]` (`const Rec*`), `-> list[Rec]` (`const std::vector<Rec>&`), unary `__neg__`. **Fix shape:** drop the second set and give the overload pair to every implicitly-readonly dunder whose return is a reference type; the `operator+` friend shims (`_gen_binary_operators` / `_gen_unary_operators`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/records.py`) need the clone-pair split `_gen_deref_operators` already does, with the receiver-constness axis on the shim's first parameter, or the two clones emit one signature twice. Four cases carry the const-only shim and change shape (`operators/op_borrow_return_alias`, `op_borrow_branch_hoist`, `op_readonly_borrow_return`, `returns/warn_return_record_borrow_dunder`); `op_borrow_return_alias`'s header states the const result as intended, but every leg of all four only READS through the result, so none exercises the write. An explicit `readonly[Acc]` return (`error_op_readonly_result_mutate`) must keep rejecting. A rule change to how dunder constness is decided, so its own unit, not a reject-queue row (user decision 2026-09-21). Probes `/tmp/agents/batch7/defects/t1_mutate.py`, `t1_sibs.py`. Found 2026-09-20. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, located; everyday shape) A container literal or comprehension whose ELEMENT slot is a view type admits no source at all.** [`view-element-slot-admits-no-source`] `def take(s: StrView): xs: list[StrView] = [s]` rejects `expr.container_literal`; so does the unannotated `xs = [b.name]` where `name` is a view getter (it infers `list[StrView]`), a dict value or set element of the same type, and `ys = [b.name for _ in range(2)]` (`expr.list_comp`, raised at the comprehension route for the same slot). A name, a parameter, a slice and a call are all refused: the `view` family of `_container_lit_elem_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) has no rows. 19 cells of the property sweep (15 literal, 4 comprehension). WORKAROUND: annotate the owning element type -- `xs: list[str] = [b.name]` renders `{std::string(b.name())}`. Deliberately NOT a lowering row: a view is a pointer into another buffer and the list can outlive it (returned, stored in a field, appended to after the source dies), and the blanket reject is what currently closes the AST-era hole the sibling entry below records (a temporary's view stored at exactly this slot). Admission is a lifetime question for the MIR; the alternative -- an unannotated `[view]` inferring the OWNING `list[str]` -- is a type-inference rule change with its own TODO design entry ("Should an unannotated container literal of views infer the owning element type?"). User decision 2026-09-21: not a batch row. Probes `/tmp/agents/batch7/ret_lit/`. Found 2026-09-20.
- **[HIGH small] (accepts invalid, C++ error) A MODULE-LEVEL `match` on a pointer-repr `Optional[record]` global emits null tests against the POINTEE, so the program never builds.** [`module-level-optional-chain-derefs-subject`] `o: Optional[Cat] = mk()` at module level, then `match o:` / `case Cat(lives=1):` / `case None:` / `case Cat():` passes the front end and g++ reports *no match for 'operator!=' (operand types are 'Cat' and 'std::nullptr_t')*: a pointer-slot global reads as `(*o)`, so the subject alias binds `Cat&` while the `if_elif_optional` tier spells its arms `__match_subject_1 != nullptr` / `(*__match_subject_1)` for the pointer repr. No capture is involved -- the three-arm program above has none. The function-parameter, method, constructor and field-source (`match h.pet:`) spellings of the same match all build and run. Site: `_lower_match_optional_chain` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`) derives its null/has-value pieces from `subj_type.uses_pointer_repr()`, which answers for the TYPE, while the subject's spelling comes from the name lowering's global-slot deref (`lc.prescan.global_slots`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`). Workaround: bind the global to a local (`v = o`) and match that, or move the match into a function. The whole-subject capture arm is fenced off this shape explicitly (the `subject_derefs` gate added 2026-09-20 with the pointer-repr capture), so only the non-capture arms reach the bad render. **Fix shape:** the tier's condition pieces belong to the lowered SUBJECT's form, not to the declared type -- take them from the same place the subject spelling comes from, so a global-slot subject either derefs consistently or is rejected with a located message. Found 2026-09-20 measuring the pointer-repr capture row.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; everyday shape) A whole-subject capture of a VALUE-repr non-scalar `Optional` (`Optional[str]`, `Optional[bytes]`) rejects, where the pointer-repr record twin binds.** [`match-optional-value-repr-full-capture`] `def pick(s: Optional[str]) -> str:` / `match s:` / `case "a": ...` / `case v:` with `if v is None:` in the arm errors *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.match)*. The capture is sema's `binds_full_optional`, so the name is the whole `str | None`, and `_lower_match_optional_chain` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`) has a local render for exactly two families: the SCALAR value-opt (`_value_opt_scalar`, which covers `Optional[int32]` and friends) and -- since 2026-09-20 -- the pointer-repr one, which binds the raw `T*`. A value-repr non-scalar has neither: its storage form is `std::optional<std::string>` and the arm would have to declare that slot and keep the body's reads on the value-opt renders. The sibling table: `Optional[int32]` compiles, `Optional[Cat]` compiles, `Optional[list[int32]]` never reaches the arm (its class pattern is refused by sema first), `Optional[str]` rejects at every position (function, method, ctor, generator, async, module). Workaround: split the arm -- `case None: ...` then `case str() as v:` -- which binds the inner value and compiles today. Pinned by `tests/cases/match/error_optional_full_capture_value_repr`. **Fix shape:** the value-opt binding registry (`lc.value_opt_bindings` / `ValueOptKind`) gains the owning-slot kind the str/bytes family needs, so the arm declares `std::optional<std::string> v = <subject>;` and the body reads ride that kind rather than the scalar one; the admission then reads the kind instead of asking `_value_opt_scalar`. Found 2026-09-20 admitting the pointer-repr twin.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; everyday shape) A `match` on a pointer-repr `Optional[record]` inside a generator or `async def` rejects as soon as an ARM SUSPENDS, whatever the subject is bound to.** [`match-optional-subject-in-suspending-arm`] `def gen(x: Optional[Cat]) -> Iterator[int32]:` / `match x:` / `case Cat(lives=1): yield 1` / `case None: yield 0` / `case Cat(): yield 2` errors *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.match)* at the `match`. Measured sibling table (2026-09-20, probes `/tmp/agents/batch7/matchimpl/bugprobe/m9_*.py`): the same body in a plain function compiles (`m9_sync.py`); the generator whose arms do NOT suspend -- assign in the arms, one `yield` after the `match` -- compiles (`m9_gen_nosusp.py`); an `async def` that awaits BEFORE the match compiles (`m9_async.py`); and an `async def` whose ARM awaits rejects (`m9_async_susp.py`). Workaround: compute the answer in a non-suspending `match` and suspend after it. **Fix shape:** the subject read is the frame's own pointer field, so the route's `pointers` reject should become a read of the frame binding the resumable admission already recorded, not a blanket refusal. Found 2026-09-20.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) Three `match` capture shapes on the RECORD tier reject: an rvalue subject under a pointer hoist, its re-seating sibling, and an `opt_storage` hoist with an lvalue subject.** [`match-capture-shape-rvalue-and-opt-storage`] All three are `stmt.match:match.capture_shape` from `_lower_match_record` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`), and all three are legal Python the deleted AST emitter rendered. (1) The hoist kind is FUNCTION-wide -- sema's borrow fact comes from a LATER lvalue match on the same name -- while this match's subject is an `Own`-returning call, so the pointer hoist meets an rvalue subject (`scripts/thir_migration/review/probes/match/r1873_ptr_hoist_rvalue_first.py`). (2) A sibling match on an `Own`-returning call re-seats a capture an earlier match pointer-hoisted: `match c: case Cat() as q:` then `match mk(): case Cat() as q:` (`q1881_reuse_rvalue_own.py`). (3) An `opt_storage` hoist with an LVALUE subject -- `match c: case Cat() as q:` where `q` is later assigned `q = mk()`, making it ever-owned (`r1889_opt_storage_lvalue.py`). The DIRECT alias `m = h.peek_ro()` is right (`const Mid& m = ...`), so the fact is available -- it just does not travel through the field hop: `_f1_const_rooted_source` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) stops at a call node, and `_expr_is_const_source`'s method-call arm is only consulted when the call IS the init, not when it is the init's receiver. The REF_ALIAS twin (`j = h.peek_ro().jar`) would emit `Jar& j = h.peek_ro().jar;` and fail the same way, which is why it is held out of the borrow-alias rung that admits the mutable flavour. - **[MED medium] (rejects valid, located; everyday shapes) Argument and receiver shapes THIR batch 7 stopped on and pinned as `error_` cases.** [`batch7-everyday-arg-rejects`] Each row of the batch admitted the temp-free half of a slot and left the half below rejecting; every one names its construct and line, none miscompiles, and the workaround is the same throughout -- bind the argument to a local first. (1) FIXED 2026-09-28: a container-returning CALL at a qualified (static / class) callee's container slot, `Holder.take_list(mk())`, hoists like the free call, since the qualified call lowers its arguments through the free call's argument path. (2) A narrowed `Optional` FIELD at a pointee slot, `if b.items is not None: take(b.items)` -> `call.arg_shape.container`; the narrowed LOCAL compiles in all eight callee families -- the narrowing fact the row reads is recorded for names only (`calls/error_arg_narrowed_opt_field`). (3) A container LITERAL at a MUTATED slot of a NESTED constructor, `Rc.new(Box(KMut([1, 2])))` -> `call.ctor_arg.container` (`calls/error_ctor_nested_mutated_literal`); the direct constructor's temporaries -- `ListTaker(copy(w.items))`, `ListTaker(mk())` -- hoist a named temp since the rvalue-call hoist row became record-or-container (`calls/ctor_mutated_slot_field_arg`). (4) A non-empty literal at a `readonly[container]` CONSTRUCTOR parameter, `Numbers([1, 2, 3])` -> `call.ctor_arg.container`; the free-function twin compiles, the method twin compiles (`readonly/error_readonly_container_literal_ctor_arg`). (5) A dict or set LITERAL at a generic callee's mutated container slot, `take_dict(1, {"b": 2})` -> `call.generic_arg_shape`; the list literal has a hoisting cell there (`calls/error_generic_call_dict_literal_arg`); a dict or set literal at a READ-ONLY generic slot rejects the same way, `size_of({"a": 1})` with `def size_of[K, V](d: dict[K, V]) -> int` (probe `/tmp/agents/bundle3/row5/impl/probes/dict_ro.py`, `set_ro.py`, 2026-09-28). (6) FIXED: the borrow declaration is a flush point like every other statement, so `got = k.pick([3, 4])` hoists the literal (`calls/method_literal_arg_mutable_slot`); its record twin `got = k.pick(R(3))` still rejects at `method.arg_shape` -- the record ctor rvalue has no hoisting cell at a mutable METHOD slot where the container literal has one. (9) `with mk().guard() as g:` -> `stmt.with`: a borrow-returning method binds the manager borrowed, so a TEMPORARY receiver would not outlive the block; the `@property` twin rejects the same way and a named receiver compiles (`records/error_method_off_temporary_receiver_with`). Fix shape for 3, 5, 6, 7: one flush position threaded to the arg gate of every callee family, so the hoisting row the free family has is reachable everywhere (the arg family sweep, `scripts/thir_migration/review/arg_family_sweep.py`, measures the 213 rows that still disagree across families); 2 needs the field-narrowing fact on the THIR read; 9 needs the receiver temp hoisted over the block. Listed 2026-09-22 at the batch's readiness gate.

- **[LOW small] (latent: the METHOD form of a borrow-returning call still binds a CONTAINER temporary inline, the shape g++ `-Wdangling-reference` flags on a free call) A method call returning a borrow of one argument, with a container literal at ANOTHER argument, renders the literal as a brace temporary inside the bound call.** [`borrow-call-container-temp-dangling-warning`] `def ro_other(self, ys: readonly[list[Rec]], xs: readonly[list[int32]]) -> readonly[Rec]: return ys[0]` called as `got = t.ro_other(src, [9, 9, 9])` emits `const Rec& got = t.ro_other(src, {9, 9, 9});` -- correct, since `got` aliases `src[0]`, which outlives the statement. - **[MED medium] (rejects valid + loud C++ build failures) A fresh reference-type argument to a base initializer is rejected -- `super().__init__([])`, `super().__init__(mk(n))`, a fresh record over container arguments (`super().__init__(Tag(["a"]))`) and the like; the workarounds are taking the value as a parameter of the child's `__init__` and forwarding it by name, or skipping the call and assigning the fields (a warned divergence). The fix is queued first in line (TODO.md "Fold the target-less base-init arg rows").** [`base-init-args-separate-lowering`] A `super().__init__(...)` / `Parent.__init__(self, ...)` argument lowers only through `_base_init_arg_ok`'s rows (`tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`: scalars, str literals / concats / f-strings / conversions, parameter names by family, a scalar-argument record constructor), which render it bare with no parameter in view; the ordinary constructor call decides each argument against its parameter (`_lower_ctor_call_args`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`). (a) Rejected at `ctor.base_init`, whatever the parameter's form: a fresh reference-type argument -- a container literal (`super().__init__([])`, `{n, 2}`), a call's by-value or `Own[T]` result (`super().__init__(mk(n))`), a constructor call over a non-scalar argument (`Tag(["a"])`), a comprehension, `[0] * n` -- a call returning `str` (`super().__init__(mk(n))` with `mk(n: int32) -> str`, at a `str` or a `StrView` parameter, `/tmp/agents/docsync_r4/strcall.py`), and a call returning a reference (`super().__init__(s.get())`). (b) Build failure, g++'s error shown to the user: a borrowed `ys: list[int32]` forwarded to an `Own[list[int32]]` parameter renders `: Base(ys)` against `Base(std::vector<int32_t>&& xs)` (`/tmp/agents/tc_own/main2.py`; CPython aliases `ys` into the base), an `Own[Payload]` parameter `q` forwarded to an `Own[Payload]` parameter renders `: Base(q)` with no move (`/tmp/agents/superinit_e4/ownrec.py`), and a `str` parameter forwarded to an `Own[str]` parameter passes the `std::string_view` to the `std::string` slot (`/tmp/agents/cgc3/own_str.py`); a borrowed `Payload` parameter at an `Own[Payload]` slot fails the same way. Of the named forwards to an `Own[T]` parameter, only the child's own `Own[list[int32]]` / `Own[str]` parameter is rejected cleanly at `ctor.base_init` (`/tmp/agents/tc_own/main.py`); a scalar (`Own[int32]`) works. Also a build failure: `_base_init_arg_ok`'s scalar-constructor row admits `super().__init__(Payload(x))` whatever the parameter and renders the bare prvalue, which g++ rejects at a pointer-form parameter -- a union of reference types (`v: A | B`, no `Base(A)` overload, `/tmp/agents/cgc/uni.py`) or `Optional[record]` (`/tmp/agents/cgc/optp2.py`) -- and at a `T&` parameter the base mutates (cannot bind an rvalue, `/tmp/agents/docsync_r4/mutrec.py`); at a `const T&` or `Own[T]` parameter it compiles and runs. CPython runs every one. `[0] * n` is not lowered as an ordinary constructor argument either (`A([0] * 3)` rejects at `call.ctor_arg.container`, `/tmp/agents/tcov_e2/rep1.py`). Fix shape: the base-init cell takes the ctor-call argument dispatch, with one fact saying whether the parameter keeps the argument (an `arg_lend_ok`-style verdict in place of per-table slot guards) and a place for temporaries at the member-init position -- a mutated `T&` parameter binds only a named temporary, and a view parameter needs a home that lives as long as the object (the record-view-field provenance question of BUGS.md#record-view-field-escapes-local-buffer); TODO.md "Fold the target-less base-init arg rows". Requirement for that unification: a fresh value at a base parameter the base MUTATES must keep rejecting or bind a named temporary, never a bare prvalue -- the case that guarded it was reverted, so the fix re-adds one. Pinned by `inheritance/error_base_init_container_rvalue` (fresh value at a `T&` parameter) and `inheritance/error_base_init_fresh_view_slot` (fresh value at a view parameter). Repros `/tmp/agents/sm_r2/p1.py`, `p3.py`, `p8.py`, `/tmp/agents/cgc/uni.py`, `optp2.py`, `borrowret.py`, `/tmp/agents/cpyparity_r2/p5.py`, `p6.py`, `p16.py`, `/tmp/agents/tcov_e2/comp.py`, `rep.py`, `/tmp/agents/superinit_e4/fresh/`. The second workaround, skipping the call and assigning the inherited fields in the child, always warns ("'Tag.__init__' does not call 'super().__init__(...)'; TPy default-constructs the 'Labeled' part instead"), even when the child assigns every inherited field, so no initialized state differs from CPython's; the skip check counts calls, not assigned fields (`/tmp/agents/rev_skipwarn/p9.py`). Probe `/tmp/agents/rev_skipwarn/p10.py`. Found 2026-09-28 by the skipped-base warning review.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, located) Arguments passed through an `__init__`-less parent whose own field has no default are rejected.** [`init-forwarding-no-default-field`] `class B(A): y: int32` under `class A: def __init__(self, x: int32)`, then `class C(B): def __init__(self): super().__init__(5); self.y = 1`: C++ `B` cannot inherit `A`'s constructors (`using A::A;` would leave `y` for the caller to read uninitialized), so `B` is built by its default constructor alone and the argument has nowhere to go; the message names the reason and the fix ("give 'B' an '__init__' or a default for 'y'"). The other reasons `_find_unique_init_parent` (`tpyc/sema/registration.py`) refuses to inherit -- a bare generic base, an `__init__`-less base of its own -- reject the same way, naming their own reason. CPython runs `A.__init__` through `B`, and `C().y` then reads the value the child assigned. Fix shape: an inherited constructor that takes the ancestor's arguments and leaves the field for the child to assign -- a design question for the placeholder rules. The check keys on the direct base the call constructs, so naming the ancestor instead (`A.__init__(self, 5)` from `C(B)`), or a multi-base `super()` / named call through such a base, is rejected the same way. Pinned by `inheritance/error_init_forwarding_no_default_field`, for the named-ancestor spelling `inheritance/error_init_forwarding_named_ancestor`, and, for the `__init__`-less base of its own, `inheritance/error_init_forwarding_base_without_init`. Repro `/tmp/agents/tcov_e2/fld.py`. Found 2026-09-26 by the parent-initializer review.

Probe `/tmp/agents/tail_sema/br2.py`. A field whose type `T()` cannot build with no arguments (a record whose `__init__` requires arguments, a union) is rejected at the split point instead ("has no default constructor"), although every branch assigns it (probe `/tmp/agents/tail_sema/br.py`). Fix shape: skip the diagnostic when flow analysis proves the field definitely assigned by the end of the body (the TODO.md item "Every declared field without a class-level default must be assigned").
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, located, pre-existing) An aggregate's zero-argument `Record()` is rejected when a field of a record type with a required-argument `__init__` has no default.** [`aggregate-nocopy-field-zero-arg-rejected`] `class Handle: def __init__(self, id: int32)` and `class Agg: h: Handle; n: int32 = 3`, then `Agg()`, rejects "'Agg()' cannot be constructed without arguments: field 'h' of type 'Handle' has no default value" (the same with `Handle` `@nocopy`); CPython runs it and leaves `h` unset (`print(a.n)` prints `3`). An `int32` field without a default is accepted and zero-initialized instead, so the rule is `_is_default_constructible` (`tpyc/sema/protocols.py`) asking whether TPy can build a fully initialized value, which is stricter than CPython's `T()` for an aggregate. Same on master. Fix shape: a design question -- admit it and leave the field to its C++ default constructor where one exists, or keep rejecting and say CPython differs (the constructor split-point check rejects the same field left unset by an `__init__`). Probe `/tmp/agents/tail_sema/agg.py`.

So does a dataclass base whose fields all have defaults, whose synthesized `__init__` is its default constructor and runs: with `x: int32 = 0`, `y: int32 = 1`, `z: int32 = 2`, `print(C())` prints `C(x=0, z=2)` where CPython prints `C(y=1, x=0, z=2)` (`/tmp/agents/rev_skipwarn/p12.py`).
