Found 2026-09-28 by the placeholder review.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, indeterminate read, no diagnostic) A walrus target bound inside a comprehension is read after the comprehension as if assigned, though an empty comprehension never binds it.** [`comprehension-walrus-read-after-empty`] `ys = [y for x in xs if (y := x * 2) > 100]` then `print(y)` with `xs == []` prints an indeterminate `int32` (`1739944528` on the branch, `-2000309680` on master `c854c7b482`) where CPython raises `UnboundLocalError`. The `ValueType` face (`(y := Noisy(x)).n > 100`, then `print(y.n)`) reads the placeholder's indeterminate field on the branch (`-2039111080`); master rejects that face at `expr.walrus`. A `ValueType` slot is now value-initialized (`Ref r{};`), so that face reads the zeros / null `Ptr` of a field-wise default constructor, or whatever an `__init__` callable without arguments set, instead of garbage; a bare scalar slot (`int32_t y;`) still reads indeterminate storage (`/tmp/agents/ready_vt/sup.py`, `walrus.py`). Either way the read stays a divergence: CPython raises. Definite assignment treats the comprehension's walrus target as bound after it; a comprehension that runs zero iterations (or whose filter never evaluates the walrus) leaves it unbound. The same class as BUGS.md#with-suppress-read-unassigned and BUGS.md#finally-read-unassigned-on-exception. Fix shape: a name bound only by a walrus inside a comprehension is maybe-unassigned after it (reject the read, `variable 'y' may not be assigned at this point`). Repros `/tmp/agents/br_safety/p18.py`, `/tmp/agents/docs_vt/p18vt.py`. Found 2026-09-25.
- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no diagnostic) A mixed union local initialised from a `ValueType` record name aliases that name, so a later rebind of the name shows through the union.** [`mixed-union-local-aliases-value-record`] `c = Coord(1); u: Coord | Node = c; c = Coord(9); show(u)` with `class Coord(ValueType)` and a plain `class Node` renders `::tpy::Union<Coord*, Node*> u{&(c)};`, so the rebind `c = Coord(9)` writes the slot `u` points at and `show(u)` prints `coord 9` where CPython prints `coord 1`. The tuple twin `t = (c, 1); c = Coord(8)` copies and matches CPython. The reference-record source (`c = Node(1)` rebound) and the scalar source (`u: int32 | Node = c` with `c` rebound) reject at `decl.ptr_union_source` on both trees, so only the value-record source reaches the `&(c)` render; a `ValueType` alternative is a value, so the union should hold a copy of it (or the source should reject like its twins). Identical on master `c854c7b482`. Repros `/tmp/agents/br_safety/p12.py`, `/tmp/agents/br_safety/p13.py` (scalar twin), `/tmp/agents/docs_vt/p12n.py` (reference twin). Found 2026-09-25.
- **[LOW small] (wrong output, CPython divergence) argparse `--help` never wraps help text and aligns it past column 24.** [`argparse-help-no-wrap`] The renderer in `lib/tpy/argparse.py` pads every row to the longest signature plus two, so one long signature (`--render {half,quad,sextant,octant,braille}`) pushes every help text to column 47, and each text stays on one line however long. CPython caps the help column at 24 (`max_help_position`), moves the help of a longer signature to the next line, and wraps every text to the terminal width (`COLUMNS`, 80 in the cpy phase). The same renderer prints `description=` and `epilog=` as written, where CPython's default formatter reflows them into paragraphs (only `RawDescriptionHelpFormatter` keeps their line breaks), so a multi-line description matches CPython only under that class. Found 2026-09-26 on a game CLI; repro: any `help=` longer than a line.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Returning or yielding a dict view is a lowering reject in every position, although CPython runs every one (spelled `KeysView[...]`).** [`dict-view-return-yield-rejected`] `def keys_of(d: dict[str, int32]) -> dict_keys[str, int32]: return d.keys()` stops with `this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return:return.slot_type)`, and so do the view of a global dict and a view returned inside a tuple; a generator yielding the view of a PARAMETER dict stops at `res.yield_type`. The lifetime rule is already in sema -- a view rooted in a local or a temporary is rejected before lowering (`tests/cases/view_lifetime/error_return_dict_view_local`) -- so what is missing is only the lowering of a dict view at a return or yield slot. Planned as unit 7 of the `collections.defaultdict` work (dict views as first-class values). CPython runs these functions only with the `typing.KeysView` / `ValuesView` / `ItemsView` return spelling: `dict_keys` is not a CPython builtin name, so `-> dict_keys[str, int32]` raises `NameError` at the `def` under CPython 3.12, and TPy does not accept the `KeysView` spelling yet (TODO.md, "as aliases for the dict views"). Probe `/tmp/agents/nbv2/dvret.py`, verified 2026-09-24.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) `copy_iter(xs)` over an UNANNOTATED literal-initialized local renders its element type argument as the literal's value.** [`copy-iter-literal-local-type-arg`] `xs = [1, 2, 3]; ys: list[int32] = []; ys.extend(copy_iter(xs))` (and `list(copy_iter(xs))`) emits `::tpy::copy_iter<1>(xs)`, which g++ rejects ("type/value mismatch at argument 1"); `xs: list[int32] = [1, 2, 3]` renders `copy_iter<int32_t>` and runs. The element type reaching the `copy_iter` template argument is still the pending integer-literal type of the inferred local, rendered as its value instead of `int32_t`. The for-head literal form (`for x in copy_iter([1, 2, 3])`) is a located reject (`tests/cases/list/error_copy_iter_literal_elements`); this named-local form reaches the C++ compiler. Probe `/tmp/agents/nbv2/ci.py` (`ci2.py` is the annotated twin), identical with and without the `CopyIter` stub, 2026-09-24. The combinator face (`list(enumerate(ws))` over a float-literal local) was fixed 2026-09-28 when generic inference started resolving float-literal bindings; this `copy_iter` face takes its element type argument through the special builtin path rather than the generic binding map and still reproduces (`/tmp/agents/bundle3/row5/cells4/copy_iter_int.py`, 2026-09-28). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent CPython divergence) `sorted()` copies reference elements with no warning, over a named list and an iterator alike.** [`sorted-ref-element-copy-unwarned`] `cs = [C(2), C(1)]; s = sorted(cs, key=key); cs[1].v = 99; print(s[0].v)` prints `1` under TPy and `99` under CPython, and `tpyc` emits nothing; `list(cs)` of the same list warns `copies C elements`. `sorted`'s stub (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_funcs.py`) takes `Iterable[T]` and returns `Own[list[T]]`, so the argument never reaches the element-copy gate the container constructors, `extend`, `+=` and slice assignment share (their `Iterable[Own[T]]` parameter, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`). A user iterable of records (`sorted(rb, key=...)`) has the same face (`/tmp/agents/dd/r46/parity/p3b.py`). Verified 2026-09-26: the stub change alone makes the warning fire, but its remedy `sorted(copy_iter(rs))` rejects at `call.native_arg.call_rvalue`, so this is blocked on `BUGS.md#sorted-of-iter-call`; land the two together (repros `/tmp/agents/dd/mgi/r5/sorted_rec.py`, `sorted_nokey.py`). - **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A generic `Span[T]` function called with a `Span[readonly[Node]]` of a reference element spells its type argument `val_or_ref<const Node>`.** [`generic-span-readonly-ref-elem-type-arg`] `def gtotal[T](xs: Span[T]) -> int32: return len(xs)` called as `sp: Span[readonly[Node]] = xs; gtotal(sp)` emits `gtotal<::tpy::val_or_ref<const Node>>(sp)`, and g++ rejects it ("could not convert `sp` from `span<const Node>` to `span<val_or_ref<const Node>>`"). - **[MED small] (rejects valid code, located) A `@native` record's constructor call cannot be returned directly -- THIR rejects it at a return.** [`native-ctor-return-unlowered`]

  asks `_ctor_shape_ok` without `native_ok`, so the native ctor face opened at
  the decl slot, the ctor MIL and the Own-arg row stays shut here. Fix shape:
  pass `native_ok` on the return slot's ctor face (the render reads the
  record's nativeness, so no new render arm), with a snapshot case and the
  `error_` pin. Opening it must wait for (or land with) the view-constructor
  borrow rule in TODO.md ("View constructors borrow their arguments"): for a

- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free, no diagnostic) A conditional of two frame-factory calls as the iterable of a `for` inside a generator / `async def` seats each call's temporary argument in the loop's `case` block, while the frame the loop drives lives on a frame field.** [`frame-select-factory-temp-in-case-block`] `for x in (one(A(4)) if flag else one(A(9))):` in a generator body (with `def one(p: A) -> Iterator[int]` that suspends before reading `p`) renders `std::optional<A> __tmp_1; std::optional<A> __tmp_2; __for_src_0.emplace(((flag) ? (__tmp_1.emplace(A(4)), one((*__tmp_1))) : ...));` -- the `__tmp_N` are locals of the resume `case` block and `__for_src_0` is a frame field, so the sub-frame reads a dead `A` after the first suspension. `--debug` exits 139 for the scalar form and for the tuple-element form `for x in (pair((A(4), r)) if flag else pair((A(9), r))):` alike; CPython prints `41`, `44`. A plain (non-conditional) factory call at the same position seats its temporary on a frame field, which is the rule the select arms miss: the conditional-operand arg-temp banking (`std::optional` locals, `argtemp.cond_*`) is the statement-level mechanism, and in a resumable body the bank has to be a frame field too. The tuple form compiled at the parent of `e901253c13` only because the handle was drained inside the expression; it now takes the scalar rule. Decided 2026-09-26: keep the reject; `tests/cases/tuple/error_frame_tuple_temp_element_no_statement_slot` pins the tuple-element form at an `assert`.   with `def bump(r: Rec) -> int32: r.n += 100; return r.n` mutates `rs`'s

  key slot of `sorted` runs on sorted's private copy of each element:
  TPy prints `[101, 103] [3, 1]` where CPython prints
  `[101, 103] [103, 101]`. At `min` / `max` the same key is a g++ error
  (`Rec&` param, called on `const T&`). A key LAMBDA and a class name
  at the key slot (`key=Key`, whose `__init__` mutates its argument)
  take const params, so their mutation is a g++ error too
  (`binding reference of type 'Rec&' to 'const Rec'`), not a TPy one.
  Design direction: a callable-effect contract -- "does not mutate
  through parameter 0" -- on the key slot, checked after the Phase-2
  fixpoint from the finalized mutation AND escape facts (the precedent
  is `finalize_borrow_checks`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`), with the body
  analysed at the ordinary `T`. Typing the param `readonly[T]` is not
  it: declared-only readonly would refuse `r.score()`, `helper(r)`,
  `Key(r)` and `-x`, which do not mutate. Related debt: the key-slot
  mode itself is keyed on the builtin names `sorted` / `min` / `max`
  in sema (`_flatten_key_kwarg`, `tpyc/sema/calls.py`), not on a fact
  of the slot. Probes `/tmp/agents/dd/keymode/s_mut_fnref.py`,
  `s_mut_fnref_min.py`, `s_mut_lam.py`, `s_callable_min.py`,
  `/tmp/agents/dd/rev1/p3b.py`, `p3c.py`. Found 2026-09-25. Needs
  `/tpy-add-feature` (the contract) and `/tpy-fix-bug`.

  mutated before `score`'s readonly-ness is known and nothing revisits

- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud) A borrow of an `Rc` / `Arc` payload reached through a TEMPORARY handle is rejected, although the payload outlives the handle.** [`shared-handle-payload-through-temp-rejected`]

  generic result slot, `map(lambda c: c.rc.clone().get(), cs)`, errors
  "Cannot return a borrow of a temporary from this lambda" (the
  lambda was accepted, and ran correctly, before that reject landed).
  The clone dies at the end of the call, but the payload it points at
  is kept alive by `c.rc`, so CPython (and a correct render) hands out
  the shared payload. Both checks follow `get`'s recorded borrow of
  `self` into the temporary receiver, and nothing tells a SHARED handle
  (`Rc`, `Arc`, `Weak`), whose payload lives in a separately owned
  cell, from an OWNING one (`Box`, whose payload dies with it) -- both
  are records with a `Ptr` field and a `__del__`. Fix shape: a TypeDef
  fact for a shared-ownership handle, read by the dangling-return walk
  and the lambda walk alike. Probes `/tmp/agents/ltb/r1/rc_def.py`
  (def), `/tmp/agents/safety-lam/rc.py` (lambda), 2026-09-27. Needs
  `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (internal compiler error) Binding a call of a recursive union alias crashes sema with `'tuple' object has no attribute 'name'`.** [`recursive-alias-call-ice`] `type Tree = Lf | list[Tree]` and `t = Tree(Lf(1))` (or `a = Tree([Lf(2)])`) inside a function stops the compile with `Internal error: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'name'` (a plain record `Lf` and a `ValueType` one alike); a non-recursive alias (`type U = Lf | int32; U(Lf(1))`) gets the located "Type alias 'U' is not callable" error. CPython rejects the call at run time (`'typing.TypeAliasType' object is not callable`), so the program is invalid either way, but TPy admits recursive-alias calls as wrapper constructors and crashes on the binding. The wrapper-constructor call (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`, the recursive-alias arm) records `FunctionInfo(params=[("value", union_type)])` -- a tuple where a `ParamInfo` belongs -- and the alias-rebind replay (`decide_rebind_storage` -> `_owned_args` -> `call_param_args`, `tpyc/sema/context.py`) reads `p.name` off it. Fix shape: build the parameter as a `ParamInfo`. Repros `/tmp/agents/split_rex/ice/main.py`, `ice2/main.py` (plain record), `ice4/main.py` (list argument), `/tmp/agents/rev_uninit_all/p6.py`. - **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) `open()` refuses its arguments by keyword.** [`builtin-open-keyword-args`] `open("b3.txt", mode="r")` errors *Keyword arguments not supported for builtin 'open'*; the positional `open("b3.txt", "r")` compiles. The builtin's `@dispatch` variants are `@native`, and the keyword path does not bind a `@native` builtin's parameters by name. CPython accepts `mode=`, `encoding=` and the rest by keyword. Repro `/tmp/agents/zlib/bugs/b3_open_mode_kw.py`. Found 2026-09-26.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic quality) A builtin file object stored into a field in a constructor warns that it copies, although the fresh result is moved.** [`builtin-file-field-ctor-rejected`] `self.fp = open(path, "rb")` with `fp: BinaryIO` (imported from `tpy`) warns *copies BinaryIO into field; use copy() to make this explicit* -- wrong, the fresh call result is moved (`fp(::tpy::builtin_open_binary(path, "rb"))`), and `BinaryIO` is move-only. The member-init itself lowers since the constructor took the field-write families. Without the `tpy` import, a bare `fp: BinaryIO` annotation (a `NameError` in CPython) resolves to a type that reports *Type mismatch in assignment: expected BinaryIO, got BinaryIO*, naming two different types by one name. Workaround: `io.FileIO(os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY))`, which `gzip` uses. Repros `/tmp/agents/zlib/bugs/b4_file_field.py`, `/tmp/agents/zlib/bugs/b4b_bare_binaryio.py`. Found 2026-09-26.

A t-string (`t"..."`) on the Python 3.12 the compiler runs under is the same face (`invalid syntax`). Repros `/tmp/agents/zlib/bugs/b6_syntax.py`, `/tmp/agents/vt_matrix/syn.py`. Found 2026-09-26 (by the zlib/gzip parity review); the duplicate entry `syntax-error-reported-as-internal-error` (2026-09-28) was folded in here and that slug is retired.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) `bytes` / `str` `strip`, `lstrip` and `rstrip` take no `chars` argument.** [`strip-chars-arg-missing`] `b"\x00\x00ab".lstrip(b"\x00")` and `"xxhixx".strip("x")` error *'lstrip' expects 0 argument(s), got 1*; only the no-argument whitespace form is declared (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_bytes.py`, `_types.py`). CPython prints `b'ab'` and `hi`. `gzip.decompress` spells CPython's `unused_data[8:].lstrip(b"\x00")` as a loop. Repro `/tmp/agents/zlib/bugs/b8_strip_chars.py`. Found 2026-09-26.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) A field passed straight to a structural-protocol parameter has no lowering.** [`field-arg-to-protocol-param-unlowered`] `n = first_len(self.fp)` with `def first_len(fp: Source)` over a `Protocol` stops at `stmt.var_decl:field.result_type`; `if first_len(self.fp) > 0:` stops at the same leaf through `stmt.if`, a generic `def first_len[F: Source](fp: F)` at `expr.call:call.generic_arg_slot`. Binding the field to a local first (`fp = self.fp; first_len(fp)`) compiles and runs. Hit in `gzip._GzipReader` (the header parser over the reader's padded file). Repro `/tmp/agents/zlib/bugs/b9_field_to_protocol.py`. Found 2026-09-26.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid code, loud) A `with` in a generator whose manager is a builtin or module-qualified CALL has no lowering.** [`with-call-manager-in-frame-unlowered`] `def lines(path) -> Iterator[str]: with open(path) as f: yield f.read()` stops at `res.with_manager`, and so does `with gzip.open(path) as f:`; a constructor (`with gzip.GzipFile(path) as f:`) and a same-module function returning `Own[T]` compile and run, as does the same `with open(...)` in a plain function. Streaming a file from a generator is an everyday shape. Neighbor of the queued field-read manager bin (`res_2004_with_field.py` in `scripts/thir_migration/review/bins_rest.json`), not the same shape. Repro `/tmp/agents/zlib/bugs/b10_with_call_gen.py`. Found 2026-09-26.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) Re-assigning a field from a module-qualified call that returns `Own[T]` has no lowering in a method.** [`field-assign-qualified-own-call-unlowered`] `self.d = zlib.decompressobj(-15)` in a method stops at `expr.method_call:method.qualcall.ret.record_f1`; the same assignment in `__init__` compiles, and so does a same-module helper returning `Own[zlib._Decompress]`, which `gzip._GzipReader` uses. Same reject leaf as `static-method-borrow-return-rejected`, different shape (an owned return, not a borrow). Repro `/tmp/agents/zlib/bugs/b11_field_qualified_ctor.py`. Found 2026-09-26.
- **[LOW small] (hidden copy, no diagnostic) A `bytes` slice passed to a `bytes` parameter is copied into an owned temporary.** [`bytes-slice-arg-copied`] `take(src[2:])` with `def take(b: bytes)` renders `take(::tpy::Bytes(::tpy::bytes_slice(src, ...)))`, although the parameter is a `::tpy::BytesView` the slice view could bind directly; the `str` twin renders `take(::tpy::str_slice(src, ...))` with no copy. The method form (`h.eat(src[3:])`) copies the same way. Hit per member by `gzip.decompress` (`do.decompress(rest[fp.tell():])`). The `view-not-copy` pitfall. Repro `/tmp/agents/zlib/r4/s.py` (str twin `t.py`). Found 2026-09-26 by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness).
- **[LOW small] (parity, rarely observable) The stdlib file objects check the closed state lazily in `__iter__`.** [`file-iter-closed-check-deferred`] `StringIO`, `BytesIO`, `io.BufferedReader` and `gzip.GzipFile` spell `__iter__` as a generator, so its closed check runs at the first `next()`: `iter(f)` on a closed file raises in CPython (`I/O operation on closed file.`) and returns an iterator in TPy; the first `next()` then raises. CPython file objects are their own iterators (`iter(f) is f`). Repro `/tmp/agents/zlib/review_parity/p_iter.py`. Found 2026-09-26 by /tpy-review (cpython-parity).
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid code, loud) A module-qualified constructor taking a freshly built `Own[T]` argument has no lowering.** [`qualified-ctor-own-arg-unlowered`] `io.BufferedReader(io.FileIO(fd))` stops at `expr.method_call:method.qualcall.arg.own`; `from io import BufferedReader, FileIO` then `BufferedReader(FileIO(fd))` compiles and runs. Repro `/tmp/agents/zlib/review_parity/p_qual.py`. Found 2026-09-26 by /tpy-review (cpython-parity).
- **[LOW small] (hidden copy, no diagnostic) A list literal of freshly built owned elements copies each element.** [`list-literal-owned-elem-initializer-copy`] `parts: list[bytes] = [bytes(src[1:])]` renders `std::vector<::tpy::Bytes> parts = {::tpy::Bytes(...)};`, a braced `std::initializer_list` init whose elements are const, so the vector copy-constructs each temporary instead of moving it (one extra allocation and memcpy per element); `parts = []` then `parts.append(bytes(src[1:]))` moves. The `make_vector` helper the moving container literal already uses (`subexpression-right-to-left-eval` names it) is the move-preserving render. `io.BufferedReader._fill` spells the append form for this reason. Repro `/tmp/agents/zlib/review2_cg/p_list.py`. Found 2026-09-27 by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness).
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output, pre-existing) A `match` pattern capture wider than a sibling arm's statement binding of the same name truncates.** [`match-capture-wider-than-arm-binding-truncates`] `case Cat(lives=v): print(v)` over an `int64` field, `case _: v = 3`, then `print(v)` prints `1410065408` inside the arm and after it (CPython `10000000000`): the name is hoisted before the `match` as `int32_t v` from the statement binding, and the capture is stored into it (`v = __case_0.lives;`). The capture is excluded from the sibling-arm join (`_enter_sibling_arm`, tpyc/sema/statements.py) and never asks the reassignment join; the capture-first order (`case Dog(): v = 3` after `case Cat(lives=v)`) is the same. Related: `BUGS.md#match-capture-reuses-local-unchecked` (a capture reusing a local bound BEFORE the `match`). Same on master `1ea64345ea`. Probe `/tmp/agents/rv4-parity/p/cap_arm.py`. Found by the review of the int/float hint/arm-join branch.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) The refusal of a binding that retypes a local an analyzed nested def, lambda or generator expression reads is order-blind.** [`captured-retype-refused-after-reader-ran`] It also fires when the reader has already run and never sees the wider value: `s = sum(i * n for i in range(5)); n = big`, `ys = [k + i for i in range(2)]` beside a consumed `(j + i for i in range(2))` then `j = big`, `apply(lambda v: v + n, 1); n = big`, and a nested def in the then-arm with `x = big` in the else-arm (`if c: x = 3; def g(): ...; g()` / `else: x = big`) -- programs master compiled and ran with CPython's output. Since the pending-integer-locals unit (2026-09-30) this is the documented order dependence of a literal-seeded local: a capture settles it from the stores seen so far (`docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` "Numeric widening across reassignments", current limitations), and a later wider store is refused naming the reader. The refusal keys on the capture site, not on whether the reader can run after the widening; knowing that is the whole-function slot fact of TODO.md "Whole-function slot and element facts" (fact C). Probes `/tmp/agents/rv4-parity/p/{gen_cap,comp_cap,lam_cap,cp_arm}.py`. Found by the review of the int/float hint/arm-join branch.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A None-seeded local's int inner type does not widen.** [`optional-int-widening-refused`] `x = None; x = 3; x = big` (`big: int64`) is refused with `Type mismatch in reassignment to 'x': expected int32, got int64`; CPython binds either value. The first value binding fixes the inner type (the "already optional" rule of `_resolve_reassignment_target_type_raw`, `tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`), where a local that was never None widens (`y = 3; y = big` makes it `int64`). Since sibling arms join, None-seeded `if` / `match` / `try` arms binding `3` and then an int64 are refused the same way (`x = None; if c: x = 3 else: x = big`; the wider-first order compiles); master `1ea64345ea` compiled those arm forms with CPython's output, because its arms did not see each other's bindings and the merge after the statement widened. Workaround: annotate `x: int64 | None`. A join of the inner type was built on the int/float hint/arm-join branch and backed out: it widens the slot after uses typed it at the narrower type, which truncates across a loop back edge (`x = None; x = a`, then a loop printing `x + 1` under `if x is not None:` before `x = big` printed `1410065409`) -- the slot fact of TODO.md "Whole-function slot and element facts" (fact C). Probes `/tmp/agents/r4b/p/{opt3,optarm2,optarm3,optwf}.py`, `/tmp/agents/rv4-cgc/p/loop.py`. Found by the review of the int/float hint/arm-join branch.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, unlocated) A method call on an empty dict literal filled by subscript stores fails with `Unknown type parameter 'K'` and no line number.** [`pending-dict-method-unknown-type-param`] `c = {}; c["a"] = 1` followed by `c.get("a")`, `c.pop("a")`, `c.setdefault("b", 2)`, `c.update({"b": 2})`, `c.items()` or `c.keys()` stops the compile with `error: Unknown type parameter 'K'` naming no line; CPython runs them, and `d: dict[str, int32] = {}` or `d = {"a": 1}` compiles. The dict is still pending at the call, and `extract_type_params` (`tpyc/modules/type_resolution.py`) maps K and V only for a concrete dict, so the method signature cannot be substituted. Binding K and V to the pending dict's key and value types was built on the int/float hint/arm-join branch and backed out: the method parameters then convert as if the element types were declared (`c = {}; c["a"] = 0.5; w = c.setdefault("b", 2)` printed `2.0`, as did a `get` / `pop` default), and a later wider store failed the C++ build (`c2 = {}; c2["a"] = 1; v = c2.get("a"); c2["z"] = big`). The fix needs the per-position element evidence of TODO.md "Whole-function slot and element facts" (fact A, `BUGS.md#inferred-container-store-converts`). Probes `/tmp/agents/rv4-parity/p/{pdict_mix,pdict_read}.py`, `/tmp/agents/rv4-cgc/p/{pd2,pd4}.py`, `/tmp/agents/r4b/p/kupd.py`. Found by the review of the int/float hint/arm-join branch.

- **[MED small] (silent lost output) A failed write to `sys.stdout` / `print` drops the output with no exception, and every write after it too.** [`stdout-write-error-silent`]
  `sys.stdout` wraps `std::cout` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/system.hpp`),
  so a short write sets the stream's badbit: nothing is raised and later
  writes are discarded until the program exits. CPython raises
  `BlockingIOError` (or `OSError`) at the failing write. Reached by
  `os.set_blocking(0, False)` on a terminal, where stdin and stdout share
  one open file: of 2 MB written to a slow pty reader only 12822 bytes
  arrived and the program exited 0. Repro `/tmp/agents/aw/hang/nb_repro.py`
  (run under a pty whose reader starts late). Found 2026-09-26 porting a
  terminal game.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; misleading message) A local bound to a list slice cannot be rebound to a list.** [`slice-local-rebind-rejected`]
  `ys = xs[1:]` then `ys = ["z"]` reports `Cannot take address of a
  temporary or expression in reassignment to 'ys'; assign to a variable
  first`. The first binding types `ys` as the `Span[str]` view a basic
  slice yields, so the list literal has nothing to point into; CPython
  just rebinds. The everyday shape is `argv = sys.argv[1:]` with a
  fallback `argv = ["--help"]`. The message names neither the view nor a
  way out (`list(...)` at the first binding, which itself rejects when the
  local is rebound: queued in
  `scripts/thir_migration/review/bins_rest.json`). Repro
  `/tmp/agents/aw/gaps2/slice_rebind_repro.py`. Found 2026-09-26.
- **[LOW small] (wrong output, CPython divergence) argparse reports a missing positional without naming it.** [`argparse-missing-positional-unnamed`]
  With `add_argument("data")` and no argument, TPy prints `error: missing
  required positional argument(s)`; CPython prints `error: the following
  arguments are required: data`. Found 2026-09-26 on a game CLI.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) argparse accepts an option's value only as the next argument: `-r8` and `--render=8` are refused.** [`argparse-attached-option-value`]
  Both fail with `error: unexpected positional argument: -r8` (and
  `--frames=5` the same), while `-r 8` and `--render 8` work. CPython takes
  the value attached to a short option and after `=` on a long one; both
  are everyday spellings. (Prefix abbreviation, `--fr 5` for `--frames`,
  is the separate `allow_abbrev` row of `docs/STDLIB_ROADMAP.md`.) The
  error also differs: CPython says `unrecognized arguments: ...`. Found
  2026-09-26 on a game CLI.

- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud) argparse refuses two options writing one `dest`.** [`argparse-shared-dest-rejected`]
  `add_argument("-r", "--render", choices=[...])` beside
  `add_argument("-8", dest="render", action="store_const", const="octant")`
  fails with `argparse: duplicate argument destination 'render'`. CPython
  lets several options set one attribute (shortcut flags, `--verbose` /
  `--quiet` pairs), the last one given winning. Found 2026-09-26 on a game
  CLI; repro `/tmp/agents/aw/gaps2/ap_digits.py`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A constructor cannot set a `bytes` field inside a `with` block.** [`ctor-field-set-in-with-block`]
  `def __init__(self, path: str) -> None: with open(path, "rb") as f:
  self.image = f.read()` fails with `field 'image' of type 'bytes' has no
  default constructor and is not initialized before the constructor body`;
  reading into a local inside the block and assigning the field after it
  compiles. CPython runs it. Repro
  `/tmp/agents/aw/gaps2/field_in_with_repro.py`. Found 2026-09-26.
- **[LOW small] (spurious warning) A local first bound in a `try` body and passed on to an `Own[T]` parameter after it warns `copies Big into owned storage`, though the emitted C++ moves it.** [`try-bound-own-move-false-copy-warning`]
  `try: b = Big() except ValueError: return` then `Holder(b)` with
  `Holder.__init__(self, b: Own[Big])` warns at the call, while the
  generated code is `Holder(std::move((*b)))` out of the hoisted
  `std::optional<Big>`; the same call after a plain binding neither warns
  nor copies. The warning pushes users to restructure code that is
  already right. Repro `/tmp/agents/aw/gaps2/try_move_repro.py`. Found
  2026-09-26.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; pre-existing for `if`, reached at `match` arms and `except` handlers by the sibling-arm join) A name an earlier sibling arm bound is not counted as assigned when a later arm binds it only inside a loop that provably runs.** [`carried-arm-name-loop-binding-unassigned`] `if k == 1: r = "one"; print(r); return` / `else: for i in range(1): r = "b"` then `print(r)` in the else arm errors *variable 'r' may not be assigned at this point* on master 40d90383db; CPython prints `b`. The same shape in a later `except` handler or `match` arm now errors too, because those arms carry the earlier arm's binding (`_enter_sibling_arm`, tpyc/sema/statements.py); a name FIRST bound in the loop body is counted assigned (`loop_bound_assigned`), a carried name rebound there is not. Probes `/tmp/agents/hj/loopcarry_if.py`, `/tmp/agents/rv6-cg/p4.py`. Found by the review of the int/float hint/arm-join branch.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught, pre-existing) A reassigned reference-type local takes a `const` pointer slot whenever ANY binding of its name in the function has a readonly source, so a mutation after a rebind to a mutable object fails the C++ build.** [`hoist-const-from-name-wide-borrow-bit`] `y = ro` (a `readonly[list[int]]`) then `y = xa; y.append(9)` renders `const std::vector<...>* y = &(ro); y = &(xa); y->push_back(9);` -- *discards qualifiers* -- although READONLY_DESIGN says the rebind to a mutable source drops readonly and sema accepts the write. The same when the readonly binding sits in a sibling arm that declares its own slot: `if c: if k > 0: y = xa` / `else: y = xa` then `y.append(9); return` / `else: y = ro; ...; return` hoists `const std::vector<...>* y;` in front of the then-arm's nested `if`. Cause: the slot's const-ness is the function-wide per-name accumulator `stmt_borrow_decls` (`record_borrow_binding`, tpyc/sema/context.py), read by every THIR hoist ladder (`_nonvalue_hoist_flavor`, tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py), not a fact of the bindings that reach that one C++ slot. A carried arm binding whose declaration would land in front of a nested block (`_place_arm_decl`, tpyc/sema/statements.py) is left undeclared when the name's bit is set and the arm's own type is mutable, so that shape keeps master's located lowering reject instead of reaching g++. Fix shape: decide the const bit per declared slot (the bindings its C++ scope receives) where sema records the predecl, and render from that. Probes `/tmp/agents/rdy/p/v1.py` (`f`), `v2.py`, `p9.py`, `p12.py`. Found fixing the arm-join branch's placed-declaration gap.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, located) A field two hops deep cannot be assigned: `self.inner.table = t`.** [`two-hop-field-write-rejected`]

  alike, from a local or straight from an `Own[...]` call result; CPython

  `/tmp/agents/aw/gaps3/two_hop_field_write_repro.py`. Found 2026-09-28
  porting a terminal game.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A `for` over a list literal of a `str` parameter and another str element is refused: `for r in [d, "x"]`.** [`for-list-literal-str-param-elems-rejected`]
  Reports `expr.container_literal` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`, not

- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) `del` of a slice is refused: `del buf[:i]`, `del xs[1:3]`.** [`del-slice-rejected`]
  `del xs[a:b]` stops with `deleting a slice ('del xs[a:b]') is not yet
  supported` on a `bytearray`, a `list` and any other container alike;
  `del xs[i]` works, and CPython removes the slice. The rejection used to
  come from the PARSER, which parsed the slice outside the subscript
  path and printed the AST node (`Unsupported expression: Slice`); since
  2026-09-28 the `del` target takes the shared subscript parse and sema's
  `_analyze_del_item` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) rejects the slice in
  plain words. What remains is the deletion itself: a slice
  `__delitem__` on the builtin containers and its lowering. The usual
  shape is dropping consumed input from a buffer; the workaround is
  rebuilding the buffer from the kept part. Pinned by
  `tests/cases/bytes/error_bytearray_del_slice`. Repro
  `/tmp/agents/aw/gaps3/del_slice_repro.py`. Found 2026-09-26 porting a
  terminal game.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) `del xs["a"]` on a `list[int]` passes sema and fails the C++ build.** [`del-item-index-type-unchecked`]
  `_analyze_del_item` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) analyzes the index but
  checks it against the container's key type only for a `dict`; a list's
  index is never matched against its `__delitem__` parameter, so a `str`
  index reaches the generated `erase` and g++ rejects it. CPython raises
  `TypeError`. Fix: resolve the `__delitem__` overload against the index
  type, as a read resolves `__getitem__`. Repros
  `/tmp/agents/bundle3/row1/d09_list_strkey/main.py`,
  `/tmp/agents/bundle3/row1/d13_strkey_ann/main.py`. Found 2026-09-28.
- **[LOW small] (rejects valid, loud; misleading remedy) `del buf[0]` on a `bytearray` tells the user to define `__delitem__` on a builtin.** [`bytearray-del-item-define-delitem`]
  `buf = bytearray(b"abc"); del buf[0]` stops with `'del' is not

- **[HIGH small] (silent CPython divergence; awaiting a language decision) An unannotated generic instance whose `T` is learned from a float literal silently converts a later int argument to float.** [`float-learned-generic-instance-converts-int`] With `class Bag[T]` holding `items: list[T]` and `def add(self, v: T): self.items.append(v)`, `b = Bag(); b.add(1.5); b.add(2); print(b.items)` prints `[1.5, 2.0]` where CPython prints `[1.5, 2]`; the constructor-seeded `c = Cell(1.5); c.add(2)` does the same. `_eagerly_resolve_pending_generic` rebinds the instance as `Bag[float]` after the first call, so the second call resolves as an ordinary `float` parameter and the int converts silently. Probes `/tmp/agents/bundle3/review2/parity/bag3.py`, `/tmp/agents/bundle3/review2/meta/cell.py`, `/tmp/agents/bundle3/review3/parity/r1.py`, `/tmp/agents/bundle3/review3/parity/r3.py`. - **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud -- raw toolchain spew) An escaping closure that MOVE-captures a non-copyable value cannot be held by the `Callable` slot it was written for.** [`move-only-closure-in-callable-slot`] `def make(g: Own[Guard]) -> Callable[[], int32]:` with a nested `def read() -> int32: return g.x` and `return read` emits `auto read = [g = std::move(g)]() -> int32_t { ... }; return read;` -- the capture is exactly the escaping `Own[T]` / `@nocopy` row the design doc prescribes, but the `std::function` return slot static-asserts `std::function target must be copy-constructible` and the build dies inside `<bits/std_function.h>` with no TPy diagnostic and no TPy source line. `Guard` here is a plain record with `__del__` (C++ deletes its copy ctor); a `@nocopy` payload does the same. The doc prescribes `std::move_only_function` for precisely this (section "`std::move_only_function` for Move-Only Captures") and TODO.md tracks the SIGNATURE half ("Closures: `std::move_only_function` for `Callable` with `Own[T]` params/returns"); this entry is the CAPTURE half, where nothing in the signature is move-only and only the closure's captures are. The lambda position at the same slot does not reach it: a lambda does not move-capture at all, and since 2026-09-10 its by-value entry over a non-copyable type rejects at the Python level (`expr.lambda`, pinned by `tests/cases/nested_def/error_lambda_nocopy_snapshot`) -- so the two positions now fail differently for the same source. Repro `/tmp/agents/fnfix/sync_nocopy_def.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] The `optional_str_to_strview` / `optional_strview_to_str` statement-expression shim binds `auto __ov = (<src>);` BY VALUE, so the produced `string_view` aliases the copy's heap buffer, freed at the closing `})` -- an ASAN-verified use-after-free at every non-SSO string.** The coercion templates in `tpyc/coercions.py` (`({ auto __ov = (x); __ov ? std::make_optional(std::string_view(*__ov)) : std::nullopt; })`, and the `std::string(*__ov)` twin) copy the source `std::optional<std::string>` into `__ov`, view INTO the copy, and destroy it before the consumer reads the view. Masked in the shipped case (`tests/cases/list/list_append_optional_strview_from_str`) because its strings fit libstdc++'s SSO buffer; reproduced under ASAN with a longer string. The template in `tpyc/coercions.py` is the single definition every lowering site wraps (`arg.opt_view_own_shim` in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` and its siblings), so the fix is one edit there plus the snapshot churn it causes. Fix shape: bind `const auto& __ov = ...` (view the SOURCE, not a copy) -- note the `strview_to_str` twin's `std::string(*__ov)` materializes and is safe either way, only the view-producing direction dangles. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, ASAN-verified; independently confirmed by safety-model) of the value-opt rekeying wave. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code) `copy()` of a NARROWED pointer-repr `Optional[record]` name at the return sink drops the deref -- emits `A(a)` where `a` is `const A*`.** `def f(a: A | None) -> Own[A]: if a is not None: return copy(a)` -- the return sink classifies its copy source against `scope.admission_pointers()`, which deliberately strips pointer-repr Optional-record names, so `copy_plain_record_source` accepts the pointer as a plain-record source; the `BORROW_BIND` read then renders the name bare (by design there -- record receivers spell `->`), giving `A(a)` instead of `A(*a)`. The other three copy sinks classify against the full `lc.pointers` and exclude the shape. **Live on the DEFAULT path since the flip**, no longer dormant: THIR authors every body, so a plain `tpy` on the repro fails the C++ build with `invalid conversion from 'const A*' to 'int32_t'` -- the bare pointer is fed to the record's own `A(int32_t)` constructor (re-verified 2026-09-02; the `-> A` spelling in the original note is rejected earlier by the borrow-return check, so the reachable form spells `-> Own[A]`). Re-rated LOW -> MED on that: `copy()` of a narrowed Optional record param is ordinary code and the failure is a build break the user cannot route around, matching how the file rates the sibling `copy-int-literal-result` and `copy-array-literal-into-list-slot`. No corpus case exercises it, so the byte-diff and ratchet stay green. Verified pre-existing -- reproduces byte-for-byte on master 31c0cd431 in a clean worktree, so the copy-row helper fold (which preserved the asymmetry exactly) neither introduced nor widened it. Surfaced by the /tpy-review safety pass on the fold. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent] An `@overload` generator implementation's body-derived facts are stamped onto the LAST STUB's FunctionInfo, using the impl's param indices.** The impl is not registered as callable, so `_analyze_function` resolves `func_overloads[-1]` (the last stub's FI) and writes the impl's body facts there (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py:~1530-1571` borrow/mutation facts incl. `generator_borrow_param_indices`; `~1284-1300` `frame_locals`/`frame_subframes` Send/Sync materials). Two consequences: (1) if a later stub declares fewer params than the impl, an impl-derived borrow index can exceed the stub's arity and corrupt `return_borrows_from`; (2) frame materials land on a stub FI whose `is_generator` is False, so any consumer gating on `fi.is_generator` before reading them misreads. Not triggered today -- `itertools.repeat` and the `overload_generator` test both have a last stub of equal arity to the impl, and no current consumer hits case (2). Became reachable when the @overload-ed generator crash was fixed (the body path was previously unreachable). Fix shape: stamp impl body facts onto an FI that represents the impl (or onto every stub by the stub's own param mapping), not blindly onto `func_overloads[-1]`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the overloaded-generator fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (precision, not unsound)** A `@native` method emitted through the frontend-IR plugin path (`tpyc/frontend_ir/lower.py` `_route_decorators` -> `BUILTIN_LOWERING(tpy.native)`) cannot express `native_preserves_refs`. That property is set by a *separate* decorator (`@native_preserves_refs`, qname `tpy.extern.native_preserves_refs`) which is not in `CORE_DECORATORS`, so a plugin can't emit it -- `_route_decorators` rejects it as an unknown decorator. `is_invalidating_method` (`tpyc/sema/receiver_calls.py`) reads `native_preserves_refs` only for *builtin* records; plugin-emitted natives are user-defined and take the `direct_self_mutated` fallback, so the borrow checker conservatively treats every plugin-lowered native method as invalidating iterators/borrowed refs, potentially yielding spurious invalidation diagnostics. Latent: no in-tree plugin emits native methods yet. Fix shape: add a `native_preserves_refs` entry to `CORE_DECORATORS` (or a `_NativeSpec` kwarg) and thread it onto `TpyFunction.native_preserves_refs` in lowering. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` (safety-model).

The `readonly` wrapper defeats the dynamic-protocol test on the `Own` slot, so the Own-dyn erasure arm never fires. Exotic shape (readonly-ness of an owned erased handle has no meaningful surface), but the user gets no explanation. Fix shape: either reject `Own[readonly[@dynamic P]]` params in sema with a real diagnostic, or peel the readonly wherever the Own-dyn form is decided (slot, signature render and call). - **[LOW small] (latent, benign as emitted) A NARROWED `Optional[container]` field at an EQUALITY operand loses its unwrap.** `if self.lst is not None: return self.lst == self.other` (on `lst: list[int32] | None`, `other: list[int32]`) emits `(this->lst == this->other)`, where the unwrapped `((*this->lst) == this->other)` is the intended form -- no corpus case witnesses it. Root cause: the compare-operand sink threads `allow_whole_optional`, which suppresses the read's `narrowed_deref` flag, while the gate (`_container_compare_pair`) keys the NARROWED analyzed types and so admits the pair; the `field.whole_optional` arm then claims the read. C++ makes the emitted form compile and (for `==`/`!=` on a proven-non-None optional) agree at runtime via `std::optional`'s mixed comparison, which is why nothing has caught it. Fix shape: do not thread `allow_whole_optional` into a compare operand whose partner is a bare container (or exclude a declared-Optional/analyzed-container mismatch from the `field.whole_optional` arm at that sink). No corpus witness. Repro `/tmp/agents/cell-optfield/b7_cmp_only.py`. Surfaced by the boundary sweep of the THIR `Optional[container]`-field cell (2026-08-19). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
