The `Ptr[Rc[readonly[T]]]` spelling fails the same way after sema also misses the readonly payload (the Safety entry on field-assign through a raw `Ptr` to a readonly-payload `Deref`). Fix shape: the field-write lowering chains the receiver's `Deref` hops the way sema resolved them. Found by the 2026-09-29 BUGS.md lifetime sweep.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught) A method returning `self.p.__deref__()` for a `Ptr` field is inferred `@readonly`, and its `const` borrow is bound into a mutable holder.** [`deref-borrow-return-const-into-mutable-holder`] `class B` with `m: M`, `p: Ptr[M]` (`self.p = take_ptr(self.m)` in `__init__`) and `def get(self) -> M: return self.p.__deref__()`; in the caller `holder = M(0); holder = b.get()` emits `M* holder = &__slot_1; holder = &(b.get());` against a `const M& get() const`, and g++ reports *invalid conversion from 'const M*' to 'M*'*. The return borrows through a `Ptr`, so the receiver is not what it lends from; either the method must not be const-inferred when its result is bound mutably, or the result's const-ness must reach the holder's type in sema. Related: `BUGS.md#self-aimed-ptr-field-borrow-unrecorded` (the lifetime half of the same shape). Found by the 2026-09-29 BUGS.md lifetime sweep.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid Python, toolchain-caught; should be a located diagnostic) Assigning an `int` (BigInt) expression to an `int32` `for` variable reaches the C++ build.** [`bigint-into-int32-loop-var-cpp-error`]
  `for n in range(2, N)` binds `n: int32`; a later `n = a * lookup[c] + d`
  with `d` read from a `list[int]` is a BigInt expression, and tpyc
  emits the assignment unchecked -- g++ stops with *cannot convert
  'tpy::BigInt' to 'int32_t' in assignment* at a generated-code line.
  Sema should refuse the rebind where the widths meet, in the words the
  int/float rebind rule uses (one numeric type per local), or convert
  with a range check. CPython runs it. Repro
  `/tmp/agents/rel06/ex2/gap_a.py`. Reported by the tpy-examples port of
  shedskin's collatz, 2026-09-29.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, located) A list local bound BEFORE a loop cannot be rebound from a comprehension INSIDE it: `xs = [0] * n; for k in range(3): xs = [c + 1 for c in xs]`.** [`prebound-list-rebound-in-loop-from-comprehension`]
  Stops with *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation
  (stmt.var_decl:container_lit.rebound)*; seeding with `xs = [0 for _ in
  range(n)]` instead compiles, so the `[0] * n` repeat form is what the
  rebind gate refuses. CPython prints `[3, 3, 3, 3]`. A `list(range(n))`
  seed rebound by a comprehension is the same gap with no loop at all,
  reported at the SEED line: `xs = list(range(n)); xs = [x + 1 for x in
  xs]` stops with `expr.call:call.special.call_type.builtin_generic`
  (int64 bounds or not; drop the rebind and it compiles; repro
  `/tmp/agents/rel06/ex2/gap_b4.py`). Distinct from the HIGH
  `container_lit.rebound` entry above, where the list is first bound
  inside the loop body and assigned outward. Repro
  `/tmp/agents/rel06/ex2/gap_c.py`. Reported by the tpy-examples port of
  shedskin's collatz, 2026-09-29.
- **[LOW small] (runtime; allocation failure throws instead of panicking) `BigInt::from_str` builds its magnitude in a `std::vector`, whose allocation failure throws `std::bad_alloc`.** [`bigint-from-str-bad-alloc-throws`] The documented rule is that BigInt allocation failure is a panic (`docs/EXCEPTION_DESIGN.md`, the `MemoryError` row; `alloc_heap` in `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/bigint.hpp` calls `tpy_panic("out of memory")`), but `from_str` (same header, the decimal parse loop) fills a `std::vector<uint64_t>` through `mul_small_inplace` / `add_small_inplace`, so an out-of-memory there escapes as a C++ exception no TPy handler names. A wide literal (`x = 123456789012345678901234567890`) is rendered through it (`codegen_cpp/int_literals.py` emits `::tpy::BigInt::from_str("...")`), as is `int(s)`. The same `std::vector` pattern sits in `mul_mag` / `add_mag` / `sub_mag` (ordinary `*`, `+`, `-`), in divmod and in decimal formatting, so the fix covers every vector site in the header, not the parse alone. Practically unreachable (the magnitude is tiny next to any real heap), so hardening only; but it contradicts the fact MIR reads, BigInt's `TypeDef.copy_may_raise=False` (allocation failure panics), under which a wide BigInt constant's materialization is modeled as unable to raise. Fix shape: build the magnitude in BigInt's own heap storage, or catch `std::bad_alloc` at the parse and panic like `alloc_heap`. Surfaced by the MIR B2 review.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud; the reason outlived) Five `str` / `bytes` field-write receivers stay rejected although the inferred field view they guarded no longer exists.** [`field-write-receiver-rejects-outlived-reason`] A `Ptr` receiver (a parameter or one held in a record field), a tuple element, a container element (`rs[0].name = "x"`, `d["k"].name = "x"`, the `*args` pack subscript), a borrow-returning call (`b.get().name = "x"`) and a `@property` getter (`h.val.name = "x"`) reject at `assign.field_write_shape` (`_viewfam_field_write_receiver_ok`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`; pinned by the five `tests/cases/records/error_str_field_write_*` cases), while the `int32` field beside them takes every receiver. The subtraction was added because an inferred one-hop field view would have survived the write with no diagnostic (`BUGS.md#field-view-escape-needs-place`). Under the one view rule (`docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` String Type Semantics) an inferred field read owns a copy, and the explicit `StrView` opt-in is unguarded at the admitted receivers as well (`BUGS.md#explicit-view-local-source-mutation-unguarded`), so the rejects no longer buy a soundness the admitted receivers have; they are kept until re-measured. Fix: re-measure each receiver against the rule (render, exec and CPython parity of a field read held across the write) and drop the subtraction where nothing dangles; each `error_` case then becomes a section of `tests/cases/records/str_field_write_receivers`. Found by the view-rule review, 2026-10-01.
- **[MED small] (hidden copy, no diagnostic; pre-existing) In an `async def`, a tuple unpack of an `await` result copies its `str` / `bytes` elements out of the single-use holder, where sync and generator bodies move them.** [`await-unpack-holder-copies`] `h, t = await other(i)` with `async def other(i: int) -> tuple[str, bytes]` renders `const auto& __tup_1 = __await_lift_0; h = std::get<0>(__tup_1); t = std::get<1>(__tup_1);`, while `h, t = pair(i)` in a generator or a plain body renders `h = std::move(std::get<0>(__tup_1));` (the holder move of the one view rule, `_move_owned_buffer_targets` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`). The await-lift slot is read once and reassigned at the next await, so it is as disposable as an rvalue holder; the copy is one buffer allocation per element per iteration. Probe `/tmp/agents/vr-review/cg/p2.py` (2026-10-01).

- **[LOW small] (lost information, runtime) A Ctrl-C partway through a blocking `socket.send()` loses the count of bytes already sent.** [`interrupted-send-loses-sent-count`] A blocking or timeout-mode `send()` of more than the socket buffer holds loops in `socket._send_waiting` (`lib/tpy/socket.py`); a Ctrl-C taken in a later wait (or pending when the last chunk completes) raises `KeyboardInterrupt` out of the `_interrupt` wait or check, so the caller cannot tell how much of the data went out. CPython returns the partial count when bytes were sent before the signal. Fix shape: return `sent` when it is non-zero and re-post the consumed interrupt (set `pending` and write the wake fd again, a new entry point in `signal_impl.cpp`) so the next check point raises it. `sendall()` is unaffected: it has no count to report. Found by the Ctrl-C branch review, 2026-09-29.
- **[LOW small] (wrong resolution, then a confusing error) A user module named like an internal stdlib module (`_interrupt`, `_bindings`, `_datetime_cal`) shadows it for the stdlib's own imports.** [`user-module-shadows-internal-stdlib-module`] The entry-point directory is searched before `lib/tpy/`, and a stdlib module's `import _interrupt` resolves through the same search, so a program shipping its own `_interrupt.py` next to `main.py` breaks `import socket` with `lib/tpy/socket.py: error: '_interrupt' is not a variable` (probe: a user `_interrupt.py` plus `import socket`; CPython has no such module and runs the program). Same class for every underscore-prefixed internal module. Fix shape: resolve a stdlib module's imports against the library path first (or reserve the underscore-prefixed names with a diagnostic at the user file). Surfaced by the Ctrl-C branch review, 2026-09-30.
- **[LOW small] (silent divergence) `str(GeneratorExit())` is `'GeneratorExit'` in TPy and `''` in CPython.** [`generatorexit-default-message`] The runtime's default constructor (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/core.hpp`, `struct GeneratorExit`) passes its own class name as the message, where every other exception defaults to an empty one. Visible through `str(e)` / `e.args`-style reads in a handler and in an uncaught report. `KeyboardInterrupt` had the same default and was fixed on the Ctrl-C branch, 2026-09-29. Fix shape: drop the default constructor so the inherited empty default applies, then check the frame-destructor and `with.__exit__` paths that construct it.
- **[LOW small] (C++ name in user-facing output) An uncaught exception is reported under its C++-qualified type name, not the Python class name.** [`uncaught-report-cpp-type-name`] `tpy_terminate_handler` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/core.hpp`) demangles `typeid(e).name()`, so `class SubInterrupt(KeyboardInterrupt)` raised uncaught prints `TurboPython panic: uncaught tpyapp::prog::SubInterrupt: why` and a stdlib exception prints e.g. `uncaught tpystd::zlib::error: ...`, where CPython names `SubInterrupt` / `zlib.error`. Breaks the no-C++-names-in-diagnostics rule (`docs/PITFALLS.md`) for every uncaught user or stdlib exception. Fix shape: have the throwable carry its Python-facing qualname (a virtual on the `TPY_THROWABLE_VIRTUALS` family, emitted per class) and print that instead of the demangled C++ name. Surfaced by the Ctrl-C branch (`tests/test_cli_signals.py` uncaught-subclass test matches only the ends of the line), 2026-09-29.

## Safety / borrow checker

- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR -- raised 2026-10-01: the one view rule makes this annotation THE zero-copy spelling at a field or an element, so the compiler must not recommend it until it is guarded, and the return-hint names only `return h.s`] (SILENT use-after-free, garbage output, no diagnostic) An explicit view local (`StrView`, `BytesView`, `Span`) takes no loan on its source, so a direct mutation of the source while the view lives prints garbage.** [`explicit-view-local-source-mutation-unguarded`] `sv: StrView = names[0]` then `names.clear(); names.append(...)` and `print(sv[:5])`; `sv: StrView = h.s` then `h.s = ...`; `sp: Span[int32] = k.items` then `k.items.append(4)` and `print(sp[0])`; `sp: Span[int32] = xs` then `xs.append(4)` -- each compiles with no diagnostic and prints garbage where CPython prints the old value (probes `/tmp/agents/vr-rule/p2_elem.py`, `p2_field.py`, `p3.py`, 2026-10-01, on 02ab5f8c89). An INFERRED view never faces these writes: a field read or a container element owns under the one view rule, and a view over a NAME owns at its bind when the function writes that name anywhere (the pre-scan's rebind facts, `root_reseated_in_body`). Four faces absorbed from the retired `view-local-outlives-receiver-rebind`, re-probed at 019184dae4 (`/tmp/agents/vr-docs/recv_rebind.py`, `field_faces.py`): the receiver rebind `a = make("first"); c: StrView = a.strip(); a = make("second")` prints garbage with no diagnostic, while its `a += "tail"` twin warns `Mutation of 'a' while borrowed ('+=' may invalidate references)` and prints garbage too; `v: StrView = h.t.name` then `h.t = Tagged(...)`, and `v: StrView = h.peek().name` (a borrow-returning accessor) then the same rebind, print garbage with no diagnostic; `v: StrView = h.first().name` (an element through an accessor) then `h.ts.clear(); h.ts.append(...)` prints the new element's text where CPython prints the old one, silently. Since the one view rule (TODO.md "`str` / `bytes` views: MIR precision over the one view rule") the explicit annotation is the opt-in to borrow a field or a container element, so this is that opt-in's known cost. Fix home: the MIR loan on view locals (`docs/MIR_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`), which then rejects the write while the view lives, or demotes an explicit view the way it demotes an inferred one -- a decision for that slice.
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output) A `match` capture into an existing local stores a wider subject unchecked.** [`match-capture-wider-store-unchecked`] With `i = 0; i = k` (`k: int32`) and `j = i`, then `match big: case j: pass` (`big: int64`), the capture writes the `int64` subject into the `int32` local `j`: TPy prints 1 where CPython prints 4294967297 (probe `/tmp/agents/safety_pint/match_derived.py`, re-probed on `pending-int-locals` 2026-09-30; pre-existing). A capture is a binding form the pending integer locals exclude, so `j` keeps its first type -- but the capture neither refuses the wider value with the annotation to write, as a plain rebind of a typed local does, nor narrows it with a check. Fix shape: run the capture through the reassignment rule like any other store into the local, which refuses a value wider than the local's first type. The other `as` bindings install a type the same way (checked 2026-10-01): a `with ... as x` over an existing local skips the reassignment check in `_analyze_with` but is refused at lowering today (`stmt.with`, the `with ... as NAME` reuse entry and `BUGS.md#with-existing-scalar-target-rejected`), and an `except ... as x` binds an exception class, whose post-handler read is the `except ... as NAME` entry -- neither stores a wider number silently. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (latent unchecked deref; sound-by-default gap) The Optional receiver check keys on a flag whose DEFAULT means "proven".** [`optional-check-flag-default-is-proven`] `TpySubscript.needs_optional_runtime_check` (set in `_analyze_subscript`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) defaults to False, and `_lower_optional_container_recv` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) renders the bare `(*recv)` unwrap whenever it is False. A subscript node sema never analyzed, or one a trial left stale, therefore renders UNCHECKED with no diagnostic. No leaking shape is known today (every analyzed subscript sets the flag, and the reset at the top of `_analyze_subscript` covers the overload trials), so this is a gap in the rule, not a reproduced crash. Fix shape: a positive proven-non-None fact on the node, with every other state rejecting or checking, as the "One checked-unwrap mechanism" TODO.md entry describes. Surfaced by the safety-model review of bug bundle 3, 2026-09-28.

- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent UB, prints correctly by luck) A tuple unpack in BOTH branches of an `if`, with a reference-record element, binds the hoisted name to a temporary scoped to the branch block.** [`branch-unpack-target-points-into-branch-temp`] `if f: v, k = mk(5), 1` / `else: v, k = mk(6), 2` with `mk() -> Own[R]` renders `v = &(__unpack_0_0);` where `__unpack_0_0` is declared inside the branch block, so `v` dangles once the block ends; later allocations may reuse the storage. Repro `/tmp/agents/design_pos/side/unpackbr.py`.
- **[HIGH medium, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free, garbage output, no diagnostic) A record carrying a view field (`StrView` / `Span` / `BytesView`) or a `Ptr` field built from a local escapes that local through a return, a yield, a frame local or an escaping closure.** [`record-view-field-escapes-local-buffer`] With `class Name(ValueType)` holding `n: StrView`, `buf = "abc..." + str(k)` then `return Name(buf)` or `v = Name(buf); return v` compiles clean and prints garbage (`buf` dies at the return); a plain (non-`ValueType`) `Name` returned as `-> Own[Name]` does the same. The escape also goes through a generator yield (`v = Name(buf); yield v`, kept past the next iteration), an `async def` return after a suspension, and a tuple return (`return (v, k)`). The view-escape check covers bare view types only (`_VIEW_RETURN_FAMILIES`, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`), so a view reached through a record field is not followed. Repros `/tmp/agents/meta/c1base.py`, `/tmp/agents/meta/c1own.py`, `/tmp/agents/safety/p10.py`, `p12.py`, `p15.py`, `p16.py`. Two more sinks: a field or container STORE -- `buf = mk(k); h.xs.append(Name(buf))` into a caller-owned `h` leaves `h.xs[0].n` reading `buf` after `fill` returns (`/tmp/agents/safety_r2/vt2.py`) -- and a TEMPORARY argument source -- `v = Name(mk(k))` dangles right after the statement, in a plain function and as a generator frame local, for the `ValueType` and the plain-record `Name` alike (`/tmp/agents/safety_r2/vt1b.py`, `vt1p.py`). The temporary source is the constructor face of `BUGS.md#native-stub-declares-no-param-retention`: nothing records that `__init__` keeps its view argument in a field, so the argument temporary is admitted as if the callee let go of it. Two more faces, both identical on master `c854c7b482`: a `Ptr` FIELD -- `class Ref(ValueType)` holding `p: Ptr[Node]`, `n = Node(k); return Ref(n)` (or `r = Ref(n); return r`) renders `return Ref(&n);` and the caller reads the dead local (`0 0` where CPython prints `3 4`, `/tmp/agents/br_safety/p9.py`); and an ESCAPING CLOSURE -- `v = Name(buf); return lambda: str(v.n)` at a `-> Callable[[], str]` copies `v` into the closure with its view into `buf` and prints garbage (`/tmp/agents/br_safety/p27.py`). The bare-view closure face is BUGS.md#escaping-lambda-captures-local-view. Found by /tpy-review of the ValueType value-form branch 2026-09-24. The base-initializer face: a `str` or `StrView` parameter the base stores into a `StrView` field, fed a concat, conversion or f-string (`super().__init__(str(n) + "abc")`, `super().__init__(f"{n}{n}")`), prints garbage (`/tmp/agents/superinit_e3/strslot.py`, `/tmp/agents/cgc3/svf3.py`, `svf4.py`); a fresh non-str value at a view parameter is rejected instead (BUGS.md#base-init-args-separate-lowering). The constructor face: a view FIELD member-initialized from a slice of a view parameter (`self.lab = text[1:3]` in `__init__`, `lab: StrView`) keeps a view of the caller's buffer, so an object that outlives that buffer reads freed memory; the member-init admits exactly what a method's field write admits, so it shares the method's hole (the lifetime of the object against its source is the MIR's to track). A view field from a METHOD LOCAL (`s = a + "!"; self.v = s[1:]`) or from a by-value param's buffer dangles the same way once the method returns: sema's temporary-view rule treats a name as durable, since it outlives the statement, and nothing checks it outlives the object. Two more names of the same kind, on master too: a match CAPTURE of a temporary subject (`match mk_obj(k): case Obj(name=n): self.v = n`, probe `/tmp/agents/r3review/safety/m1.py`) and a LOOP VARIABLE over a temporary list (`for e in mk_list(k): self.b = e`, probe `/tmp/agents/r3review/safety/vd.py`) -- the name's storage is the temporary's, which dies with the statement that made it; both print garbage. The union face: a NAME into the view member of a union field (`self.u = s` at `u: StrView | int32`) is rejected in a body write (`field_write.lift.borrow`, as master rejected it) and admitted in a member-init (`u(s)`), where it dangles like the bare view field.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free, garbage output, no diagnostic) An escaping lambda captures a `StrView` local BY VALUE, so the view outlives the buffer it points into.** [`escaping-lambda-captures-local-view`] `buf = "abc..." + str(k); sv: StrView = buf; return lambda: str(sv)` at a `-> Callable[[], str]` renders `return [sv]() -> std::string { return std::string(sv); };` and the caller's call prints garbage where CPython prints the string; identical on master `c854c7b482`. Returning `sv` itself is caught by the view-escape check (*Cannot return StrView referencing a local or temporary*, `/tmp/agents/docs_vt/p26r.py`), which does not look at an escaping closure's captures. A `str` PARAMETER captured the same way (`def mk(s: str) -> Callable[[], str]: return lambda: s`) captures the `std::string_view` parameter `[s]` too and, since the lambda body's owned-`str` coercion landed, compiles into this dangling read (`mk("abc" + str(3))()` prints `abc3` by luck, `/tmp/agents/merge_vt/lam.py`, 2026-09-26): the escaping-closure capture check that rejects a `str` parameter in a nested `def` (BUGS.md#escaping-closure-view-param-capture) does not see a lambda's captures. The record-field face is BUGS.md#record-view-field-escapes-local-buffer. Repros `/tmp/agents/br_safety/p26.py`, `/tmp/agents/docs_vt/p26s.py` (the `str` parameter). Found 2026-09-25. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (possible silent wrong value; no reproducer yet) The frame loop check reads an implicit dunder call's receiver, not its arguments.** [`implicit-dunder-args-unchecked`] Implicit calls recorded for the loop-frame and with-exit rules (`record_implicit_call` next to `tpyc/sema/receiver_calls.py`) carry the receiver only, so a user `__setitem__(k, v)` that mutates a non-value `v` the held generator borrows is caught only through the receiver or the module-global rule; the explicit `b.__setitem__(k, v)` twin also checks its arguments. Fix shape: record the argument operands with the implicit call and queue them like an explicit call's.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic; pre-existing on master) The frame loop rule does not see a user dunder a BUILTIN runs on its behalf.** [`frame-loop-builtin-runs-user-dunder`] In a generator body, `yield d[kk]` over a `dict[Key, int32]` runs `Key.__hash__` and `Key.__eq__`, and `if kk in ks:` over a `list[Key]` (or the spelled `ks.index(kk)`) runs `Key.__eq__`; a user `__hash__` / `__eq__` that grows a module global a generator held into the next pass borrows (`g = walk(DATA)`) compiles clean (probes `/tmp/agents/rv5/p7_hash.py`, `/tmp/agents/rv5/p7_eqin.py`). The loop rule counts an implicit call only where sema records one (`record_implicit_call`, `tpyc/sema/receiver_calls.py`): a user type's own dunder at an element read / store / `del`, `in`, iteration, `len()` and a truth test, and a structural protocol parameter's methods at a runtime callee (`record_protocol_arg_calls`). A builtin container's element lookup calls the KEY's or ELEMENT's dunders through the container's C++ (`std::hash` / `operator==`), which no parameter of the called stub names. Fix shape: record, at a builtin container's lookup / membership / search call, the element type's `__hash__` / `__eq__` on the key argument -- read off the TypeDef of the container, not keyed on the method name.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic) The frame loop rule does not count a hand-written awaitable's `__poll__` at an `await`.** [`frame-loop-await-poll-unrecorded`] `t += await aw` in an async body's loop, with `class Grow(Awaitable[int32])` whose `__poll__` grows `self.items` while `g = walk(aw.items)` is held into the next pass, is not rejected (probe `/tmp/agents/rv5/p9.py`): `await` records no implicit call (`ExpressionAnalyzer._mark_await_operand_mutated`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`, passes `record=False`, since an awaited coroutine frame's writes are counted at the calls that built it -- which does not hold for a user `__poll__`). The probe does not reach the hazard today: its C++ build fails first (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/async.hpp`: `'struct Grow' has no member named 'cancel'`, a hand-written `Awaitable` subclass without a `cancel` method). Fix shape: record the `__poll__` call at `await` when the operand's type is a user record rather than a coroutine frame.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent wrong value; pre-existing) A write through a local alias of `self` inside a generator loop gets past the loop-frame check.** [`loop-frame-write-through-self-alias`] In a generator method, `for row in self.rows: g = items(row); yield first(g); s = self; s.rows[0] = [7, 8]` compiles, and the previous pass's generator reads the new element (`items finally 2 7`, CPython `2 1`); the same store spelled `self.rows[0] = ...`, or a `self.reset()` that does it, is rejected by `tpyc/sema/loop_frames.py`. The check resolves a store's root syntactically for `self`, not through the alias. Probe `/tmp/agents/rv2-cp/w/m2.py`; verified identical on master 1ea64345ea. Same class as BUGS.md#field-view-escape-needs-place.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free, no diagnostic; pre-existing, locals too) A view slot bound to a view-returning FREE FUNCTION over a fresh argument is judged durable when the callee body is analyzed after the caller's.** [`strview-field-view-of-temporary`] A view field or a view local whose source's root is a fresh temporary is rejected by one sema rule (`view_source_is_temporary`, `tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`; message "Cannot bind StrView ... to a temporary view source") at every field write -- constructor, method, generator / async method, local holder -- and at an annotated local. One face stays open, and its verdict depends on ANALYSIS ORDER: for `self.v = first(mk(n))` (or `v: StrView = first(mk(n))`) with `def first(s: StrView) -> StrView`, the rule asks the callee's recorded return-borrow sources, and method bodies are analyzed before free-function bodies, so from a method or constructor those sources are not recorded yet and the call reads as durable -- the member-init renders `v(first(mk(n)))`, a view of a dead temporary. The same method calling a callee analyzed earlier is caught. It reproduces for locals on master. Fix shape: the return-borrow sources are a whole-program borrow fact, decided in Phase 2 (or from the signature before any body runs), not a per-site patch. Probes `/tmp/agents/abf/r2/v/c_call.py`, `mlocal_call.py`. A second face, a narrower rule at the other sinks: at a field the rule looks through a slot that HOLDS a view -- an Optional, tuple or union with a view member (`view_slot_source_is_temporary`) -- but an annotated LOCAL asks it only of a bare `StrView` / `BytesView` (`v: StrView | None = mk()[1:3]` keeps a view of the dead temporary), and an insert into a container of views (`xs: list[StrView]`, `xs.append(mk()[1:3])`) is not asked at all. Fix shape: the local and container-element sinks ask the same slot-aware rule. A third face: a view of a temporary object's FIELD reads as durable, because the rule counts every field access as a durable root -- `self.v = mk(a).name.strip()` in a method or a constructor and `v: StrView = mk(a).name.strip()` compile and print garbage (probes `/tmp/agents/r2review/safety/p15_strip_field_of_temp.py`, `p28_ctor_field_of_temp.py`; master too for the local). The spellings a fix has to follow through a borrow-returning callee: a static method (`v = Picker.pick(make(...)).name`, `/tmp/agents/r4review/safety/p13.py`) and a function in another module (`helpers.pick(make(...)).name`, `/tmp/agents/r4review/safety/mod/main.py`) -- the receiver-root rule needs the callee's `recorded_return_borrow_sources`, the same fact the analysis-order face needs, while a field read through a borrow of a durable receiver (`s.peek().name`, `/tmp/agents/tcrev/pk.py`) must stay admitted.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free, garbage output, no diagnostic; pre-existing) A tuple-unpack whose source call takes an inline tuple LITERAL at a tuple param and returns a borrow of it binds its targets into the dead literal.** [`tuple-literal-arg-unpack-borrow-dangles`] `def pt(t: tuple[M, int]) -> tuple[M, int]: return t[0], t[1]` and `a, n = pt((mk(9), 2))` emits `auto __tup_1 = pt(::tpy::tuple_value_to_borrow<std::tuple<M*, ::tpy::BigInt>>(std::tuple<M, ::tpy::BigInt>{mk(9), 2}));` then `a = &(... std::get<0>(__tup_1) ...)` -- the `std::tuple<M, BigInt>` temporary holding the `M` dies at the end of that statement, and `a` points into it. In a generator the read after the next allocation prints 322 where CPython prints 11; the SYNC twin (`auto&& a = ... std::get<0>(__tup_1) ...`) prints 88888 where CPython prints 5, so this is not a frame-only defect. The frame unpack's alias gate (`_hoists_arg_temp`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`, which rejects at `res.unpack` since 2026-09-28) sees only THIR arg temps and temp-bearing union lifts, and the sync unpack asks nothing: an inline tuple-literal temporary whose element the callee's result borrows is neither. The missing fact is the lend-back of a call result over a temporary argument -- the question the return-borrow fact answers for a plain record argument -- asked of each tuple element's source; one check at the unpack binding covers the sync and frame positions. The frame alias gate added in the 0.6 gate batch E (`_hoists_arg_temp`, a located `res.unpack` reject when the source hoists an arg temp or a temp-bearing union lift) misses other temp-declaring nodes the same way: a `*args` pack, `def pick(*ms: M) -> tuple[M, int]` with `a, n = pick(M(3)); await ...; a.v = 9`, emits `M __tmp_1 = M(3); std::array<M*,1> __tmp_2{&__tmp_1}; auto __tup_1 = pick(varargs<M>(__tmp_2));` inside `case S_INITIAL` and writes through the dead alias after the resume -- silent, and master renders the same (probe `/tmp/agents/chal/va.py`); a slot emplace (`__select_slot_N`) and a value select's `lhs_temp_cpp` are unrecognized too. The fix is a positive fact -- each lowered node answers "declares a statement-scoped temp" -- shared with the validator's temp-bearing-node test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic; pre-existing on master) `print(x)` and an f-string `{x}` run a user `__str__`/`__repr__` the frame loop rule never sees.** [`frame-loop-print-runs-user-str`] In a generator body, a generator `g = items(ROWS[0])` held open across a loop pass while the pass calls `print(b)` (or `s = f"{b}"`), with `Bag.__str__` appending to the module global `ROWS`, compiles clean and segfaults; the same write through `b.show()` or `str(b)` is rejected ("the loop calls '__str__', which may write the module global 'ROWS'"), and `del g` before the print makes it run correctly. `_analyze_print_call` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`) resolves print to a parameterless `FunctionInfo(is_readonly=True)`, so no implicit call is recorded for the argument's `__str__`, and `_call_write` (`tpyc/sema/loop_frames.py`) answers "writes nothing" for a readonly callee without facts before it reaches the module-global rule; the f-string replacement field records nothing either. The same `_call_write` path serves `with_exit_write`, so a `print(self)` in an `__exit__` body is likely affected too (not probed). Sibling of `frame-loop-builtin-runs-user-dunder`. Fix shape: record each print argument's and each replacement field's resolved formatter (`__str__`, or `__repr__` for `!r` and the fallback, nested element formatters included) as an implicit call, the fact the loop and `with` checks already read; the same fact lets MIR admit print of non-primitive arguments. Found 2026-09-29 by the MIR B1 design survey.
- **[MED small] (readonly hole, cross-module only) A method that passes a `Ptr` field to a mutable `Ptr` parameter is inferred `@readonly` when called from another module.** [`readonly-ptr-field-mutation-cross-module`] `class H: p: Ptr[Cell]` with `def poke(self): bump(self.p)` (`bump(p: Ptr[Cell])` writes `p.v`) is emitted `void poke() const;` and an importing module calls it through `readonly[H]` (`mutated through readonly: 1`); inside the defining module the same call is rejected (*Cannot call non-readonly method*), so the verdict depends on the caller's module. `zlib._Compress.compress` has this shape (its stream is behind a `Ptr`), so a `readonly[zlib._Compress]` can feed the compressor. Whether a write through a `Ptr` field mutates `self` is the question; the two positions must agree either way. Repros `/tmp/agents/zlibsafety/xm/`, `/tmp/agents/zlibsafety/ro.py`. Found 2026-09-26 by /tpy-review (safety-model).
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (latent, no reproducer) Deferred checks queued outside the context survive a sema trial run.** [`pending-iter-copy-checks-not-trial-scoped`] Three pending queues live on analyzer objects instead of the context, so `ctx.trial_scope()` does not roll them back: `CallAnalyzer.pending_borrow_checks` and `CallAnalyzer.pending_match_subject_checks` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`), and `TypeCompatibility.pending_iter_copy_checks` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`, the copy warning's pending-callee queue, decided in `finalize_borrow_checks`). A dry run -- overload trials, the lambda-body dry run at a Callable slot -- that queues into one of them could file a duplicate or stale check. Dispatch-overload + pending-generator probes produced one warning each (`/tmp/agents/mergechk/p10.py`, `p11.py`, 2026-09-26). Fix shape: move the three queues onto the context and have `trial_scope()` snapshot their lengths and truncate back on exit, like the other per-function diagnostic state.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free, garbage output, no diagnostic) A borrow of an element TWO subscript hops deep is never invalidated by a mutation of the inner container.** [`two-hop-element-borrow-not-invalidated`] `ws = [[A(1)]]; r = ws[0][0]; ws[0].append(A(2)); print(r.v)` compiles with no warning and prints garbage where CPython prints `1`; the frame spellings `it4 = one(ws[0][0])` and `it3 = pair((zs[0][0], 0))` (a generator over `A` / `tuple[A, int]`) followed by `ws[0].append(...)` do the same, while the one-hop `r = ws[0]` / `one(xs[0])` twins warn *Mutation of ... while borrowed*. `_borrow_storage_root` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) keys a subscript by `_storage_key` of its object, which answers only a name or a one-hop field, so `ws[0][0]` files no loan at all -- the invalidation check has nothing to meet the `ws[0]` mutation. Not the rebind of the ROOT (`BUGS.md#nested-list-literal-alias-rebind-clobbers`). Fix shape: a place-keyed loan (`Place`/`LoanInfo`) for a multi-hop element, or at least a coarse loan on the root that every mutation under it meets. Probes `/tmp/agents/sm_r2/plain.py`, `src.py` (2026-09-26). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud; also a silent copy and a slicing difference) A lambda body gets only part of the checks a `return` statement gets.** [`lambda-body-partial-return-checks`]
  **Borrow of a body temporary -- now rejected.** At a GENERIC result
  slot (`key=` of `sorted` / `min` / `max`, `map`'s function, a user
  generic's `Fn[[T], U]`) a lambda keeps its body's borrow as its
  result, so `sorted(rs, key=lambda r: mk(r).get_inner())` with
  `def mk(r: Rec) -> Own[Rec]` rendered
  `[](const Rec& r) -> const Inner& { return mk(r).get_inner(); }`, a
  reference into a value destroyed at the lambda's return (segfault).
  Sema now rejects that shape ("Cannot return a borrow of a temporary
  from this lambda ...") when the borrow PROVABLY roots in a fresh
  owned value the body creates -- a constructor, an `Own[T]` call (a
  call through an `Fn` value included), a container literal, or a
  field, subscript or borrow-returning method of one, following the
  recorded call-lending facts (`TypeCompatibility.borrow_temp_root`,
  `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`). The verdict is taken in the
  workspace-wide finalize pass, once every callee's borrow facts are
  recorded, so a lambda at module level or in a method analyzed before
  its callees is judged the same way; an overload trial never sees it.
  Pinned by `tests/cases/calls/error_lambda_key_temp_borrow` (method
  body), `error_lambda_key_temp_field` (field body) and
  `error_lambda_key_temp_module_level`; the shapes that stay borrows,
  or copy a scalar out, by
  `tests/cases/calls/lambda_generic_result_borrow`. CPython runs the
  rejected programs, so the reject is a stopgap. **What remains:**
  (a) a temporary-rooted body should return BY VALUE instead of
  rejecting; that needs lowering support too, since a by-value record
  result from a lambda body rejects at lowering by BODY SHAPE, whatever
  the callee: a bare field or method read at a by-value result rejects
  (`field.result_type` / `method.ret_type`); wrapped in `copy(...)`, a
  method read (`copy(mk(r).get_inner())`) lowers while a field read
  (`copy(mk(r).inner)`, `copy(Rec(r.n).inner)`) still rejects at
  `field.result_type`, at `sorted`, `map`, `min` and `max` alike. The message
  therefore names the one remedy verified for both shapes at every
  callee: a def with an `Own[...]` result that binds the value to a
  local and returns `tpy.copy(...)` of it (`copy(mk(r).inner)` returned
  straight from a def rejects at `field.result_type` too). (b) A borrow
  rooted in a call with NO borrow facts at finalize time (an opaque
  stub, a callee sema never analyzes) proves nothing and is kept as
  before. (c) A borrow of a shared handle's payload through a TEMPORARY
  handle (`map(lambda c: c.rc.clone().get(), cs)`) is rejected although
  the payload outlives the handle -- the verdict the def twin already
  gets (`BUGS.md#shared-handle-payload-through-temp-rejected`). The walk
  follows the recorded borrow facts only, so an owning handle (`Box`,
  `Rc.new(...)` held by nobody else) and a record with a pointer-bearing
  field are rejected alike; an interim "may hold a pointer" exemption
  was dropped because it let those dangle silently. (d) **Silent copy:** `xs = [1, 2]`
  then `f: Callable[[], Own[list[int]]] = lambda: xs` copies the list
  with no diagnostic, where the nested-def twin
  (`def g() -> Own[list[int]]: return xs`) warns "copies list[int32]
  into owned storage; use copy() to make this explicit" (probe
  `/tmp/agents/dd/r1fix/own.py`). (e) **Slicing:** at a plain `Base`
  result, a def's `return Derived()` is rejected (a `-> Base` def
  returns by reference), while the lambda returns by value and slices
  the object with only the "upcast narrows" warning (documented in
  `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`, lambda return context). Cause: the
  lambda body is analyzed inline in the enclosing function's tracking
  state, so the name-keyed facts the return pipeline
  (`StatementAnalyzer._analyze_return_value`) consults -- parameters,
  locals, borrow facts -- answer for the ENCLOSING function; two review
  rounds of per-oracle overrides did not converge. The full fix
  analyzes the lambda body under its own frame (TODO.md, "Analyze a
  lambda body under its own frame") and then runs the def return's
  checks on the body through one helper keyed on the result slot.
  Found 2026-09-25; the reject landed 2026-09-26. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free) `map` over a source whose elements are owned temporaries, with a function returning a borrow of its argument, dangles.** [`map-owned-element-borrow-result-dangles`]
  `def tail(w: str) -> StrView: return w[1:]` then
  `for v in map(tail, words())`, where `words()` yields owned `str`
  (a generator, or any source whose element is an `Own` value): the
  runtime `map_iter` / `owning_map_iter` / `map_multi_iter`
  (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/itertools.hpp`) destroys each element right
  after calling the function, so the view it returned points into freed
  storage by the time the loop body reads it (the probe prints garbage
  bytes in place of each word's head). `tail`'s signature is sound --
  the result borrows its argument -- but nothing relates the map's
  result to its source's element lifetime. The lambda spelling
  (`map(lambda w: w[1:], words())`) is refused in sema, because a
  lambda's parameter never counts as durable for a view. A tuple twin
  over `Iterator[tuple[int32, Own[Rec]]]`,
  `map(lambda p: p[1].inner, pairs())`, passes sema with an
  `Inner&` result and is stopped only by a C++ binding failure (the
  lambda takes the element tuple by rvalue reference and
  `owning_map_iter` passes an lvalue). Fix shape: `map` holds the
  current element while its result is live, or the signature relates
  the result's provenance to the source's element lifetime and an
  owned-element source takes the value. Probes
  `/tmp/agents/ltb/port/q_mapdef.py` (def twin),
  `/tmp/agents/ltb/port/tupmap.py` (tuple twin), reproduced 2026-09-26
  on `1ea64345ea`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (unsound sema, caught only by accident in C++) A lambda's borrow result escapes through a generic callee's return.** [`lambda-borrow-escapes-generic-return`]
  With `def apply[T, U](x: T, f: Fn[[T], U]) -> U: return f(x)`,
  `def g() -> Inner: r = Rec(3); x = apply(1, lambda i: r.get_inner()); return x`
  is admitted by sema: the lambda keeps its borrow of the captured local
  `r` (a by-reference capture is not freed by the lambda), and nothing
  records that `apply`'s result carries that borrow, so the return's
  dangling check sees an opaque call where the def twin rejects the
  borrow of a local. It fails only in C++, because the generic result
  renders as `val_or_ref_t<...>`, which does not bind the `Inner&`
  return; a spelling that did bind would dangle once `g` returns. Fix
  shape: a generic call's result borrows what its callable argument's
  result borrows (the callable contract,
  `docs/CALLABLE_CONTRACT_DESIGN.md`). Probe
  `/tmp/agents/ltb/port/esc.py`, reproduced 2026-09-26 on
  `1ea64345ea`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] (spurious diagnostic) A named iterator-adapter local keeps its loan on the source past its last use.** [`named-adapter-loan-outlives-last-use`] `z = zip(xs, ys); out = list(z); xs.append(4)` warns `Mutation of 'xs' while borrowed ('append' may invalidate references)` although `z` is dead after `list(z)`; the program runs and prints what CPython prints. A `Span` local over the same list releases its loan at its last use (`sp: Span[int] = xs; print(len(sp)); xs.append(3)` is silent), so the adapter's loan is scoped to the local's lexical lifetime instead of its last use. The named `copy_iter(xs)` adapter did the same while `CopyIter` was briefly declared a borrowing view (see `BUGS.md#copy-iter-send-while-borrowing`). A named `zip` in a `for` head is a located reject (`stmt.for_each:iter.user_iterator.name`), so the shape reaches the checker only through a consuming call. Probes `/tmp/agents/nbv3/zipmut2.py` (warns) and `/tmp/agents/nbv3/cp2_p7.py` (the silent `Span` twin), verified 2026-09-24.
- **[HIGH medium, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free) A view built over an OWNED local, or over a local that only looks like an alias of a parameter, is returned with no diagnostic.** [`view-root-owned-local-dangles`] The dangle checks decide whether a view's root outlives the call from "can it be returned by value" (`safe_to_return`) or from binding provenance (`bp_is_param_derived`), never from whether the local is EMITTED as a borrow of durable storage or as owning storage. Shapes that compile and return a view of a dead local (verified 2026-09-24): `xs = p.copy(); sp = Span[int32](xs); return sp`; `sp: Span[int32] = xs; return sp` over such a local; `return Span[int32](p.copy())`; `xs = [n, n]; sp = get_span(xs); return sp` (the handle's `safe_to_return` counts a movable owned local as safe); and the `str` twin `s = p; v: StrView = s; s = s + "x"; return v`, which emits `std::string s = std::string(p); std::string_view v = s; ... return v;`. A fix attempted on branch `native-borrowing-views` (commits 5e46c10db3 / 111bacb632, reverted) showed why patching the predicates does not converge: each strictness fix exposed another shape, e.g. a local rebound from a parameter after owning a buffer (`ys = [1] or [2]; ys = p`) is an owned COPY (`BUGS.md#owned-local-rebound-from-lvalue-copies-silently`), so a provenance-based "alias of p is durable" rule dangled (printed garbage where CPython prints `70`). Fix shape: ONE fact, "this root is durable", decided from the local's emitted storage form (reference alias vs owned storage; for `str` locals the deferred storage verdict, `pending_view_storage_checks`), read by every dangle consumer -- the TODO.md unit "View constructors borrow their arguments; a view root is durable by its emitted storage".
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free) An escaping closure that captures a `bytes`, `Span` or dict-view PARAMETER bound to a temporary keeps a view of the dead temporary.** [`escaping-closure-view-param-capture`] `def mk(b: bytes) -> Callable[[], int]: def f() -> int: return len(b); return f`, called as `mk(bytes([1, 2, 3]))()`, emits `auto f = [b]() ...` with `b` a `::tpy::BytesView` over the argument's `::tpy::Bytes` temporary, which dies at the end of the calling statement; the closure outlives it. The escaping-closure capture check (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`, "Reject str/StrView parameter captures") rejects only `str` / `StrView` parameters, with the `String` remedy; every other borrowing view -- `bytes` (a `BytesView` parameter), `Span`, the dict views, a user `@native(borrowing_view=True)` type -- is captured unchecked. Fix shape: key that check on the parameter's view form (`is_borrowing_view_type` of the C++ parameter shape, which includes the `str`/`bytes` view forms), with a per-family owning remedy (`bytes` -> `Own[bytes]` or `bytearray`). Probe `/tmp/agents/nbv/clo.py` (prints `3` only because `len` reads the span's size, not its bytes), verified 2026-09-24.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT dangle, no diagnostic) A borrowing view returned through a `readonly[...]` or `| None` return type is never lifetime-checked.** [`view-return-wrapped-slot-unchecked`] `def f() -> readonly[StrView]: s = String("abc"); return StrView(s)` and the `-> StrView | None` spelling of the same body both compile to `return std::string_view(s);` over the dead local, where the bare `-> StrView` is rejected ("Cannot return StrView referencing a local or temporary"); `-> readonly[Span[int32]]` over a local list does the same, and so does a user `@native(borrowing_view=True)` type (`-> readonly[Cursor]` returning a local `Buffer`'s `cursor()`). The return check asks `_dangling_view_message(return_type)` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`) about the declared type as written, and `is_borrowing_view_type` (`tpyc/type_def_registry.py`) finds no TypeDef on a `ReadonlyType` or on an Optional/union over a view, so the wrapped slot reads as a non-view and no rooting check runs. Fix shape: peel `readonly` and the view members of an Optional/union before asking the fact, at the one site that decides the return and yield checks. Sibling of the view-inner optional owned-source entry in this section (an owned temporary into the same `| None` slot). Probes `/tmp/agents/bv/cases2/ro_sv.py`, `ro_span.py`, `/tmp/agents/bv/cases/sv_opt.py`, `/tmp/agents/bv/u/x_ro.py`, verified 2026-09-24. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT dangle, no diagnostic; WORSE since v0.5.0, which warned 'Result borrows from temporary argument') A view built over a temporary as a GENERATOR call's argument is hoisted to a named view of the dead temporary.** [`generator-arg-view-temp-hoist-dangles`] `it = h.gen(StrView(String("abc")))` with `def gen(self, c: StrView) -> Iterator[int32]` emits `std::string_view __tmp_1 = std::string_view(::tpy::String("abc"));` and then `auto it = h.gen(__tmp_1);` -- the `String` temporary dies at the end of the hoist statement, so every resume of the frame reads a view of freed storage. The same view bound to a plain local first (`v = StrView(String("abc")); use(v)`) is handled: the local is promoted to an owned string. Fix shape: hoist the OWNING temporary and view it (the promoted-local shape), or reject the view-over-temporary argument at a frame factory's view slot the way an explicit `v: StrView = make()` annotation is rejected. Probes `/tmp/agents/bv/u/gentmp_sv.py` (dangling) and `loc_sv.py` (promoted), verified 2026-09-24. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (unsound trait, no current reproducer) `CopyIter` is `Send` although it holds a borrowing iterator over its source.** [`copy-iter-send-while-borrowing`] `copy_iter(xs)` over an LVALUE source builds `::tpy::CopyIter<T, Source>` whose `inner` is `detail::arg_source_t<C&>` = `borrowed_iter_source<C>` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/copy_iter.hpp`, the same per-argument holder the mixed combinators use), a reference to `xs` plus an iterator INTO it; the TypeDef (`tpyc/type_def_registry.py`, the `tpy.CopyIter` entry) inherits the value-type `is_send`/`is_sync` defaults, so the trait says the adapter may cross a thread while `xs` stays behind. `CopyIter` is deliberately NOT declared `@native(..., borrowing_view=True)`: its borrow depends on the argument's value category -- a TEMPORARY source of any kind (a container, a view, a record, an iterator: `copy_iter(make())`, `copy_iter(map(f, xs))`, `copy_iter(gen(xs))`) is moved into an `owned_iter_source` and owned -- so the whole-type fact was wrong for that form (tried 2026-09-24 and reverted: it produced a false "Result borrows from temporary argument" warning on `copy_iter(gen(xs))`, dropped the `const` of a parameter read only through a named adapter, and kept a loan alive past the adapter's last use; probes `/tmp/agents/cp2/p3.py`, `p5.py`, `/tmp/agents/sm_ci/p4.py`, `p10.py`). The lvalue form's borrow belongs on the producing call, the callable-level borrow annotation (TODO.md, "Callable-level borrow annotation for native stubs"). Fix shape for the trait: derived from the holder the source picks -- `borrowed_iter_source` is not `Send`, `owned_iter_source<C>` is as `Send` as `C` -- which is a per-call fact (the producing call's argument category), or conservatively `is_send`/`is_sync` False on the TypeDef (as `SpanIter` has). Re-checked 2026-09-26: the TypeDef still inherits the value-type defaults. Found while declaring the borrowing-view fact on stubs, 2026-09-24.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free; pre-existing) A reference-type union local initialised from `copy()` and returned points into the function's own stack slot.** [`union-copy-local-return-dangles`] `def f(pet: Dog | Cat) -> Dog | Cat: q: Dog | Cat = copy(pet); return q` renders `::tpy::Union<Cat, Dog> __slot_1 = ::tpy::to_value_variant<...>(pet); ::tpy::Union<Cat*, Dog*> q = ::tpy::to_ptr_variant(__slot_1); return q;` -- the returned pointer union aims at `__slot_1`, destroyed on return; the caller reads garbage (a test run printed invalid UTF-8). `tpy.copy(pet)` renders identically (probe `/tmp/agents/b2me/v/v.py`). The copy is a FRESH value, so the return should carry it out by value (the storage-form return) rather than the borrow local's pointer form; the return-escape check does not see the slot the copy lives in. Found 2026-09-24 while pinning the `tpy.copy` spelling at an annotated union local.
- **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, toolchain-caught, no TPy diagnostic) A local bound to the result of a BORROW-returning operator dunder is bound `const`, so a write through it does not compile.** [`binop-borrow-result-alias-bound-const`] `xs = p + q` with `def __add__(self, other: Pool) -> list[int32]: return self.xs` emits `const std::vector<int32_t>& xs = ((p) + (q));`, and `xs.append(9)` fails in the C++ compiler where CPython appends to `p.xs`; the record payload (`x = p + q; x.n = 5` with `__add__ -> R`) emits `const R& x` and fails the same way. The const is the dunder's: sema infers `__add__` readonly (its body reads only) and const-projects its borrow return (`const std::vector<int32_t>& __add__(..) const`), and the caller's write through the bound alias never reaches that inference -- for the METHOD spelling it does (`v = h.view(); v.append(5)` turns `view` non-readonly and binds `std::vector<int32_t>& v`), so the gap is mutation propagation through an OPERATOR dunder's borrow return. The container face is a located reject (`binop.shape.+.record`): the binop result gate keeps the record slice so that it stays one; the record face has always compiled into the C++ error. The fix is sema's, one edge for both families, not a per-family fence. Found by the route-merge review.
- **[HIGH small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no diagnostic; resumable frames only) A `for` loop in a GENERATOR or `async def` that unpacks a pointer-repr `Optional[T]` element out of a tuple binds the pointer into the frame's COPY of the tuple, so a mutation through it never reaches the container.** [`frame-tuple-unpack-optional-element-aliases-copy`] `def gen(pairs: list[tuple[Optional[R], int32]]) -> Iterator[int32]: for r, n in pairs: if r is not None: r.n += n; yield r.n` -- iterating `gen(pairs)` twice yields `[4, ..]` both times where CPython yields `[4, ..]` then `[7, ..]`. The frame's unpack materializes the element as a value member (`__tup_1 = <elem>`) and lifts `r = ::tpy::optional_to_ptr(std::get<0>(__tup_1))` out of that copy; the same loop in a plain function takes `tuple_to_pointer` over the element lvalue and aliases correctly. A container element (`tuple[Optional[list[int32]], int32]`) takes the same frame binding and copies the same way (that spelling was a located reject, `res.local_storage`, until the Optional-ptr binding stopped being record-only). The fix is the frame unpack's: bind the tuple element by reference or lift the pointer before the copy, as the plain-function unpack does. Found by the route-merge unit.

- **[HIGH small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no diagnostic) A borrow-returning METHOD call as a tuple-literal element is stored BY VALUE, so a write through the tuple element is lost.** [`borrow-call-tuple-element-copies`] `v = (b.m(), 1)` with `def m(self) -> Rec: return self._r`, then `v[0].x += 1` (or, for a container payload, `v = (b.d_m(), 1); v[0]["y"] = 8`): the element captures VALUE, the tuple is `std::tuple<Rec, int32_t>{b.m(), 1}`, and the write lands on the copy -- TPy prints the old value where CPython prints the new one, no warning, no escape hatch. The element chokepoint already refuses the PROPERTY-getter spelling of the same read (`(b.p, 1)`, "an accessor result that lends storage has no render at an element slot") but not the method-call spelling, so the rule is written for one of its two faces. The record face is on master; the container face (dict / list results) took the same row on 2026-09-22 when the record-or-container gate admitted it, kept consistent with the record rather than fenced per family. Fix shape: one predicate for "a borrow-returning call captured by VALUE at an aggregate element" -- a call whose `call_returns_cpp_ref` -- refused at the chokepoint like the getter, for every kind (a language-rule change: a compiling silent copy becomes a located reject). Probe `/tmp/agents/unify/review/parity/p8.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. A third face, at a MODULE GLOBAL: `G: tuple[Rec, int32] = (b.m(), 1)` with a borrow-returning `m` -- sema's `_tuple_global_binding_type` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) records the element `Own` because the call is not an lvalue (`is_lvalue`), so the global takes storage and the `top_level.tuple_global_owned_literal` row copies the borrowed result (`G = std::tuple<Rec, int32_t>{b->m(), 1};`), silently; it copied before that row too, through the old all-storage global. The predicate keyed on `call_returns_cpp_ref` that the fix shape names must also be what that sema freshness test asks, or the global face stays behind.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic) A VIEW bound from a field of a loop element dangles once the loop's temporary source is gone -- in a plain function as much as in a frame.** [`loop-elem-view-outlives-temp-source`] `v: StrView = ""` then `for c in reversed(make_cells()): v = c.name` and a read of `v` after the loop prints garbage where CPython prints the string (3/3 runs). The same escape reaches a FIELD through a callee: `for c in reversed(make_cells()): k.take(c.name)`, where `take` stores its `str` parameter, leaves `k.seen` dangling with no diagnostic either -- the callee's field write is legal on its own, so the fact that has to travel is the ARGUMENT's provenance. Surfaced by the safety review of the loop-source ownership branch, 2026-09-21. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud) The escape analysis refuses `r = x` inside a `for` over a temporary in a generator, although the frame now owns that temporary.** [`frame-loop-elem-rebind-stale-reject`] `r = Cell(0)` then `for x in cells(): r = x` (no `break`, no `else`) in a generator stops with *reference to 'x' may outlive its storage; use copy(x) for an independent value*. The premise is stale: this loop binds a name out of its elements, so the frame HOLDS `cells()` for the generator's whole life and `r` points into storage that outlives every read of it. The same body with a `break` and an `else: raise` compiles and runs correctly (`tests/cases/generators/frame_temp_loop_source`), so the reject is about the shape of the rebind rather than about the lifetime. A combinator over a temporary (`for i, c in enumerate(reversed(make_cells())): r = c`) takes the same reject even with the `break` / `else` shape; the frame can hold the combinator now (its slot type is the source's own `decltype`), so once this check asks the prescan the shape compiles. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (use-after-free, WARNED and emitted) A `for` over a borrow-returning method called on a TEMPORARY receiver binds the loop to storage the receiver owns, and the receiver dies at the end of the loop head.** [`foreach-temp-receiver-borrow-dangles`] `for x in make_holder().get_cells():` emits `auto& __obj_1 = ::tpyapp::m::make_holder().get_cells();` -- the `Holder` temporary is destroyed at the end of that full expression, so every iteration reads its freed `cells`. Measured 2026-09-21: the generator form printed `read=11471694769` where CPython prints `read=11`, and the PLAIN-FUNCTION twin dangles identically (`read=12474396626`, `read=11556457979`, and one exit 139), so this is not about frames. - **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (missing safety diagnostic, UB; pre-existing) A NO-ARGUMENT nested def that grows storage the enclosing function is iterating gives no warning at the call.** [`nested-def-grows-iterated-self-field`] In a method, `def inner() -> None: self.items.append(5)` called as `inner()` inside `for v in self.items:` is silent (identical at 64feef9932). - **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (missing safety diagnostic, UB; pre-existing) A GENERIC callee that grows its list parameter only through ANOTHER call is not reported inside a loop over that list.** [`generic-transitive-structural-mutation-unchecked`] With `def gput2[T](ys: list[T], v: T) -> bool: ys.append(v)` and `def gput[T](ys: list[T], v: T) -> bool: return gput2(ys, v)`, `for v in xs: gput2(xs, 3)` warns *Passing borrowed container 'xs' to non-readonly parameter* but `for v in xs: gput(xs, 3)` is silent (`/tmp/agents/rv2_safety/p9.py`). Fix shape: an argument or receiver whose key is a PREFIX of a key holding an invalidating loan conflicts when the callee structurally mutates that param or its receiver (the callee's facts, `-1` for the receiver); the path-level refinement (only when the callee grows that field) needs field-granular structural facts. - **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (missing safety diagnostic, UB; pre-existing) A method call that grows its receiver only TRANSITIVELY is not an invalidating mutation of an iterated receiver.** [`transitive-receiver-growth-unchecked`] `for v in self: self.push2()` with `def push2(self) -> bool: return self.push()` and `def push(self): self.items.append(9)` (and `__iter__` walking `self.items`) compiles with no diagnostic, while `for v in self: self.push()` warns *Mutation of 'self' while iterating over it ('push' invalidates the iterator)*. `is_invalidating_method` (`tpyc/sema/receiver_calls.py`) reads only the callee's DIRECT structural facts (`direct_structural_mutated_params` containing -1): body analysis runs before the Phase-2 fixpoint. Found by the round-2 test-coverage review, 2026-09-23.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic; pre-existing) A `str` view bound INSIDE the body of a `for` over a generator stays a view although a later pull rewrites the record it was taken from.** [`view-in-generator-loop-body-rewritten-by-pull`] `for x in (1 for i in range(2) if rename(r) and i == 0): lbl2 = r.name` then `return lbl2` (with `rename` assigning `r.name` a heap-sized string) returns a view into the buffer the next pull frees, and the named-generator spelling `for x in gen(r): lbl2 = r.name` (`gen` calling `rename(r)` between yields) is the same. Fix shape: a loop over a producer whose body (or whose genexpr frame's body) may write storage that a view in the loop body borrows demotes that view, as a mutating call after the binding would -- the loop head is a call to the producer on every iteration. Found by the codegen review of the genexpr creation check, 2026-09-22.
- **[HIGH medium, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-free, order-dependent) A function that returns the result of a callee DEFINED BELOW IT records no `return_borrows_from`, so its own callers take its result for fresh storage.** [`return-borrow-of-pending-callee-unrecorded`] `def via(b: B) -> Rec: return helper(b)` (or `t = helper(b); return t`) with `def helper(b: B) -> Rec: return b.m` declared after it, then `for i in range(3): b = B(i); holder = via(b)` and a read after the loop: no diagnostic, TPy `100`, CPython `102`. With `helper` declared first AND both of them free functions the fact is transitive and the caller warns and hoists. Source order is not the whole of it: record METHOD bodies are analyzed in an earlier pass than free-function bodies (`Analyzer.analyze_bodies`, passes 6 and 7), so a method wrapping a free function (`def via(self, b): return first(b)`) records nothing in ANY order (`/tmp/agents/rev_full_safety/a_order.py`). The return arm's transitive rule (8b rule 3, `tpyc/sema/statements.py`) reads the callee's fact when the wrapper's body is analyzed, where it is still None, and records nothing; the alias spelling reaches the same place through an OPAQUE loan, which `mark_param_returned` deliberately does not follow -- recording every operand there made valid code a hard error by definition order. The caller-side escape check defers its verdict for exactly this reason (`ScopeTracker.settle_deferred_escapes`); a RECORDED fact cannot be deferred the same way, because later bodies read it. Fix shape: the designed one is `docs/ESCAPE_ANALYSIS_DESIGN.md` Future-Extension 8b-A -- record the return-call edges in Phase 1 and propagate `return_borrows_from` in the Phase-2 fixpoint beside `mutated_params`, which is order- and pass-independent and cross-module. It moves the readers that need the fact during body analysis (the scope-escape hoist decision, `pending-callee-precautionary-hoist`) behind the same deferral. A NESTED def is a third face of the missing fact, and there it is a silent COPY rather than a dangle: `def inner() -> R: return GR` (a module global, or any borrow the closure can hand back) then `r = inner(); r.x += 1` binds `R r = inner();` off an `R&`-returning lambda -- TPy leaves `GR` untouched where CPython mutates it, no diagnostic; the free-function spelling of the same body aliases correctly. Since 2026-09-22 the container twin (`return GL` from a nested def, `r.append(9)`) takes the same row and copies the same way where it used to reject. Probe `/tmp/agents/bmesc/pending_ret.py`, `/tmp/agents/unify/glob_ret.py`. Found 2026-09-20. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free, garbage output) A view local bound from a view-returning call whose callee's borrow facts are still pending is taken for durable storage, so a TEMPORARY argument dangles.** [`view-local-of-pending-callee-temp-arg`] In a record METHOD body, `v = first1(s + "-tmp")` with a free `def first1(s: str) -> StrView: return s` renders `std::string_view v = first1(str_concat(s, "-tmp"));` and prints garbage (CPython: the string); the same line in a free function owns (`std::string v = std::string(...)`). The tuple-literal twin `v = first((s, 1))` dangles the same way there. Same missing fact as `BUGS.md#return-borrow-of-pending-callee-unrecorded`, a different reader: this one decides a local's storage, so it cannot wait for the fact. Fix shape: fail closed for a callee whose fact is pending (treat every operand as borrowed, as `_register_call_result_borrow` does for its OPAQUE loans), or land the Phase-2 propagation the sibling entry describes. Reproduces on master adc2bb9f1b. Probe `/tmp/agents/u1r5/meth2.py` (`OV.view`). The field face: a view FIELD from the same call over a temporary argument, `self.v = peek(own(a))` in a method with free `peek(data: StrView) -> StrView` and `own(a: str) -> str`, keeps a view of the dead temporary and prints garbage (probe `/tmp/agents/r3review/parity/p18.py`) -- the analysis-order face of `BUGS.md#strview-field-view-of-temporary`. Found 2026-09-26 fixing the tuple owned-element view regression. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (SILENT use-after-free, garbage output) A tuple NAME argument whose C++ type differs from the parameter's is converted into a temporary, and a view result of it dangles.** [`converted-tuple-name-arg-view-dangles`] `t = (s, 5); z = first(t)` with `def first(t: tuple[str, int]) -> StrView: return t[0]` deduces `t` as `std::tuple<std::string, int32_t>`, and passing it to the `const std::tuple<std::string, ::tpy::BigInt>&` parameter materializes a converted temporary; `std::string_view z = first(t);` then points into it and prints garbage. Two defects at once: the int literal element resolves to `int32` although the tuple's only use is a `tuple[str, int]` slot, and a converting argument is not recognized as a temporary. Fix shape: treat an argument whose rendered type differs from the slot's as temporary backing (the tuple-literal owned-element rule, `LendSource.temp_backed`), and/or let the pending int element settle against the slot it is passed to. Reproduces on master adc2bb9f1b. Probe `/tmp/agents/u1r5/meth2.py` (`conv`). Found 2026-09-26 fixing the tuple owned-element view regression. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium] (rejects-valid, loud; a deduced view local owns instead) A view read off ONE element of a tuple parameter is blamed on an owned element of a tuple-literal argument that could back a view.** [`tuple-param-borrow-granularity-rejects-valid`] With `def nm(t: tuple[str, A]) -> StrView: return t[1].name`, `return nm((s, a))` rejects with `Cannot return StrView referencing a local or temporary`, `v: StrView = nm((s, a))` rejects the same way, and a deduced `v = nm((s, a))` owns (`std::string v = std::string(nm(...))`); the scalar twin `nm1(s, a)` (`def nm1(s: str, a: A) -> StrView: return a.name`) returns and binds the view. Two causes. (1) PRIMARY, for a `str`/`bytes` element: the tuple parameter holds it as OWNED storage (`const std::tuple<std::string, const A*>&`) where a scalar `str` parameter is a `std::string_view`, so `nm((s, a))` copies `s` into the tuple temporary (`std::tuple<std::string, A*>{std::string(s), &(a)}`) and that copy becomes a possible backing of the view. With the view element form of `docs/TUPLE_COMPLETION_PLAN.md` U6 (D3; TODO "A tuple element does NOT behave like the same type would as a singleton", instance (1)) the argument is `{s, &(a)}`, nothing is temporary, and this spelling is accepted like the scalar twin. Fix shape for (2): per-element return-borrow facts -- the callee records which element path of a tuple parameter its result borrows (`t[1]` here) and the lending rule reads the path, not the parameter index. Probes `/tmp/agents/sm_r5/over3.py` (return), `over4.py` (deduced local), `over11.py` (annotated view). Pinned by `tests/cases/tuple/error_tuple_param_borrow_granularity` in the temporary-element spelling, so it keeps pinning (2) once U6 lands. Found 2026-09-26 refining the owned-element rule. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

A direct write in the same body demotes the view; the closure's is analysed in its own body. The same hole without a closure is two parameters bound to one object: `def p_two(ba: bytearray, bb: bytearray): v = ba[1:]; bb[1] = 90` called as `p_two(x, x)` reads the write (`False`, CPython `True`). It changes which loans are filed (new mutation-while-borrowed warnings), so it is its own unit. Probes `/tmp/agents/rev_esc_arch/nest.py`. Found 2026-09-19. The lift is half done: since 2026-09-26 the per-source enumeration is `call_lend_sources` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) and `_register_call_result_borrow`, `_provenance_storage` and the scope walk all read it; what remains is the registration's missing nested-call arm (a source with no storage key should file the loans `lend_roots` names, as `_provenance_storage` already does, before the temporary warning is considered). - **[MED medium, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic; the fact does not exist) Nothing records that a callee STASHES a borrowed argument, so an argument that lends a dying receiver's storage is admitted whenever the borrow leaves through a channel other than the return value.** [`native-stub-declares-no-param-retention`] `arg_lend_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) admits an argument only when the callee is known not to keep it alive past the call, and it reads the two per-parameter facts sema owns for a BODIED callee: `return_borrows_from` (stamped at registration for a generator or coro factory from `generator_borrow_param_indices`) and `addr_escapes_params`. Those cover the borrow leaving through the RESULT and through an ADDRESS taken of the parameter. They do not cover a third channel, and it has two faces. **TPy body**: a body that writes a VIEW-typed argument into storage reached through `self` or through another parameter (`def stash(dst: Box, s: StrView): dst.v = s`) copies a `std::string_view` rather than taking an address, so neither fact fires; `stash(box, mk().head)` compiles on master and on HEAD and prints garbage past the SSO buffer where CPython prints the string. **Native stub**: a body-less `@native` / `@cpp_template` stub has neither fact at all -- `return_borrows_from` stays None because no body was analyzed, and `addr_escapes_params` is an empty frozenset meaning "not measured" rather than "does not escape" -- so the stand-in is the whole-SIGNATURE `signature_may_return_borrow`, which registration already uses the same way for a body-less native METHOD's receiver borrow (`tpyc/sema/registration.py`). The stand-in gets the free-call corpus right: `len` / `sum` / `any` / `sorted` / `str()` admit, `reversed` / `enumerate` / `zip` / `map` / `filter` / `itertools.islice` reject because their `Iterator[T]` return is a lazy view of the argument. It is nevertheless WHOLE-signature (a stub taking two parameters and returning a view of one refuses the lend at both) and blind to a stub that writes its argument into a global or a member. Because it is blind there, `measured_arg_callee` confines it to the free-call path: at a MEMBER call the receiver outlives the call and is the natural stash target (`acc.append(v)`), so a stub callee is not consulted at all and the argument fails closed. Fix shape: make retention a DECLARED per-parameter fact -- a `ParamInfo` field set by a decorator (`@retains(...)` / its inverse), read by `arg_lend_ok` ahead of the signature fallback and checked against the runtime symbol the way `@native` names are -- and, for a TPy body, extend the escape analysis so a view-typed parameter written into storage reached through another parameter or through `self` lands in `addr_escapes_params`. It also settles `sorted(...)` vs `list(...)`, which today differ only because one stub declares `-> Own[list[T]]` and the other does not. Probe `/tmp/agents/t1r5c/p/stash2.py`. Surfaced by the property-read normalization review, rounds 4 (C13) and 5 (W31), 2026-09-18. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. A third face since 2026-09-22: `it = iter(mk()); next(it)` -- `iter` now carries the Iterator-stub retention fact, so the binding files a loan on the temporary, and `temp_arg_kept_alive` (`tpyc/sema/iter_loans.py`) mutes the dangling-temporary warning for every Iterator-returning stub as if it owned its rvalue argument the way the five combinators do; `iter()` has no owning flavor (`tpy::__iter__` has no rvalue overload), so the handle dangles with no warning. The `for`/comprehension spellings of the same shape are located rejects (`iter.call.plain`, `_iter_rvalue_source`); only the binding is unguarded.

Reproduced 2026-09-15 at `84f61a9b57` with `/tmp/agents/adv3_rb/k6_readonly_global_write.py` (control `/tmp/agents/fn_pass4/k8_lexical_control.py`). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (warned dangling borrow, wrong output) A `readonly[T]` borrow whose RECEIVER is a temporary binds to destroyed storage at every position.** [`readonly-borrow-of-temporary-receiver`] `def mkreg(n) -> Own[Reg]` with an `@readonly def view(self) -> readonly[Point]`: `v = mkreg(1).view()` emits `const Point& v = mkreg(1).view();` straight-line and `const Point* v; ... v = &(mkreg(1).view());` when the first binding is inside a branch -- the `Reg` temporary dies at the end of the statement in both, and `v.x` then reads freed storage (prints 0 where CPython prints 1). Both positions emit sema's warning *Result borrows from temporary receiver object; the temporary is destroyed at end-of-statement* (`tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~280), so the divergence is DECLARED, not silent -- and the two positions agree, which is why neither is a reject. What the warning does not do is stamp the fact anywhere the lowering can read: `is_dangling_temporary_arg` (`tpyc/sema/iter_loans.py`) is evaluated for the message and discarded, so no downstream pass can refuse or materialize the receiver. Whichever is chosen must land at BOTH positions at once: refusing one and warning at the other is the two-verdicts-by-position shape this class keeps producing. Probes `/tmp/agents/p_ro_straight_temp.py` (straight-line) and `/tmp/agents/p_ro_hoist_temp.py` (branch-first). Pre-existing at the straight-line position; the branch-first position reached it when the blanket `if.hoist_const` reject was replaced by the const-borrow classification (`tests/cases/readonly/branch_first_const_borrow` covers the NAMED-receiver shapes, which are correct and alias as CPython does). Found by /tpy-review of THIR batch 5. The `@property` spelling of the same read has no conceded tier and must not grow one: `p = mk().items` for a borrow-returning getter is a located reject (`local_decl.lends_from_temporary`), pinned by `tests/cases/records/error_property_off_temporary_receiver`, because the value-category rule asks both the accessor's return convention AND the receiver's category. Batch 6 briefly lost the second question and emitted `std::vector<int32_t>& p = mk().items();` (exit 139) for the monomorphic getter and its generic bare-`T` twin alike; whichever way this entry is settled has to settle that spelling with it. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. **Scope note (2026-09-18):** this entry is the METHOD spelling only. An accessor read through a `@property` off a temporary receiver is no longer warn-and-emit: it is a located reject at EVERY binding sink, because one `SinkForm` row answers for all of them and no sink that binds or holds a value past the full expression admits it. The positions and their pins, all under `tests/cases/records/`: local decl (`error_property_off_temporary_receiver`), branch-first decl (`..._hoisted_decl`), free-call argument (`..._arg`, which also carries the tag table), stub-method argument (`..._method_arg`), for-each (`..._foreach`) and comprehension (`..._comp`), field store (`error_property_view_store_temporary`), setitem value (`..._setitem`), `with` manager (`..._with`), return (`..._return`), `match` subject (`..._match`), module global slot (`..._global`), generator frame slot (`..._frame`); plus the aggregate ELEMENT slot, which is refused by a wider rule that holds off a NAMED receiver too (`error_property_elem_lends_storage`). TRANSIENT reads stay admitted -- `print(len(mk().items))`, `mk().items[0]`, `f"{mk().name}"`, `mk().items.count(1)`, a `+=` source, a dict key, a membership needle. An ARGUMENT asks the CALLEE rather than the position: admitted when the callee provably reads it during the call (`len` / `sum` / `any` / `sorted` / `str()` / `list()` / a user function taking a view), refused when it RETAINS (`reversed` / `enumerate` / `zip` / `map` / `filter` / any generator or coro factory, pinned by `..._retaining_builtin`). `async with` over a getter is unprobeable for this fact: the resumable `with`-manager lowering refuses any call-shaped manager first (`res.with_manager`), on master and here alike. Whether the spelled-method tier should follow is this entry's decision. Widening `lends_from_dying_source` to spelled calls (receiver or argument per `return_borrows_from`) flips at least `iterators/warn_comp_iter_mutation` and the three `records/error_property_off_temporary_receiver_{arg,foreach,method_arg}` cases (partial measurement, 2026-09-26). A one-level version of that fact is also not enough for a comprehension source (`BUGS.md#borrow-call-comp-source`).

- **[HIGH small] (silent use-after-scope, no diagnostic) A for-each over a borrow-returning METHOD read off a TEMPORARY receiver iterates a destroyed object.** [`property-off-temporary-receiver-iterated`] `def mk() -> Own[H]` with `def items_m(self) -> list[int32]: return self.xs`, then `for r in mk().items_m(): print(r)` emits `auto& __obj_0 = mk().items_m();` and builds the begin/end pair off it: the `H` temporary dies at the end of that statement, ASAN (g++-14, `-fsanitize=address`) reports `stack-use-after-scope` in `vector::begin()`, and the loop prints nothing where CPython prints every element.
