- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (rejects-valid, loud) The dangling-tuple-return root check never resolves an ALIAS hop under a FIELD borrow's dotted key.** [`field-borrow-root-skips-alias-hop`] `def via_alias(pbox: PBox) -> tuple[Counter, Counter]` whose body is `b1 = pbox` / `t = b1.pair` / `return t` is rejected with `Cannot return this tuple: its non-value elements are returned by reference into storage owned by the function`, while the direct spelling `t = pbox.pair` / `return t` is accepted. `t` borrows the storage KEY `b1.pair`; `_storage_root` cuts that to `b1`, and `_name_is_param_or_global('b1')` is False because `b1` is a local -- nothing asks what `b1` itself aliases, though its ALIAS loan on `pbox` is in the borrow graph. The returned pointers are rooted in parameter data and outlive the call, so the program is safe. Fix shape: resolve the dotted key's root through the borrow graph before the param-or-global test, i.e. ask for the roots of `b1` rather than accepting `b1` as one. Pre-existing: identical on master. This also MASKS a graph-level defect fixed on the capture-attribution branch -- a capture re-seated through two aliases of ONE storage used to resolve one path to an intermediate alias name; every source program that would expose it is rejected by this entry first, so the guard for it lives in `tpyc/test_borrow_roots.py`. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_alias_hop3.py` (both spellings in one file). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the capture-attribution branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (a premise, not an observed divergence) A `ValueType` record carrying a `Ptr[T]` field takes every "this is a value, so the copy is independent" exemption while both copies keep pointing at the same pointee.** [`value-type-ptr-field-aliases-through-copy-exemption`] `PtrType.is_value_type()` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) is True unconditionally, so a `class Handle(ValueType)` with a `p: Ptr[Node]` field passes value-type field validation; a `T: ValueType`-bounded generic then copies it into an owning slot with no diagnostic and the two Handles share the Node. Probe `/tmp/agents/final/valuetype_ptr_probe.py` prints `99` after mutating through the original's pointer -- re-measured 2026-09-08. The exemption sites are the owning-slot sinks' `_is_value_type_param` guard (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`, insert / `Own[T]` parameter / `Own[T]` return) and, more broadly, every reader that concludes independence from `is_value_type()`. **Not a CPython divergence**: both sides share the pointee, and TPy forbids writing a `ValueType` record's plain fields, so no probe distinguishes the two -- what is wrong is the PREMISE the silence rests on, which makes the exemption unsound for any future consumer that acts on "copies are independent" (and misleads a reader of the code today). Fix direction: a value type whose reachable fields include a mutable `Ptr` is copy-independent only in its own storage, so the copy-independence predicate needs to be distinct from `is_value_type()` rather than borrowed from it; the `Ptr` field itself already has the aliasing entries in this section as siblings. Predates the branch that documented the exemption. Found by the tail review of the unit-4 closing fix 2026-09-08. Re-rated MED -> LOW 2026-09-09: `Ptr` stays a value type (copied by value, like a view), the shape occurs once in the whole tree (`tpy.coro.Waker`, deliberately), and no consumer acts on copy-independence today; the entry stands as the design note that copy-independence needs its own predicate when one does.

- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic) Unpacking a `readonly[tuple[Own[T], int32]]` PARAM binds a MUTABLE alias of its element, so a write through the target mutates through a readonly param with no diagnostic.** [`readonly-own-tuple-param-unpack-mutable-alias`] `def f(p: readonly[tuple[Own[Box], int32]]) -> int32: x, k = p; x.n = 9; return p[0].n` renders `auto __tup_1 = ::tpy::tuple_to_pointer<std::tuple<Box*, int32_t>>(p); auto&& x = ...` -- a non-const `Box*` off a readonly param -- and compiles; the write is visible in the callee (the param is the `&&` owned-tuple ABI, so the caller cannot observe it). Before the live-source unpack borrowed (2026-09-22) the element was copied out, so the write hit a copy; now it hits the param. The non-`Own` twin `readonly[tuple[Box, int32]]` is refused outright (`Cannot unpack non-tuple type`), so the readonly contract is enforced at the wrong shape and skipped at this one. **Fix shape:** the unpack target's borrow inherits the source's `readonly` (as `x = items[0]` off a readonly container does), so the lift spells `const Box*` and the write is rejected at sema. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the U1 unpack fix.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent dangling views, no diagnostic) `list()` over an iterator of `StrView`/`BytesView` collects borrows rooted in the generator frame, which is destroyed once the iterator is exhausted.** [`collect-iterator-of-views-into-dead-frame`] `xs = list(g("AbCd"))` for a `def g(s: str) -> Iterator[StrView]` that yields views of its own frame locals prints `['+\x00\x00\x00', ...]` where CPython prints `['ABCD', 'abcdpadding padding ...']` (`/tmp/agents/r6_verify/m8_collect.py`); the param-derived twin, a generator yielding slices of its `str` param, prints the same kind of garbage (`m9_param_collect.py`, against CPython's `['ello there general kenobi', ...]`). Both verified 2026-09-17. The FOR-LOOP consumer of the same generator is correct -- a borrow yield is live exactly until the consumer's next step, which is the contract the loop honours and `list()` does not: the seam retains each view past the frame's death instead of materializing the owned form the collection needs. The comprehension spelling reaches no seam at all (`[x for x in g(...)]` reports *not yet supported ... (expr.list_comp)*), so `list()` is the one accepting path. Sibling of [`list-over-generator-copies-ref-elems-silently`] at the same seam -- there a REFERENCE element is silently copied where copying is wrong, here a value-typed VIEW is silently retained where copying is right -- both being the `list()` / `set()` / `dict()` constructor not reading the owning-slot verdict the element store elsewhere reads; one fix shape covers them. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (latent lifetime narrowing) An `Own[P]` static-protocol argument at an AWAIT position is captured BY REFERENCE where the pre-cutover emitter moved it in.** [`own-static-protocol-frame-capture-borrows`] Scoped 2026-09-09 to the await-arg position: the frame's own PARAM capture is fine and is now admitted (`res.param_type:own_protocol.static` is gone -- the field is the deduced `T_items items;` and the call's `std::move(...)` makes it a value), while the await-arg slot keeps a reject of its own, `res.await_param_type:own_protocol.static`. What still reproduces (with that carve-out lifted): `async def inner(s: Own[Sink]) -> int32` awaited from `async def outer(s: Own[Sink]) -> int32: v = await inner(s)` emits `std::optional<__coro_inner<::tpy::await_arg_capture_t<decltype((s))>>> __sub_0;` + `__sub_0.emplace(s);` -- a bare lvalue, so `await_arg_capture_t` deduces a reference and the sub-frame BORROWS what the slot says it owns; the AST oracle at `e5e9274af` emitted `__sub_0.emplace(std::move(s));`. Not only the forward: an argument sema has decided to COPY at the `Own` slot renders as the copy temp's lvalue too (`__sub_0.emplace((*p));` for a conformer used after the await, alongside the "copies Printer into owned storage" warning), so the promised copy would silently become an alias -- which is why the carve-out keys on the SLOT type, not on the argument's. An argument sema MOVES renders `std::move(...)` and does own correctly, but that decision is not visible at the gate. Safe as shipped only because a parked sub-future is emplaced in place and never moved; any change that relocates one, or a caller whose conformer dies before the frame, turns it into a dangling capture with no diagnostic. Same family as the frame-captures-a-borrow entries above (locals, `self`, tuple elements, `Ptr[T]` params); this is the `Own[P]` protocol-arg face. Fix shape: propagate the ENCLOSING frame's deduced form into the sub-future field (spell `__coro_inner<T_s>` and `emplace(std::forward<T_s>(s))` where `T_s` is the outer frame's own template param) instead of re-deducing off the argument expression -- an `Own` slot should move. Repro `/tmp/agents/ownproto/p18_own_proto_forward2.py`, copy-temp variant `p29_await_own_copy_temp2.py`; the reject is pinned by `tests/cases/async/error_own_protocol_await_forward`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent wrong output) A live element borrow is not invalidated by a subscript-assign write -- through a user-record `__setitem__` AND on a builtin `list` -- so the write lands THROUGH the borrow.** [`setitem-write-under-live-element-borrow`] Builtin witnesses (2026-09-03, both unwarned): `xs = [Node(1), Node(2)]; kept = xs[0]; xs[0] = Node(42); print(kept.n)` prints 42 where CPython prints 1; and `kept = xs[0]; xs[0] = None` on a `list[Node | None]` destroys the element under the alias and prints garbage (the `None` store into a pointer-repr Optional element was admitted by THIR that day; rejecting only that spelling while the plain sibling is accepted would be inconsistent, so the row stays and this entry is the gate -- `tests/cases/optional/setitem_optional_elem` deliberately aliases a different element). The original user-record witness: `p = lst[0]` then `lst[0] = Point(42)` on an `ArrayList[Point, N]` emits `Point& p = lst[0];` followed by `::tpy::__setitem__(lst, 0, Point(42));`, and `ArrayList.__setitem__` drops the old element and placement-constructs a new one in that same storage -- under the live reference. Built and run it prints `42`; CPython prints `1`, because rebinding `lst[0]` there leaves the object `p` names untouched. The borrow tracker DOES register the loan -- swapping the write for `lst.append(...)` on the same source warns `Mutation of 'lst' while borrowed ('append' may invalidate references)` -- so the gap is the subscript-ASSIGN arm in `tpyc/sema/statements.py`: it does not treat an element overwrite as invalidating, for a user `__setitem__` or for the builtin container, where the method arm does. That makes the diagnostic's absence misleading rather than merely missing: the neighbouring mutation is warned, so silence reads as safety. **PRE-EXISTING** -- byte-identical on the pre-cutover checkout. Fix shape: treat a subscript assign as an invalidating mutation of the receiver (builtin containers and user `__setitem__` alike), the same way an invalidating container method already is; pin the diagnostic, not the garbage (the divergence is use-after-destroy, so the printed value is not stable). Repro `/tmp/agents/grind2/probes2/borrow_setitem.py`; control (warns) `/tmp/agents/grind2/probes2/borrow_append.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. A user `__setitem__` that GROWS its receiver (appends to a field) now warns like the named method (the subscript-assign arm asks the receiver-call loan check for a user record); the in-place overwrite above, which grows nothing, is what stays silent.

- **[MED small] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic) A non-escaping (`Fn`) closure is captured BY REFERENCE, but nothing stops the callee from STORING it, so the capture outlives what it points at.** [`fn-slot-closure-stored-by-callee`] An `Fn` SLOT is documented as non-escaping (the capture tables in `docs/CLOSURES_CALLABLE_DESIGN.md` label their two columns "Non-escaping (`Fn`)" / "Escaping (`Callable`)" and give the `Fn` column by-reference captures on that basis), yet the implicit `Fn` -> `Callable` coercion lets a callee put one in a `std::function` field: `def register(self, f: Fn[[int32], int32]) -> None: self.cb = f` accepts `r.register(lambda i: xs[i])` from a body whose `xs` is a stack local, emitting `r.register_([&xs](int32_t i) ...)` -- the stored callback holds a reference to a vector that dies at function exit. Built and run, the later `r.cb(0)` prints garbage (`720091396`) where CPython prints `1`; no TPy diagnostic. PRE-EXISTING and not frame-specific: the sync free function is the reproducer above, and the resumable-frame position emits the same by-reference entry (`[&xs = xs]`) under the same missing check, so admitting the frame form neither created nor widened the class -- the frame's own exposure is in fact narrower, since a frame LOCAL of reference type still rejects at `expr.lambda` and only a borrowed PARAM (whose referent is the caller's, outliving the frame in every shape probed) reaches it. Related but distinct from the escape analysis that DOES exist for nested `def`s (`self.field = nested_func` / `container.append(nested_func)` / `return`, per the design doc): those check the CREATING body's own statements, while here the storing statement is in the CALLEE and the creating body only passes an argument. Fix shape: an `Fn` parameter a callee stores is escaping, so either propagate that fact back to the argument (a per-`FunctionInfo` 'stores this param' bit consulted at the lambda argument, forcing the by-value capture the `Callable` slot already gets) or reject the coercion of an `Fn` param into storage. Repro `/tmp/agents/fr14/store_fn_sync.py`; the frame twin `/tmp/agents/fr14b/store_fn_frame.py` is correct only because its referent outlives the frame. Found by the fix round on the frame lambda capture rule 2026-09-10. **Blocked on a design decision, not on analysis** (2026-09-10): the design doc promises nothing about an `Fn` VALUE escaping -- its "Implicit `Fn` -> `Callable` Coercion" section states the coercion is legal "passed to a `Callable` parameter or stored in a `Callable` field", and its worked example IS this shape (`def process(f: Fn[...]): store_callback(f)` into `self.handler = cb`), repeated as resolved decision 4. Either fix therefore rewrites that section: rejecting the coercion at storing sinks costs the safe callers too (a named function or a non-capturing lambda at an `Fn` slot borrows nothing), and propagating a 'stores this param' bit back to the argument silently turns `[&xs]` into `[xs]`, flipping the caller-visible mutation that `nested_def/container_params` and `nested_def/lambda_in_gen_method` pin. Note also that an `Fn` value legitimately outlives the call today with no `Callable` in sight (`itertools.takewhile` moves its predicate into a RETURNED generator frame; `map`/`filter` do the same), so only the STORING sink is the violation. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`, not a patch.

- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (silent memory unsafety, no diagnostic) A loan on a record local the LOOP BODY declares outlives that local's per-iteration storage.** [`loop-body-storage-outlived-by-loan`] `for i in range(2): q = Point(i); loan = take_ptr(q)` then `loan.bump(); print(loan.x)` emits `Point* loan;` before the loop and `Point q = Point(i); loan = &q;` inside it -- `q` is block-scoped per iteration, so `loan` is dangling at the closing brace. Built and run, the read through `loan` yields whatever the dead storage happens to hold -- one observed run printed `p4a: 100` where CPython prints `p4a: 101`, but the value is not reproducible; the CLASS (a read of freed storage) is what the entry pins. With a post-loop `q = Point(50)` added the read is equally dead, and there not even the alias-rebind clobber warning fires, because the loan and the rebound storage name the same already-dead object. Repro `/tmp/agents/fixround/p4a.py` and `p4a2.py`. The mirrored shape where only the HOLDER is body-declared is safe and pinned (`body_local_holder_section` of `tests/cases/records/warn_alias_rebind_clobber`): there the storage is a function-scoped slot, the loan stays valid, and the post-loop rebind warns. `_merge_loop_body_loans` (`tpyc/sema/init_tracker.py`) carries the body's loans past the loop on the holder's name alone; nothing asks whether the loan's STORAGE root outlives the loop. The plain-ALIAS two-arm loop spelling (`held = p` in both arms of an `if`/`else` under `for i in range(3): p = Point(i)`) is fixed: `p` now gets a function-scope slot and the rebind is warned, printing `2` like CPython (re-measured 2026-09-29). **Fix shape:** at the loop-exit merge, a body-end loan whose storage root is absent from the pre-loop `definitely_assigned` names storage codegen block-scopes to the body -- diagnose it there instead of carrying it out silently. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

  **The storage need not be the loop body's** -- any enclosing block that owns it does the same, and the loop is not required either. A holder bound to an element of an ARM-LOCAL list and read after the enclosing `if` prints `last 0` where CPython prints `last 8` (`/tmp/agents/review_safety_loop/q_if_local.py`); the same shape under a `with` whose `__exit__` reuses the freed storage prints `last 6` and `last 22684` (`p_if_with.py`, `m_with2.py`) -- all verified 2026-09-16. The NON-LOOP twins dangle identically (`/tmp/agents/round1_apply/x_noloop.py` prints `last 0`, `y_with_noloop.py` prints `last 25398`), so the loop is incidental: what makes the loan escape is the hoist carrying it past the block that owns its storage. The fix shape above is the one that covers all of them, with "the pre-loop assigned set" read as the assigned set before whichever block the promotion hoists out of. The resumable sibling, where the storage that dies is the loop SOURCE's holder rather than a body local, is closed: a generator or `async def` keeps a fresh loop source in the frame wherever the body binds something out of an element, and refuses the loop where it cannot name a slot for that source.

- **[MED] Resumable tuple-unpack loop over `list[tuple[P | None, ...]]`
  copies the element tuple where CPython aliases.** The frame holder is
  a bare `std::tuple<std::optional<P>, ...> __for_tup_N;` assigned BY
  VALUE from `*it++`, so the unpack targets (`a = optional_to_ptr(
  std::get<0>(__for_tup_N))`) point into a frame COPY of the list
  element -- a mutation through `a` is invisible in the source list,
  where CPython would alias `pairs[i]`'s objects. Read-only tests
  (iterators/gen_resumable_tuple_unpack_optional) cannot see it; a
  mutate-and-observe variant would fail cpy parity. Both codegen paths
  shared this render before the AST emitter was deleted, so it is not a
  lowering artifact. Surfaced by the 2026-08-04 review of the
  frame_opt_ptr unpack row.
- **[MED small] The `optional_str_to_strview` / `optional_strview_to_str` statement-expression shim binds `auto __ov = (<src>);` BY VALUE, so the produced `string_view` aliases the copy's heap buffer, freed at the closing `})` -- an ASAN-verified use-after-free at every non-SSO string.** The coercion templates in `tpyc/coercions.py` (`({ auto __ov = (x); __ov ? std::make_optional(std::string_view(*__ov)) : std::nullopt; })`, and the `std::string(*__ov)` twin) copy the source `std::optional<std::string>` into `__ov`, view INTO the copy, and destroy it before the consumer reads the view. Masked in the shipped case (`tests/cases/list/list_append_optional_strview_from_str`) because its strings fit libstdc++'s SSO buffer; reproduced under ASAN with a longer string. The template in `tpyc/coercions.py` is the single definition every lowering site wraps (`arg.opt_view_own_shim` in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` and its siblings), so the fix is one edit there plus the snapshot churn it causes. Fix shape: bind `const auto& __ov = ...` (view the SOURCE, not a copy) -- note the `strview_to_str` twin's `std::string(*__ov)` materializes and is safe either way, only the view-producing direction dangles. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, ASAN-verified; independently confirmed by safety-model) of the value-opt rekeying wave. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A `with`-target rebound from a nested def that reads the OLD target through `nonlocal` drops its manager -- the call site never mentions the name.** `def make_new(): nonlocal g; return Reg(g.n + 1000)` followed by `g = make_new()` after a branch-scoped `with Reg(1) as g:` -- the rebind's RHS reads the old `g` only through the closure, so the backward liveness walk kills `g` at the rebind before it ever reaches the closure's own `TpyNestedDef` statement (positioned before the `with`), `target_read_after` comes out False, and the already-declared target keeps a block-scoped manager. ASan-confirmed `stack-use-after-scope`; silently wrong values without it (`1 1` where CPython prints `1001 1002`). Verified pre-existing under BOTH the old source-order scan (its `_read_before_rebind` bailed the instant `g` appeared in `written_names` of the rebind, never considering that the RHS reads `g` through a closure) and the liveness pass that replaced it, so it is not a regression -- but it is the surviving face of the with-target lifetime family. Since 2026-09-30 every name a nested def captures is live at every statement, through rebinds (`BUGS.md#closure-captured-name-moved-at-last-use`), so the rebind no longer kills `g` and `target_read_after` should come out True; NOT re-verified -- the probe is gone, and the shape as written (`nonlocal g` with `g` bound only by the `with`) is now rejected up front (*No binding for nonlocal 'g'*), so a reproducer has to be rebuilt first. Same family as the `nonlocal`-rebind slot-model gaps above. Probe `/tmp/agents/probe_with/nonlocal_uaf.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the with-target liveness rebuild. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW medium, deferred: MIR] (conservative copy or reject, loud; no silent shape) A name a nested def or lambda captures is never moved in the enclosing body, even where no closure can observe it any more.** [`closure-captured-name-moved-at-last-use`] The rule (`tpyc/liveness.py`, `closure_pinned_names` and `_Walk.pinned`): a name any nested def or lambda of the body reads is live at every statement and every exit, through rebinds, and is never a last use; the finally-deferred return is the one exception: it still defers and moves after the finally, as CPython's pending return reads the object there (`BUGS.md#closure-run-after-finally-reads-moved-return` is the `__del__` hole in that). Every other consume of it takes what a live name takes: an unpack aliases, an owning argument copies with the `copies ... into owned storage` warning, a `return x` into an owning slot copies with the same warning (`TpyReturn.copies_live_name` makes the lowering spell `return Point(x);`, `return T(x);` at an open `Own[T]`, `return std::tuple<Point, int32_t>(t);` for a tuple name, since C++ would move a bare `return x;`), and a `@nocopy` one is an error. The return copy keys on the capture set itself (`ctx.func.closure_pinned`), not on liveness, so a closure-free return of a name still read on another path -- `try: validate(x); return x` with a handler reading `x`, a `return p` inside `for v in p.items` -- still moves. Known exception, still moving: a consuming-method receiver, `p.take()` on a captured `p` renders `std::move(p).take()` and a closure reading `p` afterwards sees the moved-from object (TPy `recv 3 0`, CPython `recv 3 3`, probe `/tmp/agents/r8fix/recv.py`) -- the receiver takes no `Own`-argument decision at all, `BUGS.md#consuming-call-borrowed-receiver-consumed`, MIR-gated with it. Generator expressions are outside the rule: a genexpr is a generator FRAME, and what its frame borrows -- its element reads and its source -- is the frame-lifetime question of `BUGS.md#generator-frame-borrow-outlives-consume`, not a closure capture. Sound by construction: where the closure runs -- a later call, a copy of the def handed on, a `finally`, an `__exit__`, a `__del__` after the return -- is never asked. This replaced three rounds of reach / escape / quiet-exit precision, each of which leaked a silent move (a handler's lambda consumed in the `finally`; a `__del__` running the closure after `return x` / `return (p, 1)`; a lambda passed beside the value it reads, `run(lambda: len(p.items), p)`, TPy 0 vs CPython 4). What remains is PRECISION -- a warned copy (or a `@nocopy` reject) where a move is safe: a consume on a path that leaves before the def (`if c: return sink(x)` above `def g()`), a consume after the last call of a def that never escapes, a `return x` with no `finally` / `with` / `__del__` able to run the closure, a consume after a rebind the closure never sees, and a lambda captured by value (a `Callable` local copies at creation, `BUGS.md#callable-local-lambda-copies-capture-silently`). Fix shape: a reachability and escape proof over the control-flow graph -- where the def can be defined, where it can run, and whether a holder of it outlives the consume -- which belongs on MIR, not on the AST walk. Pinned by `tests/cases/auto_move/borrowed_by_closure`, `tests/cases/auto_move/error_nocopy_closure_captured_forward`, `tests/cases/auto_move/error_nocopy_closure_captured_return` and `tests/cases/tuple/mixed_own_param_writes`.
- **[LOW small] (SILENT use-after-move; contrived) A closure run from a local's `__del__` after a finally-deferred `return x` reads the moved-from object.** [`closure-run-after-finally-reads-moved-return`] A `return x` leaving through a `finally` defers: the finally sees the object and it moves out after the chain, which matches CPython for a closure the finally runs -- so a captured name is deliberately still a candidate there (`collect_finally_return_candidates`), the one exception to `BUGS.md#closure-captured-name-moved-at-last-use`. Code that runs after the move still reaches the name: `h = Holder(lambda: grow())` (whose `__del__` calls `grow`, which appends to `x`) then `try: return x` / `finally: ...` prints `del sees 1` and returns 3 items where CPython prints `del sees 4` and returns 4. An enclosing `with` whose `__exit__` runs the closure is fine: its exit is part of the chain the move waits for (`exit sees 4`, as CPython). A closure that deletes the name is rejected (`tests/cases/exceptions/error_finally_closure_del_returned_local`). Fix shape: materialize the deferred value after the locals whose destructor can run user code are gone, or copy (warned) when such a local holds a closure capturing the name. Probe `/tmp/agents/capcons/afterfin.py` (`via_del`); pre-existing on HEAD. Found 2026-09-30.
- **[LOW small] (hidden copy, output correct; pre-existing) A `return x` of an owned name inside a `with` body copies it into the deferred return slot, unwarned, where a move is safe.** [`with-body-return-owned-name-silent-copy`] `p = P()` then `with Cm() as c: return p` at `-> Own[P]` renders `P __tpy_ret_0 = p;` ahead of the `__exit__` call and returns the slot: the value is copied although `p` is dead after the return and no closure reads it (probe `/tmp/agents/cgr6/p/p4.py`, `r_with`). The `try`/`finally` twin defers the same way and moves after the chain (`BUGS.md#closure-captured-name-moved-at-last-use`, its finally exception). Unobservable in output -- the caller receives an equal object and nothing else holds the original -- so the cost is the copy, and the missing warning a reader would need to see it. Fix shape: the `with` exit chain's return slot takes the finally-deferred return's move (the name is marked a last use there), or the slot copies with the owning-slot warning. Found 2026-09-30 narrowing the captured-name return rule to captured names.
- **[MED small] A local ALIAS of a `with` target outlives the manager with no diagnostic.** `with Reg(11) as v: keep = v` then reading `keep` after the block: the manager-keep decision asks only whether the TARGET's own name is live past the statement, so an alias that carries the borrow onward is invisible and the manager stays block-scoped -- `keep` reads freed storage (prints the `__del__` poison value where CPython prints the payload). The FRAME path is unaffected: `_prescan_with_manager_homes` promotes an owned manager whenever the target's frame field points into it, never consulting liveness, so only the non-frame `_with_manager_needs_hoist` gate has the hole -- which also means `_with_manager_needs_hoist`'s claim to ask "the same two questions" as its frame twin is false today. Reachable since the gate traded its structural conditions (`branch_hoisted` + `pointer_locals`) for the liveness question; master has no hoist at all, so it dangles there too. Two candidate fixes: drop the liveness condition from the non-frame gate so it matches the frame twin (safe, costs the earlier-destruction precision the liveness gate bought on ~6 cases), or extend the question to aliases of the target (needs the borrow tracker). Probe `/tmp/agents/lv_holes/c_alias_out.py`. Another face of the same liveness question (found 2026-09-24, pre-existing): a hoisted manager's ONE function-level slot re-emplaced on every loop iteration, so an alias kept from an earlier iteration (`with Res(i + 5) as t: if i == 0: u = t; continue`) silently sees the later manager (`/tmp/agents/lja/with_keep_prev.py` `keep_prev`: `a [6, 9] [6, 9]` where CPython prints `a [5] [6, 9]`). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the with-target liveness rebuild. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A MIXED owned+borrow tuple local in a RESUMABLE frame parks a raw pointer into caller-owned storage across every suspension, unchecked.** `p = make_mixed(b)` inside a generator / `async def`, for `make_mixed(b: Box) -> tuple[Own[Box], Box]`, renders `::tpy::frame_slot<std::tuple<Box, Box*>>` -- element 1 points at the CALLER's object, and the frame outlives the call that built it, so a parked generator whose caller-side `Box` dies reads freed memory on resume. Nothing ties the pointee's lifetime to the frame handle's. The MECHANISM is not new: `FrameLocalKind.PTR_ALIAS` has stored the same raw pointer for a plain non-value local since long before this shape existed, and this is the same family as the `__iter__`-captures-`self` / str-view / varargs frame-capture entries above -- what is new is REACHABILITY, since a mixed tuple local previously failed the C++ build in a resumable body and so could not be written at all. The shipped case (`tuple/mixed_own_tuple_frame_local`) does not open the dangling window either: `main()` keeps the caller's objects alive for the whole synchronous drive, so nothing in the corpus proves this safe. Fix belongs with the family, not with the tuple: a frame that captures a borrow needs its handle's lifetime tied to the pointee (or an escape check at the frame-construction site). **A `Ptr[T]` PARAM is a member of this family too**, and it is now demonstrably reachable rather than theoretical: a resumable frame captures the bare `T*` its sync sibling spells, and the frame outlives the call that built it, so a resume after the pointee dies reads freed storage exactly as the tuple element does. Proven live 2026-08-27 when `csv::_parse_rows` routed through it. A generic `T | None` PARAM joins the same list: at a reference-typed instantiation its per-instantiation slot (`::tpy::opt_param_t<T>`) IS the bare `T*`, parked in the frame across every suspension. No live dangle could be built for it 2026-09-08: both escape routes reject before the frame outlives the borrow -- `create_task(probe_async(c))` at lowering (`expr.call:call.arg_shape.own_protocol.dyn` since the qualified-call arguments joined the free-call path, 2026-09-28; the named form `co = probe_async(c); create_task(co)` compiles (it did before too) but was not driven past the caller's `c`) and returning the coroutine from a helper at sema -- so it is a member by shape, not a second reproducer. The family therefore covers locals, `self`, tuple elements AND params -- name all four when the escape check is built, because the shapes were found one at a time and each was believed to be the last. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the mixed-tuple decl-path fix.
- **[LOW small] An UN-ANNOTATED alias of an explicit `StrView`/`BytesView` binding is typed as the view directly, bypassing the view-vs-owned deduction entirely -- in a resumable frame it silently inherits the unchecked view contract with no visible annotation.** `view: StrView = items[0]; alias = view; await ...; print(alias)` types `alias` StrView at the assignment (the un-annotated local takes the source's nominal view type; `view_family_for_type` keys on owned/pending types, so no `ViewVarInfo` is ever registered), emitting a `std::string_view alias` frame field that dangles if `items` is mutated across the suspension -- while the same alias spelled `alias: str = view` now correctly promotes to owned via the frame view-local promotion (explicit-view LOCAL leaves are non-static in `_is_static_view_leaf`; PARAM leaves keep the borrow-checked contract). The hazard is bounded by the user's explicit view opt-in upstream (the alias is exactly as durable as the annotated binding it copies), but the inheritance is invisible at the alias site. Pre-existing route, sync included (harmless there -- same scope); the frame face is where it bites. Fix shape: route an un-annotated local whose init type is an explicit view through the same pending-view registration as the owned family, so the frame-unsafety term applies (a sync-only alias would still resolve to the view -- zero-copy preserved). Probe `/tmp/agents/prereq/aliaslaunder.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the frame view-local promotion fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code) `copy()` of a NARROWED pointer-repr `Optional[record]` name at the return sink drops the deref -- emits `A(a)` where `a` is `const A*`.** `def f(a: A | None) -> Own[A]: if a is not None: return copy(a)` -- the return sink classifies its copy source against `scope.admission_pointers()`, which deliberately strips pointer-repr Optional-record names, so `copy_plain_record_source` accepts the pointer as a plain-record source; the `BORROW_BIND` read then renders the name bare (by design there -- record receivers spell `->`), giving `A(a)` instead of `A(*a)`. The other three copy sinks classify against the full `lc.pointers` and exclude the shape. **Live on the DEFAULT path since the flip**, no longer dormant: THIR authors every body, so a plain `tpy` on the repro fails the C++ build with `invalid conversion from 'const A*' to 'int32_t'` -- the bare pointer is fed to the record's own `A(int32_t)` constructor (re-verified 2026-09-02; the `-> A` spelling in the original note is rejected earlier by the borrow-return check, so the reachable form spells `-> Own[A]`). Re-rated LOW -> MED on that: `copy()` of a narrowed Optional record param is ordinary code and the failure is a build break the user cannot route around, matching how the file rates the sibling `copy-int-literal-result` and `copy-array-literal-into-list-slot`. No corpus case exercises it, so the byte-diff and ratchet stay green. Verified pre-existing -- reproduces byte-for-byte on master 31c0cd431 in a clean worktree, so the copy-row helper fold (which preserved the asymmetry exactly) neither introduced nor widened it. Surfaced by the /tpy-review safety pass on the fold. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] An await-borrow through a BOUND handle registers no transitive alias: `c = s.get(); r = await c` leaves `r` untracked as a borrower of `s`.** The direct form (`r = await s.get()`) registers via `_register_call_result_borrow`'s TpyAwait arm (recursing into the awaited call), but a TpyName operand has no traceable roots at the await site -- the handle binding registered `c -> s`, and once `c` is consumed by the await only `r` remains, so a later move of `s` is no longer demoted. Narrow window (requires the two-step bind + a post-await consume of the source); the return-position sibling is fail-closed (`return await c` on a bound borrow handle is conservatively rejected -- a rejects-valid wart of the same shape). Fix shape: at handle-consume time, transfer (or copy) the handle's registered borrows to the await-result binder. Surfaced implementing the /tpy-review await-provenance fixes on the async borrow-return ABI branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A whole-container `Span` binding registers NO borrow, so mutating the container while the span lives warns nothing -- `sp = Span[int](xs); xs += [3]` (or `.append`) reallocates under a live span (silent UAF).** `Span[T](container)` construction is invisible to the borrow tracker: `_borrow_storage_root`/`addr_taken_roots` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) do not handle the `TpyCall` view-constructor shape, so no loan exists for the mutate-while-borrowed machinery to check (element/slice borrows DO register). Pre-existing and reachable via `.append()` on master; the pending-list `+=` fix widens the reachable surface (unannotated literals now resolve to reallocating vectors where the Array form refused to compile). Adjacent Span/view-lifetime entries below track element/iterator shapes but not this whole-container binding. Fix shape: register a view borrow at the `Span(container)`/view-constructor call, rooting through the argument like the slice arm does. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the pending-list aug-assign fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (SILENT use-after-free, garbage output) An ESCAPING closure capturing `self` holds a raw `this` that can outlive the receiver.** [`escaping-closure-captures-raw-this`] Sync nested defs / lambdas in methods now capture `self` as `this` (pointer, alias semantics); when the closure escapes the method (stored into a `Callable` field/container or returned), nothing ties the closure's lifetime to the receiver object -- if the receiver dies first the stored `this` dangles, where CPython's closure keeps the object alive. Record RELOCATION invalidates it too, and is far more common than death-before-call: a move of the receiver (container growth, `Own[T]` transfer) destroys-and-reconstructs the object, leaving the stored `this` pointing at the old storage. Sibling of the general escaping-ref-capture soundness class (local captures have escape checks; `self` has none). A lambda capturing `self` written straight into a field is refused in sema ("A lambda stored in field 'x' cannot capture 'self' ..."); two spellings of the same store are not: a nested def reading `self` stored into a field in `__init__` (`def get() -> int32: return self.n`, `self.cb = get`), and a `self`-capturing lambda bound to a local first (`f: Callable[[], int32] = lambda: self.n`, `self.cb = f`) -- after the object moves into a list (`hs.append(mk(3))`), `hs[0].cb()` prints garbage where CPython prints 30 (probes `/tmp/agents/r3review/parity/p14.py`, `p19.py`). Fix shape: one capture-set check at the store sink -- the field write refuses any closure VALUE whose capture set holds `self`, whatever spelled it, instead of the lambda-literal check it has now. Surfaced implementing the nested-def self-access fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW, latent, believed-unreachable] A generator/coro frame escaping the C++ block holding its hoisted rvalue-arg temp would dangle -- nothing ties the temp's scope to the frame's.** The call-site rvalue hoist (a reference-type rvalue arg to a resumable factory materializes `T __tmp_N = ...;` in the enclosing block, the frame borrows it) assumes the frame never outlives that block. A generator var assigned inside a loop/if body but hoisted to function scope (used after the block) would leave the frame's ref field pointing at the dead block-scoped temp. NOT reachable today: every route probed is independently blocked (cross-branch hoisted `Iterator[T]` storage codegen bug; the coroutine must-use rule; @dynamic protocols not supporting generator methods). Filed so the gap is not silently reintroduced-as-live when one of those blockers is fixed. Fix shape: emit the arg temp at the same scope the generator handle is hoisted to (or reject the escaping shape) -- a lifetime tie the borrow checker cannot express pre-region-model. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the readonly-resumable-param branch.
- **[LOW small] A `@readonly` method returning bare `self` (`-> "Cls"`) const-poisons the caller-side local only at the C++ level -- sema accepts a mutation TPy should reject.** `@readonly def me(self) -> "Box": return self; y = b.me(); y.v = 99` compiles at the TPy level and dies in g++ ("assignment of member ... in read-only object"): the C++ method is `const` and returns `const Box&`, but sema doesn't track the returned borrow as readonly (annotating the return `-> readonly[Box]` DOES reject correctly at sema). Toolchain-caught (loud), rejects-valid-diagnostic gap, not silent. Since the operator-dunder borrow-return fix, the OPERATOR face shares the gap: `c = a + b` with a plain `-> "Acc"` borrow-returning `__add__` binds `const Acc&`, and `c.n = 5` dies the same way in g++ instead of a located sema error (the `readonly[...]` spelling rejects cleanly at sema; `Own[...]` is the mutable-copy escape hatch). Fix shape: a readonly (incl. implicitly-readonly dunder) method's borrow return should be readonly-typed (or at least the caller-side binding const-tracked) -- same "readonly is sema-layer-only" family as the adjacent entries; one fix covers method and operator spellings. Reproducer /tmp/agents/glob/ro2.py. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model, verified by probe) of the identity-preserving-returns branch; operator face by the operator-dunder borrow-return fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW, latent, believed-unreachable] `foreach.consuming_iter` trusts sema's `stmt.consuming_iter_fi` unconditionally, with no re-derivation of movability.** `_for_consuming_route` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:1400`) emits the consuming/moving form (`own_iter(std::move(items))`) whenever sema set `consuming_iter_fi`, and nothing rechecks that the iterable really is a movable last use. The movability predicate still exists -- `_is_move_source` / `_is_move_source_facts`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:16419`, the `movable_locals` + `all_last_uses` join -- but the for-loop route never asks it, so a wrong sema fact MOVES the container with nothing to catch it. Believed UNREACHABLE: two /tpy-review specialists (cpython-parity + codegen-correctness) independently traced it to a single forward pass with no retroactive demotion of the same node id, so `consuming_iter_fi` and `all_last_uses` cannot diverge between sema-decision-time and lowering-read-time; no corpus case demonstrates a split. Filed so it is not re-litigated each wave. Fix shape (if ever reached): have `_for_consuming_route` re-ask `_is_move_source` on the iterable name, or make sema's decision authoritative and assert it there. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity + codegen-correctness) of the wave-12 auto_move consuming-iter arm.
- **[LOW, latent, deferred: MIR] A `Mutex`/`RwLock` guard outliving a dropped bare (non-`Arc`) `Mutex`/`RwLock` dangles (residual guard-escape hole after the runtime-lock backstop landed).** The guard holds a raw `Ptr` into the lock's heap cell with no ownership tie, so if a bare `Mutex`/`RwLock` is dropped while a guard is still live, the guard's cell pointer dangles. The two *access-without-lock* holes are now closed at runtime: guards carry a `_locked` flag (`lib/tpy/tpy/sync.py`, set in `__enter__`, cleared in `__exit__`), and `get`/`set`/`__deref__` raise `RuntimeError` if it isn't held -- so a guard bound without `with` (never acquired) or used after its block (`with ... as g:` as-var outlives the block) aborts loudly instead of racing the payload (`tests/cases/threading/guard_misuse_rejected`; the CPython stub mirrors the check). This remaining hole is the *lifetime* half -- the guard outliving the lock object -- which the runtime flag can't catch (the flag lives on the guard; the cell is already freed), so it stays region/lifetime-model-gated. Same family as the `@property`/generator borrow-escape entries below. Separately (unchanged): re-locking the same `Mutex` on one thread (`std::mutex` is non-recursive) deadlocks with no diagnostic. Not expressible as a passing test (silent UAF). Fix shape: tie the guard's borrow lifetime to the lock object (needs the region/lifetime model). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of Threading V3; access-holes hardened via /tpy-fix-bug. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` once the region model lands.
- **[MED, latent, deferred: MIR] A payload borrow extracted from a live `Mutex`/`RwLock` guard and used past the `with` block races/dangles even when the lock object stays alive (e.g. `Arc[RwLock[T]]`).** Distinct from the bare-lock guard-lifetime hole above: there the *lock object* is dropped; here the lock stays alive (the `Arc` keeps the cell), but a reference pulled *out* of the guard -- `with r.read() as g: leaked = g` (or `leaked = g.get()`, or a borrow of a reference-type field/element reached through the guard) -- outlives the guard's `with` scope and is then accessed with no lock held. The runtime `_locked` backstop only gates access *through the guard object* (`get`/`set`/`__deref__`); a raw borrow bound to an outer name bypasses it. Another thread holding a write guard concurrently then races it: for `Arc[RwLock[list]]` a writer's `append` can reallocate the buffer the escaped borrow points into -> concurrent-access data race + use-after-free, no diagnostic. Hits the canonical shared-mutable pattern; needs only a borrow bound past the block (a lock-discipline violation the type system doesn't catch). Same region/lifetime-model family as the bare-lock entry above and the `@property`/generator borrow-escape entries below -- the payload borrow's lifetime must be tied to the guard's `with` extent, which whole-function borrow facts can't express. Not expressible as a passing test (silent UAF/race). Fix shape: register the guard's `__deref__`/`get` result as a loan scoped to the guard's `with` extent and reject its escape (the MIR `Place`/`LoanInfo` model with extent-aware loans). The same escape extends to the LOCK HANDLE itself: `MutexGuard.raw_mutex()` (added for `Condvar.wait`) returns a `Ptr[_RawMutex]` that, bound past the `with`, lets a later `cv.wait()` unlock/relock a mutex outside any critical section -- corrupting lock discipline, not just racing stale data. (Access through the guard is gated by `_require_locked`; a raw `Ptr` bound to an outer name is not -- same whole-function-facts gap.) Surfaced by design review of the RwLock Sync bound (the safe `Arc[RwLock[list]]` case) + /tpy-review of the Condvar primitive. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` once the region model lands.
- **[MED, latent, deferred: MIR] A borrow taken from a nullable owning field survives that field being nulled/reassigned, then reads freed storage (silent UAF).** `raw = r.raw; r.close(); raw.read(4)` -- `Response.raw` (`@property` returning `self._raw`, an `HTTPResponse | None`) hands out a borrow of the held object; `close()` (and `with r:` `__exit__`) does `self._raw = None`, dropping it in place; the previously-taken `raw` handle (or a partially-consumed `iter_content`/`iter_lines` generator sourced from `_raw`) then reads freed/reused storage. ASan-confirmed garbage, no compiler diagnostic and no runtime check. Reachable via ordinary intended use: early-abort a stream then touch a saved `.raw`, or let an `iter_content` handle outlive a `with r:` block. Same family as the `@property` view-of-field-dangles-on-reassignment (606) and generator-captures-self (607) entries, but for a nullable OWNING field explicitly reassigned by a public `close()` -- this diff (`Response._raw`/`close`/`raw`/`iter_content`/`iter_lines`, all new) is what makes it concretely reachable. Not expressible as a passing test (silent UAF), so tracked here only. Fix shape: a borrow of a field must be invalidated when the field is reassigned/nulled (needs the region/lifetime model), or `close()`-style reassignment of a borrowed-from field must be rejected while a live borrow exists. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/streamreview/probe3.py`, `probe4.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of `requests` streaming. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` once the region model lands.
- **[LOW small] Calling a (correctly-const) method on a container-subscript element blocks readonly/const inference for the enclosing container, so a read-only method/param is emitted mutable.** `for name in other._store: self._store[name] = other._store[name].copy()` and `... self._store[name].matches(...)` -- the enclosing `CookieJar.update(other)` and `header_for(self)` bodies only READ `other`/`self`, but sema emits `void update(CookieJar& other)` / non-const `header_for` (vs the sibling `CaseInsensitiveDict::update(const CaseInsensitiveDict&)` which reads only tuple fields off the subscript and stays const). It cascades: `_request_on`'s `send_cookies: CookieJar` param is non-const purely because it calls the non-const `header_for`. NOT unsound (mutable-when-const-possible is safe) and no current call site is blocked, but it weakens the API (a caller holding only `readonly[CookieJar]` couldn't pass it as `other` or call `header_for`). Same const-receiver-drops-the-right-lowering family as the const-dict `in` entry this feature filed (its const container-read reference-local sibling has since been fixed); here it's a Phase-2 mutation-propagation gap -- a container-subscript method-call receiver isn't re-verified once the callee's readonly status resolves. Workaround: none needed (safe). Fix shape: after Phase-2 resolves a called method's readonly verdict, propagate it back to the subscript-receiver's container so the enclosing method/param can still infer const. Reproducer: `lib/tpy/tplib/requests.py` `CookieJar.update`/`header_for`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the requests cookie feature. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] Passing a self/param-field alias as a positional arg to a mutating FREE FUNCTION records no mutation-call edge, so the enclosing method can be wrongly inferred readonly (const receiver) -- ill-formed C++.** `v = self.inner; bump_val(v)` where `bump_val(x: Inner)` mutates `x`: `_record_mutation_call_edges` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`) resolves the arg only against the caller's OWN params (`name_to_idx`/`resolved`), never `"self"` or a `"self.field"` storage key, so the structural mutation of `self.inner` through the free-function call isn't propagated back to the receiver; the method infers `const` and the `const Inner& v = this->inner;` bind (or the `bump_val(v)` call passing `const Inner&` into an `Inner&` param) fails the C++ build. The method-call face IS handled (Phase-2 `_is_self_call_deferred` re-verifies a `r = self.inner; r.bump()` receiver), so the gap is specific to free-function positional args off a self/param-rooted alias. Toolchain-caught, not silent; pre-existing (reproduces at merge-base, independent of the borrow-local const-drop fix -- before the fix it hard-fails at the wrongly-const alias bind, after at the call site, same program). Workaround: mutate through a method call, or pass the field directly. Fix shape: `_record_mutation_call_edges` must resolve a free-function arg that is an alias of a self/param field back to that storage root and record the mutation edge, mirroring the method-call path. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the borrow-local const-drop fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW, latent, deferred: MIR] A generator `__iter__` (or any generator method) captures `self` by raw pointer; the frame dangles if the object is moved/destroyed while the generator is live.** `for k in headers` over a `CaseInsensitiveDict.__iter__` (`def __iter__(self): for lk in self._store: yield self._store[lk][0]`) holds a raw `this` in the generator frame; normal `for k in obj:` keeps `obj` alive for the loop, but binding the iterator and then moving/dropping `obj` (or iterating a temporary that is freed) reads freed memory. Pre-existing generator-captures-self pattern, not specific to CID -- but `__iter__` is the first method shape that exposes it to ordinary user iteration. No diagnostic. Reachable only by separating the iterator's lifetime from the object's (uncommon). Fix shape: a generator frame borrowing `self` must keep the receiver alive (or the borrow checker must reject an iterator that outlives its receiver) -- region/lifetime work, IR-gated. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the CaseInsensitiveDict `__iter__`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` once the region model lands.
- **[LOW small] The single-`__init__` `raise X(args)` arg loop skips `check_own_param`, so ownership diagnostics are silently missed on raise-site ctor args.** `tpyc/sema/statements.py` (~1855, the non-overloaded `record.init_params` branch) analyzes and coerces each arg but never calls `check_own_param`, unlike the overloaded-raise sibling loop just above it and every normal ctor path -- an `Own[T]` param on an exception's `__init__` gets no `@nocopy` rejection and no copies-into-owned-storage warning when raised (plain construction of the same class warns/errors correctly). Diagnostic gap only (codegen still copies/moves as usual); no repro committed -- needs an exception class with an `Own[T]` ctor param raised with a non-last-use local. Fix shape: add the `check_own_param` call to that loop, mirroring the overloaded branch. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the pending-arg-marks fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] A value->`Ptr` address-of coercion (`UPCAST_TO_PTR` / `record_to_ptr`) applied in a CONSTRUCTOR-ARG (or general call-arg) position does not register the borrow with the borrow-tracker, only in a local-var-decl init position.** `compatibility.py`'s `_check_compat` marks the source param mutated/addr-taken for these coercions, but the borrow-tracker's `add_borrow` registration is wired only for the var-decl-init site, so `T(&x)`-style argument coercions don't create a tracked loan. Latent: a program that takes `&x` as a call/ctor arg and then mutates `x` while the resulting pointer is live would not get the expected borrow-conflict diagnostic. Pre-existing, but first reached by routing struct-like `@builtin_type` ctors through the normal record-ctor path (`_make_waker` passes `&handle` into `Waker(...)`); dormant there because `handle` isn't mutated after. Fix shape: register the loan at the call/ctor-arg coercion site too, mirroring the var-decl-init path. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the @builtin_type-ctor normal-path routing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (parity, not unsound) Binding a borrow-yield's `next()` result to a local silently COPIES where CPython aliases.** `g = gen(); a = next(g); b = next(g)` over a generator that yields a borrow (`Iterator[list[int]]` yielding a frame-local / param / self-field) binds `a`/`b` as independent owned copies snapshotted at each `next()`, so a later mutation through `a` is not seen via `b` (or the source), nor vice versa -- CPython aliases all of them. No warning fires (unlike the `copies ... into owned storage` warning that DOES fire for a container-insert / field-store of the same value). Memory-safe (the copy owns its storage, so it survives frame destruction); purely an observable copy-vs-alias divergence. Pre-existing and independent of the frame-local borrow-yield feature -- it manifests identically for the param/self-field borrow yields that already worked; the consumer-side binding is what copies, regardless of the producer root. The for-loop consumer is unaffected (the loop var is a live borrow -- mutation IS visible on resume, matching CPython). **Fix shape:** either bind `next()` of a borrow-yield as a borrow (alias) under the same ephemeral-borrow rule the loop var uses, or at minimum emit the existing copy-into-owned-storage warning so the divergence is acknowledged + `copy()`-silenceable. Surfaced probing the yield-frame-local-borrow feature.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] Reassigning a narrowed value-Optional iterable to `None` inside a resumable-frame for-loop dangles the frame's iterator (use-after-free).** In a generator/async, `for x in b: b = None; yield x` over a narrowed `b: bytes | None` / `str | None` sets the frame's owned `std::optional<V>` field to `nullopt`, destroying the buffer the frame's `__for_it` / `__for_end` iterator fields borrow into; the next resume reads dangling iterators (UB). Sema's reassign-of-borrowed check skips value-Optionals (`OptionalType(bytes).is_value_type()` is True), so no diagnostic fires. This is another instance of the general resumable-iterable reassign-escape gap (a borrow into the iterable invalidated by reassigning/mutating it mid-loop) -- NOT a fresh root cause; the value-Optional shape became reachable when narrowed-value-Optional for-loop iteration was fixed (it was a C++ build error before). The non-resumable (sync) case is safe -- `string_view`/`span` iterators point into external data, not the optional object. Region-checker territory (cf. the async borrow-escape / `TaskGroup` work, IR-gated); do NOT re-attempt as a standalone value-Optional patch. Requires a deliberate reassign-while-iterating pattern. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the narrowed-Optional for-loop fix.

Fix shape: when the receiver is a `Ptr` whose pointee is a `Deref` type, still peel the inner deref chain for a readonly target (don't blanket-skip `PtrType`). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the deref-readonly-assignment fix.
- **[LOW small] An `unsafe_interior_mutable` field's readonly-boundary exemption only fires for a direct `self.<field>.method()` call, not a chained receiver.** `tpyc/sema/methods.py` -- the `interior_receiver` guard that suppresses self-mutation demotion checks `isinstance(expr.obj, TpyFieldAccess) and expr.obj.accessed_field_is_interior`.
