Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the interior-mutable feature.
- **[LOW small] `Rc[readonly[T]]`'s no-laundering guarantee has no C++-type backstop -- a `@native` function can mutate the payload.** `readonly[Rc[T]].clone()` yields `Own[Rc[readonly[T]]]` at the TPy level, but `ReadonlyType.to_cpp()` strips the modifier, so the C++ local is a plain `Rc<Counter>` whose mutable `get()` overload is callable. TPy sema enforces the readonly-payload contract (a TPy caller can't reach the mutable `get()`), but a `@native` function handed the C++ value, or any C++-level code, can. Pre-existing for `readonly[T]`-of-reference generally (readonly is a sema-layer/`const&`-param construct, not a deep C++ type), but materially worsened by the interior feature because `Rc`'s no-laundering soundness story rests on this invariant. No fix without a distinct C++ type for `Rc<const T>` (a real `Rc` instantiation over a const payload, vs the current modifier-strip); revisit if `@native` interop with `Rc[readonly[T]]` becomes load-bearing. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the interior-mutable feature.
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] `_view_source_is_temporary`'s method-call arm assumes a view-returning method borrows its RECEIVER, ignoring `return_borrows_from` arg indices.** `tpyc/sema/statements.py` -- for a `TpyMethodCall` whose return `is_borrowing_view_type`, the predicate recurses into `expr.obj` (receiver) only, unlike `is_dangling_return`'s method branch which checks each `return_borrows_from` index. A hypothetical view-returning method that borrows an ARG (not the receiver) with a stable receiver but a temporary arg would be classified non-temporary -> an inferred view local would NOT promote and an explicit `StrView` bind would not reject, binding a dangling view with no diagnostic. Latent: no method in scope today returns a view borrowing an arg rather than the receiver (str/bytes/Span views all borrow the receiver). Fix shape: mirror `is_dangling_return`'s per-index `return_borrows_from` traversal in `_view_source_is_temporary` (and ideally consolidate the two -- see the TODO.md duplication note). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the view-lifetime fix.
- **[MED, deferred: MIR] A str/bytes SELF-view (`a[3:9]`, `s.strip()`) silently dangles when its source local is rebound, because str/bytes self-views follow a warn-not-demote model and the warning misses plain rebinds.** `s = make(); x = s.strip(); s = make()` (method) leaves `x` a `std::string_view` into the freed first buffer -- no diagnostic, no demotion -- diverging from CPython (where the local holds an independent value); so does a nested def that rebinds the source through `nonlocal` (`v = w.strip()`, then `def f(): nonlocal w; w = PAD + "q"`, `f(); print(v)`). The slice face (`v = a[3:9]`) is fixed: it binds an owned `std::string` (re-measured 2026-09-29). Verified matrix: a **container-element** view (`x = c[0]`, list/dict/record) DEMOTES to owned on any source mutation OR rebind (sound, no warning); a **str/bytes self-view** (slice or view-returning method on a str/bytes local) instead only WARNS "while borrowed" on `+=` / method-mutation and is SILENT on a plain rebind -- so rebind falls through both guards. Two facts behind it: (1) the borrow-conflict warning treats augmented-assign / method-mutation as a conflict but not a plain rebind; (2) the view-vs-owned source-root tracking in `_infer_new_local_view_type` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) registers only `TpySubscript`/`TpyFieldAccess` *element* sources in `view_source_borrows_map`, never a str/bytes self-source (slice of a str local, or a view-returning call rooted at its receiver via `return_borrows_from`), so those views have no demotion path at all. Distinct from (and not a hole in) the compound-view-roots fix, which demotes correctly on rebind for the element sources it tracks. **Chosen fix (direction A -- the sound, model-unifying one):** register str/bytes self-source views in `view_source_borrows_map` rooted at the borrowed source (the sliced str/bytes local; a view-returning call's `return_borrows_from` receiver/args) so they DEMOTE to owned on mutation/rebind exactly like container-element views -- one model for all view sources. (The weaker alternative -- merely extending the borrow-conflict warning to rebinds -- was rejected: it labels the UB instead of removing it and keeps two divergent safety models.) This flips `tests/cases/view_lifetime/warn_view_source_mutation`'s str/slice cases from warn-and-view to demote-to-owned (the warnings become unnecessary, consistent with that test's own note that they are a stopgap pending last-use precision) -- an existing-snapshot change to confirm before regenerating. Surfaced by /tpy-fix-bug of the compound-view-source root tracking fix; own branch.
- **[LOW small, latent, deferred: MIR] Storing a dict view in a FIELD escapes the view-lifetime checks: `self.view = d.items()` of a local dict has no sema rule.** Unreachable today only because THIR refuses both halves: the store rejects at `assign.field_write_shape` and a read of the view field at `call.native_arg.record_nonf1`; once the lowering admits them the silent dangle returns. Returning a locally-backed dict view is rejected at sema since the stubs declare the views `@native(..., borrowing_view=True)` (before that, a dict view took `check_dangling_reference`'s value-type early return and only the lowering's return-slot reject stopped it), but field assignments bypass `check_dangling_reference`, and `check_escape` skips dict views because their TypeDef says `is_value_type=True`. Same pre-existing class as the StrView/Span field-storage gap, reachable for `dict_keys`/`dict_values`/`dict_items` since the views became first-class borrowing wrappers (dict-accessor aliasing work). Fix shape: route field stores of `is_borrowing_view_type` values through the same provenance check returns use (or reject storing views in fields outright until region tracking lands). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model).
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] `is_rvalue_source` classifies a subscript on an RVALUE container as a borrow -- binding it would take a pointer/reference into a dying temporary.** `tpyc/value_category.py:180` returns False for any plain `TpySubscript` without recursing into the container's own rvalue-ness (unlike the `TpyFieldAccess` arm at line 174). The predicate is still wrong; what changed is reach -- every binding position that would dangle now REJECTS rather than emitting: `v = make()[0]` with `make() -> Own[list[T]]` fails with `stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type`, and `takes(make()[0])` / `(w := make()[0])` with `stmt.expr_stmt:subscript.recv.call`. Only the read-through form still emits, and it is sound (`print(make()[0].v)` -> `::tpy::__getitem__(make(), 0).v`; the temporary outlives the full expression). So this is now a rejects-valid gap resting on a wrong predicate, not a live dangle. Fix (recurse + materialize, NOT copy): detect the rvalue container by recursing into `expr.obj` (mirror the `TpyFieldAccess` arm), then MATERIALIZE the rvalue container/receiver into an owning function-scope local and alias the element/borrow into it -- the exact idiom `match` already uses for a non-lvalue subject (`auto __match_subject = <temporary>`, gated by `match_subject_is_lvalue`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/emit_prims.py:1053`, consumed by `tpyc/thir/lower/match.py`), which is the same recursive lvalue-of-`expr.obj` test, and what `_borrow_tuple_rhs`' owning-call storage slot does. This is NOT the "copy the element" path: a reference-type element is never duplicated -- we extend the CONTAINER's lifetime (own it in a slot) and the borrow aliases into it, matching CPython. Sound iff the borrow does not outlive the slot's scope: `return <borrow>` is already caught ("Cannot return local or temporary as reference"); field/container-store and yield-across-suspend of the borrow still ride the general escape guards (the liveness work). The expression-position case (`print(f()[0].x)`) needs the container hoisted at expression scope, not just at a var-decl -- more than `match` handles (it owns its whole statement). The narrow rvalue-receiver record-`__getitem__` REJECT (`_tag_record_getitem`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py:3873`; test `tests/cases/generics/error_getitem_temp_receiver`) is the sound stopgap this general fix subsumes -- replace that reject with materialization here. The pointer-repr `Optional[record]` `'subscript'` call-arg face (`_optional_ptr_arg_face`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:9839`) gates the same shape out of a call-arg AND resumable-frame-capture position (`takes_optional(make_list()[i])` -- worse there: the dangle would persist across suspend/resume): it rejects unless the subscript container resolves through `_subscript_container_recv_type` (an lvalue name / admitted field), and rejects an unproven-Optional container so the `deref_check` is never silently dropped. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the branch-decl borrow-fact materialization; the receiver-materialization direction confirmed against `match`/tuple-RHS precedent in a follow-up /tpy-review discussion.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) A user-record `__getitem__` returning an owned `str`/`bytes` behind a view escapes the dangling-return walk, because the subscript arm follows the RECEIVER instead of the callee.** [`record-getitem-owned-return-view-dangle`] A `Box` whose `__getitem__(self, i: int32) -> str` returns a fresh string (`return self.items[i] + "!"`), read as `def view_of(b: Box) -> StrView: return b[0]`, emits `return b[0];` -- a `std::string_view` over the `std::string` that `operator[]` returned by value. The method spelling of the same code (`b.get(0)`) is caught ("Cannot return StrView referencing a local or temporary"): `is_dangling_return`'s `TpyMethodCall` arm reads the callee's return type, while its `TpySubscript` arm recurses into `expr.obj` and answers "the receiver is a param, so safe". The arm cannot simply consult the callee today -- `_tag_record_getitem` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py`) attaches `getitem_function_info` ONLY for a pointer-repr `Optional` return, deliberately, since tagging every record subscript would run the method lookup (and its module-usage side effects) on cases whose codegen must stay byte-identical. **Fix shape:** resolve the receiver's `__getitem__` for the walk without the tagging side effects (a lookup-only query), then route the subscript through the method-call arm with the receiver at index -1 and the key at index 0; the same routing closes the `Own[T]`-returning `__getitem__` face. Found auditing that arm during the generic yield-slot work. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR] An `@overload`/`@dispatch` group's body facts land on ONE member, so every other member's borrow contract is lost: the callee escapes the auto-move borrow gate in BOTH directions, and a generic generator's yield slot becomes definition-order-dependent.** [`overload-group-borrow-facts-last-entry`] Calls into an overload group resolve to the MATCHED stub FunctionInfo, but body-analysis facts land only on the group's last entry (`get_function(name)[-1]`, see the finalize sites in `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`): non-last stubs keep `return_borrows_from=None` forever. Backward-defined overloaded callees therefore never register the call-result borrow (the gate misses a real borrow -- silent use-after-move family), and the forward-reference pending set (`_seed_pending_borrow_fact_fis`) seeds only `[-1]`, so the conservative `OPAQUE` path also never fires for a stub-resolved call. **Fix shape:** propagate finalize facts to every group member -- but the param indices of `return_borrows_from` are per-signature, so the propagation needs an index mapping from the implementation's params to each stub's (or per-stub body analysis for bodied stubs); naive copying is wrong for reordered/defaulted overloads. Until then, seeding all group FIs into the pending set alone would over-demote backward-defined overloads (permanent OPAQUE) and must not ship by itself. **Witness:** `_analyze_function` stamps the body facts onto `func_overloads[-1]` under a `direct_mutated_params is None` guard, so only the FIRST-analyzed variant's facts ever land -- on the LAST-registered variant's FI, carrying the first variant's param indices (which can name a param the receiving variant does not have). Under `tpy.dispatch`, where every variant IS an implementation, the whole group's contract therefore depends on definition order: with the 1-arg `pick` first (`/tmp/agents/yv_verify/b4b.py`) the 2-arg generator lends its yield (`::tpy::yield_slot_t<T>`) while its 1-arg twin falls to the value slot `T`; swapping the two variants (`b4c.py`) makes NEITHER lend. And the auto-move gate is not the only reader -- the generic yield-slot verdict reads the same fact, so the value-slot fallback is a SILENT COPY, not just a missed diagnostic: `b6_alias.py` (dispatch spelling) prints `1` where the byte-identical non-dispatch spelling `b6_plain.py` prints `99` (CPython `99`) after the consuming loop mutates the yielded element. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the forward-ref gate fix; witness added from the generic yield-slot work. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-move, no diagnostic) A borrowing method called on a PENDING-generic receiver registers no borrow, so a later consume of the receiver moves out from under the result.** [`pending-generic-receiver-call-borrow-unregistered`] `b = Bag()` (a generic instance whose type parameter is not inferred yet), then `t = b.tag()` where `def tag(self) -> StrView: return self.name`. The ROOT FI's `return_borrows_from` is `{-1}`, but the call site resolved to the "minimal function info" that `tpyc/sema/methods.py` (~1703) builds for a pending-generic receiver, and that `FunctionInfo` copies the resumable-factory and method-kind bits and NOT `return_borrows_from`. The readiness gate in `_register_call_result_borrow` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~261) reads the RAW field, finds `None`, and the minimal FI is not in `ctx.pending_borrow_fact_fis` (that set holds the registry FIs), so the `None` falls through as "borrows nothing" and no borrow is registered at all. A later `Keeper(b)` on an `Own[Bag[int32]]` parameter then auto-moves: `Keeper k = Keeper(std::move(b));` emits while `t` is still a `std::string_view` into `b.name`. The CONCRETE-receiver twin `b = Bag[int32]()` registers the borrow and correctly demotes the consume to the copy path (`Bag<int32_t> __tmp_1 = b;`). Probes `/tmp/agents/yready/p_pend_a.py` (moves, no diagnostic) and `p_pend_b.py` (copies), verified 2026-09-17. Same family as BUGS.md#overload-group-borrow-facts-last-entry: a synthesized FI that never carries the fact, read by a gate that cannot tell "no fact" from "no borrow". **Fix shape:** either the readiness gate asks the root-aware reader `typesys.recorded_return_borrow_sources` the way every other reader now does (which also means re-expressing the pending-set membership test over roots, so the two halves still agree), or the minimal-FI path copies `return_borrows_from` alongside the bits it already copies. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR] A generator METHOD's receiver borrow is not represented, so consuming the receiver while its generator lives escapes the auto-move gate.** The generator frame stores `__self` by reference, but `return_borrows_from` cannot carry `-1` for generator methods: `-1` blocks readonly inference (a self-borrowing return pins non-const), and stamping it flips every generator method non-readonly -- observed breaking const callers of stdlib `re.Pattern.finditer`. So `g = obj.walk(...); take(obj); next(g)` silently iterates a moved-from receiver (same family as the iterable-param case, which IS gated via the param indices). **Fix shape:** either represent the receiver borrow in a channel that readonly inference ignores (a separate `frame_borrows_self` fact consumed by `_register_call_result_borrow`), or make the readonly-inference check distinguish "returns self" from "frame references self with the method's own constness". Surfaced implementing the generator-method borrow facts (forward-ref gate review round). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR] A borrow hidden inside a NESTED call argument escapes the auto-move borrow gate (asyncio.create_task shape).** `task = asyncio.create_task(total(xs))` -- `total`'s coroutine temporary stores `xs` by reference, `create_task` retains the coroutine inside the returned Task, but `_register_call_result_borrow` only relates the bound name to the OUTER call's `return_borrows_from`, so no `task -> xs` borrow is registered and a later consume of `xs` moves it while the pending task still iterates it: TPy prints `1 0` where CPython prints `1 6` (bind create_task, consume `xs`, `await task`), no diagnostics. Direct coroutine binds (`c = total(xs)`) are unaffected -- the coroutine must-use rule rejects them. The general form is any `outer(inner(xs))` where `inner` borrows and `outer` retains its argument. Note: async defs also do not set the generator-style `return_borrows_from` for their reference-stored params (`analyzer.py` gates on `is_generator` only); that fact alone is dead code today because of the must-use rule, so set it together with the transitive registration, not separately. **Fix shape:** when an argument expression is itself a call whose `return_borrows_from` roots at a name, register the outer call's bound result as borrowing that root (conservative: the callee may retain the temporary). Residual of the audit root-cause #5 fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR] A loop-var alias outliving its loop escapes the auto-move borrow gate: consuming the iterable post-loop dangles the alias.** `for x in xs: last = x` then `drop(xs)` then `last.read()` -- `last` is a reference into `xs`'s element storage, but the only BorrowTracker edge on `xs` is the `"__for_iter"` sentinel, which the gate excludes (it names no real local, and gating on it would block the loop's own consuming-iteration activation), and the prescan alias map relates `last` to `x`, not to `xs` (the loop-var -> iterable relation lives only in `loop_var_iterable`). The post-loop consume therefore still auto-moves `xs` while `last` dangles -- same silent use-after-move family as the forward-referenced-callee entry above. **Fix shape:** at for-loop analysis, register the loop var (and transitively its aliases) as a NAMED element-borrower of the iterable -- not the shared sentinel -- so the gate sees it; or fold `loop_var_iterable` into the gate's known-borrow sources. Real fix is loop-scoped borrow expiry in the MIR place/loan model. Residual of the audit root-cause #5 fix, surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. Second hazard shape, same missing edge: a loan taken INTO the loop VALUE (`for x in xs: q = take_ptr(x)`) is keyed under `x` and never propagated to `xs` either, so a post-loop STRUCTURAL mutation of the iterable is seen by neither the alias-rebind check nor the element-borrow mutation check -- eight `xs.append(...)` then `q.bump()` prints `p4b2: 106 2` where CPython prints `p4b2: 102 102`. The read and the write both land on the reallocated-away buffer, so like [`setitem-write-under-live-element-borrow`] the printed value is not stable (it is whatever the reused heap holds) -- pin the diagnostic, not the number. Repro `/tmp/agents/fixround/p4b2.py`.
- **[MED, deferred: MIR] Non-scalar match arm bindings are `auto&` borrows into the subject's storage; mutating the subject root in the arm body (or guard) dangles them.** The visible and method-call mutation shapes are now WARNED; only mutation through an ALIAS of the subject and via an opaque (unknown-readonly) method remain silent. FREE-COPY-SCALAR bindings (fixed int, bool, `char`, float, enum) are COPIED at the arm, so they survive subject mutation and match CPython at zero cost (a register move) -- this closed the originally-verified [HIGH] shapes, whose bound fields were scalar (`int32`). The binding form is a single sema fact (`bind_by_value` on each capture node, set from `is_free_copy_scalar` via the shared `iter_capture_bindings` traversal); codegen's `auto`/`auto&` choice AND the dangle warning both read it, so they cannot drift -- no capture path can silently alias a scalar (a missed path defaults to a warned `auto&`, and a codegen emit site without the per-arm map asserts). The copy is deliberately restricted to scalars: copying a heap-backed value type (`str`, `BigInt`), a view, or a reference type would pessimize the common path (performance is design goal #1) or diverge from CPython aliasing, so those keep the zero-cost `auto&` borrow and dangle if the subject root is mutated while the binding lives. The stopgap (`_warn_arm_subject_mutation`, gated on a non-scalar binding being present) now warns on: assignment to the subject path/owner prefix, an invalidating container method on the subject base (both synchronous), AND a non-readonly method call whose receiver prefix-aliases the subject (deferred to `finalize_borrow_checks` once readonly is settled; `resolve_pending_match_subject_checks`). Pointer-variant LOCAL subjects are safe (slot model). **Remaining SILENT residual:** mutation through an ALIAS of the subject (`p = h; p.swap()` / `p.pet = ...` -- needs alias tracking) and via an opaque method whose readonly verdict is unknown (`is_readonly is None`, e.g. some `@native`). **Sound fix:** register the surviving non-scalar arm bindings (and `__match_subject` for field/element sources) as loans of the subject root in the BorrowTracker for the arm's extent, and reject root mutation while they live -- a compile-time check, never a runtime copy (a copy would violate the performance goal for `str`/`BigInt`). Needs the MIR `Place`/`LoanInfo` model with arm-EXTENT-aware loans, which the current whole-function mutation facts cannot express (the deferred-check resolver is extent-blind) -- an IR-migration deliverable (see `docs/IR_DESIGN.md`). Dropped from [HIGH] to [MED] now that the verified silent shapes (scalar copy; non-scalar method-call) are closed; the remaining alias/opaque residual is rarer. Audit finding G2.
- **[LOW small] readonly is not projected onto a NESTED borrow-form tuple element on subscript.** `t[i]` where `t: readonly[tuple[..., tuple[int32, Box], ...]]` returns the inner `tuple[int32, Box]` without `readonly`, so a write through `t[i][1].field` is not rejected at sema. Root cause: the four subscript readonly-projection sites in `tpyc/sema/expressions.py` (tuple, container, protocol, record) all gate on `not elem.is_value_type()`, and `TupleType.is_value_type()` is unconditionally True -- so a tuple element (even one with borrow-form sub-elements) is treated as a copied value and skipped. The non-nested cases work (`readonly[tuple[Box, ...]]` projects `readonly[Box]`). Same family as the `readonly[list[tuple[...]]]` element-write entry above. **Fix shape:** unify the four gates to project readonly when the element is a borrow-form tuple (`TupleType.has_ref_elements()`), not only when `not is_value_type()`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the readonly-tuple-projection fix.
- **[MED, deferred: MIR] General destructive move-out of aggregate members is unimplemented beyond the whole-rvalue-tuple-unpack slice.** Moving ownership *out* of an aggregate member is supported only for whole-tuple unpack of a fresh rvalue (`a, b = make_pair()` distributes each `Own[T]` element to a movable owned local -- shipped). Named-source whole-tuple unpack (`t = make_pair(); a, b = t`) is now supported (the source is moved into the temp at its last use). Still unsupported: partial element move-out (`take(pair[0])` leaving `pair[1]` live), record-field move-out (`take(rec.field)` for a `@nocopy` field), constant/dynamic-index move-out. These need per-place partial-move state tracking: representing `pair[0]` / `rec.field` as individually movable places with their own consumed flags, propagating "partially moved" up to the aggregate (so the whole value can't be used/moved once a part is), flow-sensitive merge of partial-move state across branches, use-after-partial-move diagnostics, and rejection of un-trackable dynamic-index moves -- the `Place(Local/Field/Index/...)` move-state model the borrow-tracker/MIR notes describe as future work. Reading members in place (borrow) is unaffected. Surfaced implementing the narrow whole-tuple-unpack slice (Send/Sync Phase 4 channel). **Fix shape:** add per-place move-state tracking to the borrow/move analyzer; until then multi-owner handoff routes through whole-tuple unpack or `Rc.clone()`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (large; architectural).
- **[LOW small, deferred: MIR] Temporary-rvalue-into-view-storage is rejected for `list`/`set` `append`/`add`/`insert` only; the sibling sinks are uncovered.** The view-lifetime fix (audit #10 item 5) rejects `list[StrView].append(make())` / `set.add` / `list.insert` of a temporary, but the same dangling-view store is still silently accepted for: `dict[StrView, ...]` / `dict[..., StrView]` literal keys/values and `d[k] = make()`, `list.extend([make()])`, set/dict LITERAL elements (a `list[StrView]` literal `[make()]` now rejects at lowering), and `tuple`/comprehension element stores. (StrView FIELD stores are the separate Future field-lifetime feature, below.) Param/local-derived views stored into an ESCAPING container are also still accepted -- that needs container-lifetime (region) analysis, not just rvalue rejection. **Fix shape:** route every element-into-view-storage coercion through one chokepoint that rejects a temporary source (extend the `_view_source_is_temporary` check at the literal-element and dict/extend coercion sites); overlaps audit #11 (literal elements copy). Surfaced implementing audit #10 item 5. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (precision, not unsound)** `await x` reads the awaitable's `__poll__` `is_readonly` at Phase-1 analysis time (`_analyze_await` -> `_extract_awaitable_inner`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`); auto-readonly is a Phase-2 fixpoint fact. A *user-defined* awaitable whose `__poll__` is only inferred `@readonly` in Phase 2 (no `@readonly` annotation, no direct mutation) reads `is_readonly=False` here, so `_mark_await_operand_mutated` over-marks the awaited operand's root -- blocking the enclosing async method's auto-readonly inference even though awaiting that awaitable doesn't actually mutate it. Over-approximation: conservative and never unsound (a method wrongly kept non-readonly, never wrongly readonly), and stdlib awaitables (`Task`/`Future`/`Event`/`SleepFuture`) all mutate in `__poll__` so they're unaffected. Fix shape: defer the await-mutation mark to Phase 2 via a call edge (mirroring `_is_self_call_deferred` for `self.method()`), or consult the Phase-2-finalized `__poll__` readonly verdict. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the await-self-mutation fix.
- **[LOW small] (by design, not a regression) Post-sema `replace_expr` injects AST that bypasses sema re-analysis.** `PostSemaFunctionMacroContext.replace_expr` (inherited from `FunctionMacroContext`, `tpyc/macro_api.py`) splices nodes after pass 7, so the injected nodes get no mutation-fact collection (no `call_edges` for new calls -> Phase-2 propagation can miss a mutating call -- `PostSemaFunctionMacroContext.note_param_mutated` is a manual escape hatch for the param-rooted mutating-call sub-case, but it only seeds `direct_mutated_params`, not `direct_structural_mutated_params`, so an emitted *structurally*-mutating call (append/insert/clear on a param) is still unrecorded), no borrow-check registration, no `deref_check` insertion, and no narrowing/readonly enforcement. The contract is documented (the caller must `set_expr_type` every emitted node and is responsible for safety), and this is inherent to the whole macro system (pre-sema `replace_expr`, builder-trace `emit_function`, and class macros already inject un-rechecked AST) -- a known limitation, not a defect introduced here. A macro that injects only value-type expressions (the shipped test) is safe. **Fix shape (future):** restrict the post-sema surface to value-type replacements (enforce via `type_of`/`set_expr_type`), or re-run the relevant sema checks over injected subtrees once the IR makes that cheap. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the post-sema function-macro phase.
- **[MED, latent, deferred: MIR] A view param (`Span[T]`) stored into a field passes sema with no diagnostic -- the field dangles when the caller's buffer dies (silent UAF).** The constructor store `def __init__(self, s: Span[int32]) -> None: self._s = s` compiles with no diagnostic, and the stored span outlives whatever backing the caller passed; the METHOD store (`def keep(self, v: Span[int32]) -> None: self._s = v`) now rejects at lowering (`assign.field_write_shape`, re-measured 2026-09-29). At the `@export` CPython boundary the glue's copy-in vector dies when the wrapper returns, making the store an unconditional UAF on the next payload read for any exposed METHOD taking a `Span` param (property `Span` setters are rejected outright for exactly this reason -- a setter's purpose is storing -- so only the method surface remains exposed). The existing view-escape entries in this section cover the RETURN direction; this is the param-stored-into-field direction. Not expressible as a passing test (silent UAF). Fix shape: reject (or warn on) a view-typed param assigned into field storage, pending the region/lifetime model's loan-extent form. Probe: a `Span` setter body `self._s = v` compiled with zero diagnostics. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, safety-model) of the exposed-class @property rung. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (silent wrong output, dangling) A TEMPORARY argument or receiver of a delegated generator call dies before the embedded frame is first resumed.** [`resumable-delegate-temp-source-dangles`] A `for x in <gen call>:` with a yield/await in its body embeds the callee's frame in a `__for_src` field, and that frame BORROWS the call's arguments and receiver -- but a temporary among them is materialized in the enclosing `case S_RESUME_N: { ... }` block of the consumer's `__next__` switch (or not at all, for a view), so it is destroyed before the first `(*__for_src_0).__next__()` runs in the next case. Three reproducers, all same-module and all diverging from CPython (`PYTHONPATH=lib/cpy python3`): (a) reference-typed temporary ARGUMENT -- `def make_list() -> Own[list[int32]]: return [11, 22]`, `def walk(xs: list[int32]) -> Iterator[int32]: yield xs[0]; yield xs[1]`, `def gen() -> Iterator[int32]: yield 0; (for x in walk(make_list()): yield x)` prints `0` then two garbage integers where CPython prints `0 11 22`; this one DOES warn ("Iterator borrows from temporary argument 'xs'; the temporary is destroyed before iteration begins") yet still compiles and runs. (b) a `StrView` over a temporary `str` -- same `gen`, with `def make_str() -> str: return "abcdefgh"` and `walk(make_str()[1:4])` over `def walk(s: StrView) -> Iterator[StrView]` -- prints `start` then two blank lines where CPython prints `start bcd bcd`, with NO diagnostic: no temp is hoisted at all, the emitted `__for_src_0.emplace(walk(::tpy::str_slice(make_str(), ...)));` lets the owning `std::string` die at that statement's semicolon while the frame keeps the view. (c) a temporary RECEIVER -- `class Bag` with `readings()` yielding `self.n` and `self.n + 1`, and `for v in Bag(7).readings():` inside a resumable `gen` -- emitted `Bag __tmp_1 = Bag(7); __for_src_0.emplace(__tmp_1.readings());` and printed `0 0 1` where CPython prints `0 7 8`; this leg is FIXED -- the receiver is now hoisted into a `__coro_arg_0` frame slot and prints `0 7 8` (re-measured 2026-09-29). Root cause is one thing in all three: the delegated source's operands are given BLOCK lifetime (or, for a view, full-expression lifetime) while the frame that borrows them has FRAME lifetime -- the `__for_src` / `__for_r` slots are frame fields precisely because they must survive across suspensions, and the temporaries feeding them were not given the same treatment. PRE-EXISTING and reachable from ordinary same-module code; the (b)/(c) legs are silent, which is what makes it HIGH. Fix shape: hoist the temporary into a frame field alive for the loop's lifetime, exactly as `__for_src`/`__for_r` already are (materialize it in a `frame_slot<T>` emplaced in the same case block, destroyed at loop exit), which covers the receiver and the owning source behind a view alike; with that in place the warned case (a) becomes correct and the warning goes -- if the hoist is not taken for some operand shape, that shape must become a hard reject rather than a warning that still emits. Probes `/tmp/agents/dangtmp/{a,b,c}.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) A view returned off an IMPORTED global survives a `global` rebind in the DEFINING module.** [`imported-global-view-outlives-foreign-rebind`] `store.py` holds `S = "hello world..."` plus `def reset() -> None: global S; S = "x"`; `main.py` does `from store import S, reset` / `def view() -> StrView: return S` / `v = view(); reset(); print(v)` and prints `x llo world...` where CPython prints the original string. The same-module face of this is now a located compile error (`Cannot return a borrow of module variable 'S': function 'reset' rebinds 'S'`), decided from `SemanticContext.rebound_globals`, which `global_write_facts` fills from THIS module's bodies only -- a rebind in the defining module never reaches the importing module's certification. Fix shape: carry the rebound-globals set on the module's exports / `ModuleInfo` so the importing analyzer reads the defining module's verdict for an imported name, the way it already reads the imported type; the check site (`TypeCompatibility._check_rebound_global_borrow`) then needs no change. Probes `/tmp/agents/view_rebound_global/xmod/{store,main}.py`. Surfaced while closing the same-module `global`-rebind face of this hole (2026-09-15). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) A view returned off a module global survives a MODULE-LEVEL rebind of that global.** [`returned-view-outlives-module-level-rebind`] `S = "hello world..."` / `def view() -> StrView: return S` / `v = view()` / `S = "x"` / `print(v)` -- all four at module level, no `global` statement anywhere -- prints `x llo world...` where CPython prints the original string. The `global`-statement face is now rejected at the return, but module init rebinds the slot by plain assignment, so `global_write_facts` (which pairs a `global` declaration with a write) does not see it, and the view-invalidation rule in `tpyc/sema/expressions.py` does not either: it invalidates loans taken by a direct read of the name, not a view handed back by a call. Not simply foldable into the `global` rule: a module-level rebind is ordered relative to the calls around it (a rebind before every call is harmless, which the `global` case can never assume), so the sound form is the module-init replay (`decide_rebind_storage`) invalidating the loans a returned view holds, not a whole-name rejection. Probe `/tmp/agents/view_rebound_global/p14.py`. Surfaced while closing the same-module `global`-rebind face of this hole (2026-09-15). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR] (silent dangling view, no diagnostic) The `global`-rebind rule guards the RETURN sink only: a view stored into a field, or bound in the caller, still outlives the rebind.** [`rebound-global-borrow-open-sinks`] With `S = "hello world..."` plus `def reset() -> None: global S; S = "x"`, two sinks are unguarded. FIELD store: `class Holder` with `v: StrView` and `def take(self) -> None: self.v = S`, then `h.take(); reset(); print(h.v)` prints `x llo world...` where CPython prints the original (probe `/tmp/agents/safety4/fieldstore.py`). CALLER-side local: `v: StrView = S` in `main`, then `reset()`, prints the same divergence (`/tmp/agents/safety4/localread.py`). An un-annotated slice local `w = S[2:]` is now owned and stays right (re-measured 2026-09-29), as is the whole-name alias `v = S`. From ANOTHER module the whole-name read is a view too: `w = store.S` then `store.reset()` (which does `global S; S = ...`) prints freed bytes (`/tmp/agents/rv2r3/xmod/main.py` `g`). A view of `store.S` hoisted out of a block owns (a plain module variable is not static storage to the hoist rule); only a `Final` module constant stays a view there. The rule lives on `TypeCompatibility.check_dangling_reference`, which every borrow RETURN and borrow YIELD funnels through and nothing else does -- a field store and a local binding are checked by their own paths, which certify a module global as durable storage (`is_param_derived_expr` / `_name_is_param_or_global`) and never ask whether it is rebound. Fix shape: the fact is already module-wide (`SemanticContext.rebound_globals`, filled by `global_write_facts`) and the slot predicate already exists (`_return_borrows_global_storage`); what is missing is reaching them from the binding sinks, which needs a decision on what the rule is there -- a field store is a REJECT like the return, but a caller-side local is ordered relative to the rebind, so a whole-name rejection would refuse programs where the rebind comes first, and the sound form is loan invalidation (same shape as [`returned-view-outlives-module-level-rebind`]). **Three more faces of the same rule, all live:** (1) the fact is decided in sub-phase 3, BEFORE `_expand_function_macros` (sub-phase 4), so a `global X` write a `@function_macro` introduces is invisible to it; (2) `_return_borrows_global_storage` exempts a `Ptr[T]` / `Span[T]` HANDLE global by the SLOT's own type and never asks where the handle points, so a `Span` global that views another global's buffer would be exempted wrongly -- latent only because such a return is rejected elsewhere; (3) `+=` on a reference-typed global is an in-place extend in CPython, not a reseat, but the rebind walk pairs a `global` declaration with any binding write including `TpyAugAssign`, so it would count as one -- reachable: the borrow rule fires first, so `return XS` before a `global XS; XS += [4]` is rejected as a rebind although CPython extends in place (the lowering does not admit the aug-assign on a global yet either, `stmt.aug_assign`); the message names only the function, so the over-reject is at least not given a false reason.aug_assign` (probe `/tmp/agents/r4_fix/iadd.py`), and the lowering that admits it must not inherit the over-rejection; (4) the whole rule is same-module only -- an imported global rebound in its DEFINING module reaches no certification at all, filed separately as [`imported-global-view-outlives-foreign-rebind`], which is the same rule missing its cross-module half rather than a distinct defect. Surfaced 2026-09-15 by the review round over the same-module `global`-rebind fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. A fourth face: a view WRAPPED in a value aggregate escapes the return rule entirely -- `def v() -> Optional[StrView]: return S[0:11]` with a `global S` rebind compiles and reads freed storage (`check_dangling_reference`'s value-type early return skips it; the tuple arm mirrors that skip by design, so the two agree). Probe `/tmp/agents/safety6/p12_opt_dangle.py`.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (silent miscompile, use-after-move) In an import cycle, a call-result borrow through a peer module whose bodies have not been analyzed yet is read as "borrows nothing", so the auto-move gate moves the container out from under the live reference.** [`cycle-peer-borrow-fact-read-as-stub`] Modules `a` and `b` import each other; each has `pick(xs: list[Item]) -> Item` returning `xs[0]` and `use()` doing `it = peer.pick(xs)` then `k = sink(xs)` with `sink(xs: Own[list[Item]])`, then `return it.n + k`. Cause: `return_borrows_from` is a body-local fact consumed at the call-result bind (`tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~255-270), where `None` means BOTH "opaque stub, borrows nothing" and "body not analyzed yet"; the disambiguator `ctx.pending_borrow_fact_fis` is seeded by `_seed_pending_borrow_fact_fis` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py` ~913-944) from THIS module only, so a cycle peer is missing from the set and its `None` takes the stub leg. Step C of the TODO design entry "Call-graph fact propagation: make the unit the import COMPONENT"; the alternative is deferring cycle-peer binds to the workspace-wide finalize pass like cross-module borrow checks. The same-module forward-reference twin is closed (`fix-forward-ref-borrow-gate` seeds unanalyzed same-module callees as conservative `OPAQUE` borrows). Found 2026-09-16 by the batch-6 propagation analysis.

- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR] (rejects valid, loud) A for-each over a container more than one hop from a spellable storage key is REJECTED, because the borrow tracker keys a loan by a STRING (`name` / `name.field`) and cannot express the place the iteration borrows. One spelling escapes it in a plain `def` body -- a chain whose TAIL is a `@property`, whose loan comes from the getter's provenance instead; a resumable body rejects that one too, at `res.for_iter_borrow_unplaceable`, since its frame holds the iterators across every suspension.** [`iter-borrow-place-needs-hops`] `for b in self.grid.rows[i]`, `for b in self.inner.xs`, `for b in table[k].cells`, `for b in shelves[0].flat` and `for b in cube[i][j]` all stop with *this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:foreach.iter_borrow_unplaceable)* (the generator and `async for` twins stop at `res.for_iter_borrow_unplaceable` -- all three routes file the loan through one registration and take one verdict), while the one-hop siblings `rows[i]`, `g.rows`, `self.rows[i]`, `row.cells[i]` and `table[k]` compile and are checked. Binding the chain to a local first is the workaround. The reject is deliberate, not a codegen gap: `BorrowTracker.loans` (`tpyc/sema/context.py`) is `dict[str, dict[str, LoanInfo]]`, and `_storage_key` can spell only a name or a one-hop `obj.field` path, so a deeper chain has no key a mutating receiver could be resolved to and every invalidating mutation of what is iterated would be silent -- a cached `__beg`/`__end` into a vector that reallocates. The single element hop that IS checked rides `LoanInfo.on_element` plus `LoanInfo.elem_index` (an `element_index_key`: a non-negative int or str literal, or a bare name) rather than a key, so two literals that differ are proven distinct and everything else conflicts -- worded as certain or as possible by `element_index_relation`. Fix shape: replace the string key with a `Place` (root name plus an ordered tuple of field / index hops, an index hop carrying the same `element_index_key` and matching by `element_index_relation`), file loans under it, and make the conflict test `equal or prefix or extension` -- then the whole chain family is checkable and the reject can be lifted. Every loans-dict consumer (`has_element_borrow`, `has_iter_borrow`, `effective_storage`, `borrow_source`, `retarget_storage_borrows` and the two `storage + "."` prefix walks, `all_storage_through_borrows`) moves with it, which is why this is a design row and not a patch. The Place has a SECOND consumer that must be designed in at the same time, or the codebase ends with two key vocabularies for one question: the view tracker already spells deep dotted paths (`field_chain_storage_key`, `o.inner.tag`) and answers "does this mutation clobber that view" by a raw string PREFIX match in `mark_view_borrowers_mutated` -- exactly the `equal or prefix or extension` relation above, spelled a second way. The two fix groups of batch 6 made opposite calls here (the iteration side refused a deeper string key, the view side extended one), which is the concrete cost of leaving them apart. Pinned by `tests/cases/iterators/error_foreach_unplaceable_chain_src`, `tests/cases/iterators/error_foreach_field_chain_src` (the pure-field chain), `tests/cases/generators/error_gen_foreach_unplaceable_chain`, `tests/cases/generators/error_gen_foreach_property_chain` (the property-tail chain a plain body admits) and `tests/cases/async/error_async_for_unplaceable_chain`. Surfaced by the batch-6 review (safety C1/C2). Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. The field-read VIEW is the other half of this row: a one-hop read borrows and is demoted by a hand-kept list of write paths whose gaps are silent use-after-frees, while a deeper read copies for want of a key (`BUGS.md#field-view-escape-needs-place`). Once the tracker owns escape as a Place fact, the depth restriction, the hand-maintained write-path list and the write receivers that list cannot see all go away. Its home is NOT a new sema structure: master's analysis-only MIR (`docs/MIR_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`, M2.1) already defines `MIRPlace` rooted at a body slot with dereference and field projections plus alias bind/reseat facts, and the loan-legality, referent-lifetime and call-summary halves are the later increments; the iteration loans and the view tracker are consumers of those increments, so this row and `BUGS.md#field-view-escape-needs-place` wait for them rather than grow a second place vocabulary in `tpyc/sema/context.py`. Until then the whole borrow family stays fail-closed (located rejects with slugs), no further widening at the string-key layer (user 2026-09-17). A TUPLE element is one more such hop: `for x in t[0].xs` with `t: tuple[P, P]` (a parameter or a local) rejects at `foreach.iter_borrow_unplaceable`, as do `hp.a.xs`, `pl[0].xs` and `hp.f[0].xs` off parameters (probe `/tmp/agents/ge/file/l_tparam_for.py`, 2026-09-28); the `in` and binding reads of the same chains are `BUGS.md#deep-chain-container-field-in-and-bind-rejects`. The same chain off an element of an `Optional[list[P]]` receiver, un-narrowed or narrowed (`for v in d[0].rows`), rejects at the same key; pinned by `tests/cases/optional/error_unnarrowed_opt_elem_foreach`.

The view-family WRITE set is master's (`_field_receiver_or_unbound_self_ok` plus `_field_over_record_getitem_ok`) plus the nested field, the unproven Optional name and the unproven Optional over a field, minus the five subtracted receivers; the READ rule is master's verbatim. - **[HIGH medium] (silent heap-use-after-free) A generator or `async def` frame holds its `begin`/`end` iterators across every suspension, but the ITER loan that guards them is intra-procedural, so an invalidating mutation made by the CALLER between two resumes is never seen.** [`frame-iter-loan-blind-to-caller`] `def gen(o: Inner) -> Iterator[int32]: for b in o.boxes: yield b.n`, then a caller that does `for v in gen(o): o.boxes.append(Box(99))`, compiles with no diagnostic and is an ASAN `heap-use-after-free` (READ inside `__gen_gen::__next__`, freed by the caller's `_M_realloc_insert`; built g++ 13.3 `-fsanitize=address`). The same program with the mutation in the LOOP BODY *is* caught -- *warning: Mutation of 'o.boxes' while iterating over it* -- which is the whole gap: `BorrowTracker` answers "is this storage mutated while borrowed" over ONE body, and a frame's borrow outlives the body it was registered in. It is not a property-specific defect: the one-hop field iterable (`o.boxes`) and the one-hop `@property` iterable (`o.items`) both reach it, as does the generic bare-`T` getter at a container instantiation (`class Cell[T]` with `-> T`, driven at `Cell[list[int32]]`) -- its convention is decided at the instantiation, so it is a reference exactly as its monomorphic twin is and dangles identically (`tests/cases/generics/inherited_accessor_subst` pins that shape as compiling), and the property flavour additionally files its loan on the receiver root rather than the returned container (`property-iter-loan-misses-getter-storage`), so even its body mutation is silent. Chains deeper than one hop are refused for an unrelated reason (`iter-borrow-place-needs-hops`, no key at all), which accidentally covers them. Fix shape: what is left to decide is the CALLER-STORAGE source alone. A source that is a temporary as written the frame already OWNS in its `__for_src_N` slot; a source that names existing storage is bound by reference once at loop setup (`auto& __for_obj_N = o.boxes;`) and the frame holds `begin`/`end` into it across every suspension, which is the render above. Refusing that aliasing shape is one answer; a purely intra-procedural loan cannot be extended to answer it, since the mutating statement is in another body. A third option is open beside reject-or-own and is the only one that keeps CPython's semantics: iterate a vector-backed container by INDEX rather than by iterator pair, re-reading the container at each resume. Owning the source turns a CPython alias into a copy -- CPython's generator yields the element the caller appended between resumes, an owned snapshot never does -- while an index form keeps the alias and cannot dangle, since a reallocation moves the buffer but not the index. The frame's by-value property fence is gone (2026-09-18, see `own-property-iterable-materialize`), so every by-value getter -- `Own[...]`, `-> str`, and the VIEW-returning `-> StrView` / `Span[T]` / `BytesView` whose iterators were always safe -- is admitted in a frame on its `__for_src_N` slot, like the spelled twin. That widens the surface this entry covers rather than adding a kind: the fact still missing is the same one, whether a frame may ALIAS caller storage across a suspension at all. Surfaced by the batch-6 round-8 safety review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH medium] (silent use-after-move / use-after-free, no diagnostic) A generator frame -- a generator expression or a named generator -- borrows the names its body reads and its source container by reference, and a consume of that name while the frame is still alive moves the storage out from under it.** [`generator-frame-borrow-outlives-consume`] Three faces, all silent: an escaped genexpr's ELEMENT read, `w = passthru(len(p.items) for _ in range(2)); s.consume(p)` then pulling `w`, reads the moved-from `p` -- TPy `genexpr_passthru 0` twice, CPython `3` twice (probe `/tmp/agents/smr8/p15.py`); a genexpr's SOURCE, `w = passthru(v * 10 for v in p.items); s.consume(p); s.stored.clear()` then pulling `w`, iterates the freed buffer -- TPy `src_only 990 20 30` (the first element reads a later allocation), CPython `10 20 30` (`/tmp/agents/smt9/e4.py`); and a named generator over the same source, `w = passthru(items(p.items))`, prints nothing where CPython prints `10 20 30` (`/tmp/agents/smt9/e5.py`). Nearest existing entry: `BUGS.md#frame-iter-loan-blind-to-caller` (a caller MUTATING the storage a live frame iterates). Found 2026-09-30.

- **[HIGH medium, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-move, no diagnostic) A borrow bound LATER in a loop body is not seen at a last-use move earlier on the loop's exit path, so the value moves and the borrower reads moved-from storage.** [`loop-carried-borrower-misses-last-use-move`] `v = k.lst()` before `for i in range(2): if i == 1: o.p = x; return o.p.xs[0] * 100 + len(v) * 10 + v[0]` then `v = x.lst()` at the bottom of the body: the store `o.p = x` is `x`'s last use on the return path, so it renders `o.p = std::move(x);`, while `v` -- bound from `x` on the previous iteration and carried over the back edge -- still points into `x.xs`. - **[HIGH medium, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-move, no diagnostic) A consuming method called on a receiver the caller does not own consumes the caller's storage.** [`consuming-call-borrowed-receiver-consumed`] A consuming call renders its NAME receiver as `std::move(s).m(...)` whenever `s` is not consumed yet, whether or not `s` owns its object. With `def fin(self: Own[Self]) -> int32: return eat((self.p, self.q))` (a `return` that moves both fields into `eat(t: Own[tuple[P, P]])`): a borrowed parameter, `def borrowed_param(s: Item) -> int32: return s.fin()`, renders `return std::move(s).fin();` and empties the caller's fields -- TPy `borrowed_param 11 0 0`, CPython `11 1 1`; and a local whose field is still borrowed, `q = s.p; r = s.fin()` then `len(q.xs)`, renders `int32_t r = std::move(s).fin();` -- TPy `caller_borrow 11 0`, CPython `11 1` (probe `/tmp/agents/bugport/recv.py`). The receiver of a consuming call is an `Own[Self]` argument and needs the decision an `Own[T]` argument gets -- move at the last use of an owned name, otherwise a warned copy (an error for `@nocopy`) -- made once and shared by sema and the lowering, counting only borrowers live after the call, treating `x = x.m()` as the last use of the old `x`, and dereferencing a pointer-slot receiver in the copy render. An unmerged attempt routed the receiver through the existing `Own`-argument demotion and was abandoned because that demotion is not liveness-aware (`BUGS.md#own-arg-demotion-ignores-liveness`: it broke `s = s.grow()` and made dead borrows of a `@nocopy` receiver false errors) and sema and the lowering decided it separately. Using the loop var INSIDE the loop body, accumulating (`acc += chunk`), or copying explicitly (`first = bytes(chunk)`) are all safe -- only persisting the raw yielded value past the iteration step is wrong. Same generator-yield-borrow ABI family as the Safety-section resumable-frame borrow entries: the consumer-escape check is documented to reject re-yield/nested-capture and copy *value* stores, but a *reference-type* outer-store is neither rejected nor copied. No diagnostic; silent wrong bytes. Workaround: `x = bytes(chunk)` / `x = copy(chunk)`. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/streamprobe/breakcap2.py`. Surfaced adding `requests` streaming (`iter_content` chunks captured outward). The reachable surface now also covers the PRODUCER side of a relay: a resumable-frame borrow-tuple loop var rebound whole (`q0 = p` inside `for p in gen():`) and read after a later pull is accepted with no diagnostic and no copy, so the second frame field aliases the same inner element (probe `/tmp/agents/c1/p5.py`; it agrees with CPython only because the inner generator is materialized in the relay frame and outlives every read). Fix shape: the consumer-escape check must either reject or deep-copy a yielded reference-type value stored to a variable that outlives the iteration step. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR]** Borrow checker doesn't flag `v = d.get(k); d.pop(k); use(v)` as a dangling pointer use (the `del d[k]` face now warns).
  Use-after-free not caught by borrow checker: `old = d.get(k); del d[k]; use(old)` -- `dict.get()` returns a pointer into the dict's internal storage. `del d[k]` frees that entry, making `old` a dangling pointer. The subsequent `use(old)` is undefined behavior (reads garbage). The `del d[k]` face now warns *Mutation of 'd' while borrowed* (re-measured 2026-09-29); the `pop` face is still silent: `v = c.get("a"); x = c.pop("a"); print(v)` emits `double* v = ::tpy::dict_get(c, "a");` then `::tpy::dict_pop(c, "a")` and reads the freed entry through `v` (it happens to print `0.5`), for a declared `dict[str, float]` and an inferred `c = {}` alike. Probes `/tmp/agents/rv4-tc/{p14,p15}.py`.
- **[MED small, deferred: MIR]** Async coro **and sync generator** capturing `&list[i]` (or other container-element addresses) via the pointer-form Optional[NonValue] param shape inherits a borrow-lifetime hazard: any list mutation (push_back, pop, clear, insert) during the resumable's lifetime invalidates the captured `T*` pointer, including across suspension/yield boundaries. Existing borrow-checker covers some `T&` shapes via `return_borrows_from` but not this `T*` source: `_optional_ptr_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:6742`, gated by `_optional_ptr_arg_face`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:9839`) lifts `T&` to `&T` at the call site, the resulting pointer goes into the resumable-frame, and the caller's borrow checker doesn't see this as an escaping borrow with cross-suspension lifetime: a generator over the Optional param's `&xs[0]` whose caller appends to `xs` prints garbage under only a non-fatal, misworded *Mutation of 'xs' while iterating* warning (re-measured 2026-09-29). Pre-existing class of bug, newly reachable since `_classify_params` (gen_async.py) and `gen_generator_struct` (gen_generators.py) started emitting `const T*` / `T*` for pointer-form Optional resumable params. Fix shape: extend `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`'s `gen_borrows` injection (still `if func.is_generator:` only, line 1643) to also cover `func.is_async`, then add mutate-during-resumable-lifetime detection at the call site. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the `async-scope-reset` branch. **Same hazard class, additional route:** the for-loop pointer-form loop var binds `it = &(*(*__for_it_N)++)` (begin_end) or `it = &(unwrap_ref(...))` (iter_next) -- a `T*` aliasing a container element held across a `yield`/`await` inside the loop body. A structural mutation of the iterable during iteration invalidates it. Partially mitigated by the existing mutation-during-iteration *warning* (e.g. `tests/cases/iterators/gen_borrow_mutate_complex` warns on `items.append(...)` while iterating), but the warning is non-fatal, so the dangle is reachable; same fix direction applies. **Note (declaration-driven yield ABI):** this is the genuine *residual* of the borrow ABI -- the *consumer-side* retention of a yielded borrow past its iteration step is checked (re-yield-onward / nested-`def` capture rejected; return/stash caught by dangling/lifetime; value-stores copy), but a *caller* that mutates/frees the borrowed container while the generator is live remains only a warning, and is not closed by the consumer-escape check. **Further route:** tuple-unpack for-loops over `list[tuple[..., Rec]]` add a two-level alias -- `__for_tup = T*` aliases the container element, then each non-value unpack target binds `t = &std::get<i>(*__for_tup)` (a `Rec*` into the same element). Same container-mutation invalidation hazard, same partial warning mitigation, same fix direction. **Further route (statement-level borrow alias):** a single-assign (`a = items[0]`) or a tuple-unpack borrow target from a call/name source (`a, b = first_two(items)`) held across a suspension binds a `T*`/`const T*` frame field aliasing the live source. Same container-mutation-during-suspension invalidation hazard as the for-loop and param shapes; same escape-analysis fix direction.
- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR]** Generator yields holding references into the iterable (`tuple[..., T]` borrow form) dangle if the iterable is structurally mutated between polls.
  The frame's tuple yield slot spells `std::tuple<..., T&>` when the yield type is a non-Optional tuple of non-value elements -- the yielded tuple holds a `T&` into the iterable's backing storage. If the consumer or the generator's post-yield code structurally mutates the iterable (`items.append(...)`, `items.clear()`, dict insert that triggers rehash), already-yielded references dangle. The borrow checker doesn't track iterator-captured containers, so the unsafe pattern compiles under only a non-fatal, misworded *Mutation of 'xs' while iterating* warning (re-measured 2026-09-29: the consumer appends to `xs`, then `t[1].v` prints garbage). Fix path: extend the borrow checker to track "iterable captured by reference in generator lambda", reject structural-mutation methods on it for the duration of any outstanding yielded reference. In the meantime, falling back to value-form yields (`elem_type.to_cpp()` instead of `to_cpp_return()`) trades performance for safety -- could be wired behind an opt-in if user impact warrants.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (silent wrong value; pre-existing) A list a pending coroutine borrows is MOVED at its last use.** [`coroutine-borrowed-arg-auto-moved`] `c = work(xs); holder.append(xs); print(await c)` with `async def work(xs: list[int32])` renders `(*holder).push_back(std::move((*xs)));` while the coroutine frame holds `const std::vector<int32_t>& xs`, so `await c` sees an empty list: TPy prints `0`, CPython `3` (async body and the sync `asyncio.run(c)` spelling alike; master emits the same; probe `/tmp/agents/r5_sm/co_move2.py`). The generator twin copies and warns. Coroutines record the parameters their frame keeps in `return_borrows_from` since 2026-09-24, but the last-use auto-move gate (`compat.demoted_by_hidden_borrow`, the borrow tracker's call-result loans) does not demote on a coroutine's loan. Fix shape: register the coroutine call result's borrow on its arguments the way a generator call's is, so the hidden-borrow demotion sees it.
- **[HIGH small, deferred: MIR] (silent use-after-free, no diagnostic; pre-existing) A coroutine built over a LOCAL and returned escapes its frame's borrow.** [`returned-coroutine-borrows-dead-local`] `def f() -> Own[Cancellable[int32]]: xs = [1, 2, 3]; return work(xs)` compiles and the returned coroutine's frame keeps `const std::vector<int32_t>& xs` into `f`'s dead stack (ASan stack-use-after-return; master emits the same; probe `/tmp/agents/r5_sm/ret_coro_local.py`). The return analysis marks a returned frame's PARAMETER operands as returned borrows but raises no dangling-return error for a local root, where returning a borrow of a local is otherwise rejected (`check_dangling_reference`). Fix shape: route a returned generator or coroutine call through the same dangling-return check as a returned reference, using `frame_borrowed_operands` for its roots.
- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR]** [`create-task-ref-param-escape`] `async def` with reference-typed parameters: a `Task<T>` constructed via `asyncio.create_task` (or `Task::from_coro`) that escapes the caller's scope can dangle on those parameters. A generator face (2026-09-24): a generator name is never rebound, but a generator bound in a loop body is re-emplaced in its slot on every pass, so a task started from it -- directly (`asyncio.create_task(consume(g))`) or by a sync callee (`spawn(g)`) -- reads the next pass's generator (probes `/tmp/agents/r5_meta/c1d.py`, `c1l.py`; a record in the same position behaves the same way).
  `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py:_classify_params` stores non-value-type async-def params as C++ reference fields (`T& param`) in the coroutine struct. When the struct is moved into a `Task<T>` via `create_task` and the Task outlives the parameter's source storage, the reference becomes dangling. Per `docs/ASYNC_DESIGN.md` "Parameter capture": "For escaping calls (`create_task(some_async(items))` where `items` is local to the caller), the borrow checker rejects it." That rejection is not yet implemented. Workaround: pass `Own[T]` so the coroutine struct stores by value, or pass via `Box[T]` / `Rc[T]`, or borrow only module globals (they outlive `asyncio.run`). **Fix is gated on the IR/region migration -- do not bolt this onto the current borrow checker.** A prototype escape+discharge check confirmed the accept/reject boundary works, but it had to key borrow facts on string root names and hardcode the `Task` type / `gather` names -- exactly the "string-key => not designed yet" smell `CLAUDE.md` warns against, and enough ad-hoc machinery that it fights the migration it should be built on. The right shape (Rust's model): this is a lifetime feature. `create_task` should declare a run-stable / `'static`-equivalent **bound on its coroutine argument** in its signature, enforced by the general region checker -- so a user's own `spawn` gets safety for free with no compiler edits; the borrow-a-local-but-join variant is a structured **`TaskGroup`** API whose block scope bounds the borrowed tasks (cf. `std::thread::scope`). Neither is expressible until TPy has lifetimes/regions (the THIR/MIR work); until then this stays an open, documented footgun with the workarounds above. **Extended by M7 (generic async free functions / methods, branch `feat-generic-async-free-funcs`)** to the `_CoroParamKind.TYPE_PARAM` storage form: when T is non-value at instantiation, `val_or_ref_t<T>` resolves to `T&`, so a generic async free function or method called with a borrowed reference-type arg whose source goes out of scope before the next poll has the same dangling-ref class -- not a new symptom, just a new path through which the existing hazard can manifest. Same fix applies. **Extended by H4 (protocol-param generators)** to two more vectors: (a) `_CoroParamKind.STATIC_PROTOCOL` -- a static-protocol param captured as `T_<pname>` deduces to a reference for an lvalue arg, so the same escape applies (`create_task(consume(local_iterable))`); (b) the **sync-generator** field-store form, newly reachable now that protocol-param generators compile -- a generator that borrows a reference-type iterable (`T_it = list&`) stored into a field/container/global (`self.g = echo(local_xs)`) dangles when `local_xs` goes out of scope, with only a non-fatal "mutation while borrowed" warning at the mutation site and no escape diagnostic. The borrow-checker escape analysis is the same fix; it must cover generator factories, not just `create_task`. **Extended by the container family (2026-09-05)**: a `list` / `dict` / `set` / `bytearray` / `Array` parameter of an `async def` or a generator now lowers where the lowering used to refuse the parameter outright, so those types reach the same reference-field capture (`std::vector<int32_t>& xs` in the coroutine struct) that records already had. No new hazard class and the render is what records emit on master -- only the set of parameter types that can reach it grew. **Extended by the borrowing-VIEW family (2026-09-09)**, on the same footing: a `Span[T]` / `Span[readonly[T]]` frame param is a by-value view whose VALUE borrows the caller's storage, so `create_task(bump([1, 2, 3]))` inside a coroutine body hoists the literal's backing array into the suspending block and the task then outlives it -- byte-for-byte the behaviour the `list[T]` spelling of the same call already has (that one segfaults; the view reads garbage). The sync call site (`g = gen([1, 2, 3])`) and the inline-`await` position are NOT affected: both hoist the backing storage into a scope that outlives the frame object, pinned by `generators/gen_view_param_frame`. Only the escaping `create_task` position remains, and it remains for the reference family identically. **Narrowed and then extended by the frame-temp hoist (2026-09-11):** a temporary argument at a factory call inside a resumable body is now seated on a `__coro_arg_N` field of the ENCLOSING frame, so `create_task(bump([1, 2, 3]))` / `create_task(reader(make(3)))` is safe for as long as that frame lives (pinned by `generators/gen_view_param_frame`'s resumable sections; `async/start_server_echo` ASAN-clean). What remains is the escape of the TASK past its borrows. A helper `async def` that RETURNS the `create_task(...)` Task (`async def spawn() -> Task[int32]: return create_task(reader(make(3)))`) now rejects at `return.borrow_form` (re-measured 2026-09-29), but a SYNC helper that hands the task to its caller's list still dangles: `def helper(tasks: list[asyncio.Task[int32]]) -> None: xs = [1, 2, 3]; tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(work(xs)))`, with `async def work(xs: list[int32]) -> int32` summing `xs` after an `await`, then `for t in tasks: print(await t)` in `main`, segfaults (exit 139) where CPython prints `6`. `gen_async._hoist_frame_factory_args`'s docstring cites this entry. **Narrowed again by the shared-seat reject (2026-09-11):** the field is one per call SITE, so the seat only covers a site at which at most one handle is alive at a time; a site inside a LOOP whose handle is handed on (`create_task(f(<temp>))`, a bound handle appended to a list) would give every task the last iteration's value and is now refused with a located message (`async/error_task_temp_in_loop`) instead of being seated. The positions that consume the handle where it stands -- a `for` head, an inline `await`, a bare discard, a bind whose name is only drained -- keep sharing one field per site (`generators/gen_view_param_frame`'s loop sections). What stays open here is the site OUTSIDE a loop whose Task escapes the frame, described above. **Extended by the `_CoroParamKind.FN` form** (Fn params in resumable generators): the callable is forwarded and stored by value in the frame (sound for the callable object itself), but an `Fn` lambda that captures a local *by reference* (`[&local]`) and is passed into an escaping generator dangles when `local`'s scope ends -- the lambda's interior reference targets are not tracked, distinct from the lvalue-arg-deduces-a-reference route but the same escape class and same IR-gated fix. **One sub-class the "borrow only module globals" workaround does NOT cover:** a `@dynamic` protocol param borrows the call site's `RefAdapter` temp rather than the argument, so the frame dangles even when the argument is a module global -- no user-chosen argument lifetime makes it safe, and the fix has to own the adapter (`BUGS.md#res-param-dyn-protocol-frame`). Not reachable today, since that param shape is rejected on an async frame.
- **[MED medium, deferred: MIR]** Borrowed-mode `await` operands can dangle if the awaited reference-type object does not outlive the suspension.

This is correct for stable lvalues such as frame fields, but it is unsafe if the operand is a temporary or a shorter-lived local whose lifetime ends before the awaiter resumes. The missing borrow check is the same shape as the escaping `create_task` capture bug above: any borrowed await operand must be proven to outlive the coroutine suspension, or the compiler should reject it with a clear diagnostic. **Same gap, now reachable via more arg shapes (await of a static-protocol-param coroutine):** `await consume(rows[0])` where `consume(it: Iterable[int])` and `rows` is a param/field borrows `rows[0]` by reference into the sub-future (the forwarding-deduction field type deduces `U&` for the lvalue) and dangles if the container is structurally mutated across the suspension -- no diagnostic. Sound when `mgr` outlives the suspension (the common synchronous-shaped case); but if the async-with-containing frame escapes (e.g. `create_task`) past `mgr`'s lifetime, the manager pointer dangles -- same missing escape/outlives check, IR-gated like the rest of this entry. **Another route (abandonment-cleanup destructor):** a generator/coroutine frame suspended inside `with mgr:` (borrowed lvalue manager, `with_borrowed_fields` -> `T*` frame field) that ESCAPES the manager's scope -- verified reachable: `def make() -> Own[Iterator[int]]: cm = CM(); g = gen(cm); next(g); return g` compiles with no diagnostic -- now dereferences the dead manager in the frame DESTRUCTOR's `__exit__` cleanup as well as on the resume path (the resume-path deref predates the destructor). Same escape-analysis fix; the destructor adds the abandon-without-resume trigger.

A `str` parameter is a `std::string_view`, so the caller's `r.name[3:]` reaches the callee as a view into `r.name`'s buffer. With `class Rec` holding `name: str`, `def f(r: Rec, s: str) -> str: r.name = s; return s` and `r = Rec("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")`, the call `f(r, r.name[3:])` prints `ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\0yz` where CPython prints `defghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz`: the assignment replaces the buffer the view reads (here an overlapping self-assign, generally a freed one). Sema's borrow tracker sees no loan from a parameter to the caller's field, so neither the write nor the read after it is checked. MIR reports the body's possible conflict (`tests/cases/mir/views_as_places` `write_then_reuse`, `mir(conflict /^replacement$/)`) but proving it needs the caller's argument facts.
